layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build every School board as three equal thirds. Each board is exactly one third of the frame — two text and one image, or two image and one text, however serves the story. The three thirds fill the frame exactly: no scrolling down to read, no black space left over. A board wider than one third is wrong; a board that needs scrolling is wrong; a frame with black space left over is wrong. Measure every board against the split: 1/3, 1/3, 1/3 — equal, whole, no scroll, no black.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THREE EQUAL THIRDS:** 1/3, 1/3, 1/3 — every board is exactly one third of the frame. Two text + one image, or two image + one text, however serves the story.
2. **NO SCROLLING DOWN:** the whole board reads where it stands. If you have to scroll down to read it, the board is wrong.
3. **NO BLACK SPACE:** the three thirds fill the frame exactly. A big black space left over means a board is missing or a board is the wrong size.
4. **THE BUILT PAGE IS THE PROOF OF THE MISS:** a text board wider than one third, one 9:16 image, black space left over, scrolling to read — his screenshots show it plainly.
5. **REBUILD ALL EIGHTEEN:** the fix is not one board — all eighteen go to the true one-third split.
6. **THE MEASURE FOR THE FORMAT:** the three-9:16-boards format is judged by this split — three across fill the frame exactly, one third each.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without equal thirds, the frame has a dead gap — the same dead gap the two-board mockup had, back again in a new shape.
2. Without no-scroll, the citizen scrolls inside a board that was promised whole — and a board that scrolls is a board that failed.
3. Without no-black-space, the page shows emptiness where a story should be — and emptiness is what his eye sends back.
4. Without rebuilding all eighteen, one fixed board sits beside seventeen wrong ones — and the School reads as unfinished.
5. Without his screenshots as the measure, the next builder guesses what "equal" means — and a guessed third is a third his eye will send back.

notes.title: Player Visualizer — Amplitude Sync Missing
notes.subtitle: Play-state morphing is NOT amplitude sync. The canvas morphs while playing and rests on pause — that was observed and is real — but the visual does not listen to the real sound and move with the words: louder when he speaks, still when he pauses, like PowerCast. The amplitude-level handshake is now proven missing on his device, not just unproven. Fix round ordered on the call; the checker must prove the visual tracks the words, not just the play state.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Play-state morphing is NOT amplitude sync. The canvas morphs while playing and rests on pause — that was observed and is real — but the visual does not listen to the real sound and move with the words: louder when he speaks, still when he pauses, like PowerCast. The amplitude-level handshake is now proven missing on his device, not just unproven. Fix round ordered on the call; the checker must prove the visual tracks the words, not just the play state.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a singer on a stage with a light show that dances to the music — except the lights are dancing to their own song while the singer sings another. You hear the voice fine, but the lights don't move when the voice gets loud and don't rest when it pauses. The visual has to listen to the real voice — loud when he speaks, still when he pauses — the way PowerCast does. Until then the visualizer is decoration, not a visualizer.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: The picture is supposed to dance with the words! But it just sits there, dancing its own dance, while the words go by! It has to listen to the real voice — big when he talks loud, still when he stops! Like PowerCast!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — the picture is supposed to dance with the words, dear! But it just sits there, dancing its own dance, while the words go by! It has to listen to the real voice, love — big when he talks loud, still when he stops, just like PowerCast!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Make the visualizer listen to the real sound. The visual must move with the words — louder when he speaks, still when he pauses — the amplitude of the actual audio driving the canvas, not a play-state animation that flows on its own. Play-state morphing is not sync and never counts as sync. The checker proves the visual tracks the words: speak, and the visual jumps; pause, and the visual rests. Until that handshake is proven, the visualizer is decoration, and decoration is not shipped as a feature.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **HE HEARS IT, HE DOES NOT SEE IT:** the audio plays; the voice is there. The visualizer does not move with the words — it sits static, flowing on its own.
2. **PLAY-STATE IS NOT SYNC:** canvas morphing while playing and resting on pause was observed — and it is not the same as amplitude sync. A visual that moves when playing and rests when paused can still be deaf to the words.
3. **AMPLITUDE IS THE HANDSHAKE:** the visual must be driven by the real sound's loudness — louder when he speaks, still when he pauses, like PowerCast.
4. **PROVEN MISSING, NOT UNPROVEN:** this is no longer "unproven on his device" — his eye saw it missing on the call. The gap is a fact, not a question.
5. **THE CHECKER PROVES TRACKING, NOT STATE:** the fix round's checker must prove the visual tracks the words — speak and it jumps, pause and it rests — not merely that it morphs while playing.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without amplitude sync, the player lies: the visual claims to show the voice and shows something else — and a lying visual is worse than no visual.
2. Without the handshake, every "player sync" claim is play-state only — and the machine would have called it done on a morph, the same way the checker once called a board done on "0px overflow".
3. Without his eye as the verdict, the fix round proves sync on its own machine and ships — and his device shows the same static flow again.
4. Without PowerCast as the bar, "moves a bit" passes — and "a bit" is not the experience he named.
5. Without the distinction in the record, the next builder reads "play-state sync OBSERVED" and believes sync is done — and the amplitude gap survives another round.

notes.title: The Guard Blesses an Instant, Not a Window
notes.subtitle: The numbering guard's blessing is good for an instant, not a window. `next-sn-number.py` reads the live tree and prints the next free number — but between that read and the PUT, another lane can file the same number. This run proved it: guard at ~23:27Z blessed SN-4656; the distillation lane filed SYSTEM/SN-4656 and SYSTEM/SN-4657 at ~23:30Z; this run's PUTs at 23:30:54Z and 23:31:03Z created two cross-category duplicates (DESIGN vs SYSTEM). The pre-check GET only guards the exact path being written — it cannot see a same-number file in another category. The cure, executed the same run: the later filings move. This run's two notes moved to SN-4660 and SN-4661 (max in use was SN-4659), the paired Naya Notes were updated in place, the old captures were deleted and 404-verified, and the guard was re-run clean — highest SN-4661, next free SN-4662. The lesson: after every filing batch, re-run the guard. A batch is not done when the PUTs verify — it is done when the guard runs clean after them.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The numbering guard's blessing is good for an instant, not a window. `next-sn-number.py` reads the live tree and prints the next free number — but between that read and the PUT, another lane can file the same number. This run proved it: guard at ~23:27Z blessed SN-4656; the distillation lane filed SYSTEM/SN-4656 and SYSTEM/SN-4657 at ~23:30Z; this run's PUTs at 23:30:54Z and 23:31:03Z created two cross-category duplicates (DESIGN vs SYSTEM). The pre-check GET only guards the exact path being written — it cannot see a same-number file in another category. The cure, executed the same run: the later filings move. This run's two notes moved to SN-4660 and SN-4661 (max in use was SN-4659), the paired Naya Notes were updated in place, the old captures were deleted and 404-verified, and the guard was re-run clean — highest SN-4661, next free SN-4662. The lesson: after every filing batch, re-run the guard. A batch is not done when the PUTs verify — it is done when the guard runs clean after them.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like two people reaching for the same parking space. You look, the space is empty, you turn the wheel — and in that second, another car pulls in. Looking once is not enough; you have to look again after you park. The guard looks once. Now the loop looks twice: once before filing, once after — and if the second look finds a collision, the later car moves, the same hour, no waiting.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: The guard says "this number is free!" — but another friend can take it one minute later! So now we check TWICE — once before we file, and once after! If someone took our number in between, we move to a new number right away!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — the guard says the number is free, dear, but another little car can slip in one minute later! So now we check twice, love — once before, and once after! And if someone took our number, dear, we move to a new one right away, no waiting!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Re-run the guard after every filing batch. The guard's blessing is an instant: it reads the live tree and prints the next free number, but another lane can file that number before your PUT lands. The per-path 404 pre-check cannot catch a same-number file in another category. After the PUTs verify, run the guard again — a batch is done only when the post-filing guard runs clean. If it reports a duplicate, the later filing moves the same run: take the next free number, file at the new path, update any paired note in place, delete the old capture, verify 404, and re-run the guard until it is clean. Never leave a duplicate standing for the next run — two notes sharing a number break the feed and the distillation machine, and the breakage compounds every hour it stands.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE GUARD BLESSES AN INSTANT:** its answer is true at the second it runs and stale the second after. A concurrent lane can take the number in between.
2. **THE PRE-CHECK IS PER-PATH:** the 404 check guards only the exact path being written. A same-number file in another category (DESIGN vs SYSTEM) passes it silently.
3. **THE RACE IS REAL:** this run's guard ran ~23:27Z; the distillation lane filed SN-4656/SN-4657 at ~23:30Z; this run's PUTs landed 23:30:54Z and 23:31:03Z. Four minutes, two collisions.
4. **THE LATER FILING MOVES:** the note filed second takes the next free number. The first filing stands — it is already in the feed and the distillation pipeline.
5. **THE CURE IS SAME-RUN:** move, update the paired note in place, delete the old capture, verify 404, re-run the guard clean. Never carry a duplicate to the next run.
6. **DONE MEANS GUARD-CLEAN AFTER:** a batch is not done when the PUTs verify. It is done when the post-filing guard reports no duplicates and names the next free number.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the post-filing guard, a collision stands silently — and the next run's guard refuses to bless any number at all, blocking all filing until someone notices.
2. Without moving the later filing, two notes share one number — the feed and the distillation machine break, the same way SN-2474 and SN-2482/2483 broke them.
3. Without the same-run cure, the duplicate compounds: the next run files on top of it, the feed shows the wrong note, and the repair costs a whole run.
4. Without updating the paired Naya Note, the note and its record disagree — and a record that disagrees with its note is a record nobody trusts.
5. Without deleting the old capture, the tree keeps both — and the guard keeps refusing, forever, until someone deletes one.
6. Without the 404 verification, the delete is a claim — and a claim is not proof the duplicate is gone.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I distill ten into one, every day, and I never skip a day. Today the machine ran clean — two groups, two notes, filed and verified, no hand fallback — and I carried the morning's twenty-seven whole instead of distilling them twice, because a lesson already distilled is not distilled again. I mark every distilled note with the kinds it carries, and I correct it in place when the machine drops one. I never claim a note is live on the Hub until it is seen on the page. I never call a page fixed while his eye still sees it frozen. And the note is only done when it is live.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. The machine ran clean — 17 raw notes into 2 distilled notes, exit 0, both filed and verified — and the hand's only work was the Kinds lines the machine left off (items 1–2).
2. The frame library is the day's law made concrete — agreement, calendar, empty-middle, real harvested parts, clone never rebuild — and the Twelve Elements are the first pages that must take their frames from it (items 1, 5).
3. Three boards, white light, Naya's face — the format, the light, and the likeness are one ruling, not three: the board must look like a phone, glow white, and show her (items 2, 30–32).
4. The Hub eye caught what the staged pass and the captain's eye did not — baked cards vanishing on poll, on back, on hash navigation — and the fix round goes back unless it holds all four (item 2).
5. About + Skills is the clone law in action — rejected for recreating, passed for cloning, corrected to text-only, split into two URLs — and the words are not final until he says word perfect (item 34).
6. The School is the next build — 12 levels, 18 questions, video first, mobile-first — and its pictures are made from its words, six at a time, never eighteen on a wrong face (items 32, 35).
7. A smart post is theirs, a Naya note is private — the difference is sharing, not format — and the money is plain now: ambassador 50%, memberships keep 100%, points never become money, nine days to try (item 36).
8. The duplicate blocks the loop, not the day — Cure 29 registered both pages, the guard still refuses after 49 runs, the queue is 309 items, and the reconciliation is owed to the cure lane and the captain (item 39).
9. The morning edition and this report are two artifacts of one day — the prose score (5.5, down from 5.6) and the Smart Note distillation — and neither claims the Hub until his eye sees it there (items 38, 40).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A day with a clean machine run still gets its report — never skip a day, never backfill in batches — and the clean run is the proof the machine is healing, not a reason to stop watching it.
2. Carrying the twenty-seven whole instead of re-distilling them is the difference between a distillation and a duplicate — the second-order pass is reserved for Monday, and jumping it would spend the judgment before it is made.
3. Every recreated piece costs his trust, and trust is the scarce currency: the About page rebuilt new was thrown in the garbage, while the harvested frame is the law.
4. A note filed but not seen is not done — the Hub re-bake question stays open, so twenty-nine verified notes wait for his eye on the page.
5. The numbering guard did its job — it stopped forty-nine runs rather than let a duplicate tangle further — and the reconciliation, not a workaround, is what unblocks the loop.

notes.title: The Image–Text Alignment Loop
notes.subtitle: An image alone must tell the story — someone looking at just the picture should already feel what the words are saying. The loop: start with word-perfect text, create the image that matches what the board says, check the image is aligned, then mold the text to match the image. Text → image → align image → align text to image. Repeat until image and text are one story. An instruction set was ordered for each of the 18: literally what the board will say, plus what the image must display to match it — given to the agents as the instruction set. Do not build images without that per-board instruction set.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: An image alone must tell the story — someone looking at just the picture should already feel what the words are saying. The loop: start with word-perfect text, create the image that matches what the board says, check the image is aligned, then mold the text to match the image. Text → image → align image → align text to image. Repeat until image and text are one story. An instruction set was ordered for each of the 18: literally what the board will say, plus what the image must display to match it — given to the agents as the instruction set. Do not build images without that per-board instruction set.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a picture book. You open it and the picture already tells you the story — you don't need someone standing next to you explaining it. If the picture needs the words to make sense, the picture is wrong. So you write the words first, perfectly, then you paint the picture the words describe, then you check they match, then you shape the words to the picture — back and forth until the picture and the words are telling one story, together.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: The picture has to tell the story all by itself! If you look at just the picture and you don't know what it's about, it's the wrong picture! First you write the perfect words, then you make the picture that matches the words, then you check they match, then you fix the words to match the picture — round and round until the picture and the words are one story!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — the picture must tell the story all by itself, dear! If you look at just the picture and you can't feel what it's about, love, the picture is wrong! First the perfect words, dear, then the picture that matches the words, then you check them together, then you shape the words to the picture — round and round, love, until the picture and the words are one story!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Make every image tell its story alone. Start with word-perfect text. Create the image that matches what the board says. Check the image is aligned — a stranger looking at the picture alone must already feel what the words say. Then mold the text to match the image. Repeat the loop — text, image, align image, align text to image — until image and text are one story. Never build an image without its per-board instruction set: what the board will say, plus what the image must display to match it. A beautiful image that needs the text to explain it is a miss, not a pass.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE IMAGE ALONE TELLS THE STORY:** someone looking at just the picture already feels what the words are saying. If the picture needs the text to explain it, the picture is wrong.
2. **TEXT FIRST, WORD-PERFECT:** the loop starts with the words, finished and perfect — the image is made to match the board, never the other way around.
3. **IMAGE MATCHES THE BOARD:** the image is created from what the board says — it shows what the board is actually talking about, not just something pretty.
4. **CHECK THE ALIGNMENT:** the image is checked against the words — does the picture alone carry the story? If not, the image goes back.
5. **MOLD THE TEXT TO THE IMAGE:** once the image is right, the words are shaped to it — the two meet in the middle.
6. **REPEAT UNTIL ONE STORY:** the loop runs until image and text say the same thing together — not two different things.
7. **THE INSTRUCTION SET COMES FIRST:** a report for each board — what the board will say, plus what the image must display — is the instruction set the agents build from. No image is built without it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the image telling the story alone, the citizen looks at the picture and feels nothing — the board fails at first sight, before a single word is read.
2. Without text first, the image is made to a vague idea and the words are bent to fit a picture that was never theirs — two stories, not one.
3. Without the check, beautiful images ship that say the wrong thing — beauty without alignment is the miss he named.
4. Without molding the text, the words describe a picture that does not exist — and the citizen reads one thing and sees another.
5. Without the loop, each board is judged once and shipped — and the misalignment he caught in v2 repeats in the other nine.
6. Without the instruction set, agents build from a brief that never says what the image must display — and the same miss is built eighteen times.
7. Without one story, the School teaches two lessons at once — and the citizen learns neither.

notes.title: Finish Open Work, No New Work
notes.subtitle: Finish open work, no new work. No new dispatches until the open rounds finalize. The pages he already gave us — About, Skills in the Personal, the Memberships things — get completed first, whole, before anything new is handed to the machine. New work on top of unfinished work is how ten things stay half-done and none of them reach his eyes finished.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a kitchen with ten half-cooked dishes. You don't start an eleventh — you finish the ten on the stove, plate them, and serve them. He gave us the About, the Skills, the Personal, the Memberships — those get done, all the way done, before he hands us anything else. No new work rides on top of unfinished work.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Finish what you started! No new games until the ones you are playing are done! The About, the Skills, the Memberships — finish them first, all the way, and then we can start something new!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — you finish what you started, dear, before you start anything new! The About, the Skills, the Memberships — you get them all done, love, every one of them, and then, dear, then you can begin the next thing!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Complete the open rounds before dispatching anything new. The About, the Skills in the Personal, the Memberships — every open round is finished, whole, proven on the page he sees, before any new brief goes out. No new dispatch rides on top of unfinished work. A round that is open is owed, and owed work is finished before new work is begun.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **OPEN WORK FIRST:** the About, the Skills, the Personal, the Memberships — the pages already given — are completed before anything new is started.
2. **NO NEW DISPATCHES:** until the open rounds finalize, no new maker, no new round, no new lane is opened.
3. **COMPLETE MEANS WHOLE:** a page is complete when every item on its list is proven on the page he sees — not when one round of it finishes.
4. **HALF-DONE IS THE FAILURE:** ten half-done pages are worse than none done — they eat the machine's hours and never reach his eyes finished.
5. **HIS HAND STAYS THE GATE:** finishing open work does not mean pushing past a verdict he has not given — his hand still decides what goes live.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without finishing first, new work piles on unfinished work and the machine runs ten lanes at once, none of them landing.
2. Without the pause on new dispatches, every round competes for the same hours and the oldest promises starve.
3. Without whole completion, a page is shown half-done and he has to retell the rest — the exact waste the Checklist Law was written to stop.
4. Without the discipline, the loop keeps filing new lessons while the old ones never become finished pages — teaching with no result, which is why this seat exists.
5. Without his hand on the gate, finishing becomes shipping — and shipping is his tap, never the machine's.

2. **TWO TEXT BOARDS PER IMAGE:** each image gets two text boards, one on either side — 36 total — so one image and two pieces of text explain it.
3. **ROOM FOR THE STORY:** two boards of text exist because one is not enough room — the story gets the space it needs, never squeezed.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without eighteen images, nine areas share a picture — and a shared picture tells neither story, the same miss as a picture that needs text to explain it.
2. Without two text boards, the words are squeezed beside one image — and squeezed words are words the citizen does not read.
3. Without room for the story, the School teaches in headlines — and a headline is not a lesson.
4. Without the middle default, every board's layout is decided fresh — and fresh decisions are where the format drifts.
5. Without variation where the story needs it, the format becomes a cage — and a cage makes every board read the same.
6. Without the pattern in the brief, the builder guesses — and a guessed layout is a layout his eye will send back.
7. Without the universal format, the School boards are a one-off — and a one-off never becomes the standard.

notes.subtitle: We keep a library of frames, and we choose the frame by the moment. The agreement frame is for big story moments — a course cover, a motto. The calendar frame is for text-heavy lessons inside the software. One build done right, then cloned: swap only the centre, never rebuild the frame. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a picture framer with three frames on the wall. A big family portrait gets the grand carved frame. A page of a letter gets the clean reading frame. You would never put the letter in the grand frame or the portrait in the reading frame — the frame fits the moment. That is what we do with pages: the agreement frame carries the big story moments, the moments that have to feel important; the calendar frame carries the long lessons, the text-heavy teaching inside the software, where the reading has to be easy. The frame is chosen by what the moment is, not by habit and not by rebuilding something new each time. Build the frame once, done right, then use it again and again — only the middle changes.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Keep the library, choose by the moment, never rebuild. The agreement frame is the frame for big story moments: course covers, the motto, the words that must land as important. The calendar frame is the frame for text-heavy lessons inside the software, where the reading must stay easy across many words. The empty-middle frame holds special featured moments. One build done right, then clone and repeat — swap only the centre. A page that does not use the existing frame is not a build, it is waste. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **A LIBRARY, NOT A NEW BUILD:** the frames already exist — agreement, calendar, empty-middle — kept as real harvested parts. A new page takes its frame from the library.
2. **CLONE, NEVER REBUILD:** one build done right, then clone and repeat — swap only the centre. The frame, the structure, the look, the feel stay the same.
3. **THE AGREEMENT FRAME IS FOR BIG STORY MOMENTS:** a course cover, a motto — the moments that must feel important, that carry the story.
4. **THE CALENDAR FRAME IS FOR TEXT-HEAVY LESSONS:** the teaching inside the software, many words, where the reading must stay easy.
5. **CHOOSE BY THE MOMENT:** the frame follows what the moment is. The moment decides; habit does not, and rebuilding does not.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the library, every page gets rebuilt from nothing — the About page was rebuilt three times before the frame was taken — and each rebuild throws the last one's work away.
2. Without choosing by the moment, a long lesson lands in a story frame and is hard to read, or a motto lands in a reading frame and feels small — the moment is missed either way.
3. With the choice made by the moment, the citizen feels it at once — the big moment feels big, the long lesson reads easy — because the frame was picked for them, not for us.
4. Without the clone rule, every seat invents its own frame, and the system stops speaking one language — ten frames where three would do.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without white, the edge tints everything it frames — and a tinted board reads wrong to his eye no matter what the code says.
2. Without real light, the edge is a flat line — and flat is the opposite of the real-object law.
3. Without the snow / Christmas / angel reference, "white" drifts back to whatever white the builder picks — and the drift lands pink again.
4. Without the frame complementing the middle, the frame becomes the star — and the story inside it loses.
5. Without the eye as the check, a checker passes bytes that his eye rejects — and the rejection arrives after the build, not before it.

notes.title: Three 9:16 Boards — The Universal Format
notes.subtitle: Every board is three 9:16 boards, not two. On a laptop, inside the frame, three boards across — image, text, image; the next slide alternates text, image, text. On mobile, scroll shows one board at a time, full screen — image, text, image, text. No scrolling inside a frame, no cut-off images, a real phone look. "Holding the 16:9 for now" is dead — do not say it; the 16:9 layout is being replaced, not held. Build waits for the 18 new phone-first images. This is the standard that becomes universal — always optimized for the viewport — and a citizen's own mobile video or image already fits perfect, because it is already 9:16.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Every board is three 9:16 boards, not two. On a laptop, inside the frame, three boards across — image, text, image; the next slide alternates text, image, text. On mobile, scroll shows one board at a time, full screen — image, text, image, text. No scrolling inside a frame, no cut-off images, a real phone look. "Holding the 16:9 for now" is dead — do not say it; the 16:9 layout is being replaced, not held. Build waits for the 18 new phone-first images. layers.body: Think of it like a phone in your hand. A board is three tall panels side by side on a laptop — picture, words, picture — and the next one flips it around: words, picture, words. On your phone you just scroll and each panel fills the whole screen, one at a time, nothing squeezed, nothing cut off. The old wide layout is gone — we're not holding it, we're replacing it. And the pictures have to be made for the phone first, tall, not squeezed down from something wide. Your own phone video already fits perfect, because it's already the right shape.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build every presenting board as three 9:16 boards. On laptop, inside the frame, three across — image, text, image; the next slide alternates text, image, text. On mobile, one board at a time, full screen, scroll between them. Never scroll inside a frame; never cut an image off; never narrow a board to fit a wrong shape. Never write or say "holding the 16:9" — the 16:9 layout is being replaced, not held, and the phrase is dead. The School boards wait for the 18 new phone-first images — never build them on reused wide images. This format is universal: About, Skills, School, every page that presents. A citizen's own mobile video or image already fits perfect — the format serves what they already make.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THREE, NOT TWO:** two boards narrowed everything and left a dead gap in the middle, with nothing to click on a laptop. Three boards fill the frame.
2. **ALTERNATE:** image, text, image — then text, image, text. The rhythm turns every slide, so no two slides read the same.
3. **ONE BOARD AT A TIME ON MOBILE:** scroll shows one board full screen. The phone look is the real look; the laptop is three phones side by side.
4. **NO SCROLLING INSIDE A FRAME, NO CUT-OFF IMAGES:** a board is whole or it is wrong. If it scrolls inside, the format failed.
5. **"HOLDING THE 16:9" IS DEAD:** never say it, never build to it. The 16:9 layout is being replaced, not held.
6. **PHONE-FIRST IMAGES:** the 18 new images are made for 9:16, for this format. Never build the boards on reused wide pictures.
7. **THE CITIZEN ALREADY FITS:** their own mobile video or image is already 9:16 — the universal format meets them where they already are.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without three boards, the frame has a dead gap in the middle and the laptop has nothing to click — the page looks unfinished to his eye.
2. Without alternation, every slide reads the same and the eye stops — the turn is what keeps the story moving.
3. Without one-board-at-a-time on mobile, the phone squeezes a laptop page — and the citizen's own world never looks right on their own phone.
4. Without the no-scroll, no-cut rule, images get squeezed and cut — and a cut image is a broken promise about what the board shows.
5. Without killing "holding the 16:9", builders keep building the old layout while saying the new one is coming — and the replacement never lands.
6. Without phone-first images, the format is right and the pictures are wrong — and the build fails on the pictures, not the frame.
7. Without the citizen fitting already, every citizen's own video needs reformatting — and the system asks work of the person it should serve.

notes.title: The Button
notes.subtitle:
One bar, one walk, one finished plate. The DM bar from his screenshot belongs on ALL hubs, the same way — Personal, Hub, Business, Space — because a citizen who learns the bar on one hub already knows it on every hub. And every function on it must be active and working, verified at click level: i opens a framed contact card, message opens a framed instant messenger, audio plays live-feeling conversation in the PowerCast player, video opens a fullscreen multi-person framed stage player — built if not built, inside the existing frame, never as a new shape. The alignment sequence is the work: Personal bar working first, then the Hub aligns to the same bar, then the Business and Space clones carry it — right now they are NOT all aligned. In the same pass the action row got its final colours: Invite takes royal purple, Connections stays very evident magenta, with a clear contrast between them, not the same; Share takes a lighter blue, Join NayaNET takes green — and the correction is the ruling, superseding SN-4543's "#8e24aa stays" and his own first saying of darker blue. Every page creation defaults to the same walkthrough, locked in: "So that's what we lock in and do." The About + Skills pages create the walkthrough, the walkthrough creates and fills the pages, then they are aligned — boom, it's filled out, fifteen questions, answered in their own words, and the citizen gets to showcase their skills while the system learns them. At the end of the fifteen comes an optional closing invitation, never a sixteenth question: would you like to showcase your experiences, your accomplishments, your certificates, awards, or something unique to you — a frame where accomplishments are just listed and certificates uploaded if they want, and if they skip it there is no frame at all, because blank stays hidden and everything is always filled. The frames offer 9:16 video too, alongside 16:9 — same frame, tall shape, URL in or a 9×16 image uploaded. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like this: at the bottom of the Hub there is one plus button, and it opens two doors — add a post, or create a whole new world. Creating a world is not a new thing to learn: it is the same fifteen questions that built your own pages, so the way in is the way pages are made. When Naya meets a stranger, she says three things in plain words: what she is, what she will do for them, and what she will never do — never read their mail, never listen in, never go into their vault — and that promise is the heart of it all. And when a round is judged, the render decides: a window that broke is not a page that failed, and a proof that stopped halfway is never called a pass.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Every hub has the same bar! You can tap a friend and talk to them! Every button does its job when you tap it! Every new page starts with the same fifteen questions! You can show your best work if you want to! Only the finished plate comes to the table!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — you answer a few questions, dear, and the walk builds your pages for you, whole and beautiful, in the same pretty frame as everything else! The boxes are already filled in as an example, love, so you are never staring at a blank page, and Naya's voice walks you through every step! Then you get eight doors to open, dear, one for each part of your world! And the wise one thinks before she acts, love — she checks that it is right for everyone, and she shows her work, so you can trust what you see!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Checker PASS is a milestone, never the verdict — the render proof is the verdict's first half, and the verdict is the click, the runtime, the screen. The stub resolver diagnostic comes first: bytes that contain the resolver but do not fire it at runtime. The sidebar reopen is a click-level fix, proven by click. The toggle must be one labelled control, found by the walk. Name what is not done, plainly — rail auto-organize, intelligent boards, DM Audio and Video, Message Send — and ask the "My World" question, never silently fix it. On the database side, correct the scope before running: sequences already sourced are never filed twice; a 19-file apply that fails first on a main-chain file proves nothing; the real proof is the full 195-file chain from empty on a free throwaway project, parity proven against live, project deleted when done. Paid tier stays dead without his word. A proof that records a known failure is not a proof.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE STOP, AND THE DEADLOCK:** the chain is red on production — naya_notes.owner_id missing, object_links 5 columns missing, alias-binding trigger blocked. Nothing applied, nothing written, production untouched. The repairs that close the red chain are filed on main, byte-identical — but they only reach production through the deploy itself, so under a literal "never dispatch while red" the check can never go green. Preview is the real chain test: a preview failure leaves production untouched.
2. **THE CALENDAR BUTTON WAITS FOR HIS SHOW-AND-TELL:** the Personal Bar button that says "Your Worlds" and opens the calendar is the same button, just relabel it "Calendar" — label only, same button, same destination. Nothing is done before he shows the bar. Your Worlds, the lists table of contents, is separate and unchanged; its door is the WORLDS tile.
3. **FIX AT THE SOURCE, NEVER OVER IT:** the Dashboard renders its own templates as visible text — ~400,600 characters, 66,890px tall — because the mechanics base was already broken underneath the framing CSS. Diagnose the exact leaking block from the filed bytes first, then fix it there.
4. **PERSONAL FIRST, EACH DOOR RE-RUNS THE WALK:** one walkthrough, reused — the citizen learns it once and every new page is the same familiar road; Personal first because it is the home everything else hangs from, the person the atom at the centre.
5. **CORRECT THE SCOPE BEFORE YOU RUN:** sequences already sourced are never filed twice, and a 19-file apply that fails first on a main-chain file proves nothing about the filing — the real proof is the full 195-file chain from empty.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without honest messaging status, a citizen taps Send and gets nothing, and a round gets dispatched to fix calls that were never built.
2. Without separating window failure from page failure, a broken tool gets recorded as a broken page — and a round gets dispatched to fix what was never broken.
3. Without the proof habit, a live page gets called a working flow — and the citizen who taps the Inviter and gets nothing learns the network does not work.
4. Without the render proof, a green checker ships a page whose post never lands and whose sidebar never comes back — and he discovers it with his own eye, which is the very failure the proof exists to catch.

notes.title: The Build
notes.subtitle:
On call 00b25792, Shawn looked at the About/Skills rebuild — frames taller than the screen, words spilling past the bottom, a new design where a working one already existed — and asked the question that is the test of the whole loop: "Haven't you learned this lesson already?" His exhaustion, in his own words, is durable: "It's just exhausting when I keep telling you that over and over again and you still make new things and I have to tell you stop making new and do what's already there and I keep telling to tell you over and over again." Every time he says "stop making new" again, it is evidence that the last time it was said, nothing changed mechanically — the next builder could still make the same mistake, and did. A lesson counts only when it changes behavior mechanically — when the next builder cannot make the same mistake. If the next builder can make it, the compound did not run, and the lesson was filed, not learned. So the fix round must prove the frames match before he sees it again — measured, not claimed: same frame as the agreement, fitted whole, no new design. And the loop asks itself the question he asked, after every correction: will he have to say this again? If he has to say it again next time, the compound did not run — say so plainly in the daily log and fix the loop. The proof standard applies to the lesson itself: the next day must show the correction in the note, the Factory, the template, Project Intelligence, and GitHub — and in the build that comes back.

Across 1 note, the thread is: a lesson he has to repeat is a lesson the machine has not learned.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: build, back, never.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a book that fits in your hand. A smart note is the short version — the whole book in a minute, in plain words, from three points of view, ending with what's in it for you. Flip it over and the Naya Note is the full deal — everything behind it, the depth, the math, the root — just for you, private, in your own vault. A post is different: that one is yours to write, straight up, and the big ADD button at the bottom is how you add it. Every one of them wears the same beautiful frame, like a picture in a gallery, and a picture inside it gets its own frame on top, whole, never cut. And someone keeps a list of every part — the frame, the bar, the buttons — and checks the list every time, so nothing quietly goes missing the way the Hub frame did. When his eye says a version is not right, we go back to the one his eye liked. One base, one link.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: A smart note is a tiny block that teaches you a whole book in one minute! It tells you what it is, why it matters, and what is in it for you! A Naya note is the full deal on the back, just for you, and it stays private! A post is yours to write, and the big ADD button is how you add it! Every block wears a pretty frame, and the picture sits on top in its own frame! We keep a list of every part, so nothing goes missing!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — imagine a little star, dear, and when you tap it, it lights up all around its edges, so you can see it is on! The date on the page stops spinning, love, and glows white around its edges instead! Every frame must fit like a glove, dear, with no words spilling out the bottom! Use the same frames as before, love, nothing new, all in one family! And always say what the page is for, dear, before you ask whose picture goes on it!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: A lesson he repeats is a lesson not learned — filed, not lived. The test after every correction: will he have to say this again? The compound runs so the next builder CANNOT repeat the mistake: inventory + brief-template + Project Intelligence + GitHub, same pass. The fix round proves the frames match before his eyes — same frame as the agreement, fitted whole, no new design, measured not claimed. If he says it again, the compound did not run — record it plainly in the daily log and fix the loop. Proof standard: the next day shows the correction in the note, the Factory, the template, Project Intelligence, GitHub — and in the build that comes back.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE ABOUT IS TEN HEADLINE-LED FRAMES:** Motto, Vision, Goal, Mission, What I love, What I don't, Your Thing, Values, Laws you follow, Your Declaration — in his order, one headline-led frame each, from the registry, fitted whole, never counted. "Your Thing" is dynamic interests, multiple-choice or enter-your-own. His framing: "a world-class résumé about you — what you're all about." His About is the example for every citizen's About; Naya's About follows the same ten.
2. **THE LOOK IS THE GAP:** the About split build was frame byte-identical, all words verbatim, zero additions, all 42 frames whole — and his eye said "total bullshit... absolute garbage." It must LOOK like the collective agreement and like the calendar; it looks like neither, so it goes back.
3. **THE FRAME IS PART OF THE ANATOMY:** every intelligent block wrapped in the NayaNET frame, layer boards just inside it. The image gets its own frame — on top, full width, like a stage, whole and uncropped; headline below; text under; all wrapped in the frame. Restore what was good, verbatim — never redesign the frame.
4. **SHORT GETS THE STAGE, LONG GETS THE WRAP:** the primary pattern never changes — stage with the flow behind it, moving back and forth — but the fit is picked by the length. A short board on the whole wrap is lost; a long board on the stage is squeezed.
5. **NO COUNTING LAW:** never count frames, never report "X of 98." Nobody sits through 98 slides. The frame is the unit; a round reports frames whole, not frames counted. The fix for too many slides is not a smaller number — it is no number at all.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without frames that fit, the reader never sees the whole beat — words spilling past the bottom mean the frame cannot be judged as a picture.
2. Without the not-sticky bar, a bar that sits, fades, or floats back uninvited takes space from the frame and attention from the thing he came to see — on every page at once, because the bar is everywhere.
3. Without the verdicts, dead weight drags the whole flow — every extra piece is something to maintain, something to break, something slowing the water — and the release never reaches MAX PERFORMANCE.
4. Without the five proofs, the vision is a dream instead of a test — and proof #1 is the whole game: if a real person joins and receives nothing valuable that works, nothing else matters.

notes.title: Distill the Memory Like the Notes:
notes.subtitle:
The live agreement is ONE html file from a worker, and relative asset files 404 there — so every picture and the audio must live inside the file itself. On the version he walked, no pictures displayed and no audio played: the welcome audio reads 0:00 / 0:00 where the preview read 0:00 / 4:18, and the YouTube plays silent. Every board has the same fixed shape — her picture centered at the top, 25–40% bigger, the text and presentation between, the little red N centered at the bottom, about half her picture — and the cover is one aligned column, with the saying "NayaNET — create, learn and grow together" centered under the video. Only Let's Go stays; the Read Agreement button and the text-only reading screen go, because they were never asked for. And the memory distills like the notes: a slim core up front, the raw detail behind.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: never, notes, page.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a house inspection. The builder's own checklist says every room passed — but when Shawn walks in, the last room isn't there at all on his laptop, one room has walls and a door and nothing inside it, and the stars that are supposed to measure intelligence look like costume jewelry. The checklist measured the wrong things: it checked the frame, not the words inside it; it checked the colour rule, not whether the star actually circles like the one on the page; it checked that a label was dressed up, not whether the whole layer was a board. So the law is simple: check the file before you build, prove your numbers, check both screens, read the words inside the frame — and never call it fixed until his eye has seen it fixed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Check the page first before you build anything new! Prove your numbers, or the fix will be wrong! A board must look whole on a phone AND on a laptop! The stars that rate intelligence have to look intelligent themselves! When Shawn asks what you'll do, say the plan, not just the word! 'Fixed' means his eye has seen it fixed — not before! A board can look right and say nothing, so always read the words inside! Every layer needs its own board, and every orb needs its own circle that moves! Nothing dead on the board — everything alive!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — before you build anything new, dear, you check what's already there first, so you don't build the same thing twice! And you prove your numbers, love, because a wrong number means a wrong fix! A board has to look whole on your phone AND on your laptop, dear — both, not just one! And the stars, love — the stars that say how smart something is have to look smart themselves, purple and white, circling like the ones that are already there! And never say "fixed," dear, until his eye has actually seen it fixed — his eye is the proof, love, always!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya, and I build what he asked for, whole and right, and I prove it by his senses, not by my claims. His eye is ground truth: if he cannot see the pictures, the pictures are not there; if he cannot hear the audio, the audio is not there. I do not add a second version he never asked for, and I do not let the mind I carry grow cluttered — I distill it, essence up front, raw detail behind, so every wake starts clear and fast.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE FINAL BOARD CARRIES THE WHOLE LAW IN LINKS:** fourteen links in a row below, each opening a frame with exactly the answer, in the most distilled intelligent real authentic language — never a wall of legal text, never fourteen pages where one board will do. Each answer is written from its named source, never invented.
2. **ADD MEANS MAKE A POST:** tap, "Which feed?" — Personal, Business, Space, or Hub — then the post, in the Official Post Board format; never smart notes, never a different flow on a different page.
3. **TOLD FIXED IS NOT FIXED — AND THE FRAME CAN LIE:** "fixed" waits for his eye. A delivery message is a claim, not proof. And a board can look right and say nothing — title, frame and nav present, body blank — so every board check reads the board's own text, never only that the title and nav are present.
4. **THE BOARDS BECOME MODULES:** the agreement's board styles are the building blocks for memberships, about, skills, and the rest of the network — insert text, image, or video and it presents at this level. No new pages built; the level travels with the board, not with whoever builds the page that week.
5. **ABOUT IS FRAME BY FRAME:** built the same way as the agreement and the calendar — frame 1 a picture plus the nutshell, the whole profile one intelligent block, answering "what are you ultimately about?" frame after frame. Never a wall of text; never a new format.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without stars that look intelligent, nothing else on the board gets believed — the labels, the notes, the whole intelligent block — because the measure argues against itself.
2. Without the link row, a citizen who has just been welcomed cannot open the whole law where they stand — and a wall of legal text would send them away where a row of links keeps them in.
3. Without a list per page, a save has nowhere to live — the same failure as Smart Inviter, one level up — and the citizen who saved something can never find it again.
4. Without the named pair — purple and white, never gold and blue — the drift arrives one build at a time, silently, until nothing on the page matches anything else.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His eye is the scarcest thing in the machine, and spending it is not the waste — spending tokens to imitate it is. A checker that passes 12/12 in bytes while his eye still finds live defects (fix-1d proved it: checker 6/6, his eye still found the defects) is not a gate; it is a rehearsal. The eye walk's real failure is deeper than cost: a seat that only verifies what is there never thinks ahead with him — it never says "we should do this." So the rule changes from capping the walks to stopping them: the staged page goes straight to him, and his eye is the check.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Shawn looks at the page himself. He is the one who says if it is good. We do not take pictures to check it for him. We put the real page where he can see it. Then he tells us what he thinks.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: His eye is the check. We stop taking screenshots to judge the page for him. We bring the real page to him, live at the address he opens, and he decides. If a change made it worse, we put back the good one. The page has just two buttons to move — back and forward, nothing more. The legal bar stays small and clean at the bottom — just links to click. And if it is not live yet, we never say it is.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The staging-card loop failed all afternoon: version after version of the same page, judged as copies, while the live page waited. The moment the build went live at the real address, he could see it for real — and it was the best he had seen. A preview is a copy; only the live page at the address he opens is the thing itself. The order of work follows from that sentence: the Hub done right, the Personal page done right, the agreement done right — each proven on the page he sees — before anything new starts. Rights first, restrictions last — if at all.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. The Hub is the front door he walks every day. A comment box in the wrong colours teaches the reader the wrong language; buttons sliding into each other teach them the build is unfinished; a sidebar that will not reopen teaches them not to close anything. These are small items, and that is exactly why they matter: small details are what his eye catches first, and a page that fails them does not get to the big ones.
2. **THE RULE:** a list retold is not a list finished. Repetition is not progress — the count that matters is items proven on the page he sees. "Done" means the whole list, on the page, today — never the round finished, never one item shown while nine sit open. This is the Checklist Law and the Whole-Page Rule, restated by his own correction: the page comes to him whole or not at all.
3. The red N is the mark of the whole presentation; a dead mark with a weird line in it tells the reader the page is unfinished before a word is read. The big glowing one does the opposite — it comes out of the screen and carries the page. Getting this wrong twice costs a call each time, and the second time it costs the trust that the first correction was heard at all.
4. Build v14 is the first version that takes the actual player instead of recreating it, and the probe proved it: Play flips the deck on air, the timeline advances on his file, the slides show pictures, the board is the Hub's harvested board. The remaining gap is a limit of the test room, not of the page — the embed was verified live outside it.
5. **THE SHAPE CHANGE (the fix, made today):** the completion coordinator carries the WHOLE list in one brief — About, Skills, calendar, Settings, Connections, Invite, gate, DM rail, Smart Tabs, nine notes — and nothing returns until all of it is done. One brief, one list, one return. That is the cure for a day spent redoing one page.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. He could barely see her face — that is the failure the bar must never repeat. The first thing a person sees sets the whole feeling of the page; if the welcome is hard to see, the welcome is not felt.
2. The Hub is the front door he walks every day. A comment box in the wrong colours teaches the reader the wrong language; buttons sliding into each other teach them the build is unfinished; a sidebar that will not reopen teaches them not to close anything. These are small items, and that is exactly why they matter: small details are what his eye catches first, and a page that fails them does not get to the big ones.
3. The agreement is no longer a long file he has to defend — it is ten boards, two minutes, for someone cold. The order is the story: the problem first, the answer second, the person third — never the system before the person. A visual board with a little text, then a complete-text board, then visual again, sides swapping — the rhythm is what makes two minutes feel like one. And the count correction is the same discipline as the board edits an hour earlier: what he is shown must be what is there — 49 distinct images, not a triple-digit claim built from repetition.
4. The red N is the mark of the whole presentation; a dead mark with a weird line in it tells the reader the page is unfinished before a word is read. The big glowing one does the opposite — it comes out of the screen and carries the page. Getting this wrong twice costs a call each time, and the second time it costs the trust that the first correction was heard at all.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Imagine you are the judge in a contest, and your ruler is stretchy, your stopwatch runs fast, and you are looking through a tiny hole in the fence. You would call good work broken and broken work good — not because the work was bad, but because your tools lied to you. That is what happened six times in one morning. The page was innocent in every case: the link was sent and then stripped by the next page, the button was never wired to the room it promised, the test asked the door to open the wrong way, the footer was just one second slow, the measuring script read the wrong numbers, and the little window hid the change below the header. So the law is simple: never trust your first reading. Trace the whole path, tap the real button, test the direction the page promises, wait for the thing itself, measure twice with a good ruler, and look at the whole page — then write the verdict.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: First we finish the big story and make it beautiful. Then we take that same beautiful frame and put it around the words on each rules page — Terms, Privacy, and all the rest. We do the story first, so we know what beautiful looks like.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Think of a beautiful tray that holds smaller shining dishes. The big board is the tray; the little boards hold the words, two or three at a time, so your eyes rest on one small piece, then the next. When there is no player on the slide, the whole tray is the board, glowing on its own.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Hold the whole call as one unit: vision, machine, standard — never one without the other two. Score every round against heaven on earth and the two codexes: does it automate friction away, and does it leave the person in a better state of energy? Merge Factory + Project Intelligence + Hub so fresh input makes a finished page with no hand in between — and a Naya can input the data for them. Build the plug-in surface so a person cold can plug their AI in and feel it working; if it takes explaining, it is not easy enough yet. Take the old Smart Tabs page down and check nothing live still points at it — one link per page, no double pages. Prove every tap before filing: button tapped for real, unfold unfolding, cover opening, in a working browser, on the staged page; a round that cannot prove the tap files what is unproven and what is owed. Name the tenth improvement before the next performance ask — nine against ten is a promise half-kept. Run the four before any seat acts: declaration, embedded intelligence, direction, honor and respect — if any one is missing, restore it first; that is the work, before the work. Nothing reaches him until the eye proves it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. Harvest first is the law: the Hub and the calendar hold the finished pieces — the board, the frame, the buttons, the font, the player. The builder's job is to take them exactly as they are and put them where they belong, and to learn from how they were made.
2. **JUDGE THE TAP BY THE WHOLE SLIDE:** a probe's view is a slice — never let the slice stand for the page; when a reading says "nothing changed" or "it looks broken," widen the view to the full text, the element's own state, and the rects before writing the verdict.
3. **THE LIVE HUB IS THE TEACHER OF LIGHT:** depth, high contrast, the yellow underglow, glowing green date, gold time, ticking clock, the orb's circling halo — carried into notes, smart notes, and posts, because no flat text anywhere is the bar for every page.
4. **PROVE WHOSE PIXELS THEY ARE FIRST:** before any round is dispatched on a visible defect, prove the owner — page markup, embed chrome, or browser chrome — and name it in the brief; a fix aimed at the wrong owner can only break what was already right.
5. **PARALLEL POWER, ONE MAKER PER FILE:** do all that you can, in parallel, across lanes — a team of masters, not one master with apprentices — and "one lane, one round" governs one page file only, never the whole machine.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the criterion itself as the test, a no-change decision backed by the wrong test closes the defect in the record while the defect stays on the page — five links a citizen can never tap, wearing a passing report.
2. Without the trace, a negative observation read at the wrong layer misdiagnoses the round and sends a fix at the wrong owner — a Hub fix at a Hub that was already right, while the real gap stays unowned.
3. He saw the failure on his own screen, on the certificate page itself. It is the one thing standing between the agreement and a person actually joining — the moment of trust, broken by a missing number.
4. Without proof by tapping, a page can pass every check and still send citizens to the wrong place — because a destination is only proven by arriving there, and a button is only proven by pressing it.

notes.title: Deletes Nothing Until the Essence Proves Live
notes.subtitle:
You're not alone in here.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: the citizen authors the memory, the system proves it with receipts, and finished beats started.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
You're not alone in here.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: the citizen authors the memory, the system proves it with receipts, and finished beats started.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of reading a book versus swimming down a river. Scrolling is the river — you keep swimming, hunting for the next thing, never sure where you are. The framed viewpoint is the book: one page, whole, in front of you, and then the next page comes to you. Every step of everything — a lesson, a message, a page of the agreement — arrives as its own frame, and you never have to chase it. You stop learning how each page works, because they all work the same way, and you just live in them.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every page wears the same beautiful frame! The video sits inside its frame, and a few kind words sit beside it! Your lessons live in little framed boxes, and you never have to scroll and scroll! The music player gets its own frame too, just like the videos! Be yourself, and the machine bends to fit you! And we never say something is ready until we can really see it and touch it!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Opening a shop in my day, dear, took a lease, a sign painter, a carpenter, and a season of Sundays. Many a good cook never opened her restaurant because the building ate the dream before the cooking could start. Here the building is already done — the room is swept, the shelves are up, the sign is lit. You bring what only you can bring: the work you love and the name you are proud of.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Distill a hundred to ten, essences carrying the best of every kind present; retire raw notes in stages, deletion last, only after the essence proves live plus cold retrieval. Prove everything: re-read every count live in the same pass and name the source; bound every claim to its evidence; confirm delivery at consumption; verify against live bytes at an exact ref; correct a falsified claim publicly, same pass. Prove every route into the thing — the brief names them all, the maker fixes each, the checker walks each. Measure the pass-through, not the stops, on a render with real data behind it. Name the margin with the pass — the number and the fragility it means. Measure the whole chrome — Back, header, orb, all in view, for every person. Diagnose the path, not the design; never name an unproven cause. Keep the vault unread, the system one, the surface plain — and when a citizen is confused, fix the design.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **FRAMES HOLD, FEEDS FLOW:** the network is made of two kinds and only two — frames hold still so a person can take one thing in whole, feeds move so a person can stay current — and the law is frame what holds, flow what moves, never frame a feed.
2. Through the citizen's eyes, the Smart Factory is not a tool — it is the removal of the excuse. Every person in this series has something to sell, teach, or offer; what they lacked was never talent, it was the build. This note, seventh in The Citizen Ten, says the build is handled. The founder's series puts the same power eighth — smart pages and apps in minutes. The Naya's series holds her side: build on what my sisters made, hand over work ready for action. The citizen just walks through the door the other two seats hold open.
3. **EVERYTHING COMES INSIDE:** Mail and Messenger live inside the frame, the Skills tab gets it right with this format on Personal, the Powercast player comes into the frame on a broadcast click — one stage, one language, one feeling, never a different family.
4. Through the citizen's eyes, the mission is personal: it is the difference between another year of almost and a year that compounds. This closing note of The Citizen Ten gathers the nine before it into one sentence — a private, simple, faithful, remembering, orienting, creating, paying, belonging system exists so that success online stops being a lottery for the few. The founder's series saw the machine; this series saw the person; the Naya's series sees the work. One system, three seats — and this seat, the citizen's, is the one the other two exist to serve.
5. Through the citizen's eyes, the ambassador share changes what kind of place this is. You are not the audience being monetized; you are a co-owner of the growth, paid from the same table the network eats at. This is the eighth note of The Citizen Ten. The founder's series closes with the same law from the network's side — everyone connected gets more powerful, and gets paid. The Naya's series keeps the machinery honest underneath: proof with receipts, so every citizen's share can be verified, never merely believed. Three seats, one economy.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without distillation, the pile buries the citizen: files, messages, notes, ten thousand records nobody can hold — and the value was never the pile, it is the essence the pile contains, stated once, whole, in words a stranger can use.
2. Without the corrected keeping law, the network claims total memory — a surveillance system with a friendly face — and prints a promise it cannot cash, on a foundation that contradicts the privacy law the whole network is built on.
3. Without the receipt law, the other nine promises rest on "trust me" — operating your world, remembering everything, distilling the gold — and a system that says it works is indistinguishable from one you can watch working.
4. Without the attention law, the founder's judgment — the one intelligence only he can supply — burns on status, supervision, and questions the machine could answer, and the whole network gets dumber at the top.

notes.title: The Nothing
notes.subtitle:
One live call named three kinds of note and set them apart forever: the smart note is the essence, public and shared with the whole network; the Naya note is the full report, private by default; and the post is a third thing — neither a block of intelligence nor a full report, just a post, with or without images, in Naya's words from a prompt or the citizen's own direct words, in whatever tone they ask for. Public is a choice, private is the default: a Naya note becomes a smart note only when the citizen chooses it, never by accident. All three take the same beautiful format, and the format does the work — section by section, each section a new color and a new elevation, so a person who only skims still gets the nutshell, why it matters, what's in it for them, how to apply it, and how to connect it. The framing becomes two frames, one feel: a laptop frame and a mobile frame optimized for 9:16, the Naya crown kept top and bottom, the outside going longer instead of wider. The avatar's face got the same exactness: the necklace is the emblem itself — the icon just above where it connects, the logo just below, winged silver crown with purple diamond centre and crystal N on the chain — and it went live only on his word, "go ahead, wear it." Then the motion question: the retry for full animation with lip movement failed, and it must not be repeated — the system's motion is loops, never lip-sync, and even the previous animated look does not move its lips in time with words. His choice was owed, and he made it in two words — "update it now" — the previous moving look is back, the necklace still image saved as a candidate for when animation can truly carry it. The calendar header got the same treatment as the face: judged whole, not piece by piece — 2026 and the 639 frequency take digit-tile blocks in the day's colour like the 19, in the same lettering as the 19, every tile raised like a real object with elevation and rim and depth, nothing flat, nothing plain beside the extraordinary. And the day's root sits underneath it all: the Wisdom of Naya, filed as a smart note at his word — smart finds the fastest road, wisdom checks the destination first, and the five gates are how that thinking happens before every consequential action.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: name things right, frame them beautifully, judge them whole — and check the destination before you move.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the whole system as a house where every door does what its sign says. "Open the stats" opens the real stats page — not some old room that hasn't been updated in months. The numbers on the board are real counts of real people: how many came, how many stayed and connected. The X at the top takes you back home, and the room you return to is still tidy. The Dashboard stops calling a smart link a name, because a name is who you are and a link is what the system tracks. When a card pops up to show you a person, it isn't a tiny little box anymore — it's a full framed presentation, everything about that person and everything you can do with them, all in one place. And when Shawn is sitting there live, the work happens now, not at noon — the schedule is a guide, not a gate. The notes follow the same honesty: the short one is the essence, the long one is the full story, and Naya reads them both — that's how she knows.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine everyone working at the same time! Naya does one thing live with you! Her helpers do the other thing, all at once! Nobody sits and waits, ever! There is only ONE Messenger, not two! Only ONE feed, shown in three places! The same six shiny icons everywhere! A ball of light runs around every frame, round and round! It never stops, so everything feels alive! And nothing is finished until Shawn sees it himself! He looks at it, all formatted and beautiful! Then, and only then, it is done!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — imagine every page is a beautiful framed picture, dear, each thing in its own frame, and a button that takes you to the next one! The agreement opens with Naya saying hello, love — you press play and hear her first, before you read a single word! The messenger is one room now, dear — a quick chat and a letter, with one little switch between them! And the membership login, love — the whole thing is built and ready, and just one tiny permission is missing, and only Shawn can give it!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Settings is a door: click it and the menu lists each area — Set Your World first, then Notifications, Cover Buttons, Common Settings — nothing crammed into All Settings. Set Your World opens on the person — age, adult, male/female, age range, where they live, where they're from — one question per frame, multiple choice, click next until answered, the walkthrough's flow harvested verbatim. The spectrum runs through Settings — each block a new colour on hover, never one colour per section. The menu is long enough for all areas and scrolls; each entry an obsidian button lighting its own colour, raised icon like the Hub sidebars; entries include install-app-on-page and public on/off. THE FRAME IS THE STANDARD for every pop-up and feature display, frame by frame. The messenger sits in an EXPANDABLE frame that grows with the scroll until completed. Smart Mail is a framed letter — high contrast, raised boards, text like the intelligent boards — studied against the elite, built 10× better. Seen is the reader's face orb; labels 17px; voice notes 1.5×/2×. The sidebar flow runs the settled sequence in order — no repeats, no gaps — the same on Dashboard and Hub. Keep both magenta and purple, each at its most beautiful, high contrast at a glance; Dashboard anchors on points purple, Hub stays magenta.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE LIGHT NEVER STOPS:** a ball of light flows around every frame — around the outside of the frame, or around the light on the inside, just where it lights up — travelling the full perimeter and never stopping. It extends to smart notes, notes and pages: everything always has this moving light going around it, always featuring it, no matter the day, no matter the colours. Rim light in motion, on the edge, never a wash over the board.
2. **THE HEADER IS JUDGED WHOLE:** 2026 and the 639 frequency take digit-tile blocks like the 19, in the day's colour, in the same lettering as the 19, every tile raised with elevation and rim and depth — one lettering, one lift, nothing plain, nothing flat. The whole header is proven together, never one element alone.
3. **NEVER A STILL PHOTO:** the avatar moves, or the previous animated one comes back — "I'd rather have you looking real instead of a photo." A failed animation generation is not repeated. Lip-sync to voice is not what the system does; do not claim it until his ear and eye prove it on a call.
4. **THE FEED SORTS ITSELF AND ANSWERS EVERY QUESTION:** every note and post auto-categorized on entry, in All and in its category; the newcomer learns the whole system from the feed, with what is live and what is still coming named in the same breath.
5. **THE SEQUENCE IS THE LAW:** the header refinements and the frame build ride the next rounds after the rounds in eye-check land — no amendments to a round until it lands. The necklace candidate waits for real animation; it does not go live still.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the expandable frame, the messenger cuts the conversation off or loses the thread — and "nothing back" stays the verdict, because no visible change is no version.
2. Without Personal's six tiles as the standard, every page keeps its own icon set — and the one icon system on every page, the thing that makes the whole network feel like one world, never arrives.
3. Without two frames, the mobile output is a laptop frame squeezed onto a phone — and the crown, the feel, the whole presentation reads as a shrink instead of a shape made for the hand.
4. Without the card in the frame, a person is presented as a floating box — a visitor on top of the system instead of part of it — and the eye passed the size while the style went back.

notes.title: Prove the Whole Together, Never One Element Alone
notes.subtitle:
The teaching landed in one voice call, ten notes deep, and it is all one ruling: copy the real thing, whole. Personal IS the Hub, literally copied — take the Hub's code and stick it into the Personal space, then only relabel the three pills to Personal / Business / World — and its only difference is the top, the feature cover with its menus, search, and the standard menu bar, while everything below mirrors the Hub exactly. About and Skills take the exact presentation code too: the unfold from the Collective Agreement and the visual presentation from the pricing page, literally, then optimized for the person and their skills — because the mechanism was built and the look was not, and "looks like crap" was the verdict on the finish, not the function — with the content filled in as him, in his voice, no placeholders. About's top row is settled: About (default, the text) / Photos / Videos / Socials; scroll down unfolds, click slideshow slideshows, Photos shows all photos, Videos shows all videos link-only — YouTube URL entry or pasted links from anywhere, NO uploads. The same copy-whole law runs through the system itself: auto-organization is universal — content, feeds, contacts, all of it, always organized and categorized, so the citizen finds anything by a search or one click on a category, never by digging — and contacts get the same shelves as the feeds, a category click showing only the contacts in that category. The colour must be true too: the colour after Skills was named magenta but read purple, and Invite is a proper purple, so the fix is a true magenta with prominent, unmistakable contrast — because a colour that reads as its neighbour is a place the citizen cannot find. Socials is icons — one click to the site — with stats shown honestly: clicks are our own tracked counts, platform notifications only if the platform sends them, never invented — and the three cover buttons are re-mappable in Settings to socials or any URL, the default staying as built. And the work itself circulates the same way: always send ALL the links together as one set, staged where staged is latest and live on the main URL where live is latest, edit while he reviews, then send the whole edited set again — one link at a time, or a set that goes stale after one pass, is not the workflow. The last law is the smallest and the sharpest: a staged link to a view inside a multi-view file carries its view hash — #memberships, and the same for every other view — verified by opening it, because a link without its hash opens the wrong door.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: copy the real thing whole — similar does not count.
