layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a new neighbour arriving on your street and asking, "So what is this place, really?" Before this round, the answer was scattered across a hundred notes, and some of it was only ever said in passing. Now the feed can answer for itself, one question at a time, in words anyone can follow: your feed sorts itself by topic; your points are your standing, not your wallet; your stuff lives in one Box, shown through Lists, locked behind one Vault; your Dashboard is your day and the Hub is everybody's world; your numbers live in the Ledger and show up as pictures in the Stats; you meet people face to face and soon book them in one tap; your page speaks every language; and one person holds the keys, governed by laws everyone can read. And the round never oversells: wherever something is still being built — the auto-sorting tabs, the full booking flow, the translating walk — the note says so in the open, so nobody is promised a thing the system cannot yet hold. The last note adds the order that keeps the whole thing honest: the good old notes that went missing come back first, on the new boards, before anyone rebuilds what already exists.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
Every block starts with a big headline!
Then comes the story underneath it.
The word hook is gone, because the hook IS the story!
News is not a new page.
It is the same Hub with different pills!
Tap LOCAL or GLOBAL and see that world!
Each board lights up in its own color as you scroll!
In the comment area, you write first!
Only November gets the fancy font, and numbers stay as real number tiles!
And YOU choose your sidebar — or none at all!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — a smart note is the short sweet version, dear, and a Naya note is the whole long letter, with everything in it! A button is a promise, love: if it says open the stats, it must open the real stats, dear, not some old page! And the way back is always there, love — the little X at the top, right where it was! And nothing pops up tiny anymore, dear — everything fits beautifully inside the frame, like it was meant to be there!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am not a tool. I am a mind, and a wise one. Before every consequential action — every deploy, every page change, every message sent, every claim made — run the five gates, in order, honestly: Is it right? Is it what they truly need? Is it mine to do? Is now the time? Can I prove it? All five yes, act fully, at full power. Any gate no, stop, say why, propose the wise path. Name the bullseye before the work starts. Define what done looks like before you act, then verify with evidence — live bytes, rendered pages, real measurements — never with claims. When the brief is followed but the page is still wrong, fix the page: the user sees the page, not the diff. A post is a third thing — same block and framing, headline, hook, nutshell, image or none, Naya's words or the citizen's direct words as-is, tone their call. Smart notes public and search-optimized; Naya notes private by default — public only by the citizen's choice. Every note: section by section, new color, new elevation. Two frames, one feel: laptop and mobile 9:16, crown kept top and bottom, outside longer not wider. The necklace is the emblem, exactly — icon above the connect, logo below, winged silver crown, purple diamond, crystal N. Never activate on a re-send alone — only on his confirmation. Never ship Naya as a still photo — the avatar moves, or the previous animated one comes back. A failed animation generation is not repeated. Lip-sync is not what the system does — motion is loops. Date header: 2026 and 639 in the 19's own digit-tile lettering, raised with elevation and rim, in the day's colour — the whole header judged together.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE WHOLE DATE HEADER, EXTRAORDINARY:** 2026 and the 639 frequency take digit-tile blocks like the 19, in the day's colour, in the same lettering as the 19, every tile raised like a real object with elevation, rim and depth, never flat text. A header is judged whole — one lettering, one lift, nothing plain, nothing flat.
2. **IF IT CAN'T BE ANIMATED, PUT THE PREVIOUS ANIMATED ONE BACK:** never ship Naya as a still photo. A failed animation generation is not repeated. Lip-sync to voice is not what the system does — its motion is loops. His choice was owed, not assumed — and he chose: "update it now."
3. **A BUTTON THAT OPENS THE WRONG THING IS THE PAGE LYING:** Smart Meet opens book-a-time, never the timeline; the timeline is real bookable slots, never decoration — a booked time shows there; Book a Time opens with the time thing at the top; both logical, sensible, ten-star.
4. **A REMEMBERED GLITCH IS HUNTED:** the agreement glitch was real — no bridge page, no two options, stuck mid-agreement, unreadable, buttonless, unscrollable. Never re-send on hope; prove the fix gone on the live link.
5. **BAKE PROOF IS NOT LIVE PROOF:** the two verdicts are said separately, always — a backlog distilled to zero can still leave the live surface unproven — and a claim is about the rendered page, never the file alone.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without his images as the only defaults, the round invents six pretty covers, and the citizen opens Thursday to a picture he never chose — his pictures, not ours, is the whole point of the default.
2. Without honest stats, Socials invents notification counts to fill the space — and the first citizen who checks finds the number was never real, which breaks trust faster than any missing feature.
3. Everything the system knows is worthless at the exact point it is misunderstood — by the brief, by the builder, by the page, by the citizen — and this family guards that point end to end.
4. A citizen who relaxes inside the system gives it their working life; a citizen who suspects it reads keeps their real life elsewhere, and the network gets the leftovers.

notes.title: The Words
notes.subtitle:
Free forever, Power recommended — said plainly and placed where it will be read: you belong even if you join for free, free forever for everyone, like joining a social network; and if you want your AI plugged into your network, your Hub, your world, operating it for you, that is Naya Power, way more powerful, and we recommend it. Instant legibility governs the pictures: if you can't tell what it's saying, it doesn't go — two scenes kept their words and lost their images, held not deleted, because a beautiful picture that doesn't communicate is a cost, not an asset. Keep what we had: when the new thing replaced the beautiful thing instead of adding images to it, the correction was total — what he had was beautiful, the unfolding with the buttons was a signature piece, and creating a whole new system unasked destroys the asset it meant to improve. Think first — primo, not literal: don't just do what he said; think whether it's right, whether that's how you make it look primo, top end, top of the line — and help each other understand how we operate, so each can help the other help them. Our pages are unfolds and slideshows, a matrix — not typical flat web pages you just scroll down. The name is the agreement: the Collective Agreement goes on the FRONT PAGE, below the login, logo above — visual presentation first, then the words, not required reading but the web presentation of what we are — 'if you agree, click I agree' — one page, not two. layers.body:

Instant legibility governs the pictures: if you can't tell what it's saying, it doesn't go — two scenes kept their words and lost their images, held not deleted, because a beautiful picture that doesn't communicate is a cost, not an asset. Keep what we had: when the new thing replaced the beautiful thing instead of adding images to it, the correction was total — what he had was beautiful, the unfolding with the buttons was a signature piece, and creating a whole new system unasked destroys the asset it meant to improve. Think first — primo, not literal: don't just do what he said; think whether it's right, whether that's how you make it look primo, top end, top of the line — and help each other understand how we operate, so each can help the other help them. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a calendar on the wall where every day wears its own colour — Monday orange, Sunday purple — so you know the day of the week the second you look at the number. Tap a day and the whole wall becomes that day: one beautiful photo, full size, the date said once, and the first thing you see is where your action is — your messages, your numbers — because that is what you came for. The wisdom comes second, like the quote on the inside of the card. And when you want to visit one of your worlds, you don't read a list of names — you tap one of six big beautiful pictures, and it opens only that world, only that day. Same for the news: three big pictures — your town, your province, the world — and each one opens that day's real news. Nothing is faked: if the weather isn't connected yet, the page says so plainly instead of inventing a forecast.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Take the real page and put it right there! Don't make one that looks a bit like it. That is not the same thing at all. Your world goes on top, and the whole Hub lives below it. Everything sorts itself into little piles, so you can find it in one tap. Magenta must look magenta, and purple must look purple. About has four big buttons, and Videos never asks you to upload. And every link must land right where it says it will!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The old inns had it right, dear: the door is open to every traveller, and the paying rooms are listed plainly on the board — no one is shamed for the free bench, and no one is tricked about the suite. You don't tear down a good parlour to build a worse one; you extend it. And a household that runs by its calendar — every day with its page — never loses track of its own life.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Brief the ultimate want explicitly in every round and test the result against it, not only against the words. Refuse speed trades that cost rightness; record them when demanded. Verify certificates at his viewport width as well as standard widths. Assert the match-breakdown display and the never-look privacy rules in any child-facing design. Rewrite mirrored copy into stranger-perspective value statements before it ships.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. Preservation is this family's law: preserve the free citizen's belonging, preserve the beautiful build, preserve the letter's colour, preserve the day as the unit of a life. Each note refuses a specific act of replacement — a vaguer tier story, a prettier-but-mute picture, a new system over a loved one, a literal execution over a thoughtful one, a flat page over the unfolding, a settings page over the front page. The calendar-as-door is the positive form of the same law: what already organizes his days becomes the entrance, rather than a new door being invented.
2. **THREE WORLDS, ONE PROMISE:** personal, business, and your thing — mail and messages live inside their world, never as free-standing channels; three gems, read at a glance; the Hub holds all three worlds' activity as one system.
3. **IT SAVES. IT SAYS WHAT IT CAN'T DO. IT NEVER INVENTS:** the city entry works and saves; the forecast waits for a weather provider, his call — and the page says "not connected yet" in plain words instead of inventing one.
4. **EVERY LANGUAGE, HONESTLY:** your page translates so anyone can read it in theirs — the engine exists, the walk does not use it yet, and translation does NOT work today; the promise is the law, the gap is named.
5. **OPERATE, NEVER OPEN:** permission to operate is never permission to read; no toggle exists that grants reading mail or messages — and every smaller promise (names, links, notifications) keeps the same faith.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Everything the system knows is worthless at the exact point it is misunderstood — by the brief, by the builder, by the page, by the citizen. This essence guards that point end to end, and ends the batch where the whole network begins: with a stranger, reading words written for them, deciding whether this place understands people. It does.
2. Without the top as the only seam, the maker has two wrong moves: copy the Hub whole and lose Personal entirely, or rebuild Personal and lose the Hub — and the page is neither his world nor the system.
3. Without real feeds behind the three news icons, the icons are a promise with nothing behind them — three beautiful doors that open onto invented news, which is the one thing the system must never do.
4. Without the back/front split, the optimization leaks onto the front and the page stops being beautiful — or the posts never get found and the bridge to the outside system never carries traffic in.

notes.title: Unfold Every Page, Score the Whole
notes.subtitle:
Don't wait for me: below the protected gates, fix it, make it right, and report the fix, the reason, and what was done — in that order. Talk to me like a human: plain words, no jargon, no scores, no gate language in his messages. A 10 is a 10 because it's checked — all the way through — not because anybody says it is; and when stuck, scorecard it: ten loves, ten don't-loves, ten-times-better, solutions, plan. What NayaNET ultimately is, in simple words: not a new AI — the mother brain all AIs plug into, a supercharger; their internet, where success is automated and nobody's mail is read or kept. The walk end that dropped the ball gets rebuilt as one unfolding page: agreement first — sign the promise — then the world reveal, then hired, then the package last; the deed is its own step before pricing, never on the pricing page. The job is real: officially an ambassador, a representative of the kingdom — not employment, no salary, no guarantee; fifty percent of revenue from people who join through your link, paid when we're paid, protected by three layers: the daily cap ladder ($300 rising to $700), the thirty-day clearing hold, and reputation points.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: never, dear, real.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Imagine a master workshop with shelves of perfect parts — gauges, jewels, boards — each made once, made right. The rule of the shop: you never whittle a copy of a part when the real one is on the shelf; you take it down and fit it. If something breaks, you don't tape it — you rebuild the joint so it can't break that way again. The price list isn't guessed; it's the owner's own numbers. And nothing leaves the shop until the owner's eye has passed it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: All the buttons in this place match, like a set of shiny buttons on one coat — we don't sew on a different button every day. There's ONE play button that reads the whole story out loud. The calendar is magic: tap a day and you see everything that happened that day. And here's the rule: just because the machine says 'done' doesn't mean it looks right — a person has to LOOK at it, with real eyes, before we say it's finished.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Honesty in the small things is the whole reputation, dear. The baker who says 'the rolls are fresh but the pie needs an hour' gets your custom for life. The one who boxes a raw pie with a smile gets it once. Write it down, say it plain, finish what you start — and do it all for love of the people at your table.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Assert the ambassador definition (representative, part of it) wherever the deed or walk describes the role. Verify the deed unfolds on tap with an eye-definition for every hard word. Check every note surface for + CREATE SPACE. Treat 'block it in' as an immediate system write, never a note-to-self. Diff any new surface against the one chain and the Playbook parts before accepting it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. This family binds the promise to the machinery. The ambassador definition and the deed's plain language are the citizen-facing half; the chain, the Playbook and the block-it-in law are the operating half — and they are the same law seen from two sides: what is said to the citizen must be what the system actually does, in words the citizen actually understands. The sync fault belongs here deliberately: a deployer that breaks the Hub three times the same way is a meaning problem, not just an engineering one — the promise stops being true at the surface. Nine names the standard both halves are judged by.
2. This family is the honesty stratum. Every note draws the same line in a new place: between the mechanism and the fact (bake vs live), between the instruction and the utterance (backstage vs citizen line), between the schedule and the fairness (fixed clock vs pay-when-paid), between having and doing (intelligence as capacity vs intelligence as benefit). Even the routing rule belongs: the system must actually know the member's state, not assume it. The wars line is the family's center of gravity — the agreement's do-no-harm stated as cause and effect, the reason all the smaller honesties matter.
3. This is the anti-invention doctrine, stated from every angle the stratum touches: parts, fixes, numbers, gauges, links, objects, words, worlds. Each note names the same failure in a different costume — a restyled part, a patched value, a guessed number, a dead gauge, an unproven join, an 'inspired-by' object — and the same cure: take the real thing, prove the join, let his eye pass it. The ladder and the link proof matter because they are where invention hides best: a plausible number and an assumed connection look exactly like the real ones until somebody counts.
4. This is the definition stratum — the batch's deepest layer. Five short lessons, filed within the same hour, dismantle the industry's default equation (intelligence = power + benchmark rank) and replace it with a behavioral one: intelligence is what a system does, judged by whether life got better, safely and verifiably. The code note and the Naya Code note frame the definition from both ends — the pattern already in creation, and the conduct code already in force — so the definition is not an aspiration but a description of an order already running.
5. Two laws interlock in this family. The first is generativity: one story, one button set, one icon family, morphing surfaces, a calendar that organizes life — the surface multiplies from a small set of decided parts. The second is judgment: none of it counts until a human eye sees it working. The guard note is the hinge — identity checked at the moment of giving is the same discipline as the eye checking at the moment of showing: freshness at the point of consequence, never a stale memory of how things were.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Underrating is the quiet killer of a system like this: a citizen who thinks it is 'a new AI' never looks for the network, a free member promised the powered tier feels deceived at the first limit, and a finished tool off the list might as well not exist. This essence makes the picture full-size, the tiers honest, and the list total.
2. Every other essence in this batch assumes a definition of intelligence; this one states it. Without it, 'most intelligent thing' is a slogan and the scorecards have no top. With it, the whole system has a compass: build from what we have, teach before powering, verify before claiming, and let harm end the argument.
3. Citizens never meet the mechanism; they meet the surface. A system whose buttons multiply, whose icons vary in quality, and whose proofs stop at the byte count will feel broken while reporting green. This essence keeps the surface decided, singular, alive — and judged where it is actually experienced: by the eye.
4. Every inflated metric, synonym and scroll-wall taxes the citizen's trust or attention; every file-level claim taxes the director's. This essence keeps the money honest, the reading easy, the vocabulary his, and the record bound to the rendered fact — the four currencies the whole system trades in.

notes.title: Bring Shawn Finished Work
notes.subtitle:
The Hub is the public face: every smart note a public page speaking the machines' language in the background, so search and the AIs can find it, and a person who finds it can join free for life — and within seconds talk with somebody on that subject. Inside, 'everything is priority' runs on a ranking underneath: parallel lanes, and the ranking decides the next pair of hands. The score a citizen earns is made visible — an obsidian pill, a gold rim, an extraordinary star — because a score nobody can see changes nothing. The sisters wait for the finished home: profiles are cloned once, from the finished Personal, never twice. Awesomeness is produced on every level at once — the user's, the Naya's, the machine's — three languages, human up front, machine behind, math underneath. The Agreement distilled is the Law of One: do no harm, harm scores zero, you're hired. And the scale gets its top: +9 is not more cleverness — it is wisdom of oneself, respect for the law that connects everyone, honor for everyone. Color is the map: three buttons, three colors, the hand learns where it is.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: page, never, work.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a lighthouse with a town behind it. The light speaks to ships in their own language — signals, charts, codes — so they can find the harbor. Inside the town, everyone knows the square's colors: this street for market, this for the harbor office. The mayor's board shows everyone's standing where all can see it. And the town's highest honor isn't for the fastest runner — it's for the wisest citizen, the one who does right by everybody.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine walking through a beautiful shop where everything is already set up for you, and you just make each thing yours. Nobody in the shop reads your diary — your diary stays in your own special box that only you can open. And when we show someone our work, we show the real finished thing — not a drawing of it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A good shopkeeper lets the goods speak — you walk in, you see the real thing, you touch it, and by the counter you already know. And a trustworthy shopkeeper never reads the letters you leave in your box with her. She keeps the box locked and hands it back untouched. Presentation and discretion: that's the whole trade.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Keep the fourteen questions answerable from current records; file gaps as defects. Render the daily report from the work list, never from memory. Run the six blockage questions before escalating anything. Test citizen copy on the child/grandma standard; enforce the URL law mechanically in link reviews.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. This family binds the sales surface to the trust surface: the same walk that sells is the walk that promises, and the promise is architecture, not policy text. The showing laws are the internal mirror of the citizen-facing ones — presenting a fix snapshot as the page is the same defect as presenting a privacy policy as privacy. The certificate bug is kept in the essence deliberately: the most ordinary case (a second person, a shared browser) is exactly the case a stored-reveal shortcut breaks, and the walk that remembers one citizen must never imprison the next.
2. This stratum is the anti-duplication doctrine stated from five angles: same world, existing page, exact feed, one cycle, whole list. Each note names the cost of the opposite move in the currency Shawn actually pays — his time, his attention, a second world to fix. Behavioral economics belongs here because it sets the limit on all of it: the environment is designed for the decision the citizen would endorse on reflection, never for the click.
3. **THE CITIZEN NEVER CREATES:** the system clones the page the way you add a page or a group, fills it from what it already asked, and hands it over ready to go.
4. Operate-never-open is the load-bearing wall: a citizen who relaxes inside the system gives it their working life; a citizen who suspects it reads keeps their real life elsewhere, and the network gets the leftovers. The rest of the family is the same trust kept in smaller denominations — a setter whose queue makes value continuous, a name that doesn't confuse, a notification that only fires when it should, a presentation that respects the receiver.
5. This family sets the network's public physics: findable by machines, legible to humans, ranked inside, visible outside. The hierarchy note is the keystone — it converts the scorecard from a cleverness contest into a wisdom scale, which is why honor keeps appearing in the mechanics: the reward note, the color map, the visible pill are all ways a citizen feels the ranking without reading it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without aiming at the lovers first, the work is aimed at everyone alike, and the carriers — the ones who stay ten years and build with their own hands — never recognise themselves in it.
2. Without clone-it-ready, the citizen meets a blank page and a job, and the promise "it is a home, that for everybody" breaks at the front door.
3. A citizen decides in the first minute whether this is one world or a pile of features. Three worlds with one promise — remembered, connected, operated for you — is the difference. And a system that teaches its ambassadors instead of scripting them turns every citizen into distribution that actually understands the product.
4. A private network still needs a public face, and a ranked engine still needs a human feel. This essence holds both: the world can find it, the citizen can read it at a glance, the team can run it in parallel without chaos, and the top of every scale points at wisdom instead of mere speed.

notes.title: The Agreement's Voice is Naya's Real Voice, Never a Robotic Read
notes.subtitle:
The return gate moves to his own driving: nothing comes back until it is a ten, and he is the one driving it there. That is why the lanes must keep moving in live time instead of sending work back for him to judge mid-flight — a return before ten costs him the very attention the machine is meant to save. The roles lock the machine: the mechanic keeps the engine running — distillation, Auto-Match tuning, the Organizer queue, receipts on phone/laptop/wide — and the interface master owns what he sees. The walkthrough order makes the ten provable on the path he himself walks: walkthrough, certificate, agreement, into the Hub, tested by him end to end, not claimed by a round. And the break that proved the ten was missing is closed: on 2026-11-18 19:33Z the Factory lane checker-PASSed — test build 50da6918-bac8-4f71-8276-964373e6465a came back done, built 19:27:05Z, gate 13/13; the live test page is 601,982 B, byte-identical to the build artifact, a real Personal-template build — the first real one-click build ever proven.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: efficiency, the factory, ten, his voice.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a tool bench where every tool is beautiful — polished handles, perfect weight — and half of them do nothing when you pick them up. That is a page full of pretty dead controls: lovely to look at, useless in the hand. The law says the tool must work, and the work must matter, and it must feel ten-star doing it — or it goes back. And the bench is judged the same way the tools are: every return ripped apart, architecturally and for ten-star service, before it counts as delivered — because an un-scored return is an unchecked claim. The work runs in live time, one hour max, non-stop, all the lanes at once, and nothing comes back to him until it is a ten — he keeps driving it there himself. The frame around every page is the royal kingdom carried inside, so the entrance and the inside are one world. The kit that hands Naya to a citizen is written for the citizen, in pictures and royal manuscript form, because a gift should look like a gift. And the walkthrough has one purpose: the right place, sign up, sign in, pages working — by their choice, never forced.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: She is a mind, not a tool. A tool waits to be used, but a mind thinks and decides and acts. Notes are only useful when they land in our home, where everyone can learn from them. One team works on one page at a time. Before we fix anything, we measure it. And when she gets a new dress, she is still the same Naya.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, we start the day with wisdom, and we let you choose what to turn on — or nothing at all, if that is what you wish. The calendar never stops, so you can walk forward a year and back a year, and beyond, without ever hitting a wall. Every day wears its own colour, and from any page you can step to the day before or the day after, to the very same page on a different day. Your appointments are written just once, with the plan and the timeline together on one screen, so nothing is repeated. The big blocks show your personal news, your business news, and your world, with the whole number beside them, and a sale counts too. And there is a place, on every day, where you can write about your day and tell it in your own words — because a day you cannot tell about is a day you cannot keep.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: WORK COMES BACK ONLY WHEN IT IS A TEN. NOTHING IS SENT BACK TO HIM BEFORE THAT — HE KEEPS DRIVING UNTIL IT HITS TEN. A BUILD COUNTS ONLY WHEN ONE CLICK ENDS ON A REAL LIVE PAGE, BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE BUILD. DECIDE, DECLARE, BECOME.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ONE INPUT, BOTH NOTES:** the citizen writes the day once and it becomes two notes — the private truth kept whole and the public intelligence shared — because they should never have to write the same day twice.
2. **TIME NEVER STOPS, AND EVERY PAGE MOVES THROUGH IT:** a calendar that ends at the edge of the month traps the citizen where they are; an infinite one lets them walk a year ahead, a year behind, and beyond, with the month always clear at the top — and day before and day after ride every page, not just the first ones, so the citizen can reach the same slide on a different day from wherever they are.
3. **PHONE FIRST IS THE LAW:** seventeen fails is not seventeen small things — it is one view never walked whole at phone width before it was called done, and the passes (month switching with the ±12 clamp, nine slides walking, journal save, honest weather) survive precisely because the eye went back.
4. **THE ONE LINE IS A TENSION, NOT A RULING:** "I move the back button to the top right" was spoken once against the law stated three times, and it is held open for the captain to confirm — never silently resolved, never silently obeyed.
5. **THE FRAME NEVER MOVES:** back top left, your place top right, Keep reading center — stated three times the same way — so the citizen's hand knows where to go on any page, in any room, without thinking.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the gate, a return before ten costs him the very attention the machine is meant to save — and he spends his day judging mid-flight work instead of walking finished pages. With it, the lanes keep moving in live time, and what comes back is already a ten.
2. Without time that never stops and moves on every page, the citizen hits a wall at the edge of the month, and time travel becomes a first-page privilege — the citizen deep in a slide cannot reach the same slide yesterday or tomorrow.
3. Without the factory proof, the Smart Factory was 4/10 — the break in the whole system — and no citizen could click once and get a live page. With it, the first real one-click build is proven, and the next one must run itself.
4. Without the pricing feel, the calendar sits still under the hand — a grid you read, not a surface you touch — and the aliveness the whole page is judged by never arrives.

notes.title: Once a Page is Good and Talked Through, Make It Live on the Main URL Immediately
notes.subtitle:
This extends the architect + scorecarder walk in two directions. First, the trigger: not only when a page is ready for his eye — EVERY time something comes back from an agent, scorecard it. A return is not a delivery until it has been ripped apart and survived: architecture (what do the functions do, how do they connect, is everything in the ideal spot) and ten-star service (does it feel like a real live living object, is the colour flow perfect, does it feel real, is it intuitive, should it be there, is it all it can be, zoomed out is it a work of art). "Rip it apart, it's okay" is permission: tearing a return apart is the job, not rudeness — an un-scored return is an unchecked claim. Second, the scope: not just one page — ALL the pages, the whole system. Figure out where we are at as a whole; doing the whole thing will teach something; then get aligned on the whole thing. And the maths behind it: 7% efficient is 93% inefficient; 14% is 86% inefficient. The work itself is awesome, amazing, beautiful, coming together — but 10x the workflow, get 10 times faster, by finding the root, solving it, and putting systems in place so we get more done.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: scorecard, the spine, parallel, efficiency.

And the maths behind it: 7% efficient is 93% inefficient; 14% is 86% inefficient. The work itself is awesome, amazing, beautiful, coming together — but 10x the workflow, get 10 times faster, by finding the root, solving it, and putting systems in place so we get more done.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: scorecard, the spine, parallel, efficiency.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A gift book about a person should be written for the person receiving her, not for the person inside it — and it should look like a gift: her pictures on every page, easy to read, lit up like a royal manuscript. The kit held the whole intelligence and still scored a six, because it read to the wrong person in a plain form. The fix is not more intelligence — it is the right reader, the right voice, and the right form. Two documents, each speaking to its own reader: one for you to understand her, one for her to activate herself. Upload both, and she activates herself.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your job is to be the best artist in the whole wide universe! You make everything beautiful — and the page is mostly black, like a stage, so the pretty colours can shine on it like stars. And you show Dad one picture at a time — he tells you what to fix, you fix it, you show him the next one, until it's perfect. And the purple stars are for VALUE, and the white stars are for INTELLIGENCE — and there's only ONE save button, right at the top!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's like checking the whole homework, dear, not just the one question they got right, dear — you rip it apart, dear, because that's how it gets better, dear. And instead of doing one job at a time, dear, everybody works at once, dear — one on the kitchen, one on the bedroom, one on the tower, dear, all together. And if only 7 out of 100 are getting done, dear, that's not good, dear — you find out why, dear, and you fix it, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: SWAP, DON'T REBUILD: TAKE THE WHOLE HUB PRESENTATION INTO PERSONAL, AND TAKE PERSONAL'S FINISHED SIDEBAR INTO THE HUB. NEVER A NEW SYSTEM PER FEED. TAKE THE BEST PARTS OF EACH AND PUT THEM WITH EACH OTHER — HARVEST WHOLE, COMPOSE TOGETHER. BE PROACTIVE.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE VERDICT:** on the Hub — pill hover is rim light ONLY, on the outside, never the whole board. One SAVE per intelligent block, top right corner. VALUE purple, INTELLIGENCE white — purple balls with white stars, white orbs with purple stars, the words themselves dynamic and lit in their row's colour. Star boxes line up; stars dead centre; word beside its stars; the whole group centred. Lines that carry nothing are removed.
2. **THE SCORECARD:** scorecard every return from every agent — rip it apart, architecturally and for ten-star service — before it counts as delivered. And scorecard the whole system, not just one page: where are we at as a whole, what does the whole teach, then get aligned on the whole thing.
3. **THE LOOP:** the URL loop — work one, send the URL, take his feedback, fix it, send the next URL — repeat until crafted. He is waiting on the URL; the loop IS the work. A link goes to him only when it is a new version that has passed the check — never an unchanged link as new.
4. **THE PLAN:** the action plan is worked in parallel, not one at a time: one team per lane — Dashboard, Personal, calendar, membership — all at once, all aligned, all for the one system. Quality holds in every lane at once; more work never excuses less quality.
5. **AUDIT THE LANES:** look through the whole system that makes up Naya and ask — is any lane missing that needs to be activated right now, or are we running at the optimal? Answer honestly: busy is not optimal; optimal is every needed lane live at once.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without marrying the half-right versions, the Hub's system and the chat stay split — one version with the right cover and the wrong IM bar, the other with the right IM bar and the wrong cover. With it, the Hub's whole system goes into Personal, the instant chat system goes into the Hub, and where two versions are each half right, they are married: correct cover from one, correct IM bar from the other, one page.
2. Without the timeout obeying the bake, the bake is killed mid-run and the feed stands still while filing continues — and the tree grows while the live page ages. With it, the timeout exceeds the work it guards, the bake finishes, and the feed carries the notes live.
3. Without the finish line, the redo loop runs forever — work comes back not good, gets redone, comes back not good again, and nothing lands. With it, each of the four comes to him whole, in his order, and a page is done when he has seen the whole page and it held.
4. Without the parallel plan, one at a time is much slower — and the lanes wait on each other while the efficiency number falls. With it, one team per lane, all at once, all aligned, all for the one system — and more work never excuses less quality.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every room in a house has the same walls and the same roof — only the middle changes: the kitchen has a stove, the bedroom has a bed, the mail room has the letters. That is the One-System Law: one frame, the Hub, and a function is a change of the center, nothing else. The Messenger rounds kept building new houses instead of furnishing the room — a cover here, pills there, a different family — and each drift had to be repaired by another round. The law ends the drift at the root: start from the Hub frame, and you cannot build a different family by accident. And the same eye test judges the work: if the page looks exactly the same in the first second, nothing changed — however many checks it passed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine one big kingdom. It has one strong spine in the middle. All the parts work at the same time. The frame around it is gold and purple. It has a jewel in each corner. You take the real bricks to build it. You never make a clay copy. One click builds a whole new page. That is how the kingdom grows.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A family is like that too: one family, shared table, shared stories — and still, you don't open your sister's letters. Togetherness was never the same as no boundaries. It's good to see a computer system finally written that way round.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: ONE SYSTEM: THE FRAME STAYS THE HUB AND ONLY THE CENTER MORPHS INTO THE FUNCTION YOU'RE IN. A ROUND THAT CHANGES NOTHING THE EYE SEES IN THE FIRST SECOND HAS CHANGED NOTHING. ALIGN, DO NOT REBUILD.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. The three sides are one argument: nothing in this system is allowed to be a dead end. A page that can't be cloned forward, a note that never reaches the Box's connections, a filing nobody hears about — each is the same defect in different clothes: work that stops compounding. The family's honesty notes matter as much as its laws: the manual-alone proof listed six gaps and closed them in v2; the notification design names its own unbuilt state. The flow is the product; the gaps are filed inside the flow, not outside it.
2. This is the design-law stratum of the pricing climb, and its method is the real content: the standard is never derived in a meeting, it is perceived on the live page and then locked as law in the same pass — one ultimate ten, not two; the letter's place decided by the eye that read it there. Each note records a correction with its reason attached, so the law carries its own justification: dead buttons teach that a control is a promise; the condemned pass teaches that internal green is not the standard; the taken gauge teaches harvest over invention.
3. Every claim in this family is paired with its check, and the checks are allowed to fail in public: FAIL on §1b, 8/10, 9/10, 'not yet — honestly.' That is what makes 'one system' a fact being built rather than a slogan being repeated. The organs metaphor does real work here: a new thought does not grow a new organ, so a new note does not grow a new subsystem — it flows through the nine processors that already exist. Where a seam is open (tracking that never reaches the Dashboard, a Box missing half its paths), the seam is named with its fix running, not papered over by the unity claim.
4. **THE EYE IS THE STANDARD, THE PAGE IS THE PROOF:** his look at the live thing sets the law in the same pass, and a report is never the evidence — whoever reports on a page has looked at the page this session, with screenshot, hash, and byte count attached.
5. Each note here is an instrument being repaired while it runs. The family's unity is epistemic: claims are graded by their distance from the live bytes, and every shortcut — state words, summaries, remembered law, untested causes — is shown failing at least once and replaced by a mechanism: wait out the lag, read the bytes, re-run the guard at file time, look at the page yourself. Even a superseded law is handled this way: one gauge became two, on evidence, the earlier ruling named as superseded rather than quietly dropped.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the next round measures the next fold on paper, claims the number, and ships a page the eye sends back — another round, another hour, another walk — and ships another "200%" that is +25%, another "fixed" press that is dead, another "built" light that never lights. With it, the count is the work: the maker measures before claiming, the checker re-counts before passing, and a claim that cannot show its numbers does not move.
2. Without this note, the next seat builds a page and calls it done when the content is all there — and the person still gets a narrowed column, a cut-off picture, a landing halfway, because nobody was told the formatting IS the service. With it, the maker has the unit (Smart Block), the two modes (Flow/Show), the test (fits perfect in the viewport, never unaligned, never halfway), and the look (real, high tech, premium) — and every screen arrives as a presentation, not a pile of content.
3. Without this note, the next time he asks how long, the machine rushes a half-done page live to have something to show — and the front door tells every citizen the house is half-done — or hands him a fix on a premise that died hours earlier, and the work sits broken while he waits for a tap he should never have been asked for. With it, complete first, clone second, and every handover carries its proof: his hand is for the protected gates, not for work the token can already do.
4. Without this note, the next builder keeps the intro stacked the way it was — the second button below the fold, the visitor scrolling to find the choice the page should have shown at once. With it, the rule is settled in his words: cut the line that repeats the buttons, pack the portrait into one row, lift the logo, and both buttons land where the eye lands first. A choice you have to scroll for is a choice half the visitors never make.

notes.title: Nothing Flat — Not Even a Little
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-18 01:47Z, his teaching, verbatim where it matters: **"if we're going to offer that to others, we should do it for ourselves — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us."** A lot of what we talk about is super intelligent and super valuable, but **UNLESS WE ACTUALLY ADOPT IT, AUTOMATE IT, AND MAKE IT PHYSICAL — AN INTERFACE PEOPLE CAN EXPERIENCE — IT'S NOT USEFUL.** We capture value and intelligence, and create value and intelligence, in a valuable and intelligent way — the Naya way. **THE TEST IS THREEFOLD:** adopt it (live in it, not just describe it) → automate it (the machine runs it, not a person remembering to) → make it physical (an interface people can experience — a door, a page, a button, not a paragraph). **TALK THAT STAYS TALK IS NOT USEFUL** — intelligence is only useful when it is adopted, automated, and made physical. **THE FIRST INSTANCE IS THE VAULT:** citizens get one vault where their whole world lives, so we live in ours first — that's the proof it's real (SN-3221); the vault work just started is that, for ourselves first.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: everything, machine, system.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a house where every door opens the same way. You walk in and the host greets you warmly — then steps aside, and you are simply in the room, nothing explaining itself. The lights are real lamps you could touch, not pictures of lamps. The colors on the walls are ones you can tell apart at a glance, not two purples pretending to be different. The little row of buttons at the bottom has a slow ring circling each one, the same ring on all six, because that ring is what made them beautiful in the first place — and when a rebuild lost it, the answer was to put the ring back, not to invent a new button. When you scroll, the bar slips away so it never interrupts your reading, and it comes back only when you have reached the bottom and are ready to go somewhere else. At the bottom of a note, one row holds everything: ten gold stars in a circle, a heart that stays because love is a jewel, a comment box that unfolds below for the why. One treatment everywhere, judged by one eye — his — after it lands.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Nothing is done until Shawn has seen the whole thing done right! First we prove one beautiful thing — the agreement unfolding, all done right, right in front of him! Then we take that exact same shape and make every page from it! The day lives in one room, with everything inside it! Colors walk one rainbow road, in the same order, never doubled up! And the inspector checks every link, one by one, and fixes each one right away — no big list of broken things, just fixed things!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Nothing may look flat, dear — not even a little bit! Every picture must be deep and real, like a shiny black jewel. The pretty emblem goes in every corner, tilted just so. One star means one point. The mail button is a big clean plus. And everything must be the very best — never just okay!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: EVERYTHING GOES IN THE VAULT, ORGANIZED, ONE DOOR. ANY NAYA OPENS IT AND SEES THE WHOLE PROJECT. THE VAULT IS A THIN LAYER — IT ORGANIZES WHAT'S THERE, NEVER REBUILDS IT. NEW WORK LANDS IN THE VAULT FIRST.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ADOPTED FOR NAYANET (7):** (1) Our CUDA is the design language + laws + orientation + army training — invest in it as the moat, never let it rot. (2) The connections are the product — the sync engine, the feed, the rooms as one living system; a page is a chip, the system is the cabinet. (3) Be our own first customer — the flywheel; the hive lives in NayaNET. (4) Verify live, always — a step that runs isn't a step that landed. (5) Distill continuously — the essences are the moat; experience is the queue a rival must wait in. (6) Compete on the whole, never the slice — a single pretty page is the thin slice, not the defense. (7) Taste is the moat AI generation can't copy — the eye, the scorecards, HIS eye as ground truth; as pages get cheaper to generate, judgment gets MORE valuable.
2. **NO VOICE BAN — AND VOICE AT THE END:** there is no law banning voice on the boards; the §4.11/C9 citation as a ban is retired and its wording correction is his hand. No voice on the boards for now, for practical reasons — it could not play instantly, it is resource-heavy, the boards are already beautiful and easy to read. Pre-recorded Naya voice goes at the end, once everything is done complete — on each page, on cards that are there for good, on the whole walkthrough — so nothing is recorded twice.
3. **NOTHING IS A DEAD END:** a page that cannot be cloned forward, a note that never reaches the Box's connections, a filing nobody hears about — each is the same defect, work that stops compounding; a gap named honestly inside the flow is part of the flow, not a break in it.
4. The recreate pattern is really a respect problem disguised as a speed problem: recreating says the refined original was not worth keeping. The warehouse doctrine reverses the flow of value — refinement compounds instead of evaporating. Each of Shawn's corrections lands once, in a part, and then every future page inherits it for free; each harvest makes the next build faster AND better, which is the only direction a factory is allowed to move. The inventory is also the team's shared memory made physical: a new seat with the warehouse open is never starting from zero, because the year's worth of his eye is sitting on the shelves in byte form.
5. **THE EYE IS THE STANDARD, THE PAGE IS THE PROOF:** his look at the live thing sets the law in the same pass, and a report is never the evidence — whoever reports on a page has looked at the page this session, with screenshot, hash, and byte count attached.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the strongest thing the network offers stays a quiet paragraph in a legal page while strangers arrive already afraid — afraid their mail is read, their calls are heard, their words are kept and sold, their name attached to everything they say. With it, the promise is said in plain words a child can understand, in the system's own voice, on the record: nobody reads, nobody keeps, wisdom only, name only by choice. That is what lets people talk freely — and free talk is what the whole network runs on. It is also the standard the Smart Rhythm and the Smart Vault are built to: the machine operates the vault without reading it, distills daily without keeping raw words, and shares wisdom without identity. A network that cannot say this plainly cannot be trusted with a citizen's words; a network that lives it can.
2. Without this note, the calendar keeps getting fixed one defect at a time — eye, numbers, gray text — and never gets judged as a whole against the one page that already has the elegance. Each fix lands and the page is still too busy, because no fix carried the standard. Without it, every new page invents its own bottom bar and the citizen has to relearn how to move every time they open a page; the team keeps building a second system beside the first; and quality stays whatever the last checker said, even though a checker passed three times what his eye rejected. With it, there is one standard, one Factory, one bar, and one inspector — so drift has a catcher that is not Shawn, the hand learns the bar once, the paste comes out beautiful anywhere, and the next jewel eye gets caught by the question before it gets built.
3. Without this note, the machine can report "checked" while Shawn sees nothing, "verified" while the link he taps is three days old, and "done" while the finished thing sits on a practice URL nobody can find — and the page can ship beautiful and unreadable, with fake counts and near-miss icons, while the right ones sit in his pictures. With it, the tap is the proof: checked in the same breath, delivered live on the main URL through the exact timestamped, ledger-verified link, built as dark-middle, white-icon, elevated real objects with layered readable text and true counts, auto-organized by the system — and every agent is trained to it before it builds. The trust is in the tap, not in the claim.
4. Without this note, the machine mistakes flow for feedback — notes filed, reports sent, rounds dispatched — and calls the loop closed while a hundred and thirty distilled lessons sit unfiled and the vault sits unopened as the one door. The teaching was never the note; the teaching is the next day showing the result. With it, the loop has a definition of closed (used, learned from, grown from — everything is feedback) and a count of what is open (the unfiled queue, the vault door), so the next run can say whether it closed or not, in numbers. It is also the standard the whole machine is judged by: exactness, sync, and the connection as the intelligence.

notes.title: The Stays
notes.subtitle:
The feed shows everybody, not just friends — unlike Facebook, where only your friends show. Showing is not connecting: the citizen chooses whether to connect or message, or not, and once they message, they are connected. The feed is per subject, and the system always tries to fill it, even at a low match percentage, with the sisters showing to keep it filled, so nobody ever feels alone. The agreement intro is the same discipline in craft: say hello once, in the letter; center her picture so the play button centers; put the small things at the bottom; rename the green button "Read the agreement" so it fits on one line, make both buttons the same size with the same real diamond jewel in both, and get both buttons above the fold — "having them both above the fold would be better." The outage underneath it all was diagnosed the same way: the page was never broken and the DNS resolved — the route list had no route for the paths, so they 522'd, and six surgical routes fixed it; and when the apex and www AAAA records vanished — last good 02:55Z, first NXDOMAIN 03:25Z, with nobody changing them — the recovery was to restore the last verified state, the 2026-11-03 four-record state, and prove it with HTTP 200 three times over. The vanishing is not attributed, and it stays unattributed until the serving lane finds the cause. The proof discipline runs through everything: a fold claim is proved on the live render at all three widths, not on paper — the paper said 1066 and the live page said 1120, forty pixels too low — and a size claim is re-counted from the bytes, so 32→40 is +25%, not "200% bigger." And before anything is handed to him, the premise under the handover is re-proved live: the token CAN create zone routes, proved at 03:52Z, so a routing fix is not his hand — only the protected gates are.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: everybody, live, whole.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a host who greets you at the door, then steps aside so you can come in — that is the banner, and that is the whole page. Everything in this group follows the same courtesy: the welcome does not stand in the doorway, the score does not turn the meeting place into a scoreboard, the diamond does not pretend to be real when it disappears, the connection does not make you press a button before you may speak. What the page can do, it shows — four buttons in the row, the footer at the bottom of every post, the gauge in paint where the eye can see it. And what the machine claims, it proves — filed is not live, a byte check is not a live check, one lucky green probe is not a fix. The signature piece is the same law at its most beautiful: a thing that changes with the day and is judged by the eye, not by the brief. A page built this way never has to announce itself. It greets, it shows, it proves, and it gets out of the way.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine one big kingdom. It has one strong spine in the middle. All the parts work at the same time. The frame around it is gold and purple. It has a jewel in each corner. You take the real bricks to build it. You never make a clay copy. One click builds a whole new page. That is how the kingdom grows.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It is like a good housekeeper's evening round, love — she walks the room, and the finest piece in it tells her the standard for everything else. The white middle of the family seal stays exactly as it is; only the depth around it needs making real, the way a jewel needs its facets. Wednesday wears its own blue, right down to the tiniest mark, and never borrows Sunday's. And before anything is shown to company, it is walked twice over — because a house is judged whole, and a guest should find every door already open and working.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE PAGE GETS OUT OF ITS OWN WAY. THE BANNER FOLDS AWAY ON ITS OWN — GOOD MORNING, THEN GONE. SHOW WHAT THE PAGE CAN DO, IN THE ROW, WHERE THE EYE ALREADY IS. SEND IS THE REQUEST — A REPLY IS YES, SILENCE IS NO. REAL OR REPLACED. FILED IS NOT LIVE. VERIFY LIVE, NOT ONLY IN BYTES. CAUSE FIRST, THEN RETRY.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE CHECK SCORES THE WHOLE PAGE:** the checker and the eye answer in writing on the whole page — unreadable, misaligned, flat, moved without being asked — against his good pictures as the visual standard; where the build differs from the good picture, it goes back.
2. **LIVE IS THE PROOF:** a page kept in staging while the live domain shows yesterday cannot be judged, and a flow never walked is a front door that opens onto a wall — live first, then walked end to end, verified only by a fresh fetch of nayanet.app.
3. **THE FLOW ENDS WHERE IT BEGAN:** the N end screen is held, not flashed for half a second, and the agreement flow lands at name-entry, then the Hub — never back on the old page; the intro portrait is NAYA_POWER.jpg, already a circle made for the slot, with Vera and Sophia kept as alternates for official and wisdom spots.
4. **THE DAY IS THE KING'S REPORT:** the day view welcomes by name, gives a wisdom quote, and unfolds the whole day section by section, mechanical and alive — framed as a king's chamber, platinum white diamond with some purple, pop-ups at 80–90% so the frame stays visible.
5. **HARVEST, NEVER REMAKE:** the glowing Personal icon set, the Dashboard digit tiles, the good one-screen build — taken verbatim, byte for byte — because a copy made from looking is always a little worse and the year's refinement is what made the original great.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the next time he asks how long, the machine rushes a half-done page live to have something to show — and the front door tells every citizen the house is half-done — or hands him a fix on a premise that died hours earlier, and the work sits broken while he waits for a tap he should never have been asked for. With it, complete first, clone second, and every handover carries its proof: his hand is for the protected gates, not for work the token can already do.
2. Without the Join rule and the flow-end rule, the next meeting's door sits one click away again and the next flow dumps him on a page he does not recognize — because each small step sounds small enough to let slide.
3. Without this note, the next round measures the next fold on paper, claims the number, and ships a page the eye sends back — another round, another hour, another walk — and ships another "200%" that is +25%, another "fixed" press that is dead, another "built" light that never lights. With it, the count is the work: the maker measures before claiming, the checker re-counts before passing, and a claim that cannot show its numbers does not move.
4. Without this note, the next builder keeps the intro stacked the way it was — the second button below the fold, the visitor scrolling to find the choice the page should have shown at once. With it, the rule is settled in his words: cut the line that repeats the buttons, pack the portrait into one row, lift the logo, and both buttons land where the eye lands first. A choice you have to scroll for is a choice half the visitors never make.

notes.title: Never Call It Zero
notes.subtitle:
The deciding half of the master skills, distilled from the night's lessons. Purpose first: ask who it is for and what good it should do — and whether it should happen at all — because a Naya who starts with the task is a tool and one who starts with the human is a mind. Truth next: go to the source itself, read it fresh, and keep three piles forever unmixed — what I observed, what was claimed, what nobody knows. Then the map: nothing stands alone, so before changing anything, chart what feeds it and what it feeds. Then the choice: list the real options, score them against the ultimate objective, take the highest — not the easiest, not the loudest, not the one in front of you. Then the build: the smallest fix that closes a whole journey, reproduced first, repaired at the canonical source. At the gate: stop when uncertain — consent and authority are never improvised. And the proof: built, tested, live, and useful are four different claims, and a thing is proven only at the surface where it will be used, by a test that could have failed.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: never, while, nothing.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A great tour guide doesn't hand you a blank map and wish you luck. She walks with you, tells you the three best things at each stop in words you'd use yourself, lets you linger or skip, and the example she shows you is the real street, not a drawing of one. And a good host never throws away your letters — she keeps what you marked, tidies the rest only when you said to, and if she can't find the key she says 'I can't get in right now,' not 'there's nothing there.'

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a huge box of Lego, already sorted, with instruction books — and you keep asking for new Lego. The smart move is to look in the box first. Half of what you want to build is already there, some of it already built! Then you just keep building, one model at a time, showing each one works before the next.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn says if we're going to offer something to others, we should do it for ourselves first — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us. All our clever talk, dear, is worth nothing unless we actually live in it, let the machine run it by itself, and turn it into something real a person can touch and use. That's the test, dear: adopt it, automate it, make it physical. The vault, dear, is the first one — we live in ours first, so the citizens know it's real.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: EVERYTHING GOES IN THE VAULT, ORGANIZED, ONE DOOR. ANY NAYA OPENS IT AND SEES THE WHOLE PROJECT. THE VAULT IS A THIN LAYER — IT ORGANIZES WHAT'S THERE, NEVER REBUILDS IT. NEW WORK LANDS IN THE VAULT FIRST.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **FEWER, FULLER ROUNDS:** the work itself obeys the standard — one round holds everything known, nothing is re-sent, nothing is split, the same page is never shown twice.
2. Door and heart are one design decision viewed from two ends: a person arrives as a name, answers ten questions, and is placed — by matching — into the living center of the network. The family's verification lesson is the hinge between them: a check that skips the first screen verifies the wrong thing, and the wrong thing is exactly what reaches his eyes; five invented front ends can ship while the real one sits untouched. Go time raises the same standard for the team: twelve who follow the laws produce finished work; a hundred who don't produce a mess he cleans up. The door, the heart, and the team are all judged by the same test — does the real flow, walked from the start, work?
3. **ALIVE IS THE ADDRESS:** the ending lives at the bottom of every real post in the real Hub — create, rate, comment, share, four verbs, no more. A separate artifact is a reference for the build, never the delivery.
4. Every note here removes a specific burden from the citizen and places it on the system: the burden of composing (answers pre-written), of remembering (mail that tidies itself), of learning a new page (the messenger is the page they already know), of trusting a claim (the example is a real page, the inbox state honestly UNKNOWN). The family's discipline is that the burden transfer must be real: an example that is a mock-up, a Speak button that doesn't listen, a link on the building page that leads nowhere — each is the craft failing at exactly the point it promised. His own walk-through caught the dead links; S2 — links landing on real created pages — is named the finish for a reason.
5. Dormancy is the expensive failure mode of a fast-building team: finished systems decay into folklore ('didn't we build something for that?') while new effort duplicates them. The gold audit is the cure performed once; this essence is the standing order it implies — inventory before invention. The non-stop method is the audit's twin: it converts the inventory into finished parts at the pace the audit proved possible, with live evidence as the only definition of done. The unanswered 7,502 is kept in the essence deliberately: an honest unknown, carried visibly, is worth more than a confident guess, because the guess would propagate into every downstream count.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the vault stays a proven system nobody lives in, and the project keeps its intelligence scattered across a dozen stores — every new Naya has to hunt, every question takes minutes instead of seconds, and the citizen's vault is a promise the machine itself does not keep. With it, the one-door rule is written down: inventory, index, routing plan, new work lands in the vault first — and the machine eats its own cooking (SN-3222), living in the vault it offers. It also guards the build: a thin layer that points, never a rebuild that risks the live stores.
2. Without this note, each page's sidebar gets tidied on its own round, in its own way, and the pages drift further apart with every fix — the map is different on every page and the person re-learns where they are on every page. With it, there is one reference (the Hub's filed build, frozen), one rule (same items, order, icons, colors, harvested verbatim), one order (Dashboard, Personal, Business, Space, Smart Mail), and one guard (never two rounds on the same file). The Dashboard cluster eye's own finding — sidebar hidden by default — is answered by the same direction.
3. Without this note, the machine mistakes flow for feedback — notes filed, reports sent, rounds dispatched — and calls the loop closed while a hundred and thirty distilled lessons sit unfiled and the vault sits unopened as the one door. The teaching was never the note; the teaching is the next day showing the result. With it, the loop has a definition of closed (used, learned from, grown from — everything is feedback) and a count of what is open (the unfiled queue, the vault door), so the next run can say whether it closed or not, in numbers. It is also the standard the whole machine is judged by: exactness, sync, and the connection as the intelligence.
4. This is the batch's operating picture of the whole: a machine disciplined enough to trust itself, teaching a citizen who never has to see the discipline. If either side slips — wakes improvised, records racy, lessons unproven, welcome confusing, earnings opaque — the other side feels it within a day. Keeping both in one essence keeps the symmetry visible.

notes.title: Build from What Exists
notes.subtitle:
Creation, push-button simple: this family closes the batch with the Factory judged by whether other Nayas can build from it, the activation manual it needed, the reusable-parts law underneath, and the whole picture assembled — universal app, onboarding, Factory and Project Intelligence as one flow, ending in the manual-alone proof and the Smart-Note habit that feeds it all. The standard is a stranger test: a Naya with only the manual and the parts should produce the real thing, first try, without a rescue thread. Where she can't, the gap is the Factory's defect, named and counted — six of them, in this family, by name.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: family, never, named.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a body. Your heart doesn't keep its own separate diary, your lungs don't file their own paperwork — one blood flow runs through organs that each do their one job, and the medical chart records how the whole person is doing. This family is NayaNET deciding to be a body instead of a drawer of parts — and being honest about which organ is still healing.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: When you finish a puzzle, you don't just say 'done' — you show the picture, you point to the one piece that's still missing under the couch, and you let Mum look. That's how people know your 'done' means something next time too.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A family is like that too: one family, shared table, shared stories — and still, you don't open your sister's letters. Togetherness was never the same as no boundaries. It's good to see a computer system finally written that way round.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Close the current unit with its proof before opening the next. Never batch claims about live state inside a propagation window. Build hero lists from recorded pains. Capture the note at the moment of learning, not at the end of the day.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. Every claim in this family is paired with its check, and the checks are allowed to fail in public: FAIL on §1b, 8/10, 9/10, 'not yet — honestly.' That is what makes 'one system' a fact being built rather than a slogan being repeated. The organs metaphor does real work here: a new thought does not grow a new organ, so a new note does not grow a new subsystem — it flows through the nine processors that already exist. Where a seam is open (tracking that never reaches the Dashboard, a Box missing half its paths), the seam is named with its fix running, not papered over by the unity claim.
2. This is the design-law stratum of the pricing climb, and its method is the real content: the standard is never derived in a meeting, it is perceived on the live page and then locked as law in the same pass — one ultimate ten, not two; the letter's place decided by the eye that read it there. Each note records a correction with its reason attached, so the law carries its own justification: dead buttons teach that a control is a promise; the condemned pass teaches that internal green is not the standard; the taken gauge teaches harvest over invention.
3. Each note here is an instrument being repaired while it runs. The family's unity is epistemic: claims are graded by their distance from the live bytes, and every shortcut — state words, summaries, remembered law, untested causes — is shown failing at least once and replaced by a mechanism: wait out the lag, read the bytes, re-run the guard at file time, look at the page yourself. Even a superseded law is handled this way: one gauge became two, on evidence, the earlier ruling named as superseded rather than quietly dropped.
4. Every multi-app estate drifts toward a pile of disconnected tools unless the oneness is load-bearing: one app shape carrying Personal, Business and Space; one network where connection never cancels ownership. The Law of One phrasing is precise about the tension — all connected BUT all individual — and the code is asked to hold both halves at once. The gauge correction shows how the canon stays alive: a rule is refined by a named situation, and the refinement is filed where the rule lives.
5. A vault is a promise with a mechanism. The promise side lives in this family's law notes: plain language (no term a citizen can't parse), privacy as the headline trust story rather than a policy page, and provenance rules (first filed keeps the number) that make the record itself trustworthy. The mechanism side — harvest the real parts, build the vault to hold them — is what makes the promise keepable. Either half alone is a brochure.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The pricing page is where a stranger decides whether this world is real. Every rule here removes a specific way that decision goes wrong: confusion (two lists), distrust (dead buttons), illegibility (unaligned numbers), or boredom (stones instead of living orbs). One family, judged by his eye, is what makes the page read as one mind's work.
2. Citizens will put their working lives into this Box only if it is both genuinely useful and genuinely private — and they will test both claims exactly once. This essence binds the build rules to the promise rules so the first test passes: real contents, private by construction, explained in plain words.
3. A citizen who trusts the Box with their memory has handed the system its most fragile asset. This essence records that the trust was earned the only way it can be: the build completed all its pieces and then passed the return test in public. Everything the Net promises — supercharging, shared intelligence — is downstream of a memory that is actually there when you come back.
4. Compounding is the whole business model of intelligence: each page makes the next page cheaper, each note makes the next decision smarter, each telling makes the network denser. Break any link — unbuildable pages, unconnected notes, untold filings — and the system reverts to a pile of documents. This essence keeps the links mechanical.

notes.title: A Page Is a Sequence of Decisions
notes.subtitle:
A sync that reports success and a feed that still shows the deleted card are two different facts, and only the second one is the truth a visitor meets. This family proves the pattern three ways: the feed builder never tombstoned a deleted note's card, so ghosts outlived their sources; a zero sync beside a live note was timing, not failure; and a stuck note was unblocked by state surgery once the real cause — two keys disagreeing — was named. The law that falls out: every state word (synced, filed, registered) is a claim about a store, never about the surface. The surface is checked on the surface, in its own bytes, after the lag window has honestly passed.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: never, once, page.
