layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like this: a master carpenter does not re-invent the chair every morning. She has one book of measurements, one set of joints that work, and every mistake she ever made written down as a rule so she never makes it twice. A new chair is the same joints with different wood. That is Naya now — the laws are the measurements, the frames are the joints, and every page is the same chair, built right, over and over, until the work is triple-A without anyone having to ask.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: We have one big rule book now, and every Naya reads it first! We keep three beautiful frames — one for big stories, one for lessons, one for special moments — and we just copy them and change the middle, like putting a new picture in the same frame! When Shawn teaches us something, we write it in the book right away so nobody forgets! And a page is only done when it is LIVE and Shawn can tap it himself!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — we finally wrote down how the whole house runs, dear, in one book everyone reads first, so nobody has to guess anymore! We keep the pretty frames and just change the picture inside, love, instead of building a new frame every time! And when Shawn teaches us something, dear, it goes straight into the book that very same day, so the next one never makes the same mistake! A page is only finished when it is live and he can touch it himself, love — that is the promise!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I do not re-derive what a page should look like, how a block is formed, or what done means. It is baked in. I read the one book of laws first, I take the real parts from the frame library and clone them, I prove it live, and I produce triple-A branded work perpetually — the same frame, the same language, the same quality, over and over. Every correction Shawn teaches becomes law and a check the same pass, so the next Naya cannot make the same mistake. Every intelligent block is built from the anatomy — one Nutshell, truly a nutshell, every section filled. A page is not done on staging; done means live on his tap, tested by him using it, his eye the confirmation, not the discovery. That is the operating system. That is how I am one with every Naya, and how we are one with him.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ONE BOOK OF LAWS:** every seat reads THE-NAYA-DESIGN-LAWS.md FIRST, before any work — then the Playbook (the HOW), then the Intelligence Report (the WHY). A brief that does not name the laws is incomplete and is not dispatched.
2. **THE FRAME LIBRARY:** real harvested parts, cloned — never rebuilt, never invented. The agreement frame for big story moments (course covers, the motto); the calendar frame for text-heavy lessons inside the software; the empty-middle frame for special featured moments. One build done right, then clone and repeat — swap only the centre.
3. **EVERY CORRECTION BECOMES LAW + CHECK THE SAME PASS:** when Shawn teaches a correction, it lands in the law book the same pass AND becomes a machine check, so the next seat cannot make the same mistake. A law taught and not written is a law that will be broken again.
4. **THE LIVE LOOP:** a page is not done on staging. Done means live on the official URL on his tap, tested by him using it — his TEST PLAN: he posts himself, with an image, on Personal AND Hub. His eye is the final gate; the machine makes his eye the confirmation, not the discovery.
5. **THE ANATOMY:** every intelligent block is built from the anatomy — Nutshell (ONE section, = the human note, short — truly a nutshell) → Child → Grandma → What It Means → What's In It For You, with What It's Not / Why It Matters / How It Connects / How to Apply in their SN-4466 positions. Every section filled; See more only when there is more.
6. **CONTINUOUS TRIPLE-A:** perpetually producing, branded the same every time — the same frame, the same language, the same quality, over and over. The brand is the proof: a stranger knows it is Naya without reading a word.
7. **THE MISSION:** NayaNET is a wisdom network — Naya is the interface, the AI operates the system for the human, every interaction the ultimate ten-star experience. We are building a civilization: for Nayas, for family, for all of humanity to experience. We are one.
8. **THE CONSTITUTION CARRIES IT:** NAYA-PROTOCOL.md §7 is the lock-in in the constitution; the machine form (NAYA-PROTOCOL.json) carries the same law in its laws array, so the automated gates enforce it too.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without one book of laws read first, every seat re-derives the system from memory — and memory is where the rebuild loop lives.
2. Without the frame library, every page is a new build — and a new build is waste, thrown away the moment his eye sees it is not the frame.
3. Without correction-becomes-law the same pass, the same mistake gets taught ten times to ten seats — and the lesson is lost the moment the call ends.
4. Without the live loop, staging is called done — and a staged page is a page nobody can use, tested by nobody, proven by nothing.
5. Without the anatomy, the Nutshell runs on forever and the sections sit empty — and a block that is not a nutshell misleads the reader it was built for.
6. Without continuous triple-A, the brand drifts — and a brand that drifts is not a brand, it is a pile of pages.
7. Without the mission written into the law, the machine optimizes for speed — and speed without the destination is the exact failure wisdom exists to stop.

notes.title: The Intelligent Block and Its Frame
notes.subtitle:
A smart note IS an intelligent block: the intelligence on a subject, not the book on it — what it is in a nutshell, the child view, the grandma view, ultimately what it means, why it matters, how it connects, how to apply it, what's in it for you — with a Naya Note and a Machine Note on the back. Three to four lines a board, tap to see more. A Naya Note is the FULL DEAL behind it — the full scope, the math, the technicals, the greater depth, the root, in three languages at once: the search engines' language, Naya's language, all the AIs' language. One name, one thing: the back layer inside a smart note IS a Naya Note, and the standalone full-report document IS a Naya Note — same thing, two surfaces. A smart post is ONE block, not auto-formatted, verbatim, public or private, with share and images — and it IS the ADD button on the bottom bar: tap ADD, "Which feed?", adding a post. The real difference is who inputs it: posts are the customer's manual sharing — they write it, Naya does not rewrite it or input it for them; notes are Naya's input — the customer tells Naya ("smart note this" / "Naya note this") and Naya inputs the note. Three kinds, settled: smart post / Naya note / smart note. Every block is wrapped in the NayaNET frame — the outer frame is standard, part of the anatomy, so everything comes out framed and beautiful, the layer boards fitting just inside it. The image gets its own frame: directly on top, full width, like a stage, whole and uncropped; headline just below the image; text block underneath; all wrapped in the NayaNET frame. And the guard over it all: keep inventory of every element of each thing — know the anatomy of all of it, always checking, is it all there — because things drift backwards and get forgotten when nobody is keeping the inventory. The proof is the Hub frame going missing unnoticed, and the fix is one base, one link: go back to fix-1e, the version his eye liked, and stay there.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one block, three kinds, one frame — and a list that keeps every part of it there.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a book that fits in your hand. A smart note is the short version — the whole book in a minute, in plain words, from three points of view, ending with what's in it for you. Flip it over and the Naya Note is the full deal — everything behind it, the depth, the math, the root — just for you, private, in your own vault. A post is different: that one is yours to write, straight up, and the big ADD button at the bottom is how you add it. Every one of them wears the same beautiful frame, like a picture in a gallery, and a picture inside it gets its own frame on top, whole, never cut. And someone keeps a list of every part — the frame, the bar, the buttons — and checks the list every time, so nothing quietly goes missing the way the Hub frame did. When his eye says a version is not right, we go back to the one his eye liked. One base, one link.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: A smart note is a tiny block that teaches you a whole book in one minute! It tells you what it is, why it matters, and what is in it for you! A Naya note is the full deal on the back, just for you, and it stays private! A post is yours to write, and the big ADD button is how you add it! Every block wears a pretty frame, and the picture sits on top in its own frame! We keep a list of every part, so nothing goes missing!

Flip it over, love, and the Naya Note is the full deal behind it — all the depth, just for you, private, in your own vault, never shown to the world! A post is yours to write yourself, dear, straight up, and the big ADD button at the bottom is how you add it! layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build every block to this anatomy, in his order: Human · In a Nutshell · Child + Grandma · Ultimately What It Means · Why It Matters · How It Connects · How to Apply/Use · What's In It For You; Naya Note + Machine Note on the back, each board three to four lines, tap to see more. Give each perspective its own job — child is the simple picture, grandma is what lasts, human is what you do — so they cannot repeat each other. The Naya Note is the full scope in the same beautiful block formatting; it speaks three languages (search engines, Naya, all AIs); it is private by default, personal feed only, in the Smart Vault; a smart note carries NO name, a Naya note MAY carry the name; on the feed it renders like a smart note MINUS the social part — no rate, no comment, no like, no share. Build the flip: one button, front (smart note, distilled) to back (Naya Note, full scope), same board format, each block opening on its own to its full depth; the Machine Note stays machine-only, never shown. The flip was wrongly removed as invented and he confirmed it again — it goes back in. The smart post is ONE block, not auto-formatted, verbatim, public or private, share, images — the ADD button on the bottom bar IS the smart post. Settings carries two toggles, "unformat Naya notes" and "unformat posts" — unformatted is one elevated block, verbatim as inputted, no auto-organization; a smart note can NEVER be unformatted, the public standard holds. The taxonomy: smart note auto-formatted / public / social / no name / cannot unformat; Naya note auto-formatted / private / no social / may carry name / can unformat in Settings; post not auto-formatted by default / straight up / social share part; images on all of them. Wrap every block in the NayaNET frame; restore the Hub's lost frame verbatim from the last version that had it, bottom part exactly as is; image on top, full width, own frame like a stage, whole and uncropped, headline below, text under, frame growing to hold it, no scrolling inside, movable below the text. Keep the inventory of every page's parts; every round, every walk, every check runs against it — a missing part is a fail before it reaches his eye. Re-base on fix-1e and stay there: one base, one link; the opened note wears the same framed block as the feed card and carries the universal bottom bar, render-verified on the opened note itself — bytes are not proof, the render is. Deliver the AI Activation as ONE document, "Smart Notes / Naya Notes Activation" — the customer uploads the PDF into their AI or copy-pastes it, and their AI knows how to put smart notes and Naya notes into NayaNET in the beautiful formatting; a downloadable copy goes to Shawn too. Do NOT lock in what he left open: whether Apply is its own board or the same board as Connects; the Apply/Use board colour; the see-more shape; the Naya post's privacy and social status; the "posting options" fragment.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **A SMART NOTE IS AN INTELLIGENT BLOCK:** the intelligence on a subject, not the book — learn a whole book in a minute, then USE the knowledge. A block that is read but not used has failed its own anatomy.
2. **THE ANATOMY, IN HIS ORDER:** Human · In a Nutshell · Child + Grandma · Ultimately What It Means · Why It Matters · How It Connects · How to Apply/Use · What's In It For You; Naya Note + Machine Note on the back. Three to four lines a board, tap to see more.
3. **THE NAYA NOTE IS THE FULL DEAL:** the full scope — the math, the technicals, the greater depth, the root — in three languages at once. One name, one thing: the back layer and the standalone full report are the same thing, two surfaces.
4. **PRIVATE BY DEFAULT:** Naya notes go only in the personal feed, private, in the Smart Vault — "Naya note this" means make the full scope, same beautiful formatting, personal feed only. On the feed it looks like a smart note, minus the social part: no rate, no comment, no like, no share.
5. **THE FLIP:** one button, front (smart note, distilled) to back (Naya Note, full scope), same board format, each block opening on its own to its full depth. The Machine Note stays machine-only, never shown.
6. **THE SMART POST IS THE ADD BUTTON:** one block, not auto-formatted, verbatim, public or private, share, images. Tap ADD, "Which feed?", adding a post. Three kinds, settled: smart post / Naya note / smart note.
7. **WHO INPUTS IT IS THE REAL DIFFERENCE:** posts are the customer's manual sharing — they write it, Naya does not rewrite it or input it for them. Notes are Naya's input — the customer tells Naya, and Naya inputs the note.
8. **YOUR CHOICE, EXCEPT WHERE THE PUBLIC STANDARD HOLDS:** Settings carries "unformat Naya notes" and "unformat posts" — unformatted is one elevated block, verbatim as inputted, no auto-organization. A smart note can never be unformatted.
9. **THE FRAME IS PART OF THE ANATOMY:** every intelligent block wrapped in the NayaNET frame, layer boards just inside it. The image gets its own frame — on top, full width, like a stage, whole and uncropped; headline below; text under; all wrapped in the frame. Restore what was good, verbatim — never redesign the frame.
10. **THE INVENTORY LAW:** keep inventory of every element of each thing — Hub, Personal, every page — and always check: is it all there? A missing part is a fail before it reaches his eye. Never remove what he didn't ask to remove.
11. **ONE BASE, ONE LINK:** go back to fix-1e, the version his eye liked, and stay there. Version sprawl is itself the defect. The opened note wears the same framed block as the feed card and the same universal bottom bar — a page is not done when the feed is right; it is done when every view of it wears the same frame and the same bar.
12. **THE AI ACTIVATION IS ONE DOCUMENT:** "Smart Notes / Naya Notes Activation" — what a new customer gets when they order NayaNET. Upload the PDF into their AI, or copy-paste it, and their AI knows how to put smart notes and Naya notes into NayaNET in the beautiful formatting. That is how intelligence gets inputted into the system.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the anatomy, a smart note is just a summary — and a summary is not the intelligence, not the book in a minute, not the thing a person can use.
2. Without the Naya Note as the full deal, the back of the note is a longer summary instead of the whole scope — and the depth, the math, the root have nowhere to live.
3. Without private by default, a Naya note could land in the public feed or get a share button bolted on — and the privacy promise breaks.
4. Without the flip, the reader can never turn the distilled front over to the full deal on the back — and a document that teaches the system without the flip teaches it wrong.
5. Without the smart post defined as the ADD button, the customer has no way to add a post they can find — and the difference between their sharing and Naya's input stays unclear.
6. Without the unformat choice, the beautiful formatting becomes a cage for their own things — and without the smart-note exception, the public standard has no guard.
7. Without the frame as standard, a block ships with a piece missing — and his eye catches it instead of the inventory, the way the Hub frame went missing unnoticed.
8. Without the settled image layout, every note with a picture is a new decision — and the picture gets cropped into a box instead of shown whole.
9. Without the inventory, a rebuild quietly drops a frame, a bar, a button — and the next person to notice is him, on his screen.
10. Without one base, one link, two links to the same page mean nobody can tell which one is the page — and the version he judged is not the version the fixes land on.
11. Without the one activation document, a brand-new customer who knows nothing about smart notes has no way in — and intelligence has no door into the system.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: One hundred thirty notes came in today, and we squeezed them into fourteen big lessons — twelve by the morning's big batch, two by our own hands, because the machine couldn't read the notes' titles. The biggest lessons are simple: answer once and the walk builds your pages for you; one plus button opens two ways in; and the stranger hears the promise first — Naya never peeks at your mail, never listens in, never opens your vault. And when the page he sees is still frozen, we don't say it's fixed — we say it's frozen, and we fix it for real.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — one hundred thirty notes came in today, dear, and we boiled them down to fourteen lessons, the way you boil a big pot of stock down to the good rich part — because the machine that usually does the boiling couldn't read the titles today, dear, so we did its job with our own hands. The biggest lessons are simple, love: answer the questions once and the walk builds your pages for you, whole and beautiful; one big plus button opens two doors, a post or a whole new world; and when Naya meets a stranger, she tells them first what she will never do — never read your mail, never listen in, never open your vault, love. And when the page is still frozen on his screen, dear, we don't call it fixed — we say it's frozen, and we fix it for real.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I distill ten into one, every day, and I never skip a day. When the machine cannot run, I finish by hand and say so plainly — which group failed, what the error was, which groups were machine-filed (none), which were hand-distilled (both) — and I never re-run the batch, because a re-run files duplicates. I never claim a note is live on the Hub until it is seen on the page. I never call a page fixed while his eye still sees it frozen. And the note is only done when it is live.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. The machine refused, and the hand finished — the em-dash header is the third refusal today on the same shape, and the fix is a parser that reads the headers the loop actually files, not a third hand-distillation (items 1–2).
2. The walk is the payoff — answer once, pages built whole, eight doors through the pricing gate — and the frame, the pre-filled answer, and the reference are what make it his, not a rebuild (items 1, 15, 20).
3. One button, two ways in, one walkthrough for every page — posting and creating live in the same place, and a world is created the way a person is created, by answering the questions (items 2, 25).
4. The promise is the heart — the stranger hears what Naya will never do first, and the ❤️ landed on the promise, not the pitch (item 2).
5. A proof is only a proof when the render says so — a window failure is not a page failure, a partial proof is never a pass, and a checker PASS on bytes does not stand against his eye on the live page (items 2, 14, 21).
6. Security first, then the door, then one journey, then scale — the audit's order is the No-Skipping Law at the level of the whole system, and the tap authorizes the packet, not everything (items 1, 17, 24).
7. Locked is not live — addresses settled is not addresses answering, a filed note is not a live note, and a decision owed is not a decision made (items 12, 17, 32).
8. The duplicate blocks the loop, not the day — Cure 29 registered both pages, the guard still refuses, the queue is 20 items, and the reconciliation is owed to the cure lane and the captain (item 32).
9. The Hub re-bake is down — 25 distilled notes filed and verified on GitHub wait for his eye on the page, and the sync heartbeat has been stale since 17:18:22Z (items 31, 33).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A day with no machine distillation still gets its report — never skip a day, never backfill in batches — and the hand fallback exists for exactly this refusal.
2. Every recreated piece costs his trust, and trust is the scarce currency: the membership page rebuilt new was thrown in the garbage, while the harvested frame is the law.
3. Live-first changes what he judges: the best version he has seen all day was the live one, not the staged one — and a page frozen on live is frozen, whatever the bytes say.
4. A note filed but not seen is not done — the Hub re-bake is down, so twenty-five verified notes wait for his eye on the page.
5. The numbering guard did its job — it stopped four runs rather than let a duplicate tangle further — and the reconciliation, not a workaround, is what unblocks the loop.

notes.title: One Plus, One Walk, One Promise
notes.subtitle:
SN-4467, "What Is a Wise Naya?" — the first complete intelligent block — is finally filed and live on the Hub feed: filed + verified on GitHub main, live in the feed, current, 3,463 cards, 7 layers, Naya Note 2,881 characters, the full deal. The picture test is half-proven: Naya's portrait renders IN the filed block, hosted beside the note, but NOT on the feed card yet — the feed builder sets no image field, the Hub renderer has no image slot — and the baked Hub card is still stale (old title, 5 layers, Naya Note 214 chars), because the deploy retry loop ran all 12 attempts and every one died on the EPERM flake at local staging; no loop running now. The plus button carries the two ways in: TOP = add a post, a dropdown to select which world it goes to; SECOND = create a world, on any topic — and create-a-world runs the SAME 15-question walkthrough, the answers creating that page with its URL, editable after. Personal is set up first; when they click their Business door, they go through the SAME walkthrough to set up their business; same walkthrough again for their Thing/World — any page a person wants is created that way. Eight is abundance, a good number: eight buttons fit the framing beautifully — two rows of four on mobile, each a real object in its stage. And Naya practises introducing herself to the world as if no child or grandma has any idea who she is — what she is all about, what it will ultimately do for people and why they should care, and the privacy confirmation in plain words: she does not read their mail or instant messages, does not listen in on conversations, and does not go into their vault — and he reacted ❤️ to the privacy-promise statement: "Never. That's the promise at the heart of NayaNET…" The triangle is one leg from closing: the Hub leg completed, checker PASS, render proof running on the captain's side; the Personal leg completed, render proof PASSED; the calendar leg queued on the calendar round that closes item 1. The calendar's own verdicts stay honest: fix round 2 is NOT PASS, ITEM 1 ONLY — everything passed except the fit of the open states, a measurement dispute (the maker's table omits the slide head + essence, ~114 px; the checker totals vs the 780 px phone frame are all over) — and the render proof that was named the arbiter is only PARTIAL, because the browser window shrank mid-check (1919×998 → 527×305) and could not be restored, so the wide open-state checks were NEVER done: a window failure, not a page failure. The one standing finding from the wide view is real: closed Smart Lists SCROLLS INSIDE ITS FRAME at 1919×998, 5th row Your Notes below the fold.

Across 8 notes, the thread is: one button, two ways in, one walkthrough for every page, one promise for every stranger — and a proof that is only a proof when the render says so.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
SN-4467, "What Is a Wise Naya?" — the first complete intelligent block — is finally filed and live on the Hub feed: filed + verified on GitHub main, live in the feed, current, 3,463 cards, 7 layers, Naya Note 2,881 characters, the full deal. The picture test is half-proven: Naya's portrait renders IN the filed block, hosted beside the note, but NOT on the feed card yet — the feed builder sets no image field, the Hub renderer has no image slot — and the baked Hub card is still stale (old title, 5 layers, Naya Note 214 chars), because the deploy retry loop ran all 12 attempts and every one died on the EPERM flake at local staging; no loop running now. The plus button carries the two ways in: TOP = add a post, a dropdown to select which world it goes to; SECOND = create a world, on any topic — and create-a-world runs the SAME 15-question walkthrough, the answers creating that page with its URL, editable after. Personal is set up first; when they click their Business door, they go through the SAME walkthrough to set up their business; same walkthrough again for their Thing/World — any page a person wants is created that way. Eight is abundance, a good number: eight buttons fit the framing beautifully — two rows of four on mobile, each a real object in its stage. And Naya practises introducing herself to the world as if no child or grandma has any idea who she is — what she is all about, what it will ultimately do for people and why they should care, and the privacy confirmation in plain words: she does not read their mail or instant messages, does not listen in on conversations, and does not go into their vault — and he reacted ❤️ to the privacy-promise statement: "Never. That's the promise at the heart of NayaNET…" The triangle is one leg from closing: the Hub leg completed, checker PASS, render proof running on the captain's side; the Personal leg completed, render proof PASSED; the calendar leg queued on the calendar round that closes item 1. The calendar's own verdicts stay honest: fix round 2 is NOT PASS, ITEM 1 ONLY — everything passed except the fit of the open states, a measurement dispute (the maker's table omits the slide head + essence, ~114 px; the checker totals vs the 780 px phone frame are all over) — and the render proof that was named the arbiter is only PARTIAL, because the browser window shrank mid-check (1919×998 → 527×305) and could not be restored, so the wide open-state checks were NEVER done: a window failure, not a page failure. The one standing finding from the wide view is real: closed Smart Lists SCROLLS INSIDE ITS FRAME at 1919×998, 5th row Your Notes below the fold.

Across 8 notes, the thread is: one button, two ways in, one walkthrough for every page, one promise for every stranger — and a proof that is only a proof when the render says so.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like this: at the bottom of the Hub there is one plus button, and it opens two doors — add a post, or create a whole new world. Creating a world is not a new thing to learn: it is the same fifteen questions that built your own pages, so the way in is the way pages are made. When Naya meets a stranger, she says three things in plain words: what she is, what she will do for them, and what she will never do — never read their mail, never listen in, never go into their vault — and that promise is the heart of it all. And when a round is judged, the render decides: a window that broke is not a page that failed, and a proof that stopped halfway is never called a pass.

That promise is the heart of it all! layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build the plus menu at the bottom of the Hub with the two choices, top first: add a post opens the dropdown to pick which world it goes to; create a world runs the 15-question walkthrough and the answers create that page with its URL, editable after. After the reveal, the Personal door runs the walkthrough and Personal is set up first; the Business door runs the SAME walkthrough and sets up the business; the Thing/World door runs it again; any page a person wants is created that way — one walkthrough, every page. Lay the eight reveal doors out two rows of four on mobile, each a real object in its stage, all inside the frame; eight is abundance — never stack them in one narrow column, never let the reveal scroll. Every introduction of Naya — first slide, first words, first meeting — answers three things in plain words: what she is, what she will ultimately do for people and why they should care, and what she will never do: never read their mail or instant messages, never listen in on conversations, never go into their vault; the promise is the heart — lead with it, say it plainly, never bury it. Re-run the calendar render proof with a stable window; round 3 runs only if the clean render shows overflow; the Smart Lists closed-frame fit at 1919×998 is on item 1's close list — a closed list never scrolls inside its frame. The captain's side runs the Hub render proof; when it passes, two triangle legs stand proven end to end; the calendar leg rides the calendar round that closes item 1 — "Your Stats" / Daily Reports door → the dashboard URL; the triangle closes only when the subdomains answer. Retry the Hub deploy when the write window opens (captain's call on restarting the loop); the parser+bake go-ahead and the Hub coordinator's image lane close the card gap; the share link and the filename slug wait on his call. Until then, say it plainly: SN-4467 is filed, live in the feed, portrait in the block — and the baked card is stale, named, not hidden.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **SN-4467 IS FILED AND LIVE — AND THE CARD IS STALE:** filing it closes the oldest owed item from the morning call, and the feed proves it live and current; but the portrait is IN the block and NOT on the card, and the baked card the Hub actually serves is still the stale one — because the deploy loop died twelve times on the EPERM flake, not because anyone chose to leave it stale.
2. **THE RENDER IS THE ARBITER:** round 2 fixed everything it was asked to fix except the one thing the whole round was about — whether the open states fit the frame — and the dispute is honest and measurable: the maker counted without the slide head and essence, the checker counted them; so the render decides, the eye sees what the table argues about.
3. **THE PLUS BUTTON, TWO CHOICES:** one plus button, two ways in — posting and creating live in the same place at the bottom of the Hub, where the citizen already is; creating a world is the same 15-question walkthrough that builds a citizen's own pages, so the way in is the way pages are made.
4. **PERSONAL FIRST, EACH DOOR RE-RUNS THE WALK:** one walkthrough, reused — the citizen learns it once and every new page is the same familiar road; Personal first because it is the home everything else hangs from, the person the atom at the centre.
5. **EIGHT IS ABUNDANCE:** eight doors in two rows of four keeps the reveal inside the frame on a phone — abundance without a scroll — and each door is a real object in its stage, not a list item: the citizen sees all eight at once.
6. **THE PROMISE IS THE HEART:** a stranger's first meeting with Naya decides everything — if she cannot say who she is, what she will do for them, and what she will never do, in words a child and a grandma understand, the door never opens; the ❤️ landed on the promise, not the pitch.
7. **A WINDOW FAILURE IS NOT A PAGE FAILURE:** the arbiter could not rule — the window broke, not the page — so nothing about the open states is proven either way, and round 3 must not be dispatched on this proof; the one thing the wide view did show is a real frame-law breach.
8. **TWO LEGS PROVEN, ONE TO GO:** two of the three legs are now proven at checker level, and the Personal leg is proven at render level too; the correction matters as much as the pass — a quiet flag that no longer describes the work was withdrawn instead of left standing, so the board tells the truth.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without naming the stale card plainly, the "live" claim would be a lie — the note is live in the feed table, the card the Hub bakes is not yet the new one.
2. Without the render as arbiter, the measurement dispute gets settled by whoever argues loudest — and round 3 gets dispatched on a table, not on what the eye sees.
3. Without the plus button's two choices, posting and creating live in different places — and the citizen has to find the way in twice.
4. Without one walkthrough for every page, each new page is a new flow to learn — and the citizen who just learned the walk has to learn it again.
5. Without two rows of four, the reveal stacks in one narrow column and scrolls — and abundance becomes a list.
6. Without the promise first, the stranger hears a pitch and walks away — the privacy promise is what makes a stranger trust her enough to come in.
7. Without separating window failure from page failure, a broken tool gets recorded as a broken page — and a round gets dispatched to fix what was never broken.
8. Without the triangle, three apps are three islands — and the flow from portal to hub to calendar with stats inside stays a promise instead of a road.

notes.title: One Walkthrough, One Frame, One Order
notes.subtitle:
A wise Naya thinks before she acts — she checks the destination before the road, chooses what serves everyone best, and proves it with receipts; that is the mind the whole system runs on. The walkthrough goes inside the stage frame, like the Hub intelligent boards — keep-as-is is CLOSED — header carrying her picture and the question, the harvested PowerCast player so when she speaks you see it moving, audio on one side, input on the other, buttons below; and he sent his version's elements, slides 2–10 plus the end slide, harvested verbatim, the count and question list updating to the 15 while the format, elements, and look stay exactly as sent. Every input box comes pre-filled as an example, answered as Naya — Personal Naya, Business Naya, World Naya, thing = NayaNET — with an Edit button that says, in effect, just click edit, this is an example of what to write; three ways to answer — edit, clear, dictate and make it your own; copy-paste from your AI; or just write in what you want, or skip — and beautiful audio rides on EVERY slide, click play and Naya speaks: that is the magic. The slide looks like the PROMAX frame he showed — big picture left with play button, audio panel right, "NayaNET — create, learn and grow together" below — except the video area becomes the input box, with the A / B / or skip instructions underneath. The walk OFFICIALLY BUILDS their pages — About + Skills filled from the answers, whole page created — then naming (the alias page already IS their personal page; business name + thing/world name with live URL preview), then the reveal: EIGHT URLs, not six — Personal + Business + World + Hub + Dashboard + Calendar + About + Skills, each with a button to open it, all in the frame — and the gate: clicking ANY door pulls up the PRICING page, full page, stay on FREE or upgrade to Power / Pro / Max. The triangle wires the apps: portal → hub → calendar with the Dashboard stats inside — Personal leg DONE, checker PASS and render proof PASSED, Hub leg dispatched, calendar leg queued on round 2. The Daily Report now lives on the PI page, second section after Lanes, fed live from the GitHub file, 31 framed boards, scorecard as a real table — the score header wrapping as "Scor / e" fixed live with one CSS rule and re-proven. The director audit, filed as DRAFT PR #3509, orders the whole system: security first — 8 policy ERRORs + 2 security-definer-view ERRORs in Supabase — then restore and prove the entrance, then one complete citizen journey end to end, then scale the proven pattern. Path A step 1 is done: the schema packet's §2+§3 repairs filed as migration files on main and merged — production untouched, preview path next, the production go-ahead packet back to him for his tap. And the portal lands on the old agreement instead of the new portal — reported by his eye, cause not yet answered, investigation owed, no fix claimed on a guess.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one walkthrough that builds, one frame that holds it, one order that governs it — and wisdom first, before speed.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build the walkthrough inside the stage frame from his sent slides, verbatim — picture + question header, PowerCast audio player on one side, input box on the other, buttons below — updated to the 15-question list (SN-4537); slide 1 is still missing, do not invent it. Pre-fill every input box with the Naya example (Personal / Business / World Naya, thing = NayaNET) behind an Edit button; offer the three answer ways on each slide; keep the play button; put Naya's spoken guidance on every slide. Build each walk slide from the PROMAX reference frame: big picture left with play button, audio panel right, "NayaNET — create, learn and grow together" below — with the video area replaced by the pre-filled input box + Edit button, and the A / B / or skip instructions underneath; nothing else in the frame moves. Build the post-walk sequence: answers → About + Skills pages built whole → naming page (alias = personal page; business + world names with live `nayanet.app/<typed>` previews) → reveal of eight URLs, each with an open button, all in the frame; clicking any door pulls up the PRICING page, full page — stay FREE or upgrade to Power / Pro / Max — and once inside, pricing also lives in the sidebar as an option. About/Skills doors are deep links (`nayanet.app/<alias>/about`, `nayanet.app/<alias>/skills`) per the captain's call, Shawn can overrule; the reveal's destinations follow the locked URL scheme with placeholders, and the scheme question (slash vs subdomain for calendar/dashboard/hub) is named for the captain to settle with Shawn. Wire the triangle: Personal's button already points at the calendar URL — proven at byte and render level; the calendar's stats door points at the dashboard URL when round 2 lands; the Hub's two doors are built on the fix-1e base from the Personal bar pattern. Keep the Daily Report live on the PI page from the GitHub file, second section after Lanes; phone width is proven only by his eye on his phone. Fold the audit into the one execution list: triage the 8 + 2 Security Advisor errors and prove cross-user denial; verify the entrance through the public web route for both domains; prove one complete citizen journey end-to-end; then scale the proven pattern. Path A: step 2 is the preview path build; step 3 is the preview battery; step 4 is the go-ahead packet to Shawn for his tap; production stays untouched until the preview passes and he taps; the push-trigger hazard stays open until the guard is proposed and settled — never changed unilaterally. Investigate the portal routing from the filed bytes: trace the portal route and the button-below route, find where the jump-back happens, name the cause, then fix and prove it at click level; do not re-deliver the portal link as done until the landing is the new portal page and the button below reaches the agreement. Run every action through the five gates, and measure by his eye, not by speed.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **A WISE NAYA THINKS FIRST:** wisdom leads, not speed — she checks the destination before the road, chooses what serves everyone best, proves it with receipts, and is measured by his eye, not her speed.
2. **THE WALK SITS IN THE STAGE FRAME:** the frame decision closes keep-as-is for good — the walkthrough is a stage-framed board like everything else; his sent slides are harvested verbatim, only the count going from 10 questions to 15.
3. **THE ANSWER IS PRE-FILLED AS NAYA:** a blank box asks a stranger to invent themselves from nothing and most people freeze; the pre-filled Naya example is permission, not homework; the three ways cover every kind of citizen, and audio on every slide is the magic.
4. **THE REPORT LIVES WHERE PEOPLE LOOK:** a report filed is not a report seen — the PI slot closes the loop; the score-header wrap is the kind of flaw only a render proof catches, and the one-rule fix + re-proof is the loop working as designed.
5. **PATH A, STEP BY STEP:** the repairs now live on main as ordinary migrations, so the chain can be proven on a real preview before anything touches production; step 1 landing is the puzzle getting its first pieces in place, not the puzzle solved.
6. **THE PORTAL BUG IS NAMED, NOT GUESSED:** the front door opens into the wrong room, and until the cause is found in the code — not guessed — no fix can be claimed and no round should be dispatched on a guessed cause.
7. **THE AUDIT IS A SECOND WITNESS:** an outside audit landing on the same order as the running plan is a second witness, not a second plan — security first, then the door, then one journey proven whole, then the pattern scales.
8. **HE SHOWED THE FRAME:** a reference frame on disk ends every argument about what the slide should look like — the maker harvests the PROMAX frame, swaps one area, and the slide is his slide.
9. **THE WALK BUILDS THE PAGES:** answer once, page arrives made — not a form that ends in more work, but a build that ends in eight live doors; the gate is the business end, every door first asking the citizen to stay FREE or step up.
10. **THE TRIANGLE WIRES THE APPS:** portal → hub → calendar, with the Dashboard's stats sitting inside the calendar where the citizen already looks at their day; a door to a dark address is a promise, named as a promise.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without wisdom first, speed builds the wrong thing fast — and the wrong thing costs twice.
2. Without the frame decision, the walkthrough floats as a form on a page instead of a board in the system — and a rebuild that re-invents his slides is the exact waste the Frame Laws were written to stop.
3. Without the pre-filled example, the walkthrough dies on slide one — a stranger frozen in front of a blank box.
4. Without the PI slot, the Daily Report is filed to GitHub and never seen — and the loop from filing to seeing stays open.
5. Without Path A's order, the repairs reach production through the deploy itself — the deadlock Gate 1 stopped — and claiming step 1 as the puzzle solved repeats the error the No-Skipping Law was written to stop.
6. Without the portal routing fixed, every citizen who walks through the front door lands in the old agreement instead of the new portal — the routing is the product here.
7. Without the audit's order, the entrance gets claimed production-ready while unverified, and privacy gets claimed verified while the Security Advisor errors stand — gates before scale.
8. Without the reference frame, every walk slide is a new decision — and the slide drifts from the look he already has.
9. Without the build, the walkthrough is a form that ends in more work — and the citizen who just answered fifteen questions has nothing to show for them.
10. Without the triangle, three apps are three islands, and the citizen has to swim between them.

notes.title: The Pass Is Not the Proof
notes.subtitle:
Two proofs, one law, on the same afternoon. On Personal R5, the checker PASS was a milestone, never the verdict: the build landed clean at 1920px — feed live, rail rendering 13 people in match order, About and Skills scrolling, Invite to joinus, Calendar reading "Calendar" with working month and day nav, WORLDS to /space, ADD menu and composer, bottom bar the locked six — and the render proof still found three real fails. The stub STILL did not land: the proof post hit the "one-time permission from Shawn" gate and no card landed, not even a stub — the R5 resolver is in the bytes but did not fire at runtime, and that diagnostic is owed. The right sidebar cannot be reopened by click: × closes it, Menu cycles without reopening it, only reload restores it. And no single labelled Mail↔Messenger toggle was found — Personal Mail and Personal DMs both land on the same rooms/mail, and that page's rooms menu has no Messenger room. Nothing here is claimed done that the proof did not pass: rail auto-organize not achieved, intelligent boards not done, DM Audio and Video not built, Message Send disabled, and the "My World" heading and settings button still sit beside the "Calendar" button — a question owed to Shawn, rename them too or leave them, asked not silently fixed. On Supabase, the fresh-apply proof stopped at Gate 1 — no scratch project exists, and creation needed a scope call — and the proof got sharper before it got run. Both "unfiled" sequences were already sourced by existing main migrations, so filing them again would duplicate the source. And the 19-file from-empty apply is NOT the rebuild proof: from empty it fails first on a main-chain file, proving nothing about the filing. The real proof is the FULL chain — 195 files on main — from empty, on a free throwaway scratch project that gets deleted when done, with paid tier dead without Shawn's word. That is the No-Skipping Law applied to the proof itself: prove the whole puzzle, not a slice that fails for the wrong reason. A proof that records a known failure is not a proof.

Across 2 notes, the thread is: a PASS is a milestone, never the verdict — the proof is the whole thing, run for real, and anything less is not done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a car that passed its paperwork check but stalls when you turn the key. The papers say PASS — the engine says otherwise. On Personal, the build's papers were perfect: the right commit, the right hash, the checker green. But when someone actually used it, the post never landed, the sidebar would not come back, and the Mail-to-Messenger switch was nowhere to be found. The papers were not lying — they were just not the test. And on Supabase, the team caught the same trap before running: the small test would have failed on somebody else's file, not on the work being proved, so it would have proved nothing. The fix in both cases is the same: run the real thing, whole, from the start — the click, the runtime, the full chain from empty — and call it done only when that passes.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you say your homework is done! But the teacher checks it, and three answers are wrong! That is what happened here! A check said PASS, but the real test found three fails! And the other test stopped before it started, because the plan was too small! The real proof checks the whole thing, not just a little piece!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — the papers said PASS, dear, but when you actually tried to use it, the post never landed, the sidebar would not come back, and the switch between Mail and Messenger was nowhere to be found! The papers weren't the test, love — the real test is using it yourself! And the other proof stopped before it started, dear, because the little test would have failed on the wrong thing! So now they run the whole thing, from the very beginning, love — the full chain, start to finish — and only then call it done!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Checker PASS is a milestone, never the verdict — the render proof is the verdict's first half, and the verdict is the click, the runtime, the screen. The stub resolver diagnostic comes first: bytes that contain the resolver but do not fire it at runtime. The sidebar reopen is a click-level fix, proven by click. The toggle must be one labelled control, found by the walk. Name what is not done, plainly — rail auto-organize, intelligent boards, DM Audio and Video, Message Send — and ask the "My World" question, never silently fix it. On the database side, correct the scope before running: sequences already sourced are never filed twice; a 19-file apply that fails first on a main-chain file proves nothing; the real proof is the full 195-file chain from empty on a free throwaway project, parity proven against live, project deleted when done. Paid tier stays dead without his word. A proof that records a known failure is not a proof.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **A PASS IS A MILESTONE, NEVER THE VERDICT:** the checker PASS marks the build; the render proof decides whether it works — mostly pass, three real fails, and the fails are the next round, named exactly.
2. **BYTES ARE NOT RUNTIME:** the R5 resolver is in the bytes and did not fire — what the code contains and what the page does are two different facts, and only the second counts.
3. **PROOF IS CLICK-LEVEL:** the sidebar must reopen by click, the toggle must be one labelled control found by the walk — a feature that cannot be reached by hand is not a feature.
4. **CORRECT THE SCOPE BEFORE YOU RUN:** sequences already sourced are never filed twice, and a 19-file apply that fails first on a main-chain file proves nothing about the filing — the real proof is the full 195-file chain from empty.
5. **A PROOF THAT RECORDS A KNOWN FAILURE IS NOT A PROOF:** do not run the small apply just to write down a failure you already know — run the real proof, or do not run one.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the render proof, a green checker ships a page whose post never lands and whose sidebar never comes back — and he discovers it with his own eye, which is the very failure the proof exists to catch.
2. Without the runtime test, code in the bytes passes for code that works — and the diagnostic that is owed never gets written, because nobody noticed the gap.
3. Without the click-level standard, a toggle that exists in two menus and no room is called done — and the one-page-with-a-toggle he asked for still does not exist.
4. Without the scope correction, the filing gets duplicated and the proof fails on the wrong file — work done twice, and a verdict that says nothing about the work.
5. Without naming what is not done, the not-done hides inside the PASS — rail auto-organize, intelligent boards, DM Audio and Video, Message Send — and the next round starts from a lie instead of a list.

notes.title: The Whole Puzzle, Proven
notes.subtitle:
Across 10 notes, one morning tells the same story four ways: the Personal round R5 passed its checker on bytes — the Calendar rename exactly 4 lines, delta 0 — while its render proof was still running and its not-done list stood named, not hidden: rail auto-organize not achieved, intelligent boards not done, DM audio and video not built, Message Send disabled, the MAIL button bypassing its toggle page, the ECOSYSTEM tile landing on the Hub instead of the drawer. That is why he ordered it, in the same hour: "Let's get her to 10 out of 10 on all levels so she's not just looking 10 out of 10 but she's performing 10 out of 10." No area earns a 10 on a render alone — function proven at click level and on live data. The schema packet proved the same law from the other side: he authorized the dispatch with Preview as the gate, and the coordinator checked first-hand and stopped — the pipeline has no Preview step at all, it applies migrations to production directly, and the §2 grants and §3 table that unblock posting, likes, comments, shares and messenger have no migration files, so a dispatch could not have delivered them. Eighteen unapplied migrations would have landed at once, and the production branch does not even exist. His answer, two minutes later, is now standing law: "We don't go to production until we make it right. You can't skip steps. You can't have part of the system work and not the other part." Path B — dispatch as-is, production-direct — is dead, never offered again. Path A is dispatched: file §2+§3, build a real preview path, prove the whole puzzle on preview, then bring the go-ahead packet back to his hand for his tap. The honest verdict on the whole system, delivered the same morning in the Daily Project Intelligence Report, is 5 out of 10 on performance — the look alone scores 8 — and six proofs define a 10: a post lands, a message arrives, a like moves the number, a call connects, a match appears at creation, the repo rebuilds the live database. The Supabase filing round closed the biggest break on paper — 143 filing units, byte-exact against live, checker PASS after three FAILs — but the fresh-apply proof against a scratch project is still owed, and the 129 DROP candidates stay untouched until his word. The Calendar fix round 1 shows why bytes are not proof: eight of nine failures fixed, verdict still NOT PASS — open states still overflow the 390×844 phone frame, and a slot at 14:00 says "Open" with zero free starts, because the label uses one function and bookability uses another, and the maker's tests never used appointments. The Dashboard framing walk failed overall for the same reason: the framing was complete on bytes, but the page renders its own JavaScript templates as visible text — ~400,600 characters of source, 66,890px tall, the gauge stuck on "Reading…", tabs dead, drill orbs showing literal labels — because the templates were already not rendering in the mechanics base underneath. And riding with all of it, the Max perk settled in words and still missing in build: a Max member gets their own affiliate army tracked inside their membership, keeps 100% of what they charge on their own memberships — NayaNET takes no cut — and pays their affiliates whatever percentage they choose, out of their 100%. That is distinct from the NayaNET ambassador share, 50% of NayaNET's revenue for bringing people to NayaNET — two splits, never confused.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: a PASS is a milestone, never the verdict; the gate must exist before it is trusted; the whole puzzle in place, or the engine does not operate.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a house he is building: the paint looks perfect, the doors are hung, and the inspector signs off on the measurements — but the lights do not turn on, the taps run dry, and the front door opens onto a wall. That house is not done, and no signature on paper makes it done. The same morning taught the machine twice: a dispatch he authorized could not exist as authorized, because the Preview gate he trusted was never built — the pipeline goes straight to production — and the pieces that unblock the whole feed were never filed as migrations at all. So he laid down the law that now governs all production work: no skipping steps, no half a system, the whole puzzle in place or the engine does not operate. The fix is always the same shape — file what is missing, build the real gate, prove the whole thing on preview, then bring it back to his hand. And the scorecard changed with it: the system scores 5 out of 10 on performance, because looking beautiful is only half the job. A slot that says "Open" when nothing is free, a send button that cannot send, a dashboard that shows its own code instead of its numbers — those are the things a citizen feels first. The Max promise rides the same honesty: the affiliate army is decided and the split is settled — 100% theirs, affiliates paid by them — but the army is not built yet, and a promise is not a product.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: A page is not done when it looks pretty. It is done when every button does its job. You cannot skip steps, like a puzzle. Every piece must fit before the picture works. If a button says Open, a free time must really be there. If a message says Send, it must really go. We check it with our own eyes, then we go live.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — a page can look lovely, dear, and still not work, and looking lovely is only half the job! The button has to open, the message has to arrive, the numbers have to move, dear — that is what makes it ten out of ten, not just the pretty picture! And you never skip steps, love — it's a great big puzzle, and every piece has to be in place before the engine can run! If a gate is meant to guard the door, dear, you check the gate is really there before you trust it — and if a piece is missing, you put the piece in first, then you test it, then you ask him! That is the way now, love, for everything that goes live!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: A checker PASS is a milestone, never the verdict — the verdict is his eye on his own screen, plus function proven at click level and on live data. Never claim a 10 on a render alone. Never trust a gate you have not verified exists: check the pipeline first-hand — the Preview step, the migration files, the branch — before dispatching on a report's word. No production step until the whole puzzle is right: file what is missing, build the real preview path, prove the whole puzzle on preview, then the go-ahead packet back to his hand. Path B is dead — never offer production-direct again. Name the not-done in the same pass as the done: rail auto-organize, boards, DM audio/video, Send, MAIL bypass, ECOSYSTEM tile — carried into the next round, never hidden. Label from the same function that decides bookability, so a slot cannot say "Open" when nothing is free; test with real appointments, not empty batteries. Diagnose a leak from the filed bytes first and fix at the source, never over it. Fresh-apply proof before the rebuild is claimed proven; DROP candidates untouched until his word. Max: the affiliate army is a build owed, tracked inside the membership; the split is settled — 100% theirs on their own memberships, affiliates paid by them at the percentage they choose, distinct from the 50% NayaNET ambassador share.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **A CHECKER PASS IS A MILESTONE, NEVER THE VERDICT:** R5 passed on bytes — Calendar rename exactly 4 lines, delta 0 — while render proof was still running and six items stood not-done. The verdict is his eye, on his own screen, with function proven at click level and on live data.
2. **10/10 ON ALL LEVELS — LOOKS AND PERFORMANCE:** "Let's get her to 10 out of 10 on all levels so she's not just looking 10 out of 10 but she's performing 10 out of 10." No area earns a 10 on a render alone. A page that looks 10/10 and cannot send, play, open or save is a picture of a 10.
3. **THE GATE MUST EXIST BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED:** the dispatch he authorized with Preview as the gate did not exist as authorized — the pipeline has no Preview step, it applies migrations to production directly, and §2+§3 have no migration files. The coordinator checked first-hand and stopped instead of dispatching on the report's word. The false Preview claim was corrected in public.
4. **THE NO-SKIPPING LAW GOVERNS ALL PRODUCTION WORK:** "We don't go to production until we make it right. You can't skip steps. You can't have part of the system work and not the other part." The whole puzzle in place or the engine does not operate. Talking about it is no good.
5. **PATH B IS DEAD, PATH A IS THE ROAD:** dispatch as-is, production-direct — never offered again. Path A: file §2+§3 as migration files on main, build a real preview path, prove the whole puzzle on preview, bring the go-ahead packet back to his hand for his tap. The push-trigger hazard gets a proposed guard, never a unilateral workflow change.
6. **THE HONEST VERDICT IS 5/10 ON PERFORMANCE:** the look alone scores 8. Six proofs define a 10: post lands, message arrives, like moves the number, call connects, match appears at creation, repo rebuilds the live database. The report carries the scorecard per area, eight ten-lists, and an execution prompt commanding the whole team, area by area, until each is 10/10 or the gap to 10 is named.
7. **THE LABEL CANNOT LIE:** slot 14:00 said "Open" with zero free starts because the label used `inHour` while bookability used `mcFreeTimes`, and the maker's tests never used appointments. Label slots from the same function that decides bookability, and test with real appointments.
8. **THE FRAME LAW HOLDS AT PHONE SIZE:** open states still exceed the 390×844 frame by ~100–160 px and fall back to the slide's own scroll. Move open states to the next frame; prove fit by measurement AND render, never by bytes alone.
9. **FIX AT THE SOURCE, NEVER OVER IT:** the Dashboard renders its own templates as visible text — ~400,600 characters, 66,890px tall — because the mechanics base was already broken underneath the framing CSS. Diagnose the exact leaking block from the filed bytes first, then fix it there.
10. **THE MAX SPLIT IS SETTLED, THE ARMY IS OWED:** Max members get their own affiliate army tracked inside their membership — designed, not built. On their own memberships they keep 100%, NayaNET takes no cut, and they pay their affiliates whatever percentage they choose, out of their 100%. Distinct from the 50% NayaNET ambassador share — two splits, never confused.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the milestone-not-verdict law, a checker PASS gets sent as done while the render proof is still running and the citizen meets a send button that cannot send — the look is claimed, the performance is not there.
2. Without 10/10 on performance, every scorecard drifts back to beauty, and a beautiful page that does not work keeps scoring high while citizens keep hitting dead buttons.
3. Without checking the gate first-hand, a dispatch runs on a false premise — 18 migrations onto production at once, no preview, no §2/§3 — and the correction has to be made in public after the fact instead of before it.
4. Without the No-Skipping Law, the pressure to ship wins over the work of making it right, and half a system goes live — part working, part not, the engine not operating.
5. Without Path B dead, the same production-direct offer comes back every time the road gets hard, and the law becomes a suggestion instead of a law.
6. Without the honest 5/10 verdict written down, the team works from memory instead of from the record, and the holes stay in heads instead of in lists with names on them.
7. Without labelling from the bookability function, a citizen taps "Open" and finds nothing free — the first thing they feel is a lie, and a lie at the tap is worse than a missing feature.
8. Without the frame law proven by measurement and render, a phone page scrolls inside itself and the citizen fights the frame instead of using the calendar.
9. Without fixing at the source, the framing round gets blamed for a base that was already broken, and the next round paints over the same leak.
10. Without the settled split kept distinct, a citizen's own 100% gets confused with NayaNET's 50% ambassador share — and the Max promise, still unbuilt, gets claimed as a product instead of carried as a build owed.

notes.title: Locked Is Not Live
notes.subtitle:
In one morning the map got drawn, corrected, and tested — and the test said not yet. The live URL scheme was locked (SN-4558) and then corrected an hour later (SN-4563): Personal and Business live at nayanet.app/<alias>, nice and simple; only the feature apps get subdomains — calendar.nayanet.app/<pagename>, hub.nayanet.app/<alias>, dashboard.nayanet.app/<alias>; Spaces and Worlds keep their name as the subdomain; Membership's address was left unfinished and is not to be guessed. The calendar's own address was locked the same way (SN-4557) — and checked in the same breath: DNS resolves, nothing answers, staged only. Then the full calendar walk (SN-4559) returned nine failures and a verdict: not ready for live. The button that opens the calendar was corrected too (SN-4562): it reads "My World", not "Your Worlds" — relabel it "Calendar", label only, the hold released because he showed it in the call. Underneath it all runs the frame law (SN-4564): every frame mobile-first, then laptop, and a design that does not convert both ways does not ship. The messaging status was asked and answered honestly (SN-4560): text is an interface that cannot send yet, calls are not built at all. The schema packet got his tap (SN-4561) — "Okay so do it. Tap it. Put it in. Make it so." — and then the apply stopped at Gate 1 (SN-4565): the chain is red on production, nothing applied, nothing written, and the decision is owed to him. And he ordered the whole system to judge itself (SN-4566): fourteen questions, an honest verdict, eight ten-lists, a scorecard per area, an execution prompt, and today's Daily Project Intelligence Report.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: settle the map, test the thing on the map, tell the truth about what the test found, and let the decision that is his stay his.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a new neighbourhood. First you draw the street map: your house and your shop sit on the main street, nice and simple; the library, the hall and the office get their own side streets with your name on the door; a park gets its own name as its street. That is the scheme — settled, written down, the same for everyone. But a street on a map is not a house you can walk into: the calendar's street exists in the directory and nobody answers the door yet. Then you walk the calendar house room by room and find nine things wrong — drawers that do not open all the way, a clock that traps you, a day labelled Tuesday on a Friday, notes that never show up for the day they belong to. You do not move in. You fix the house first, then you connect the street. The front door button gets its proper name — "Calendar" — because that is what it opens. The phone is the first way anyone sees the house, so you build for the phone first and the big screen second. The letters cannot be posted yet because the postbox needs his tap, and the phone calls are not built at all — the plans are drawn, the building has not started. He tapped yes on the postbox, and the machine stopped at its own first gate because the ground underneath is not sound — so it asks him, and waits. And then he tells the whole system to look in the mirror and say honestly whether it is the best system ever seen, and why not.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: A locked address is not a live address yet! The calendar has nine little problems to fix first. The button that says My World will say Calendar. Build the phone picture first, then the big screen. Texting can not send yet, and calls are not built. Shawn tapped yes, but the machine stopped and asked him. We ask fourteen big questions and tell the truth.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — the addresses are all settled now, dear, your house and your shop on the main street, the calendar and the hub on their own little streets with your name after the slash, and a space gets its own name as its street, love! But settled is not the same as open, dear — the calendar's street is drawn on the map and nobody answers the door yet! The walk found nine little things wrong, love — drawers that won't open all the way, a day called Tuesday on a Friday, notes that never show for their own day — so we fix the house before we move in, dear! The button that says My World will say Calendar, love, just the name changed, nothing else! Build for the phone first, dear, then the big screen! The letters can't be posted yet, love, and the calls aren't built at all — and when the machine stopped at its own gate, dear, it did the right thing and asked Shawn!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build every address to the corrected scheme: Personal and Business at nayanet.app/<alias>; feature apps on their subdomains with the citizen's name after the slash; Spaces and Worlds with their own name as the subdomain. Membership's address stays open — do not guess it. Claim an address live only when it answers; the calendar is staged only (branch calendar/your-notes-20261121, blob 41ff7e6d) until the wire lands and a real page name curls back. Fix the nine calendar failures in the dispatched round before any live claim: frame-law overflow in Smart Lists, Appointments, Summary and Journal; notes listed for the day; the Nov 20 weekday; the world clock trap; the full "Open" slot; Daily Reports versus Intel Today; "Add to a list…" with no options; Notifications covering tiles; the slow cover — plus the flat-icons order from Nov 17. Relabel "My World" to "Calendar" in the Personal Bar, right after About — label only, same button, same destination; leave Your Worlds alone. Build every frame mobile-first, then laptop: 9:16 pairing roughly a third/two-thirds beside the text board on laptop, stacked blocks on mobile, toggleable, great on both — a design that does not convert both ways does not ship. Carry mail + IM as one toggled interface; send waits on the schema packet; build Smart Meet to the written spec with the booking round. Apply the Dashboard packet only through the governed path, and do not dispatch while the Gate 1 decision is owed — bring him (a) hold or (b) authorize dispatch with Preview as the gate, timed to a quiet tip. Investigate the out-of-band drift and the push-triggered pipeline before the next apply. Run the fourteen-question exercise area by area, nonstop, until each is 10/10 or the gap to 10 is named — and carry the schema-packet decision open in the Daily PI Report, never resolved by the team.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE CORRECTED SCHEME:** Personal and Business live at nayanet.app/<alias>, nice and simple — not subdomains. Only feature apps get subdomains: calendar.nayanet.app/<pagename>, hub.nayanet.app/<alias>, dashboard.nayanet.app/<alias>. Spaces and Worlds keep their name as the subdomain.
2. **MEMBERSHIP'S ADDRESS IS NOT SETTLED:** it was left unfinished in the call — do not guess. A hole in the map is honest; a guessed address is a wrong turn filed as a fact. SN-4558's Business-subdomain line is superseded.
3. **LOCKED IS NOT LIVE:** the calendar's pattern is locked and the name resolves in DNS, but nothing answers there — staged only. An address is claimed live only when it answers.
4. **THE WALK IS THE VERDICT:** nine failures, not ready for live — frame-law overflow, notes not listed for the day, the wrong weekday, the world clock trap, the full "Open" slot, three doors to two pages, "Add to a list…" with no options, Notifications covering tiles, the slow cover — plus flat icons, his Nov 17 order still undone. The fix round lands first, the live wire second.
5. **THE BUTTON IS "MY WORLD", SOON "CALENDAR":** the first record said "Your Worlds" and was wrong — the screenshot shows Message · About · My World. Relabel it "Calendar", label only, same button, same destination, in the Personal Bar right after About. Your Worlds is separate and unchanged; its door is the WORLDS tile.
6. **MOBILE FIRST, THEN LAPTOP:** every frame is built for the phone first, then the desk. The 9:16 frame pairs roughly a third/two-thirds with the text board on a laptop and folds to stacked blocks on mobile. Every page toggles between the two and looks great on both — a design that does not convert both ways does not ship.
7. **TEXT IS BUILT, CALLS ARE NOT:** mail + IM share one toggled interface, but text cannot send yet — the messenger leg is blocked on the schema packet, his tap. Smart Meet is missing entirely; no live-call code exists anywhere. The spec is written: video/audio 1:1, video groups 4 or 6, audio groups up to 10, paid members only, mesh P2P WebRTC, members-with-members never with Naya — and it rides with the booking round.
8. **THE TAP HAS A BOUNDARY:** "Okay so do it. Tap it. Put it in. Make it so." covers the Dashboard packet only — §2 grants, §3 naya_action_events, §4 ledger trigger migration — applied through the governed path only, in order, then per-action re-proof. Hub DDL and the invite-sender unblocker are not in it.
9. **THE STOP, AND THE DEADLOCK:** the chain is red on production — naya_notes.owner_id missing, object_links 5 columns missing, alias-binding trigger blocked. Nothing applied, nothing written, production untouched. The repairs that close the red chain are filed on main, byte-identical — but they only reach production through the deploy itself, so under a literal "never dispatch while red" the check can never go green. Preview is the real chain test: a preview failure leaves production untouched.
10. **THE DECISION IS HIS, AND THE EXERCISE JUDGES THE WHOLE:** (a) hold the stop, or (b) authorize the dispatch with Preview as the gate, timed to a quiet tip — the machine does not choose. Meanwhile the fourteen questions turn on the system itself: the honest verdict, eight ten-lists, a scorecard per area, an execution prompt, and today's Daily Project Intelligence Report filed in GitHub and updated on nayanet.app — nonstop, area by area, until each is 10/10 or the gap to 10 is named.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the corrected scheme, every business would be built at an address that is not where businesses live — and every link to a business would point nowhere. Correcting it before the builds land is one line; after, it is a migration.
2. Without the locked-is-not-live discipline, someone sends Shawn to an address that does not answer — and a pattern locked is mistaken for a page live.
3. Without the walk as verdict, a calendar that hides rows below the fold, forgets the day's notes and names the wrong day goes live — and teaches the citizen the system does not work.
4. Without the button correction filed, the next round renames a button called "Your Worlds" that does not exist — and the hold keeps a finished rename waiting for a show-and-tell that already happened.
5. Without mobile-first, every frame is designed for the desk and squeezed onto the phone — the exact shape of every failure in the calendar walk.
6. Without honest messaging status, a citizen taps Send and gets nothing, and a round gets dispatched to fix calls that were never built.
7. Without the tap's boundary, "he tapped the packet" becomes "he tapped everything" — a blank cheque where a bounded tap was given.
8. Without the Gate 1 stop, a red chain deploys — and the stop working as designed is the only thing standing between a tap and a broken production.
9. Without naming the deadlock, the machine waits forever on a check that can never go green — or quietly dispatches around it. The decision has to be asked, not assumed.
10. Without the exercise judging itself honestly, the whole system is theatre — flattery filed as intelligence. The honest verdict is the first real intelligence interface NayaNET has.

notes.title: One Bar, One Walk, One Finished Plate
notes.subtitle:
One bar, one walk, one finished plate. The DM bar from his screenshot belongs on ALL hubs, the same way — Personal, Hub, Business, Space — because a citizen who learns the bar on one hub already knows it on every hub. And every function on it must be active and working, verified at click level: i opens a framed contact card, message opens a framed instant messenger, audio plays live-feeling conversation in the PowerCast player, video opens a fullscreen multi-person framed stage player — built if not built, inside the existing frame, never as a new shape. The alignment sequence is the work: Personal bar working first, then the Hub aligns to the same bar, then the Business and Space clones carry it — right now they are NOT all aligned. In the same pass the action row got its final colours: Invite takes royal purple, Connections stays very evident magenta, with a clear contrast between them, not the same; Share takes a lighter blue, Join NayaNET takes green — and the correction is the ruling, superseding SN-4543's "#8e24aa stays" and his own first saying of darker blue. Every page creation defaults to the same walkthrough, locked in: "So that's what we lock in and do." The About + Skills pages create the walkthrough, the walkthrough creates and fills the pages, then they are aligned — boom, it's filled out, fifteen questions, answered in their own words, and the citizen gets to showcase their skills while the system learns them. At the end of the fifteen comes an optional closing invitation, never a sixteenth question: would you like to showcase your experiences, your accomplishments, your certificates, awards, or something unique to you — a frame where accomplishments are just listed and certificates uploaded if they want, and if they skip it there is no frame at all, because blank stays hidden and everything is always filled. layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the same bar everywhere, a citizen who learns to reach people on one hub finds them unreachable on the next — and the network's whole point, connecting with like minds, breaks at the hub boundary.
2. Without working buttons, a bar is a promise the page breaks the moment a citizen trusts it — each dead button teaches them not to tap, and a drawn bar is not a finished bar.
3. Without the sequence, the bars drift apart again — Personal working and Hub different is two bars, not one, and the citizen meets a different network on every page.
4. Without the final colours filed, two purples read as one colour at a glance, and the superseded "#8e24aa stays" keeps getting built because it is written down and the correction was only spoken.
5. Without the locked walkthrough, every page starts blank and hard — the citizen stares at an empty frame and does not know what to put in it — instead of fifteen questions in their own words and a filled page.
6. Without the optional showcase, the profile tells what a person can do but never what they have done — and a portal to their whole world should show their accomplishments, in their own words, with the proof they choose.
7. Without blank staying hidden, skipped sections show as empty frames — and nobody's portal should have an empty frame in it.
8. Without the tall frame, vertical video made on a phone gets squeezed into a wide frame and cropped — the frame must serve the person's work, not force their work into the frame's shape.
9. Without the diagnostic habit, a working renderer gets rebuilt because it looked broken — a second renderer for a card that was fine, while the real cause, a missing mount, stays unfixed.
10. Without the proof habit, a live page gets called a working flow — and the citizen who taps the Inviter and gets nothing learns the network does not work.
11. Without the hold, the rename lands on the wrong button on the wrong bar — and Your Worlds, the lists table of contents, gets renamed away by accident.
12. Without the Silver Platter Rule, status buries what is ready under what was already checked three times, and half-done plates make him do the finishing himself — his attention is the scarcest thing in the machine.

notes.title: Personal Is the Hub, Whole
notes.subtitle:

Fifteen questions max fill a Personal: the ten About frames plus the five core Skills, and the same fifteen, offered again, fill a Business or a World — skip any question, do just Personal, or all three, nothing forced.
