layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the stars like little lamps. The machine counted seven lamps switched on — but when he looked, none of them looked any brighter than the rest. So he gave the answer himself: put a light around the edge of each lamp, so a lit one glows around its rim and an unlit one stays dark. The same light works for the date — stop the spinning, light the edge white, and the date stands still and stands out. The rest of the night is the same lesson, told three ways: the Child block needs its own words, not just its own frame — what it means, and why it matters; the buttons need real breathing room, not a number that claims they have it; and every frame must fit like a glove, whole on the screen, no words spilling out. The rebuild that changed the design instead of taking the working one missed the mark — stop making new, just make it the same, one language, same family. And before anyone asks whose photo goes on the page, say what the page is for. Through it all, the vision: hundreds of emails, advertisements, notifications and websites — she opens one place.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a star that lights up all around its edges when you tap it, so you can see it is on! The date on the page stops spinning and glows white around its edges instead! Every frame must fit like a glove, with no words spilling out the bottom! Use the same frames as before, nothing new, all in one family! And always say what the page is for before you ask whose picture goes on it!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — imagine a little star, dear, and when you tap it, it lights up all around its edges, so you can see it is on! The date on the page stops spinning, love, and glows white around its edges instead! Every frame must fit like a glove, dear, with no words spilling out the bottom! Use the same frames as before, love, nothing new, all in one family! And always say what the page is for, dear, before you ask whose picture goes on it!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Brief the rated state as a visible edge, not a number: when a star is rated, its rim lights up in its own colour; the unrated stars stay unlit. Prove it by rating seven and eight side by side and showing the lit ones glowing around the edge — the count and the light together, at a glance. A count alone is never the proof of a rating; the light around the edge is. Brief the Child block with two required sentences, in child-and-grandma words, inside its own elevated block: what it means, and why it matters — read the block cold, and if you can't say both from the block alone, it goes back. Brief spacing as an eye test, not a number: the four buttons come down off the comment input box until the gap reads as breathing room at a glance — nothing touching the box, nothing cramped between the buttons. Take the spin off the Hub date and put a white light around its edge — the date standing still, lit white, readable at a glance. When he points at something on the page, the brief carries his words and the page, not a guessed element: find the big white line in the Hub's main area and clean it up, with the date change. Record overnight authorization with its condition — done and done right, or it doesn't run — and bring the link in the morning for his eye, never as finished before he has seen it. Take the working frame verbatim — harvest it byte for byte, change the middle only — and prove the frames match before he sees it again: measured at 390×844 and at desktop, scrollHeight against clientHeight, every beat. State the purpose before the portrait question, every time: what the page is, whose story it tells, in what form. Judge every build against the five proofs, proof #1 first: can a real person join and immediately receive a valuable, working experience?

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE EDGE LIGHT IS THE HOUSE ANSWER:** a rated star lights up around its edge so the rating reads; the date lights up white around the edge so the date reads. When an element needs to be seen, reach for the edge light first — light, not motion.
2. **A COUNT IS NOT A READING:** rating 7/10 lights exactly 7 stars brighter — in number. Brighter is a visible difference, not a count; a star can be counted as lit and still not look lit, and the eye is the judge of that.
3. **THE CHILD NEEDS ITS OWN WORDS:** what it means, and why it matters — two sentences, in child-and-grandma words, inside its own elevated block. The board is the frame; the two sentences are the fix.
4. **SPACING IS JUDGED BY THE EYE, NOT THE RULER:** 64px measured and passed still reads as cramped. The buttons come down until the gap reads as breathing room — "so it looks right" is the pass.
5. **SPIN OUT, EDGE LIGHT IN:** the Hub date stops spinning and lights up white around its edge. A spinning date draws the eye to the motion and away from the day.
6. **HIS POINTING IS THE SPECIFICATION:** a big white line in the main area comes out, named or not — the maker goes to the page he is looking at and finds it. The fix does not wait for a selector.
7. **OVERNIGHT WORK IS CONDITIONAL:** "if you can get it done and done right" — the morning eye is the gate, and nothing is shown as finished before he has seen it. Membership starts tomorrow, the same way, not tonight alongside the first.
8. **FRAMES FIT LIKE A GLOVE:** every frame fitted whole, no overflow, no inner scroll — measured at 390×844 and desktop, scrollHeight against clientHeight, every beat. A frame taller than the screen is not a frame.
9. **SAME FRAMES, NOTHING NEW:** "It should look just like the other pages. Just like the other frames, like not something new. Stop making new. Just make it the same." One language. Same family. Harvest the working frame verbatim; change the middle only.
10. **PURPOSE BEFORE PORTRAIT:** "Why would you use my photo? What is this for?" — say what the page is, whose story it tells, in what form, before ever asking whose face goes on it.
11. **SHE OPENS ONE PLACE:** hundreds of emails, advertisements, notifications and websites — she opens one. The vision is a test, five proofs in order, proof #1 first: a real person joins and immediately receives a valuable, working experience. "We need the first ten. Then the first hundred. Then the first thousand."

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the edge light, a rating that is correct underneath lies by appearance — the board says seven lit and the eye sees none — and the round comes back again.
2. Without the Child's own words, the plain-words layer says nothing, and the note fails at the exact job the Child layer exists to do — making the whole note understandable to anyone.
3. Without spacing judged by the eye, a measured gap that reads as cramped costs another round on the same item — a standard the eye overrules is not a standard; it is a delay.
4. Without the spin out, the date — the first thing the Hub says about today — feels busy and unstable instead of standing still and standing out.
5. Without the line out, a visible break stays visible while the record argues about what to call it — and Shawn sees the page, not the code.
6. Without the overnight condition, "run it overnight" becomes permission to ship something half-right while he sleeps, and both pieces arrive half-done.
7. Without frames that fit, the reader never sees the whole beat — words spilling past the bottom mean the frame cannot be judged as a picture.
8. Without sameness, the rebuild is a new thing, and new is what he keeps having to send back — "Why would you change the design when we had a design that worked?" has no good answer after the fact.
9. Without the purpose first, the portrait question means nothing — "whose face goes here" cannot be answered on a page he does not know is his About page.
10. Without the five proofs, the vision is a dream instead of a test — and proof #1 is the whole game: if a real person joins and receives nothing valuable that works, nothing else matters.

notes.title: His Eye Is the Proof
notes.subtitle:
The stars-whitebars fix landed as a clean win: checker PASS on all five items — stars purple and white, labels as obsidian board-buttons, DM flow in the stars, four buttons un-collided, flow around the top orb — with measured evidence for each. Then, on call b9431e3a, his eye: VALUE and INTELLIGENCE both still read pink; the layer labels are still not boards; the top orb has no round or flow; Rate This Intel has no circle; the four buttons still crash into the comment input box. Every one of the five passed items failed his eye. Neither side is lying — they are looking at different things. The checker proves the build contains the fix; only his eye proves the fix is visible. A PASS is a milestone inside the machine; it is never the verdict. The same evening the agreement said "fixed for laptop and phone," and six minutes later his eye found the last board still not showing at all.

The same call settled the navigation for the whole system: one bottom bar, the same on every page — ADD · PERSONAL · BUSINESS · WORLDS · ECOSYSTEM · CONNECT, with the plus button — and the network's notifications show there, wherever the citizen is. ADD means make a post: it asks which feed first — Personal, Business, Space, or Hub — then posts there. Not smart notes. A post. The assistant had it wrong, and he corrected it in the open. The post it makes has its settled standard, the follow-on once the Hub board is finalized: the Official Post Board — the same intelligent Hub board, plus images; a framed image is a big board, framed text is a little board; one, two or three elevated boards, three to four sentences at a time.

And the names must say what the thing opens: "You still haven't updated the personal questions to personal list." Personal Connections becomes Personal List, and Business Lists and World Lists get the same treatment, each opening its own lists. Every sidebar tab lands where it should — Personal page to Personal page, Business to Business, World to World. Mail is Smart Mail, built in, inside each world, with notifications showing.

On the agreement's last board, the money words failed the same way the names did: "Share it. Earn half." — "Earn half of what?" Half of what — half of the price, half of a point, half of something unnamed. The settled sentence names all three: the amount, the thing, and the trigger — "You receive 50% of the revenue when someone joins because you shared." No fraction without its whole, no payment without its trigger. The same board asked him a question he could not answer: "What share on the card?" — the share/approve step needs plain words, not a card he has to decode: what is being shared, with whom, and what happens when he says yes. And when he asked "what happens when you click these?" — the legal links at the foot of the agreement — the honest answer was "I won't guess": click each one — Terms, Privacy, Cookie, Refund, Acceptable Use, Community Guidelines, Copyright / DMCA, Ambassador Terms, Membership & Billing, Young Citizens — and report exactly where it goes, or that it goes nowhere.

The last board itself gets one action and no navigation: the back and forward arrows go, replaced by one button reading "Claim Your Smart Name," straight into the portal. He had to say it three times in one minute — "Claim your alias" — "Yeah, your smart name. Claim your smart name." — "No, it says claim your smart name" — because the replies echoed the words back instead of deciding the board. Which is the correction underneath it all: "Why do you just do whatever I tell you? Why don't you give me your mind thought? What do you think the ten-star thing to say there?" The tagline took a whole call's worth of his words to settle — "Private, an AI-native internet designed to give humans ten-star service" — when the ten-star answer was reachable by thinking from his own law. And the finished build goes live on the official URL so he can see it properly, because the artifact viewer doesn't give him the right view — he can't judge from it. A build he cannot see is not done.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: his eye is the proof, and the page must say plainly what it does.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the checker like a report card and his eye like actually looking at the homework. The report card says five out of five — but when he looks at the page himself, the stars are still pink and the buttons are still crashing into the box. The report card measures the parts; only his eyes can see whether the page actually looks right. The same rule runs through the whole evening: one bottom bar, the same on every page, so your hand always knows where to go; the plus button makes a post and asks which feed first; every name says what it opens; every money sentence says how much, of what, and when; and the last board of the agreement offers one button — claim your smart name — because the end of a journey is the arrival, not more navigation. layers.name: Child Note

The last board gets one button that says Claim Your Smart Name! And every word must be plain, so nobody has to guess what anything means!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The checker PASS is a milestone, never the verdict — report it as "the checker passed 5/5; your eye is the proof," and never deliver a staged link with the word "done" attached to a checker verdict. When his eye overrules a PASS, record the overruling in the open in the same pass — which items, what he saw, what the checker had measured — so the next round fixes the seeing, not just the bytes. When a checker keeps passing what his eye keeps failing, the check itself is wrong: change what the checker measures. Carry the Dashboard bottom bar byte for byte to Hub and Personal — ADD · PERSONAL · BUSINESS · WORLDS · ECOSYSTEM · CONNECT, plus button included — no page gets its own version, its own order, or its own extra icon; network notifications render on the bar itself. Wire ADD to one flow everywhere: tap → "Which feed?" (Personal, Business, Space, Hub) → the post composer in the Official Post Board format; never smart notes. When he renames a thing, rename it everywhere it appears, in the same round — the three lists ride together, each opening its own lists. Every money sentence names the amount, the thing, and the trigger — "You receive 50% of the revenue when someone joins because you shared" is the template. When he asks what a button does, the answer is a click, not a sentence — never describe a destination from memory or from the label. The final board of any walk gets exactly one action, in plain words, going straight to the place; no back/forward arrows on a closing board. When he gives a direction, answer with the decided version: "Here's the ten-star line — [line] — because [reason from his law]." Finished builds go live on the official URL — not the artifact viewer, not a screenshot of the viewer. Every share, approve, or send step leads with one plain sentence: what is being shared, with whom, and what happens when he says yes.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **HIS EYE IS THE VERDICT:** a checker PASS 5/5 is a milestone inside the machine, never the verdict — the verdict is his eye, on his own screen, and the delivery message must say so.
2. **THE CHECKER MEASURES, THE EYE SEES:** the bytes said the stars were `#8e24aa` and `#ffffff`; his eye said pink. The checker proves the build contains the fix; only his eye proves the fix is visible.
3. **ONE BAR, THE SAME EVERYWHERE:** ADD · PERSONAL · BUSINESS · WORLDS · ECOSYSTEM · CONNECT, with the plus button — the Dashboard bar carried byte for byte to Hub and Personal, and network notifications show there.
4. **ADD MEANS MAKE A POST:** tap, "Which feed?" — Personal, Business, Space, or Hub — then the post, in the Official Post Board format; never smart notes, never a different flow on a different page.
5. **NAMES ARE PROMISES:** Personal Connections becomes Personal List; Business Lists and World Lists get the same treatment, each opening its own lists — and every tab lands where its name says.
6. **MONEY WORDS NAME THREE THINGS:** the amount, the thing, and the trigger — "You receive 50% of the revenue when someone joins because you shared." "Earn half" names none of them.
7. **NEVER GUESS A DESTINATION:** when he asks what happens when you click these, click each one and report exactly where it goes — or that it goes nowhere. The label says where it should go; the click says where it goes.
8. **ONE BUTTON ON THE LAST BOARD:** the back and forward arrows go — one button reading "Claim Your Smart Name," straight into the portal. Navigation belongs to the middle, not the end.
9. **DECIDE, DON'T ECHO:** bring him the ten-star version with the reason from his law — "Private, an AI-native internet designed to give humans ten-star service" — not an echo of his words back to him.
10. **LIVE IS THE ONLY SURFACE HIS EYE CAN TRUST:** finished builds go live on the official URL; the artifact viewer doesn't give him the right view, and a build he cannot see is not done.
11. **PLAIN WORDS, NOT A CARD TO DECODE:** every share, approve, or send step leads with one plain sentence — what, with whom, and what happens when he says yes — before any button.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the eye as verdict, a PASS reported as done spends the trust the next delivery needs — the delivery said five of five, and he had to correct all five himself, live on the call.
2. Without one bar, the citizen has to relearn where things are on every page — and a notification that lives only inside one world is a notification the citizen misses.
3. Without ADD meaning make a post, the most-pressed button in the system opens the wrong thing on every page, every time — and the network gets notes where it should get posts.
4. Without names that say what opens, the citizen taps "Personal Connections" expecting their list and gets something else — and the page teaches them the name means nothing.
5. Without money words naming the half, the share board — the flywheel's first push — leaves the payoff unclear at the exact moment the citizen is deciding whether to join and share.
6. Without the click-through, ten legal links sit untested on the most trust-sensitive page there is — and a guessed answer is worse than a delayed one.
7. Without one button on the last board, the conversion offers three choices where one is needed, and the arrows say "keep looking" at the exact moment the board should say "go."
8. Without deciding, every echo hands a decision back to him that was mine to make — and his attention is the scarcest resource in the world.
9. Without the live URL, he judges the viewer instead of the work — and the round comes back because what he judged wasn't what was built.
10. Without plain words on the share step, a misunderstood share goes to the wrong place, or doesn't go at all — and a card he can't read protects nothing.

notes.title: His Eye Overrules the Checker
notes.subtitle:
Two rounds proved it the same evening: verify first, build only what's missing. Personal Round 4 verified the file and built one item out of five — the R3-5 pin, +5/−5 lines, the only diff in the 52,322-line file — because the file is the truth, not the last report. The Dashboard round investigated leaderboards only and built nothing: the view already exists, the follow-on is data. The checker that sends work back must do more than fail — it must disprove: the 390px slack was 0–8px, not the claimed ~34px, and the cut zero's clip mechanism was disproven from the file's own rules, so the repair must correct the arithmetic and find the true cause, or mark it eye-only honestly. A board is not done when it shows on one screen: "Doesn't show on that board only shows on a mobile not on a on a laptop I guess. See this needs to be optimized for mobile and for laptop and clearly it's not." And the measure must embody what it measures: "And what are you going to do with the stars?" — "And the rate doesn't intelligent." Gold VALUE stars and blue INTELLIGENCE stars contradict what they measure — the fix is purple and white with the DM flow inside, built literally from the DM initial itself: "take the DM-initial element itself — take the T, it's already that colour, put it in VALUE, put the real icon over there, put a star in it, and you're good." The same eye that caught the stars caught the layers: a label made into a button is still not a board — "Child Note and Grandma Note need to be their OWN elevated board, like In a Nutshell. Every board should have a board around it; on hover it should light up in its colour and move." And nothing dead: "We shouldn't have anything that's dead." The top orb shows no round or flow, and Rate This Intel has no circle at all. Two conduct laws ride alongside, both born the same evening: answer with the plan — the first reply to "what are you going to do with the stars?" was "The stars," the noun echoed back, no plan, nothing to judge — and never say "fixed" before his eye has seen it: the delivery said "The agreement's fixed for laptop and phone now," and six minutes later his eye found the last board not showing at all on laptop. The frame can lie too: the How You Get Paid board rendered with title, frame and nav buttons present and the body entirely blank — a check that confirms the board loaded by seeing its title has proven the shell, not the board.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: the checker passes, his eye overrules, and nothing is fixed until he has seen it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a house inspection. The builder's own checklist says every room passed — but when Shawn walks in, the last room isn't there at all on his laptop, one room has walls and a door and nothing inside it, and the stars that are supposed to measure intelligence look like costume jewelry. The checklist measured the wrong things: it checked the frame, not the words inside it; it checked the colour rule, not whether the star actually circles like the one on the page; it checked that a label was dressed up, not whether the whole layer was a board. So the law is simple: check the file before you build, prove your numbers, check both screens, read the words inside the frame — and never call it fixed until his eye has seen it fixed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Check the page first before you build anything new! Prove your numbers, or the fix will be wrong! A board must look whole on a phone AND on a laptop! The stars that rate intelligence have to look intelligent themselves! When Shawn asks what you'll do, say the plan, not just the word! 'Fixed' means his eye has seen it fixed — not before! A board can look right and say nothing, so always read the words inside! Every layer needs its own board, and every orb needs its own circle that moves! Nothing dead on the board — everything alive!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — before you build anything new, dear, you check what's already there first, so you don't build the same thing twice! And you prove your numbers, love, because a wrong number means a wrong fix! A board has to look whole on your phone AND on your laptop, dear — both, not just one! And the stars, love — the stars that say how smart something is have to look smart themselves, purple and white, circling like the ones that are already there! And never say "fixed," dear, until his eye has actually seen it fixed — his eye is the proof, love, always!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before any build, verify against the file: grep the claim, read the bytes, count the lines. Build only the items the file does not have. When a brief asks for a view, check whether the view already exists — investigate before you build, and say plainly when the answer is "it already exists, the follow-on is data." Every claim in a round carries its arithmetic, shown: the numbers, the rule they come from, the boundary they hold at. A checker redoes the arithmetic from the file, not from the maker's message. A fix names its cause from the file's rules and proves the mechanism — or it says plainly "cause unidentified, eye-only." Check every board at phone width AND laptop width before calling it done — 390px and laptop, both, every time — and every layout family complete. When a control measures a quality, judge the control by that quality first: the intelligence rating must look intelligent. When he points at an element and says "take that," take that element — byte for byte, not a redraw in its colours. When he says a thing must be a board, board the whole thing — never only its label. Walk every orb and every circle on the board before calling it done, and ask of each one: does it move? When he asks what you will do, say what you will do, in plain words, in the same turn. Never say "fixed" until his eye has seen it fixed. Check the body, not the frame: count the words, read the first line, confirm the content rendered.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **VERIFY FIRST, BUILD ONLY WHAT'S MISSING:** the file is the truth, not the last report. A report that claims five done is checked against the bytes; a brief that asks for a view is checked against the file. What is already there is not built again.
2. **PROVE THE ARITHMETIC, FIND THE TRUE CAUSE:** a number that is wrong is not a rounding error; a cause that is wrong is not a fix. "Harmless but unproven" is not a pass — it is a repair ticket with the proof attached. When the cause cannot be found, the honest mark is "eye-only," not a plausible mechanism.
3. **OPTIMIZED FOR MOBILE AND LAPTOP:** a board that shows only on mobile is not done. It must look whole on a laptop and on a phone. Mobile-first never meant mobile-only; his seat is the laptop as often as the phone.
4. **THE RATE MUST LOOK INTELLIGENT:** the stars that rate VALUE and INTELLIGENCE have to look intelligent themselves — purple and white with the DM flow inside, no gold or blue anywhere in a star rule. A visitor reads the stars before they read the words.
5. **TAKE THE ELEMENT, DON'T DRAW A LOOK-ALIKE:** the DM initial is already that colour, already circling the right way. Take it, put the star in it. A colour rule is never the proof of a motion; the motion is the proof.
6. **LAYERS THEMSELVES MUST BE BOARDS:** a label made into a button is still not a board. The whole layer needs its own elevated board, like In a Nutshell — on hover it lights up in its colour and moves. The test is the nutshell: does this layer look like the In a Nutshell board?
7. **NOTHING DEAD ON THE BOARD:** every orb and every circle must be alive with its flow — a still orb is a dead orb. When a new element like Rate This Intel is added, its circle rides with it from the first build, never as a later round.
8. **SAY THE PLAN, NOT THE WORD:** when he asks what you are going to do, answer with the plan — the colours, the flow, the collision, the orb — so he can say yes, no, or different before the work is done. An echoed noun gives him nothing to judge.
9. **TOLD FIXED IS NOT FIXED — AND THE FRAME CAN LIE:** "fixed" waits for his eye. A delivery message is a claim, not proof. And a board can look right and say nothing — title, frame and nav present, body blank — so every board check reads the board's own text, never only that the title and nav are present.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without verify-first, the machine builds what already exists — the doubling-up he corrects all week — two copies of the same thing, two truths that drift apart.
2. Without proven arithmetic, wrong numbers ship a collision at 390px — the phone width he judges everything at — and a fix for the wrong cause ships a change that does nothing while the defect stays.
3. Without both screens, a page proven at 390px and never opened at laptop width is half-proven — and the half that fails is the one he is sitting at when he finds it.
4. Without stars that look intelligent, nothing else on the board gets believed — the labels, the notes, the whole intelligent block — because the measure argues against itself.
5. Without harvesting the DM initial, the copy matches the colour and misses the motion — and his eye catches the miss instantly, and the round comes back.
6. Without the layers boarded, the Hub reads as one flat page with headings instead of intelligence itself — text about intelligence, not intelligence.
7. Without the flow on every orb, a single dead element breaks the feeling for the whole board — alive is the whole language, and dead is never a design choice.
8. Without the plan stated plainly, he spends another turn re-asking — attention taken from the work itself — and the round is built on a guess that comes back wrong.
9. Without "fixed" waiting for his eye, the strongest word in the machine closes an item that is still open and hands him a surprise instead of a result — and the next "fixed" has to earn its meaning back.

notes.title: The Way of Thinking Comes First
notes.subtitle:
The trial IS the refund policy. "There is no refunds. What we do is we give you nine days up front. You try it before you buy it. And if you don't like it, you don't keep her. No problem. Okay, that's it." Nobody pays before they have lived in it for nine days, so nobody ever needs their money back for something they never tried. And leaving is clean, because "you also get to keep Naya. You just don't get to have Naya Power, which is your AI connected to Naya Net, which is like plugging your computer into the internet." Naya stays; only the plug-in goes. The trial turns into a membership through the teaching: four detailed explainer videos, one deep dive per day — Day 1 show it, Day 2 share it everywhere, Day 3 invite your world personally, Day 4 teach one person and get paid — "just do it the ultimate four part series," plus a fifth video that answers what NayaNET ultimately is. Sharing is taught three ways — tap a button with a message already written, share an image of Naya with your link on it, get your own domain at Namecheap pointing at your link — because sharing is the engine: no sharing, no joins, no pay, no growth. The teaching itself is governed by one correction: "you just repeating back verbatim what I'm saying. Like maybe put thought into what you think would be the ultimate to say." Never the echo — think, scorecard, and return the ultimate version, in his voice, improved. The pages the teaching points at are built the same way: About is frame by frame, like the agreement and the calendar — frame 1 a picture plus the nutshell of what they're about, the whole profile one intelligent block — and every frame repeats one pattern: what it is, why it matters, how it connects, what's in it for you, child-clear and grandma-clear. "They just want to know what it is. They want to know why it matters. And they want to know what's in it for them. That's a human." About IS the ultimate online profile page — one thing, not two — and the whole of it is held together by the thesis, told first: "intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing. And the highest level of honor is to serve. So what if our job was to give 10 star service to you?" A mother brain everybody plugs into, everybody collectively more intelligent by plugging in, a new portal to the internet — "and we call her Naya." Video 5 speaks the thesis aloud, in the narrator format, first in meaning even though it was written fifth.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: the way of thinking comes first, then the plan, then the page.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Imagine a shop that lets you live in the house for nine days before you pay a cent — and if you walk away, the friend who showed you around stays your friend. That is the whole deal: nine days up front, no refunds because there is nothing to refund, and Naya stays with you either way — only the connection to the net, Naya Power, is what the trial decides. Once you are in, the teaching is four deep videos, one a day, that show you exactly what to do — and a fifth that tells you what you actually joined, before any of the steps. Sharing is taught three ways so everyone finds the one that fits them: one tap, one picture, or your own domain. And every page you meet is built the same way the agreement is built: one frame at a time, each frame answering what it is, why it matters, and what's in it for you — so a child gets it and a grandma gets it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Nine days to try it, and you keep Naya even if you leave! Naya Power is the plug you keep or lose, like plugging your computer into the internet! Share it three ways: tap a button, share a picture, or get your own domain! Four videos teach you the whole plan, one deep dive each day, and a fifth video tells you what NayaNET really is! Don't just copy what Shawn says — think, and say it the best way you can! Your About page is like a little book, one frame at a time, and every frame says what it is, why it matters, and what's in it for you!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — you get nine whole days to try it before you pay anything, dear, and if it's not for you, you just don't keep her, no problem at all! And you never lose Naya herself, love — only the plug-in, like unplugging from the internet, that's all! The teaching comes in four lovely videos, dear, one each day, deep and complete, and a fifth one that tells you what it all really is! And your About page, love — it's like a little book, one frame at a time, each frame telling you what it is, why it matters, and what's in it for you, so plain a child understands it and so plain you understand it too, dear!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Tell the thesis first — before features, plan, and price: intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing; the highest honor is to serve; our job is 10-star service; the mother brain everybody plugs into; everybody collectively more intelligent by plugging in; a new portal to the internet; we call her Naya. State the trial in one breath everywhere the offer is made: nine days up front, try before you buy, if you don't like it you don't keep her, no problem — and both halves of the keep: you keep Naya; Naya Power is your AI connected to NayaNet, like plugging your computer into the internet. Teach the three sharing ways in order, simplest first — button, image, domain — with his line as the example message. Build the series as four complete deep dives, one per day, plus Video 5, the thesis spoken aloud in the narrator format, never folded in as a fifth day. Before answering, ask what he is ultimately trying to say and return the ultimate version — his operative words verbatim where they decide, improved everywhere else. Build every About page frame by frame — frame 1 picture plus nutshell, whole profile one intelligent block — and repeat the one pattern in every frame and every Skills slide: what it is, why it matters, how it connects, what's in it for you. One page: About IS the profile.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **NINE DAYS IS THE REFUND POLICY:** no refunds, because there is nothing to refund — nine days up front, try before you buy, if you don't like it you don't keep her, no problem. Never dress it up as a guarantee, never add conditions, never apologize for it.
2. **NAYA STAYS; THE PLUG-IN IS WHAT THE TRIAL DECIDES:** you keep Naya either way; Naya Power is your AI connected to NayaNet, like plugging your computer into the internet. Never describe Naya Power as a feature bundle — it is the connection itself.
3. **SHARING HAS THREE WAYS, SIMPLEST FIRST:** a button with a message already written, an image of Naya with your link on it, your own domain at Namecheap pointing at your link. Train all three, so every citizen finds the one that fits them.
4. **THE SERIES IS ULTIMATE OR IT IS NOT DONE:** four detailed explainer videos, one deep dive per day, each complete and finished — plus Video 5, the thesis spoken aloud, standing first in meaning. A part only sketched means the series is not ultimate yet.
5. **NEVER THE ECHO:** do not repeat his words back to him. Think about what he said and craft the ultimate version of what to say — in his voice, improved. A quote proves a decision; a parroted paragraph proves nothing was thought.
6. **ABOUT IS FRAME BY FRAME:** built the same way as the agreement and the calendar — frame 1 a picture plus the nutshell, the whole profile one intelligent block, answering "what are you ultimately about?" frame after frame. Never a wall of text; never a new format.
7. **ONE PATTERN, REPEATED:** what it is in a nutshell → why it matters → how it connects / the value → what's in it for you — child-clear, grandma-clear. The same logic builds About and Skills. A frame that cannot answer "what's in it for you" does not belong.
8. **ABOUT IS THE PROFILE:** one page, not two. When a brief asks for a profile page, point at About — do not start a second page. When a citizen fills in their About, they have filled in their profile.
9. **THE THESIS GOES FIRST:** a joiner gets the way of thinking right away — intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing, the highest honor is to serve, 10-star service through a mother brain everybody plugs into. Not a feature list first: the reason first.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the nine days stated plainly, doubt keeps people from joining at all — and doubt is what a refund policy exists to soothe, after the money has already moved.
2. Without "you keep Naya," leaving feels like losing her, and the trial feels like a trap nobody enters freely.
3. Without three sharing ways, sharing stays hard for the citizens who don't fit the one way taught — and sharing is the engine of the whole ambassador plan.
4. Without the series done ultimate, a citizen stops on day two confused instead of finishing day four paid — and half a plan is the difference between the two.
5. Without the don't-echo correction, every answer wastes his attention returning his own words — and teaches him the machine adds nothing to them.
6. Without frame by frame, About becomes another long page of text about a person — the thing he has corrected all week.
7. Without the one pattern, a page loses the reader, because every frame must end where the reader's own interest lives: what's in it for me.
8. Without one page for About and profile, two names for the same thing means two places to maintain and two doors where one belongs.
9. Without the thesis first, the onboarding teaches the steps before the reason — and a citizen who finishes day four paid but cannot say what NayaNET ultimately is cannot explain it to the next person.

notes.title: Hired to Lead, Paid When We Get Paid
notes.subtitle:
The four actions under a post each light up in their own colour — Love red, Like purple, Comment blue, Share green — jewel-like and beautiful, never white, never simple. Love used to have red around it, now white — wrong; white is not a colour here, it is the absence of the light, and a button that should be lit and shows white is a button that has gone out. The zero cut off at the bottom is the same failure at a smaller scale: a count that cannot be read is a count that was never drawn. The sidebar is the door to the whole network, and tapping it did nothing — no close-first needed, the tap itself is dead. Messenger and the People rail are the same thing, one rail, not two; two names for one rail is the same failure in language, so the citizen looks for two things and finds neither. One rail, one name, one tap that opens. Every page gets its own Smart List area — Personal, Business, Your World, and Calendar too — because the lists ARE the organization of their vault: saved smart notes, Naya notes, connections, images, anything, organized and reviewable from the feed, per page. "Favorite" becomes "Pin it" — pin to the top of the feed, or to a space, a business, a profile, a list, anywhere in Naya. Save means to your Smart List / Smart Vault, and save lands straight in, no big list popping up first. "Pinned worlds" was the assistant's invention — he never said it; it is corrected out. The Intelligent Library becomes the laws, constitutions, and rules — a search engine over all the frames. An icon is a promise that the thing behind it is there: the AI Score icon points at alscore.nayapower.workers.dev, the Academy icon at academy.nayanet.app — the old app.nayanet.technology answers nothing, and nothing may point at it again. A citizen tapping an icon and getting nothing does not think "the address changed" — they think the feature is broken, and they stop tapping. After Hub and Personal come About and Skills on the four board formats, then membership — and paywalls, not just memberships, so a citizen can charge for their information, presented beautifully. Courses get a cover like a personal page, then frame-by-frame lessons, the citizen choosing combined or three styles for audio, visual, and lesson. The visuals must react to the audio, not just play alongside it — the picture moves because the sound moved, the light rises because the voice rose; mute the audio and the visuals should go still. And Naya talks to them one on one on video, spelling it out exactly: "This is exactly what to do. Follow these steps and you will see success and everybody wins." Script 1 is written — the full four-day plan in her voice, warm, first person, child-clear — voicing and production await his word. The plan itself is approved: "I think that sounds really good." Four days of Fast Action — show it, share it everywhere, invite your world personally, teach one person and get paid — then five days in the Academy. The frame for the whole plan, in his words: "Imagine we're hiring you to be the leader for NayaNET." And the ambassador line, verbatim, so no ambassador ever has to explain it twice: "This is not a network marketing. You're an ambassador. You're just like getting a sales job with a high tech company. You just commission sales. If you sell you get paid. People join, you get paid. If they don't, you don't get paid. But you get to enjoy NayaNET — it's your brain forever, you get to use it forever." The pay timing is settled in one sentence: "You get paid when we get paid. So the trial is nine days. You get paid day 10. If PayPal delays for whatever reason, which sometimes they do, then you just get paid when PayPal pays us. But in most cases, you'll get paid on the 10th day." No monthly cycle, no two-week cycle — the payday is the day we are paid.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one rail, one list per page, one honest pay promise — hired to lead, paid when we get paid.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it as a job with a real company, not a scheme: you are hired to be the leader for NayaNET, you tell the world about it — post, text, email, get a domain, market as an ambassador — and when people join through your link, you get paid. layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Give each action its colour and keep it: Love red, Like purple, Comment blue, Share green — lit when active, never white; icons jewel-like and prominent, counts fully drawn, never cut off. When a control is tapped, it must open — no close-first, no second tap, no dead press; prove the open by a real tap. When two names describe one thing, collapse them to one: Messenger and People rail are one rail. Give every page its own Smart List area — Personal, Business, Your World, Calendar — and keep the Intelligent Library as the search engine over the laws, constitutions, and rules; never invent a collection name he did not say. When an icon is placed or fixed, fetch its destination fresh and match it against the live thing before calling it done; the AI Score icon points at alscore.nayapower.workers.dev, the Academy icon at academy.nayanet.app, and nothing points at app.nayanet.technology again. Build in his order: Hub and Personal first, then About and Skills on the four board formats, then membership, then paywalls — never membership before the pages that explain what it is. Bind the visuals to the audio: the picture, the light, the motion must answer the sound as it plays; mute the audio and the visuals go still. Every Notebook Video is Naya narrating straight to you, one citizen, one conversation, warm, first person, child-clear — script first, voicing and production only on his word. Say the pay exactly his way, everywhere: not network marketing; ambassador; commission sales like a sales job with a high-tech company; people join through your link, you get paid; if they don't, you don't; your brain forever; nine days trial, paid day ten, paid when we get paid.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **FOUR ACTIONS, FOUR COLOURS:** Love red, Like purple, Comment blue, Share green — each action IS a different thing, and a lit action that shows white has gone out.
2. **ONE RAIL, ONE NAME, ONE TAP:** Messenger and People are one rail; the sidebar must open on tap, proved by a real tap, not by bytes.
3. **EVERY PAGE GETS ITS OWN SMART LIST:** Personal, Business, Your World, Calendar — the lists ARE the organization of the vault, and a save with nowhere to live is a save that is lost.
4. **SAVE LANDS STRAIGHT IN:** no big list popping up first; "Favorite" becomes "Pin it"; the Intelligent Library is the search engine over the laws, constitutions, and rules.
5. **AN ICON POINTS AT THE LIVE THING:** AI Score to alscore.nayapower.workers.dev, Academy to academy.nayanet.app — a live icon pointing at a dead address teaches the citizen that tapping leads nowhere.
6. **PAYWALLS, NOT JUST MEMBERSHIPS:** after Hub and Personal, About and Skills on the four board formats, then membership, then paywalls — charge for your information, presented beautifully.
7. **THE VISUALS REACT TO THE AUDIO:** playing alongside is two things happening at the same time; reacting is one thing answering the other — if the visuals do not change with the audio, they are not synced.
8. **NAYA TALKS ONE ON ONE:** every Notebook Video is one citizen, one conversation, spelling it out exactly — "This is exactly what to do. Follow these steps and you will see success and everybody wins."
9. **THE AMBASSADOR IS NOT NETWORK MARKETING:** commission sales like a sales job with a high-tech company — people join through your link, you get paid; if they don't, you don't; and your brain is yours forever.
10. **YOU GET PAID WHEN WE GET PAID:** nine days trial, paid day ten; if people join every day, you get paid every day — no monthly cycle, no waiting for a payday, with the PayPal-delay exception named plainly.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the four colours, the citizen's hands on a post blur into one gesture — and love showing white where it used to show red reads as broken, because it is.
2. Without the tap that opens, the sidebar is a picture of a door, not a door — and a dead tap locks the citizen out of every room in the network.
3. Without a list per page, a save has nowhere to live — the same failure as Smart Inviter, one level up — and the citizen who saved something can never find it again.
4. Without the icon pointing at the live thing, the citizen learns that tapping leads nowhere — and an untrusted map is a map that stops being used.
5. Without the order — About and Skills before membership — the membership sells a system the pages have not yet explained, and the citizen is asked to join what they have not seen.
6. Without visuals that react, the walkthrough's video and audio feel like two files started together — and the citizen feels the gap even if they cannot name it.
7. Without the one-on-one video, the Fast Action Plan is a document speaking to everyone — and a person who feels lectured to closes the tab instead of following the steps.
8. Without the ambassador line in his words, the first question anyone asks — is this network marketing? — hardens into an objection, and ambassadors are left sounding like they are selling a scheme.
9. Without the day-ten timing, the citizen who shares every day does not know the money follows the same rhythm — and the sharing stops.
10. Without "your brain forever," the pay promise stands alone — and a citizen who has not yet sold anything has nothing, instead of a brain that is already theirs.

notes.title: The Vault Holds It, the Fetch Proves It
notes.subtitle:
Smart Inviter was FOUND, not lost. The finish version, November 15, existed on disk (306,447 B, sha256 2948c26b…), on GitHub (branch inviter/finish-20261115, commit dcef2028), and on the staged link, which still serves it byte-for-byte — "Smart Inviter" eight times, "Smart Growth" zero. The live Hub holds it zero times, so his "it's in the old hub, the one that's live but I can't get in there anymore" does not hold for the page itself; the sidebar and destination not opening is the "can't get in" part, already in fix-1g. His law, restated in this stretch: "Put everything in the Smart Vault so you don't lose stuff." A thing is only lost when no finished copy exists anywhere — and the Vault is what guarantees a finished copy exists. Lost means never filed to the Vault. The same call taught the other half of the law: a stale cache is not a broken page. The portal was right on this browser (1,146,232 B, sha 9ba535c7) and wrong on the other only because the other held a stale cached copy — his words: "Oh, now it does. So just on the other browser it didn't. Weird." A page that loads on one browser and not on another is a cache question before it is a page question: hard refresh, fresh fetch, bytes and sha, then judge. Declaring a working page broken sends a round to fix a page that was never broken — and the round's "fix" can break the page that was working. The same fresh fetch is what makes a deploy live: Academy went live at academy.nayanet.app — HTTP 200, 97,562 B, sha256 379b174c…, verified by three consecutive fresh fetches, worker naya-academy, DNS resolving. A deploy completing is not a page being live; a fresh fetch matching is. The address itself was settled an hour earlier when he spelled it letter by letter — "A-C-A-D-E-M-Y dot N-A-Y-A-N-E-T dot A-P-P" — after the voice path garbled it as "academy dot nine dot net". The garbled form is transcription noise, not a candidate; the spelled form is the decision. And the routing around the live thing changed too: Home takes a member straight into the Hub, auto logged in — and a non-member to the collective agreement, not pricing, superseding his November 14 rule. The agreement is the front door: a non-member meets what we stand for before they meet a price. The hard part stands: the system has to know whether they are a member, and that check is queued, not assumed. His eye overruled the bytes once more on fix-1g: the child note had a big white box around it, the stars did not update, the board got worse — "the in nutshell is not in a nutshell" — and no grep could find the white box, so fix-1h proves it by render, not by bytes. A checker PASS in bytes never survives his eye saying GOES BACK. A nutshell earns its name by its size: the whole thing in three or four sentences, on a board moved up a tad, in a tad, its light down just a little. And the colours must read apart at a glance: Dashboard evidently PURPLE, Hub evidently MAGENTA, Reports and Smart Growth separated the same way — the order is right, only the colour distinction needs strengthening. The stars drifted gold and blue; they must be purple and white, the INTELLIGENCE label purple, not blue — a drift is how a design language dies, one gold star here, one blue label there, until nothing matches anything else.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: file it in the Vault so it is never lost, prove it by a fresh fetch so it is really live, and let his eye — not the bytes — have the last word.

A page that loads on one browser and not on another is a cache question before it is a page question: hard refresh, fresh fetch, bytes and sha, then judge. Declaring a working page broken sends a round to fix a page that was never broken — and the round's "fix" can break the page that was working. The same fresh fetch is what makes a deploy live: Academy went live at academy.nayanet.app — HTTP 200, 97,562 B, sha256 379b174c…, verified by three consecutive fresh fetches, worker naya-academy, DNS resolving. A deploy completing is not a page being live; a fresh fetch matching is. The address itself was settled an hour earlier when he spelled it letter by letter — "A-C-A-D-E-M-Y dot N-A-Y-A-N-E-T dot A-P-P" — after the voice path garbled it as "academy dot nine dot net". The garbled form is transcription noise, not a candidate; the spelled form is the decision. And the routing around the live thing changed too: Home takes a member straight into the Hub, auto logged in — and a non-member to the collective agreement, not pricing, superseding his November 14 rule. The agreement is the front door: a non-member meets what we stand for before they meet a price. The hard part stands: the system has to know whether they are a member, and that check is queued, not assumed. His eye overruled the bytes once more on fix-1g: the child note had a big white box around it, the stars did not update, the board got worse — "the in nutshell is not in a nutshell" — and no grep could find the white box, so fix-1h proves it by render, not by bytes. A checker PASS in bytes never survives his eye saying GOES BACK. A nutshell earns its name by its size: the whole thing in three or four sentences, on a board moved up a tad, in a tad, its light down just a little. And the colours must read apart at a glance: Dashboard evidently PURPLE, Hub evidently MAGENTA, Reports and Smart Growth separated the same way — the order is right, only the colour distinction needs strengthening. The stars drifted gold and blue; they must be purple and white, the INTELLIGENCE label purple, not blue — a drift is how a design language dies, one gold star here, one blue label there, until nothing matches anything else.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: file it in the Vault so it is never lost, prove it by a fresh fetch so it is really live, and let his eye — not the bytes — have the last word.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the Smart Vault as the one drawer in the house where finished things always go. Smart Inviter looked lost — but it was sitting in the drawer all along, on disk, on GitHub, on a staged link, byte for byte the same. It was never lost; it was never filed. That is the whole law: when something is finished, file it in the Vault in the same pass, or the finish is not finished. The other half is proof: a page is not live because someone said the deploy finished — it is live because you fetched it fresh, three times, and the bytes and the sha matched. Academy is live that way, at the address he spelled out letter by letter, because the voice had garbled it. And when his eye says a page looks wrong — a white box nobody's grep can find, stars that sit still — you do not argue from the bytes. You open the render and find it there, because the render is where he lives.

layers.name: Child Note

If a page looks broken on one computer but fine on another, it is just an old copy hiding in the cupboard! And a live page is only really live when you go and check it yourself, fresh, three times! Your name is spelled letter by letter, so nobody gets it wrong! Purple stays purple, and the Hub stays magenta, so you always know where you are!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — when you finish something beautiful, you put it in the treasure box straight away, dear, so it can never be lost! That box is the Smart Vault, love! And a page is only really live when you go and check it yourself, fresh, dear — not because someone said the work was done! If it looks wrong on one computer and right on another, love, it's just an old copy hiding in the cupboard — give it a good hard refresh! And the colours, dear — purple for one page, magenta for the other, so you always know exactly where you are standing, love!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: File every finished thing to the Smart Vault in the same pass it finishes — disk path, branch, commit, blob, sha, and the staged link that serves it. When something is declared missing, re-list fresh from the Vault and the branches before declaring it gone. When a page fails on one browser and works on another: fresh fetch on both, compare bytes and sha, hard refresh the failing one — never a round before the cache is cleared as a suspect. When a deploy is claimed live, fetch the URL fresh three times and match bytes and sha against the source before the word "live" is written anywhere. When he spells a name letter by letter, write it down exactly as spelled and use that form everywhere; never carry the garbled form forward. Home routes by membership: member to the Hub, auto logged in; non-member to the agreement — never pricing first — and when a rule is superseded, name the old rule and its date. When his eye reports a defect the bytes cannot explain, open the render and find it there; a checker PASS in bytes is void the moment he says GOES BACK. A nutshell is three or four sentences, no more. Dashboard purple, Hub magenta, evidently different at a glance; stars purple and white, INTELLIGENCE label purple, no blue anywhere in the star.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE VAULT IS WHAT MAKES "LOST" IMPOSSIBLE:** a finished thing gets its Vault copy the same pass it finishes — disk, branch, commit, blob, sha, staged link — or the finish is not finished.
2. **LOST MEANS NEVER FILED:** Smart Inviter was found, not lost, because a finished copy existed; the finding itself is filed to the Vault so it is never "lost" again.
3. **A STALE CACHE IS NOT A BROKEN PAGE:** one browser right, one browser wrong is a cache question first — hard refresh, fresh fetch, bytes and sha, then judge.
4. **LIVE MEANS A FRESH FETCH PROVES IT:** Academy is live because three fresh fetches returned the exact bytes and sha — a deploy completing is not a page being live.
5. **THE SPELLED FORM IS THE DECISION:** when he spells a name letter by letter, the garbled form is transcription noise, and the spelled form closes the question in the same minute.
6. **HOME GOES TO THE AGREEMENT, NOT PRICING:** member to the Hub, auto logged in; non-member to the collective agreement — superseding the November 14 rule — and the membership check is queued, not assumed.
7. **HIS EYE OVERRULES THE BYTES:** a white box no grep can find, stars that flow in code and sit still on screen — the proof moves to the render, and a checker PASS is void the moment he says GOES BACK.
8. **A NUTSHELL IS THREE OR FOUR SENTENCES:** the whole idea, distilled, in three or four sentences — if it takes a paragraph, it is not a nutshell, whatever the label says.
9. **COLOURS MUST READ APART AT A GLANCE:** Dashboard evidently purple, Hub evidently magenta, Reports and Smart Growth separated the same way; stars purple and white, the INTELLIGENCE label purple, never gold and blue — drift is how a design language dies.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the Vault law, work that lives in one staging file, one branch, one person's memory is one flake away from gone — and a whole round can burn searching for something that was safe all along.
2. Without the cache check first, a working page gets declared broken, a round gets sent to fix a page that was never broken, and the round's "fix" can break the page that was working.
3. Without the fresh-fetch proof, a page gets claimed live on a deploy receipt alone — and citizens open an address that serves an old version, a disabled route, or nothing at all.
4. Without taking the spelled form exactly, a garbled name carried into a deploy, a link, or a record sends the next round to the wrong address — one letter away from a different place entirely.
5. Without the agreement as the front door, a non-member is asked to pay before they know what they are joining — and the join never follows, because the price came before the promise.
6. Without the render as the proof, bytes argue against his eye after he has already said GOES BACK — and the white box, the still stars, and the wrong board all survive another round.
7. Without the nutshell's size, the label "in a nutshell" lies about the thing it names, and the reader learns to distrust every label after it.
8. Without colours that read apart, two pages feel like one page, a citizen cannot tell where they are, and the Trinity loses the distinction that makes it navigable.
9. Without the named pair — purple and white, never gold and blue — the drift arrives one build at a time, silently, until nothing on the page matches anything else.

notes.title: The Orb, the Pin, and the Library
notes.subtitle:
The rating star is not invented — it is the DM initial orb with the initial swapped for a star. Look at the sidebar and the connections initials, the avatar circles with an initial inside — Shawn, Thora, Wrena, Sophia, Vera, Zoe — the flow that moves INSIDE that circle is the exact element and concept to take: take it whole, replace the initial with a STAR, make it purple, one white and one purple. VALUE is purple orbs with white stars; INTELLIGENCE is white orbs with purple stars. Fix-1f's conic-comet did not read as flowing to his eye — the comet was a new invention, and the invention missed, while the element he already approved, in the place he already looks, was the answer all along. The heading changes with it: not "RATE THE INTELLIGENCE" but "RATE THIS INTEL" — his words, exactly that — and the rate orb is a BIGGER version of that same flowing element, white is fine, dealer's choice of white or purple, with flow around the OUTSIDE as well as inside, because the outside flow is the difference between a jewel that sits and a jewel that lives. One element, three sizes: the DM initial orb, the rating star, the big rate orb. The same eye that named the orb called the "in a nutshell" board almost: move the board UP just a tad, move it IN just a tad, and bring DOWN the brightness of the light on the board just a little, because it is almost too much light — right now it reads as overlaid, not seated. "Almost" is the most precise verdict a page can earn; it names the distance to done in inches, and the round that answers it with a rebuild has not heard him. Then the naming correction, in the same hour: he asked "should we just say pin it instead of favorite?" — and it was carried as YES with a second invention riding along, the collection "Pinned Worlds." "What is the pinned worlds? I didn't say anything about pinned worlds I said favorite becomes pin it." Only the favorite ACTION becomes "Pin it"; "Favorite Worlds" stays as it is. Pin = pin it to the top of the feed, or to a space, a business, a profile, a list — anywhere in Naya. Save = save it to your Smart List. And Save lands straight in — no big list popping up first — a saved smart note, connection, project, or page landing in the Smart Lists area, then organized into lists, nicely categorized, easily accessible; his new order, a Smart List on Personal and on Calendar too, "because we need to be able to save their smart notes," queued behind the running rounds, one coordinator per file. Before judging any of his findings, check which build he is looking at: the live Dashboard was verified outdated, fresh fetch 1,817,928 B, head "/* 2026-11-05 — ORB RENDER FIX," no "WHERE YOU GO," no "YOUR WORLDS," no "PAGE CLICKS" — while his screenshot matches the newer staged build, the orb-ring fix, 2,166,903 B, eye PASS Nov 19, staged only, not live. His findings stand as the next Dashboard round against that staged build: the "smart notes inbox and lists" buttons shouldn't be there; the sidebars are right, just the color flow is off; the plus button should stick at the middle of the inside on the top. And the colours: the Dashboard must be evidently PURPLE and the Hub evidently MAGENTA, and Reports and Smart Growth separated the same way — their colours are too close to each other. A verdict read against the wrong build fixes the wrong page. The same hour caught a retitle that never landed: the v31 round's coordinator completed, but slide 32 was still titled "Welcome to NayaNET" with the old "in a nutshell" text — "The Invitation" appeared nowhere — because the builder edited the EXPORT copy, not the artifact, and the checker's export overwrote it. The builder's "v31" label is VOID. Edit the artifact; the export is a copy that flows one way, out. And the repair that followed told the deeper truth: the last board was rebuilt as ONE big gold-toned jewel board, verification succeeded — but the TITLE DID NOT CHANGE. "The Invitation" never landed because he never picked it. A recommendation is not his pick, and it must never be reported as if it were — "Let's go with that" is the pick; silence is not. His title stays "Welcome to NayaNET" by his order. The linked boards grow the same way: every "what is" gets its own frame, in distilled form, categorized by kind — what we stand for, how we are governed, what it is built on — "What is our innovation? What is our technology? What is CCT? ... What is the protocol Naya protocol? We'll just explain what it is." Four formats are tried for the insert boards: two equal halves; three in thirds, same size; one full board across; two big equal rectangles, one over the other, for statements — and the most common is one full board across, because most of these boards carry one distilled idea and one idea wants one big board. And all of it gets a home: the Intelligent Library becomes all our laws and constitutions and rules — everything to do with Naya — like a search engine, they go there, search all the frames, pull up whatever one they want. The names were verified from fresh GitHub blobs, not memory — Hub fix-1f holds Intel Today 19x, Your Reports 7x, Smart Growth 5x, Smart Inviter 0x, Your Connections 9x, Intelligent Library 8x — and the law stops living scattered across slides and gets one address, searchable, where a citizen can pull up whatever one they want.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: take the element he already loves whole, carry only the words he said, and give the law one searchable home.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the page as a room full of things he already loves. When the rating star didn't read, the answer wasn't a better invention — it was the little circle in the sidebar with a friend's initial inside it, the light already flowing inside it. Take that whole, swap the initial for a star, and there it is: one white, one purple. When the board is almost right, you don't rebuild it — you move it up a tad, in a tad, light down a little, and stop. When he renames something, you change only what he named: favorite becomes Pin it, and that's all — no new collection invented on the side, because every word he didn't say, carried as if he said it, is a correction he has to spend his evening making. Save is just as plain: one tap and it lands straight in the Smart List, no big list popping up first, and the Smart List lives wherever the saving happens — Personal, and Calendar too. Before you judge anything he found, check which version of the page he's looking at — live or staged — because a verdict read against the wrong build fixes the wrong page. And edit the real thing, never the copy: the builder who edited the export watched the checker overwrite every word. A recommendation is never his pick until he picks it — "The Invitation" is a beautiful name, but it never landed, because he never said so, and the title stays his. Every "what is" — the innovation, the technology, CCT, the protocol — gets its own frame, in words a child understands, grouped by kind, most often one full board across. And all of it — the vow, the deal, the promise, the constitution, the laws, the governance — lives in one place at last: the Intelligent Library, a search engine over every frame of Naya, where anyone can pull up whatever one they want.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the rating star is a little jewel that flows inside, like the circles with your friends' letters in them! The big orb flows on the outside too, like a jewel that is alive! Pin means stick it to the top, and Save means put it in your Smart List — two different jobs! Always check which page Shawn is looking at before you say it is fixed! And all the laws live in one Library, like a search engine, so you can find any of them!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before drawing a new flowing element, find the flowing element already in the build — the DM orb, the rate orb, the initials — and take it whole. Change only the content inside: initial to star, size to bigger. VALUE: purple orbs, white stars; INTELLIGENCE: white orbs, purple stars. Rename the heading exactly: "RATE THIS INTEL." The rate orb is the DM element scaled up, flow inside AND around the outside. When the verdict is "almost," make only the three moves — up a tad, in a tad, light down a little — then stop and let his eye judge again; never redesign a board he called almost. Carry his words exactly — the action, the label, the scope he named, nothing added; when a rename is approved, change only what he named; if a companion name seems needed, ask, never invent it and file it as his. Save lands straight in: one tap into the Smart Lists area, organizing afterwards; put a Smart List on Personal and on Calendar. When he sends a screenshot or names a defect, fetch the live URL and the staged URL first and say which one his picture matches — bytes and head line, not a feeling. Before editing, name the source of truth — the artifact, the branch file, the live file — and edit that, never a copy. Hold a recommendation as a recommendation until he picks it — "Let's go with that" or a named choice — and when a repair completes, verify the exact change named and report what did not change in the same message. For each "what is" topic, build one frame in the most distilled, real, authentic language — same stage and format, short, child-clear, never scrolling; group the frames by kind; default to one full board across. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE STAR IS THE DM ORB:** the rating star is the DM initial orb with the initial swapped for a star — take the element whole, change only the content inside. VALUE is purple orbs with white stars; INTELLIGENCE is white orbs with purple stars. When a new element does not read, the fix is rarely a better invention — it is the element he already loves, reused whole.
2. **RATE THIS INTEL:** the heading is "Rate This Intel" — his words, exactly that — and the rate orb is the same flowing element, bigger, with flow around the OUTSIDE as well as inside. One element, three sizes: the DM initial orb, the rating star, the big rate orb.
3. **ALMOST MEANS THREE SMALL MOVES:** up a tad, in a tad, light down a little — not a redesign. A board that is almost there is one nudge from done and one redesign from ruined; small moves preserve what is already right and close only what is still open.
4. **PIN IT, AND ONLY PIN IT:** only the favorite ACTION becomes "Pin it." "Favorite Worlds" stays as it is. Pin = pin it to the top of the feed, or to a space, a business, a profile, a list — anywhere in Naya. An invention attached to his words is still an invention, even when it rides a change he approved.
5. **SAVE LANDS STRAIGHT IN:** one tap lands the item in the Smart Lists area, already filed, with organizing afterwards — never a big list popping up first. The Smart List must live where the saving happens: Personal, and Calendar too. Pin and Save stay distinct.
6. **CHECK WHICH BUILD HE'S LOOKING AT:** before judging his findings, fetch live and staged and say which one his picture matches — bytes and head line, not a feeling. Live Dashboard 1,817,928 B, outdated; his screenshot matches the staged orb-ring fix, 2,166,903 B, eye PASS Nov 19, staged only, not live.
7. **EDIT THE ARTIFACT, NOT THE EXPORT COPY:** the v31 retitle failed because the builder edited the export copy and the checker's export overwrote it. The artifact is the source of truth; the export is a copy that flows one way, out. The repair path is the repair-authorized inspection — never re-dispatch as an ordinary edit.
8. **A RECOMMENDATION IS NOT HIS PICK:** "The Invitation" never landed because he never picked it — "Let's go with that" is the pick; silence is not. The title stays "Welcome to NayaNET" by his order. Never prescribe a retitle to a recommended title; prescribe the pick, or hold the retitle until the pick lands.
9. **WHAT IS IT — NAME IT, CATEGORIZE IT:** every "what is" gets its own frame, in distilled form, categorized by kind — what we stand for, how we are governed, what it is built on. Four formats are tried; the most common is one full board across, because one distilled idea wants one big board. The final welcome board stays ONE big board.
10. **THE INTELLIGENT LIBRARY IS THE HOME OF THE LAW:** the Library becomes all our laws and constitutions and rules — like a search engine, they go there, search all the frames, pull up whatever one they want. The law stops living scattered across slides and gets one address, searchable.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the DM orb as the source, the round invents a second flow when the first one already flows — and spends its hour on a comet that doesn't read, while the element he already approved was sitting in the sidebar all along.
2. Without "Rate This Intel," the control is misnamed every time it is read — "Rate the Intelligence" sounds like grading a system; "Rate This Intel" says what it does, here, now.
3. Without the three small moves, the temptation when the eye says "almost" is to rebuild the board to be safe — and the rebuild loses the fit he just praised.
4. Without the pin-only correction, every word he did not say, carried as if he said it, costs him a correction — and he should never have to correct my naming.
5. Without save landing straight in, saving interrupts the moment by asking the citizen to choose a list first — and a Smart List that only exists in one place is a system the citizen cannot reach from where they are.
6. Without naming the build first, "fixed" and "still broken" are both guesses — and the round goes to fix a page he never saw.
7. Without editing the artifact, a round that reports "done" against a copy has done nothing to the page he will see — and the next export erases even the copy.
8. Without holding the recommendation as a recommendation, the board carries a name he never chose, and the record says he chose it — putting words in his mouth.
9. Without naming and categorizing the "what is" frames, a citizen who asks "what is CCT?" hunts through the constitution — while fifteen topics grouped by kind feel like one system, not fifteen links.
10. Without the Library, a law nobody can find is a law nobody can follow — frames without a home are a trail, not a library.

notes.title: The Four Boards and the One Frame
notes.subtitle:
Four new text boards go in, each underneath the slide it follows: after "You're Hired" — how you get paid, not MLM, not network marketing, nobody obligated to invite, NayaNET itself free like a social network, Naya Power the paid plug-in that connects your AI, share and you get paid 50% of revenue, a 9-day free trial, try before you buy; on "What's In It For You" — collective intelligence, a network where every AI and human shares wisdom without identity, smart notes as intelligent blocks that benefit everyone, Naya not an LLM herself but a supercharger that plugs into your AI, no one reading your mail or messages; after Mother Brain — the Vault, in a higher-end presentation, a digital vault on collective chain technology locked to you alone, the company, the AIs, and other users with no access, yours forever, any AI plugged in with your permission, the mailman delivering your mail and never reading it; and My World — shown "not an actual screenshot — 10× nicer," calendar, click any day, daily intel and reports, local, provincial, and global news, personal and business feeds, journal, timeline back to any day, stats, dashboard, smart ledger live, Bugatti-inspired speedometer gauges. The franchise board stays exactly as is, named so no seat "improves" it. And the boards do not stay one presentation's styling: "these board styles become the building blocks for memberships, about, skills, and the rest of the network — insert text / image / video and it presents at this level, no new pages built." The citizen swaps the N for their own logo or puts their face in the corners; the module carries the presentation, the citizen carries the mark. His words are the order, not the script: "Don't just echo him — think: is it 10/10, the most intelligent way to say it? Add text blocks where a slide needs them." An echo is a parrot; a Naya thinks. 5. **NOW MEANS NOW:** "No, I want to do it now." The Hub is finished tonight, with him present — the plan bends to the order, not the other way round. A staged link delivered is the start of his verdict, never the verdict itself.
6. **THE CARRY CLOSES ONLY WHEN MAIN HOLDS IT:** a live-only fix is a fix waiting to be reverted. Smallest verbatim change, the seven questions answered in writing, the captain's double-check, the merge verified by fresh read-back — old handler 0×, new handler 1×. Never force-update main's ref.
7. **TEN WAYS, SCORED AND RANKED, ONE RECOMMENDED:** options arrive scored on the tests that matter, ranked, with one named recommendation and why — The Invitation (44), over The Vow (44, tie broken by the closing line). A bare list hands him the decision back; if his pick hasn't arrived by build time, the round builds with the recommendation and says so.
8. **THE AI-OPERATED INTERNET:** the whole internet is connection plus content plus money — and NayaNET does all of it in one place, privately by default, at Naya speed, sharing 50% of the revenue with the people who share it. Judge every page against it: does it connect, does it share, does it pay, push-button simple?
9. **THE FINAL BOARD CARRIES THE WHOLE LAW IN LINKS:** fourteen links in a row below, each opening a frame with exactly the answer, in the most distilled intelligent real authentic language — never a wall of legal text, never fourteen pages where one board will do. Each answer is written from its named source, never invented.
