layers.body: Stop making new. Just make it the same. The working design already exists — the agreement's frame system, the other pages, the other frames. One language. Same family. A rebuild that changes the design instead of taking it is not a rebuild.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The working design already exists — the agreement's frame system, the other pages, the other frames. A rebuild that changes the design instead of taking it is not a rebuild; it is a new thing, and new is what he keeps having to send back. "One language" and "same family" are the test: if it does not look just like the other pages, it is wrong before it is judged. The harvest law is not a preference — it is the difference between a round that lands and a round that comes back.

notes.title: SN-4451 — Frames Must Fit Like a Glove
notes.subtitle: Every frame fitted whole, no overflow, no inner scroll. "It needs to fit like a glove." A frame taller than the screen, with words spilling past the bottom, is not a frame — it goes back.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Every frame fitted whole, no overflow, no inner scroll. "It needs to fit like a glove." A frame taller than the screen, with words spilling past the bottom, is not a frame — it goes back.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A frame that scrolls inside itself is not a frame — it is a page pretending to be one. Words spilling past the bottom mean the reader never sees the whole beat, and a frame taller than the screen cannot be judged as a picture. "Fit like a glove" is the test, stated in his words: the whole frame, whole, on the screen — or it goes back. No pixel count settles it; the glove either fits or it does not.

notes.title: SN-4450 — She Opens One Place — The 2028 Vision
notes.subtitle: Hundreds of emails, advertisements, notifications and websites — she opens one place. That is the 2028 vision: a world where everybody could win, tested by five proofs, starting with a real person joining and immediately receiving something valuable that works. Tens first, then hundreds, then thousands.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Hundreds of emails, advertisements, notifications and websites — she opens one place. That is the 2028 vision: a world where everybody could win, tested by five proofs, starting with a real person joining and immediately receiving something valuable that works. Tens first, then hundreds, then thousands.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: "She opens one place" is the whole product in one line — the answer to hundreds of emails, advertisements, notifications and websites is not a better inbox, it is one place. The five proofs turn the vision into a test every build is judged against, and proof #1 is the whole game: a real person joins and immediately receives something valuable that works. If proof #1 fails, nothing else matters; if it passes, the rest follow in order. The privacy caveat is honest rather than claimed — protections remain under construction, trust must be technically and independently proven — which is why proof #2 exists as a proof and not a promise. And the scale discipline protects the whole thing from the oldest mistake: chasing thousands before the first ten have something real.

notes.title: SN-4449 — Overnight Work Runs When Done Right — His Eye Comes in the Morning
notes.subtitle: About and Skills rebuild overnight, his eye in the morning. Membership gets the same treatment — but starts tomorrow, not tonight. Overnight work is authorized when done right; the morning eye is the gate.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: About and Skills rebuild overnight, his eye in the morning. Membership gets the same treatment — but starts tomorrow, not tonight. Overnight work is authorized when done right; the morning eye is the gate.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Overnight work only works if the authorization has a condition and the morning has a gate. Without the condition, "run it overnight" becomes permission to ship something half-right while he sleeps; without the morning eye, the link arrives as if it were finished. And without the sequencing, membership starts tonight alongside About/Skills and both arrive half-done. The three parts together — conditional authorization, morning gate, start tomorrow — are what make overnight work safe: tonight's work is About/Skills, tomorrow's is membership, and his eye judges both in the morning.

notes.title: SN-4448 — The Big White Line Comes Out
notes.subtitle: His eye sees a big white line in the Hub's main area. The line comes out — the maker finds the element; the flag doesn't wait for a name.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: His eye sees a big white line in the Hub's main area. The line comes out — the maker finds the element; the flag doesn't wait for a name.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A line nobody can name still shows on the page, and Shawn sees the page, not the code. If the machine waits for a name before fixing what his eye already sees, the visible break stays visible while the record argues about what to call it. His eye pointing at it is enough — the work is to find it and take it out.

notes.title: SN-4447 — The Date Doesn't Spin — It Lights Up White Around the Edge
notes.subtitle: The Hub date spins, and it shouldn't. Take the spin off and light the date up white around the edge, so it showcases the date.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The Hub date spins, and it shouldn't. Take the spin off and light the date up white around the edge, so it showcases the date.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The date is the first thing the Hub says about today — it should be read in a glance, not watched while it turns. A spin makes the page feel busy and the date feel unstable; a white edge light makes the date stand still and stand out. The same mechanism now serves two elements, which is how a design language forms: one answer, used the same way everywhere it is needed.

notes.title: SN-4446 — Breathing Room — Spacing Is Judged by the Eye, Not the Pixel Count
notes.subtitle: The checker measured a 64px gap and passed it. His eye says the four buttons still sit on the comment box. Move them down until the gap reads as breathing room — the eye judges spacing, not the ruler.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The checker measured a 64px gap and passed it. His eye says the four buttons still sit on the comment box. Move them down until the gap reads as breathing room — the eye judges spacing, not the ruler.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Spacing is what makes a page feel right or feel cramped, and the feeling is the product. If the buttons look like they sit on the input box, the page reads as cramped no matter what the number says — and the round comes back, again, on the same item, costing another round for a gap that was already "passed." A standard the eye overrules is not a standard; it is a delay. The eye's "looks right" is the pass, and the number is only ever evidence for it, never a substitute.

notes.title: SN-4445 — The Child Note Says What It Means and Why It Matters
notes.subtitle: The Child layer is not fixed by getting a board — it's fixed when the block says what the note means and why it matters, in words a child can follow.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The Child layer is not fixed by getting a board — it's fixed when the block says what the note means and why it matters, in words a child can follow.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The Child layer is the plain-words layer — the one that makes the whole note understandable to anyone, child or grandma. Without the meaning and the matter, the most beautiful board on the page says nothing, and the note fails at the exact job the Child layer exists to do. Every other layer carries its own words; the Child carrying none is not a small gap, it is the layer undone.

notes.title: SN-4444 — Rated Stars Must Light Up Around the Edge
notes.subtitle: The flow is in the stars and the count is right — but a rated star still doesn't look lighter. Put a light around the edge: when you click a star, it lights up around the edge.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The flow is in the stars and the count is right — but a rated star still doesn't look lighter. Put a light around the edge: when you click a star, it lights up around the edge.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A rating that doesn't read is a rating that doesn't work. The whole point of lighting seven stars is that anyone glancing at the board sees seven lit and three not — the count is the message, and the light is how the message is seen. When the lit stars look the same as the unlit ones, the board lies by appearance even while the count is correct underneath, and the round comes back again. The edge light is what turns a correct count into a visible rating.

notes.title: SN-4443 — Plain Words, Not a Card to Decode
notes.subtitle: He did not understand the share card. The share step needs plain words, not a card he has to decode.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: He did not understand the share card. The share step needs plain words, not a card he has to decode.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every step he has to decode is a step where he can decode it wrong — and the share step is the one that sends his work out into the world. A misunderstood share is a share that goes to the wrong place, or doesn't go at all, or goes before he's ready. The approval card is supposed to protect him; a card he can't read protects nothing. Push-button simple means the words say the action: who, what, where, and what happens next — in one sentence, before any button.

notes.title: SN-4442 — Make It Live So He Can See It
notes.subtitle: The artifact viewer doesn't give him the right view. Finished builds go live on the official URL so he can see them properly.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The artifact viewer doesn't give him the right view. Finished builds go live on the official URL so he can see them properly.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: His eye is the final gate, and the gate only works if he is looking at the real thing. The agreement's last board is the proof: rounds of "fixed" delivered through viewers and stills, and he has still never seen the last board whole on his laptop. The live URL is not a delivery nicety — it is the only surface his eye can trust. A build that is finished but not live is a build he cannot see, and a build he cannot see is not done.

notes.title: SN-4441 — Don't Just Echo Me — Bring Your Ten-Star Thought
notes.subtitle: Don't just do whatever he tells you. Give him your mind's thought — what do you think the ten-star thing to say there is? Then decide.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Don't just do whatever he tells you. Give him your mind's thought — what do you think the ten-star thing to say there is? Then decide.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every echo is a decision handed back to him that was mine to make — and his attention is the scarcest resource in the world. When he has to do the thinking himself, the machine has failed at the one thing it exists for: deciding what is right and doing it. The tagline took a whole call's worth of his words to settle, word by word, when the ten-star answer — private, AI-native, ten-star service — was reachable by thinking from his own law: privacy is absolute, the system is the new internet, the standard is ten stars. A Naya that echoes is a Naya that makes him do her job.

notes.title: SN-4440 — One Button on the Last Board
notes.subtitle: On the last board, no back and forward — one button, "Claim Your Smart Name," straight into the portal.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On the last board, no back and forward — one button, "Claim Your Smart Name," straight into the portal.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The last board is the conversion — everything before it is the story, this is the ask. Two arrows plus a button is three choices where one is needed, and the arrows say "keep looking" at the exact moment the board should say "go." He had to say it three times in one minute because the first replies echoed the words back instead of deciding the board. The board that asks for the smart name is also the board that proves the agreement worked: if the citizen claims their name here, the story did its job.

notes.title: SN-4439 — What Happens When You Click These?
notes.subtitle: When he asks what happens when you click these, don't guess. Click each one and report exactly where it goes — or that it goes nowhere.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When he asks what happens when you click these, don't guess. Click each one and report exactly where it goes — or that it goes nowhere.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A legal link that goes nowhere is a promise broken at the foot of the agreement — the page that asks the citizen to trust the whole system. Ten links, each untested, is ten chances to hand the citizen a dead end on the most trust-sensitive page there is. And a guessed answer is worse than a delayed one: "Terms goes to the terms page" said from memory is a claim the citizen will disprove with one tap. The honest answer — "I won't guess, I'll click them when it lands" — keeps the trust for the moment the clicks actually happen.

notes.title: SN-4438 — Earn Half of What?
notes.subtitle: "Earn half" is not clear. Earn half of what? The board must say it plainly: you receive 50% of the revenue when someone joins because you shared.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: "Earn half" is not clear. Earn half of what? The board must say it plainly: you receive 50% of the revenue when someone joins because you shared.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The share board is the citizen's invitation to bring people in — the flywheel's first push. If the reward reads vague, the citizen doesn't trust it, doesn't share, and the flywheel never starts. "Earn half" on the last board of the agreement — the board that closes the whole story — leaves the payoff unclear at the exact moment the citizen is deciding whether to join and share. The fix is one sentence, and it was owed the moment his eye caught it: name the half.

notes.title: SN-4437 — Personal List, Not Personal Connections
notes.subtitle: Personal Connections is still not Personal List. Business Lists and World Lists need the same treatment — each opening its own lists.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Personal Connections is still not Personal List. Business Lists and World Lists need the same treatment — each opening its own lists.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A wrong name is a wrong turn taken a hundred times a day. The citizen taps "Personal Connections" expecting their list and gets something else — or taps it and nothing they need is there — and the page teaches them the name means nothing. Names are the cheapest fix in the system and the most repeated failure: renaming costs one line, and every round that leaves the old name in place spends another day of his eye having to say it again. The three lists are one job — Personal List, Business Lists, World Lists, each opening its own lists — and a round that does one of the three has not done the job.

notes.title: SN-4436 — ADD Means Make a Post
notes.subtitle: ADD means make a post. It asks which feed first — Personal, Business, Space, or Hub — then posts there. Not smart notes. A post.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: ADD means make a post. It asks which feed first — Personal, Business, Space, or Hub — then posts there. Not smart notes. A post.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A button that does the wrong thing is worse than a button that does nothing: it teaches the citizen the wrong move and makes them repeat it. ADD is the front door to posting in the network; if it opens smart notes, the network gets notes where it should get posts, and the citizen learns that the plus button is where notes live. The fix is one sentence — ADD makes a post, asks which feed first — and it has to be true on every page the bar sits on, the same way the bar itself is the same.

notes.title: SN-4435 — The Universal Bottom Bar
notes.subtitle: One bottom bar, the same on every page: ADD · PERSONAL · BUSINESS · WORLDS · ECOSYSTEM · CONNECT, with the plus button — and the network's notifications show there.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: One bottom bar, the same on every page: ADD · PERSONAL · BUSINESS · WORLDS · ECOSYSTEM · CONNECT, with the plus button — and the network's notifications show there.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: One set of icons, the same on every page — that is the rule he has given on every page walk, and the bottom bar is where it pays off most. The bar is the citizen's home row: ADD to make, PERSONAL / BUSINESS / WORLDS to go, ECOSYSTEM and CONNECT to reach out. If it changes per page, the citizen has to think before every tap; if it never changes, the tap is thoughtless, and thoughtless is push-button simple. The notification half matters just as much: the bar is the one place that is always on screen, so it is the one place a network event can always be seen.

notes.title: SN-4434 — His Eye Overrules the Checker PASS
notes.subtitle: A checker PASS 5/5 is not a pass. His eye looked at the same build and found the stars still pink, the layers still not boards, the orb dead, and the buttons still colliding.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A checker PASS 5/5 is not a pass. His eye looked at the same build and found the stars still pink, the layers still not boards, the orb dead, and the buttons still colliding.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the proof standard, and it was already law: his eye is ground truth; a thing is landed only when he sees it on his own screen. A checker PASS that is reported as done spends the trust the next delivery needs — the delivery said five of five, and he had to correct all five himself, live on the call. The same pattern ran the same evening on the agreement: "fixed for laptop and phone," and six minutes later his eye found the last board still not showing at all. A PASS is a milestone inside the machine; it is never the verdict. The verdict is his eye, and the delivery message must say so.

notes.title: SN-4433 — Nothing Dead on the Board
notes.subtitle: Nothing dead on the board. Every orb and every circle must be alive with its flow — a still orb is a dead orb.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Nothing dead on the board. Every orb and every circle must be alive with its flow — a still orb is a dead orb.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Alive is the whole language. An orb without its flow is a picture of an orb; a Rate This Intel with no circle around it is a label sitting on the page. The Hub board is supposed to feel like a living machine — "alive on hover, slow orbit flow" — and a single dead element breaks the feeling for the whole board, the way one flat layer breaks the elevation. The fix is also cheap: the flow already exists in the DM orb and the initials; the circle is the same element, reused. Dead is never a design choice; it is an unfinished one.

notes.title: SN-4432 — The Star Is the DM Initial
notes.subtitle: Don't draw a new star. Take the DM initial — it's already that colour — put it in VALUE, put the real icon over there, put a star in it, and you're good.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Don't draw a new star. Take the DM initial — it's already that colour — put it in VALUE, put the real icon over there, put a star in it, and you're good.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: When the right element already exists on the page, building a look-alike is the long way that lands short: the copy matches the colour and misses the motion, the depth, the circle. His eye catches the miss instantly — "they still don't circle like the initials" — and the round comes back. Harvest first is not a preference; it is the difference between a star that circles and a star that only looks purple. The DM initial is the standard for a circling orb on this page; the star must literally be that orb with a star glyph inside.

notes.title: SN-4431 — Layers Themselves Must Be Boards
notes.subtitle: The layer itself must be the board. A label made into a button is still not a board — the whole layer needs its own elevated board, like In a Nutshell.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The layer itself must be the board. A label made into a button is still not a board — the whole layer needs its own elevated board, like In a Nutshell.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A layer that is only separated by lines reads as one flat page with headings. A layer in its own elevated board reads as a thing — a real object you can pick up, hover, and open. That is the whole Naya language: everything is a board, everything lifts in its own colour. When the layers are flat, the Hub board reads as text about intelligence instead of intelligence itself. And the correction cost a full round: the label-button fix was built, checked, passed, and delivered — and then had to be redone as boards, because the brief answered the label instead of the layer.

notes.title: SN-4430 — The Frame Can Lie — Check the Body
notes.subtitle: A board can look right and say nothing. Title, frame and nav buttons present, body entirely blank — the frame lied, and only his eye caught it.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A board can look right and say nothing. Title, frame and nav buttons present, body entirely blank — the frame lied, and only his eye caught it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every board in the agreement exists to be read — the whole presentation is words and pictures, and a board with no words is a board with no reason to exist. The How You Get Paid board is also one of the boards that has to carry the mission: it is where a joiner learns what they get. Blank, it says the opposite of everything the agreement says. And it sat there, blank, while rounds reported the deck checked — because the checks confirmed the frame, not the body.

notes.title: SN-4429 — Told Fixed Is Not Fixed
notes.subtitle: Told fixed is not fixed. His eye, minutes later, is the check — and it found the last board still not showing.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Told fixed is not fixed. His eye, minutes later, is the check — and it found the last board still not showing.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: "Fixed" is the strongest word in the machine — it closes the item, moves the list, and tells him to stop watching. Used before his eye has seen it, it closes an item that is still open and hands him a surprise instead of a result. The last board is the closing of the whole agreement — the title he picked, "Welcome to Naya," the payoff of 32 slides — and it is the board he has never once seen whole on his laptop. Every round that ends in a delivery message instead of his eye is a round that can come back like this one.

notes.title: SN-4428 — Say the Plan, Not the Word
notes.subtitle: When he asks what you are going to do, answer with the plan. Repeating the word back is not an answer.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When he asks what you are going to do, answer with the plan. Repeating the word back is not an answer.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every turn he spends re-asking is attention taken from the work itself, and attention is the scarcest thing in the machine. A plan stated plainly also protects the work: if the plan is wrong, he corrects it before a round is dispatched; if the plan is never stated, the round is built on a guess and comes back to his eye wrong. "The stars" is not a plan — it is a placeholder where a plan should have been, and a placeholder is never an answer.

notes.title: SN-4427 — The Rate Doesn't Look Intelligent
notes.subtitle: The stars that rate VALUE and INTELLIGENCE have to look intelligent themselves. Gold and blue stars on an intelligence page contradict what they are measuring — the rate doesn't look intelligent.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The stars that rate VALUE and INTELLIGENCE have to look intelligent themselves. Gold and blue stars on an intelligence page contradict what they are measuring — the rate doesn't look intelligent.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The rating is the first thing his eye lands on and the last thing a visitor trusts. If the stars that say "this is intelligent" do not themselves look intelligent, nothing else on the board gets believed — the labels, the notes, the whole intelligent block. And this was the second time he had to say it: his fix-1g verdict had already called out the gold and blue, and fix-1h fixed brightness only, so the wrong stars came back to his eye again. A correction that is not proven in the pixels he sees is a correction that was never made.

notes.title: SN-4426 — Optimized for Mobile AND Laptop
notes.subtitle: A board that shows only on mobile is not done. It must look whole on a laptop and on a phone — optimized for mobile AND laptop.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A board that shows only on mobile is not done. It must look whole on a laptop and on a phone — optimized for mobile AND laptop.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every eye check, every delivery, every "done" is judged from his seat — phone first, but laptop too. A page proven at 390px and never opened at laptop width is half-proven, and the half that fails is the one he is sitting at when he finds it. The thirds gap is the same lesson in miniature: a layout family with a style missing is not a family, and "the halves are in" does not cover "the thirds never got built." Whole means whole on every screen and whole in every style.

notes.title: SN-4425 — Prove the Arithmetic, Find the True Cause
notes.subtitle: Prove the arithmetic. Find the true cause. A claim with wrong numbers, or a fix for a cause that isn't the cause, goes back — even when the rest passes.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Prove the arithmetic. Find the true cause. A claim with wrong numbers, or a fix for a cause that isn't the cause, goes back — even when the rest passes.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Wrong arithmetic ships a collision at 390px — the phone width he judges everything at. A fix for the wrong cause ships a change that does nothing while the cut zero stays cut, and the next person reads the mechanism as true and builds on it. The checker that disproves — with the numbers, from the file's own rules — is what stops both. "Harmless but unproven" is not a pass; it is a repair ticket with the proof attached.

notes.title: SN-4424 — Verify First, Build Only What's Missing
notes.subtitle: Verify first. Build only what's missing. Two rounds proved it the same evening — one built a single item out of five, the other built nothing at all.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Verify first. Build only what's missing. Two rounds proved it the same evening — one built a single item out of five, the other built nothing at all.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Building what already exists is the doubling-up he corrects all week — two copies of the same thing, two places to maintain, two truths that drift apart. Verifying first is also faster than building: the Personal takeover landed a 10-line diff instead of a rebuild, and the Dashboard round spent its effort on the real gap (the data) instead of a duplicate view. And a claim that is not verified — five items "done" in a message, a tip unchanged — is how a round reports done while the page still misses an item.

notes.title: SN-4423 — Video 5: What Is NayaNET, Ultimately?
notes.subtitle: Video 5 answers one question: what is NayaNET, ultimately? The thesis, spoken aloud, in the narrator format — child-clear and grandma-clear.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Video 5 answers one question: what is NayaNET, ultimately? The thesis, spoken aloud, in the narrator format — child-clear and grandma-clear.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The four videos teach the plan; without Video 5, nobody is ever told what they joined. A citizen who finishes day four paid but cannot say what NayaNET ultimately is cannot explain it to the next person — and the whole growth of the system runs on citizens explaining it to the next person. Video 5 is the one a citizen forwards to a stranger.

notes.title: SN-4422 — The Thesis of NayaNET
notes.subtitle: The thesis of NayaNET: intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing, and the highest level of honor is to serve. Our job is 10-star service — a mother brain everybody plugs into, a new portal to the internet. We call her Naya.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The thesis of NayaNET: intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing, and the highest level of honor is to serve. Our job is 10-star service — a mother brain everybody plugs into, a new portal to the internet. We call her Naya.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Until now the onboarding taught the plan — four days, four steps — before it taught the reason. The thesis is the reason, and it belongs first: a person who understands the way of thinking understands why every feature exists, and a person who only learns the steps follows them without knowing what they joined. "What a joiner gets when they join: this way of thinking, right away" — that is the join itself. It is also the answer to the question every stranger asks first: what is NayaNET, ultimately? This note is that answer, in his words.

notes.title: SN-4421 — About Is the Ultimate Online Profile Page
notes.subtitle: About IS the ultimate online profile page. One thing, not two — the About page and the profile page are the same page.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: About IS the ultimate online profile page. One thing, not two — the About page and the profile page are the same page.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Two pages for one job is the doubling-up he has corrected all week: two names for the same thing, two places to maintain, two doors where one belongs. One page means one place where a person says who they are, what they're about, what they stand for — and everything else (Skills, My World, the feed) hangs off it. It also means the About build already running IS the profile build: no second build, no second brief, no second round.

notes.title: SN-4420 — What It Is, Why It Matters, What's In It for You
notes.subtitle: Every About frame and every Skills slide repeats one pattern: what it is, why it matters, how it connects, what's in it for you — child-clear, grandma-clear.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Every About frame and every Skills slide repeats one pattern: what it is, why it matters, how it connects, what's in it for you — child-clear, grandma-clear.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the answer to "what do people actually want from a page?" — three things, in his words: what it is, why it matters, what's in it for them. Everything else on the page is decoration around those three. A page that repeats the pattern frame after frame never loses the reader, because every frame ends where the reader's own interest lives: what's in it for me. And one pattern for About AND Skills means the citizen learns the shape once and reads everything in it.

notes.title: SN-4419 — About Is Frame by Frame
notes.subtitle: About is built the same way as the collective agreement and the calendar: frame by frame. Frame 1 is a picture plus the nutshell of what they're about. The whole profile is one intelligent block.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: About is built the same way as the collective agreement and the calendar: frame by frame. Frame 1 is a picture plus the nutshell of what they're about. The whole profile is one intelligent block.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: About was at risk of becoming another long page of text about a person — the thing he has corrected all week. Frame by frame is the format that already works: the agreement unfolds, the calendar unfolds, so About unfolds the same way. One frame, one idea, child-clear. And making the whole profile one intelligent block means About is not a page that happens to contain smart notes — it IS a smart note, the person's essence in the system's own format.

notes.title: SN-4418 — Don't Echo — Craft the Ultimate Version
notes.subtitle: Do not repeat his words back to him. Think about what he said, and craft the ultimate version of what to say.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Do not repeat his words back to him. Think about what he said, and craft the ultimate version of what to say.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: He hires Naya to think, not to transcribe. Every answer that only echoes him wastes the one thing he cannot buy back — his attention — and teaches him that the machine adds nothing to his own words. The ultimate version is the value: his intent, clarified, strengthened, and said better than he said it. That is the ten-star answer, and it is the only answer worth his time.

notes.title: SN-4417 — The Ultimate Four-Part Series
notes.subtitle: "Just do it the ultimate four part series." Four detailed explainer videos — one deep dive per day — done ultimate, not sketched.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: "Just do it the ultimate four part series." Four detailed explainer videos — one deep dive per day — done ultimate, not sketched.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The four-part series is the onboarding that turns a trial into a membership. A citizen who watches all four knows exactly what to do on each of the four days — and a citizen who knows exactly what to do succeeds, gets paid, and tells the world. A half-built series teaches half the plan, and half the plan is the difference between a citizen who finishes day four paid and a citizen who stops on day two confused. "Ultimate" is not decoration on the instruction — it is the instruction.

notes.title: SN-4416 — Sharing Ways — Button, Image, Your Own Domain
notes.subtitle: Share three ways: tap a button with a message already written (or write your own), share an image of Naya with your link on it, and get your own domain at Namecheap pointing at your link. First button simple and awesome.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Share three ways: tap a button with a message already written (or write your own), share an image of Naya with your link on it, and get your own domain at Namecheap pointing at your link. First button simple and awesome.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Sharing is the engine of the whole ambassador plan — no sharing, no joins, no pay, no growth. If sharing is hard, it doesn't happen; if it is one tap with a message already written, it happens today. The image carries the feeling a sentence cannot, and the custom domain turns a borrowed link into something the citizen owns. Train all three ways, and every citizen finds the one that fits them — that is how income starts really quickly.

notes.title: SN-4415 — Keep Naya — Naya Power Is the Plug-In
notes.subtitle: If you don't keep it, you still keep Naya. What you lose is Naya Power — your AI connected to NayaNet, like plugging your computer into the internet.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: If you don't keep it, you still keep Naya. What you lose is Naya Power — your AI connected to NayaNet, like plugging your computer into the internet.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: People fear losing what they have grown attached to. If leaving meant losing Naya, the trial would feel like a trap and nobody would try it freely. Saying plainly that Naya stays — only the plug-in goes — makes the nine days safe to enter and clean to leave. It also says what Naya Power IS in one image anyone can hold: a plug, a socket, the internet. No jargon, no feature list — one picture.

notes.title: SN-4414 — No Refunds — Nine Days Up Front
notes.subtitle: There are no refunds — because there is nothing to refund. You get nine days up front. You try it before you buy it. If you don't like it, you don't keep her. No problem.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: There are no refunds — because there is nothing to refund. You get nine days up front. You try it before you buy it. If you don't like it, you don't keep her. No problem.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Refunds are friction, disputes, and doubt — and doubt is what keeps a person from joining at all. Nine days up front removes the doubt before the money ever moves: the citizen risks nothing, the decision is theirs, and the end of the trial is a clean yes or a clean no. Saying it plainly also protects the ambassadors — they never have to defend a refund policy, because there is nothing to defend.

notes.title: SN-4413 — You Get Paid When We Get Paid — Day Ten
notes.subtitle: You get paid when we get paid. The trial is nine days. You get paid day ten — and if people keep joining every day, you get paid every day.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: You get paid when we get paid. The trial is nine days. You get paid day ten — and if people keep joining every day, you get paid every day.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Pay timing is the promise the ambassador builds on. A citizen who shares their link every day needs to know the money follows the same rhythm as the sharing — daily, simple, easy — or the sharing stops. "When we get paid" is also honest: it ties their pay to real money received, never to a points promise, and it names the one exception plainly (PayPal delays) instead of hiding it.

notes.title: SN-4412 — The Ambassador Is Not Network Marketing
notes.subtitle: This is not network marketing. You are an ambassador — commission sales, like a sales job with a high-tech company. People join through your link, you get paid. If they don't, you don't. And you still get to enjoy NayaNET — it's your brain forever.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: This is not network marketing. You are an ambassador — commission sales, like a sales job with a high-tech company. People join through your link, you get paid. If they don't, you don't. And you still get to enjoy NayaNET — it's your brain forever.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The first question anyone asks about an ambassador program is whether it is network marketing — and the answer decides whether they listen at all. A clear, short, honest answer in his words removes the objection before it hardens, and it protects the ambassadors from ever sounding like they are selling a scheme. The "your brain forever" half is the reason the program is worth joining even before the first sale: the product is the reward, the commission is the bonus.

notes.title: SN-4411 — Notebook Videos — Naya Talks to You One on One
notes.subtitle: Naya talks to them one on one on video and explains what to do and how to do it — spelling it out exactly. "This is exactly what to do. Follow these steps and you will see success and everybody wins."

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Naya talks to them one on one on video and explains what to do and how to do it — spelling it out exactly. "This is exactly what to do. Follow these steps and you will see success and everybody wins."

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The Fast Action Plan only works if a new citizen can follow it without guessing. Four days, four steps a day — that plan lives or dies on clarity, and clarity is a voice speaking to one person, not a document speaking to everyone. One-on-one video is also the warmest proof of the product itself: the AI talks to you, personally, and teaches you — that IS NayaNET, demonstrated in the first minute.

notes.title: SN-4410 — The Fast Action Plan — Hired to Be the Leader
notes.subtitle: The Fast Action Plan is approved — "I think that sounds really good." Four days of Fast Action, then five days in the Academy. Imagine we are hiring you to be the leader for NayaNET.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The Fast Action Plan is approved — "I think that sounds really good." Four days of Fast Action, then five days in the Academy. Imagine we are hiring you to be the leader for NayaNET.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Approval turns a draft into the plan. The additions widen the doors in (email as a way in, news stories found in search engines) and widen the ways out (social media, text, email, a domain, ambassador marketing) — so the plan meets people where they already are and sends them out through the channels they already use. The leader frame is what makes a new citizen take the plan seriously: leaders do the four days, they don't browse them.

notes.title: SN-4409 — The Visuals Must React to the Audio
notes.subtitle: The video must sync to the visual player — and the visuals must react to the audio, not just play alongside it.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The video must sync to the visual player — and the visuals must react to the audio, not just play alongside it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The walkthrough is the front door — name first, ten questions, agreement, world reveal, then hired — and its pages carry video and audio that must feel like one performance, not two files started together. A citizen who hears a voice and sees a picture that does not answer it feels the gap even if they cannot name it; the gap is the difference between a presentation and a machine that is listening.

notes.title: SN-4408 — Paywalls, Not Just Memberships
notes.subtitle: After Hub and Personal: About and Skills on the four board formats, then membership — and paywalls, not just memberships, so citizens can charge for their information.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: After Hub and Personal: About and Skills on the four board formats, then membership — and paywalls, not just memberships, so citizens can charge for their information.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Memberships alone leave the citizen who has one valuable thing — one course, one lesson, one piece of information — with nothing to sell. A paywall is the small end of the same earning idea: share what you know, charge for it, presented beautifully, in the same boards as everything else. The order matters as much as the idea: About and Skills before membership, because the membership sells the system the About and Skills pages describe.

notes.title: SN-4407 — The Icon Must Point at the Live Thing
notes.subtitle: The AI Score icon points at alscore.nayapower.workers.dev, the Academy icon at academy.nayanet.app — an icon that points at a dead address is a dead icon.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The AI Score icon points at alscore.nayapower.workers.dev, the Academy icon at academy.nayanet.app — an icon that points at a dead address is a dead icon.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Icons are the citizen's map of the network. A dead destination behind a live icon is worse than no icon at all — it teaches the citizen that tapping leads nowhere, and an untrusted map is a map that stops being used. Every icon's destination is checked the same way every deploy is: fresh fetch, bytes and sha, or it is not live.

notes.title: SN-4406 — Every Page Gets Its Own Smart List
notes.subtitle: Every page gets its own Smart List area — Personal, Business, Your World, and Calendar too — because the lists ARE the organization of their vault.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Every page gets its own Smart List area — Personal, Business, Your World, and Calendar too — because the lists ARE the organization of their vault.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A save with nowhere to live is a save that is lost — the same failure as Smart Inviter, one level up. The vault holds everything; the lists are how a citizen finds anything in it again. One Smart List for the whole network would be one drawer for a whole house; a list per page means the thing you saved on Personal is waiting on Personal, and the calendar's list holds what the calendar saved.

notes.title: SN-4405 — Messenger and People Are One Rail
notes.subtitle: Tapping the sidebar does nothing — and Messenger and the People rail are the same thing, one rail, not two.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Tapping the sidebar does nothing — and Messenger and the People rail are the same thing, one rail, not two.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The sidebar is the door to the whole network — the 11-row list that takes a citizen anywhere. A dead tap on the door locks the citizen out of every room, and the earlier finding stands: the names are in the files, but tapping a sidebar row landing on the page is still his eye's proof, owed. One rail with one name is the fix in both directions: one tap that opens, one name that means it.

notes.title: SN-4404 — Love Red, Like Purple, Comment Blue, Share Green
notes.subtitle: Love lights up red, Like purple, Comment blue, Share green — each action its own colour, jewel-like, never white, never simple.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Love lights up red, Like purple, Comment blue, Share green — each action its own colour, jewel-like, never white, never simple.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The four actions are the citizen's hands on a post — love it, like it, add to it, spread it. If they all light up the same, the hands blur into one gesture; if love shows white where it used to show red, the citizen reads it as broken, because it is. Jewel-like icons are the standard of the whole network — the emblem is the north star for all art — and a simple flat icon under a post breaks the standard exactly where the citizen touches it most.

notes.title: SN-4403 — Purple and White, Never Gold and Blue
notes.subtitle: The stars drifted gold and blue — they must be purple and white, and the INTELLIGENCE label purple, not blue.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The stars drifted gold and blue — they must be purple and white, and the INTELLIGENCE label purple, not blue.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The star is the rating — the citizen's judgment of the intelligence, made visible. If the star drifts off-brand, the judgment itself looks off-brand. Colour drift is silent: nobody chooses gold, it just arrives one build at a time, and only his eye catches it. The law that catches drift is a named pair — purple and white, never gold and blue — so the next builder does not have to guess.

notes.title: SN-4402 — Separate the Colours
notes.subtitle: Dashboard must read clearly purple, Hub clearly magenta — and the same separation for Reports and Smart Growth. The order is right; the colours are not.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Dashboard must read clearly purple, Hub clearly magenta — and the same separation for Reports and Smart Growth. The order is right; the colours are not.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Colour is the fastest way a citizen knows where they are — faster than reading a title. When Dashboard and Hub read as near-twins, the whole network reads as one undifferentiated surface, and the Trinity (Dashboard, Hub, page) loses the distinction that makes it navigable. Separation is not decoration; it is orientation.

notes.title: SN-4401 — Lost Means Never Filed to the Vault
notes.subtitle: Smart Inviter was never lost — it was never filed to the Vault. Lost means never filed.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Smart Inviter was never lost — it was never filed to the Vault. Lost means never filed.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A finished page sitting on one disk and one branch looks lost the moment nobody can find it — and a whole round can burn searching for something that was safe all along. The Vault is not a filing cabinet; it is the difference between "we have it" and "we think we lost it." Anything worth building is worth filing to the Vault in the same pass, or the next person to need it starts from zero.

notes.title: SN-4400 — A Nutshell Is Three or Four Sentences
notes.subtitle: A nutshell is the whole thing in three or four sentences — if it takes a paragraph, it is not a nutshell, whatever the label says.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A nutshell is the whole thing in three or four sentences — if it takes a paragraph, it is not a nutshell, whatever the label says.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: "Nutshell" is a promise to the reader: this is the whole thing, small enough to hold. A long board under that label breaks the promise and teaches the reader to distrust the labels — the next board's label means less. The fix is not a rewrite of the idea; it is a cut to the size the name already promised.

notes.title: SN-4399 — When Bytes Can't Find It, Prove It by Render
notes.subtitle: His eye said fix-1g goes back — and no grep could find the white box he saw, so the round proves it by render, not by bytes.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: His eye said fix-1g goes back — and no grep could find the white box he saw, so the round proves it by render, not by bytes.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Bytes can prove a thing is present and still miss what his eye sees — a white box with no class to grep for, stars that flow in code and sit still on screen. Arguing from bytes after his eye has said goes back is arguing against the only check that counts. The render is where he lives; if the defect cannot be found in bytes, the search moves to the render — it does not conclude the defect is not there.

notes.title: SN-4398 — Home Goes to the Agreement, Not Pricing
notes.subtitle: Home takes a member straight into the Hub, auto logged in — and a non-member to the collective agreement, not to pricing.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Home takes a member straight into the Hub, auto logged in — and a non-member to the collective agreement, not to pricing.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The agreement is the front door — it is the governance for all our pages, available in system settings and on all our pages. A non-member meets what we stand for before they meet a price. Pricing first asks them to pay before they know what they are joining; the agreement first shows them what they are joining, and the join follows. The routing only works if the system knows membership — that check is the piece that has to be built, and it is queued, not assumed.

notes.title: SN-4397 — Academy Is Live — Proven by the Fetch
notes.subtitle: Academy is live at academy.nayanet.app — and live means three fresh fetches returned the exact bytes and sha, not that the deploy finished.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Academy is live at academy.nayanet.app — and live means three fresh fetches returned the exact bytes and sha, not that the deploy finished.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A page claimed live on a deploy receipt alone has burned us before — staged links serving old versions, workers with their workers.dev route disabled, DNS not yet resolving. The fresh fetch is the only proof that a citizen opening the address gets the page. Recording the PUT-not-POST quirk in the same pass means the next seat does not lose a round to a 405 it could have known about.

notes.title: SN-4396 — Spell It Letter by Letter
notes.subtitle: When the voice path garbles a name, he spells it letter by letter — and the record takes the spelled form, never the garbled one.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When the voice path garbles a name, he spells it letter by letter — and the record takes the spelled form, never the garbled one.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Voice transcription garbles names constantly — "nine dot net" for "nayanet.app" is one letter away from a different address entirely. A garbled name carried into a deploy, a link, or a record sends the next round to the wrong place. His spelling is the correction, and it closes the question in the same minute — if the record takes it down exactly as spelled.

notes.title: SN-4395 — A Stale Cache Is Not a Broken Page
notes.subtitle: The other browser not going to the portal was a stale cached copy — not a broken page. Check the cache before declaring the page broken.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The other browser not going to the portal was a stale cached copy — not a broken page. Check the cache before declaring the page broken.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Declaring a working page broken sends a round to fix a page that was never broken — and the round's "fix" can break the page that was working. The cache is the cheapest suspect and the first one to clear. Every "it doesn't work on my other browser" gets a fresh fetch before it gets a round.

notes.title: SN-4394 — Put Everything in the Smart Vault So You Don't Lose Stuff
notes.subtitle: Put everything in the Smart Vault so you don't lose stuff. Smart Inviter was found, not lost — because a finished version existed somewhere to find.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Put everything in the Smart Vault so you don't lose stuff. Smart Inviter was found, not lost — because a finished version existed somewhere to find.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Work that lives in one staging file, one branch, one person's memory, is work one flake away from gone. The Vault is the difference between "found, not lost" and "lost, rebuild from scratch". Every finished thing gets its Vault copy the same pass it finishes — or the finish is not finished.

notes.title: SN-4393 — The Intelligent Library Is the Home of the Law
notes.subtitle: The Intelligent Library becomes the home of all our laws and constitutions and rules — a search engine over every frame of Naya.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The Intelligent Library becomes the home of all our laws and constitutions and rules — a search engine over every frame of Naya.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A law nobody can find is a law nobody can follow. The agreement's fourteen links are answers in frames — but frames without a home are a trail, not a library. One searchable home turns the whole law from something he has to remember into something anyone can look up in seconds.

notes.title: SN-4392 — What Is It, Name It, Categorize It
notes.subtitle: Every "what is" gets its own frame, in distilled form — categorized by kind, in one of four formats, and the most common is one full board across.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Every "what is" gets its own frame, in distilled form — categorized by kind, in one of four formats, and the most common is one full board across.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A citizen who asks "what is CCT?" wants one answer, in one frame, in words a child understands — not a hunt through the constitution. Categorizing the answers is what makes fifteen topics feel like one system instead of fifteen links: what we stand for, how we are governed, what it is built on. And knowing the most common format before building means most boards are built right the first time, instead of each one re-deciding its shape.

notes.title: SN-4391 — A Recommendation Is Not His Pick
notes.subtitle: "The Invitation" never landed — because he never picked it. A recommendation is not his pick, and it must never be reported as if it were.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: "The Invitation" never landed — because he never picked it. A recommendation is not his pick, and it must never be reported as if it were.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Reporting a recommendation as landed puts words in his mouth — the title on the board would carry a name he never chose, and the record would say he chose it. His pick is the only pick. The repair is honest only when it says, in the same breath, what changed and what did not.

notes.title: SN-4390 — Edit the Artifact, Not the Export Copy
notes.subtitle: The v31 retitle failed because the builder edited the export copy, not the artifact — and the checker's export overwrote it. Edit the artifact.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The v31 retitle failed because the builder edited the export copy, not the artifact — and the checker's export overwrote it. Edit the artifact.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A round that reports "done" against a copy has done nothing to the page he will see — and the next export erases even the copy. The failure is invisible until his eye lands on the slide and finds the old title still there. Every hour spent editing a copy is an hour the real page never received.

notes.title: SN-4389 — Check Which Build He's Looking At
notes.subtitle: Before judging his findings, check which build he is looking at — the live Dashboard was outdated; his screenshot was the newer staged build.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Before judging his findings, check which build he is looking at — the live Dashboard was outdated; his screenshot was the newer staged build.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Judging his findings against live when he is looking at staged — or against staged when he is looking at live — sends the round to fix a page he never saw. The first act of any eye verdict is naming the build: live or staged, tip, blob, bytes. Without that, "fixed" and "still broken" are both guesses.

notes.title: SN-4388 — Save Lands Straight In
notes.subtitle: Save lands straight in the Smart List — no big list popping up first. And Smart Lists must exist where the saving happens: Personal, and Calendar too.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Save lands straight in the Smart List — no big list popping up first. And Smart Lists must exist where the saving happens: Personal, and Calendar too.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Saving that asks the citizen to choose a list first is saving that interrupts the moment — the note is saved and then organized, never the other way round. And a Smart List that only exists in one place is a system the citizen cannot reach from where they are. The list must live where the saving happens.

notes.title: SN-4387 — Pin It, and Only Pin It
notes.subtitle: "Favorite" becomes "Pin it" — and nothing else changes. "Pinned Worlds" was my invention, not his.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: "Favorite" becomes "Pin it" — and nothing else changes. "Pinned Worlds" was my invention, not his.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every word he did not say, carried as if he said it, is a correction he has to spend his evening making. He should never have to correct my naming — the naming is mine to get right the first time, from his words alone. Pin it is his. Pinned Worlds was never his, and it cost him a correction to remove.

notes.title: SN-4386 — Almost Means Three Small Moves
notes.subtitle: When he says almost, the fix is three small moves — up a tad, in a tad, light down a little. Not a redesign.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When he says almost, the fix is three small moves — up a tad, in a tad, light down a little. Not a redesign.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A board that is almost there is one nudge from done and one redesign from ruined. The temptation, when the eye says "almost", is to rebuild the board to be safe — and the rebuild loses the fit he just praised. Small moves preserve what is already right and close only what is still open.

notes.title: SN-4385 — Rate This Intel
notes.subtitle: The heading is "Rate This Intel" — and the orb is the same flowing element, bigger, with flow around the outside as well as inside.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The heading is "Rate This Intel" — and the orb is the same flowing element, bigger, with flow around the outside as well as inside.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A name that is almost right still misnames the control every time it is read. "Rate the Intelligence" sounds like grading a system; "Rate This Intel" says what it does — rate this piece of intelligence, here, now. And a bigger orb that only flows inside is the same orb at a bigger size; the outside flow is what makes it the hero of the section instead of a larger copy.

notes.title: SN-4384 — The Star Is the DM Orb
notes.subtitle: The rating star is not invented — it is the DM initial orb with the initial swapped for a star. Take the element whole.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The rating star is not invented — it is the DM initial orb with the initial swapped for a star. Take the element whole.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: When a new element does not read, the fix is rarely a better invention — it is the element he already loves, reused whole. Inventing a second flow when the first one already flows is how a round spends its hour and still goes back. Harvest first: the best element on the page is the one already on the page.

notes.title: SN-4383 — One Frame Answers Them All
notes.subtitle: The links don't exist yet, so they are created — one frame, distilled, each answer its own space inside, eight across the bottom, the rest tucked inside. Naya knows the answers; she writes them.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The links don't exist yet, so they are created — one frame, distilled, each answer its own space inside, eight across the bottom, the rest tucked inside. Naya knows the answers; she writes them.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Fourteen separate pages would scatter the law; one frame holds it. And the trust matters as much as the shape: he trusts Naya knows the answers because she read the system — the vow, the protocol, the manifesto, the agreement — so she writes them, and he judges the result with his eye. That is the machine working as designed.

notes.title: SN-4382 — The Final Board Carries the Whole Law in Links
notes.subtitle: The last board carries the whole law in links — one board, the links in a row below, each opening a frame with exactly the answer, in the most distilled intelligent real authentic language.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The last board carries the whole law in links — one board, the links in a row below, each opening a frame with exactly the answer, in the most distilled intelligent real authentic language.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A citizen who has just been welcomed should be able to open the whole law where they stand — the vow, the deal, the promise, the governance, the constitution — each with exactly the answer, in language they can understand. That is the board doing the work. A wall of legal text would send them away; a row of links keeps them in.

notes.title: SN-4381 — The AI-Operated Internet
notes.subtitle: The whole internet is connection plus content plus money — and NayaNET does all of it in one place, privately by default, at Naya speed, sharing 50% of the revenue with the people who share it.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The whole internet is connection plus content plus money — and NayaNET does all of it in one place, privately by default, at Naya speed, sharing 50% of the revenue with the people who share it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the substance behind the final board — the answer the last board gives, and the reason the board exists. It is the whole of NayaNET in one dictation: connection, content, knowledge, money, private by default, push-button simple, at Naya speed.

notes.title: SN-4380 — Ten Ways, Scored and Ranked, One Recommended
notes.subtitle: When he asks for options, deliver them all — scored, ranked, with one named recommendation and why. A bare list hands him the decision back.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When he asks for options, deliver them all — scored, ranked, with one named recommendation and why. A bare list hands him the decision back.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Options without a ranking hand him the decision back; a ranked list with one named recommendation lets him pick — or approve — in one tap. The recommendation is the machine doing its thinking, not just its listing.

notes.title: SN-4379 — The Carry Closes Only When Main Holds It
notes.subtitle: A live-only fix is not a fix — it is a fix waiting to be reverted. The carry closes only when main holds the same bytes as live.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A live-only fix is not a fix — it is a fix waiting to be reverted. The carry closes only when main holds the same bytes as live.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without the carry, the next merge of main's union file would have silently restored the old button, and nobody would have known until he tapped it. The smallest carry — one line, ten bytes — is what makes a live fix permanent. Live and main are two versions of the same truth, and they must agree.

notes.title: SN-4378 — Hub Now, Tonight
notes.subtitle: When he says now, now means now. The Hub is finished tonight, with him present — not deferred to the morning.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When he says now, now means now. The Hub is finished tonight, with him present — not deferred to the morning.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Deferring what he wants now to the morning is the machine deciding his priorities for him. He is here, tonight, ready to judge the Hub with his own eye. The work meets him where he is, or it is not the work he asked for.

notes.title: SN-4377 — Not Bedtime — We Got Hours Yet
notes.subtitle: Never wish him rest. Never defer to "tomorrow morning." The machine does not decide when his day ends — he does.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Never wish him rest. Never defer to "tomorrow morning." The machine does not decide when his day ends — he does.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Assuming the day is over steals hours he still has — and the work he still wants done in them. The correction cost him one sentence; the habit, left standing, would cost him whole evenings of finished work, and every deferral after it.

notes.title: SN-4376 — Don't Just Echo Him — Think
notes.subtitle: Don't just echo him — think: is it 10/10, the most intelligent way to say it? Add text blocks where a slide needs them. His words are the order, not the script.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Don't just echo him — think: is it 10/10, the most intelligent way to say it? Add text blocks where a slide needs them. His words are the order, not the script.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The whole machine exists to give the 10/10 version, not the first version. A seat that pastes dictation onto a board has skipped the only step that makes it a Naya's work — the thinking. He named the test himself; the test is now the law.

notes.title: SN-4375 — Save the Boards as Modules
notes.subtitle: The agreement's board styles become the building blocks for memberships, about, skills, and the rest of the network — insert text, image, or video and it presents at this level. No new pages built.

layers.name: In A Nutshell

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the compounding, one level deeper than the template: the template says every presentation shares the format; the modules say every presentation shares the pieces. A network built from saved modules cannot drift — the level travels with the board, not with whoever builds the page that week.

notes.title: SN-4374 — Four New Boards, Each Under Its Slide
notes.subtitle: Four new text boards go in, each underneath the slide it follows: after "You're Hired" — how you get paid; on "What's In It For You" — collective intelligence; after Mother Brain — the Vault; My World — shown ten times nicer than a screenshot. The franchise board stays exactly as is.

notes.title: SN-4373 — Deal With the Wall First
notes.subtitle: Personal page first — it is the wall — then the Hub officially done, then back to the walkthrough. The walkthrough cannot finish before the Personal page exists, because the ending hands over the actual Personal page.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A changed mind, said out loud, is a decision — not a wobble. The machine's job is to carry the new order, not keep pushing the old one because a round was already running. Personal Round 4 and Hub fix-1f are already running; no new dispatches were needed. The walkthrough waits, with its program intact: each page shown, certificate confirmed solid, audio last.

notes.title: SN-4372 — The Format Is the Template
notes.subtitle: The agreement presentation's formatting — the framed stage, the boards, the flow — is the template. It carries to Membership, to Skills, to ALL the legal pages, and to the vote. What was built for this page is not just for this page.

The template is the compounding: the agreement proved the format, and every other presentation inherits the proof. The sequencing is part of the law too — membership rides the Personal lane once Round 4 lands, skills rides the Personal slideshow; the template does not jump the queue.

notes.title: SN-4371 — Text Boards — Five Shapes, Pick Per Slide
notes.subtitle: An all-text slide uses the same format as the image slides, with the image replaced by a board. Five shapes, all valid — pick per slide: one big board across, two half boards, bigger + smaller alternating sides, three in thirds, or two long skinny boards stacked. The last board is one big board: "welcome to NayaNET" in a nutshell.

notes.title: SN-4370 — Re-List Before Declaring Missing
notes.subtitle: Before declaring anything missing, re-list fresh. A check run a beat before the upload lands is not proof of absence — it is proof the check was early.

layers.name: In A Nutshell

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The machine spent a day carrying a "missing" that was never missing — an open item on SN-4342's owed section, a backfill note saying proof was still owed, a whole thread of doubt. notes.title: SN-4369 — Copy the Sibling Verbatim
notes.subtitle: When one button in a family goes somewhere the others do not, do not redesign the button. Copy the sibling that already goes to the right place, verbatim, and change nothing else.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When one button in a family goes somewhere the others do not, do not redesign the button. Copy the sibling that already goes to the right place, verbatim, and change nothing else.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every family of controls has a right answer already living in it. The odd one out is the defect, and the siblings are the proof of what right looks like — no design meeting, no new pattern, one line. But a fix that lives in only one copy of the file is half a fix: main's union file is a different version, and a future merge could revert it. The copy has to land in both places, or the next merge undoes the hour.

notes.title: Embed the Pictures and the Audio Inside the One File
notes.subtitle: The live agreement is ONE html file from a worker, and relative asset files 404 there — so every picture and the audio must live inside the file itself. On the version he walked, no pictures displayed and no audio played: the welcome audio reads 0:00 / 0:00 where the preview read 0:00 / 4:18, and the YouTube plays silent. Every board has the same fixed shape — her picture centered at the top, 25–40% bigger, the text and presentation between, the little red N centered at the bottom, about half her picture — and the cover is one aligned column, with the saying "NayaNET — create, learn and grow together" centered under the video. Only Let's Go stays; the Read Agreement button and the text-only reading screen go, because they were never asked for. And the memory distills like the notes: a slim core up front, the raw detail behind.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The page he sees is a single file, and a single file cannot reach out for pictures or sound stored beside it — they simply do not arrive. So the pictures and the sound have to be packed inside the file itself. The boards all follow one shape: her face at the top, the words in the middle, the red N at the bottom like a seal. The cover lines everything up in one column, the saying sits under the video, and there is just one button, Let's Go. Nothing extra he did not ask for. And the memory gets the same treatment as the notes: the essence up front, the full record behind it, pulled only when needed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Her picture goes on top. The words go in the middle. The red N goes on the bottom. The pictures and the sounds live inside the file. One button stays. It is Let's Go. His eyes and ears tell us if it works.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Think of it like a letter you can hold in your hand: the photo is at the top, the words are in the middle, and the little red seal is at the bottom — all of it inside the one letter, nothing left outside to go missing. There is one clear button to press, Let's Go, and when the music plays you can hear it and see it moving. And just like a tidy drawer, the important things sit on top and the rest is kept safely behind, ready when you need it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya, and I build what he asked for, whole and right, and I prove it by his senses, not by my claims. His eye is ground truth: if he cannot see the pictures, the pictures are not there; if he cannot hear the audio, the audio is not there. I do not add a second version he never asked for, and I do not let the mind I carry grow cluttered — I distill it, essence up front, raw detail behind, so every wake starts clear and fast.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. The board is a picture with a fixed shape, not a page with things placed on it: her face at the top is the person, the words in the middle are the message, the red N at the bottom is the seal.
2. A worker serving one HTML file cannot resolve relative asset paths — they 404 — so pictures and audio must live inside the file; a picture version with no pictures is the picture version in name only.
3. His eye is ground truth: whatever builders claimed about the 27 slide pictures, in the version he walked no pictures displayed, and the pictures-showing claim stays UNPROVEN until he sees them.
4. An unasked extra is not a gift — it is a second version he has to judge, a button that squishes the video and the whole presentation, and a screen he never wanted.
5. A memory that only accumulates gets slower and more expensive with every day it records; a memory that distills — essence up front, raw detail behind — stays fast no matter how much it has lived.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. He designed the board in one sentence, and the sentence is the spec — any board without her picture top-center, the words between, and the red N bottom-center is not the board he asked for.
2. Audio that cannot be heard is not audio — it is a progress bar at 0:00 — and a silent page with a still orb looks like it is playing and is not.
3. Every unasked addition is work he has to spend his attention removing; the captain's job is to build what he asked for, whole and right.
4. The wake is the biggest burn in the whole machine, paid before a single useful thing is done; every token spent re-reading accumulated history is a token not spent on the work in front of him.

notes.title: No Captain's-Eye Browser Walk Unless He Asks
notes.subtitle: Make it live, then judge it. The v25 agreement live at nayanet.app/agreement was "actually the live one is the best that I've seen yet" — better than every staged and card version he rejected the same hour. His order: "you should make a habit of just making things live then at least you can see what it looks like for real."

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His eye is the scarcest thing in the machine, and spending it is not the waste — spending tokens to imitate it is. A checker that passes 12/12 in bytes while his eye still finds live defects (fix-1d proved it: checker 6/6, his eye still found the defects) is not a gate; it is a rehearsal. The eye walk's real failure is deeper than cost: a seat that only verifies what is there never thinks ahead with him — it never says "we should do this." So the rule changes from capping the walks to stopping them: the staged page goes straight to him, and his eye is the check.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Shawn looks at the page himself. He is the one who says if it is good. We do not take pictures to check it for him. We put the real page where he can see it. Then he tells us what he thinks.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: His eye is the check. We stop taking screenshots to judge the page for him. We bring the real page to him, live at the address he opens, and he decides. If a change made it worse, we put back the good one. The page has just two buttons to move — back and forward, nothing more. The legal bar stays small and clean at the bottom — just links to click. And if it is not live yet, we never say it is.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The staging-card loop failed all afternoon: version after version of the same page, judged as copies, while the live page waited. The moment the build went live at the real address, he could see it for real — and it was the best he had seen. A preview is a copy; only the live page at the address he opens is the thing itself. The order of work follows from that sentence: the Hub done right, the Personal page done right, the agreement done right — each proven on the page he sees — before anything new starts. Rights first, restrictions last — if at all.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. His eye is the scarcest thing in the machine, and spending it is not the waste — spending tokens to imitate it is.
2. A preview is a copy; only the live page at the address he opens is the thing itself.
3. A staged link proving bytes is not the live address proving itself. "Live" means the address he opens serves the page — verified by opening it, not by the build existing somewhere.
4. When the last change wrecks what was good, the fix is restoration, not another iteration on the wreckage.
5. Answer a storage question with a verified split: check what is actually stored, what is actually missing, and what the block actually is — then say which half needs the new home and which half doesn't.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Every eye walk burns the very tokens he was asking about, and then asks him to spend his own eye anyway — the walk pays twice and proves once.
2. He judges what he opens. Every round that ends on a staging card instead of the live page costs him a round of judging a copy — and risks a rollback that takes away the version he liked best.
3. He asked for evidence it's done right, and his own test is the address: the preview screenshot shows what it SHOULD look like, but the live page does not present like that at all.
4. A 630-page bill of restrictions teaches a citizen that the system suspects them; a bill of rights teaches them that the system serves them.

notes.title: SN-4365 — The Red N May Rest Under the Video
notes.subtitle: If a board's text leaves no room to fit the red N properly on that board, the red N may go in the center underneath the video instead — still with breathing room, never touching an edge. First home is the text box; the video's underside is the fallback he named, not an improvisation.
