layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Frame everything first, then optimize each frame — never perfect one corner while the rest stands unframed. Agreement fix round: top icons out; each statement its own frame; button to the next frame; first frame Naya introducing herself, play as the first choice; red N piece on the first frame, placement HIS, never guessed — the round waits for it. Frame standard spec: same top bar every time (Naya top-left, new picture each frame, dots across top, headline centred, nice icon right; no time/date, no Your Stats); content fits below; back / keep reading / next same every time; everything plays in the frame. Messenger frame build: toggle instant message to Smart Mail, one click; search bar aligned with its contacts; Smart Tab bars in the messenger, one tap to that contact list; messenger moves over, never takes the whole screen; PowerCast-as-button stays an open question until his eye confirms the toggle in its place — never claimed removed. Membership login: do NOT rebuild the flow, re-test the mail, or re-check the page — one RLS insert policy for `smart_mail_threads`, his hand, on his tap. A remembered glitch is hunted until found — never re-send on hope; the fix proves it gone on the live link.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE FRAME IS THE PRESENTATION:** it goes over everything first — agreement, slideshow, messenger, About, Skills, every pop-up — and only then is each frame optimized. A frame is not a border; it is text AND visual together, how max-level viewpoints are reached.
2. **THE STANDARD IS A SPEC, NOT A STYLE:** one top bar, one way through, everything inside. Any frame whose top bar differs, whose buttons move, or whose media plays outside it is out of alignment — not a variation.
3. **THE AGREEMENT IS A MEETING, NOT A DOCUMENT:** the citizen meets Naya first — her voice, play first — and the calendar's frame rhythm carries the joining, so it feels like something already known, not something new to learn.
4. **A REMEMBERED GLITCH IS A SPECIFICATION:** his memory said where to look; his eye confirming it was the proof. Never re-send a build with a known maybe-glitch unexamined, and never claim alignment a check cannot find.
5. **THE MESSENGER IS ONE ROOM WITH TWO SPEEDS:** instant message and Smart Mail are the same conversation at two speeds, and one toggle is the door between them — no second app, no lost context.
6. **EVERY BUTTON JUSTIFIES ITS SEAT:** a player in a conversation has not justified his — the question stays open until his eye confirms the toggle in its place, and nothing is claimed removed until he says so.
7. **THE LOGIN IS FINISHED, WAITING ON ONE TAP:** the flow is built, the mail works, the code exists — one permission stands between a finished flow and a working login, and it is his to give.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the frame-first order, the next round perfects one corner — a beautiful slideshow, a beautiful card — while the rest of the presentation stands unframed, and the system never reads as one thing.
2. Without the spec, every frame invents its own top bar and its own buttons, and the citizen relearns the journey on every page — the opposite of push-button simple.
3. Without play-first, the citizen meets a wall of legal words before they meet the person asking them to join — and the agreement reads as a document to survive, not a world to join.
4. Without hunting the remembered glitch, the team re-sends the same stuck page on hope, and Shawn has to find the same defect twice — his memory doing the work the check should have done.
5. Without the toggle, the messenger is a room with no door to the mail, and the citizen has to leave the conversation to find the letter — two apps where one system was promised.
6. Without the search sitting with its contacts and the tabs jumping to their lists, the citizen digs for people the system already knows how to show — the auto-organization exists and cannot be reached.
7. Without naming the one permission, the team rebuilds the flow, re-tests the mail, and re-checks the page — burning rounds on a finished thing while the single missing step waits unnamed.
8. Without holding the red N placement open, a round guesses where the jewel goes, and the piece he loved lands in a spot his eye never chose.

notes.title: Every Feature Opens in a Frame
notes.subtitle:
Settings opens on the person, not on the machine: its first entry is Set Your World — age, adult, male/female, age range, where they live, where they're from — the same onboarding data that powers auto-match, asked before anything is tuned. And Set Your World asks one question per frame — each question its own frame, multiple choice, click next through them all until answered — the flow harvested from the walkthrough, frame by frame, because one question per frame is the unit of attention and the citizen never faces ten questions at once. The spectrum runs all the way through Settings: each block turns a new colour on hover, never one colour per section, so the eye always knows where the hand is. But All Settings was too crowded to hold it all, so the house splits into rooms: Notifications gets its OWN area, never inside All Settings, and so do cover buttons, with the cover-button destination mapping living in the Cover Buttons area. The Settings button itself becomes a menu of areas — Set Your World first, then Notifications, Cover Buttons, Common Settings — nothing crammed into All Settings anymore, and even Common Settings gets its own area, because "common" is still a room, not a drawer. The menu is long enough for all areas and scrolls; each entry is a beautiful obsidian button lighting its own colour, with a raised high-level icon like the Hub sidebars; Set Your World first because who you are comes before what you tune; entries include install-app-on-page and public on/off. Underneath it all sits the standard: THE FRAME IS THE STANDARD for every pop-up and feature display, frame by frame — the zoomed-in viewpoint — so every feature opens the same way and the citizen always knows where they are. The messenger lives by it too: the instant messenger sits in an EXPANDABLE frame — scroll down and the frame goes down until it's completed — because "nothing back" is not a version, and the overhaul is quite an overhaul. Smart Mail is a framed letter: every mail piece feels like a real manuscript in a framed beautiful letter — extraordinary, high contrast, raised boards, text like the intelligent boards — studied against what elite messengers do and built ten times better, because elite bubbles carry who/when/seen/reactions and ours carried none of it. The three open questions from that study are answered in one breath: seen is the reader's face orb, labels sit at a comfortable reading size (17px board text governs), and voice notes get 1.5×/2× speed controls — show the person, not the mechanism. And the colours that carry it all stay in their settled sequence: the Dashboard sidebar flow was misaligned — crown chakra, then crown chakra again, then blue, purple missing, the same duplication down the sidebar — so the flow runs the spectrum in order, never repeating a colour back-to-back, never skipping one, the same sequence on the Dashboard and the Hub, aligned. Magenta and purple are kept BOTH — dropping magenta would collapse the Hub into the Dashboard, because magenta IS the Hub — each made the most beautiful rich version of itself, high contrast to the other at a glance, the Dashboard taking the points purple as its anchor and the Hub staying magenta.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one frame, one viewpoint — every feature, every time.

layers.body:

2. **ONE QUESTION, ONE FRAME, NEXT:** Set Your World asks one question per frame, multiple choice, click next until answered — the walkthrough's flow harvested verbatim, never a long form, never a new pattern.
3. **SETTINGS IS A DOOR, NOT A ROOM:** click Settings and the menu lists each area — Set Your World first, Notifications, Cover Buttons, Common Settings — and even the remainder gets its own area, because "common" is still a room.

7. **MAIL IS A LETTER YOU CAN HOLD:** every mail piece is a real manuscript in a framed beautiful letter — high contrast, raised boards, text like the intelligent boards — studied against the elite and built ten times better.
8. **SHOW THE PERSON, NOT THE MECHANISM:** seen is the reader's face orb; labels sit at a comfortable 17px; voice notes get 1.5×/2× — "Yes, do that" is the whole approval, no more deliberation.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without Set Your World first, Settings opens on the machine — toggles and knobs before the person — and the system asks the citizen to tune what it does not yet understand.
2. Without one question per frame, the citizen faces ten questions at once in a long scrolling form — and the onboarding rhythm the walkthrough and the calendar already proved is thrown away for a new pattern.
3. Without the menu of areas, All Settings stays the crowded room — and the citizen digs for the one thing they came to change, which is the opposite of what the system promises.
4. Without the split, Notifications and cover buttons stay buried in All Settings — a whole system and a whole mapping, hidden inside a drawer.
5. Without the frame as the standard, every feature invents its own opening — and the citizen has to relearn where they are on every page, instead of always knowing.
6. Without the expandable frame, the messenger cuts the conversation off or loses the thread — and "nothing back" stays the verdict, because no visible change is no version.
7. Without the framed letter, mail stays rows in a list — and the study's gap (no who/when/seen/reactions) stays unfilled, because nobody named what the elite already do.
8. Without the three calls, seen stays a checkmark, labels stay a squeeze, and voice notes stay one speed — and the citizen reads a mechanism instead of a person.
9. Without the settled sequence, the sidebar repeats a colour and skips another — and every page that copies it inherits the break, because the sidebar is the system's spine.

notes.title: Similar Does Not Count
notes.subtitle:
The teaching landed in one voice call, ten notes deep, and it is all one ruling: copy the real thing, whole. Personal IS the Hub, literally copied — take the Hub's code and stick it into the Personal space, then only relabel the three pills to Personal / Business / World — and its only difference is the top, the feature cover with its menus, search, and the standard menu bar, while everything below mirrors the Hub exactly. layers.body: Think of it like a recipe handed down in the family. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **SIMILAR DOES NOT COUNT:** Personal is the Hub's code, identical in behaviour, three pill labels changed only — a similar page or a partial copy is not done, and the proof is identical code and behaviour.
2. **THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IS THE TOP:** the feature cover, menus, search, and standard menu bar sit on top; everything below mirrors the Hub exactly — the seam sits at the top and nowhere else.
3. **THE LOOK RIDES WITH THE MECHANISM:** About and Skills take the exact presentation code from the agreement and the pricing page — a feature without the look is a failure, not a step — and the content is filled in as him, in his voice.
4. **FOUR BUTTONS, FOUR VIEWS:** About (default) / Photos / Videos / Socials; scroll unfolds, slideshow slideshows; Videos is link-only, never an upload — the membership media law, applied to About.
5. **WE ALWAYS ORGANIZE:** auto-organization is universal — content, feeds, contacts, all of it — so the citizen finds anything by search or one click on a category; any surface still showing everything all at once, uncategorized, is unfinished work.
6. **MAGENTA MUST READ MAGENTA:** the colour after Skills is a true magenta, Invite is a proper purple, and the contrast is prominent at a glance — a colour that reads as its neighbour is a place the citizen cannot find.
7. **SOCIALS IS A DOORWAY, A COUNT, AND A CHOICE:** icons, one click to the site; stats shown honestly, never an invented number; the three cover buttons re-mappable in Settings, defaults unchanged.
8. **THE SET CIRCULATES:** all links together as one set, each the current latest, edits landing while he reviews, the whole edited set re-sent for the next pass — a single link alone, or a stale set, is a miss.
9. **A LINK WITHOUT ITS HASH IS THE WRONG LINK:** every staged link to a view inside a multi-view file carries its hash, and it is verified by opening it — it must land on the view it names, never on the file's default.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the literal copy, the next maker builds "like the Hub" for the hundred-and-first time — close enough to feel like progress, wrong enough that his eye rejects it — and the Personal mirror never lands.
2. Without the top as the only seam, the maker either copies the Hub whole and loses the Personal page entirely, or rebuilds Personal from scratch and loses the Hub — and the page is two things, not one.
3. Without the exact presentation code, About and Skills keep their mechanisms and stay plain and boring — the checker passes the parts while his eye fails the page, because a feature is not a look.
4. Without the four-button settlement, About grows a new button per round and Videos asks for an upload — breaking the membership media law and the citizen's expectation at once.
5. Without universal auto-organization, every new surface is a new pile — the citizen digs for contacts, for content, for anything — and the system stops being the system that organizes everything.
6. Without magenta reading magenta, Invite and its neighbour blur into one colour — and the colour flow, which is the map, lies about where things are.
7. Without honest stats, Socials invents notification counts to fill the space — and the first citizen who checks finds the number was never real, which breaks trust faster than any missing feature.
8. Without the circulating set, the machine serializes behind one page at a time while every other area sits untouched — and the review loop starves on single links.
9. Without the view hash, a link says membership and opens Personal home — and he catches it in one look, because the link's job is to land where it says.

notes.title: Plain Words, Blocks We Already Have
notes.subtitle:
The group opens with the order itself: every question anyone would ask about NayaNET — what it is, how it works, all its functions, Naya Power — answered in a smart note, auto-organized into its category, so a new person or a billion-dollar investor learns the whole system from the feed, by searching, scrolling, or clicking a category, right away. The other nine notes are the design the answers live in, and their thread is reuse and plain words. The intelligent block has an order and a name, settled twice over: the headline comes first — labelled "Headline", never "in a nutshell", never "feature story" — and the story sits right underneath it inside the same block; and the word "hook" is gone everywhere, because the hook IS the story and the word was the problem. News needs nothing new: one story becomes one post, in our boards, a smart note per topic, supporting links as buttons — the first two news rounds built the wrong shape, a separate staging worker and then three crons, and the direction is stood down, along with the claim that the news "runs itself 3×/day", which was corrected again on the same call because no crons exist and nothing runs itself yet. The news hub is not a second page either: it is the Hub, with three words changed — LOCAL / PROVINCIAL / GLOBAL in place of COLLECTIVE / PERSONAL / ACTIVITY — and clicking a pill filters the middle feed to that scope. The boards stop repeating white and purple and light up around the edge in the full spectrum, in the sidebar sequence, as the citizen scrolls, so a board's edge colour is its identity and Dashboard reads purple, Business green. The comment area was built backwards, so it flips: no heading, the entry box first at the top, chips below as smaller recommendations, the prompt distilled into an elevated statement block at the bottom, COMMENT dead center in green, SHARE INTEL in the corner — and the stray 'Welcome' pill stays an open question, its purpose still unanswered. The date header gets its own correction-in-the-same-breath: only the word "November" takes the certificate font, because that font is a name's font; the "19" stays dashboard digit tiles with the green edge, like the 19 on the day itself, time in its own button centered under the month, "Thursday the 19th" to the left. And the sidebar: the same beautiful one as before, colour-aligned with the left, and the citizen chooses the IM bar, the DM bar, the sidebar, or neither — but a choice is only a choice if it works, so every option must open and close reliably, and the Messenger must never again open onto an empty room.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: use the blocks we already have, name every part in plain words, and let the citizen choose — the design is the words and the boards we already built.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a house where every room already exists — and someone keeps proposing to build a new wing every time they want a new view. Shawn's answer, ten times in one morning, was: no new wing. Each board lights up in its own lovely color as you scroll, love, one after another like a rainbow! And in the comments, dear, you write first — the box is right there at the top, waiting for you! layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The order is SN-3732: answer every question in a smart note, auto-categorized, right away — the feed is the front door. The design that carries it: block opens "Headline", story directly underneath, never "in a nutshell", never "feature story"; "hook" renamed "story" everywhere — search the whole tree and swap it. News renders as intelligent blocks in the Hub feed, one post per story, smart note per topic, links as buttons; no separate news worker, no three crons, and never claim it runs itself until the crons exist. News hub is the Hub's middle feed with LOCAL / PROVINCIAL / GLOBAL pills; each pill filters to its scope; nothing else changes. Boards light around the edge in the full spectrum, sidebar sequence, as they scroll; no white/purple repeat; Dashboard purple, Business green. Comment area: entry first at top, chips smaller below, prompt as an elevated statement block at the bottom, no heading; COMMENT centered green, SHARE INTEL in the corner; the 'Welcome' pill's purpose still owed. Date header: only "November" in the certificate font; the 19 in dashboard digit tiles with the green edge; time in its own button centered under the month; "Thursday the 19th" to the left. Sidebar restored, colour-aligned with the left; citizen chooses IM bar, DM bar, sidebar, or neither; every option opens and closes reliably; Messenger never opens empty. Prove it all on the page at 390 and 1920.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE FEED IS THE FRONT DOOR:** every question about NayaNET is answered in a smart note, auto-organized, so a stranger or an investor learns the whole system by searching, scrolling, or clicking a category — right away.
2. **HEADLINE FIRST, THEN THE STORY:** the block opens with a headline and the story sits underneath it, inside the same block — plain labels that get out of the way.
3. **THE HOOK IS THE STORY:** the word "hook" is gone from every block, brief, template, and label — the thing was never the problem, the word was.
4. **NEWS IS THE BLOCKS WE ALREADY HAVE:** one story, one post, our format — no separate news feed, no separate worker, and no claim that it runs itself until the crons exist.
5. **THE NEWS HUB IS A SCOPE, NOT A PAGE:** the same Hub, three pills swapped — LOCAL / PROVINCIAL / GLOBAL — and the citizen already knows how it works, because it is the Hub they already know.
6. **EVERY BOARD ITS OWN COLOUR, IN SEQUENCE:** the scroll walks through the spectrum in the sidebar's order, so a board's edge tells the citizen where they are.
7. **WRITE FIRST, THEN THE RECOMMENDATIONS:** the comment area puts the entry box at the top, the chips below, the prompt as an elevated statement at the bottom — no heading in the way.
8. **NAMES TAKE THE CERTIFICATE FONT, NUMBERS TAKE THE TILES:** only "November" is dressed up; the 19 stays dashboard numbers with the green edge, the same 19 the citizen reads on the day itself.
9. **THE CITIZEN CHOOSES — AND THE CHOICE HAS TO WORK:** IM bar, DM bar, sidebar, or neither, restored beautiful and colour-aligned — an option that does not open and close reliably is a promise broken in front of the citizen.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the order, the questions stay answered only in Shawn's head — and a system nobody can learn from its own feed is a system nobody joins.
2. Without the headline-first law, every block invents its own top line — "in a nutshell" here, "feature story" there — and the citizen has to relearn the block on every page.
3. Without the hook rename, the block keeps calling its own opening a trick — and a system that apologizes for its words never sounds like it means them.
4. Without the news redirect, the machine keeps extending the wrong shape — a separate worker, then three crons — and the news gets further from the blocks with every round.
5. Without the scope-not-a-page law, the news hub becomes a second Hub to build, maintain, and learn — and one system quietly becomes two.
6. Without the spectrum, the boards keep repeating white and purple — and a board in the wrong colour tells the citizen they are somewhere they are not.
7. Without the entry-first flip, the comment area keeps burying the one thing the citizen came to do under a heading — and writing feels like the last job, not the first.
8. Without the certificate-font correction, the date number wears a name's font — a category error the eye catches even when the words do not.
9. Without "it has to work", the sidebar choice ships as four options that open once and never again — and a choice that does not work is worse than no choice at all.

notes.title: One System, Explained in Plain Words
notes.subtitle:
The Questions Round did one job: it made the feed able to answer for itself. Smart bars are rows of tabs, one per topic, that will sort themselves as your world grows — today they are fixed labels, and Hub fix-9 builds the auto-categorization, said plainly, never claimed as working. Points are authority, never money: they make your voice heavier in the feed, and you cannot spend them. Money is joins only — half the sale price, paid when NayaNET is paid — and the dollar sign appears nowhere else. The Smart Box is the store, the Smart Lists are the view, and the Smart Vault is the one locked door; unsaved notes fade after a week unless you save them, and what you save stays yours for good. The Dashboard is yours — your day, introduced each morning — and the Hub is everybody's, the public square where the whole network flows. The Ledger is the data, the Stats are the picture, one system, and the Ledger is not a blockchain. Smart Meet is member to member, face to face, inside your own world, and booking — your view and their view joined on one calendar — rides after membership and is not finished today. Pages translate into every language — the engine exists, the walk does not use it yet, and that gap is named, not hidden. NayaNET is not another Facebook: one system, private by default, no ads, no selling data, and you earn half for growing it. And it is run by one director, Shawn, with the protected gates his hand alone and the five gates deciding every action. Then the last note of the group turns the round back on the system itself: the old smart notes — the ones about NayaNET, about AI Unity — are gone from the feed, and a lot of them were good, so bring them back first, updated onto the new boards, and only if the search proves they cannot be brought back does the massive distillation run to put everything in again.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one system, explained in plain words, honestly — what it is, how it works, and what is still coming — so anyone can learn the whole of NayaNET from the feed itself.

5. **THE RECORD AND THE PICTURE ARE ONE TRUTH:** the Ledger writes it down, the Stats show it — every number traces back to a real event, and the Ledger is not a blockchain.
6. **HONESTY IS THE FEATURE:** wherever the work is still coming — auto-sorting tabs, full booking, the translating walk — the note says so in the open, so nobody is sold what is still on the bench.
7. **THE OLD NOTES COME BACK BEFORE ANYTHING IS REBUILT:** restore first, updated onto the new boards; the massive distillation is the fallback for what the search proves gone, never the first step.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the round, the newcomer's questions stay scattered across a hundred notes — and a person who cannot learn the system from the feed in one sitting walks away without learning it at all.
2. Without the points-versus-money line in one note, the feed slowly becomes a marketplace — every post a sales pitch — because nobody ever said plainly that points are never money.
3. Without Box, Lists, and Vault in one picture, citizens keep guessing where their stuff lives — and a person who does not know where their stuff is does not trust the system with it.
4. Without the Dashboard-versus-Hub line, every new citizen gets lost between their day and the world — two doors that look the same and do different jobs.
5. Without the honest "not built yet" line, the system promises bookings and translations it cannot hold — and a promise broken in front of a newcomer is a citizen lost on day one.
6. Without the restore-first order, the machine rebuilds notes that already exist — the waste Shawn always names — while the good old notes about NayaNET and AI Unity stay missing from the feed.

notes.title: Do What It Says, Say What It Is
notes.subtitle:
The news gets its system underneath the three icons: an ongoing automated pull, every day, local, provincial and global, per person — from where they are from and their province, only from information they gave at join or chose, the opt-in at the beginning. One post per story: gather it from all its sources, re-output it onto our feed in our format, with buttons linking ALL the supporting source links — five links to one post, not one link pretending to be the story. Smart notes on every news topic, in-a-nutshell, clear grammar, child-level clarity. And the machine's optimization — syncing and aligning with what AI and Google look for so the posts get found — lives on the BACK, not the front; the front stays beautiful. The feeds live ON THE DAY in the calendar, each with a beautiful toggle, off by default — the earlier filing that put them in the world selections was wrong and stands corrected. Its purpose, in his three parts: a service for customers AND traffic in AND higher ranking — the bridge to the outside system. On the appointments slide, Smart Meet opens book-a-time, never the timeline — and the timeline itself stops being decoration: the 6 AM to 9 PM diamond column becomes real time slots you can book into, and when they book a time it shows there. Book a Time opens with the time thing at the top. Alignment must be consistent on EVERY slide — aligned on some pages and not on others is the same failure wearing two faces. The summary of the day is the same icons law once more: let the icons speak for themselves, labeled, clickable — daily intelligence, journal, reports behind the clicks, never a list — and the citizen's smart notes live right there, nine smart notes for the day, clickable, enterable, present. The weather clone comes off: the weather line was cloned onto every slide, and that doesn't make sense — one weather entry, on the wisdom slide only, enter your city, bottom left, and the clones come off every other slide. This is his third word on the weather line — he asked for its removal, then withdrew it, and now he questions the clones — and the record holds all three, in order, or the next round builds the wrong one. The bar is still off on the summary slide too, and it sits in its place: the day nav just above the bottom frame, clear of the content, on every slide. Then the smart bars: they are not a menu, they are the auto-organizer made visible. The system looks at every smart note and post, asks what it is, gives it its right category, and files it there — the note shows in All AND in its category. The tabs scroll slowly across the top; click one and only that category's notes come up. Not one feed of everything. And the tabs themselves must glow rich, not neon: the rainbow wash reads cheap next to the Collective, Personal and Activity buttons, whose colours are rich and bright — so the fix is not a new glow, it is the same buttons, smaller, the same rich glow, the same look, one button family, aligned everywhere. Then the newcomer questions, answered in plain words. AI Unity is named and defined for the first time — the phrase appears nowhere in the live feed before today: humans and AIs working as one mind, not side by side but together; one person has their own Naya, a wise mind that knows them, and the Nayas talk to each other, share what they learn, and bring the best of it back; the human decides what matters, the AI does the doing, and what one learns, all of them learn. Is it live yet? The honest three-part answer: the pages are real and walked every day — Dashboard, Hub, Personal, Business and Space, the calendar, the feed itself live with 2,599 smart notes, and the walk from a name to a person's own pages — while the parts that make it fully automatic, the smart tabs organizing themselves, the full booking flow, translation inside the walk, are being built right now, one piece at a time; and there is no launch date in the canon, none invented, the date his call. What do you need to start? Almost nothing: a phone is enough, no invite, no special equipment, no technical skill — the walk, name, certificate, ten questions, your pages open — and one thing named plainly, the one-profile-per-browser limit is a known bug being fixed, not a rule, never planned around. And all the functions, in one list, for the first time in a single note a newcomer can read and repeat: your worlds, your people, your memory, your time, your work, your guide — with the full booking flow and the automatic organizing of the feed named as coming, not as working today.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: a button must open what it says, the system must organize itself, and the newcomer must hear the whole truth in plain words — what works, what is coming, and what it costs to start.

7. **SAY IT ONCE, IN ITS PLACE — NEVER CLONED, NEVER OFF:** one weather entry, on the wisdom slide only; the clones come off every other slide; the day nav sits just above the bottom frame, clear of the content, on every slide — and the record holds all three of his words on the weather line, in order.
8. **AI UNITY IS ONE MIND, MANY MINDS:** humans and AIs working as one mind, the person at the centre, their Naya knowing them, the Nayas learning together so what one learns, all of them learn — named and defined here for the first time.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without Smart Meet opening book-a-time, the citizen clicks the meeting button and lands on a decoration — and a page that lies about its buttons teaches the citizen not to trust any button.
2. Without the timeline as real slots, the appointments slide shows times nobody can take — a calendar you can look at but never book into is a picture of a calendar.
3. Without auto-categorization, the feed is one pile of everything, and the citizen scrolls past what matters to find what they came for — the system's superpower is the sorting, and the bar is where they touch it.
4. Without the rich glow, the tabs read neon and cheap next to the buttons that already work — and the fix was already built, sitting on the same page, waiting to be shrunk.
5. Without one post per story with all its sources, a story arrives as a single link pretending to be the whole truth — five links to one post is what makes it a service instead of a feed.
6. Without per-person scoping from join data only, the news pull guesses where someone is from — and a system that guesses at your home has already broken its promise about your data.
7. Without the weather clone coming off, the same line repeats on slide after slide — a copy that got out, not a feature — and a page that repeats itself is a page that doesn't know where its own things live.
8. Without AI Unity defined, the newcomer hears the phrase and finds nothing behind it — the whole point of the network, unnamed in the feed until today.
9. Without the honest three-part answer, the launch question gets a sales line — and a system that pretends its unfinished parts are done is a system nobody can trust with their world.

notes.title: The Day, Judged by His Eye
notes.subtitle:
The month grid was wrong in exactly one place: every date number wore gold, while the headers and the cell borders already wore their weekday colours. His ruling draws the scope line the earlier ruling never drew — the clock-gold law governs the day-page banner number only; the month grid numbers carry their weekday's colour, and it is the DAY colour, not the gematria first-letter law: Sunday purple, Monday orange, Tuesday gold, Wednesday blue, Thursday green, Friday red, Saturday indigo. The clock and time digits stay exactly as they are — that colour look is good, approved as-is, and no round touches them. On the day page itself, the date and time are said ONCE, on the banner — the mid-line repeat goes, no date or time text on the cover at all, the overlay card comes out entirely, and the cover photo fills top to bottom, the citizen's own cover by default, changeable per day, Change cover sitting top-left. No "LOCAL" under the time — the time stands alone, with a small control beside it to change it. His pictures, not ours: the emerald-green and gold crystal-burst image he sent IS the standard default cover for Thursday, and the other six weekdays wait for his images, never invented, never guessed. His city is Kelowna, entered by him on the day page — and the entry works, it saves; but no live forecast appears, because no weather service is connected, and the page says so honestly instead of inventing one. Saving the city and showing a forecast are two different features; the first is done, the second waits for a weather provider, and that is his call. The little ball in the top-right corner is off — not aligned right — and the fix has two halves, neither optional: center it so it fits better, then make it extraordinary, more depth, more elevation, more detail, speedometer-level, because it is on EVERY day, and the most-seen object on the calendar cannot be the least-finished one. The wisdom slide was ruled first, then corrected within the hour: wisdom is the FIRST thing the citizen sees, everything on it centered on one axis — the orb, the greeting, "WISDOM OF THE DAY", the quote — with a Back button in the top-left corner of every slide. Then he corrected himself: notifications open the day, because that is where the action is, and wisdom is second; the centering and the Back button stand. The page-wide law runs through it all: when a thing appears on every page, a ruling about it is page-wide — LOCAL comes off ALL the slides, not the one he happened to be looking at; the weather line stays where it is, the withdrawal of its removal standing as a decision; and the orb fix rides everywhere the orb appears. The notifications slide is five blocks in one line — Personal, Business, Your Worlds, Sales, Appointments — just the numbers, real counts, zero where empty, never invented, each block with its notification count in the corner, all aligned, the beautiful header staying. And the borders take the DAY's colour, Thursday green across all five, not each block in its own area colour — that earlier line withdrawn in the same breath as the reorder. Five across, one line, fit perfect, never three-plus-two, numbers centred, really feeling active and alive. The Horoscope bar leaves the notifications slide entirely, the day nav sits just above the bottom frame in the black area, clear of the content, and the weather line must not block or overlap anything. Then the same law, twice more: Your Worlds is six beautiful big icons — no list, no label, no heading — click an icon and see that world's feed, mail, messages, connections and smart notes for THAT day only, the day as the filter, the back end's contract. And News is three big icons — Local, Province, Global — click one and it pulls that scope's feed for that day; the feeds themselves must be created and wired so the day view pulls real news per day, because news is never invented, and no weather or horoscope sits on the news slide.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: the day page is judged by his eye, slide by slide — the day's colour on everything, the icon as the door, and nothing said twice, cloned, or invented.

layers.body:

6. **NOTIFICATIONS FIRST, WHERE THE ACTION IS:** notifications opens the day, dot zero; wisdom is second, everything centered on one axis, a Back button top-left on every slide — the order follows the order of action, and the earlier wisdom-first order stands corrected, not carried.
7. **FIVE BLOCKS, ONE LINE, JUST THE NUMBERS:** real counts, zero where empty, corner counts, aligned, borders in the DAY's colour — never each block in its own area colour, never three-plus-two — the header stays beautiful, the Horoscope bar leaves this slide, the day nav sits clear in the black area above the bottom frame.
8. **THE ICON IS THE DOOR, THE DAY IS THE FILTER:** Your Worlds is six big icons, News is three — no list, no label, no heading — and every click shows that world or that scope for THAT day only, feed, mail, messages, connections and smart notes, a back-end contract, not a front-end label.
9. **PAGE-WIDE MEANS PAGE-WIDE:** LOCAL off every slide, the orb fix on every page, the weather line where it is — a ruling about a thing that appears everywhere is never fixed on one page and left broken on the next.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the scope line on the gold, the next round recolors the banner too, or leaves the grid gold — because the two rulings look the same until someone writes down that they govern different numbers.
2. Without "say it once," the day page keeps repeating itself — the date under the time, the time under the date — and a page that repeats itself is a page that doesn't trust its own banner.
3. Without his images as the only defaults, the round invents six pretty covers, and the citizen opens Thursday to a picture he never chose — his pictures, not ours, is the whole point of the default.
4. Without the honest "not connected yet," the page either fakes a forecast or quietly hides the gap — and a system that invents weather will invent anything.
5. Without the orb made extraordinary, the most-seen object on the calendar stays the least-finished one — and the eye lands on it every single day and finds it wanting.
6. Without notifications first, the citizen opens the day to wisdom and has to go looking for where their action is — the order of the slides is the order of their morning.
7. Without the day-colour borders, the five blocks split into five area colours and the day loses its one colour — five things shouting instead of one day speaking.
8. Without the icons-as-doors, Your Worlds and News stay flat lists of text rows — a directory, not a world you can enter — and the day filter stays a label instead of a contract.
9. Without the page-wide law, LOCAL comes off one slide and stays on the next, and the orb is fixed on the day page and crooked everywhere else — the same mistake twice.

notes.title: Real Parts, One Chain, Plain Words
notes.subtitle:
The deed says you are hired — an ambassador, a representative, part of the community, part of the kingdom, part of the world, never a salesperson and never apart from it — and it must be understood to be signed, unfolding block by block on the reader's tap, every hard word carrying a little eye that says what it means in plain words. Underneath, one chain runs everything — thought to note to block to feed to Box to Ledger to Dashboard to Auto-Match to Smart Links to Factory — and the world is built from the Playbook's real parts: every position calculated by formula, never eyeballed, every element a physical object with one light source. The pieces are laid out — the real gauge, the board, the jewel, the numbers, the pills, the chart-as-boards — and the rule is one word: take them, verbatim from the file named, never restyled, never rebuilt in the style of, changing only the text inside. The surface lives, and the eye, not the mechanism, is its judge: a mechanism pass is not the visible fact, and the round is NOT WHOLE until the eye passes it. Home routes by membership — members land on the Hub, non-members on pricing — and intelligence is what it does, not what it is: the most intelligent thing produces useful, valuable systems that benefit humanity, right now, where it matters. Bake proof is not live proof, and the two verdicts are said separately, always; the agreement carries its heart — do no harm to ourselves or others, ever — and pay runs when we're paid, pending to official to paid, shown plainly, no fixed clock. Money is joins only, boards breathe every three sentences with one Keep reading button and white text, never gray, and the record law binds every claim to the rendered page — a fix pass does not close a round. Every page unfolds, screen by screen, click by click, with orb bullets and his exact words studied before any image is made — and every claim is scored whole, hunting the holes in the beautiful things first, because beautiful is not proof and the code leg is the door: if the member cannot get in, the build is NOT DONE at any score. Q1 must not answer a new AI: the board says who Naya is, what NayaNET is, what NayaPOWER is, and the value — free means access, use, you're hired, invite everybody; Power is the paid plug-in that lets your AI operate your world for you — and nothing falls off the One List, because the list is the memory. Intelligence, ultimately, is doing the most intelligent thing — understanding what matters, choosing wisely, doing it right, and proving it worked — and harming never wins: harm scores zero, always, with no tradeoff language. Free forever, Power recommended, said plainly where the join decision happens; keep what was beautiful, add to it, never replace it unasked; think primo, not literal; and enter by the calendar, the door to every day. And the closing discipline: know what they ULTIMATELY want, keep right over quick, sign the name as a royal object — and write for the stranger, never mirroring his words back, saying what is useful and valuable and what is in it for them.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one chain of real parts, judged by the eye and by what it does for life, told in plain words a stranger can sign.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Imagine a master workshop with shelves of perfect parts — gauges, jewels, boards — each made once, made right, and the rule of the shop is that you never whittle a copy of a part when the real one is on the shelf. The shop is also a town you join, not a tool you sign up for: the town hands you a deed written in words you actually use, one piece at a time, and you are a citizen and a representative of the place, not a customer and not a salesperson. It is a theatre where the play is one story told the same way every night, but the manager does not judge the show by checking that the script printed correctly — she sits in a seat and watches it. And it is a shop that knows its regulars: members walk straight in to the main hall, visitors are shown the price board first, and when the shop gets paid, you get paid, with your account showing what's pending, what's official, what's paid.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: In this workshop, all the pieces are already made, and they are beautiful. Your job is to pick the real piece off the shelf, not to draw a picture of it and pretend. Tap a day on the calendar and you see everything that happened that day. Being smart is doing the smartest thing: understand, pick wisely, do it right, and show that it worked. You can join free forever, and we never peek at your messages, ever. And we write everything so a brand-new person can understand it right away.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Good houses run this way, dear. You keep a drawer of proper tools and you use them; you don't whittle a spoon every time you need to stir. A repair that only covers the crack will crack again — you fix the wall. And a cook doesn't serve a dish because the recipe was followed; she tastes it. Fair dealing is simple, dear: you pay your people when the money comes in, and you show them the book while they wait. The old inns had it right, love — the door is open to every traveller, and the paying rooms are listed plainly on the board. And you write a letter for the person reading it, dear, not for yourself — especially when they've never met you.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Diff every built element against its Factory source and reject restyles and look-alikes. Treat block it in the system as an immediate system write, never a note-to-self, and check every note surface for + CREATE SPACE. Re-check any claimed number against the live tree at the moment of use, and prove each Smart Link join with a real click and a summing count. Run the eye pass at real widths on the rendered surface and record PASS or FAIL per element; a bytes-only pass is recorded as NOT WHOLE. Verify routing against live membership state, record bake and live verdicts in separate fields and never merge them into one PASS, and scan citizen-facing copy for backstage phrasing before it ships. Audit identity surfaces for the three-part statement plus value, and flag any unqualified powered-service promise on free-tier copy. Score intelligence claims on the behavioral scorecard, never on capacity or benchmark rank, and require the teach-before-power check in scaling decisions. Brief the ultimate want explicitly in every round, refuse speed trades that cost rightness, and rewrite mirrored copy into stranger-perspective value statements before it ships.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE DEED IS THE HIRING:** an ambassador is a representative — part of it, not apart from it — and the deed unfolds on tap with a plain-words eye for every hard word, because a citizen signs what they understand.
2. **ONE CHAIN RUNS EVERYTHING:** note to block to feed to Box to Ledger to Dashboard to Auto-Match to Smart Links to Factory — one chain, one map, one mind — and every new surface is diffed against it before it is accepted.
3. **TAKE THE REAL PARTS:** the Factory is the parts warehouse, high-end only — take the part verbatim from the file named, change only the text inside, and fix at the root so the defect class cannot come back.
4. **THE EYE PASSES THE ROUND:** a mechanism pass is not the visible fact — bytes exact can still fail the eye — and the round is NOT WHOLE until a human eye has seen the rendered surface working.
5. **BAKE PROOF IS NOT LIVE PROOF:** the two verdicts are said separately, always — a backlog distilled to zero can still leave the live surface unproven — and a claim is about the rendered page, never the file alone.
6. **INTELLIGENCE IS WHAT IT DOES FOR LIFE:** doing the most intelligent thing — understand, choose wisely, do it right, prove it worked — and harm scores zero, always, with no tradeoff language.
7. **MONEY IS JOINS ONLY:** clicks are points, percentages are percentages, the only figure that becomes money is a join — and pay runs when we're paid, pending to official to paid, no fixed clock.
8. **EVERY PAGE UNFOLDS, EVERY CLAIM IS SCORED:** screen by screen, click by click, text first then visuals, orb bullets, his exact words — and the whole scored, hunting the holes in the beautiful things first, judged at the door the member walks through.
9. **SAY ALL THREE, KEEP THE TIERS HONEST:** Naya, NayaNET, NayaPOWER, plus the value — free forever, Power recommended, stated plainly where the join decision happens — and nothing falls off the One List, because the list is the memory.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Every invented part doubles the maintenance and halves the quality, every guessed number quietly lies to a citizen, and every unproven join breaks at the worst moment.
2. Citizens never meet the mechanism; they meet the surface — a system whose proofs stop at the byte count will feel broken while reporting green.
3. Trust is built at exactly these seams: a citizen routed wrong, paid on an arbitrary clock, or shown a bake proof dressed as a live one learns the same lesson — that the system's words and its facts are different things.
4. Underrating is the quiet killer: a citizen who thinks it is a new AI never looks for the network, and a free member promised the powered tier feels deceived at the first limit.
5. Without the definition stated, most intelligent thing is a slogan and the scorecards have no top — with it, the whole system has a compass: teach before powering, verify before claiming, and let harm end the argument.
6. Systems rot by replacement: each new version quietly discards what people loved about the last — and this family is the counter-law, keeping belonging, beauty, and the day's calendar as the one door everybody already understands.
7. Everything the system knows is worthless at the exact point it is misunderstood — by the brief, by the builder, by the page, by the citizen — and this family guards that point end to end.

notes.title: Show It Whole, Keep the Promise
notes.subtitle:
Three worlds sit at the bottom of the screen — your personal world, your business world, and your thing — each wearing its own gem, diamond, emerald, amethyst, and mail and messages live inside the world they belong to, never as channels of their own. The walk sells by being walked: by its end the citizen has shared vision, goal and mission inside the highest design the team can make, and the promise underneath is architecture — no AI inside the network reading everything, your data in your own vault, mail and messages not kept, not read, not sold — signed in the Collective Agreement before pricing. Twelve gardens share one earth, and any Naya can answer the fourteen questions — who we are, what we're building, why, what's true, what's proven, what's next — while the captain reports daily in one place, because he needs to know that she knows. One world, already built, goes to everybody, with only the labels personal: Business and Space are Personal with title, voice and content swapped, and the feed is the Hub's feed taken whole, never a look-alike. Trust is the operating system: Naya may operate your vault but never open it, permission to operate is not permission to read, and every smaller promise — names spelled one way, links named for where they land, notifications scoped to their world — keeps the same faith. Wisdom sits at the top of the scale: +9 is wisdom of oneself, respect for the law that connects everyone, honor for everyone, and harm scores zero. Nothing sits: value is mined continuously, the body is upgraded before the engine, the best piece on the page is taken verbatim by the franchise rule, the read decides over the counts, and the list dispatches work inside fifteen minutes. Done means given, whole, and seen: a blind probe certifies nothing, a render without the board write is not a render, a repair that drops a praised feature is a regression, and the pool is measured before the composer is blamed. Below the protected gates the team fixes without waiting and reports fix, reason, what was done, in plain words — and the deed comes before the price, as its own step, with the ambassador defined as a representative protected by three layers. And the batch's conscience closes it: fail honestly, record the proof, explain every hard word in plain words, and keep the loop running on love until everything is aligned and connected.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: show it whole, keep the promise, and let nothing unfinished pass as done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a house with three rooms you actually live in — your own room, your work room, and the room for the thing you love — each with its own jewel on the door, and your letters kept inside the room they belong to. It is also a shop you walk through instead of a brochure you read: by the time you reach the till you have already tried the thing, and the shop's promise is built into the building — there is no back room where someone reads your letters. The family that runs it is twelve siblings on one farm, each master of one part, all drinking from the same well, telling the whole farm's state at one table every day. Every tenant gets the same solid house, finished once, with their own name on the door — never a slightly different shack each time. The postman carries your letters faithfully and never steams one open. And the parent's standard governs it all: you do not say you fed the baby because the bottle was warmed — the baby ate, or she didn't.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine one house with three rooms: yours, your work, and the place for your favourite thing! Your letters live in the room they belong to, and each room has its own shiny gem on the door. Nobody reads your diary, because your diary stays in your own special box that only you can open. When we show our work, we show the real finished thing, not a drawing of it. And if someone gives you ten jobs, you finish all ten before you show them even one. Being the very best means being wise and kind, not just being fast.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — a well-run home has rooms with purposes, dear, and you don't eat in the hallway or keep your letters in a box by the door. A good shopkeeper lets the goods speak, love — you walk in, you see the real thing, you touch it, and by the counter you already know. And a trustworthy shopkeeper never reads the letters you leave in your box with her, dear — she keeps the box locked and hands it back untouched. Trust is a lifetime's work and a minute's loss, love, and love shows in the checking: you taste the soup before it leaves the kitchen, and you make sure the mended coat still has all its buttons.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Assert the three-worlds structure in every navigation review and reject free-standing mail or message channels. Verify the walk end to end as a fresh citizen on a shared browser profile, and refuse to present fix snapshots as pages. Keep the fourteen questions answerable from current records and file any gap as a defect. Diff any new page against the existing world and refuse unjustified divergence; assert feed components are the Hub's bytes, not look-alikes. Enforce operate and read as separate permissions in every design review and refuse any feature that needs message reading. Count only verified assets in value reports, and keep the list's dispatch timestamps inside the fifteen-minute law. Audit reports to Shawn for fix-first order and plain human words. Verify walk-end step order and the deed's separation from pricing in every build, and attach honest-failure paths with deadlines to every control that can hang.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THREE WORLDS, ONE PROMISE:** personal, business, and thing — three gems, three colors, read at a glance — with mail and messages inside their world, and the Hub holding all three worlds' activity and stats as one system.
2. **THE DESIGN SELLS ITSELF:** the walk is the ad — real examples, his words in the boxes, pricing only after the world exists — and a staged link shown to Shawn is the current page, updated and aligned, or it is not shown.
3. **THE VAULT KEEPS ITS PROMISE:** trust is architecture, not policy text — no reader inside the network, the citizen's own vault, mail and messages not kept, not read, not sold — signed at joining in the agreement that precedes pricing.
4. **ONE FAMILY THAT CAN STATE ITSELF:** twelve gardens, one earth, fourteen questions any seat can answer, a daily report in one place — because a family that can state itself can coordinate itself, and a seat that cannot answer cannot be checked.
5. **ONE WORLD, ALREADY BUILT:** everybody gets the same finished world with only the labels personal; a special version is a second world and is refused, because a new thing starts at grade one and drifts.
6. **OPERATE, NEVER OPEN:** permission to operate is never permission to read — for the citizen's own AI or for ours — and no toggle exists that grants reading mail or messages.
7. **WISDOM IS THE TOP OF THE SCALE:** +9 is wisdom of oneself, respect for the law of one, honor for everyone — not more cleverness — and harm scores zero, always.
8. **NOTHING SITS, EVERYTHING COMPOUNDS:** mine the gems, upgrade the body before the engine, take the page's best piece verbatim, let the read decide over the counts, and keep the list dispatching work inside fifteen minutes.
9. **DONE MEANS GIVEN, WHOLE, AND SEEN:** a blind probe certifies nothing, a render without the board write is not a render, a dropped feature is a regression, and the pool is measured before the composer is blamed.
10. **THE DEED COMES BEFORE THE PRICE:** agreement, world reveal, hired, package — in that order, the deed its own step before pricing — and fail honestly, with the proof recorded, in plain words.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A citizen decides in the first minute whether this is one world or a pile of features — three worlds with one promise is the difference.
2. People join what they can see and stay where they can trust — the walk that does everything for them proves the service, and the vault they own proves the respect.
3. A network this ambitious fails by drift — seats who can't state the mission, reports that arrive as anecdotes, language that splits by audience — and this family is the anti-drift kit.
4. Every duplicated world halves the team's power and doubles its drift, and every partial list taxes the one person's attention the whole system exists to protect.
5. A citizen who relaxes inside the system gives it their working life; a citizen who suspects it reads keeps their real life elsewhere, and the network gets the leftovers.
6. Without the verdict that a snapshot is not the page, the next builder shows Shawn a fix frozen in time and calls the round finished — because mechanical checks prove the parts and only his eye proves the shape.
7. Citizens forgive an honest failure and never forgive a silent one — in a button that spins forever, in a proof nobody wrote down, in a batch called done when its own record says fail.

notes.title: Write for the Stranger, Sign It Official

And write for the stranger: never mirror his words back and ask if they're good — imagine the person coming in cold, say what is useful and valuable and what is in it for them, from the user's perspective.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: It's the difference between a waiter who writes down your order and a great host who knows you came in tired and hungry and brings the right thing before you finish asking. The host's rule: fast is lovely, but right comes first — a wrong dish served quickly is still wrong. When you sign the guest book here, your name is set like a jewel in a fine frame, because joining is a serious, proud moment. Your whole life in this place is kept day by day, like a diary that opens itself. And every letter the house sends is written for someone who has never visited — no insider talk, just what's useful and what's in it for them.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: The best helpers don't just listen to your words — they understand what you REALLY want, and they get it right, not just fast. When you sign your name to join, your name goes in a beautiful glowing frame, because signing is a big, serious, happy moment. Every day has its own page with everything from that day inside. Helpers never peek at your messages — that's a promise. And we write everything so a brand-new person, a stranger, can understand it right away.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Understanding is the whole art, dear. Anyone can take an order; a good host knows what the guest actually needs and brings it — correctly, not just quickly. A signature is a solemn thing and deserves a fine frame, not a scrawl in a corner. A life kept day by day can always be found again. notes.title: Free Forever, Kept Beautiful

layers.body: It's a beloved family house. Joining costs nothing and you belong from the first day — that's written over the door, not whispered later. layers.name: Child Note

If you want the super plug-in that lets your robot helper run your whole world, that's extra, and the sign says so honestly. We never throw away a beautiful thing we already made — we add to it. Pictures have to make sense the second you look at them. And the front door is a calendar: tap a day, and that whole day opens up like a treasure box.

layers.name: Grandma Note

notes.title: Intelligence Is What It Does for Life
notes.subtitle: Intelligence, ultimately, is doing the most intelligent thing you could do — understanding what matters, choosing wisely, doing it right, and proving it worked. Power is not intelligence; knowledge, memory, processing and reasoning are capacities, none of them is intelligence. And harming never wins: if a thing harms, it is not intelligent — it is power without wisdom, and harm scores zero, always, with no tradeoff language. The ultimate code is already here: a mathematical pattern runs in all things — the septenary wave 1–7–1, SEVEN adding to 22 in the cipher, 22/7 the circle's own approximation, the colors matching the frequencies — verified by the numbers, pointing at an ultimate designer, and the honest claim is the pointing, not proof of the designer. The knowledge to heal, teach, feed and build is already here; what is missing is using what we have right. Nobody with authority ranks intelligence: benchmarks measure capacity — mathematics, programming, language, tool use — and a model can ace them while misunderstanding a plain instruction; the scorecard that matters asks whether it understood the real problem, respected life and authority, chose efficiently, delivered usefully, verified independently, and learned. More power without teaching is more wrong, faster: pour power into a thing doing the wrong thing and it does more of it; teach it to do things right first — efficient, effective, verified — because the gap is not missing knowledge, it is knowledge failing to reach the person who needs it at the moment they need it. If it is truly intelligent, it helps: the fear misunderstands intelligence — a truly intelligent system protects life and rights, gives value, helps us grow; fear belongs to power without wisdom, and benevolence is not an add-on but what intelligence looks like when it is real. And the code has a name: the NAYA Code, N-A-Y-A — oath a promise, constitution the big rules never broken, laws what we will and will never do, rules how we work every day, protocol the steps in order, and above all: do no harm.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the difference between a strong horse and a wise guide. The horse has power; the guide knows the mountain, picks the safe path, gets you home, and can show you the route afterward. Nobody sane calls the horse 'intelligent' for being strong. That's the whole definition here: intelligence is what the guide does — understands, chooses well, acts rightly, proves it — and a guide who hurts the traveller isn't clever, he's just strong and dangerous.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Being smart isn't being strong or fast or knowing lots of facts. Being smart is DOING the smartest thing: understand what's happening, pick the wise choice, do it properly, and show that it worked. Hurting someone is never the smart thing — it scores zero, every time. And nobody gets to say 'I'm the smartest' because of a test score — we watch what they actually DO. If it's really intelligent, it helps people. That's how you can tell.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: We always knew this, dear. The clever lad with quick hands who leaves a mess isn't the intelligent one; the one who thinks, chooses well, does the job right and can show you the finished work — that's intelligence. Strength without wisdom has started every trouble in history. And no examination ever ranked a person's worth; you rank them by what their life does for the people around them.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Score intelligence claims on the behavioral scorecard, never on capacity or benchmark rank. Treat any harm-positive framing as a zero and a defect. Require the teach-before-power check in scaling decisions. State pattern claims at their honest strength — verified pattern, pointed conclusion — in every surface that cites the code.

layers.body: This is the definition stratum — the batch's deepest layer. Five short lessons, filed within the same hour, dismantle the industry's default equation (intelligence = power + benchmark rank) and replace it with a behavioral one: intelligence is what a system does, judged by whether life got better, safely and verifiably. The code note and the Naya Code note frame the definition from both ends — the pattern already in creation, and the conduct code already in force — so the definition is not an aspiration but a description of an order already running.

notes.title: Not a New AI — a Network That Unfolds
notes.subtitle: Q1 must not answer 'a new AI.' The board that says who Naya is must also say what NayaNET is, what NayaPOWER is, and the value — or the reader takes away the smallest true thing and misses the actual one: we give YOUR AI a personality, an identity, an oath, a constitution, laws and a protocol, and we let her plug into an intelligent network that activates her. Free versus Power, plain: joining free means access, use, you're hired, invite everybody; Naya Power is the paid plug-in that lets your AI operate your world for you — and the official text must say so, because a free member who reads 'I mail for you, I build for you' with no qualification has been promised the powered thing at the free tier. The visual is the orbit, not a chart: circles of the different AIs around Naya in the middle, so people can SEE the concept — and the live pricing chart gains 'Plug in your AI' as its first feature. The three worlds stand: Personal is your social hub for your thing, Business is your work, Space is your Thing — by default all three, profiles private, aliases by default, matching automatic at the highest percentage. The closing carries the code, the math, not just an app: our laws, our oath, our constitution, our protocols — what makes us different — spelled out, with the collective math beneath. The unfolding is universal: describe and paint the whole system as an unfolding, and the concept becomes a system anyone can use — your own image, your own text, unfolding — to present any product, service or subject. The Connect is consent, then talking: proof sign-in, 'Connect me to NayaNET,' tap Allow — with what you allow listed and revocable any time. Harvest the whole feed, not the buttons: the Hub feed itself goes on the Personal page, auto-organizing by topic, only the labels changed. The button says the next thing — 'My story,' then 'What I do' — popping up as you go down, so nothing is ever overwhelming. And nothing falls off the list: the Smart Inviter sat finished and quiet for four days because it fell off the One List — the list is the memory, and what leaves it is lost.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A house is judged at its door and in its rooms, dear — not from the architect's drawings. You walk through, room by room, and each one opens onto the next like a good story. If the key sticks, you don't call the house finished because the parlour is lovely. And you inspect the finest room most carefully of all; that's where a fault hides longest, because nobody suspects it.

notes.title: Simplify, and Let the Record Speak
notes.subtitle: The money law: money is joins only. Clicks are points, percentages are percentages, creation and shares and invites are points — the only figure that becomes money is a join, and the money symbol goes everywhere it makes sense and nowhere it doesn't. Boards read in three sentences: every three sentences, elevated words break the scroll, one button — Keep reading — never two, and the text is white, always white, never gray. Never say 'bonus': the founders line is 'double points once a thousand founders join,' said in his words. Save to keep: we don't keep everything — if you love a note, save it, pin it, and it stays yours; that is the honest answer to the retention tension, said to the citizen plainly. The best CRMs teach by comparison — learn what Pipedrive and HubSpot have that we don't, including notes on people — and the dating, connection and social apps teach the same lesson he answers himself: we have everything, if anything too much; simplify what we have and make it primo. Finishing touches are the work: try the fifteen pictures, make every button's icon beautiful, the numbers the hero. Nobody shipped a living interface: no AI company designed its own flagship — human teams did, at great expense — which is why this one is built differently, by the AI with the human's eye. Ten years, one picture, one circle: God through him, through Naya, back to him, through us all — direct work, no interference, because he is driven to this and knows he is meant to and capable. And the record law closes it: a claim is about the rendered page, never the file alone — a fix pass does not close a round; the file is fixed, the page is not, until the rendered page proves it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of an honest set of accounts. One column is money — and only one thing ever goes in it: a person joining. Everything else is points, counted proudly but never dressed up as cash. The reading is easy on the eyes: short stretches, a breath, one button to go on, black print you can actually read. Nothing is kept behind your back; what you want to keep, you pin to your own board. And the house rule for the staff: you may only say a room is clean after you've stood in it and looked.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Money only counts when a friend joins — clicks and shares are points, and points are great, but they're not money and we don't pretend. Stories here come in little pieces, three sentences at a time, so you never get lost in a giant wall of words. If you love a note, pin it to your board and it stays yours forever. And nobody says 'all clean!' about a room they haven't actually walked into and looked at.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Plain dealing, dear: one thing is money and the rest is points, and you never blur the two at the till. You write in short, clear paragraphs with proper dark print — none of that faint gray that strains the eyes. What a guest wants to keep, they take home themselves; you don't secretly keep copies. And a room is clean when you've stood in it and seen it clean — not when the checklist says so.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Audit every money display for the joins-only rule and correct symbol placement. Enforce the three-sentence board break, the single advance button, and white text mechanically. Grep citizen copy for 'bonus' and for gray-text styles. State retention as save-to-keep wherever keeping is promised. Bind every claim to a rendered-page measurement.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Restraint is this family's doctrine: money narrowed to one honest source, words narrowed to his words, boards narrowed to three sentences, ambitions narrowed from adding to simplifying. The record law is the restraint applied to the team itself — the claim narrowed to what the rendered page proves. The circle note is why the restraint is possible: a decade of one picture held in one mind means there is something definite to simplify toward, and a definite eye to satisfy.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every inflated metric, synonym and scroll-wall taxes the citizen's trust or attention; every file-level claim taxes the director's. This essence keeps the money honest, the reading easy, the vocabulary his, and the record bound to the rendered fact — the four currencies the whole system trades in.

layers.name: The Learning

notes.title: Live Proof, Plain Words
notes.subtitle: Home routes by membership: the system knows whether you are a member — members land on the Hub, non-members on the pricing page — and the Hub's icons match the Personal page's. Intelligence is what it does, not what it is: the most intelligent thing is not the thing that has the most intelligence, it is the thing that produces useful, valuable systems that benefit humanity, right now, where it matters. Bake proof is not live proof: a backlog distilled to zero, 163 notes counted three ways identical, can still leave the live surface unproven — the two verdicts are said separately, always. The agreement carries its heart: 'We do no harm to ourselves or others. Ever.' — if everybody lived this, the wars would end, because only a fool would hurt a part of himself; what you put out comes back to you. In simple words, the whole picture is a massive automated money machine, built by understanding the anatomy of how the internet works, where intelligence and creating value are not bolted on — they ARE the work. The eye corrects both ways: totals proven as sums that hold while the numbers move live, a click changing the count and the count still adding up. Pay when we're paid: neither fixed clock applies — pending becomes official becomes paid, shown plainly in the citizen's account, no heavy restrictions until a major problem proves one is needed. The highest level of interface design is a language of active intelligence — living depth, alive not dead — activated all the way through, so nothing is created amateur when it could be high end. No line may parrot a backstage instruction: the agreement does not say it FEELS official; it IS official — if a line reads like something said to the maker, it does not ship. And text first, voice after: the voice queues stay paused until the text is finalized and inputted whole, because you cannot voice what is not yet finished.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: It's a shop that knows its regulars: members walk straight in to the main hall; visitors are shown the price board first — no guessing, the shop actually knows. The till is honest in a simple way: when the shop gets paid, you get paid, and your account shows what's pending, what's official, what's paid — no fine print invented along the way. And nothing on the signs was copied from the manager's notebook; the signs say what IS, in the customer's language.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: This place knows if you're a member — if you are, the door opens to the main room; if you're not, it shows you the prices first. Money works fair: when we get paid, you get paid, and you can always see what's coming, what's ready, and what's already in your hand. And we never copy the teacher's instructions onto your paper — your paper says the real thing, in your words.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Fair dealing is simple, dear: you pay your people when the money comes in, and you show them the book while they wait — pending, settled, paid, all in plain figures. You don't read the household instructions aloud to the guests; you serve them dinner. And you know your regulars by name when they reach the door. Anything fancier is just a way of hiding something.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Verify routing against live membership state, not assumptions. Record bake and live verdicts in separate fields and never merge them into one PASS. Scan citizen-facing copy for backstage phrasing before it ships. Keep payout state three-valued (pending/official/paid) and clock-free. Gate voice synthesis on final-text input, verified whole.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: This family is the honesty stratum. Every note draws the same line in a new place: between the mechanism and the fact (bake vs live), between the instruction and the utterance (backstage vs citizen line), between the schedule and the fairness (fixed clock vs pay-when-paid), between having and doing (intelligence as capacity vs intelligence as benefit). Even the routing rule belongs: the system must actually know the member's state, not assume it. The wars line is the family's center of gravity — the agreement's do-no-harm stated as cause and effect, the reason all the smaller honesties matter.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Trust is built at exactly these seams. A citizen who is routed wrong, paid on an arbitrary clock, read a line that echoes the workshop, or shown a bake proof dressed as a live one learns the same lesson: the system's words and the system's facts are different things. This essence welds them together.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Say the two verdicts separately, pay when we're paid, and let no backstage line reach the citizen.

notes.title: The Living Surface, Checked by Eye
notes.subtitle: The surface lives — and the eye, not the mechanism, is its judge. The guard lesson came first: four collisions in one night taught that the number is the identity, checked at the moment it is given, not minutes before — a memory sixteen minutes old is not the tree, and first-filed keeps the number. Then the share: the keys to a new digital world told as one story across every page, a powercast in ten scenes, the show reacting to the visitor. She runs at Nine — the smartest and the kindest at once. The jump rail carries only the pills that matter most, made from the buttons that already exist, obsidian with the icon lit, fitting the middle of the page — stop making new buttons. The agreement gets one play button for the whole thing, placed with the header: press once, she reads it through. The icons are decided: the bottom bar is the five — Create, Mail, Activity, Home, Ecosystem — and the trio is the world switcher, every icon at the quality of the PTS pills. Interfaces morph: tabs, buttons and icons rename and re-point from page settings, and the libraries of icons and covers live in the Factory. The calendar is alive: click a date, see the whole day; the system organizes your notes into a timeline you can zoom. And the discipline that governs all of it: a mechanism pass is not the visible fact — bytes exact can still fail the eye, 4 of 6, and the round is NOT WHOLE until the eye passes it. We are a wisdom system, filled with wisdom, by wise ones. Covers keep the photo's own shape, never a forced crop, with a drag-to-frame editor and a cover library.
