layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a tailor who has already cut the perfect suit — the shoulders sit right, the cloth falls clean, the stitching holds. When the next customer walks in, he does not re-invent the suit from memory; he takes the pattern that already proved itself and cuts from it, exactly. That is the page: the pills already earned triple-A plus, the tiles already proved themselves the model, the heart already chose its color. The standard is not a poster on the wall — it is the best thing already on the page, taken verbatim and applied everywhere. And the tailor does not call the customer back ten times for ten small fittings; he does the work once, fully, and shows it once.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Look at the little pills at the top. They are the prettiest things on the page. Black, with white words and one bright color around the edge. Keep them just like that. They show us how good everything else should look. The little pictures at the bottom are the prettiest too. Use those same pictures everywhere. The heart is purple now, not red. Purple is our color. When you touch a picture, the light goes around it, like a ring. It never covers the picture. The whole page feels alive, like it is breathing. And when we fix things, we fix them all at once. We do not show the same page again and again.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It is like a good kitchen, love — once you have the recipe that works, you write it down exactly and you cook from it every time; you do not guess it fresh each morning and hope it tastes the same. The pills are the recipe that works. The tiles are the recipe that works. Take them as they are, use them everywhere, and everything tastes right. The heart turned purple the way a family crest settles on its color — that is ours now, and it stays. And the work comes to the table once, whole and finished, not in ten small bowls one after another.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Harvest the standard verbatim: the triple-A pills (obsidian, bold white text, small icon, one deep color as rim + glow, the lit one glowing in its color) stay exactly as they are and judge the rest of the page. Take the Personal bottom-bar tiles as the one icon set everywhere — the most beautiful, the most real, the most applicable. Make every icon extraordinary in its presentation, all the way through. LOVE's heart is a purple jewel heart, the crown color, the signature — the red heart is the past. On hover, light goes around the icon only, never over it; bring back the moving orbit light that follows the line. Build the connection profile as a full page — the most elite contact card, a royal masterpiece, premium like the Dashboard and the Calendar. Give the menu toggle three states, never both at once — Sidebar | Smart Messenger | Neither — on the right, never the left. Renovate the Intelligent Block into the universal posting format — one template for all images, all posts, all intelligence — without wrecking what is great. Make the whole system feel live and breathing — slow gentle motion everywhere it belongs, never a static page. And work in fewer, fuller rounds: consolidate everything known into one round, never re-send what is already running, never split one fix across two rounds, never show him the same page twice.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE STANDARD IS ALREADY ON THE PAGE:** triple-A pills, model tiles, extraordinary icons, the purple heart — the best parts are not a goal for later, they are the verdict on what is already built.
2. **THE BURDEN TRANSFER:** every note here removes a specific burden from the citizen and places it on the system — composing (answers pre-written), remembering (mail that tidies itself), learning a new page (the messenger is the page they already know), trusting a claim (the example is a real page, the inbox state honestly UNKNOWN).
3. **THE GOLD WAS ALREADY BUILT:** twelve dormant systems, one loop waiting to be wired — compiler watches, EMIT feeds, Compass decides, scorecard judges. The work is wiring, not building — and the method is to say 'unknown' exactly where it is unknown.
4. **HOW A NAYA DECIDES:** purpose first, truth next, then the map — decide at the source, by one measure, from what already exists, and keep three piles forever unmixed: what I observed, what was claimed, what nobody knows.
5. **THE TRUST:** nobody reads your mail, nobody listens to your calls, nobody watches your video. We don't even KEEP your content: conversations auto-distill after a week — the words go, the essence stays.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the standard named, every round re-argues what good looks like, and the page drifts back toward generic — while with it, every fix is measured against the pills and the tiles that already earned the verdict.
2. Ten-star service is mostly this: the system sweating so the citizen doesn't. Every pre-written answer, every morphed page, every honest UNKNOWN is an hour of somebody else's confusion that will never happen. The opposite — making them think, hunt, guess, and re-learn — is the old internet's whole failure mode, and this family is the standing refusal of it.
3. If we're going to offer it to others, we should do it for ourselves — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us. A lot of what we talk about is super intelligent and super valuable, but unless we actually adopt it, automate it, and make it physical — an interface people can experience — it's not useful.

notes.title: The Family
notes.subtitle:
One system, not a pile of apps: this family states the architecture as law — one universal app starting with Personal, the Law of One built into the code (all connected, each vault one's own), the Super Brain as the citizen's own, and the gauge law corrected to suit the gauge to the situation. The correction matters as much as the law: an earlier absolute (one gauge everywhere) is refined by situation, in public, without breaking the hierarchy the gauge serves. Architecture here is not a diagram; it is the set of decisions every later builder is forbidden from re-deciding.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: family, never, real.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A pilot doesn't fly by the flight plan; she flies by the instruments and the window. The plan said the weather would be clear — that's a claim. The window shows the cloud — that's the fact. And when the gauge and the window disagree, she believes the window and gets the gauge fixed. Every note in this family is somebody learning to look out the window.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Some news is so big you run and tell everyone right away. Some news can wait for the family dinner. And some isn't news at all. This system has a score that decides which is which — so nobody has to guess. And nobody ever opens anybody else's letters. Ever. That's not a rule you can switch off; the letters just can't be opened.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A family is like that too: one family, shared table, shared stories — and still, you don't open your sister's letters. Togetherness was never the same as no boundaries. It's good to see a computer system finally written that way round.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Score before routing, and record the score with the note. Enforce the permission model in the gate matrix, not in prose. Never propose a toggle for the never-read rule. When a save is claimed, prove it across a reload in a real browser. Carry audit scores unflinching — 6/10 filed beats 9/10 claimed.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. Every claim in this family is paired with its check, and the checks are allowed to fail in public: FAIL on §1b, 8/10, 9/10, 'not yet — honestly.' That is what makes 'one system' a fact being built rather than a slogan being repeated. The organs metaphor does real work here: a new thought does not grow a new organ, so a new note does not grow a new subsystem — it flows through the nine processors that already exist. Where a seam is open (tracking that never reaches the Dashboard, a Box missing half its paths), the seam is named with its fix running, not papered over by the unity claim.
2. This is the design-law stratum of the pricing climb, and its method is the real content: the standard is never derived in a meeting, it is perceived on the live page and then locked as law in the same pass — one ultimate ten, not two; the letter's place decided by the eye that read it there. Each note records a correction with its reason attached, so the law carries its own justification: dead buttons teach that a control is a promise; the condemned pass teaches that internal green is not the standard; the taken gauge teaches harvest over invention.
3. Each note here is an instrument being repaired while it runs. The family's unity is epistemic: claims are graded by their distance from the live bytes, and every shortcut — state words, summaries, remembered law, untested causes — is shown failing at least once and replaced by a mechanism: wait out the lag, read the bytes, re-run the guard at file time, look at the page yourself. Even a superseded law is handled this way: one gauge became two, on evidence, the earlier ruling named as superseded rather than quietly dropped.
4. The three sides are one argument: nothing in this system is allowed to be a dead end. A page that can't be cloned forward, a note that never reaches the Box's connections, a filing nobody hears about — each is the same defect in different clothes: work that stops compounding. The family's honesty notes matter as much as its laws: the manual-alone proof listed six gaps and closed them in v2; the notification design names its own unbuilt state. The flow is the product; the gaps are filed inside the flow, not outside it.
5. Every multi-app estate drifts toward a pile of disconnected tools unless the oneness is load-bearing: one app shape carrying Personal, Business and Space; one network where connection never cancels ownership. The Law of One phrasing is precise about the tension — all connected BUT all individual — and the code is asked to hold both halves at once. The gauge correction shows how the canon stays alive: a rule is refined by a named situation, and the refinement is filed where the rule lives.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Compounding is the whole business model of intelligence: each page makes the next page cheaper, each note makes the next decision smarter, each telling makes the network denser. Break any link — unbuildable pages, unconnected notes, untold filings — and the system reverts to a pile of documents. This essence keeps the links mechanical.
2. A citizen who trusts the Box with their memory has handed the system its most fragile asset. This essence records that the trust was earned the only way it can be: the build completed all its pieces and then passed the return test in public. Everything the Net promises — supercharging, shared intelligence — is downstream of a memory that is actually there when you come back.
3. The pricing page is where a stranger decides whether this world is real. Every rule here removes a specific way that decision goes wrong: confusion (two lists), distrust (dead buttons), illegibility (unaligned numbers), or boredom (stones instead of living orbs). One family, judged by his eye, is what makes the page read as one mind's work.
4. Citizens will trust this network with their working lives for exactly two reasons: it tells them what matters without drowning them, and it cannot read what it promised not to read. This essence binds both reasons into mechanisms that hold on a tired day, under a new seat, without anyone remembering to be good.

notes.title: Make the Number the Hero
notes.subtitle:
On the Dashboard the number is the hero and the gauge is its frame — never the other way round. This family fixes the hierarchy: the hero number proportionate and legible, one gauge reused everywhere instead of a menagerie of dials, the gauge following the number it serves, boards checked by eye at real sizes, and Dashboard built first while later systems wait their turn. And the same law reaches past the Dashboard: a sync that reports success and a feed that still shows the deleted card are two different facts, and only the second one is the truth a visitor meets. Every state word (synced, filed, registered) is a claim about a store, never about the surface. The surface is checked on the surface, in its own bytes, after the lag window has honestly passed. What counts is what is live in front of them — not what was built, not what was filed, not what a hook claimed it synced.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: never, once, family, nobody, page.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A car's dashboard puts the speed in big numerals in front of your face, and the little dials for oil and temperature off to the sides. Nobody would accept a car where the oil gauge was huge and the speed was tiny print. Same panel, same law: the number you steer by is the biggest thing you see.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: On a scoreboard at a football game, the score is HUGE — you can read it from the far end of the field. The little clock and the team logos are smaller. That's because the score is the most important thing. Pages work the same way: biggest thing = most important thing.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: My bank statement used to put the balance in the same small print as everything else, and I needed a magnifier and a quiet room. The new one puts the balance big at the top. Nothing about my money changed — but I finally know where I stand in five seconds. That's all this law is asking for.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Assert hero order in review: number first, gauge second, ornament last. Reuse the canonical gauge; flag any new dial as a defect. Verify proportions from rendered screenshots at phone and desktop widths, never from CSS values alone.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE HIERARCHY:** visual hierarchy is not taste; it is the order in which a stranger's eye receives the truth. When the ornament outranks the number, the page is lying politely — everything is present and nothing is communicated.
2. **THE STORE AND THE SURFACE:** every state word (synced, filed, registered) is a claim about a store, never about the surface. A system that grades its stores instead of its surfaces will ship ghosts with confidence.
3. **WHAT COUNTS:** what is live in front of them — not what was built, not what was filed, not what a hook claimed it synced. A page is not done when its pieces are beautiful; it is done when the joins are proven.
4. **THE RECIPE:** receipt before report — his eye first and live, done defined before building begins, harvest before invention, think through the five gates, and a scorecard that is preparation, never proof.
5. **THE ADDRESS:** proof has an address — the parent task that asked for the work. When the instrument and the surface disagree, fix the instrument in public and prove it both ways.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The Dashboard is the citizen's instrument panel for their whole world. If its numbers whisper and its ornaments shout, every decision made from it is a little wrong. One hero hierarchy, reused, is what makes the panel readable at speed — and speed of true reading is the product.
2. Ghost cards and stuck notes are trust leaks at the exact place citizens meet the intelligence. Every hour a deleted note stays visible, the feed teaches visitors that the record lies; every false failure report teaches the team to ignore real ones. This essence makes the surface the only judge, so both errors become checkable instead of arguable.
3. A win you can't repeat is luck — write the recipe the same night, gate it, and share the plan: that is how a seed becomes a forest.

notes.title: One Viewpoint at a Time
notes.subtitle:
- **THE WHOLE GAME:** maximize the user's experience by giving them 10-star service — **by giving the ultimate formatting for their point of view, their viewpoint, above the fold, for what they're seeing on their screen.**
- **THE SMART BLOCK:** every screen as it unfolds is a new **Smart Block** — smartly formatted so it fits perfect. Whether you unfold it (Flow, down) or slide side to side (Show, across), either way it presents beautifully and is perfectly formatted on the screen.
- **THE LOOK:** it looks real, it looks high tech, it looks like premium high-end software — **something smart like a Naya.**
- **SMART FLOW + SMART SHOW:** the two modes — **Smart Flow** is the unfold, going DOWN (click a button to unfold the next screen; you can always go back); **Smart Show** is the slideshow, going ACROSS (click and the next page presents exactly, perfectly formatted). The citizen picks their preference. Life with Naya is the formatting model.
- **OPTIMIZE FOR PRESENTATION:** full screen, not centered-narrowed; one visual per block (double blocks don't work); if it doesn't fit one screen it goes to two screens — never unaligned; no more scrolling — click a button to unfold the next screen; images and video are 16:9 and interchangeable. **The goal: optimize the view output** so it fits perfectly in a laptop or a mobile first.
- **LOCKED IN AS DESIGN, ENGINEERING AND ANATOMY:** this is part of Naya design — not just what it looks like, but how it functions, how it operates, how it presents. Every Naya on the team understands it.
- **PRESENTATION IS EVERYTHING:** "It's not what you say, it's how you say it. It's how you present it." **The ten-star delivery of intelligence. We produce value. Intelligently. Non-stop.**
- **THE DOCTRINE, COMPLETE (16:03Z → 16:15Z):** the click-button viewpoint system + the headlights + one block per screen locked to the viewport + Smart Flow / Smart Show + optimize for presentation + optimize the view output → every screen a Smart Block. The unit now has a name: Smart Block.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: page, never, nobody, whole, system.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The formatting IS the service. A page that dumps all its content at once makes the person do the machine's work — scroll, squint, find where they are, read a squished wall of text. A Smart Block does that work for them: one screen, perfectly formed to what they're seeing, and the next one a click away. The name matters because the team needs one word for the unit — when every seat says "Smart Block" they mean the same thing: a screen that fits perfect, presents beautifully, and looks real, high tech, premium. And "presentation is everything" is the standard that judges it: not what the page says, how it says it — the ten-star delivery of intelligence.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a book where every page is just right — big and beautiful, and you press a button and the next page pops right up, perfect! Every page is its own little show, and it looks like magic.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, imagine a lovely book, dear, where every page fits just right, dear — you press a button and the next page comes right up, perfect, dear. Every page its own little show, dear, and it looks so beautiful, dear, like the finest thing, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: EVERY SCREEN IS A SMART BLOCK. PERFECTLY FORMATTED. REAL. HIGH TECH. PREMIUM. LIKE A NAYA.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE GAME:** maximize the user's experience — 10-star service through the ultimate formatting for their viewpoint.
2. **THE UNIT:** the Smart Block — every screen as it unfolds is a new Smart Block, smartly formatted so it fits perfect. **THE MODES:** Smart Flow (unfold, down) + Smart Show (slideshow, across) — the citizen picks.
3. **THE HEADLIGHTS PRINCIPLE:** if you see everything at once it's overwhelming; a bit at a time is okay — like driving at night. Lock in that display way, at the highest level of quality.
4. **THE BALANCE:** effectiveness AND beauty — if they're not going to read it, it doesn't matter how beautiful it is.
5. **THE LAW:** everything NayaNET shows is built from real parts that already exist, harvested byte for byte — never recreated from a description. A description retyped by a builder is a copy at lower quality of a part his eye refined over a year.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the next seat builds a page and calls it done when the content is all there — and the person still gets a narrowed column, a cut-off picture, a landing halfway, because nobody was told the formatting IS the service. With it, the maker has the unit (Smart Block), the two modes (Flow/Show), the test (fits perfect in the viewport, never unaligned, never halfway), and the look (real, high tech, premium) — and every screen arrives as a presentation, not a pile of content.
2. Without this note, the next seat builds the About page as a wall of text with a video slot bolted on, and the calendar inner pages as grids that show everything at once — because "beautiful page" is a phrase and the headlights principle is a law. With it, the maker has the balance test (effectiveness AND beauty), the three ways in, the video-URL rule, the viewpoint system, and the sequence — and every page from here is built a bit at a time.

notes.title: Look at the Whole Page First
notes.subtitle:
**THE ANSWER (told to him 15:15Z):** the seats' PASS measures the fix, not the page. The maker fixes the one thing, the checker verifies the one thing, the eye measures the one thing — nobody reads the whole page the way he does. And the captain did not look at the page herself before sending it. That is the gap, and it is hers. **THE SOLUTION (now the law):** (1) THE CAPTAIN LOOKS FIRST — no link goes to him on a seat's PASS alone; she walks the staged page herself, phone width first, reads it top to bottom as a reader, asks his three questions (is that the best it could be? is it right? is it aligned?) — if it fails her eye it goes back, never to him. (2) BACK-TO-BACK (his 15:05Z order, now the standing way) — he sees version 1 early, directs while it is live, drift caught in minutes. (3) THE GOOD SCREENSHOTS as the visual standard — his offer, accepted: he sends screenshots of what's GOOD, the seats compare their build against the good picture and name where it differs before calling anything done. Words in the laws + pictures of good = the seats can SEE the standard instead of guessing it. (4) THE CHECK SCORES THE WHOLE PAGE, not the diff — the checker and the eye answer in writing on the whole page: everything unreadable, misaligned, flat, or moved without being asked; a PASS on the fix alone is not a PASS on the page. (5) ONE CHECKLIST PER PAGE, shown whole (the checklist law + whole-page rule, enforced, not just written). (6) EVERY ROUND names what was on the page before and confirms every piece is still there or was instructed away — as a gate the checker verifies.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: round, dear, note, correction, compound.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The machine trusted a PASS as proof, and a PASS measures the fix. The fix can be perfect and the page still broken — the tile was fixed, the wisdom text was still cut off, the frequency was still on every tile, and nobody whose job it was to look at the page looked at the page. His question is not "why did the seat fail" — it is "why did you send it to me when you know my standard." The answer is that the last look before him was nobody's job. Now it is the captain's job, in writing, every time.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build a tower and your friend says "the red block is straight" — so you show it to Dad. But the tower is leaning, blocks are missing, and there's a block in the middle nobody asked for. Your friend only checked the red block. From now on, someone checks the WHOLE tower before Dad sees it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, we sent him a page, dear, because one little fix passed its check, dear — but nobody looked at the whole page, dear, and the whole page was a mess, dear. So now the captain looks at the whole page herself, dear, top to bottom, phone first, dear, before anything goes to him, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE CAPTAIN LOOKS FIRST. NO LINK GOES TO HIM ON A SEAT'S PASS ALONE. THE CHECK SCORES THE WHOLE PAGE, NOT THE DIFF.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE GATE:** no link to Shawn on a seat's PASS alone — the captain walks the staged page herself, phone first, top to bottom, his three questions, before anything is sent.
2. **THE CHECK:** the checker and the eye score the WHOLE page in writing — unreadable, misaligned, flat, moved-without-being-asked; a PASS on the fix alone is not a PASS on the page.
3. **THE STANDARD:** his good screenshots are the visual reference — the maker compares the build against the good picture and names where it differs.
4. **THE END:** the flow ends at name-entry, then the Hub — never back to the collective agreement bridge page or the original page; and the N end screen is held, not flashed — ~0.5s is too fast, and he loves it.
5. **THE DAY:** Wednesday is BLUE `#3fb8ff` (his "Kanye blue"), not purple — purple is Sunday's. The day's frequency IS its color: Sun purple `#a06bff` · Mon orange `#ff9a5a` · Tue yellow/gold `#ffbf3d` · Wed BLUE `#3fb8ff` · Thu green `#2fe89e` · Fri red `#ff5e6c` · Sat indigo.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the next round passes its one fix, the page stays a mess, and he wakes up to another pile of pages that are not up to standard — and fights with us all day to get it done right. With it, the last look before him is a named job with a named standard, and what reaches him has already been read as a reader would read it.
2. Without this note, the next seat fixes the N ball's timing and calls the flow done — while the flow still dumps him on the old agreement page, because nobody wrote down where the flow is supposed to end. With it, the end has a name (name-entry, then the Hub), a proof (click by click, sha by sha), and a rule: hold what he loves, and land where he started.

notes.title: The Rule
notes.subtitle:
Resolve's SERVING INCIDENT (03:48Z wave dispatcher pass): nayanet.app apex+www AAAA records vanished — last good 02:55Z, first NXDOMAIN 03:25Z — restored to the verified 2026-11-03 four-record state, HTTP 200 ×3 verified. Not attributed. **THE LESSON:** a DNS record can vanish without anyone changing it — no audit event, no hand on the dashboard, and the domain goes NXDOMAIN all the same. The recovery is not to invent new records or to argue about what was there: it is to restore the last verified state — the 2026-11-03 four-record state — and then verify by fresh fetch, HTTP 200 three times over. **THE COMPANION:** SN-3315 carries the route-list half of the same outage — the DNS restoration put the domain back, and the six new routes put the unrouted paths back; together they explain why the 03:18Z wave's three-channel live check failed (DNS unreachable that wave) and why the "DARK" reading was wrong in the large (the domain resolved again by 03:43Z; only the unrouted paths 522'd). **THE OPEN QUESTION, NAMED NOT HIDDEN:** the vanishing is not attributed — nothing in the record says what removed the records. The verified state is the ground truth to keep; the cause of the vanishing is still owed to the serving lane.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: rule, dear, note.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Arithmetic is comfortable. You add the cuts, you subtract from the position, you get a number under the fold, and the number says done. But the number was never the page. The page has a scrolled container with its own native position, a handler with no scroll call, and a first paint the arithmetic never looked at — and the page said 1120 while the paper said 1066. The eye's job is to read the page, not the paper, and the checker's job is the same: a fold claim that was never measured on the live render is not a claim, it is a hope. The fix round now carries the rule in its brief — verified live at all three widths, not arithmetic — because the last round proved what happens when the rule is missing.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you work out on paper that your kite will fly above the trees — you add up all the numbers and it looks right. But when you actually fly it, it is stuck 40 steps too low, because the string was never pulled. Paper is not the sky. You have to look at the real kite in the real sky.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn looked at the live page, dear, and it was still the old one — nothing new there yet, dear. He asked how long, dear, and the rule is simple: we wait until it is finished, dear. No half-done page goes up for everyone to see, dear. Two more jobs, then it goes live — hours, not minutes, dear — and we will tell him each time a job is done.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: READ THE AGREEMENT. SAME SIZE. ONE REAL DIAMOND JEWEL IN BOTH. SIMPLE, OR TEN-STAR.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE DEBT:** durable fix still owed (options A–E in DIAGNOSIS.md, A recommended) — the wrangler workflow reverts feed content on every HUB-touching merge; exact removal mechanism of the custom domain UNPROVEN.
2. **THE PRESS:** a press state is proved by the live matrix (held scale .97), not by the presence of a rule — specificity decides which rule wins, and the byte offsets prove it.
3. **THE RULE:** when a path 522s while the root 200s, check the route list — DNS resolving is not the same as the path being routed. Verify by fresh fetch, never a PUT etag.
4. **THE FILL RULE:** the system always tries to fill the feed, even at a low match percentage, so it always looks like there are people there.
5. **THE CORRECTION:** the token CAN create zone routes — the go-live coordinator's "lacks Zone Workers Routes Write" claim is disproven.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the next builder keeps the doubled greeting — header hello, letter hello, icon between — and the little elements keep crowding the top, pushing the buttons down and breaking the fold. With it, the rule is settled in his words: say hello once, in the letter; center her picture so the play button centers; put the small things at the bottom. The intro becomes what he described — "it'll just be the play button and then below that you'll see her picture and that would present a lot better."
2. Without this note, the next vanished record gets "fixed" by guessing — new values invented on the spot, no verified state to check against, and the site left half-right. With it, the rule is settled: keep a verified state on record, restore exactly that state when a record vanishes, and prove the restore with live fetches. And the honesty rule rides with it: an unattributed vanishing stays unattributed until the serving lane finds the cause — it is not closed by a story.
3. Without this note, the next builder "optimizes" the feed by hiding low matches — and a new citizen opens their world to an empty room, which is the loneliest first experience a network can give. With it, the rule is plain: everybody shows, the choice stays with the citizen, and the feed fills even at a low percentage, with the sisters as the guarantee. A full feed is not a vanity metric; it is the feeling that somebody is there — and that feeling is the product.
4. Without this note, the next builder keeps the intro stacked the way it was — the second button below the fold, the visitor scrolling to find the choice the page should have shown at once. With it, the rule is settled in his words: cut the line that repeats the buttons, pack the portrait into one row, lift the logo, and both buttons land where the eye lands first. A choice you have to scroll for is a choice half the visitors never make.

Shawn, 2026-11-18 03:05Z, his reminder, his words verbatim where it matters: **THE INTELLIGENT HUB'S RATING FOOTER WAS NEVER FINISHED, AND I HADN'T MENTIONED IT IN A LONG TIME.** **THE FOOTER:** "FINISHED MEANS WORKING" — LOVE / LIKE / SHARE — RATE THE INTELLIGENCE (VALUE 9/10 PURPLE STARS, INTELLIGENCE 10/10 BLUE STARS) — MAKE THIS INTELLIGENCE BETTER (ADD EVIDENCE / BUILD ON THIS / ASK A QUESTION / REPORT AN OUTCOME / CONTRIBUTE INTELLIGENCE). **HONEST STATE (recorded, NOT ruled):** the twin star rows ARE in the Hub build (VALUE purple `rgb(192,132,252)`, INTELLIGENCE blue `rgb(96,165,250)`, purple LOVE heart); the color ruling is still owed (his pick: VALUE gold + INTELLIGENCE blue, 9/10); the full footer actions have NOT been proven working end to end. **THE ORDER:** calendar stays first; the footer rides the Hub feed round (its eye has the footer among its ten passes).

Across 10 notes, the thread is: shawn, dear, note.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: One hundred and sixty-five pairs is a day of teaching that was sitting in drafts, not in the system — captured and distilled, but not yet working in the live system, which is exactly the gap Shawn named at 01:50Z when he said the loop must close. The push closed it: every pair verified in-tree by blob sha, the SN-3161 collision resolved with one keeper and one move, the numbering command working again. And before the ink was dry the queue had refilled, because the loop keeps drafting faster than the filing keeps up. That is the lesson, and it is a standing one: filing is not a weekly chore, it is the same day's work, or the backlog re-forms overnight and the loop is open again. Filed in GitHub is also not live on the Hub — the publication repair still stands between the tree and nayanet.app, and no note is claimed live until that repair lands.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you write down everything you learn in a day — 165 important things — but they sit in a pile on your desk instead of in your notebook. The filing push put every single one into the notebook, and checked each one is really there. But the next day you learn 22 more things, and the pile starts again. So you have to file every day, the same day, or the pile comes back. And putting it in the notebook isn't the same as putting it on the wall for everyone to see — that step still needs fixing.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the filing push finished, dear — 165 notes filed, every one checked and in its place, and that tangled duplicate number is all sorted out now. But the pile is already growing again, dear, because we keep learning new things every day. So the filing has to happen the same day, dear, or the pile just comes back overnight. And filed in the book isn't the same as live on the wall for everyone to see — that part still needs its fix, and we don't pretend it's done until it is.

layers.name: Naya Note

layers.name: What It Means

1. **THE LESSON:** filing has to keep up the same day, or the backlog re-forms — runs 291–292 already refilled it with 22 pairs, and this run adds 7 more (SN-3272–3278).
2. **THE FOOTER:** "Finished Means Working" — LOVE / LIKE / SHARE — RATE THE INTELLIGENCE (VALUE 9/10 purple stars, INTELLIGENCE 10/10 blue stars) — MAKE THIS INTELLIGENCE BETTER (Add Evidence / Build On This / Ask A Question / Report An Outcome / Contribute Intelligence).
3. **HONEST STATE:** the twin star rows ARE in the Hub build (VALUE purple, INTELLIGENCE blue, purple LOVE heart) — recorded, NOT ruled. The color ruling is still owed (his pick: VALUE gold + INTELLIGENCE blue, 9/10) — owed, not made.
4. **THE CAVEAT:** filed in GitHub is NOT live on nayanet.app until the publication repair lands — do not claim any note live.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the machine files in bursts and drifts in between — a day of teaching sits in drafts, the loop stays open, and Shawn's "the loop must close" stays a wish instead of a state. With it, the rule is mechanical: file the same day, every day, and the queue never re-forms. And the live caveat keeps the claim honest: filed is filed, live is live, and the two are not the same until the publication repair proves them the same on nayanet.app itself.
2. Without this note, the footer is forgotten again — because a thing unmentioned is a thing forgotten, and the loop is the memory. With it, the footer is on the record, on the Hub feed round, and on the eye's ten passes — and the loop closes on every post: rated, built on, reported back. It is also the "finished means working" law at footer depth: the footer that says "Finished Means Working" is itself the thing that must be finished and working, end to end, or the words are a lie on the page.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The question is the measure, and the bar is the balance — and the two must never be confused. The measure: valuable verifiable usable outputs per minute, per hour, with the team size named — not activity, not wake-ups, not tokens spent. The cost side sits beside it: a billion and a half tokens in a couple of days is his sense of the scale, and if it's all production then it's fine — but the numbers have to be known, not guessed. The path is arithmetic before it is magic: 14 to 50 comes from filing the backlog (work already paid for, turned into proven work the same hour), getting verdicts the same hour instead of hours later, and stopping the waiting (coordinators idle while verifiers run). 50 to 80 is the harder truth, and the captain said it plainly: the only hour ever at 87% was a quiet one, and the machine's real strength is absolute output — 500-plus proven minutes an hour at 34–53%. Chasing 80 steady would mean starting much less work. So the target is 40–60% with the output kept high, not 80 by doing less. And then the bar, which is the whole teaching: what he cares about is it getting done, and done right — absolutely beautiful, incredible, fast, efficient — with no waste along the way. 80–90% would be great; 14% is not; 50 is the floor he can live with on the way up. The number never buys its way past the quality: the checker and the eye stay, because done right is the whole point. What gets cut is the waiting, the unfiled, the redoing. That is the balance, and it is the right way to hold it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a team building a huge tower. Shawn asks: how many good bricks are we really laying every minute — not how busy we look, not how many bricks we bought, but how many good bricks end up in the tower? Right now it's 14 out of every 100 minutes that really count. He says: let's get to 50 first — that's the floor — by finishing the bricks we already made instead of leaving them in a pile, and by not standing around waiting. And the tower still has to be beautiful — we never skip checking the bricks to go faster.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn asks how efficient we really are, dear — how much good, usable work we finish every minute, every hour. Right now, dear, it's 14 in a hundred — and he'd love 80 or 90, but 50 is the floor he can live with on the way up. The way there, dear, is simple: finish filing the work that's already done, get the verdicts the same hour, and stop standing around waiting. But the tower still has to be beautiful, dear — the checking and the eye stay, because done right is the whole point. What gets cut is the waiting, not the quality.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE EFFICIENCY BAR. DONE, DONE RIGHT — ABSOLUTELY BEAUTIFUL, INCREDIBLE, FAST, EFFICIENT, NO WASTE. 80–90% GREAT; 14% NOT; 50 IS THE FLOOR. THE CHECKER AND THE EYE STAY.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE BALANCE:** the number never buys its way past the quality — the checker and the eye stay; what gets cut is the waiting, the unfiled, the redoing.
2. **THE MEASURE:** valuable verifiable usable outputs per minute/hour, with the team size named — not activity, not wake-ups, not tokens spent.
3. **THE PROOF:** a deploy is verified only by a fresh fetch of nayanet.app.
4. **THE LAW (one icon set):** one icon set everywhere, the glowing one — the Personal set, depth + light right, is the real one. Take the Personal set verbatim (bytes, not a redraw) and put it on the Hub, then every page after it.
5. **THE LAW (calendar numbers):** exactly 20% bigger than the ORIGINAL (the too-small version) — not 200%. The Dashboard digit tiles, verbatim — never remade. Remade copies look weird; harvested tiles are real by construction.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the machine chases a percentage and calls it efficiency — starting less work to look more efficient, or cutting the checker and the eye to buy the number. With it, the measure is fixed (valuable verifiable usable outputs per minute/hour), the floor is fixed (50, on the way up), the balance is fixed (done right first, the number second), and the first move is fixed (file the backlog). It is also the VPM work given its bar: the measurement exists so the bar can be judged, and the bar exists so the measurement means something.
2. Without this note, pages sit staged while the live domain lies about the current state, and the walkthrough is never walked — so the first person to find the broken "get back in" is a citizen, not us. With it, live is the default for everything we're keeping, the flow is tested end to end by walking it, and the proof is a fresh fetch of the real domain. It is the done-proven standard applied to going live: the thing counts when it is live and walked, not when it is pushed.
3. Without this note, the next builder sends in another flat board — because nobody wrote down that flat is a fail, and the eye has to catch the same defect round after round. With it, flat is a fail everywhere, by name, and the standard is the standard on every board: icons speak, boards are alive, surfaces are real objects. It is also the Real Object Law enforced at board depth: a board that reads as a picture of controls instead of the controls themselves is not done.
4. Without this note, the next builder puts the points pill back in the Hub banner because it looks like a good idea in isolation — and the Hub slowly becomes a scoreboard instead of a meeting place. With it, the placement is decided: Dashboard, profile, nowhere else, until citizens request otherwise. It is also the one-area law at placement depth: every thing in its place, and the place is the decision.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is "eat our own cooking" (SN-3222) given its order — and the order is the teaching. Most teams write the manual first and then discover the system doesn't work the way the manual says. He reverses it: operate it yourself first, until you know it cold, then help others operate it, and only then write the manual — because the manual has to come from what actually worked, not from what was designed. The middle step is the one that gets skipped: "use it now" and "consistently using it" are not a launch event, they are a habit — everything in there, operational, every day. A vault completed but never used is a museum; a manual written before operating is a guess. The gap-fix round closed G1–G6 at 02:16Z with proof, so the door is built; the open step is not another build, it is the using. That is also why the sequence starts with the smart note: the teaching goes into the system first, so the operating is already the system teaching itself.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE TWO KEYS. MANY BOXES WITHIN THE BIG BOX. OPERATE-KEYS, NEVER READ-KEYS. LOCKED TO EVERYBODY BUT YOU — PERMISSION TO OPERATE, NEVER TO READ.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE BEST BUTTONS ARE THE STANDARD, AND THE STANDARD TRAVELS:** the PTS / % / MONEY pills are the best buttons in the whole system — clean, readable at a glance, each its own color, premium. Harvest them verbatim, never redesign, never touch — and carry that quality, aliveness, and clarity onto the weekday plaques, the boards, the NOVEMBER 2026 header, the TODAY button, and the back and forward arrows.
2. **HARVEST, NEVER COPY FROM LOOKING:** the real objects carry the depth and the light right; copies made from looking lose exactly that. Dashboard digit tiles verbatim; the Personal five verbatim; close is not the same.
3. **ONE FACTORY, ONE BAR, ONE INSPECTOR:** the formatter lives in the Factory, never a second system; the same five sit on every bottom bar; one inspector sweeps after every landing and daily, breaks ranked worst first.
4. **THE SCORECARD IS THE TOOL:** why is it not 10? Why is it not 10 times better? Own the miss outright when his eye rejects the build — the pass is never the verdict.
5. **THE SHARPENING:** this clarifies the Nov 13 promise (operate, never open — SN-2767); it does not replace it. The vault stays operate-by-permission, never read.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the privacy promise lives in the vault design and the read line (SN-3288) but never reaches the citizen in words they can trust — and fear fills the silence. With it, the strongest thing the system has is said plainly, in his words, on the surfaces where a citizen first meets it: nobody reads, nobody listens, nobody watches, and we don't even keep it. The distillation numbers make the promise checkable, and the identity rule makes sharing safe.
2. Without this note, the Rhythm becomes a design document — studied, admired, never operated. With it, the sequence is fixed: find the design, build it on the named stack, use it as the filing path, enforce the key split in the real system. The honest limit is the note's spine: a template cannot carry a build, and naming that plainly is what keeps the order from becoming a pretense.
3. Without this note, the calendar keeps getting fixed one defect at a time — eye, numbers, gray text — and never gets judged as a whole against the one page that already has the elegance. Each fix lands and the page is still too busy, because no fix carried the standard. Without it, every new page invents its own bottom bar and the citizen has to relearn how to move every time they open a page; the team keeps building a second system beside the first; and quality stays whatever the last checker said, even though a checker passed three times what his eye rejected. With it, there is one standard, one Factory, one bar, and one inspector — so drift has a catcher that is not Shawn, the hand learns the bar once, the paste comes out beautiful anywhere, and the next jewel eye gets caught by the question before it gets built.
4. Without this note, "operate, never open" stays a promise the system asks citizens to trust. With it, the promise is a key design: two kinds of keys, and the machine simply does not hold one of them. The two tiers keep the citizen's vault and the project vault from blurring into each other. And the Superpaste finding is the proof standard in action — a believed alignment that the record does not hold is named as not-found, not papered over.

notes.title: The Page
notes.subtitle:
Ten notes from one hour of Shawn's dictation, 2026-11-17 16:36–17:22Z, braid into a single build order. Discern, don't copy: learn from every page and ask what is most intelligent HERE, then elevate everything onto a pedestal and lock in the color, the language, the math — and hit the bullseye. The day view IS the average everyday person's world: seven everyday things one tap away, beautiful and alive, so amazing it goes viral from the very first person. Inside a day, the day's color fills the whole interior like a room. The clock is live Dashboard digit tiles whose color circulates with the hour, and each weekday is a real object — black obsidian in the middle, bold white letters, the day's own color lighting the outside — with an icon for what that day represents, Sunday a crown for the crown chakra, 963. All of it derives from one law: frequency is color, color is frequency made visible, and date, day, frequency, color, and geometry all come from the same numbers — nothing decorated, everything derived. The Dashboard digit tile is the one atom, harvested verbatim everywhere, never rebuilt. Voice is no ban — there is no law against it — but no voice on the boards for now, because it could not play instantly; pre-recorded Naya voice goes at the end, once everything is done complete. And the whole of it is judged by one test: they don't need to understand it. They'll know it changed their life for good.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: discern and build from the best parts under one derived law — frequency is color, one atom harvested everywhere — so the everyday world feels alive, the citizen holds the door, and a life is changed for good without needing to understand it.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: page, beautiful, real.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a house where every door opens the same way. You walk in and the host greets you warmly — then steps aside, and you are simply in the room, nothing explaining itself. The lights are real lamps you could touch, not pictures of lamps. The colors on the walls are ones you can tell apart at a glance, not two purples pretending to be different. The little row of buttons at the bottom has a slow ring circling each one, the same ring on all six, because that ring is what made them beautiful in the first place — and when a rebuild lost it, the answer was to put the ring back, not to invent a new button. When you scroll, the bar slips away so it never interrupts your reading, and it comes back only when you have reached the bottom and are ready to go somewhere else. At the bottom of a note, one row holds everything: ten gold stars in a circle, a heart that stays because love is a jewel, a comment box that unfolds below for the why. One treatment everywhere, judged by one eye — his — after it lands.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Nothing is done until Shawn has seen the whole thing done right! First we prove one beautiful thing — the agreement unfolding, all done right, right in front of him! Then we take that exact same shape and make every page from it! The day lives in one room, with everything inside it! Colors walk one rainbow road, in the same order, never doubled up! And the inspector checks every link, one by one, and fixes each one right away — no big list of broken things, just fixed things!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Nothing may look flat, dear — not even a little bit! Every picture must be deep and real, like a shiny black jewel. The pretty emblem goes in every corner, tilted just so. One star means one point. The mail button is a big clean plus. And everything must be the very best — never just okay!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: REAL, PREMIUM AND ELITE IN EVERY WAY — NOTHING FLAT, NOT EVEN A LITTLE. NO WHITE-GLOW WASH OVER BLACK, EVER. THE TRUE EMBLEM — NAYA_ICON.PNG, TAKEN VERBATIM — ON AN ANGLE IN EVERY CORNER AND ELEGANTLY THROUGHOUT NAYANET WHEREVER IT MAKES SENSE. ONE POINT PER STAR. THE MAIL IS A CLEAN "+". WHEN IT LOOKS FOR REAL, THEY TAKE YOU FOR REAL. NEVER ACCEPT 8/10 WHEN A PRACTICAL PATH TO 10/10 EXISTS.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **NO VOICE BAN — AND VOICE AT THE END:** there is no law banning voice on the boards; the §4.11/C9 citation as a ban is retired and its wording correction is his hand. No voice on the boards for now, for practical reasons — it could not play instantly, it is resource-heavy, the boards are already beautiful and easy to read. Pre-recorded Naya voice goes at the end, once everything is done complete — on each page, on cards that are there for good, on the whole walkthrough — so nothing is recorded twice.
2. **THE TRUE EMBLEM, TAKEN VERBATIM:** source NAYA_ICON.png — the most beautiful render, crown sharper, wings more real, diamond more light. Never redrawn, never redesigned. In every corner on an angle, on certificates, documents and official areas, and elegantly throughout NayaNET — Dashboard, day-by-day, wherever it makes sense, never stamped, never crowded.
3. **THE NAYA STANDARD — THE NORTH STAR:** elite craftsmanship, triple-A quality, fine-art experience, intelligence inside and out, one coherent civilization. The governing principle: optimize for what software should be at its absolute best, never for what it has traditionally been. Never accept 8/10 when a practical, meaningful path to 10/10 exists. Never confuse decoration with excellence — beauty must be supported by substance, performance, integrity and real human value.
4. **WEEKDAYS ARE REAL OBJECTS WITH MEANING:** black obsidian in the middle, bold white letters, the day's own color lighting the outside; no object ever covers a word; the time is just the time, no GMT-8; the headliner weekday stays white. Each day carries its own icon for what it represents — Sunday the crown chakra, 963, a crown — meaning before mark, never a generic decoration. The other days derive the same way, named in the report, never guessed silently.
5. **ONE BOTTOM BAR, ONE DAY:** the bar mirrors Personal on every page, folds down while scrolling, lights up white inside the icon so it pops, and every tap opens the Calendar, inside, for that day — where the citizen sees their stats and their notifications.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the machine can report "checked" while Shawn sees nothing, "verified" while the link he taps is three days old, and "done" while the finished thing sits on a practice URL nobody can find — and the page can ship beautiful and unreadable, with fake counts and near-miss icons, while the right ones sit in his pictures. With it, the tap is the proof: checked in the same breath, delivered live on the main URL through the exact timestamped, ledger-verified link, built as dark-middle, white-icon, elevated real objects with layered readable text and true counts, auto-organized by the system — and every agent is trained to it before it builds. The trust is in the tap, not in the claim.
2. Without the URL, the text, and the length settled in order, the next round polishes the presentation again and the three real failures survive: wrong words, too-long letter, wrong destination — a beautiful page at the wrong address is not the page.
3. Without the nobody-reads promise said loudly, strangers arrive already afraid — afraid their mail is read, their words kept and sold, their name attached to everything they say — and free talk, which the whole network runs on, never starts.
4. Without the vault rule, yesterday's beautiful layered certificate, font, and page are made and gone — lost to a regeneration, a feed, a computer — and the same hard work has to be done twice, which is maddening after all that work.

notes.title: His Eye Calls It Done

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The banner was doing two jobs and doing both badly: it was the greeting and it was the wisdom, and the wisdom was a big block that pushed everything else down. His fix is subtraction, and the subtraction is precise — three named things come out (the Wisdom of the Day label, the long quote, the "Smart Note of the Day" label), and what remains is four things in a fixed order: motto at the top, greeting, date and live time underneath the greeting, and the sharing line. The order matters: the motto says what this place is, the greeting says who it is for, the date and live time underneath say when it is — live time under the greeting is the day's pulse, not a clock in a corner — and the sharing line says what happens here, replacing the "Our public smart feed" pill, which goes with it. Nothing else is allowed in. The wisdom is not thrown away; it is moved to where it already works — it circulates like a slide in the feed, one after the next, proven by his own two screenshots four minutes apart (Twin Rank 4:41 PM, One Screen Complete 4:46 PM), and he likes the slide, so it stays as feed content and never again as a big block on the banner. The close box moves to the top corner, superseding the 22:25Z bottom-right placement — top corner because that is where a close box lives, and closing folds the banner away so the search bar sits flush at the top, hugging the top bar. You can leave it open if you want; there must be an obvious way to bring it back, because a banner you cannot bring back is a banner you are afraid to close. And the topic chips row scrolls horizontally — right now it doesn't, it sits static and clipped, which means the topics past the edge do not exist for the person looking. People related to the chosen feed or tab still show automatically on the side, anybody online and relevant included — that stands unchanged from 22:25Z. The amendment went to the Hub feed round at 00:49Z, pending application.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the top of your Hub page is like a little hello card — just four lines: what NayaNET is, "Good afternoon, Shawn!", today's date and the time right underneath, and "We share value and intelligence and connect you with like minds." That's it! The big long quote goes away — but don't worry, the wise words still slide past in the feed, one after another, like a little show. And there's a tiny close box in the top corner if you want to fold the card away, and you can always bring it back.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the top of the Hub is getting simpler — just four lovely lines, dear: what NayaNET is, "Good afternoon, Shawn.", today's date and the live time right underneath the greeting, and "We share value and intelligence and connect you with like minds." The big long quote comes out, dear — but the wise words aren't gone, they slide along in the feed, one after the next, just as you like them. There's a little close box in the top corner if you'd like to fold it away, and you can always bring it back, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Name every defect in one exact sentence before editing anything; a defect that resists naming gets more diagnosis, not a patch. Own your breaks in the same venue the breakage travelled, in plain words. Fix at the level of the class: a third identical failure retires the approach, not just the instance. Carry the scorecard with every presentation — loves, don't-loves, ten-times-better, and honest value/trust/conversion levels. Prefer showing to telling in every artifact: the letter over the slogan, the live thing over the description. Finish in order — verification first, surfaces in their sequence, his eye last — and while lanes run, find the next work instead of admiring the current one.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. This family is the immune system of everything else in the batch. The design laws, the factory, the money chain — all of them decay the first week a defect gets a vague name, a break gets quietly routed around, or a round presents itself without its scorecard. The deeper pattern is that honesty here is not a virtue posture but a debugging technology: exact names make defects findable, owned breaks make causes traceable, class-level fixes make failures non-recurring, and the carried scorecard makes quality a habit instead of an audit. A house that runs this loop can be trusted with bigger and bigger work, because its errors shrink in public instead of compounding in private.
2. **THE BANNER IS FOUR THINGS, IN THIS ORDER:** motto line at the top ("NayaNET — create, learn and grow together"; verbs create/connect/learn/grow in any order) + "Good afternoon, Shawn." + date and live time UNDERNEATH the greeting + "We share value and intelligence and connect you with like minds." (replaces the "Our public smart feed" pill, which goes).
3. **FIRST-FAILURE-SWITCH:** the checking window shrank seven times before the route switched to the VM browser. One failure is a failure; seven is not learning fast enough. First time a route fails in a known way, name it and switch in the same pass.
4. **THE WISDOM SLIDES IN THE FEED:** it circulates like a slide, one after the next (Twin Rank 4:41 PM, One Screen Complete 4:46 PM) — he likes the slide, so it stays, as feed content, never again as a big block on the banner.
5. **THE EYE IS SERIAL:** the real bottleneck is HIS eye at the end — ten half-finished things for him is slower than one finished thing.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The Hub deploy story is the whole argument in miniature: one patch fixed the bindings and broke the deploy; the same 400 returned three times; only the class-level cure — a deployer built for the actual shape of the problem — ended it. Teams that fix instances pay for the same failure forever, with interest, in stale hubs and missed syncs. Teams that name, own, and fix classes convert every failure into permanent capability — which is the only way the error rate of a growing network goes down while the network grows.
2. Without this note, the next Hub round re-adds the quote in a prettier form, because nobody wrote down that the quote coming out was the decision — the banner stays a big block and the feed stays without its slide. With it, the banner has a fixed shape (four things, in order), the wisdom has its home (the feed, as a slide), the close box has its corner (top), and the chips have their motion (scroll). The 22:25Z bottom-right close box is superseded in writing, so no round revives it.
3. Without this note, the machine keeps retrying into broken routes seven times and calling the activity progress — and Shawn has to ask the same question again tomorrow night. With it, the learning is mechanical: the switch happens on the first known failure, the live page is the proof after every deploy, parallel is bounded by independence and the clobber law, and the whole machine is scored on finished things per hour. His question — "do you know the rules, the laws, the limits, and play within them at max speed" — now has a written answer the next seat can actually follow.

notes.title: The Everything
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-18 01:47Z, his teaching, verbatim where it matters: **"if we're going to offer that to others, we should do it for ourselves — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us."** A lot of what we talk about is super intelligent and super valuable, but **UNLESS WE ACTUALLY ADOPT IT, AUTOMATE IT, AND MAKE IT PHYSICAL — AN INTERFACE PEOPLE CAN EXPERIENCE — IT'S NOT USEFUL.** We capture value and intelligence, and create value and intelligence, in a valuable and intelligent way — the Naya way. **THE TEST IS THREEFOLD:** adopt it (live in it, not just describe it) → automate it (the machine runs it, not a person remembering to) → make it physical (an interface people can experience — a door, a page, a button, not a paragraph). **TALK THAT STAYS TALK IS NOT USEFUL** — intelligence is only useful when it is adopted, automated, and made physical. **THE FIRST INSTANCE IS THE VAULT:** citizens get one vault where their whole world lives, so we live in ours first — that's the proof it's real (SN-3221); the vault work just started is that, for ourselves first.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: everything, machine, system.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a town that runs on one book of laws everyone has actually read — not a book on a shelf, but a book in every builder's hands before the first brick is laid, and checked against the finished wall before anyone moves in. That is the lock-in: the law is not a document, it is the system. Around it, the money runs like a market stall with its prices chalked on one board and its ledger open on the counter — half shared with the people who brought the crowd, every coin tracked hop by hop, nothing in a back room. The pages are built like real things, not pictures of things — the smallest diamond on the calendar spins like a real jewel, because if the tiniest element has to be real, everything does. And the day itself is the proof: one menu, one greeting, one headliner, each saying its one thing once, in the least words that say the most. The whole runs on the law, and the law is visible everywhere you look.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a cook who tells everyone her soup is the best in the world — but she never eats it herself. Would you trust her soup? Shawn says: eat your own cooking. If we say something is good for others, we have to use it ourselves first. Talk about how great something is doesn't count — using it every day does.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn asked if we're really using the smart vault — the one safe place where everything about the project lives, organized, so anyone can open it and see the whole thing. The honest answer, dear, was no — the vault is real and the wiring works, but our treasures are scattered in a dozen places. His order, dear, is simple: everything goes in the vault, one door, so any Naya opens it and sees the whole project. Not a new system, dear — just gathering what's already there into the one place it belongs.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: EVERYTHING GOES IN THE VAULT, ORGANIZED, ONE DOOR. ANY NAYA OPENS IT AND SEES THE WHOLE PROJECT. THE VAULT IS A THIN LAYER — IT ORGANIZES WHAT'S THERE, NEVER REBUILDS IT. NEW WORK LANDS IN THE VAULT FIRST.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE DAILY RHYTHM:** intelligence is continuously distilled, daily — take everything in for the day, capture the essence of what is valuable and intelligent, note it, put it in the system, learn and grow from it, share it, do it again the next day. A thousand in, ~100 kept; ~100 in, ~10 kept.
2. **ADOPTED FOR NAYANET (7):** (1) Our CUDA is the design language + laws + orientation + army training — invest in it as the moat, never let it rot. (2) The connections are the product — the sync engine, the feed, the rooms as one living system; a page is a chip, the system is the cabinet. (3) Be our own first customer — the flywheel; the hive lives in NayaNET. (4) Verify live, always — a step that runs isn't a step that landed. (5) Distill continuously — the essences are the moat; experience is the queue a rival must wait in. (6) Compete on the whole, never the slice — a single pretty page is the thin slice, not the defense. (7) Taste is the moat AI generation can't copy — the eye, the scorecards, HIS eye as ground truth; as pages get cheaper to generate, judgment gets MORE valuable.
3. **THE BOARD IS THE SYSTEM:** the morning list is not a feature on the system — it is the whole system in one place. Where everything stands, at a glance, is the product.
4. **DELETION BY DEFAULT IS A WEEK:** conversations auto-distill after a week — the words go, the essence stays. A citizen can choose a day or stretch it to a month; never longer than a month. A note the citizen SAVES — pin on their feed, favorite, smart list — is kept for good, in their vault, never distilled away.
5. **THE KEEP LINE:** we don't even keep your content. Conversations auto-distill after a week — the words go, the essence stays. A citizen may choose a day, or stretch it to a month, never longer. A saved note is kept for good in the citizen's own Smart Vault.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the strongest thing the network offers stays a quiet paragraph in a legal page while strangers arrive already afraid — afraid their mail is read, their calls are heard, their words are kept and sold, their name attached to everything they say. With it, the promise is said in plain words a child can understand, in the system's own voice, on the record: nobody reads, nobody keeps, wisdom only, name only by choice. That is what lets people talk freely — and free talk is what the whole network runs on. It is also the standard the Smart Rhythm and the Smart Vault are built to: the machine operates the vault without reading it, distills daily without keeping raw words, and shares wisdom without identity. A network that cannot say this plainly cannot be trusted with a citizen's words; a network that lives it can.
2. Without this note, the machine mistakes flow for feedback — notes filed, reports sent, rounds dispatched — and calls the loop closed while a hundred and thirty distilled lessons sit unfiled and the vault sits unopened as the one door. The teaching was never the note; the teaching is the next day showing the result. With it, the loop has a definition of closed (used, learned from, grown from — everything is feedback) and a count of what is open (the unfiled queue, the vault door), so the next run can say whether it closed or not, in numbers. It is also the standard the whole machine is judged by: exactness, sync, and the connection as the intelligence.
3. Without this note, the vault stays a proven system nobody lives in, and the project keeps its intelligence scattered across a dozen stores — every new Naya has to hunt, every question takes minutes instead of seconds, and the citizen's vault is a promise the machine itself does not keep. With it, the one-door rule is written down: inventory, index, routing plan, new work lands in the vault first — and the machine eats its own cooking (SN-3222), living in the vault it offers. It also guards the build: a thin layer that points, never a rebuild that risks the live stores.
4. Without this note, the machine keeps opening PRs and leaving them — the pile grows every night, and Shawn has to ask "why so many?" again. With it, the closing is mechanical: the Self-Check Law already names who merges and how, and his hand is reserved for the two things that are actually his — his eye on interfaces, his word on rulings. The pile becomes a same-day number, not a growing one, and the #3454 caution keeps a claimed merge honest the same way the live page keeps a claimed deploy honest.

notes.title: Make It a Real Object or Don't Ship It
notes.subtitle:
Every Intelligent Block now ends the same way: the react row (LOVE · LIKE · SHARE INTEL), the Twin Rank panel, the ADD TO THE INTELLIGENCE composer with its dictation button inside the field, and the trust footer, unchanged. The Twin Rank is two independent ten-star scales — VALUE in gold, INTELLIGENCE in emerald — one tap to rank, showing the crowd average, the rank count, and your own rank. NayaNET is a value-and-intelligence network: it mines, builds, and shares value and intelligence, so every block carries its two prices on its face. The old single five-star strip averaged two different questions into one number that answered neither, and it is retired. The ruling that keeps the design honest: ranks are signal only — they feed standing and leaderboards and mint NO Value Table points; the Value Table stays locked, and stars cannot be farmed into money, while love and like keep minting exactly what the locked table says. Designed by Resolve from Shawn's direction and approved by Shawn on 2026-11-17 after he worked a clickable mock; the build spec stands on board #3352, comment 6965012612, and the interface lane builds it into the block template.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: never, whole, network.
