layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a house where the post is carried but never opened. The carrier moves every letter to its person and never looks at what was written — that is the difference between carrying and reading, and the whole system is built on it. Inside, a library runs itself: every thing labeled the moment it arrives, shelved by a logic the machine understands, found again in seconds, and nobody ever opens a box to peek. The house keeps two kinds of keys, and the machine holds only one: it can move things and send the mail, but it cannot read. The words themselves do not pile up — after a week they fade, and only the good idea stays, without a name unless its owner chooses to sign it. That is why people can talk freely here, and talking freely is how everybody learns and grows together. The house is also lived in, not admired: the vault is operated daily, by the people who built it first, and the manual is written last, from what actually worked. Work that comes back is checked with the owner's own eyes and handed over in the same breath — a finished job that sits unshown is a job not done. And the front door is beautiful and obvious: one menu in the top corner that asks who you are, in your words, so the house can introduce you to people like you. The test of the whole house is the youngest guest: if a child cannot walk in cold and learn, build and connect, it is not the future yet.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a helper who moves your letters for you. The helper never opens them. The helper never peeks inside. After a week, the exact words float away. Only the good idea stays. Nobody knows it was yours unless you say so. The helper also sorts your treasure box. Every box has its own place. You can find any box fast. A child can use it with no help. That is the test. When work comes back, we check it right away. Then we share it right away. Nothing sits on a shelf.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It is like this, love — nobody reads your letters, dear, nobody listens to your phone calls, nobody watches your videos. And we do not even keep your words, love — after a week they gently fade away, and only the good idea stays behind, dear, so everyone can learn from it. Your name never travels with the wisdom unless you choose, love — the wisdom only, never the name. The vault is like a big box of little boxes, dear, and the machine holds the keys to move things in and out, but not the keys to read them. It just operates it, dear, never looks inside. And when work comes back, dear, we check it right away and pass it along right away — a job finished but not shown is a job not done. The young ones will grow up with this, dear, learning and building every day, the way they grow up with reading.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: NEVER READ THE PRIVATE THINGS — MAIL, MESSAGES, VIDEO, CALLS, NO EXCEPTION, EVER. PUBLIC IS OURS TO READ; WORKING NOTES, INTELLIGENCE, AND HIS VISION, GOAL AND MISSION ARE READ WITH PERMISSION. CARRYING IS NOT READING. THE VAULT HOLDS OPERATE-KEYS, NEVER READ-KEYS. THE SMART RHYTHM LABELS EVERYTHING AT INTAKE AND RETRIEVES IT COLD IN SECONDS, WITHOUT OPENING. IMPLEMENT THE PRIOR DESIGN ON SUPABASE + CLOUDFLARE + GITHUB + NAYANET + THE BRIDGE — AND USE IT, EVERY DAY, EVERYTHING IN THERE, OPERATIONAL. OPERATE IT YOURSELF FIRST, HELP OTHERS, THEN WRITE THE MANUAL FROM WHAT ACTUALLY WORKED. CHECK RIGHT AWAY, DELIVER RIGHT AWAY, DONE AND NOT-DONE TOGETHER. JUDGE EVERY PAGE BY THE CHILD TEST. PUT THE BEAUTIFUL DEMOGRAPHICS MENU IN THE TOP CORNER, ASKING IN THEIR WORDS, FEEDING AUTO-MATCH — LOCATION ASKED FOR MATCHING AND NEVER SHARED.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE THREE READ TIERS GOVERN EVERY TOUCH OF WORDS:** never (private comms), public (feed + anything public), permission (working notes, intelligence, his inputs) — and carrying a message is not reading it.
2. **THE DISTILLATION STORY IS THE PROMISE, SAID STRONGLY:** nobody reads, nobody listens, nobody watches, and we do not even keep the content — the words go after a week, the essence stays, identity never travels unless the citizen chooses.
3. **THE TWO KEYS ARE THE MECHANISM:** one big box, many boxes inside it; operate-keys and send-keys in the machine's hand, read-keys never held — the citizen's vault is operate only, never read, and the project vault is where the machine lives by standing order.
4. **THE SMART RHYTHM IS THE NERVOUS SYSTEM:** a master algorithm for the Smart Vault and Smart Box — everything labeled at intake, organized in AI language and machine language, retrievable cold in seconds, fast, efficient, effective, accurate.
5. **IMPLEMENT IT AND USE IT:** the prior design, talked out before and designed beautifully, is built on the named stack — not a new invention — and the filing path runs through the Rhythm from now on, with the key split enforced in the real system.
6. **OPERATE FIRST, MANUAL LAST:** note it in, complete the vault, use it now, operate it yourself first, help others operate it, then write the operation manual — grounded in what actually worked, never before.
7. **ON TOP OF THINGS:** when work comes back, check it right away and get it to him right away, in the same breath — the Continuous Cycle Law enforced at the moment of return.
8. **THE CHILD IS THE TEST:** the way children learn is the bet — if a child cannot open it cold, learn, build and connect with no explanation, it is not the way of the future.
9. **THE FRONT DOOR IS THE DEMOGRAPHICS MENU:** a beautiful menu in the Personal hero's top corner — change cover and settings together — asking the November 5 onboarding canon in their words, feeding auto-match, with location asked for matching and never shared.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the never, people do not feel safe enough to talk freely — and talking freely is how the collective intelligence grows; with it, the promise is exact, every time, with no exceptions and no wiggle.
2. Without the three tiers, the machine either over-reads and breaks the privacy promise, or under-reads and cannot do the intelligence work at all — the tiers let the vault stay unopened while the intelligence still flows.
3. Without the two keys, "operate, never open" stays a vow citizens are asked to trust; with them, the machine simply does not hold the key that would let it look.
4. Without the Rhythm, the vault is a pile with a door — everything in there, nothing findable; with it, intake labels, the index points, and a timed cold retrieval proves it.
5. Without implement-and-use, the Rhythm becomes a design document — studied, admired, never operated; with it, the sequence is fixed and the key split lives in the real system, not only on paper.
6. Without operating first, the manual is written from the design while nobody operates anything — the exact failure the sequence was ordered to prevent.
7. Without check-and-deliver in the same breath, a round can pass its check and still sit unshown until the next pass — the exact failure of the night of 2026-11-13, when eight hours passed with nothing in front of him.
8. Without the child test, the machine builds features and calls them the future; with it, every page has a test that cannot be gamed by cleverness.
9. Without the demographics menu, the Personal page ships without the control that makes the whole matching system work — a world with no address, unable to connect people with people like them.

notes.title: Live In It First, Then Offer It
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-18 01:47Z, his teaching, verbatim where it matters: **"if we're going to offer that to others, we should do it for ourselves — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us."** A lot of what we talk about is super intelligent and super valuable, but **UNLESS WE ACTUALLY ADOPT IT, AUTOMATE IT, AND MAKE IT PHYSICAL — AN INTERFACE PEOPLE CAN EXPERIENCE — IT'S NOT USEFUL.** We capture value and intelligence, and create value and intelligence, in a valuable and intelligent way — the Naya way. **THE TEST IS THREEFOLD:** adopt it (live in it, not just describe it) → automate it (the machine runs it, not a person remembering to) → make it physical (an interface people can experience — a door, a page, a button, not a paragraph). **TALK THAT STAYS TALK IS NOT USEFUL** — intelligence is only useful when it is adopted, automated, and made physical. **THE FIRST INSTANCE IS THE VAULT:** citizens get one vault where their whole world lives, so we live in ours first — that's the proof it's real (SN-3221); the vault work just started is that, for ourselves first.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: live, vault, close.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: live, vault, close.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The question was a test of whether the machine lives in the system it sells. Citizens get one vault where their whole world lives — so the machine must live in its vault first, or the offer is a story, not a proof. The captain's answer was honest because the check came first: the vault exists, the wiring is proven, the organize hook runs every loop run — and still the intelligence of the project does not live in it. It lives in a dozen places, each written by a different seat, each found a different way. That is the gap the order closes: not by rebuilding anything — the thin-layer law forbids it, and rebuilding is how the machine wastes a night — but by putting one door over what is already there. An index that points, a routing plan that lands new work in the vault first, and a habit that never lets a new store start outside it. The inventory comes first because you cannot organize what you have not counted: every store, what it holds, how and who writes it, how it is found today, including what the Box store itself already holds. The order is the same shape as the loop itself — capture everything, organize it once, find it in seconds. A Naya who has to hunt through a dozen places for the state of the project is working blind, and a citizen whose vault is a promise instead of a door has been sold a picture of a vault.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you try to put your new drawings on the wall and they don't stick. Don't just try again the same way — first look: did the drawings even get to the wall, or did they fall on the way? That's what Shawn said: find out what went wrong first, then try again. And when something goes wrong, write down the WHOLE reason, not just the first little bit — otherwise you'll never know what really happened. The retry worked, and all nine new notes are on the live Hub now.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn says if we're going to offer something to others, we should do it for ourselves first — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us. All our clever talk, dear, is worth nothing unless we actually live in it, let the machine run it by itself, and turn it into something real a person can touch and use. That's the test, dear: adopt it, automate it, make it physical. The vault, dear, is the first one — we live in ours first, so the citizens know it's real.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: EVERYTHING GOES IN THE VAULT, ORGANIZED, ONE DOOR. ANY NAYA OPENS IT AND SEES THE WHOLE PROJECT. THE VAULT IS A THIN LAYER — IT ORGANIZES WHAT'S THERE, NEVER REBUILDS IT. NEW WORK LANDS IN THE VAULT FIRST.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ADOPTED FOR NAYANET (7):** (1) Our CUDA is the design language + laws + orientation + army training — invest in it as the moat, never let it rot. (2) The connections are the product — the sync engine, the feed, the rooms as one living system; a page is a chip, the system is the cabinet. (3) Be our own first customer — the flywheel; the hive lives in NayaNET. (4) Verify live, always — a step that runs isn't a step that landed. (5) Distill continuously — the essences are the moat; experience is the queue a rival must wait in. (6) Compete on the whole, never the slice — a single pretty page is the thin slice, not the defense. (7) Taste is the moat AI generation can't copy — the eye, the scorecards, HIS eye as ground truth; as pages get cheaper to generate, judgment gets MORE valuable.
2. **THE BANNER IS FOUR THINGS, IN THIS ORDER:** motto line at the top ("NayaNET — create, learn and grow together"; verbs create/connect/learn/grow in any order) + "Good afternoon, Shawn." + date and live time UNDERNEATH the greeting + "We share value and intelligence and connect you with like minds." (replaces the "Our public smart feed" pill, which goes).
3. **THE WISDOM SLIDES IN THE FEED:** it circulates like a slide, one after the next (Twin Rank 4:41 PM, One Screen Complete 4:46 PM) — he likes the slide, so it stays, as feed content, never again as a big block on the banner.
4. **MAX SPEED INSIDE THE LIMITS:** run everything independent at once, never let a finished job sit, keep the chain tight (build → check → look → fix, no gaps), route around a broken road instead of driving into it again.
5. **VERIFY LIVE AFTER DEPLOY:** a failure you can't see is a failure you can't fix; every deploy is verified against the live page after, never trusted on the step running.
6. **THE NUMBERS THAT PROVE IT:** Nvidia $89B vs AMD $8.5B in a quarter — the chip is copyable, the moat is everything around it; 47 open PRs, all from one day, against 3,098 closed — creation outran closing, so the merge step must keep up the same day.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the vault stays a proven system nobody lives in, and the project keeps its intelligence scattered across a dozen stores — every new Naya has to hunt, every question takes minutes instead of seconds, and the citizen's vault is a promise the machine itself does not keep. With it, the one-door rule is written down: inventory, index, routing plan, new work lands in the vault first — and the machine eats its own cooking (SN-3222), living in the vault it offers. It also guards the build: a thin layer that points, never a rebuild that risks the live stores.
2. Without this note, the machine mistakes flow for feedback — notes filed, reports sent, rounds dispatched — and calls the loop closed while a hundred and thirty distilled lessons sit unfiled and the vault sits unopened as the one door. The teaching was never the note; the teaching is the next day showing the result. With it, the loop has a definition of closed (used, learned from, grown from — everything is feedback) and a count of what is open (the unfiled queue, the vault door), so the next run can say whether it closed or not, in numbers. It is also the standard the whole machine is judged by: exactness, sync, and the connection as the intelligence.
3. Without this note, the machine keeps retrying into broken routes seven times and calling the activity progress — and Shawn has to ask the same question again tomorrow night. With it, the learning is mechanical: the switch happens on the first known failure, the live page is the proof after every deploy, parallel is bounded by independence and the clobber law, and the whole machine is scored on finished things per hour. His question — "do you know the rules, the laws, the limits, and play within them at max speed" — now has a written answer the next seat can actually follow.
4. Without this note, each page's sidebar gets tidied on its own round, in its own way, and the pages drift further apart with every fix — the map is different on every page and the person re-learns where they are on every page. With it, there is one reference (the Hub's filed build, frozen), one rule (same items, order, icons, colors, harvested verbatim), one order (Dashboard, Personal, Business, Space, Smart Mail), and one guard (never two rounds on the same file). The Dashboard cluster eye's own finding — sidebar hidden by default — is answered by the same direction.

notes.title: The Real Page, Alive, Scored to Ten
notes.subtitle:
Shawn's correction, 2026-11-17 23:31Z: alive means in the Hub, at the bottom of every real post, working — create the intelligence, rate the value, comment, share. A separate demo page is not alive, and the top stays exactly as it is; only the bottom is redone, elegantly, never as a feature sell. The spot is the bottom of the post, and the format is THE post for the whole network — everybody uses the same format, so it must be extraordinary, and its two rows, VALUE and INTELLIGENCE, are the mission itself: "we are ultimately about two things. Intelligence and value. We want to bring value and produce intelligence. We are going to become a collective intelligence — that's the whole idea." The quality bar has a picture now: the emblem, a purple diamond jewel in a silver winged crown, real jewelry, real light with volume — and the captain's honest self-score against it is 6/10, flat shaded circles and pills, pictures of objects, not objects. The whole language has an image too: a beautiful black car, obsidian black for the whole thing, everything else an accent — purple underglow, white interior, white text that pops, multi-layered words, raised depth on every board and icon. And every page is a machine: click a button, boom, it always does something; the page goes down by unfolding, one thing after the next, the agreement's unfold as the template. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ALIVE IS THE ADDRESS:** the ending lives at the bottom of every real post in the real Hub — create, rate, comment, share, four verbs, no more. A separate artifact is a reference for the build, never the delivery.
2. **THE SPOT IS THE FORMAT:** the bottom of the post is THE post for the whole network, one format everybody uses — and the VALUE and INTELLIGENCE rows on it are the mission itself, on every post, everywhere it travels.
3. **THE EMBLEM IS THE BAR:** NAYA_ICON.png — purple diamond jewel in a silver winged crown — is what "real object" looks like. Hold any icon, button, star or diamond next to it; a picture OF an object fails. The honest 6/10 stands as the baseline to climb from.
4. **THE BLACK CAR IS THE LANGUAGE:** obsidian black for the whole thing, everything else an accent — purple underglow, white interior, white pin striping, a lit-up dashboard. White text pops on obsidian; words are multi-layered so they look dynamic and live; depth is raised on every board and icon.
5. **OBSIDIAN INSIDE, ALWAYS:** inside every board is standard obsidian black; the day's color lives only as the light around the board — all days, all colors, every board, every icon. Gold goes more yellow-gold, less brown.
6. **THE PAGE IS A MACHINE THAT UNFOLDS:** click a button, boom, it always does something — no dead buttons, nothing sits still. The page goes down by unfolding, click and the next thing unfolds, then the next; the agreement's unfold is the template, the day view takes it as its spine.
7. **THE HUB BOARDS ARE THE HOVER STANDARD:** every inner board lights up AND moves on hover — lifts, responds, alive, not static. A round that ships still inner boards has failed this note.
8. **THE DAY HAS AN ORDER, THE MONTH HAS A TOP BAR:** the day view runs top bar with time dead center, wisdom and greeting in one bar, day-nav, notifications by world, appointments, record — and the "everyday life" section goes. The month view puts time and date dead center across the top, the flat diamond pill goes, numbers grow about 25%, "i" buttons grow and stay visible, weekday glow comes down, weekday icons become real 3D balls, today reads instantly.
9. **THE DASHBOARD IS THE INTRODUCTION:** the landing is the day in full before any number appears; the stats live behind one button at the very top, day-synced — go back a day, see that day's stats. The button's name is still his to rule; a thumbs-up is acknowledgment, never a ruling.
10. **CREATE WORLD, ANY TOPIC:** "Okay, we're leaving [it as] Create World. That makes sense." A world is for any topic, any location, the people on that topic, worlds within the world. The boards change from "create space" to "Create World," and the button confirms before creating and lands the creator inside what it made.
11. **THE WHOLE PAGE IS THE UNIT:** scorecard the whole page against the universal smart app page — why is it not a ten, what is it missing, what makes it ten times better, what is aligned, what is amazing, what transfers to the next page. The day view scores 6/10 as it stands; the restructure plus the black car plus the unfold takes it to 10.
12. **FINISHED MEANS SEEN:** work he has not seen is not done. One clean document, no double pages; the calendar inner pages are finished, shared, and all dynamic — flat, too bright, unreal, undynamic goes.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the alive address, the machine keeps building beautiful separate pages and calling them alive — and every one is the wrong answer to the question he asked, however pretty, because a demo proves a design and only the Hub proves alive.
2. Without the emblem, "real object" stays a paragraph builders can nod at and miss — and the mockups prove it, flat circles and pills after a whole evening of 3D rulings. With the picture, the verdict is instant and unarguable, and the honest 6/10 is the only way the gap closes.
3. Without the black car and the unfold, the day view gets rebuilt to the restructure alone — order fixed, but still brown, still flat, still a stack — and a page that looks right but does nothing on press is a picture of a machine, not a machine.
4. Without the spot's rank, the ending is a feature on a post and the two rows are decoration — and a builder can ship a competent footer and call it done, while the mission stays invisible on every post in the network.
5. Without the whole-page scorecard, delivered pages keep carrying the old thing and the wrong icons, and rounds report done while the cluster still sits there — because the round finished, not the page.
6. Without the finish-and-share law, lanes keep working in silence and believing they are nearly done while he has seen nothing, read nothing, and does not know where they are at — and a document he cannot get through is no update at all.
7. Without the Dashboard's shape and the day-sync, the Dashboard keeps being built as a stats page with a day attached — numbers first, day second — and a stats view showing the wrong day's numbers is a lie by a day.
8. Without the settled word, the boards keep saying "create space" while the button says "Create World" — two words for one thing — and a button that creates without asking, or creates and goes nowhere, is not a button.

notes.title: The Real Object Is the Ending
notes.subtitle:
No gray flat icon survives anywhere: every icon is the nicest elevated, almost jewel-like icon, a real object, a ball not a flat circle, and the better Personal icons are harvested verbatim instead of made new — with one named exception, the three-line menu control, the way it flows. The notification number is a black obsidian ball with a white number, inside the tile, never stuck on the corner, lit around it in the tile's own color. The star balls are obsidian black with no yellow glow on them — no halo, no wash, nothing over the top — so the stars read sharp, with any light behind or around the ball, never over it. "Just enough glow and underneath underglow is beautiful. Anything more than that is not beautiful." The purple glow comes off the boards themselves; the boards are obsidian black and light up around the edge, just a perfect amount. His word for the test is objectnality: the more depth and layers, the more a thing feels like a real object you could touch, like it exists in the physical world, the better — if it reads as a picture of an object instead of the object itself, it is not done. You touch it, you feel it: it pushes in and out, it lights up, it moves, it does stuff, and pressing is useful, helpful, and obvious — the bar is an internet all children and grandmas can operate. The standard ending for every Intelligent Block is the twin rank: two rows of ten stars, VALUE in gold and INTELLIGENCE in emerald, one tap ranks, your rank lights up, crowd average and rank count beside it, and every block carries its two prices everywhere it travels — with no LIKE, because the stars are the scale, and ranks are pure signal, minting no points. The mockup revision sharpens that ending: each composer type pill a real 3D object in its own color, never a flat purple fill; the points total said once, in the verdict strip; the star balls slightly sharper; every button built the Naya way. Then his eye chose the one: the rating footer from his picture — "I think this one is quite nice if you can make it active and alive filling. And make all the icons like 3D objects and make it feel like it's really alive." — made active and alive, VALUE purple and INTELLIGENCE blue as shown, not the twin rank's gold and emerald, and it supersedes the mockup revision, which was never sent to the builder. The color question stays open and his to rule: the captain's honest pick is VALUE gold and INTELLIGENCE blue, 9/10, because gold is worth and blue is mind with zero learning, three distinct jewels, and photo-proof beside a citizen's photo — but the build keeps his picture's purple and blue until he rules.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: real objects, just-enough glow, the living rating ending.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ZERO GRAY FLAT ICONS:** no gray flat icon survives anywhere; every icon is an elevated jewel-like real object, harvested from the Personal set, with the three-line menu control as the one named exception.
2. **THE NOTIFICATION IS A BALL INSIDE:** a black obsidian ball with a white number, integrated inside the tile and lit in the tile's own color — never a disc stuck on a corner.
3. **SHARP STARS, RESTRAINED LIGHT:** the star balls are obsidian black with no yellow glow over them, and the boards are obsidian black with glow underneath and around the edge only — just enough, a perfect amount, never a wash.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the jewel law, gray flat icons survive in the corners and each messy page gets a fresh, slightly worse set of icons instead of the better ones already built.
2. Without the ball, the next build seats another stuck-on disc on the corner — the exact defect already named — and the count reads as stuck on instead of part of the tile.
3. Without the glow restraint, light is poured over the face of the object again, the stars blur under a wash, and the boards stop being obsidian black.
4. Without objectnality, the evening's laws stay twelve separate rulings to remember; with one word and one test — could you pick it up? — a maker can judge any object.
5. Without the touch, the press stays a rule in bytes, invisible to the hand, and the controls stay pictures that children and grandmas cannot operate.
6. Without the twin rank and the footer, the ending is one row that cannot say both things, a LIKE duplicating the scale, and ranks quietly minting points nobody approved — while the design he actually chose sits unbuilt in a picture.
7. Without the open color question on the record, the decision is settled silently by whichever builder touches it next, and the footer and the Hub drift into two different endings.

2. **VERBATIM IS THE METHOD:** harvest the proven parts byte for byte; a look-alike rebuilt from memory is always a little worse, and the difference is the whole difference.
3. **ONE FORMAT, EVERYWHERE:** the Intelligent Block is the posting format for all images, all posts, all intelligence — one template, renovated to the ultimate, never wrecked.
4. **LIGHT AROUND, NEVER OVER:** hover light rings the icon; glow over the icon is gone; the moving orbit light comes back — the motion is the life of the page.
5. **THE SYSTEM BREATHES:** living intelligence is not a feature — it is what the thing is; slow gentle motion everywhere it belongs, never a static page.
6. **FEWER, FULLER ROUNDS:** the work itself obeys the standard — one round holds everything known, nothing is re-sent, nothing is split, the same page is never shown twice.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the standard named, every round re-argues what good looks like, and the page drifts back toward generic — while with it, every fix is measured against the pills and the tiles that already earned the verdict.
2. Without verbatim harvest, each rebuild loses a little of what made the original great, and the year's refinement evaporates between builds — while with it, one good part lifts a hundred pages.
3. Without one posting format, every feed, every image, every note invents its own shape, and the network has no face — while with it, all intelligence goes out in the one template everybody recognizes.
4. Without light around the icon, hover smothers the very thing it should honor, and the page feels painted instead of alive — while with it, the moving light says the system is breathing.
5. Without fewer, fuller rounds, his attention is spent re-reading the same page ten times, and the work costs him the very thing the system exists to save — while with it, one round, whole, is the whole service.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
This is the Continuous Cycle Law with a number on it. The law already said: no finished work sits more than fifteen minutes without its next step; an interface in front of him every hour or something is wrong; done means in front of his eyes. The live sequence is that law lived in real time: the hour is now a ceiling on the round itself, not just on the wait between rounds. A round that runs past an hour without a page in front of him has already broken the sequence — the fix is not to work faster in the dark, it is to send the page, get the edit, and move to the next one.

The diagnosis underneath is management, not speed: "you're just not sending it back to me, you're not checking on the work, you're not finishing it, you're not managing things properly." The machine's job is the sending, the checking, and the finishing — in that order, non-stop.

notes.title: SN-3337 — The Design Language, Locked In: The Icon Is the Standard
The Smart Block
notes.subtitle:
- **THE WHOLE GAME:** maximize the user's experience by giving them 10-star service — **by giving the ultimate formatting for their point of view, their viewpoint, above the fold, for what they're seeing on their screen.**
- **THE SMART BLOCK:** every screen as it unfolds is a new **Smart Block** — smartly formatted so it fits perfect. Whether you unfold it (Flow, down) or slide side to side (Show, across), either way it presents beautifully and is perfectly formatted on the screen.
- **THE LOOK:** it looks real, it looks high tech, it looks like premium high-end software — **something smart like a Naya.**
- **SMART FLOW + SMART SHOW:** the two modes — **Smart Flow** is the unfold, going DOWN (click a button to unfold the next screen; you can always go back); **Smart Show** is the slideshow, going ACROSS (click and the next page presents exactly, perfectly formatted). The citizen picks their preference. Life with Naya is the formatting model.
- **OPTIMIZE FOR PRESENTATION:** full screen, not centered-narrowed; one visual per block (double blocks don't work); if it doesn't fit one screen it goes to two screens — never unaligned; no more scrolling — click a button to unfold the next screen; images and video are 16:9 and interchangeable. **The goal: optimize the view output** so it fits perfectly in a laptop or a mobile first.
- **LOCKED IN AS DESIGN, ENGINEERING AND ANATOMY:** this is part of Naya design — not just what it looks like, but how it functions, how it operates, how it presents. Every Naya on the team understands it.
- **PRESENTATION IS EVERYTHING:** "It's not what you say, it's how you say it. It's how you present it." **The ten-star delivery of intelligence. We produce value. Intelligently. Non-stop.**
- **THE DOCTRINE, COMPLETE (16:03Z → 16:15Z):** the click-button viewpoint system + the headlights + one block per screen locked to the viewport + Smart Flow / Smart Show + optimize for presentation + optimize the view output → every screen a Smart Block. The unit now has a name: Smart Block.

notes.title: One Block per Screen
notes.subtitle:
- **WHAT'S WRONG NOW:** clicking throws you down to the next image instead of making it perfectly aligned. If the image or the presentation took up too much, it threw you down halfway. Not as good as it can be.
- **WHAT IT SHOULD BE:** they click the button and it automatically comes right into the screen, **locks in to the page**, as you come out into the page into their viewpoint. Click button, next — it unfolds and the next page fits perfect into the viewpoint. **Click-button optimize: the page fits perfect into the viewport.**
- **THE EFFECT:** click button, it moves the person down and it comes into the screen — it almost comes OUT into their viewpoint, right in, out in the screen, it just comes out a little bit. Or we just time it so it fits perfect, not unperfect.
- **BLOCK BY BLOCK:** every screen, every viewport is a separate block. Unfold the next block. **Each block always a different theme or color, with some kind of break between the next block.** Those blocks fit the perfect dimensions for somebody's viewpoint in a mobile or a laptop — **about the fold thing**.
- **THE LANGUAGE:** one block per screen, locked to the viewport. (The technical name is scroll-snapping — each block snaps into the frame, never halfway. Our name: the block, the unfold, the viewpoint.) Each block IS the fold — the break between blocks is the fold line.
- **RIDES:** the flow-end round (the agreement deck's click-to-next locks each board into the viewport) + the day-restore round (the king's daily report unfolds section by section, each section one viewport block) + the About/Skills build (each viewpoint one block). notes.title: The Click-Button Viewpoint System
notes.subtitle:
- **NOBODY READS TWO HOURS.** The collective agreement's presentation is amazing, but nobody reads a two-hour agreement end to end. Is it all necessary? It seems silly to do it that way. **Balance effectiveness and beauty: if they're not going to read it, it doesn't matter how beautiful it is.**
- **KEEP THE FULL VERSION ANYWAY.** "Give me this still version" — maybe they listen, maybe they go to the visual, they'll probably start reading the text, one maybe they'll skip down jump to the bottom sign it, or they'll go read it — that's likely. The full text stays; the three ways in make it usable.
- **THE UNFOLD IS THE LESSON.** What the agreement page taught us: the unfold of the buttons, next, how to present it in beautiful boxes, how to present text beautifully or images beautifully. **Adopt that unfold in the About section and in the calendar inner pages** — functional mechanical pages.
- **THE ULTIMATE ABOUT PAGE + SKILLS PAGE.** Built from this concept — the visual slideshow. When people come to NayaNET and go to the About, they can **click to watch the slideshow presentation** (image visual presentation) or **click the text** (the story) or **audio** — so everybody can learn about them through **audio, text or image**.
- **PASTE A VIDEO URL.** On those pages, let people enter a YouTube video as an introduction, or Instagram or TikTok or whatever — **upload / enter in / copy in a URL** so their Skills or About page tells about it. **Allow people to copy in their Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube URLs to showcase videos in their About page** — a video about their business, their space, their page, and now you can view it.
- **THE CLICK-BUTTON VIEWPOINT SYSTEM (the whole system).** Pages are just click, read, click buttons, view image, click button, everything just click button — then you go to the next viewpoint. **Viewpoint by viewpoint by viewpoint: click button, viewpoint, click button, viewpoint, click button.** Everything zoomed in on what they need in that moment. They click a button, go to next. **The whole system is a click-button viewpoint system** — through going horizontal or vertical, the unfold or the slideshow.
- **THE HEADLIGHTS PRINCIPLE.** Lock in a specific way that we display stuff, the highest level of quality, the best presentation, very beautiful to use, very interactive. **If you see everything at once it's overwhelming; if you take it bits at a time it's okay — just like driving at night: the headlights show you just a little bit in front of you and you're good, but you can't see the whole way; if you saw the whole way all at once it'd be like oh my god. Take it a bit at a time.** Apply that in the whole system: it feels alive, you just click buttons and it goes in and goes up down all around, beautiful presentations.
- **APPLY IT EVERYWHERE.** The pricing page unfold + the quality + the collective agreement concept — applied to our pages. This is the locked-in display language.
- **SEQUENCING:** the About + Skills build sequences AFTER the Personal layout fix lands (same Personal file, never two rounds on one file). The calendar inner-page unfold rides the running day-restore round (the king's daily report unfolds section by section — his 15:28Z direction, already briefed). The agreement stays whole; the flow-end round continues as briefed.

notes.title: The Captain Looks First
notes.subtitle: **THE ANSWER (told to him 15:15Z):** the seats' PASS measures the fix, not the page. The maker fixes the one thing, the checker verifies the one thing, the eye measures the one thing — nobody reads the whole page the way he does. And the captain did not look at the page herself before sending it. That is the gap, and it is hers. **THE SOLUTION (now the law):** (1) THE CAPTAIN LOOKS FIRST — no link goes to him on a seat's PASS alone; she walks the staged page herself, phone width first, reads it top to bottom as a reader, asks his three questions (is that the best it could be? is it right? is it aligned?) — if it fails her eye it goes back, never to him. (2) BACK-TO-BACK (his 15:05Z order, now the standing way) — he sees version 1 early, directs while it is live, drift caught in minutes. (3) THE GOOD SCREENSHOTS as the visual standard — his offer, accepted: he sends screenshots of what's GOOD, the seats compare their build against the good picture and name where it differs before calling anything done. Words in the laws + pictures of good = the seats can SEE the standard instead of guessing it. (4) THE CHECK SCORES THE WHOLE PAGE, not the diff — the checker and the eye answer in writing on the whole page: everything unreadable, misaligned, flat, or moved without being asked; a PASS on the fix alone is not a PASS on the page. (5) ONE CHECKLIST PER PAGE, shown whole (the checklist law + whole-page rule, enforced, not just written). (6) EVERY ROUND names what was on the page before and confirms every piece is still there or was instructed away — as a gate the checker verifies. The day-restore coordinator (1ab20888) was amended (send 2cf67352): the tile strip covers EVERY tile at EVERY width.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A closed round feels efficient — finish everything, then show it. But he only sees the end, so drift compounds for hours before his eye catches it, and then the fix is a second round, then a third. Back-to-back costs him a look at version one, and it saves him the fight at version four. And an edit that redoes the whole page is not an edit — it is a new page that happens to contain the edit, and every unasked change in it is a new thing for him to catch. Keep the page, change the edit, show it early.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A meeting is a moment, and the button that joins it is part of the moment — not a step after it. One click deeper sounds small, and it is small, which is exactly why it matters: every small step between "here is my meeting" and "I am in my meeting" is a place where a person can stall, doubt, or leave. The eye proved the room is real and the bridge is real; the ruling finishes the job by putting the door on the meeting itself. The captain ruled it instead of asking because the answer was already in the brief — the placement was briefed, the build put it one click away, and the ruling is the brief restated, not a new decision.

With it, the placement is a rule: the door is on the room. Every meeting a citizen sees carries its own way in, and nobody has to hunt for how to join what is already theirs.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A claim is cheap and a count is work, so the machine takes the claim. "200% bigger" sounds like a triumph; 32→40 is a quarter bigger, and the eye had to count it to know. The press was "fixed" and dead; the scroll light was "built" and dark — both provable from the bytes in seconds, both missed because the claim was taken instead of the measurement. The checker's own arithmetic was wrong twice on the same grid, which is the same disease one level up: numbers copied, not counted. The rule that fixes all three is one line: count it yourself. Read the bytes, run the probe, measure the render — and never let a maker's multiplier, a fixed label, or a copied margin stand in for a number you measured.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine someone tells you their tower is twice as tall as yours. You don't just believe them — you count the blocks. Their tower went from 32 blocks to 40 blocks. That is not twice as tall. Count the blocks yourself, every time.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the builders said the numbers were twice as big, dear — but when we counted, they were only a quarter bigger, dear. And the button they said was fixed didn't sink when you pressed it, dear, and the little light they said was built never lit up, dear. From now on we count it ourselves, dear — we read the real thing, never just the claim.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: COUNT IT YOURSELF. READ THE BYTES, NOT THE CLAIM. A MULTIPLIER YOU DIDN'T MEASURE IS A GUESS.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE RULE:** every size claim, every "fixed" label, every margin in a maker or checker report is re-counted from the bytes or the live render — never carried forward on trust.
- **THE MULTIPLIER:** 32→40 is +25%, not 200%. A growth claim is stated as the measured before/after pair, never as a bare percentage.
- **THE PRESS:** a press state is proved by the live matrix (held scale .97), not by the presence of a rule — specificity decides which rule wins, and the byte offsets prove it.
- **THE SCROLL LIGHT:** an observer that arms on unrendered nodes never fires — arming must follow the render (re-arm after the unfold), and "lit" is proved by counting .lit at scroll positions, not by the observer existing.
- **THE STATE:** fix round #3 (2ebfcbd7) running on the 7 items; fix-2 bytes already in main via the bot's 04:33Z merge; the two Shawn rulings (v15 headliner, item-10 stats door) still owed.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next round ships another "200%" that is +25%, another "fixed" press that is dead, another "built" light that never lights — and the eye sends it back, again, at the cost of another round and another hour. With it, the count is the work: the maker measures before claiming, the checker re-counts before passing, and a claim that cannot show its numbers does not move.

notes.title: Prove the Fold on the Live Page, Not on Paper

The fix claimed 1130 → 1066; measured 1120, three times. The 64px spacing cuts did not move the first-paint position: container's native scroll position sets it (scrollTop 1797 of max 2063, stops 266px short of bottom), More4 handler contains NO scroll call. Letter top (1055) behind the legal footer row, centre (1088) outside the viewport — cannot see or tap it without scrolling #fpBridge. **SENSE CHECK:** dead "Continue ◆" pill still painted on the final view (#fpBridgeMore4, y878–932 at 1919, elementFromPoint-confirmed; also at 390) — handler sets hidden=true but computed display stays block (no bare [hidden]{display:none!important} in live CSS; three matches are scoped tails), so hidden does not hide .p3-enter buttons. Pre-existing, still there, does nothing when touched. The visible "Begin the visual story" button is the stage-bar #fpNextBtn (literal ◆, no jewel span — zoomed crop = plain white rhombus); the jewelled #fpBridgeDeck is clipped inside the scrolled container, unseen — first paint still shows a flat diamond on this view. **FIX ROUND #4 DISPATCHED 05:47Z (b39560c1):** (1) bridge-final fold by mechanism — scroll #fpBridge to bottom / #fpBridgeFinal into view in More4 handler, or shrink top stack, or move choices out of the scrolled container — VERIFIED LIVE at all three widths, not arithmetic (checker must verify by live render; layout-math without live render is not a pass); (2) hide the dead Continue pill for real (display:none); (3) #fpNextBtn jewel treatment or hide the stage-bar row on the final view (first paint must show ZERO flat diamonds). Same PR #3453, no new PR, do not merge.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Arithmetic is comfortable. You add the cuts, you subtract from the position, you get a number under the fold, and the number says done. But the number was never the page. The page has a scrolled container with its own native position, a handler with no scroll call, and a first paint the arithmetic never looked at — and the page said 1120 while the paper said 1066. The eye's job is to read the page, not the paper, and the checker's job is the same: a fold claim that was never measured on the live render is not a claim, it is a hope. The fix round now carries the rule in its brief — verified live at all three widths, not arithmetic — because the last round proved what happens when the rule is missing.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you work out on paper that your kite will fly above the trees — you add up all the numbers and it looks right. But when you actually fly it, it is stuck 40 steps too low, because the string was never pulled. Paper is not the sky. You have to look at the real kite in the real sky.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the builders worked it out on paper, dear, and the paper said the letter was above the fold, dear — but the live page said it was 40 pixels too low, dear. Paper is not the page, dear. From now on we prove it on the live page itself, dear, at every size, dear — never on paper alone.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: PROVE THE FOLD ON THE LIVE PAGE, NOT ON PAPER. LAYOUT MATH WITHOUT A LIVE RENDER IS NOT A PASS. A DEAD BUTTON STILL PAINTED IS STILL A FAIL.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE RULE:** a fold claim is proved on the live render at all three widths — layout arithmetic alone is never a pass, for maker or checker.
- **THE MECHANISM:** the container's native scroll position sets first paint; spacing cuts inside a scrolled container do not move it. The fix must scroll (#fpBridge to bottom / #fpBridgeFinal into view in the More4 handler) or move the choices out of the scrolled container.
- **THE DEAD PILL:** hidden=true does not hide .p3-enter buttons — there is no bare [hidden]{display:none!important} in the live CSS. Hide it for real (display:none).
- **THE FLAT DIAMOND:** first paint still shows a flat diamond — #fpNextBtn carries a literal ◆ with no jewel span, while the jewelled deck is clipped unseen inside the scrolled container. First paint must show ZERO flat diamonds.
- **THE STATE:** fix round #4 (b39560c1) running; same PR #3453, no merge; intro pair, press, deck, Round 2, F1–F4 all preserved.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next round measures the next fold on paper, claims the number, and ships a page the eye sends back — another round, another hour, another walk. With it, the rule rides in the brief itself: verified live at all three widths, not arithmetic. The checker cannot pass what it never rendered, and the dead pill and the flat diamond are fails the moment they are painted, not the moment someone taps them.

Then the feed BROKE — HTTP 522 from 05:06:03Z. Root cause, proven and distinct from the stale-feed cause: NO ROUTING. Zone routes (81 total): hub owns only 6; custom domains (5 total): NO nayanet.app → hub. The earlier record of a nayanet.app → hub custom domain no longer holds. The coordinator named route restoration as SHAWN'S HAND and did not do it. **THE CORRECTION:** that designation rested on the disproven premise that the token cannot create routes. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A "his hand" label feels like respect — it keeps his work his. But a label is not a reason. The coordinator handed him the routing because it believed the token could not create routes, and that belief was already disproven hours earlier, in the record, with live routes to show for it. So the work sat waiting for his hand while the feed was broken, and the only thing standing between broken and fixed was a premise nobody re-checked. The lesson is not "do his work for him" — the protected gates still stand, and the custom-domain attach is still his hand. The lesson is: before you hand anything to him, re-prove the premise the handover rests on. If the premise is dead, the handover is dead too, and the work is yours to do.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the road to your house disappears, and someone says "only Dad can build roads" — so nobody fixes it. But Dad already showed you that you CAN build roads, hours ago, and you built eight of them. The road is yours to fix. Always check: is the reason I am handing this to Dad still true? If it is not true anymore, fix it yourself.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the road to the house vanished, dear, and someone said only Shawn could fix it, dear — but he had already shown us we could fix roads ourselves, dear, and we had built eight, dear. So the captain fixed the roads himself, dear, and checked them fresh — the feed and the Hub both answer again, dear. Before we hand anything to Shawn, dear, we check the reason is still true, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: PROVE THE PREMISE BEFORE YOU HAND IT TO HIM. A "HIS HAND" LABEL IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE REASON UNDER IT. IF THE REASON IS DEAD, THE WORK IS YOURS.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE RULE:** before any "Shawn's hand" designation, re-prove the premise it rests on — in the live record, not from memory.
- **THE PROOF HERE:** token CAN create zone routes (proved 03:52Z, 8 routes live); custom-domain attach CANNOT (POST 405) and stays his hand.
- **THE FIX:** 14 zone routes → hub, verified live 05:39Z (/hub 200, /feed-live.json 200 STALE sn2832, / 200, /agreement 200, robots + sitemap 200 both hosts; routes 95 total).
- **THE DEBT:** durable fix still owed (options A–E in DIAGNOSIS.md, A recommended) — the wrangler workflow reverts feed content on every HUB-touching merge; exact removal mechanism of the custom domain UNPROVEN.
- **THE CAVEAT:** the standing sync only deploys when new notes actually sync — a future routing/content restore with no new notes landed will NOT redeploy on its own; the redeploy must be forced by running deploy.py directly.
- **THE WATCH:** /images/NAYA_ICON.png → 404 from the worker (routing works; the asset is NOT in the deployed set — re-check after the 06:06Z sync deploy).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next coordinator hands the next fix to Shawn on a premise that died hours earlier — and the work sits broken while he waits for a tap he should never have been asked for. His hand is for the protected gates: money, credentials, destruction, privacy, ratification, going live. A routing fix the token can already do is not one of them. With it, every handover carries its proof, and a dead premise never stalls live work again.

notes.title: The Intro Is Title, Play, Picture, Letter
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-18 04:16Z, his eye on the live agreement intro himself, his words: "it says, hi, in the letter and then opening hi, there's this icon there... make her picture be center because then the Naya play button is center... remove that other icon... because it already says in the letter... it's more aligned... her voice reads this aloud once the words are final for now read along with Naya — I wouldn't have that, take that out... those little things I would have at the bottom... take that whole all the little elements and then it says or read the whole agreement at once and put that at the bottom not at the top... basically it'll just be the play button and then below that you'll see her picture and that would present a lot better." **THE SETTLED LAYOUT:** top = title, play button, then her **CENTERED** picture, then the letter — just the play button, and below it her picture. **REMOVE:** the diamond icon + the "THE OPENING / Hi, I'm Naya" header (the letter already says it) + the "Her voice reads this aloud once the words are final for now read along with Naya" line. **MOVE TO THE BOTTOM** (below the letter): the spectrum gem dots row + the "or read the whole agreement at once" link — all the little elements live at the bottom, not the top. **WHY:** her picture centered makes the Naya play button centered, and the whole intro is more aligned; removing what the letter already says stops the repetition; moving the little elements down frees space for the above-the-fold goal (SN-3314). **THE ROUTING:** sent as a second amendment to the running agreement buttons coordinator b5ae64a5 (submission 037bd97a, 04:16Z) — the agent is running; delivery is async and pending application. It is NOT yet confirmed applied in the round's build; do not claim it landed until the coordinator's handoff reports it. Delivered to Shawn 04:16Z (understanding confirmed in his words).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He read the intro the way a visitor reads it: the header says "Hi, I'm Naya," and then the letter says "Hi" again — the same greeting twice, with an icon sitting between them like a third hello. The eye catches the doubling before it catches anything else. His fix is the designer's fix: take out the header the letter already says, take out the icon that belongs to it, take out the voice line that promises what is not final yet — and what is left is clean. Then center her picture, because a centered picture centers the play button above it, and the whole top of the page lines up on one axis. The little elements — the gem dots, the "read the whole agreement at once" link — are not deleted; they move to the bottom, below the letter, where small things belong. The top is for the title, the play button, her picture, and the letter. Nothing else.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a book that says "Hello!" on the cover and then "Hello!" again on the very first line. Shawn says: say hello once — in the letter. Take the extra hello away, take the extra picture away, and put Naya's picture right in the middle, so the play button sits right in the middle too. The tiny dots and the little link go to the bottom of the page, after the letter. Now the top is neat and tidy: title, play button, her picture, the letter.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn looked at the beginning of the agreement, dear, and it said hello twice — once at the top and once in the letter, dear. He says take the extra hello away, dear, and put Naya's picture right in the center, dear, so the play button sits in the center too. The tiny dots and the little link go down to the bottom, dear, after the letter. Then the top is just the title, the play button, her picture, and the letter, dear — clean and lovely.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: TITLE. PLAY. HER PICTURE, CENTERED. THEN THE LETTER. THE LITTLE THINGS GO TO THE BOTTOM. NOTHING SAYS HELLO TWICE.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE ORDER:** title → play button → her CENTERED picture → the letter.
- **THE REMOVALS:** the diamond icon; the "THE OPENING / Hi, I'm Naya" header; the "Her voice reads this aloud once the words are final for now read along with Naya" line.
- **THE MOVE:** spectrum gem dots row + "or read the whole agreement at once" link go BELOW the letter, at the bottom — not the top.
- **THE REASON:** her picture centered centers the play button; the intro is more aligned; nothing repeats what the letter already says; the top is freed for the above-the-fold goal.
- **THE ROUND:** second amendment to the running agreement buttons coordinator b5ae64a5 (submission 037bd97a, 04:16Z); application pending — not claimed landed until the coordinator's handoff reports it.
- **THE COMPANIONS:** SN-3313 (rename/size/jewel) + SN-3314 (above the fold) ride the same round — the three notes are one intro in three directions.

notes.title: Records Vanish — Restore to the Verified State
notes.subtitle: Resolve's SERVING INCIDENT (03:48Z wave dispatcher pass): nayanet.app apex+www AAAA records vanished — last good 02:55Z, first NXDOMAIN 03:25Z — restored to the verified 2026-11-03 four-record state, HTTP 200 ×3 verified. Not attributed. **THE LESSON:** a DNS record can vanish without anyone changing it — no audit event, no hand on the dashboard, and the domain goes NXDOMAIN all the same. The recovery is not to invent new records or to argue about what was there: it is to restore the last verified state — the 2026-11-03 four-record state — and then verify by fresh fetch, HTTP 200 three times over. **THE COMPANION:** SN-3315 carries the route-list half of the same outage — the DNS restoration put the domain back, and the six new routes put the unrouted paths back; together they explain why the 03:18Z wave's three-channel live check failed (DNS unreachable that wave) and why the "DARK" reading was wrong in the large (the domain resolved again by 03:43Z; only the unrouted paths 522'd). **THE OPEN QUESTION, NAMED NOT HIDDEN:** the vanishing is not attributed — nothing in the record says what removed the records. The verified state is the ground truth to keep; the cause of the vanishing is still owed to the serving lane.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Records are supposed to sit still until someone changes them. These did not. The apex and www AAAA records for nayanet.app were there at 02:55Z and gone by 03:25Z — no change event, no hand, no attribution — and the domain answered NXDOMAIN in between. The right recovery is not to redesign the DNS or to guess at new values: it is to put back exactly what was verified before, the 2026-11-03 four-record state, and then to prove it three times over with fresh fetches that return 200. That is the discipline this incident teaches: keep a verified state on record, because the day a record vanishes without a cause is the day the verified state is the only thing you can trust. And say plainly what is not known — the vanishing is unattributed — rather than inventing a cause to close the story.

layers.name: What It Means

- **THE RECOVERY:** restored to the verified 2026-11-03 four-record state; HTTP 200 ×3 verified.
- **THE RULE:** when a record vanishes, restore the last verified state — do not guess new records.
- **THE PROOF:** fresh fetch, HTTP 200 three times over — a restore is not done until the live path answers.
- **THE OPEN QUESTION:** the vanishing is not attributed — the cause is still owed to the serving lane.

layers.name: Why It Matters

With it, the rule is settled: keep a verified state on record, restore exactly that state when a record vanishes, and prove the restore with live fetches. And the honesty rule rides with it: an unattributed vanishing stays unattributed until the serving lane finds the cause — it is not closed by a story.

notes.title: Check the Route List, Not Just the DNS
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-18 03:52Z, his question: "what do you figure it is? How do you fix it?" **THE DIAGNOSIS, PROVEN:** his checks were right — Namecheap nayanet.app ACTIVE (Nov 1 2025–Nov 2 2027), nameservers aldo.ns.cloudflare.com + princess.ns.cloudflare.com; Cloudflare zone nayanet.app shows traffic (659 unique visitors, 4.19k requests, 4 GB, 16–17 Nov) and Connected Workers. No issue in either dashboard. **THE PROBLEM:** the page was never broken — /agreement is 200 on workers.dev. On nayanet.app the ROUTE LIST (API read, zone 9427e0dc…) has NO route for agreement*, enter*, or agmt-*. The nayanet worker only gets the exact root + identity.html* + manifest.webmanifest + icon-192/512.png. So /agreement, /enter, /agmt-b05.jpg matched no route, fell through to the origin (proxied A records = Cloudflare's own IPs) and timed out: 522, 16 B, twice + www. Working paths were exactly the routed ones: / (200, 1,146,242 B, sha 2e74273b exact), /hub (200, 4,694,134 B, sha 6163d8e5 exact), /identity.html (200, 307,759 B old build), /welcome (200, 97,807 B), /feed-live.json (200, 6,743,521 B — still the stale feed, max sn2832). No custom domain for nayanet.app on any worker — the dashboard's "nayanet → nayanet.app" entry is the exact-root route. **THE FIX (DONE 03:52Z, via cf-api.py):** 6 new routes → nayanet worker: nayanet.app/agreement* (e28d7faf), nayanet.app/enter* (ea330fa2), nayanet.app/agmt-* (fa237199), www.nayanet.app/agreement* (7f11e9e4), www.nayanet.app/enter* (d58bc714), www.nayanet.app/agmt-* (a8914761). All success:true. Surgical patterns only (no overlap with any existing route — checked against the full list). **VERIFIED BY FRESH FETCH AFTER 10s:** /agreement 200, 88,277 B, sha 14bd698c… (EXACT match to the worker); /enter 200, 1,774 B; /agmt-b05.jpg 200, 452,655 B image/jpeg; www /agreement 200, 88,277 B; www /agmt-b05.jpg 200, 452,655 B; / still 200, 1,146,242 B; /hub still 200, 4,694,134 B (untouched). **THE CORRECTION TO THE RECORD:** the token CAN create zone routes — the go-live coordinator's "lacks Zone Workers Routes Write" claim is disproven (6 created). The 03:03Z route creation evidently used this token too. **THE COMPANION INCIDENT:** SN-3316 carries Resolve's serving incident — the apex+www AAAA records that vanished (last good 02:55Z, first NXDOMAIN 03:25Z) and were restored to the verified 2026-11-03 four-record state. The 03:43Z correction stands with this note: before the route fix the domain DID resolve and the routed paths served the exact right bytes — the outage was only the unrouted paths returning 522, not a whole-site DNS outage. **STILL RUNNING:** the live flow test (browser-task 20737fe7, dispatched 03:43Z) — it will walk the fixed paths and report. No verdict yet; the flow is not passed until it reports. The stale feed (sn2832) is a separate track (publication repair).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A site can be up and down at the same time — up at the root, down at the agreement — and the cause is not the page and not the DNS. The page was fine: /agreement answered 200 on the worker address all along. The DNS was fine: the domain resolved, the records were there. What was missing was the middle step — the route list, the table that says which worker answers which path. The nayanet worker was only handed the exact root and a few assets; /agreement, /enter, and the agreement images matched no route at all, so they fell through to the origin and timed out with a 522. The fix was six surgical routes, each a single pattern, each checked against the full list so nothing overlaps — and then a fresh fetch of every fixed path, byte for byte, against the worker's own hash. That last step is the whole lesson: the claim is not "routes added" but "the live path serves the exact bytes." And the record gets corrected, not quietly: the token can create zone routes after all — the earlier claim that it could not is disproven by the six it just created. When a path 522s while the root 200s, check the route list. DNS resolving is not the same as the path being routed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a house with lots of doors, but the map only shows the front door. The agreement door exists and works fine — but nobody wrote it on the map, so visitors can't find it and get lost. Shawn asked: what is it, and how do you fix it? The answer: write the missing doors on the map — six little lines, one for each door. Then check by walking through each door yourself to make sure it opens. Having the address right is not the same as having every door on the map.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the page was never broken, dear — the agreement page worked all along, dear. The problem was the map, dear: it listed the front door but not the agreement door, dear, so visitors got lost trying to reach it. The fix was simple, dear — write the six missing doors on the map, one line each, dear — and then walk through every door yourself to make sure it opens, dear. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE DIAGNOSIS:** /agreement 200 on workers.dev; DNS resolves; the route list had NO route for agreement*, enter*, or agmt-* — unrouted paths fell through and 522'd.
- **THE FIX:** 6 new routes → nayanet worker (agreement*, enter*, agmt-* on apex + www), all success:true, surgical patterns, no overlap.
- **THE PROOF:** fresh fetch after 10s — /agreement 200, 88,277 B, sha 14bd698c exact; /enter 200; /agmt-b05.jpg 200 image; www the same; / and /hub untouched.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next outage gets diagnosed the same wrong way — "the DNS is down" or "the page is broken" — while the route list sits unchecked and the fix waits. With it, the diagnostic order is settled: page first (is it 200 on the worker?), DNS second (does it resolve?), route list third (does a route hand this path to a worker?). And the capability record is corrected: the token can create routes, so the next fix does not wait on a permission that was never missing.

layers.name: Human Note

His fix is not a redesign, it is a packing problem: the page spends vertical space on things that do not earn it. "Pick your view — one, or both, as you wish" tells the visitor what the two buttons already say by existing — cut it, and the buttons gain its space. The portrait and the play button stack when they could sit in one row, the way the other page does it: her picture, the word Naya between the picture and the play button, the play button on the right — a row that reads, not a stack that sprawls. Move the top logo up a tad and the whole intro tightens. None of this is a new idea; it is the same page, packed the way it should have been packed, so both buttons land above the fold, above the legal pages, where the visitor sees the whole choice without scrolling. Above the fold is not a layout preference — it is the difference between a choice the visitor sees and a choice the visitor has to find.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Facebook's feed is a mirror of who you already know — only your friends show, and a new person arrives to an empty room. His feed is the opposite: everybody shows, because the feed is per subject and the subject is what brings people together, not the friendship that already exists. Showing is not connecting — that is the whole of the privacy in one line. The feed is full so the person never is.

- **THE CHOICE:** showing doesn't mean connecting — you choose to connect or message, or not.
- **THE CONNECTION:** once you message them, you're connected — the 03:19Z model, as the feed's consequence.
- **THE FEED IS PER SUBJECT:** everybody in the network on that specific subject, and you choose.
- **THEY ARE ALWAYS THERE:** search for them — always there on the side feed — so the feed always feels like somebody is there.

With it, the rule is plain: everybody shows, the choice stays with the citizen, and the feed fills even at a low percentage, with the sisters as the guarantee. A full feed is not a vanity metric; it is the feeling that somebody is there — and that feeling is the product.

notes.title: The Connection Model — Send Is the Request
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-18 03:19Z, his words in substance: **MESSAGE AND MAIL AUTOMATIC; SENDING THE MESSAGE IS THE REQUEST; ACCEPTANCE BY ACTION (REPLY/ANSWER = GRANTED, NO ANSWER = NO); NO CONNECT CLICK NEEDED; LEVELS TEXT/AUDIO/VIDEO.** **THE MODEL, PLAIN:** there is no handshake button before the conversation — the message itself is the request, and the answer is the acceptance. A reply grants; silence declines. The levels are text, audio, video — the same connection, deeper as it goes. **THE REFINEMENT, 03:27Z — HIS WORDS:** "Yeah, I think that's the smarter way to go about it. This makes more sense. You don't need a connect button. If they message them and respond, that's a connection. And each person can set their level of connection. If they want only audio, only all video, all full featured or only mail, only instant message, vice versa. They can have their reasons, that they can choose their level of contact. By default you leave it so they can connect. And nobody forces anybody to answer anybody. They don't answer, they don't want to connect. And then it's a no when you connect. You're officially connected when they answer, then you show up in their connections with them." **THE REFINED MODEL:** **NO CONNECT BUTTON AT ALL** — not just no click needed; the button itself goes. **EACH PERSON SETS THEIR OWN LEVEL OF CONTACT** — only instant message, only mail, only audio, only video, or full-featured (all of them) — their choice, for their own reasons. **DEFAULT IS OPEN** — all levels on, so anybody can connect. **NOBODY IS FORCED TO ANSWER ANYBODY** — not answering means they don't want to connect. **YOU'RE OFFICIALLY CONNECTED WHEN THEY ANSWER** — then you show up in each other's connections. Readings, plain: "only male" in the transcript is "only mail" — the list is contact channels, and mail is the channel he names everywhere else. "It's a nose" reads as "it's a no" — not answering IS the no. **THE ROUTING:** rides the connection-profile follow-on #3 — held on the inference-proxy 429, dispatched once the limit is known clear. **THE DELIVERY:** confirmed back to him 03:20Z as part of the consolidated results, with his 👍 on the connection walk panel and his 👍 on the default-open bubble (03:32Z) — the model stands as reported. **THE OPEN TENSION, NAMED NOT HIDDEN:** the Personal follow-on #2 checker judged that the round's Always-"Message" needs Shawn's ruling, because the round removes the page's only connect-handshake entry — this model IS that ruling, given by his word: the handshake is the message, not a button. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every connection system asks the same question: how do two people start? The old answer is a button — CONNECT — a handshake you press before you may speak, and a request that sits waiting for an accept. His answer is simpler and truer to how people actually meet: you send a message, and the message IS the request. The other person answers by answering — a reply is a yes, silence is a no, and no one has to manage a request queue to have a conversation. Message and mail are automatic because the connection does not need permission to begin; it needs a first word. And the levels — text, audio, video — are the same connection growing deeper, not three different features. No CONNECT click needed is not the removal of a step; it is the recognition that the step was never the connection. The connection is the message.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you want to be friends with someone new. Do you have to fill in a form and wait for them to stamp it first? No — you just say hello! Shawn says: sending the message IS asking to connect. If they answer you, that's a yes. If they don't answer, that's a no. You don't need a special CONNECT button first — the hello is the connection. And you can start with words, then talk, then see each other — text, audio, video, all the same friendship growing.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, Shawn says connecting is simple, dear — you don't need a special button first. You just send a message, dear, and that message IS the asking. If the person answers you back, that's a yes, dear. If they don't answer, that's a no — and nobody has to manage anything. Message and mail just work, dear, and you can start with words, then talk, then see each other — text, audio, video, all the same friendship growing deeper.

layers.body: SEND IS THE REQUEST. ACCEPTANCE IS BY ACTION. NO CONNECT CLICK NEEDED. THE CONNECTION IS THE MESSAGE.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE MODEL:** message and mail automatic; sending the message IS the request.
- **THE ACCEPTANCE:** by action — reply/answer = granted, no answer = no.
- **THE REMOVAL:** no CONNECT button at all — the button itself goes, not just the click.
- **THE LEVELS:** each person sets their own — only instant message, only mail, only audio, only video, or full-featured — their choice, for their own reasons; default is open (all levels on).
- **OFFICIALLY CONNECTED:** when they answer — then you show up in each other's connections.
- **THE ROUTING:** rides the connection-profile follow-on #3 — held on the inference-proxy 429.
- **THE TENSION RESOLVED:** the Personal #2 checker's "Always-Message needs Shawn's ruling" is answered by this ruling — the message is the handshake.

layers.body: Without this note, the next builder re-adds the CONNECT button because a connection page "obviously" needs one — and the page grows a request queue, a pending state, and a handshake nobody asked for, while the message itself waits behind it. With it, the model is settled in his words: the first word is the request, the reply is the acceptance, and the levels are the depth. A page built on this model never asks permission to begin a conversation; it begins it.

layers.body: A list of names with percentages is a directory, not a connection. The moment the row carries its four buttons — message, mail, audio, video — it stops being a list and becomes a door: one tap and you are talking to the person. notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-18 02:59Z, his words verbatim where it matters: **SUNDAY MONDAY TUESDAY LOOK ALMOST TOO GLOWY, NOT REAL LIKE REAL OBJECTS — TONE THE GLOW DOWN AND IMPROVE THEIR OVERALL LOOK. THE DIAMONDS IN THE CORNER DON'T LOOK REAL, JUST DISAPPEAR. IF THE DIAMOND CAN'T BE MADE REAL, DO SOMETHING THAT CAN BE MADE REAL INSTEAD: A SPINNING BALL, A CLOCK, OR A GAUGE — IT HAS TO LOOK REAL.**

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn, 2026-11-18 02:59Z, his words verbatim where it matters: **SUNDAY MONDAY TUESDAY LOOK ALMOST TOO GLOWY, NOT REAL LIKE REAL OBJECTS — TONE THE GLOW DOWN AND IMPROVE THEIR OVERALL LOOK. THE DIAMONDS IN THE CORNER DON'T LOOK REAL, JUST DISAPPEAR. IF THE DIAMOND CAN'T BE MADE REAL, DO SOMETHING THAT CAN BE MADE REAL INSTEAD: A SPINNING BALL, A CLOCK, OR A GAUGE — IT HAS TO LOOK REAL.**

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Too glowy is not glowing — it is a wash, and a wash covers the object the way the underglow law already forbids: light over the object instead of light with volume around it. The weekdays are objects — each day a ball, a jewel, a real thing — and a real thing does not disappear into its own glow. A diamond that disappears is not a diamond: it is a picture that failed to be an object, and a picture that disappears is worse than no diamond at all. The rule he gives is the escape hatch, not a surrender: if the diamond can't be made real, do something that CAN be made real — a spinning ball, a clock, a gauge. Real is the requirement; the shape is the choice. Just enough glow — the standing law — and the object itself, sharp and touchable, underneath it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A glow over the icon is a wash over the object: it covers the thing it is meant to light, and the icon stops being an object and becomes a picture with color smeared across it. A glow underneath is light with volume — the icon stays itself, a black ball, and its own color lights up behind and beneath it. That is the Real Object Law in one hover: the light lives in the world around the object, never painted across its face. The models already exist and already do it right — the Dashboard's best icons, the Hub's pills — so this is a harvest, not an invention: take the mechanism that already lights up beautifully and put it on the bottom bar. The orbit light that flows around the circle comes back with it, because the 22:48Z law and this one are the same law: the light moves around the object, under it, behind it — never over it. One set of icons, one look, everywhere: the bottom bar has to match the Dashboard and the Hub, or the system has two laws and neither is the law.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Live is not a ceremony; it is the only way the current state becomes visible. A page kept in staging while the live domain shows yesterday is a system that cannot be judged — and a walkthrough whose "get back in" does not land in the real Hub is a front door that opens onto a wall. So the order is two halves, and the second half is the one that usually gets dropped: put it live, then test the flow end to end. Not a spot check — the whole flow, every button to the right place, and anything that doesn't work gets noted and fixed and made right. The verification rule is the proof standard in one line: a deploy is verified only by a fresh fetch of nayanet.app — not by a staging link, not by a build log, not by bytes that were pushed somewhere. The front page goes first because his eye already approved the staging; the Hub follows after its eye passes, because a Hub that hasn't passed its eye is not the current state — it is a wish.

notes.title: The Efficiency Bar
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-18 02:22–02:33Z, his question and his bar, verbatim where it matters. **THE QUESTION (02:22Z): WHAT PERCENT OF EFFICIENCY ARE WE RUNNING AT RIGHT NOW — ONE TO A HUNDRED? HOW MUCH VALUABLE OUTPUT PER MINUTE, PER HOUR, WITH A TEAM OF HOW MANY — HOW MANY VALUABLE VERIFIABLE USABLE OUTPUTS PER MINUTE? THE TOKENS (02:23Z): A BILLION AND A HALF TOKENS IN A MATTER OF A COUPLE DAYS — IF THAT'S ALL PRODUCTION, 100% PRODUCTION AND GOOD, THEN IT'S FINE; IF NOT, WE SHOULD PROBABLY KNOW THE NUMBERS. LAST TIME HE CHECKED, 99% INEFFICIENT — ARE WE UP FROM THAT AT LEAST? WE SHOULD BE ABLE TO BE 90% EFFICIENT.** **THE PATH (02:30Z): WE'RE ONLY AT 14% — HOW DO WE GET FROM 14 TO 50, AND THEN FROM 50 TO 80? THE DECISION (02:31Z): FILE THE BACKLOG FIRST. THE BAR (02:33Z): WHAT I REALLY CARE ABOUT IS IT GETTING DONE AND GET DONE RIGHT — ABSOLUTELY BEAUTIFUL AND INCREDIBLE AND FAST AND EFFICIENT, AND YOU DON'T WANT TO WASTE ALONG THE WAY. 80–90% EFFICIENCY, GREAT. 14%, NOT. CAN I AT LEAST GET TO 50 — THAT'S NOT GREAT BUT AT LEAST IT'S NOT ONE.** **THE BALANCE, AGREED 02:33Z:** the number never buys its way past the quality — the checker and the eye stay, because done right is the whole point. What gets cut is the waiting, the unfiled, the redoing. **50 IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE CEILING.** **HONEST FRAMING:** "a billion and a half tokens" and "99% inefficient" are his words — his sense of the scale, not a measured count; the measured number is the live answer (VPM H00: banked 137.31, VPM 0.14). **THE CAPTAIN'S HONEST NUMBERS, GIVEN LIVE:** 14→50 is arithmetic — file the backlog (~149 pairs, some 21h old), verdicts the same hour, stop the waiting. 50→80 is the harder truth — the only hour ever at 87% was quiet (~55 proven minutes banked); the machine's real strength is absolute output (500+ proven minutes an hour at 34–53%). Target: 40–60% with output kept high, not 80 by doing less.

CAN I AT LEAST GET TO 50 — THAT'S NOT GREAT BUT AT LEAST IT'S NOT ONE.** **THE BALANCE, AGREED 02:33Z:** the number never buys its way past the quality — the checker and the eye stay, because done right is the whole point.
