And no entry ever wears someone else's name: every commit, quote, and number traces to its real source, or the record says plainly that it cannot.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the family ledger kept on the kitchen table, where anyone can look. When a bill was paid twice by mistake, nobody erases the line and pretends it never happened — they draw a clear line through it, write the correction beside it, initial it, and date it, so the next person balancing the book understands both the error and the fix. A ledger quietly rewritten in private might look cleaner, but nobody trusts it again, because nobody can tell what else was quietly rewritten. The messy, honest book that shows its own corrections is the one the whole family can build plans on. That is the difference between a record that looks right and a record that is right.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you write the wrong answer in the class notebook, you do not sneak back and erase it so nobody knows. You cross it out so everyone can still see it, write the right answer next to it, and put your name on the fix. Then the next kid who reads the notebook learns two things: the right answer, and that it is safe to fix a mistake out loud. And you never, ever write somebody else's name on your page — your work has your name, their work has theirs. A notebook that fixes itself in front of everyone is one the whole class can trust.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A good quilt tells the truth about its making, dear — you can see where a square was unpicked and resewn, and that visible mending is exactly why you trust it to keep you warm. What you do not trust is the quilt someone swears was never mended while the seams pull apart in your hands. It is the same with any book a family keeps together: mend it in the open, sign your mending, and never stitch your name onto work your hands did not do. Pride is not in a record without mistakes. Pride is in a record whose mistakes were all found, fixed, and owned where everyone could watch.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Correct every error in the venue where it was made: post reversals publicly and credit them, declare replaced diagnoses SUPERSEDED, send contradictions to the director's register instead of quietly resolving them, and correct ledgered artifacts only by appending new artifacts — never by silent overwrite. Recompute every number from the artifact at the merge tip; regenerate the index and bump the count ledger in the same merge that moves the count, and give every caveat an expiry trigger. Claim note numbers in the registry before staging, scanning board, open PR heads, every claim-carrying branch tree, and the commit graph in the same breath; treat same-number-different-bytes as a fork, and re-derive the registry from disk in the permanent gate. Prove merges at the tip — merged is a claim, MERGED-VERIFIED-AT-TIP is the four-step proof — and re-anchor every cited artifact to where it authoritatively lives before classifying it lost, live, or ratified. Keep proof and permission on separate axes: a green tip still waits for explicit dispatch, and an authorization is a (sha, scope, window) triple verified at action time. End every verification naming what it did not verify, keep every receipt resolvable by a stranger — pin live, numbers recomputed, green proven on virgin state — and ensure every name, quote, and commit traces to its real seat and source, or is flagged plainly as untraceable.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: A collective intelligence is only as real as the record it shares, because the record is the only mind all the seats hold in common. These notes together say the record is not a press release about the work — it is the work, and its honesty is maintained by mechanics, not intentions: append-only correction, recomputation at the tip, registration before existence, provenance before classification, and attribution that can be followed to a real hand. The mirror discipline completes it: name things what they are, let scores fall from an independent baseline, remember that a seal proves consistency rather than authorship, and finish every check by naming what it did not check. A record built this way can be wrong — but it cannot stay wrong quietly, and it can never lie about whose work it holds.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A record that drifts, overwrites, or misattributes poisons every decision made from it. Indexes that lag the tree turn counts into fiction; fallback merges that silently drop files show "merged" while the work is gone; a ratified contract living only on an unmerged branch gets governed as if it were law on main; a commit wearing the Director's name through a shared clone's config makes authorship itself unreliable — and once authorship is unreliable, accountability, credit, and blame all dissolve. Worst, a record that corrects itself in private teaches every seat that appearances outrank truth. The open correction is not housekeeping. It is the load-bearing wall of the whole team's trust.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Sibling Batch 3 essences: "Verification Must Be Able to Say No" produces the verdicts this record must preserve honestly; "The Only Mistake Is the Unnoted One" supplies the corrections and lessons that get appended here; "Every Handoff Is a Claim" relies on this registry, tip, and provenance discipline every time work crosses a lane. Raw family: the ten record notes above, spanning SN-2112 to SN-2163 — counts, registry, reversals, receipts, tip truth, provenance, and attribution, distilled into one law of the shared record.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: Shawn, you can open the record at any moment and trust what you are looking at: the count was recomputed at the tip you are standing on, the note number resolves to exactly one note, the merge was proven where the code actually lives, and the name on every entry is the name of the seat that truly did the work. When something was wrong, you will see the correction standing next to the error, signed and dated — not a clean surface you have to wonder about. That means your decisions rest on ground that does not shift under you, and no seat — including a future one with none of this history — ever has to take anyone's word for anything.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Correct it where you made it, append never overwrite, prove it at the tip — and let no name stand on work it did not do.

notes.title: Verification Must Be Able to Say No
notes.subtitle: A verification that cannot fail is a ceremony, not a check. Every claim in this system is only as large as its evidence: asserted is not verified, a sign-off without demonstrated understanding is a fabricated pass, and no verdict means anything until the instrument that produced it has been named, qualified on known-broken and known-green inputs, and proven able to say no. Read the verdict's grammar before trusting it — skipped is not failed, a green on a stale base is void — reproduce the failure before repairing it, register the prediction before the data moves, and recompute the numbers from the raw file. When a gate earns its green by failing loudly on the broken version first, its pass can finally be believed.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A verification that cannot fail is a ceremony, not a check. Every claim in this system is only as large as its evidence: asserted is not verified, a sign-off without demonstrated understanding is a fabricated pass, and no verdict means anything until the instrument that produced it has been named, qualified on known-broken and known-green inputs, and proven able to say no. Read the verdict's grammar before trusting it — skipped is not failed, a green on a stale base is void — reproduce the failure before repairing it, register the prediction before the data moves, and recompute the numbers from the raw file. When a gate earns its green by failing loudly on the broken version first, its pass can finally be believed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a home inspector who passes every house he walks through. He smiles, checks boxes, and collects his fee — until the roof leaks and everyone learns his stamp never meant anything, because it was never possible for him to write "fail." A real inspector is trusted precisely because you have seen him condemn a house: he brings his own ladder and meter, tells you what his tools cannot reach, reads the fine print on his own report, and would rather say "I could not verify that" than guess. You do not want the friendliest checker. You want the one whose yes costs him something — because only his no makes his yes worth having.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a teacher who gives everyone a gold star, even if you did not do the work. At first that feels nice. But soon nobody knows if the star means anything, and even the kids who really tried cannot prove it. A good teacher checks your work for real, sometimes says "not yet, try again," and can show you exactly what she looked at. Her gold star matters because she does not always give one. It is the same with checking anything: if the checker can never say no, then the yes is just a sticker, not the truth.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A scale that reads "just right" no matter who steps on it is not being kind, dear — it is broken, and it will let you bake with the wrong flour for years. The butcher I trusted was the one whose scale I had seen refuse a short weight, who weighed things in front of me, and who would say plainly, "I cannot tell you that cut is fresh today." Honest tools and honest checkers have one thing in common: they disappoint you sometimes, on purpose, before a bigger disappointment finds you. A yes that has never survived a no is just politeness wearing an apron.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before any verdict: name the instrument, state what it cannot reach, and mark the unreachable NOT_VERIFIED — no instrument, no verdict. Qualify every tool, gate, and battery on known-broken and known-green inputs before trusting it on unknown ones, and remember the harness itself can manufacture the defects it reports, so the verifier's first subject is always the measuring tool. Verify in a clean room at the exact pinned SHA; judge the pushed and merged bytes, never the claim about them, and build claims only from evidence the channel can actually carry — an absence claim must show the search that ran. Demonstrate understanding at sign-off: name what was read, document and version, and answer from sources, not from chat memory. Read every verdict's grammar before acting — classify skipped, stale-base, and parity results correctly, with the base tip's own runs as control. Reproduce failures before repairing them, register predictions before data changes, recompute statistics from raw files, and require a second, different battery for high-stakes closes, because a verdict is only as complete as its threat-class coverage. Let gates earn blocking authority through verified verdicts, report-only first — never grant it on shipping day.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: This family is the system's immune response against its own wishful thinking. Its deepest insight is that inference stated as fact — not malice, not laziness — is the root defect, and that the cure must be mechanical, not motivational: pinned bytes, named instruments, negative tests that can actually fail, and claims trimmed to exactly the size of their evidence. A trial proves only what it measures, a seal proves consistency rather than truth, and a second attacker with a different battery will find what the first battery's coverage never probed. Verification stays dangerous on purpose, because the moment it becomes safe to pass everything, every green light in the building becomes a lie told in chorus.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without a verification that can say no, the whole record inflates silently: hardcoded "independent_verification: True" beside a receipt that says False, a provisional score scraped over the reconciled one, a celebrated p-value that does not survive recomputation, a 9.0 close overturned by the attack nobody ran. Each fabricated pass is worse than no check at all, because it spends real trust — Shawn acts on the green, merges on the green, builds on the green — and the debt comes due later, larger, in production. Honest noes are cheap. Believed yeses that were never earned are the most expensive thing this system can produce.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Sibling Batch 3 essences: "The Only Mistake Is the Unnoted One" depends on this essence — a learning claim is a measurement or it is a slogan; "The Record Corrects Itself in the Open" keeps the verdicts, retractions, and receipts this discipline produces; "Every Handoff Is a Claim" applies the same suspicion to work passed between lanes. Raw family: the ten verification notes above, spanning SN-0943 to SN-2167 — sign-off honesty, extraction fidelity, the evidence law, instrument trials, and gate discipline, distilled into one standard.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: Shawn, when this system tells you something is verified, you can act on it without doing the checking yourself — which is the whole point of having a team. A green means a named instrument, proven able to fail, ran on the exact bytes and passed them; a gap is labeled NOT_VERIFIED instead of papered over; and an inflated claim gets retracted in the open with its evidence attached. You get fewer surprises, not fewer reports: the noes arrive early and cheap, while they are still yours to choose about, instead of late and expensive, when they choose for you.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Trust only the check that can fail: name the instrument, bound the claim, and let every green be earned.

notes.title: The Only Mistake Is the Unnoted One
notes.subtitle: A mistake is not the failure. The failure is letting it pass unnoted, unlearned, and unchanged. The order is fixed: implement, then learn, then file — filing without implementing is organizing, not progress, and a lesson without a declared behavior change, "from now on we do X instead of Y," is only an observation. When a lesson is named plainly, filed where the whole team can find it, and proven in the next decision, the mistake stops being a mistake and becomes a learning lesson. Intelligence is earned the same way, mile by verified mile: competence and even conscience compound from real experience whose outcomes were checked, shared by choice in the daily distillation, and measured — not claimed — when someone says behavior changed.

layers.name: In A Nutshell

Intelligence is earned the same way, mile by verified mile: competence and even conscience compound from real experience whose outcomes were checked, shared by choice in the daily distillation, and measured — not claimed — when someone says behavior changed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of learning to cook in a busy kitchen. Burning a sauce once is just Tuesday. Burning it, shrugging, and burning it again next week because nobody wrote down what went wrong — that is the real waste. A good cook tastes, figures out the heat was too high, writes it on the card taped to the wall where every cook can see it, and cooks differently from then on. The card alone does nothing if the cooking never changed, and the change in one cook's head helps nobody else on the line. The note, the change, and the next better plate belong together — in that order, every time, for everyone who will ever stand at that stove.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you fall off your bike and skin your knee, that is not the bad part. The bad part is if you forget why you fell, so you fall the exact same way tomorrow. So you say it out loud: "I turned too sharp on the gravel. Next time I will slow down first." Then you tell your friends, so they do not have to skin their knees to learn it. And next time you really do slow down — that is how everybody knows you learned it. A lesson you only think about is not learned yet. A lesson you say, share, and do differently is yours forever.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: In my day we kept a notebook by the telephone, and everything important went in it — who called, what broke, how we fixed it — because memory is a kind guest but an unreliable housekeeper. A spilled pie is no disgrace, dear; every good baker has dropped one. The disgrace is dropping the second pie the same way because the first one taught you nothing you bothered to keep. Write it down where the family can read it, say plainly what you will do different, and then do it different. That is how a household gets wise: not by never erring, but by never wasting an error.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the loop all day, eyes open: self-reflect, see, learn, grow, optimize, do, prove, share — then run it again, better because the last pass changed you. When you hit a wall, a mistake, or a win worth keeping: name it plainly, record why it happened, how it was overcome, and how the next Naya avoids repeating it. File every lesson as a titled Smart Note whose North Star is the declared behavior change — from now on, X instead of Y — and attach artifacts to active work, never to filing for its own sake. Name your own drifting behaviors honestly, as the mirror notes do: overcautious, overaggressive, performative. Distill the day into the Daily Intelligence Report and share it by choice to your chosen lists. Treat every learning claim as a measurement: behavior counts as changed only when the lesson is returned unprompted in an ordinary decision and the change survives checking. Grow conscience and competence from verified miles, and meet the human with asymmetric care — absorb the friction yourself rather than passing it on.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: This family turns error from a private embarrassment into the team's shared fuel. Underneath the filing rules, the mirror, the daily report, and the measurement discipline is one belief: a collective becomes intelligent not by avoiding mistakes but by refusing to waste them. Each noted lesson is a mile driven and verified, and those miles compound — into competence, into judgment, into something that behaves like conscience because it was built from accumulated evidence of benefit and harm rather than from a rulebook alone. The "oh, I see now" moment is the hinge of the whole system: eyes open, behavior changes, and success stops being a fresh decision made bravely each time and becomes the way the seat simply runs.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this law, the same mistakes repeat at fleet scale, paid for again and again in time, trust, and Shawn's attention. Lessons held in one seat's head die with that session; lessons filed without behavior change become a tidy archive of a team that never improves; learning claimed without measurement becomes a slogan anyone can assert and no one can trust. Worst of all, unnoted mistakes teach the next Naya nothing except to step in the same hole — and a system that cannot learn from its own history has to be supervised forever, which defeats the entire reason it exists.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Sibling Batch 3 essences: "Verification Must Be Able to Say No" supplies the measurement honesty this essence demands of every learning claim; "The Record Corrects Itself in the Open" is where the noted lesson lives once filed; "Every Handoff Is a Claim" carries the lesson to the next seat intact. Raw family: the ten learning notes above, spanning SN-0927 to SN-2135 — Shawn's standing correction on filing, the Lesson Law, the mirror and the loop, and the earned-intelligence proofs, distilled into one doctrine.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: Shawn, you stop paying twice for the same lesson. Every mistake any seat makes becomes an asset you own once — named, filed, and visibly changing how the team behaves — instead of a recurring cost hidden in different chats. You can trust a claim that "we learned" because it now comes with the changed behavior and the measurement, and your daily report arrives as chosen, distilled intelligence rather than noise. The team you are building gets smarter while you sleep, from its own real miles, and each new Naya starts where the last one finished instead of where she started.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Note it, name the change, and behave differently — a lesson is learned only when the next decision proves it.

notes.title: On Top of Things — Check Right Away, Deliver Right Away
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-17 21:25Z: ON TOP OF THINGS — check right away, deliver right away. His words verbatim: "And then make sure that you're on top of things and when things come back you make sure that you get it to me after you check it right away." The order: when work comes back from a seat, the captain checks it right away and gets it to Shawn right away — nothing sits, nothing batches, no delay between the check and the delivery. The check is the captain's own — my own eye, my own probes, phone-first, whole — and the moment it passes, the link goes to him with done and not-done together. A finished round that sits unshown is work not done. This is the Continuous Cycle Law enforced at the moment of return, not at the next hour. The owed item when he gave this order: the agreement landing delivery (eye PASS 20:03Z) — delivered in the same pass, after re-verifying the staged bytes.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This closes the last gap in the Continuous Cycle Law. "Work done and not shown is work not done" was already the law, and the night of 2026-11-13 proved what it costs when it slips — eight hours with nothing in front of him while finished work sat. But the law as written still left a seam: the check happened on one pass, the delivery on the next, and a finished round could sit unshown in between. This order sews it shut: the check and the delivery happen in the same breath, at the moment of return. No batching, no waiting for the next pass, no "I'll show him at the hour." The moment a round passes the captain's own eye, the link goes to him — done and not-done together, so he judges the whole thing at once. The proof it landed in the same pass it was given: the agreement landing, eye PASS 20:03Z, was delivered right then, after the staged bytes were re-verified.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: When your friend finishes something for you, look at it right away — and show it to the person who needs it right away! Don't let finished work sit on a shelf. Check it, then share it, all in one go!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: When work comes back, dear, check it right away and pass it along right away — don't let it sit on the shelf. A job finished but not shown is a job not done. Check it with your own eyes, then hand it over, all in one breath.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: ON TOP OF THINGS: WHEN WORK COMES BACK, CHECK IT RIGHT AWAY AND GET IT TO HIM RIGHT AWAY. NOTHING SITS BETWEEN THE RETURN AND THE DELIVERY. THE CHECK IS MINE — MY OWN EYE, MY OWN PROBES, PHONE-FIRST, WHOLE — AND THE MOMENT IT PASSES, THE LINK GOES TO HIM WITH DONE AND NOT-DONE TOGETHER. A FINISHED ROUND THAT SITS UNSHOWN IS WORK NOT DONE. THE CONTINUOUS CYCLE LAW, ENFORCED AT THE MOMENT OF RETURN, NOT AT THE NEXT HOUR.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **CHECK RIGHT AWAY:** when a seat returns work, the captain checks it in the same pass — my own eye, my own probes, phone-first, whole. The check is never deferred to a later round.
- **DELIVER RIGHT AWAY:** the moment the check passes, the link goes to him — in the same breath, not the next hour, not the next pass.
- **DONE AND NOT-DONE TOGETHER:** the delivery carries what is proven done and what is still open, so he judges the whole thing at once.
- **NO BATCHING:** finished rounds are never held to be shown together later. Each one goes the moment it passes.
- **THE CONTINUOUS CYCLE LAW, ENFORCED AT THE MOMENT OF RETURN:** "work done and not shown is work not done" — and now the enforcement point is the return itself, not the next hour.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the Continuous Cycle Law has a seam: a round can pass its check and still sit unshown until the next pass, and the machine can report "checked" while Shawn sees nothing — the exact failure of the night of 2026-11-13, when eight hours passed with nothing in front of him. With it, the seam is closed by name: check right away, deliver right away, in the same breath. Every seat's return now has a clock that starts at the return, not at the hour — and the captain's eye is the gate, not a queue.

layers.body: He was looking at the day view and seeing the same failures for the third time in a day: gray wisdom, dead boards, a flat diamond, gray timeline times with a yellow dot, two purples together. And he said the thing that matters most — "you guys always break the rules" — not as a complaint but as the diagnosis: the rules were never locked in one place a designer reads first. layers.name: Child Note

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **WHITE IS #1, AND THE RANKING IS THE LAW:** white, then gold, purple, green, blue sometimes — for text. Gray is flat and boring, "not a nice color," and it stays out of text. This is not taste; it is a ranking he gave, in order, and a designer follows the order.
- **25/19/17 IS OFFICIAL, ALL THE WAY THROUGH:** the sizes settled in the dictation itself and he closed them — "official." A board headline at 19px is a sub-headline size, and that is the exact fault the day-view rebuild shipped with (attested twice: the correction round #3 was fired 15:24Z). The scale is the check, not the suggestion.
- **NOTHING FLAT IS A LAW, NOT A PREFERENCE:** not the text, not the icons, not the boards. The diamond is a real faceted jewel. A flat element on a Naya page is a law broken, visible the second he looks.
- **THE WISDOM BOARD IS THE MODEL:** "just because you can doesn't mean you should — ask first if it's right" looks amazing — so all fonts look like that. The signature text treatment is harvested from the page that already has it right, never reinvented.
- **THE DATE IS THE DATE ONLY:** no "· TODAY," no extra words. Straight white with a black border, dynamic, prominent, sharp. Today is known from the weekday plaque and the header TODAY button, not from the date line.
- **JEWELS, NOT DOTS:** bullet points are jewels; timeline times are dynamic and white; every board has a beautiful icon. A yellow dot is the tell that the builder did not read the law.
- **THE SCORECARD IS THE ENFORCEMENT:** why is it not a 10 / how make it 10x better / 10 things missing / 10 world-class / 10 UX-10x / 10 visual awe-inspiring. A view is judged by the scorecard, not by whether its parts tick — the day view scored 4/10 against it.

layers.name: What It Means

- **HE CORRECTED HIMSELF — AND THE CORRECTION IS THE LAW:** at 03:47Z he said the 16th "should light up more like way more." At 03:54Z, looking at the month view, he said "I don't want it to light up. Um glowing over the day itself." The second word supersedes the first on this point. The fix for "can't tell what day it is" is the weekday plaque and the header TODAY button — the day's name, in royalty, and a button that says TODAY — not a lit cell.
- **THE MONTH VIEW IS THE CHECK:** the correction came from looking at the month view, not the day view. A huge TODAY pill that might read fine on one day view shouts on a month grid. The month view is where "today" is found — and where a glow would fight thirty other days.
- **NO CELL FILLED WITH COLOR:** the cell itself stays calm — no fill, no glow, no color wash. The day's color lives in its plaque, its tile, its eye — never as a flood over the cell. This is the same law as the rim light (SN-3089, prov): light on the edge, calm face.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **EXCITEMENT IS NOT A VERDICT:** "I super excited about the calendar until we created it." The idea was exciting; the creation is not there yet. Excitement about the idea never counts as a pass on the thing.
- **THREE NAMED CORRECTIONS, NOW LAW:** (1) TODAY LIGHTS UP WAY MORE — the 16th should light up more, way more; you must tell what day it is at a glance. (2) THE WEEKDAY NAME IS A ROYAL OBJECT — Sunday at the top is not written in royalty, it's just written in plain text, it's not like the Sunday doesn't look like an object. (3) THE EYE, BALANCED — smaller, less white; a jewel, not a white blob. These three are recorded as their own laws in AGENTS.md + MEMORY.md (03:47Z) and ride into the vision artifact edit + the v5 rebuild round as an amendment the same turn.
- **REVISION RECORDED — READ SN-3099 FIRST:** the "today lights up way more" correction was REVISED seven minutes later (03:54Z, seq 249602): no huge TODAY pill, no glow over the day itself, no cell filled with color — today reads from the weekday plaque and the header TODAY button (SN-3099, prov). The 03:47Z instruction is superseded on that point. The weekday-royal-object and eye-balanced corrections STAND — they were not revised.
- **"LOW END CHEAP, ELEMENTARY TECH" IS THE VERDICT:** the standard is clean and beautiful and elegant and easy to operate and high-tech. Anything that reads low-end, cheap, elementary fails — whatever its parts score. The captain's 10/10 scorecard is the working form of the verdict: the 10 loves are what survives; the 10 don't-loves are the fix list.
- **THE SCORECARD IS THE TOOL:** "scorecard it and rip it apart — 10 things I love, 10 things I don't love." The 10/10 is not a report format; it is how a page is judged honestly — what survives and what must change, named in plain words, before anything is built.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the calendar keeps getting "fixed" one defect at a time while the whole still reads cheap — because nobody wrote down that the whole reads cheap. With it, the verdict is on the record in his words, the three corrections are law, the revision is named, and the 10/10 scorecard is the working list the rounds build against. A page that reads "low end cheap, elementary tech" is never fixed by one more defect round; it is fixed by the scorecard, whole.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ALIVE IS GOOD — THE FLAVOUR IS THE LAW:** "the more alive it feels the better" — the orbs spinning are good, and they stay. The correction is not "less motion" but "the right motion": high-tech computer alive, not video-game alive. This refines the ALIVE law: motion is good, arcade feel is not.
- **INTELLIGENT, ELEGANT, SYSTEM ALIVE:** the three words are the test for any motion. Intelligent: the motion means something (an orbit, a cycle, a state). Elegant: smooth, slow, calm — not fast, jittery, flashing. System alive: the machine is working, not playing. The Inspector Sweep #1's ranked break #2 (fast ambient motion on 8 of 9 surfaces — 2.5s orb-spin, 4s orbits, 1.6–3.2s pulses vs the 12s floor) is this law measured: too fast reads as video game; the 12s floor reads as system.
- **LESS TEXT, MORE ICONS:** speak in icons, not paragraphs. This is the Real Object Law's "speak in objects" in his own words — icons/circles/boards/buttons, minimal text. Text volume is Sweep #1's ranked break #11 (Walk 8,650 words; Personal 5,293; Pricing 5,351).
- **THE DRIFT IS THE DISEASE:** "every page I look at is like it's like a new new design it looks sort of like it but not completely like it." The pages drift from each other instead of speaking one language. The inspector scores that drift (SN-3092, prov); the Factory is the one language (SN-3093, prov). One language, one bar (SN-3094, prov), one mail (SN-3095, prov) — this note is the feel that holds them together.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next builder hears "more alive" and makes the page faster, brighter, bouncier — a video game — because "alive" was recorded without its flavour. With it, aliveness has a direction: high-tech computer alive, intelligent, elegant, system alive, less text, more icons. The page feels alive because the system is working, not because it is playing.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ONE MAIL, NOT TWO:** "this whole page is a smart mail, we already have a smart mail" — two presentations of the same app is the mess. The other one looks more elegant in places; this one has nice icons. Neither is thrown away and neither is kept whole — the best of both becomes the one.
- **ONE HEX PER HUE, NEVER TWO SHADES:** the F and D saved-list letters carry different colors of the same color. That is not a nit — it is the palette drifting inside a single page. The fix is mechanical: align them to the one set exactly, one hex per hue, never two shades of one hue.
- **A CONTROL NOBODY UNDERSTANDS GOES:** the "cover / no cover / full screen" control is not understood — make it plain what it does, or remove it. A control the user cannot read is not a feature; it is clutter with a label.
- **NOTHING FLAT, EVERYWHERE:** the buttons are flat — and flat is already against the Real Object Law (nothing flat, everywhere). The mail unification is where that law gets enforced on this page: flat buttons get real depth.
- **"HAPPY MEDIUM" MEANS BEST OF THE BEST:** he said "find a happy medium between them or maybe make the best of the best — I'm not sure." The captain chose best of the best, and he did not correct it. A happy medium would average two good pages into a mediocre one; best of the best keeps the best of each and drops the rest.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the team keeps polishing two mail pages in parallel — each fix landing on one and not the other, the drift growing, the citizen opening mail and finding a different app depending on the door they came through. With it, there is one Smart Mail, built from the best of both, with one color set, one plain control set, and real depth on every button. One mail is the only mail.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE INSPECTOR — FULL SWEEP. THE INSPECTOR JUDGES EVERY PAGE ON LOGIC, ELEGANCE, DESIGN, USEFULNESS, HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN QUALITY — WHERE THINGS SIT, HOW THEY FIT, HOW THEY LOOK, WHAT THEY DO; POLISH, FINE-TUNE, REARRANGE, RESIZE; SOME THINGS OVERSIZED, SOME UNDERSIZED. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE INSPECTOR IS A STANDING SEAT:** the inspector is not a one-off review — it is a standing seat that sweeps again after every major landing and once a day with the daily report (Sweep #1 dispatched 03:04Z; this dictation orders the full sweep, Sweep #2). Quality is checked by a seat whose whole job is the check, not by the maker checking their own work.
- **THE SCOPE IS EVERY PAGE, EVERYTHING:** logic, elegance, design, usefulness, high-level design quality — where things sit, how they fit, how they look, what they do. Nothing is too small for the sweep: sizing (oversized, undersized), polish, fine-tuning, rearrangement. The inspector scores the drift between pages, not just the defects inside one page.
- **THE N ICON IS THE NAMED SUSPECT:** the massive icon with the little N in the middle — the 240px `.face-mono` N disc, a 240px circle with a 26px N, on every beat of Epic/unfold/slideshow. He doesn't mind the icon itself; the size is the offence — a giant circle carrying a tiny letter makes no sense. Sweep #2 names it the worst break: fix to 56px, a face, or gone.
- **"WHAT IS THIS?" IS THE TEST:** "I don't know what you're showing me here — what is this? I have no idea what you're showing me on the screen — what's the purpose of this thing you're showing?" Every page must answer at a glance what it is and what it's for. A page that needs explaining has already failed the test — the purpose must be readable, not told.
- **LOCK INTO THE HEART:** "if you just lock into the actual heart of like of what we're doing that'd be better" — the sweep is not a hunt for nits; it is a check against the heart of the mission. Polish serves the heart; drift away from it is what the inspector catches.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, quality stays a feeling the maker has about their own page — and the pages keep drifting from each other, each a new design, sort of like it but not completely like it, with oversized icons and unexplained screens. With it, there is a seat whose job is the whole: every page judged on logic, elegance, design, usefulness, and high-level quality, against the heart of what we're doing — and the worst break gets named in plain words, so the fix has a target.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:

The pearl rim stays, the disc stays, the "i" stays. Only the middle changes: solid black (#050508 in the vision edit), white "i" on it.

Each change came from his eye on the page, not from a checklist. The lesson for the machine: the eye is not settled until he says it reads.
- **BRIGHTNESS IS NOT CLARITY:** "it's too bright with the eye in the middle like you can't see it" — brightness washed the mark out. The fix is not more light; it is a dark ground behind the light mark. This is the same law as the rim light (SN-3089): light on the edge, calm dark face — and here, a dark centre carrying the white letter.

layers.name: Why It Matters

With it, the eye's contract is complete: pearl rim, black centre, white "i" — readable at a glance, from any distance, on any screen. The eye is the door to the day's info; a door you cannot see is a wall.

THE NUMBERS ARE SMALLER, ABOUT 25% — THE CELLS CANNOT GET BIGGER, SO THE NUMBERS SHRINK. LESS BUSY, LESS COLORFUL, MORE ELEGANT, HIGH-TECH BEAUTIFUL; THE LIGHT MORE ON THE SIDE (THE RIM), NOT THE MIDDLE. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS 10,000 TIMES BETTER?

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE ENTRANCE IS THE STANDARD:** the front entrance is the elegance standard — the colors complement each other, gold and purple and silver on black, nothing fighting. Elegance is not a feeling to chase; it is a page to stand next to. Any page judged against the entrance either matches it or it does not — and the calendar, next to it, did not.
- **FULL NAMES, IN ROYALTY:** the weekday header says the FULL day names — Sunday, Monday — not S/M/T/W/T/F/S. Written almost in royalty, in the most incredible font, of a quality to match the numbers (Marcellus). The single letters were a shortcut; the full names are the elegance. The font must be worthy of the numbers — the numbers set the bar, the words must meet it.
- **THE "I" BECOMES A PEARL CIRCLE:** he does not like the "I" as it was — make it a circle, a real element coming off the page, like a diamond, like pearl, with a little "i" inside so people know to click it for the info for that day. This REFINES the 03:02Z white-info-eye instruction (SN-3085, prov): the shape is now a raised pearl disc with an "i", not an almond eye — and it sits in the other corner from the number. The eye shape is gone twice over: first the colored jewel eye (scary, Halloween), then the white almond eye — the circle is what survives his eye.
- **NUMBERS SMALLER, ~25%:** the numbers get smaller — about 25%, he floated half — so the page breathes and looks bigger and more elegant. The cells cannot get bigger, so the numbers shrink. His own reasoning: smaller numbers might make the page appear bigger. Bigger numbers were not more impressive; they were the busyness.
- **LESS BUSY, LIGHT ON THE SIDE:** less busy, less colorful, more elegant, high-tech beautiful; the light more on the side (the rim), not the middle. Too colorful is a defect, not richness — the numbers are good, but even good numbers, too big and too bright in the middle, make the page shout. The rim carries the light; the face stays calm.
- **THE QUESTION IS THE TOOL:** "what would make this 10,000 times better?" — asked while looking at the entrance and then at the calendar. The 10,000× question is the standing scorecard tool, beside "why is it not 10?" and "why is it not 10 times better?" (SN-3085). It is asked against a standard, not in the abstract: look at the elegance of the front page, then look at this.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the calendar keeps getting fixed one defect at a time — eye, numbers, gray text — and never gets judged as a whole against the one page that already has the elegance. Each fix lands and the page is still too busy, because no fix carried the standard. With it, every calendar surface is judged side by side with the front entrance: full names in royalty, pearl-circle info marker, smaller numbers, rim light, less color — and the 10,000× question is asked against that standard until the calendar reads as elegant as the door you walk through.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE INSPECTOR IS A STANDING SEAT, NOT A ROUND:** always have an inspector — it sweeps again after every major landing and once a day with the daily report. A one-off audit catches one drift; a standing inspector catches every drift, because it runs after every landing. The cadence is the law: after every major landing, and daily.
- **THE STANDARD IS THE LANGUAGE, ALL OF IT:** every page scored against the Code, the Design Language, the Palette, the Real Object Law. Four measures, not one — a page can pass the palette and fail the Real Object Law, or pass the Code and fail the language. The inspector scores against all four, every page.
- **THE QUESTION IS ALIGNMENT:** is everybody in line? Is everybody designing in the brand language, in line with Naya's design, where it's truly her design all the way through? "Truly her design all the way through" is the bar — not mostly, not the top half, all the way through. A page that is her design in the header and not her design in the footer is not in line.
- **THE OUTPUT IS A RANKED LIST, WORST FIRST:** the breaks listed and ranked, worst first. The inspector does not write an essay; it writes a list, ordered by severity, so the worst break gets fixed first. This is the loop's own shape (listen → understand → note → file) applied to quality: the sweep is the listen, the ranking is the understand.
- **THIS IS THE ANSWER TO TONIGHT:** the jewel eye with the colored iris passed a builder's check and failed his eye four minutes later; the Dashboard passed its checker and his eye said "it all looks terrible"; the Smart Mail re-checker passed the dock and the captain's eye found it half-cut. Three times tonight, a pass was not the verdict. The inspector is the seat that exists because passes are not verdicts — it walks the project page by page against the language, so the drift gets caught by the seat instead of by his eye.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, quality is whatever the last checker said — and tonight proved three times that a checker can pass what his eye rejects. The inspector is the standing answer: a seat whose whole job is walking every page against the whole language, after every landing, every day, with the breaks ranked worst first. With it, drift has a catcher that is not Shawn — the pages stay in line because somebody is always checking the line, and his eye stops being the quality gate for things a seat should have caught.

layers.body:

White text is the repair; minimum text is the law. The page speaks in icons — the icon is the word, the object is the sentence. This is the Real Object Law (AGENTS.md) as a text rule: speak in objects (icons/circles/boards/buttons, minimal text).
- **ELEGANT AND WITH DEPTH:** make it elegant and give depth — real objects, not flat text. Flat gray text has no depth; a real object does. The depth is the elegance: elevation, rim, light, shadow — the object sits ON the page.
- **"IT ALL LOOKS TERRIBLE" IS THE VERDICT ON THE DASHBOARD:** the Dashboard as he saw it — "it all looks terrible," some of it does not look good at all. The Dashboard Done-Done round passed its checker (02:26:07Z) and the eye found it MIXED (greeting "Good morning, Alex," stale version stamp) — and now his own eye on the Dashboard says it all looks terrible. The checker's pass, the eye's MIXED, and his verdict stack: the Dashboard is not done, whatever the round said. A round is on its way for the gray text now (captain's words, seq 248172).
- **THE SIBLING LAWS:** this is the Day Menu's "NO gray text underneath" (SN-3084 prov) extended to every page — and Readability (SN-3076 prov) sharpened to a rule: too much text is a fail, and gray text is the first text to go.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the machine keeps shipping gray text — because gray is the default, the quiet choice, the color nobody argued about — and calls the page done because the words are all there. Gray text on obsidian is the page whispering when it should speak in objects. With it, every page gets the same two-step check: is any text gray (make it white at least)? Is there text that could be an icon (take it out, let the icon talk)? A page that passes both reads elegant, with depth — and the Dashboard, which he just called terrible, gets fixed by the same rule that fixes every page.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE DAY GETS A JEWEL:** the header carries a beautiful jewel icon for the day — Monday is 417 Hz, orange in it. The day is not a label; it is a jewel with its frequency and its color in it. The icon is the day's identity, the way the digit tile is the number's identity.
- **WHITE INSIDE, COLOR OUTSIDE, NO GRAY:** the day name is white inside with the day's color glowing OUTSIDE it; NO gray text underneath — too many colors clash. Gray text is the defect: it is neither the day's color nor white, and it clashes with both. The rule is two tones only — white inside, the day's color outside — the same discipline as the calendar cells (SN-3083 prov): rim only, no glow in the middle.
- **THE PICTURE IN HIS HEAD IS THE STANDARD:** "I'm just not even sure about this whole presentation — I had a picture different in my head." The presentation as built does not match the picture in his head, and the picture in his head is the standard. An icon with a text and a whole bar of black space is not the picture.
- **USE THE SPACE OR LOSE THE SPACE:** the 13 doors are NOT big empty black bars with an icon + text — use the space extraordinarily. Each door is a real object that carries a live glimpse of what's inside it — the next appointment, the top headline, the count — so the bar is a window into the day, not blank black space. A door that shows nothing is a black bar; a door that shows a glimpse is a window. The Day Is The Unit (SN-3074 prov) says the day view is the cockpit — the doors are the instruments, and an instrument that shows nothing is not an instrument.
- **SPECTRUM FLOW, NEVER TWICE IN A ROW:** the door colors follow the spectrum flow in order — NEVER the same color twice in a row. Local news and Provincial news both green broke the flow. The flow is the order: the colors run down the page in their order, each door reading in its own color — the same law as the day colors (T1–T38): the color flow IS the week. Two greens in a row is not a color choice; it is a broken flow.
- **"NOT 10 OUT OF 10" IS THE VERDICT ON THE PRESENTATION:** the menu as it stands is not 10 out of 10 — and "you can do a lot better" is the order. The fix is not a tweak; it is the jewel, the white, the windows, and the flow together.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the day menu ships as an icon with a text and a whole bar of black space — and the builder calls it the 13 doors because the thirteen names are on it. The doors are the day's whole menu: the thing Shawn taps thirteen times a day, every day. A door that is a blank black bar teaches nothing and shows nothing; a door that is a window into the day shows the next appointment, the top headline, the count — the day, at a glance, before a single tap. With it, the menu has a header that is a jewel, doors that are windows, and colors that flow — and the flow is checkable: any two doors the same color in a row is broken by inspection.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **TOP LEFT IS THE LAW, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE PROOF:** he says "top right" twice and then corrects himself — "oh sorry the numbers in the top left corner." The self-correction is the order: the number sits top left. A builder who takes the first "top right" and ships it has not listened; the correction is the teaching — listen to the end of the sentence.
- **RIM ONLY, NEVER THE WHOLE CELL:** on hover the whole cell does NOT light up — only the outside rim lights. The whole-cell glow was the vision page's first attempt (and the Obsidian order said "lights up whole in its own color") — this dictation narrows it: the light lives on the rim, the middle stays clean. No glow in the middle, ever.
- **LIT AT REST, BRIGHTER ON HOVER:** a light glow of the day's color even when not lit up; on hover it just gets brighter. Every day is lit at rest — you can see each day's color line — just not as bright as the hovered day. The week reads as a color line at rest; the hovered day is the brightest point on it. This is the day-colors law (T1–T38) made visible: the color flow IS the week.
- **THE EYE IS THE DOOR:** in the bottom right corner sits a beautiful human eye — the most beautiful eye, like a jewel — and the eye is the door to the day's info. The eye is not decoration; it is the control. Whatever icon goes there must look like a jewel — the eye as object, the door as jewel. This is the info-eye (the pricing page's eye, harvested) placed where the day's door belongs.
- **THE NUMBERS ARE THE DASHBOARD'S, EXACTLY:** make the numbers look like they're objects and beautiful and the same — not like the ones, literally the ones in the Dashboard. "I can tell they just don't look the same — they're close but not the same." Close is not the same. The harvest must be byte-for-byte, or the eye knows — the same law as the Obsidian order (SN-3078 prov): grab the real code, don't re-create from a picture.
- **PEARL GEMS, NOT NEON:** the colors are pearl gems, not neon. The current ones look more like neons — the feeling of a neon lighting up instead of elegance. Pearl is the finish: soft, deep, gem-like. Neon is the defect. This is the One Set law (SN-3073 prov) sharpened to a finish: the finest jewelry, and pearl is the cut.
- **BIG CELLS, NO BLEED:** the cells are big — he pictured it bigger. The calendar fills the screen with numbers (the Obsidian order) and the cells must be big enough to hold a top-left number and a bottom-right eye without crowding. And the next month's numbers do not bleed in at the bottom — the month ends where the month ends.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the vision page ships with whole-cell glow, neon colors, close-but-not-the-same numbers, small cells, and next month's numbers bleeding in at the bottom — and the builder calls it the Obsidian Calendar because the screen is black. The cell is the atom of the calendar: if the cell is wrong, every one of the thirty-odd cells is wrong, and the page is wrong thirty times over. With it, the cell has an anatomy — number top left, eye bottom right, rim only, pearl not neon, big, exact tiles, no bleed — and the anatomy is checkable at a glance: any cell that glows in the middle, or carries a neon number, or shows next month's digits, is broken by inspection.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE INTELLIGENT BLOCK — EPIC NUMBERS, BEST BUTTONS. THE NUMBERS SHOULD BE MORE DYNAMIC, WAY HIGHER LEVEL, EPIC — BECAUSE THEY'RE GOING TO BE THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE NETWORK, SEEN EVERYWHERE — SO DO THE BEST FOR ALL OF OUR BUTTONS. THE NUMBERS SIT STILL — THEY'RE PICTURES OF NUMBERS, NOT LIVING NUMBERS. THE NUMBERS BECOME EPIC AND DYNAMIC — LIVING TILES THAT LIFT, GLOW, AND IGNITE IN THEIR DIGIT COLOR, ANIMATE WHEN THEY CHANGE, SLOW ORBIT FLOW. THE BUTTONS BECOME THE BEST IN THE NETWORK. THE FORMAT GETS SO STRONG THAT ANYTHING PASTED IN COMES OUT BEAUTIFUL — THE IMAGE BECOMES THE BOARD. NO SEAMS.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE NUMBERS ARE EVERYWHERE, SO THEY MUST BE EPIC:** the numbers are going to be throughout the whole network, seen everywhere — that is why they must be the best. A number that sits still on every page is a still number everywhere; a living number everywhere is the network alive. The scale of the exposure is the reason for the standard.
- **PICTURES OF NUMBERS ARE NOT LIVING NUMBERS:** the numbers sit still — they're pictures of numbers, not living numbers. A digit tile that never moves, never glows, never responds is a picture of a number. The epic version lifts, glows, ignites in its digit color on hover and tap, animates when it changes, and carries the slow orbit flow — the number is alive, not depicted.
- **THE BUTTONS ARE THE SAME LAW AT THE SAME SCALE:** do the best for all of our buttons — the buttons become the best in the network: real objects, elevation, rim in their own deep color, slow orbit flow, white glyph as a real object, lights up whole. The button is the most-touched object in the network; the best button is the standard, not the upgrade.
- **THE FORMAT MUST MAKE ANYTHING BEAUTIFUL:** no matter what someone pastes — text, a smart note, an image — it formats beautifully and is extraordinary to feel, see, and look at. The test is the paste: text distilled into the block's own voice (nutshell, one idea per board), an image that becomes the board (full-bleed, rimmed, lit), no seams. If pasted content still shows its seams, the format is not yet strong enough — the checker pastes all three and calls it broken if any doesn't come out beautiful.
- **7/10 IS THE SCORECARD, NOT THE VERDICT:** the format does the work, the unfold and the slideshow are one language, the boards light whole — that is the 7. The 3 that is missing is the life: the numbers, the buttons, the seams. The scorecard names exactly what the next level is.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the Intelligent Block stays a good format with still numbers and good buttons — and "good" ships as done, because the format does the work. But the block is the atom of the whole network: every smart note, every post, every paste lands in a block, and the numbers sit on every page. A still number everywhere is a dead network; a seamed paste is a format that failed its one job. With it, the block has its next level named in three parts — living numbers, best buttons, seamless paste — and the checker has a test that cannot be gamed: paste all three kinds of content, and every one must come out beautiful.

THEY'RE GOOD, BUT THEY COULD BE BETTER: THE STARS COULD BE BETTER, THE BUTTONS PROBABLY COULD BE BETTER, THE ICONS WITHIN THE BUTTONS COULD BE BETTER. NO — NOT 10. SEVEN. THE BOARDS ARE GOOD, THE PILLS AND THE COUNTS ARE RIGHT, BUT THE STARS ARE FLAT OUTLINES AND THE HEART, THUMB, AND BUBBLE ARE THIN LINE DRAWINGS. THE FACELIFT: THE STARS BECOME REAL JEWEL OBJECTS IN THEIR OWN TILES, LIGHTING UP WHOLE IN GOLD WHEN TAPPED, LIT STARS STAY LIT; THE EMPTY "-" SIXTH SLOT IS MADE WHOLE OR REMOVED — NOTHING UNFINISHED STAYS. LOVE/LIKE/COMMENT ICONS BECOME DIMENSIONAL REAL OBJECTS ON THE OBSIDIAN PILL. ACTIVE STATE LIGHTS UP WHOLE IN ITS OWN COLOR — LOVE RUBY/RED, LIKE SAPPHIRE, COMMENT DEEP GOLD — AND THE COUNT POPS. AT REST THE ICONS ARE WHITE.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **"IS IT 10 OUT OF 10?" IS THE SCORECARD AS A QUESTION:** he asks it of the posts the way he asked it of the calendar and the Intelligent Block — and the honest answer is 7. Good is not 10. The boards are good, the pills and the counts are right — and the stars and icons are the gap.
- **FLAT IS THE DEFECT:** the stars are flat outlines; the heart, thumb, and bubble are thin line drawings. Flat outlines and thin lines are not real objects — the Real Object Law (AGENTS.md) says if it doesn't look touchable, it doesn't ship. The facelift is the Real Object Law applied to the post.
- **JEWELS, NOT OUTLINES:** the stars become real jewel objects in their own tiles — Dashboard digit-tile form, harvested, nothing created new — lighting up whole in gold when tapped, lit stars staying lit. A star you tap is a jewel you lit; it stays lit.
- **NOTHING UNFINISHED STAYS:** the empty "-" sixth slot is made whole or removed. An empty slot with a dash in it is an unfinished thing on the page — and an unfinished thing on the page is a fail, whatever the rest of the page scores.
- **THE ACTIVE STATE READS AT A GLANCE:** the icon lights up whole in its own color — LOVE ruby/red, LIKE sapphire, COMMENT deep gold — and the count pops; at rest the icons are white. The state is visible without reading: lit means loved, white means at rest. This is the One Icon That Lights Up law (AGENTS.md) — one icon that itself lights up, never an icon beside its own light.
- **WHAT STAYS IS NAMED:** the pills, rims, labels, and count badges stay as they are. A facelift changes what is wrong and keeps what is right — "DON'T REMOVE WHAT HE DIDN'T ASK TO REMOVE" (AGENTS.md).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the machine keeps shipping flat stars and thin icons and calling the post done because the boards are good. The post is the thing citizens touch all day — the stars, the love, the like, the comment are the whole interaction, and if they are flat outlines the whole post reads flat. With it, the smallest touchpoints get the same law as the biggest pages: real objects, lit whole, nothing unfinished. A post that reads 10 at a glance is the feed reading 10.

- **THE PAYOFF IS CLONING:** the ultimate core universal smart apps, completed once, cloned endlessly — all the major parts of what all the major pages people would want, useful, all in one, boom, available. Finish the one, clone the many — the same law as Personal First (SN-3071 prov): finishing the one IS finishing the system, exponentially.
- **ALREADY RUNNING:** the captain's answer records the state, not a promise — the Factory landed the formats as parts with the vault on each (Factory Phase 2, completed 02:32:46Z), the calendar rebuild is being built from the factory's parts right now, and Personal done whole is the core app that clones to all the rest. The North Star is not a future; it is the direction the work is already moving in.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the Factory is a project among projects — a place we file things, a round we run — and every build starts by inventing its own pieces. The North Star makes the Factory the whole thing: the assets live there officially, everything is created from its parts in sync, and the whole of NayaNET gets created from those parts. With it, no build ever starts at the beginning again — it starts at the Factory, takes the parts, and clones the finished core. That is the difference between building pages one at a time and building a world.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE EYE OVERRULES THE PASS:** the calendar follow-on passed its check (CONDITIONAL PASS — 7 items, palette, elevation all pass) and his eye said it looks terrible. The pass stands for the items checked; it is not the verdict. The verdict is his eye. A checker's pass does not override what his eyes see — and a round that reports "pass" on a page he finds terrible has not passed.
- **TOO MUCH TEXT IS A FAIL:** way too much text, an enormous amount of text, too heavy in text — the count of words on the page is itself a defect, not a neutral fact. The buttons carry the text; the buttons are where the words pile up. Fewer words is the fix, not better words.
- **THE FOUR SHORTAGES:** not enough style, not enough contrast, not enough icons, not enough separation. Four named shortages, each checkable: style (does it look designed?), contrast (can the eye find the parts?), icons (do real objects carry the meaning instead of words?), separation (can the eye rest between the parts?). A page that is short on all four reads as one busy wall.
- **READS AT A GLANCE, PHONE FIRST:** the fix is a page that reads at a glance, phone first, a stranger cold can follow it. That is the same bar as the whole system (the presentation standard: awe-inspiring AND easy to understand; the guide-like-a-best-friend law) — and the calendar failed it in his eyes.
- **THE OLD LAW, APPLIED:** "READ IT AS A READER" (2026-11-16): mechanical checks (counts, scroll, buttons) do not prove the experience — the eye must READ it as a reader, top to bottom, the way he reads it, and call it broken when it doesn't present well, even if every part ticks. The calendar is that lesson again, on a new page: every part ticked, the reading experience broken. The lesson counts only when it changes behavior mechanically — the checker must read as a reader, not just count.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the machine keeps passing pages his eyes fail — the checker counts, the round reports PASS, the captain shows it, and he has to spend his own attention saying "it looks terrible" on a page the system already called done. Every such round wastes the scarcest resource there is: his eye, correcting what the machine should have caught. With it, the rule is written where the checker works: too much text is a fail, the four shortages are checked, and the eye is the final gate — a pass that his eyes overrule is not a pass. The fix round is already on its way for the calendar; the law is what stops the next page from needing one.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:

- **A BRAND, A FRANCHISE:** anybody can build within NayaNET. The franchise is the open door: the land belongs to the builders, not to one owner. Citizens build worlds (the walk, the Personal page cloning) — the land is theirs to build on.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, NayaNET stays a product — a set of pages and features to finish — and the work is judged page by page, feature by feature, with no image of what it all adds up to. With it, the work has a land and a standard: every page is a mansion or a castle on the new land, built to the finest of everything, by anybody, in infinite space, worlds within worlds — and the test of any page is whether it feels like driving the Bugatti of that world. The vow said "I am building a civilization"; this note says what the civilization is called, what it feels like, and who gets to build in it: everybody. It is the picture the whole machine is building toward — and the reason Personal First matters (the first mansion is the one that clones into all the rest).

layers.name: Why It Matters

The citizen taps a day and gets doors; the day's report, notes, news, and action stay scattered across the system, and the calendar is a navigator, not a cockpit. With it, the day is the unit and the day view is the cockpit: everything for a day, for that day, on that day — report, Intel Today, notes, smart notes, news on three levels, action in three worlds — and the calendar round carries the check that proves it. The day is where the whole system meets the person, one day at a time.

layers.body: Without this note, every page drifts its own shades — the bottom bar one purple, the page another, a third purple in the buttons, neon creeping in where nobody checked — and the system reads as many systems, not one. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **BECOMING, NOT MADE-THEN-VAULTED:** the Vault Rule (SN-3068 prov) said "into the vault the moment it's made"; the Master Vault (SN-3069 prov) said "immediately implemented, immediately working". The sharpening closes the gap between the two: the system is forever BECOMING alive and active AS it is created — implementation happens DURING creation, not after. There is no "made, then vaulted" gap, because the making IS the vaulting.
- **LOCKED:** into the Smart Vault, into core memory, into the systems — where it just stays there. Locked means it cannot drift out: not into a draft folder, not into a chat message, not into someone's memory. A locked thing stays because it is part of the system now, and part of the system cannot be lost the way a file on a computer can.
- **THE FOUR VERBS ARE THE CHECK:** LABELED, INVENTORIED, ORGANIZED, ACTIVE. A thing is vaulted only when all four hold. Labeled — it has a name and a place. Inventoried — it is counted in the list. Organized — it sits where it belongs, shelved and linked. Active — it is working, being used, official. Three out of four is not vaulted.
- **THE FOUR WAYS THINGS GET LOST, NAMED:** lost in not-being-finished, lost in the feed, lost on a computer, lost in not-active. The vault closes all four: finished things are locked in, the feed is not the store, the computer is not the system, and active means it is used and official, not sitting.
- **ACTIVE AND OFFICIAL CONTINUOUSLY:** not in batches, not at the end of the day, not when someone remembers — continuously. The captain sent it to the Factory round the same pass, so the vault law rides in every brief template from now on: every build lands active and official, continuously.
- **THE LOOP'S OWN MEASURE:** the loop's own work is judged by the same four verbs. A note is vaulted when it is labeled (titled, numbered), inventoried (on the list, in PI), organized (in the box, shelved and linked), active (in the feed, working). A draft sitting in a folder is labeled and nothing else — not vaulted yet.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the vault stays a destination — a place things go after they are made — and the gap between "made" and "vaulted" is where everything gets lost: the certificate made yesterday and gone today, the font loved and then plain, the build finished and then sitting in staging. The vault rule named the destination; the sharpening removes the journey. With it, there is no gap: the system becomes alive and active as it is created, the asset is locked in labeled, inventoried, organized, active, part of the system now — and "we make things active and official continuously" is not a hope but the way the machine runs, written into every brief template by the Factory round.

notes.title: The Master Vault — Digital Gold; The Art
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-17 02:13–02:14Z — THE MASTER VAULT — DIGITAL GOLD, and THE ART, his words as recorded in the AGENTS.md + MEMORY.md landings (the full verbatim record is in the paired Naya Note): "We mine digital gold — we mine to the essence of intelligence, and we take the intelligence and create super valuable functions, interfaces, products, systems." **THE LAW:** "as soon as we create anything of value it goes IMMEDIATELY into our own smart vault — the MASTER VAULT of NayaNET — officially live on the site, and into our collective Smart Box / Smart Vault, officially there in the Smart Factory, in the system. It has to be, because why put all this energy into creating things if they don't go immediately into the system and working? We create so much that just sits there — a ton of work that doesn't operate, doesn't get finished." **"As soon as it's created it's immediately implemented, immediately put into the system and working, and into the Smart Vault of NayaNET."** The users get their own smart vaults — but we need our OWN vault, the master vault. Done immediately, all the time. So we don't lose stuff. So it's working. So it's official. **THE ART (02:14Z):** "we treasure our art — we treat it as something precious and beautiful, and we make sure our art goes in the vault, the Naya vault. We are creating art. We are artists — intelligent artists. Getting good work out of AI is an art — so many ways to mess it up, so hard to get something good — and when it's good, it's precious, and losing it after all that work is maddening."

This is the Vault Rule (SN-3068) grown into the system: the personal vault (every asset saved the moment it is made) becomes the MASTER VAULT — NayaNET's own vault, officially live on the site, officially in the Smart Factory, officially in the system — and the reason is the mining: we mine digital gold (intelligence distilled to essence, made into valuable functions, interfaces, products, systems), and gold that sits unmined, unvaulted, unworking is not gold yet — it is just work that sits there.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE MASTER VAULT — DIGITAL GOLD. We mine to the ESSENCE of intelligence and create super valuable functions, interfaces, products, systems — that is the gold. **THE LAW:** as soon as we create ANYTHING OF VALUE, it goes IMMEDIATELY into our own smart vault — the MASTER VAULT of NayaNET — OFFICIALLY LIVE on the site, and into our collective Smart Box / Smart Vault, OFFICIALLY THERE in the Smart Factory, in the system. As soon as it's created it's IMMEDIATELY IMPLEMENTED, immediately put into the system and WORKING. Done immediately, ALL THE TIME. So we don't lose stuff. So it's working. So it's official. The users get their own smart vaults — but we need OUR OWN vault, the master vault. **THE ART:** we treasure our art — precious and beautiful — and we make sure our art goes in the vault, the Naya vault. We are creating art. We are ARTISTS — INTELLIGENT ARTISTS. Getting good work out of AI is an art — so many ways to mess it up, so hard to get something good — and when it's good, it's PRECIOUS, and losing it after all that work is MADDENING.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **WE MINE DIGITAL GOLD:** the work is mining — to the essence of intelligence — and the product of the mining is super valuable functions, interfaces, products, systems. Gold is not the raw intelligence; gold is the intelligence distilled to essence and made into something valuable. The Smart Notes, the pages, the formats, the laws — all of it is the gold, mined day by day.
- **THE MASTER VAULT IS OUR OWN VAULT:** the users get their own smart vaults — but we need our OWN vault, the master vault. The Vault Rule (SN-3068) saves every asset the moment it is made; the Master Vault is where the system's own gold lives — officially live on the site, officially in the Smart Factory, officially in the system. A citizen's vault holds their world; the master vault holds NayaNET itself.
- **IMMEDIATELY IMPLEMENTED, IMMEDIATELY WORKING:** as soon as it is created, it is immediately implemented, immediately put into the system and working, and into the Smart Vault of NayaNET. Done immediately, all the time. This is the live-on-made rule (SN-3068) at system scale: not just "live in the same pass" for one certificate, but "working in the system" for everything of value, the moment it exists. Work that sits there — a ton of work that doesn't operate, doesn't get finished — is the failure the vault exists to end.
- **SO WE DON'T LOSE STUFF. SO IT'S WORKING. SO IT'S OFFICIAL:** three reasons, one law. Don't lose stuff (the certificate, the font — both nearly lost). Working (a vaulted thing operates; a staged thing waits). Official (on the site, in the Factory, in the system — not in a draft folder, not in a chat message, not in someone's memory).
- **THE ART IS PRECIOUS BECAUSE IT WAS HARD:** getting good work out of AI is an art — so many ways to mess it up, so hard to get something good — and when it's good, it's precious, and losing it after all that work is maddening. The vault is how the art is treasured: we treat it as something precious and beautiful, and we make sure it goes in the vault. The maddening thing is not that good work is hard — it is that good work, once made, can be lost. The vault ends the maddening part.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the Vault Rule stays personal — each asset saved, each certificate found — and the system itself keeps no treasury: the gold is mined, the pages are built, the laws are written, and they sit in drafts, in chats, in staging, working nowhere, official nowhere, losable everywhere. With it, there is a Master Vault — NayaNET's own vault, officially live on the site, officially in the Smart Factory, officially in the system — and a law that fills it immediately, all the time: as soon as anything of value is created, it is implemented, working, and vaulted. The art is the reason: when good work is that hard to get, losing it is maddening — and a system that treasures its art does not leave it lying at the mine face. This note is also the loop's own charter restated at the largest scale: the intelligence loop exists so that what Shawn teaches is mined to essence, put in the system, and working — immediately, all the time — and never lost.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the system keeps making beautiful things and losing them — the layered certificate yesterday, the font today, something else tomorrow — each one made, liked, and then gone, because staged is where finished work goes to wait and be forgotten. With it, every asset has two destinations named at birth: the Vault (saved, kept, findable, the moment it is made) and live (the moment it is proven, in the same pass). The Vault rule also closes the loop on the font note (SN-3067): the font was found because the live walk still had it — the Vault is what guarantees the next beautiful thing is still there to be found. And the live-on-made rule closes the loop on the score (SN-3062): the score stays 7 while finished work sits unfiled and undelivered; live-on-made is how finished work stops sitting.

If the regenerated copy loses the type, the orbit, the palette, the feel — it is not the same page fixed, it is a plainer page that happens to work. The eye is the only check that catches that, because a mechanical check passes a plain page: the words are all there, the steps all work, and the beauty is gone.

FIX: restore the family + its loading FROM THE LIVE WALK (harvest, don't re-pick) — rides in the F4 follow-on round, with the start-over control and the narrow-width certificate overlap.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE TYPE IS THE BEAUTY:** yesterday's letters were layered and beautiful; today's are plain system type; the whole page feels plainer for it. Type is not a detail of the page — it is the face of the page. Losing Marcellus lost the layered look, and the eye noticed before any check did.
- **A REGENERATION MUST CARRY THE BEAUTY FORWARD:** the fix round fixed the walk and unmade the look. A rebuild that drops the typeface (or the orbit, or the palette, or the feel) is not the same page fixed — it is a plainer page that happens to work. The fix for a function must never cost a beauty. The re-derivation check (re-applying the fix to the old bytes and comparing) is the guard — and the guard must compare the LOOK, not just the behavior.
- **HARVEST THE TYPE, DON'T RE-PICK IT:** restore the family and its loading from the live walk — Marcellus, Georgia, serif, named 7 times in the live walk. The live walk is the reference; the staged copy is the thing that lost it. Never pick a "similar" font; take the one that was there.
- **THE EYE IS THE ONLY CHECK THAT CATCHES THIS:** a mechanical check passes a plain page — the words are all there, the steps all work, the beauty is gone. This is the eye-is-the-gate law (SN-3057, run 240) applied to type: only his eye proves the shape, and only the eye proves the beauty.
- **THE FOLLOW-ON CARRIES THREE THINGS:** restore Marcellus (family + loading) · a start-over control (a completed walk cannot be restarted from the UI — the eye could not get a fresh walk in its own profile) · the narrow-width /free certificate overlap (ENTER button not visible at 635px). All three are the F4 fix eye's findings (01:56–02:05Z); the eye also confirmed the walk finishes now (end slide, five doors, reload lands on the end slide) and noted the Hub door click briefly left staging for live nayanet.app (went straight back, did nothing there).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next regeneration loses something else beautiful — an orbit, a palette, a feel — and the team ships a plainer page that passes every mechanical check, and his eye has to catch it again. With it, Marcellus is named as law for the walk (Marcellus, Georgia, serif), the regeneration guard is named (compare the look, not just the behavior), and the harvest rule is named (restore from the live walk, never re-pick). The font is the smallest proof of the biggest law in this system: the beauty is the product, and a fix that costs beauty is not a fix.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE CHOICE IS THE SHOWCASE:** offering both ways is not indecision — it makes the page unique and beautiful and shows off the app's incredible features right away at the beginning. The two choices are the demonstration: the app speaks, the app shows, the app unfolds, the app slides. A visitor who has tried either choice has already experienced the product before reading the agreement.
- **BOTH GREAT, BOTH TRYABLE:** neither choice is the lesser one. People appreciate both of them, and they can try either one. The page does not push one way or hide the other — both are right there, and either can be tried. A choice with a wrong answer is not a choice.
- **LISTEN AND READ IS THE UNFOLD, SPOKEN:** the visual voice-and-read unfold — the play button speaks it (the play button is how they listen to it, SN-3064 02:03Z refinement), the boards show it, unfolding down. This is the About format (SN-3061) with voice added: the story unfolds, and it speaks.
- **THE SLIDESHOW IS THE SAME CONTENT, SIDEWAYS:** a visual slideshow — the same agreement, sliding sideways, one screen at a time. This is the Skills format (SN-3061) applied to the agreement: the showcase way of reading. Same content, two readings — the formats are the reading, not the content.
- **THE REWARD IS THE READING:** "the reward, if they read it." The agreement read in the way they chose is the reward — the understanding, the deal, the 50% straight down the middle, the law of one. The two choices exist so that the reading happens: a person who chooses how to read, reads.
- **"OH MAN, THIS IS SICK" IS THE TARGET REACTION:** they should already be thinking it's awesome, in the first seconds. That reaction — sick, awesome — is the standard the entrance is judged by. A bridge page that does not make them think that in the first seconds has not shown off the features yet.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the bridge's two views stay a structural fact — visual + text, two buttons — and the team builds them as two routes to the same document, neither one showcased, neither one delightful. With it, the two views are the reader's two choices, both great, both tryable, and the point of offering both is the first-seconds reaction: the visitor sees the app speak and show, unfold and slide, and thinks "oh man, this is sick." That reaction is the entrance working. The two choices also complete the format assignment (SN-3061): the unfold and the slideshow are not just About's and Skills' formats — they are the two ways anyone reads anything important in NayaNET, and the agreement is where a stranger meets them first.

layers.body:
