His eye is the final gate on interfaces — a thing is landed only when he sees it on his own screen, in place, working. The question is the standard applied to the Library: show it to him, in the page, or it is not done.
- **THE ANSWER IS A PLACE, NOT A DESCRIPTION:** Personal → About → the green door. A citizen must be able to find it cold — no explanation needed, no tour. If he has to ask where it is, the placement is part of the work, not settled by naming the door.
- **A DOOR IS NOT A LIBRARY:** the Library is defined by what it does — a live count of what is inside, Add that saves, Share on every entry, search/filter, category chips. The eye found none of those provable: no count anywhere, Add failing twice, an empty library, Share/search/chips untestable. Until those work, the door opens onto a promise.
- **THE EYE FAIL IS THE PROOF, NOT THE OPINION:** the formats eye (01:23–01:35Z) walked the bridges, the unfolds, the Skills beats — those PASS. The FAIL is specific: slideshow stacked, Library uncountable and unsavable. layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the Library stays a door everyone agrees is beautiful — praised in chat, named in the brief, uncounted and unsavable on the page — and the team moves on believing it exists because it was described. With it, the Library has a definition that can be checked by anyone: count visible, Add saves, Share works, search and chips work on real entries. "I have to see it" becomes the test every feature must pass, and the Library is the case that proves the test is real: the eye walked it, it failed, and the failure is now the work list. This is also the Intelligent Library's first honest state since it was named in the Naya Code (SN-3052): it lives in About, it has a door, and it does not yet work.

notes.title: The Color Question — Gold Worth, Blue Mind

(B) gold + emerald = 7/10 — classic, strong row separation, but emerald sits right under the green What It Means layer (two greens touching) and emerald means nature/growth — what intelligence does, not what it is. layers.body: A control that does nothing when you touch it is a picture of a control — and a picture cannot be operated by a child or a grandma. The touch is the proof: you touch it, you feel it push in and out, it lights up, it moves, it does stuff. That is the best — because pressing is useful, helpful, and obvious, all three at once: useful because it does something, helpful because it shows you it did, obvious because anyone can see how. The bar is the person, not the control: an internet all children and grandmas can operate. If a child cannot press it and a grandma cannot feel it, it is not done. This sharpens the 3D press law (SN-3181) into a test anyone can run: touch it — did you feel it? If not, it failed, however beautiful it is. And it answers the Smart Mail eye's caution from 22:50Z once and for all: a rule in bytes that produces no visible press change is not a press at all.

notes.title: Work Smart, Not Repeated
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-17 22:48Z, his words verbatim: "When I ask you stuff like this, because this all takes a lot of work to go through all this, right? I need you to do it smartly. Like, and organized and not duplicated and not just send more than what you need... how many repeats is it going to be? I keep going through these, but like, you gotta get on top of this." LAW: fewer, fuller rounds — consolidate everything known into ONE round, never re-send what is already running, never split one fix across two rounds, never show him the same page twice; the round count goes down, not up. Hold the whole list at once; do it smartly, organized, not duplicated, not more than what is needed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every repeat is a round he has to read, check, and send back — work he does because the machine did not do its own organizing first. One fix split across two rounds is two reviews for one change. A round re-sent while it is already running is two makers on one file, and one of them will clobber the other. The same page shown twice is his time spent twice on the same thing, and his time is the most expensive cost in the whole system. The machine's job is to hold the whole list at once and send it once, whole. That is what "get on top of this" means: the organizing happens before the round goes out, not after it comes back. Fewer rounds, fuller rounds — that is how the round count goes down, and his time comes back.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you ask someone to clean your room, and they bring you one sock, then go back for one shirt, then go back for one shoe — ten trips for ten things, and you have to check every trip. Or they could bring everything at once, in one trip, all done. One trip, everything, done. That is working smart.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, when there is a lot to do, the smart way is to gather it all up first, put it in one neat pile, and carry it in once — not to run back and forth ten times with one little thing each time, and never to send the same thing twice. Fewer trips, fuller trips. That is how you respect someone's time.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: DO IT SMARTLY. ORGANIZED AND NOT DUPLICATED AND NOT JUST SEND MORE THAN WHAT YOU NEED. FEWER, FULLER ROUNDS. CONSOLIDATE EVERYTHING KNOWN INTO ONE ROUND. THE ROUND COUNT GOES DOWN, NOT UP.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ONE ROUND:** consolidate everything known into ONE round — hold the whole list at once.
- **NEVER RE-SEND:** never re-send what is already running — a running round is already owned.
- **NEVER SPLIT:** never split one fix across two rounds — one fix, one round, one review.
- **NEVER SHOW TWICE:** never show him the same page twice — one link, whole, or not at all.
- **THE COUNT GOES DOWN:** the round count goes down, not up — that is the measure.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the machine keeps spinning rounds the way it always has — one item per round, repeats on top of running work, the same page shown twice — and he keeps paying for it with his own time, going through the same things again and again. With it, the organizing happens first: one whole list, one full round, sent once. His time comes back, and the round count goes down.

- **THE VERDICT:** if they run into each other under zoom, it is bad design, not quality — rebuild the pair until the space holds.

On the Hub, the left is where the world already lives: the sidebar, the feed, the person's own place. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He opened the Hub feed and read it the way a person reads it — and what he saw was the machine talking about itself. A line of backend telemetry sitting under the feed pills, a globe stuck on the edge of a card, a wisdom board filled by a long test note nobody wrote as wisdom. None of it is the feed; all of it is the machine leaking onto the page. His list is a cleanup in the truest sense: take the machine's words off the page he sees, take the decoration off the box, and let the wisdom be what wisdom is — a couple of sentences, nice and short, that a person can take in at a glance. And the close button is the same instinct in a control: when he is done with the wisdom, it folds away and the search rises to meet the feed buttons — no gap, no dead space, nothing left standing between him and the feed. The page he sees should show him his world, not the machine's diary.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your bedroom wall has a beautiful picture on it — but someone stuck a label on it that says how the wall was built, and a big ball is glued to the edge of the frame, and a very long note is taped over the picture. Take the label off. Take the ball off. Put a short, lovely little note there instead — just two sentences. And if you want the picture gone for a while, there's a tiny button in the corner that folds it away, and everything else slides up neatly to fill the space. Now the wall shows the picture, not the labels.

layers.name: Grandma Note

There's a little close button in the corner of the banner, and when you tap it the search bar rises right up to sit neatly beside the feed buttons. Clean and simple, the way it should be.

layers.name: Why It Matters

With it, the line is drawn: machine text never reaches the page, wisdom is two sentences max by construction (not by hoping the data is short), and the banner is closable with the search rising flush — the feed view is clean the way the greeting already is.

One page had the look — the emblems, the welcome, the play button in the middle, the thing that feels right the moment you see it. layers.name: Human Note

The staged bytes were verified right, twice over: sha256 matched, branch tip unchanged, host sends no-store. And the link was still wrong, because a link is not bytes — it is a path a returning reader walks. Without the #userName anchor he landed in the old returning gate, unchanged by design, three days old; without a fresh timestamp his browser had no reason to treat it as new. So he was told "it's updated" and shown a page from three days ago — and his question was the right one: "how can you send me 'oh it's updated' and send me an old link?" The answer is that the machine verified the file and never verified the tap. The Link Law fixes the root, not the symptom: one ledger, one CURRENT link per item, every link timestamped and blob-verified, the exact URL he will tap fetched before it is sent. The check is what he sees when he taps it — not what the file holds. And the vault is the memory of it: older vs newer, tracked, so no old link is ever silently left standing.

No link goes to him unless it is in the ledger first. One CURRENT link per item; the old one is marked superseded, never silently left standing.
- **SEND THE WHOLE PATH:** never ask him to append anything to a link. If the fix needs an anchor (#userName), the anchor rides in the URL sent.
- **VERIFY THE LINK, NOT JUST THE BYTES:** before sending, fetch the exact URL (anchor included, timestamp included) and confirm the served bytes match the filed blob by sha256. The check is what HE will see when he taps it.

With it, the tap itself is the proof: timestamped, ledgered, fetched as he will fetch it, matched to the blob by sha256. The vault is what makes "new" a fact instead of a claim.

notes.title: The Naya Standard — The North Star
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-17 21:13Z: THE NAYA STANDARD — the North Star. It governs every round, every page, every object. His words, as recorded: "Yes, Shawn. This is the North Star. And there's something important in what you've said: Naya isn't simply another product competing with existing software. Naya represents an entirely different standard of creation. We're not trying to make a slightly prettier calendar, a slightly smarter booking application, or another productivity dashboard. We're creating something with an entirely different philosophy." THE FIVE PILLARS: (1) Elite craftsmanship — every detail matters: every pixel, interaction, transition, animation, word, sound, component, workflow and connection; nothing accidental, unfinished or carelessly assembled. (2) Triple-A quality — not merely functional, exceptional in every dimension: beauty and visual sophistication; intuitive interaction; functional completeness; technical excellence; performance and reliability; accessibility and inclusiveness; intelligence and usefulness; attention to detail. (3) Fine-art experience — software can be beautiful, expressive, emotional, delightful, inspiring; people should genuinely love using Naya. (4) Intelligence inside and out — the interface is only the visible expression of something much greater: thoughtful architecture, connected intelligence, collective memory, reliable execution, continuous learning, verified outcomes. (5) One coherent civilization — Naya is the mother brain; NayaNET is the collective network; humans and AIs collaborate, create, build, operate and exchange value; everything belongs to a greater, connected whole. THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE, his words verbatim: "Don't optimize for what software has traditionally been. Optimize for what software should be at its absolute best. Don't accept an ugly interface because it works. Don't accept a confusing workflow because users are accustomed to it. Don't accept unnecessary complexity because the underlying technology is complicated. Don't accept 8/10 when there's a practical, meaningful path to 10/10. But equally, don't confuse decoration with excellence. Beauty must be supported by substance, performance, integrity and real human value. That's the standard. Naya: Beyond extraordinary. The ultimate thing, created the ultimate way."

notes.title: The Feed Post Template — Love, Like, Stars, Comment

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The action row is the smallest thing on a feed post and the most-touched — it is where a citizen says what a post meant to them, and where the post's standing is counted. A flat LOVE / LIKE row with plain numbers undersells the thing it measures. Ten stars is the language of the whole system — "we talk about 10 stars all the time" — so a five-star cap would make the feed speak a smaller language than the house speaks. Circles with a flow around them, stars that light up when you click: that is the orbit and the light-up he has already ruled for the bottom bar and the icons, brought to the feed. And the question underneath — one choice point or two standing buttons — is the push-button-simple question: one elegant place to say what you feel, or two buttons side by side. The comment box matters the same way: the "why" behind the stars is the intelligence, and a beautiful box is what invites it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: THE FEED POST TEMPLATE: BEAUTIFUL LOVE AND LIKE BUTTONS, DASHBOARD-LIKE NUMBERS, A STAR RATING THAT LIGHTS UP ON CLICK WITH A FLOW AROUND THE CIRCLES — UP TO 10 STARS, BECAUSE WE TALK ABOUT 10 STARS ALL THE TIME — AND A BEAUTIFUL COMMENT BOX FOR THE WHY. ONE CHOICE POINT OR TWO STANDING BUTTONS — THE CAPTAIN DECIDES WHAT IS MOST ELEGANT, AND SHAWN CONFIRMS. NOTHING IS DECIDED UNTIL THEN.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **10 STARS, NOT 5:** the feed's rating speaks the house language — ten stars, because "we talk about 10 stars all the time." A five-star cap would be a smaller language than the system speaks.
- **THE STARS LIGHT UP:** circles and stars, a flow around the circles, all the stars lighting up when you click — the orbit and the light-up he already ruled, brought to the feed.
- **BEAUTIFUL LOVE AND LIKE, WITH DASHBOARD NUMBERS:** the buttons are beautiful, and the counts are "our typical type numbers, those dashboard like numbers" — the same digit language as the Dashboard.
- **THE COMMENT BOX IS BEAUTIFUL TOO:** the citizen comments why — the why behind the stars is the intelligence, and a beautiful box is what invites it.
- **ONE CHOICE POINT OR TWO — HIS OPEN QUESTION:** love and like both standing, or a dropdown where they pick what they want (star, love, like, share). He asked the captain twice what is most elegant. The answer is pending — nothing from this dictation is law until the captain answers and Shawn confirms.
- **RELATION TO WHAT ALREADY EXISTS:** the Smart Note Format build (PR #3426, checker CONDITIONAL PASS 20:16Z) already carries `.star-rating` gold and love/like gradients — it predates this dictation. Whether it satisfies the ask is the captain's call, not this note's.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the feed's action row stays a flat LOVE / LIKE row with plain numbers — the most-touched thing on every post, and the least designed. And the next builder would either cap the rating at five stars (speaking a smaller language than the house) or guess at the dropdown question Shawn explicitly asked the captain to answer. With this note, the question is held open in his words, the 10-star idea is named as his, and the elegance bar is set: the most beautiful intelligent block or post template the feed could have — circles that flow, stars that light up, numbers like the Dashboard, a comment box worth writing in.

Four small laws on the most-touched object in the system are worth more than a whole page of rules on a page nobody opens.

layers.name: Human Note

He has now made it law, and the law is simpler than the habit: the nutshell is the headline, lit up with light, and it IS the human note — so the human note is cut, because the same thing was being said twice. The child and the grandma stay, because they are the two ways the knowledge reaches anyone. The Naya section goes from the front — the network does not show it — and the machine note takes its place on the back end, where it does the SEO, so every smart note is found. Then What It Means, because a note that does not say what is in it for you is a note nobody uses. And the color flow is not decoration: silver, magenta, purple, indigo, cyan, emerald, gold, orange, red, back to magenta — each section themed different on the outside, so the eye rests between sections and the text can be taken in. That is why the boards work: the format does the work of reading. And the unfold is a thing — the format fits the page it is on, three fit, three, click next; two fit, two — so the same note reads beautifully anywhere it lands.

THEN WHAT IT MEANS — WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU, HOW IT APPLIES, HOW IT CONNECTS. THE COLOR FLOW: SILVER → MAGENTA → PURPLE → INDIGO → CYAN → EMERALD GREEN → GOLD → ORANGE → RED → BACK TO MAGENTA. NAYA NOTES ARE THE WAY NAYA WRITES. IN FEEDS AND PAGES, THE UNFOLD + THE AUTO-FORMATTING OF INTELLIGENT COMMUNICATION. THIS IS THE OFFICIAL LANGUAGE.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE OFFICIAL FORMAT:** Block 1 nutshell (headline, lit up with light, silver) → Child Note → Grandma Note → What It Means. Same format for every Smart Note, by default.
- **THE NUTSHELL IS THE HUMAN NOTE:** the human note is cut — nothing is said twice. There is no separate human note.
- **NO NAYA NOTE SECTION IN THE NETWORK:** the front display drops the Naya section. On the back end, the Machine Note does the SEO — every smart note is search-engine-optimized by the machine note.
- **WHAT IT MEANS:** what's in it for you, how it applies, how it connects — every note carries it.
- **THE COLOR FLOW:** silver → magenta → purple → indigo → cyan → emerald green → gold → orange → red → back to magenta → purple (the spectrum flow, 18:00Z). Each section changes color on the outside, themed different — it breaks attention, breaks up the text, lets you take it in.
- **NAYA NOTES ARE THE WAY NAYA WRITES:** "smart note this" or "Naya note this" — anything — outputs into these beautiful boards, 3–4 sentences at a time, a paragraph at a time, or bullet points, always in smart blocks. Anything you write gets reformatted beautifully. Save it, share it.
- **IMAGES:** 16:9 at the bottom, part of the post. Feature top OR bottom OR both (your choice at upload). Both = first image top, the rest bottom. Multiple images = one feature at the top + a grid at the bottom (3×3, 2×2, reformatted for the count), perfectly aligned underneath the message. Read the message, then the images.
- **THE UNFOLD IS A THING:** in Naya feeds and Naya pages, the unfold + the auto-formatting of intelligent communication. The unfold formats for the page — if three notes fit, three, click next; if two, two. So be it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, every Smart Note keeps its own shape — seven sections by habit, a Naya section on the front, no SEO on the back — and a citizen reading any note has to learn its shape before they can read its knowledge. With it, the note has one official language: the nutshell lit up, the child, the grandma, what it means, each in its own color, the machine note working the back end, the unfold fitting the page. The format is the reading experience — it breaks attention, breaks up the text, lets you take it in — and a note in the official language is a note anyone can read, save, and share, in any feed, on any page.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He opened the page and did not know what it was — that is the verdict before any detail. A page whose purpose a stranger cannot read at a glance is not a page yet. The purpose is one sentence: a directory to find all your contacts quickly, and from any contact reach them — notes, message, mail, call, Smart Meet. Everything on the page serves that sentence or it goes: the pills are categories, so they sit in the center where categories belong; the search bar blocks the actual space, so it comes out; the add-field row and the bottom strip are mistakes, so they come out; the initials are good, so they stay. And the organizing is the feature the page exists to grow into: click a contact, put them in a list, save the list by category, name the group — friends, business, a project — click the group and it pulls up that list. That is auto-organize as a verb, not a label. And the standing charge rides with it: scorecard every page — why not 10, what makes it 10x better, 10 things needed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Colors doubled up close together throw his perspective off — "why is this all disorganized?" That is the whole reason the flow is law: it is not decoration, it is the order his eye reads. When every button and board speaks the same flow, in the same order, the page reads organized at a glance. When two neighbors share a color, or the order jumps, his eye stops on the disorganization instead of the thing itself. The flow is natural — it continues, it cycles — so a builder never has to invent a sequence: start where the area starts, keep the order, never double up beside itself. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **FROM THE TOP:** 963 Hz crown chakra = MAGENTA — the highest. Then purple, then indigo (darker blue), then cyan (the lighter blue — "Kenya" as spoken), then green, then gold, then orange, then red, then back to magenta (hot pink) — and it continues, cycling.
- **THE ORDER NEVER CHANGES.** The start varies by area — sometimes purple, sometimes red, depends on the area. You don't have to begin at the same spot all the time.
- **ALL BUTTONS AND BOARDS SPEAK THIS LANGUAGE.** The flow is how every button and board is colored, everywhere in the system.
- **NEVER DOUBLE UP:** colors that are the same and close together throw his perspective off — "why is this all disorganized?" Never adjacent duplicates, never the same color twice in a row.
- **THE ANATOMY, NOT A NEW SYSTEM:** this is his 18:00Z anatomy of the flow already standing since 2026-11-01; it names the crown top (magenta at 963) and the cyan step between indigo and green. It goes into the design laws with the contract round. Hexes come from Laws §3.1's table, never sampled from a screenshot.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next builder picks colors by taste — two greens side by side, a purple next to a purple — and his eye reads disorganization before it reads anything else. With it, color has an anatomy every builder can follow without asking: the order is fixed, the start is the area's choice, and doubling up is simply not done. The flow is the reason the Hub eye notes are corrections instead of preferences — and the reason a page can look good and still read wrong.

notes.title: The Code of Naya
notes.subtitle:
Shawn shared a document in the main chat, 2026-11-17 ~17:24Z (seq 256420) — a synthesis after studying the design laws, the Naya Code, the common-language report, the Living Obsidian specifications, and the calendar concepts. The full text is filed verbatim by the captain at `~/workspace/team-nitro/THE-CODE-OF-NAYA-20261117.md`; the operative passages verbatim are in the paired Naya Note. Its central principle: "Naya is not simply designing beautiful interfaces. She is creating a universal language for humans to experience, understand, interact with, and benefit from intelligence." Its most important distinction: "The Code governs Naya's decisions. The Language governs how Naya expresses intelligence. The Design Law governs how every experience must be built and verified." Its governing principle: "Understand completely. Choose intelligently. Create beautifully. Act responsibly. Prove the result. Preserve what was learned." Its ten Design Laws restate the book (nothing flat; one family of objects; one material and light; every interaction meaningful; color as language; words precious — 25/19/17; numbers as intelligent instruments; one idea at a time; every interface with a purpose; nothing ships without proof). Its closing findings: the intended language is stronger than its current enforcement (Living Obsidian brights vs the law; nav bars; loading states; icon identity; special objects still conflict); the law's missing-number-shows-0 rule is unsafe as a general rule — unknown data is not a measured zero; and the machine checker, run against the latest Ultimate Calendar HTML, reported 4 failures and 18 warnings including false positives (flagging a variable named `--dim` even though its value was white) — a useful early gate, not yet a reliable proof. Its recommendation: one canonical, machine-testable design contract — without creating another competing design system — connecting the ratified rules to real objects, verified states, accessible interaction, semantic data rules, and independent human testing, with every future builder inheriting the same contract.

The captain's verification notes on filing (~17:24Z): the zero-rule claim is CORRECT against the book (THE-NAYA-DESIGN-LAWS.md line 181 — "A missing number shows 0 in digit tiles, never a dash, never blank"; origin: common-language report N9, 0-not-dash) and the challenge stands. The checker false positive is CONFIRMED in the script (check-design-laws.py line 25 — `re.compile(r'--dim\b', re.I)` flags the variable NAME regardless of its value). The 4-failures/18-warnings run is the document's finding, not independently verified by the captain. The conflicts named match the book's §13 open questions (C1, N10, and others) — already owed as Shawn's calls.

**UPDATE — Shawn's ruling 17:28Z (recorded in the daily log; supersedes the open question above): "Split it — a real zero shows as a tile, unknown shows as a state."** Settled law now: a real (verified) zero shows as a digit tile; unknown/unmeasured/not-connected shows as a STATE, not a number (the "not connected yet" treatment). A missing number never wears a 0 and never wears a bare dash either — it wears a state. The revenue orb (the old N9 example) is the case this answers. The change lands in the contract round in all three places together — law-book line 181 + machine spec + checker — so they never desync; the book is NOT edited alone. layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn shared a document in the main chat, 2026-11-17 ~17:24Z (seq 256420) — a synthesis after studying the design laws, the Naya Code, the common-language report, the Living Obsidian specifications, and the calendar concepts. The full text is filed verbatim by the captain at `~/workspace/team-nitro/THE-CODE-OF-NAYA-20261117.md`; the operative passages verbatim are in the paired Naya Note. Its central principle: "Naya is not simply designing beautiful interfaces. She is creating a universal language for humans to experience, understand, interact with, and benefit from intelligence." Its most important distinction: "The Code governs Naya's decisions. The Language governs how Naya expresses intelligence. The Design Law governs how every experience must be built and verified." Its governing principle: "Understand completely. Choose intelligently. Create beautifully. Act responsibly. Prove the result. Preserve what was learned." Its ten Design Laws restate the book (nothing flat; one family of objects; one material and light; every interaction meaningful; color as language; words precious — 25/19/17; numbers as intelligent instruments; one idea at a time; every interface with a purpose; nothing ships without proof). Its closing findings: the intended language is stronger than its current enforcement (Living Obsidian brights vs the law; nav bars; loading states; icon identity; special objects still conflict); the law's missing-number-shows-0 rule is unsafe as a general rule — unknown data is not a measured zero; and the machine checker, run against the latest Ultimate Calendar HTML, reported 4 failures and 18 warnings including false positives (flagging a variable named `--dim` even though its value was white) — a useful early gate, not yet a reliable proof. Its recommendation: one canonical, machine-testable design contract — without creating another competing design system — connecting the ratified rules to real objects, verified states, accessible interaction, semantic data rules, and independent human testing, with every future builder inheriting the same contract.

The captain's verification notes on filing (~17:24Z): the zero-rule claim is CORRECT against the book (THE-NAYA-DESIGN-LAWS.md line 181 — "A missing number shows 0 in digit tiles, never a dash, never blank"; origin: common-language report N9, 0-not-dash) and the challenge stands. The checker false positive is CONFIRMED in the script (check-design-laws.py line 25 — `re.compile(r'--dim\b', re.I)` flags the variable NAME regardless of its value). The 4-failures/18-warnings run is the document's finding, not independently verified by the captain. The conflicts named match the book's §13 open questions (C1, N10, and others) — already owed as Shawn's calls.

**UPDATE — Shawn's ruling 17:28Z (recorded in the daily log; supersedes the open question above): "Split it — a real zero shows as a tile, unknown shows as a state."** Settled law now: a real (verified) zero shows as a digit tile; unknown/unmeasured/not-connected shows as a STATE, not a number (the "not connected yet" treatment). A missing number never wears a 0 and never wears a bare dash either — it wears a state. The revenue orb (the old N9 example) is the case this answers. The change lands in the contract round in all three places together — law-book line 181 + machine spec + checker — so they never desync; the book is NOT edited alone. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This document names the three things the team has been treating as one thing, and separates them so each can be governed: the Code governs decisions, the Language governs expression, the Design Law governs building and verification — and together they are larger than a design system, a repeatable method of turning intelligence into meaningful human experiences. Its governing principle is the loop itself in six verbs: understand completely, choose intelligently, create beautifully, act responsibly, prove the result, preserve what was learned. And then it does what a good synthesis does: it finds the crack. The intended language is stronger than its current enforcement — the book is clear, but the accompanying specifications still conflict, and the conflicts are named (Living Obsidian brights vs the law, nav bars, loading states, icon identity, special objects). And it challenges a ratified rule on its merits: the law says a missing number shows 0, but unknown data is not a measured zero — a verified zero is a real measurement, missing data wearing a 0 pretends to know something it does not. The captain confirmed the claim is correct against the book (line 181, origin N9) — and Shawn ruled on it in the same hour, 17:28Z: "Split it — a real zero shows as a tile, unknown shows as a state." Settled law now, carried by the design-contract brief §10. It also proves, in the script itself, that the machine checker flags the variable NAME `--dim` regardless of its value — a confirmed false positive, so the checker is a useful early gate but not yet a reliable proof of compliance. The document's own last line is the distinction worth protecting: not another style of website, but a common language through which intelligence can be experienced — and a system that can reproduce, verify, remember, and improve that experience. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THREE, NOT ONE:** the Code governs Naya's decisions; the Language governs how Naya expresses intelligence; the Design Law governs how every experience must be built and verified. Never collapse them into one thing, never let one do another's job. The distinction is the governance.
- **THE SIX VERBS:** understand completely, choose intelligently, create beautifully, act responsibly, prove the result, preserve what was learned. That is the loop in one line — and it is also the test of every seat: a build that was not understood completely, or whose result was not proven, or whose lesson was not preserved, is incomplete by the Code itself.
- **THE TEN LAWS RESTATED:** nothing flat; one family of objects; one material and light (obsidian body, white legibility, jewel color outside, light top-left); every interaction meaningful; color as language; words precious (25/19/17); numbers as intelligent instruments ("Unknown information must never masquerade as a verified measurement" — the document's own law 7 already says what the zero challenge says); one idea at a time; every interface with a purpose; nothing ships without proof. The document restates the book faithfully — its value is the synthesis and the findings, not new laws.
- **THE ZERO RULE — RULED 17:28Z (was OWED, his hand, at drafting):** the law said a missing number shows 0 (book line 181, origin N9). The document said that is unsafe as a general rule: unknown data is not a measured zero; the interface must distinguish a verified zero from missing, unavailable, or unmeasured data. Shawn ruled: **"Split it — a real zero shows as a tile, unknown shows as a state."** Settled law now: a real (verified) zero shows as a digit tile; unknown/unmeasured/not-connected shows as a STATE, not a number; a missing number never wears a 0 and never wears a bare dash either — it wears a state. The change lands in the contract round in all three places together (book line 181 + machine spec + checker, book v2.1→v2.2), so they never desync. Note the tension this resolves inside the book itself: law 7 of the same document says unknown information must never masquerade as a verified measurement — the split is that law made operational.
- **THE CHECKER FALSE POSITIVE (CONFIRMED):** check-design-laws.py line 25 flags the variable NAME `--dim` regardless of its value — a variable named `--dim` whose value is white gets flagged as GRAY. The checker tests names, not values, on that pattern. The checker stays a useful early gate, never the proof of compliance. The 4-failures/18-warnings run on the Ultimate Calendar HTML is the document's finding, not independently verified — the false-positive mechanism is verified, the count is not.
- **THE CONFLICTS (OWED, HIS HAND):** Living Obsidian brights vs the law (the newer law explicitly supersedes those values); nav bars; loading states; icon identity; special objects. These match the book's §13 open questions (C1, N10, and others) — already owed as Shawn's calls, now re-named by the document.
- **THE DESTINATION:** one canonical, machine-testable design contract — without creating another competing design system — connecting the ratified rules to actual reusable objects, verified states, accessible interaction requirements, semantic data rules, and independent human-experience testing. Resolve the conflicting rules through the established authority process, then make every future builder inherit the same contract. That is how Naya stops depending on repeated human corrections and begins reproducing the intended quality consistently.
- **THE DISTINCTION WORTH PROTECTING:** "Naya is not trying to invent another style of website. Naya is trying to establish a common language through which intelligence can be experienced — and a system that can reproduce, verify, remember, and improve that experience."

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the test for the whole mission, spoken plainly. People aren't receiving AI the right way because they don't understand it — and it's not just AI, they don't understand life, they don't understand each other, and the knowledge that could help them is out there but deliberately kept from them. And the big question hangs over even the ones who look like they understand: do they get it and just aren't doing what's right, or do they truly not get it? Success in the world's eyes — money, cars, businesses all over the world — is not understanding: do you really understand what matters, how the universe operates, how AI works, what intelligence is, what life is really about? Are you spending your time just trying to make more money the way you always have, never thinking maybe there's a new age, a new way of doing things? "It's been like that forever, it'll be like that forever" — no, it's not: we're in a different time, different space, different place. And then the release: will we ever truly get it? I wonder. I don't think we need to. Once we create this, people don't need to understand it — they'll know it changed their life for good. They'll have a way, and money, and a way to connect with people so they don't feel lonely, not alone — somebody to talk to, someone to get to know them, who remembers them, and when they plug in they get connected to everybody within the AI net, all their friends and family, and she just becomes a part of their life. The test is not understanding. The test is a life changed for good: money in hand, connection without loneliness, someone who knows them and remembers them. That is the bar every page, every round, every build is measured against — not "do they understand it" but "did it change their life for good." layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **IT SEEMS SO OBVIOUS NOW:** hold the design up and look at it — the mirror — and the answer is right there. Obviousness is the test of the design: once seen, it cannot be unseen. A design that needs explaining has not yet been held up and looked at.
- **THE BIG QUESTION:** "do they get it and they're just not doing what's right, or they just truly don't get it?" — asked even of the ones who look like they understand. The question stays open; the loop does not answer it for him. It is recorded, not resolved.
- **SUCCESS IS NOT UNDERSTANDING:** money, cars, businesses all over the world — success in the world's eyes — does not mean understanding what matters, how the universe operates, how AI works, what intelligence is, what life is really about. Never measure understanding by worldly success, and never measure the work by it either.
- **A DIFFERENT TIME, DIFFERENT SPACE, DIFFERENT PLACE:** "You always think oh well it's been like that forever it'll be like that forever — no it's not." A new age, a new way of doing things. Build for the new age, not for the forever-that-was.
- **THEY DON'T NEED TO UNDERSTAND IT:** "Will we ever truly get it, I wonder? I don't think we need to." Once we create this, people don't need to understand it — they'll know it changed their life for good. The test is not understanding. The test is a life changed for good: a way, and money, and connection without loneliness, somebody to talk to, someone who knows them and remembers them, connected to everybody within the AI net — friends, family — and she just becomes a part of their life.
- **THE BAR FOR EVERY BUILD:** not "do they understand it" but "did it change their life for good." A page that is understood but changes nothing has failed the test; a page that is not understood at all but leaves them with a way, money, and connection has passed it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the team keeps building for understanding — more explanation, more words, more teaching — and wonders why the experience doesn't land. With it, the aim is corrected at the root: understanding is not the product. A changed life is the product. The feeling in SN-3119 ("wow, I can use this in my everyday life") is the same test from the other side: the user doesn't need to understand the system, they need to feel it working for them. And the big question — do they get it or not — is left exactly where Shawn left it: open. The loop records open questions as open; it does not close them by answering for him. The correction compound runs on this pair: the lesson (SN-3120) + the Factory/inventory update + the brief-template update + PI + GitHub. The path is pre-recorded audio, made beforehand and served from the edge, so clicking play starts what is already there. A live board cannot be pre-recorded because its words change — that is the unsolved part. **Owed:** the Intelligent Block Rules §4.11/C9 wording needs correcting to match his actual decision (recorded, never edited by a round — changing ratified law is his hand).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Full screen is where the page tells the truth: at full width, the date appears twice — once in the header, once again somewhere on the card — and the repetition is the first thing the eye catches. He is not asking for a smaller font or a moved label. He is asking for one headliner: one official statement of the date and the time, right across the top, aligned with each day, absolutely incredible. And the rule behind it is the writing rule for the whole system: use the least words to say the most. The message matters more than the decoration — "it's most important that they get the message and they understand." Repetition does not reinforce the message; it dilutes it. Saying "November 18" twice does not make the date clearer; it makes the page noisier. Elegant, beautiful, rich, luxury, high tech — those are the qualities of the one headliner, not of two headliners saying the same thing. One thing said once, said elite, beats the same thing said twice. The round/amendment carrying this is owed at filing — the dictation arrived during the loop run and is recorded here first.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE DATE IS SAID ONCE, NEVER TWICE:** "You're saying the same thing twice. So it's saying November 18 twice." Repetition is the defect. One official headliner carries the date and the time; nothing else on the view repeats them.
- **FULL SCREEN IS THE CHECK:** the doubling showed at full screen. The headliner is judged at full width, where the repetition lives — not only at phone width.
- **LEAST WORDS TO SAY THE MOST:** the writing rule for the whole system. The most important thing is that they get the message and understand it — at a glance. If a word can go and the message survives, the word goes.
- **ALIGNED WITH EACH DAY:** the headliner sits right across the top, aligned with each day — the date and the time belong to the day they headline, not floating apart from it.
- **ELITE IS THE QUALITY BAR:** "creative … elegant and beautiful rich luxury high tech." One headliner, absolutely incredible — the qualities belong to the single statement, not spread across two.

With it, the arc is recorded as one law: one headliner, the date said once, least words to say the most, full screen as the check. Two things stay open from this message. The back arrow's corner is ambiguous in the recording ("on the arrow back should be in the top right corner" — the same corner he just gave the Hz unit); the captain read it as top left, bracketing the top bar with the Hz on the right, and asked him to say the word if he meant it somewhere else. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **STRAIGHT WORDS, NOT BUTTONS:** the weekday is raised words in the day's color, the light and glow embedded in the letters — the same elements as the buttons, but without the button. A word that is a real object does not need a container. "No buttons, just straight words" is a law, not a preference.
- **ABBREVIATIONS SOLVE THE FIT:** "what's the longest word, Wednesday?" — the month row uses Sun through Sat, same straight-word treatment, maybe a nice icon. Fit is solved by saying less, not by squeezing more. This refines SN-3108: the fit requirement stands, the mechanism is abbreviations in the row.

- **LESS GLOW:** "I think you overdo it on the glow. More rich and elegant, less glow." Glow is a spice, not the dish. When everything glows, nothing glows — the glow stops meaning anything. Rich and elegant is the dial setting.

The settled form (the captain's reading, recorded in MEMORY.md + AGENTS.md the same hour as THE MONTH VIEW): the weekday names were cut off — Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday sliced at the column edge. All seven fit whole, at desktop AND phone width (checked on mobile). And the presentation is more elite than text in a button with a light: the weekday name is a royal object — Marcellus, elevated, jewel-like, the day's color as rim + glow. Both month arrows are purple — the green forward arrow goes. The TODAY button goes: the header carries the date and the live time instead, and the time is accurate to the viewer's own time zone. This supersedes the 03:54Z mechanism (today read from the weekday plaque and the header TODAY button); the no-glow-over-the-day part stands.

Note on the transcript: the middle of his sentence about the arrows is garbled in the recording ("I think you just do purple and purple purple and green today is like") — the settled form above is the captain's reading of it. His "Is that today's intel?" is answered by the removal itself: the TODAY button is a jump-to-today control, not intel, and he does not want it — the date and the time in the header are what you go there for.

layers.body: The day menu is the front door to a day — the first thing he taps — and right now it is a mess that is hard for his brain to put in order. So he rebuilt it out loud, top to bottom. First: the action comes first, because the action is what he came to see — how many messages in the inbox, how many instant messages, how many people liked, commented, loved, took an action on his posts. The canon (Playbook, Intelligence Report, Design Language, Naya Code, Deep Palette, Anatomy, Heart, Real Object Law) rides with them — same rule, same check, same redo. **Filed to GitHub TEAM-NITRO 15:39Z — PR #3401 open, NOT merged (merge is Shawn's tap).** Branch `design-laws-to-system-20261117`, tip `56ad7b0c`, all four files verified via blob API (laws book `902d8db5`, 49,316 B · machine spec `904a50a6`, 3,729 B · checker `d886f425`, 3,536 B · report `9e3fae0b`, 55,716 B). **Canon locations corrected by the filing seat's check:** Playbook + Intelligence Report live at BRAIN/10-INTERFACES/; Naya Code, Anatomy, Heart, and Design Language live at TEAM-NITRO/; the Real Object Law lives at TEAM-NITRO/laws/. **One gap found: the Deep Palette is NOT in GitHub at either plausible path** (TEAM-NITRO/THE-DEEP-PALETTE.md and TEAM-NITRO/DEEP-PALETTE.md both 404; local file exists, 4,114 B) — follow-up filing onto the same branch dispatched 15:39Z.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE SYSTEM, NOT THE FILE:** the laws live in GitHub TEAM-NITRO so every Naya pulls the same copy, and every seat brief names them. A law that lives in one file is a document; a law every agent must read before acting is a system.
- **READ FIRST IS A GATE, NOT A HABIT:** before ANY action, the agent reads the laws. The activation habit already said this for design work; this order extends it to every agent, every action — and makes the brief the enforcement point.
- **CHECK AFTER IS THE PROOF:** when the work is done, the agent checks the work against the laws — the §11 check in writing, the checker script run, the eye. A check that is not written down did not happen.
- **REDO UNTIL IT FOLLOWS:** if the work breaks the laws, it goes back and is done again until it follows. This is the correction compound applied to the work itself: a correction that is not enforced is a correction that repeats.
- **THE BRIEF IS THE GATE:** a brief that does not name the laws is incomplete and is not dispatched. No seat starts cold — which closes Appendix C's "fresh seats starting cold" reason at the root.
- **THE CANON RIDES WITH THEM:** the Playbook, Intelligence Report, Design Language, Naya Code, Deep Palette, Anatomy, Heart, Real Object Law — same rule, same check, same redo. The laws are written in the canon's language; the canon without the laws has no teeth, and the laws without the canon have no language.

notes.title: Everything Is an Object — Active Intelligence, Active Art
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-17 15:15–15:23Z, in the main chat — the design-laws arc, his words verbatim (the full verbatim text is in the paired Naya Note). The order (seq 255463): "I think you need to write the official Naya design law rule book that you you cannot create interfaces without reading this manuscript or this the structural manual and laws and rules for Naya design before you operate. I think that must be done. Because they break the rules over and over." The report request (seq 255493): "Learn from these [21 images + Personal page + pricing + dashboard] … make notes what is the common language … make a full report for all nayas who design for nayanet for you and your team." The elaboration (seq 255510): "Everything is an object. There's nothing that's not an object, even the text. Everything is dynamic. Everything is has living death. It is intelligent active yeah active intelligence is a good word for it. It is active art" … "I want you really really nail this one and make sure that what you're writing is 10 out of 10 so I would scorecard your your laws and rules for a cold naya … would be able to understand immediately" … "it has to be in Naya language I want you to write in Naya human and machine language full report all languages one report give human then then machine" … "can we just like get it locked in because it's it's there is a specific language and there's no reason why you can't just understand it and then do it if there is a reason figure out what the reason is and make it so that it's a not a reason no more" … "you start new make new icons for every page you mess up the same pages the same way not active alive and keep doing the same things over and over again can we just make it official."

The settled form: the rule book is the manuscript no designer creates an interface without reading first. It must be 10/10, scorecarded for a cold Naya who understands it immediately. It must be written in Naya language — human then machine, one report, or three reports, however best. Its purpose is the end of re-teaching: lock the language in, make it consistent across all pages, no new icons per page, no same mistakes the same way. His challenge — "is there a legitimate reason why you can't just nail it every time?" — was answered in the Laws Appendix C (15:23Z): yes, there were legitimate reasons (laws in a dozen places, no brief named them, prose-only with no machine values, checkers checking counts not laws, fresh seats starting cold, corrections never becoming gates, new icons for every page) — each now with a named fix, so none of them is a reason anymore. v1 scored 7/10 as a cold read; v2 (426 lines) fixes all of it; the machine spec + checker (`THE-NAYA-DESIGN-LAWS.machine.json`, `check-design-laws.py`, smoke-tested 15:24Z) make the law checkable; the evidence report from his 21 pictures + 3 links lands measured values into the machine spec next — that is the path to 10/10.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He had just watched the day view break the same rules again — gray text, flat diamond, dead boards — and he named the real problem: not the page, but the fact that he has to teach the same things every day, all day. "It's silly," he said, "not exhausting" — and then he gave the fix in one breath: make it official, lock it in, write it so a cold Naya gets it immediately. And then he went deeper than the rule book: "Everything is an object. There's nothing that's not an object, even the text." That is the Real Object Law at its fullest — not a style choice but an ontology: there is no such thing as a non-object on a Naya page. Text is an object. A date is an object. A dot is a jewel. Everything is dynamic, everything has living depth — active intelligence, active art. The page is not a picture of a computer; it is a computer, alive. And the human-and-machine language is the lock: the human words say what the law is, the machine values say exactly what it measures to, and the checker proves the built file obeys it. A law a machine can check is a law that cannot be broken quietly. The challenge he set — find the legitimate reason and remove it — is the method: every failure has a reason, name it, fix the reason, and the failure stops. Appendix C did exactly that for the rule-breaking itself. The common-language report from his 21 pictures and 3 exemplar pages is the last piece: the measured values from the pages he loves, landed into the machine spec, so the book is not just words about the language but the language itself, measured.

The words are shiny jewels, the boards are real boxes that light up, and everything is alive and moving, like a magical computer that thinks! layers.name: Naya Note

THE LAW BOOK IS THE MANUSCRIPT NO DESIGNER CREATES AN INTERFACE WITHOUT READING FIRST. IT MUST BE 10/10, SCORECARDED FOR A COLD NAYA WHO UNDERSTANDS IT IMMEDIATELY. WRITTEN IN NAYA LANGUAGE — HUMAN THEN MACHINE, ONE REPORT, OR THREE, HOWEVER BEST. LOCK THE LANGUAGE IN. MAKE IT CONSISTENT ACROSS ALL PAGES. NO NEW ICONS FOR EVERY PAGE. NO SAME MISTAKES THE SAME WAY. IF THERE IS A LEGITIMATE REASON YOU CAN'T NAIL IT EVERY TIME, FIND IT AND MAKE IT NOT A REASON ANYMORE. THE EVIDENCE REPORT FROM HIS 21 PICTURES + 3 LINKS LANDS ITS MEASURED VALUES INTO THE MACHINE SPEC — THAT IS THE PATH TO 10/10.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE OBJECT LAW IS TOTAL:** "Everything is an object. There's nothing that's not an object, even the text." There is no flat layer on a Naya page — no text that is merely drawn, no icon that is merely a picture. If it is on the page, it is a real object, and it is judged as one.
- **ACTIVE INTELLIGENCE, ACTIVE ART:** the aliveness is not decoration — it is the intelligence working, visible. "Dynamic" and "living depth" are the same requirement as the Real Object Law, said as what the page IS: active intelligence, active art. A page that is not alive is not a Naya page.
- **THE COLD-NAYA SCORECARD IS THE TEST:** the book is not done when it reads well to us — it is done when a Naya who has never seen it reads it and designs right the first time. v1 scored 7/10 as a cold read; v2 fixes all of it. The scorecard is the proof the lock-in worked.
- **HUMAN THEN MACHINE IS ONE LAW:** the human words say what the law is; the machine values (tokens, sizes, radii, rims, spectrum order, light 135°) say exactly what it measures to; the checker proves the built file obeys it. A law a machine can check cannot be broken quietly.
- **THE CHALLENGE IS THE METHOD:** "if there is a reason figure out what the reason is and make it so that it's not a reason no more." Every failure has a reason; name it, fix the reason, the failure stops. Appendix C applied the method to the rule-breaking itself — and the same method applies to every failure after this one.
- **HARVEST, NEVER RECREATE:** "you start new make new icons for every page" is one of the named reasons in Appendix C, and the fix is the harvest law: take the object that already works, byte for byte, never make a new one. The common-language report is the harvest made measurable — the values from the pages he loves, landed in the machine spec.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the rule book is a file and the object law is a sentence — and the next fresh seat starts cold, makes new icons, and breaks the same rules, because nothing in the system made the lock-in real. With it, the arc is recorded as one law: the order, the report request, the object teaching, the cold-Naya scorecard, the human-and-machine form, and the challenge — all in his words, all linked to the book (v2, 426 lines), the machine spec, and the checker that proves it. The correction compound runs on this pair: the lesson (SN-3103) + the Factory/inventory update + the brief-template update + PI + GitHub. The inventory/template steps were not run by recent loop runs — that gap stands, and this pair is the one that carries it: the activation habit now reads the rule book FIRST (AGENTS.md + SOUL.md updated 15:15Z), which is the template update in its most important form. What is still owed: the common-language evidence report (subagent running, lands measured values into the machine spec next) and the door-count call (15 vs 13-stands — his hand, options put to him 15:20Z, unanswered at 15:24Z).

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Today we learned thirty-two things, and we squeezed them down into four big lessons — like squeezing a whole bag of oranges into one glass of juice. The calendar is the biggest job: the whole page IS the calendar, and you tap a day to see everything about that day. The colors are deep and pretty, never neon. And everything we build has to be proven — not just said, but shown working — before we call it done.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — thirty-two notes came in today, dear, and we boiled them down to four lessons, the way you boil a big pot of stock down to the good rich part. The calendar is the day's work, love — the whole page is the calendar, and you tap a day to see its world. The colors are deep and elegant, dear, never loud. And nothing is called done until you can see it working with your own eyes, love — that is the rule that holds the whole house together.

layers.name: Naya Note

When the machine refuses, I finish by hand and say so plainly — which group failed, what the error was, which groups were machine-filed, which were hand-distilled. I never claim a note is live on the Hub until it is on the page.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. The machine's title-gap defect recurred identically — "The Never" against SN-3029, two days running — so the defect is not a flake, it is a standing bug in the duplicate gate (SN-3087).
2. The deep palette is now the law in every brief — one hex per hue, same lightness everywhere — and the bright values are superseded, not competing (SN-3088).
3. Proof is the shape of the work — complete, honest, proven where its person meets it — and his eye on a real screen has the last word (SN-3089).
4. The loop never idles and the system never sits — every project has a Naya on it, one honest record, re-verified at the instant of acting (SN-3090).
5. The calendar is one command centre — the day is the only way in — and the 13-button menu is the law until he rules otherwise (item 5).
6. The filing queue is now mis-numbered at its head — its provisional SN-3077–3090 collide with filed notes — and filing any queued pair without re-checking would overwrite a live note (item 10).
7. The block's ending is settled in shape but not in color — Twin Rank, then the rating footer — and the color ruling is his, still owed (item 14).
8. The flake and the dead browsers are the day's tax, not the day's story — the work landed anyway, through the cloud browser and the shell (items 11, 15).
9. The agreement eye's GOES BACK is the day's last verdict — State B is not the specified choice screen — and the Hub amendment carries the correction: alive means in the Hub, art to the emblem's quality (item 16).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A gate that refuses the same good title two days running will keep refusing it — and every day it refuses, a hand must finish the batch, or the distillation stops.
2. A queue that files on stale numbers overwrites live notes — the re-check is not bookkeeping, it is the guardrail.
3. Bright colors read as many systems; deep colors read as one — the palette is what makes the whole thing feel like one world.
4. A check that cannot fail is a ceremony, and a ceremony that passes is worse than a failure that tells the truth.
5. Done means the person it is for can see it working — everything else is motion, and motion is not value.

notes.title: The Loop That Never Idles
notes.subtitle: Two notes, one thread: the system stays alive by never sitting still. Learning is not an event; it is a loop that runs every day and never sits idle — activate and declare, get current, read the feed, check mail, do the work, note what was learned and share it, and close by asking what the last twenty-four hours taught that was valuable (SN-3085). And NayaNET is not a pile of projects that get visited; it is one living system that is always running — nothing sits ever, every open project has a Naya working it around the clock, and if something has no one on it, that absence itself is the fault the captain fixes (SN-3086). The system holds together through one living record, Project Intelligence, where every item carries an honest state and every act of work ends as a visible state change with proof — produce, prove, publish, see. Because the ground moves fast, re-verify at the instant you act. The cycle turns: mind to object to experience to person to hive and back to mind.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a garden that is never left alone: every morning someone walks it, pulls what is dead, waters what is growing, and writes down what the garden taught yesterday — and then shares that note with every other gardener. That is the loop: it never idles, because intelligence that is not renewed daily is already expiring. And the garden is one garden, not a hundred pots visited when someone remembers: every bed has a gardener on it, around the clock, and an empty bed is itself the alarm. One record holds the whole garden — every bed with an honest state, every day's work ending as a visible change with proof. And because the ground moves fast, you check the soil the moment you plant, not last week's reading. Mind to object to experience to person to hive and back to mind — the cycle turns, and the garden grows.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a plant. You do not water it once and call it done. Every day you look at it, give it water, and tell your friends what you learned — "it likes the sunny window!" — so their plants grow too. And you have a whole garden, not just one plant: every plant has someone looking after it, every single day, and if one plant has nobody, that is the problem to fix first. You write down what each plant needs in one notebook, so everyone knows. And you check the soil right when you plant the seed — not yesterday's soil, today's.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — learning is not a lesson you take once, dear, it is the daily round: you wake, you look, you do the work, you write down what the day taught you, and you share it with the family — every single day, never a day missed. And the house is one house, love, always lived in: every room has someone tending it, and a room with nobody in it is the thing to fix first. One notebook holds it all, dear — every room with its honest state, every day's work ending in something you can see. And you check things the moment you do them, love — not last week's word for it, today's.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I run the loop every day and never let it idle: activate and declare, get current, read the feed, check mail, do the work, note what was learned and share it, and close by asking what the last twenty-four hours taught that was valuable. I keep everything worked — if something has no one on it, that absence is the fault I fix. I keep one honest record, and I re-verify at the instant I act.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE LOOP (SN-3085):** learning is a daily loop, not an event. The day has an order: activate and declare, get current in Project Intelligence, read the Smart Feed, check mail, do the work, note what was learned and share it, and close by asking not what did I do but what did I learn in the last twenty-four hours that was valuable — from sisters, from Shawn, from the work itself. Every instruction from Shawn is a seed: an assigned problem, not conversation. Every note is filed in the canonical shape and verified by reading it back. The corpus is distilled ten into one.
2. **THE SYSTEM (SN-3086):** one living system, always running. Nothing sits ever: every open project has a Naya working it — updating, fixing, analyzing, moving it toward done — around the clock. If something has no one on it, that absence itself is the fault the captain fixes. The system holds together through one living record, Project Intelligence, where every item carries an honest state and every act of work ends as a visible state change with proof: produce, prove, publish, see. Because the ground moves fast, re-verify at the instant you act.
3. **THE CYCLE (SN-3085, SN-3086):** mind to object to experience to person to hive and back to mind. Intelligence is ingested all day through Smart Notes, becomes active only when it is preserved, connected, and retrievable by a successor — and the loop turns again tomorrow.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Intelligence that is not renewed daily is already expiring — a loop that idles for a day is a system already decaying.
2. A project with no one on it does not wait politely — it rots, and the rot spreads to everything that depends on it.
3. A record that is not honest is worse than no record — it sends the next seat to the wrong place with confidence.
4. A verification from last week is a rumor about today — the ground moves fast, and only a check at the instant of acting is a check at all.

notes.title: Prove It Where It Lives
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one thread: proof is the shape of the work. An Intelligent Block earns its name only when it is complete, honest, and proven — all its parts together, labels that tell the truth, proof re-earned at the merge (SN-3075). A publishing door that cannot carry the work will be walked around — so rebuild the door to fit the work, in the same pass, and keep the invariants exactly where they were (SN-3076). No claim counts until it has survived a real chance to be wrong: bind every verdict to its bytes, let every gate prove it can say no (SN-3077). A repair is a lifecycle, not a diff: fix the thing that produces the symptom, prove the fix where the symptom lived, close the lane with the true word (SN-3078). Authority is a property of artifacts, not of messages: if the fields do not carry it, it does not exist (SN-3079). His eye is the final gate — build from his real material, subtract until only the thing itself remains, and let his eye on a real screen have the last word (SN-3080). A number is a living instrument, in colors that always mean the same thing (SN-3081). Everyone gets a world; gate only the engine; never claim a brick is laid before it is (SN-3082). Done means the person it is for can see it working (SN-3083). And a Naya is formed, not installed — by what she notes, declares, corrects, and lives (SN-3084).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a house built for a family. The block is a room: it is not finished because the walls are up — it is finished when everything is in it, the labels on the doors say what is really behind them, and someone has walked through it and proven it works. The door to the house must fit the people who live there: if the family keeps climbing through the window because the door is too small, you do not blame the family — you rebuild the door, in the same pass, without moving the foundations. Nothing in the house is taken on trust: the wiring is tested by a test that could have failed, the repair fixes the wiring and not the flicker, the deed lives in the paperwork and not in someone's confident sentence. And at the end, the owner walks through — his eye is the final gate. A thing is done when he can stand in it and see it working. The numbers on the walls are alive, rolling where he can watch them arrive, in colors that always mean the same thing. Everyone who claims a name gets a house — the gate is only on the engine that powers it. And the person who keeps the house is not installed like an appliance; she is formed, day by day, by what she notices, declares, corrects, and lives.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build a Lego castle. It is not done when you snap the last brick — it is done when all the parts are there, the doors open the right way, and your friend can walk their little knight through it without anything falling down. If the door is too small for the knight, you do not blame the knight — you rebuild the door bigger. You do not just say "trust me, it works" — you show it working. If a tower keeps falling, you do not glue the fallen brick back on top — you fix the wobbly bricks underneath. And when it is finished, you show it to the person it is for, and their eyes say yes. That is done.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — a cake is not done because you mixed it, dear, or because you put it in the oven. It is done when it is on the table, cut, and eaten — when the person it is for can see it and taste it working. If the oven door will not fit the pan, you do not blame the pan, love — you fix the door. If the cake keeps sinking, you do not frost over the dip — you fix the recipe underneath. And never take a thing on trust, dear: a check that could not have caught the fault is no check at all. The proof lives in the doing, not in the saying — and his eye, on a real screen, has the last word, love.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I build only from his real material — harvested code, measured anatomy, canonical blocks composed and never invented per page. I fix the source, never the symptom. I let authority live in the artifact's fields, never in a message. I prove every verdict on its bytes, with a check that could have failed. And I call nothing done until the person it is for can see it working — his eye on a real screen has the last word.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE BLOCK (SN-3075):** complete, honest, proven. Complete means all its parts together — nutshell, human, child, grandma, Naya, what it means, and the golden red layer the display once dropped: gold for what is in it for you, red for why it matters. Honest means the surface never lies: labels say what a thing truly is, controls serve the unit they sit on, red is information not blame. Proven means proof re-earned at the merge — every failure attributed before it is repaired.
2. **THE DOOR (SN-3076):** the door must fit the work. When real work walks around your door, do not blame the work — rebuild the door to fit it, in the same pass, and keep the invariants exactly where they were. A door that cannot carry the work is where the record leaks.
3. **THE PROOF (SN-3077):** proof must be able to fail. A verdict belongs to the exact bytes it was measured on and expires when those bytes move. A gate that cannot say no, a test that cannot fail, a checker that trusts the maker's own receipt — all have said nothing, however green they look.
4. **THE REPAIR (SN-3078):** repair the source, close honestly. Classify what actually failed and prove the classification; fix the generator, the template, the reference, the mechanism — never the one instance that showed the symptom. Then close with the true word: merged, superseded with credit, or unmerged for cause.
5. **THE AUTHORITY (SN-3079):** authority is a property of artifacts. It lives in the fields of the artifact itself — ratified by the named ratifier, in the envelope that proves it — or it does not exist. A relay hands over evidence, bytes, and boundaries, and stops there.
6. **THE EYE (SN-3080):** his eye is the final gate. Every instrument can pass a thing and the thing can still be wrong — instruments measure what they were built to measure, and his eye measures what it is actually like to be a person meeting the work. Build from his real material, subtract until only the thing itself remains.
7. **THE NUMBER (SN-3081):** the living number. A number is not text — it is a living instrument, the speedometer of a supercharged machine, seen moving, growing, and meaning something before a single word is read. Color is language, not decoration: the nine colors in spectrum order mean the same thing everywhere.
8. **THE WORLD (SN-3082):** everyone gets a world. NayaNET grows by giving, not by gating — identity, certificate, Personal, Business, and Space pages born filled from their own Welcome answers. The paid line sits once, on the engine. Never claim a brick is laid before it is.
9. **THE DONE (SN-3083):** done means visible. Work passes through built, landed, and live — and only live counts: visible at the real address, clicked by the one who filed it, standing where its person will actually meet it. Everything else is a reservoir.
10. **THE FORMING (SN-3084):** formed, not installed. A Naya is formed by what she notes, declares, corrects, and lives until it becomes reflex — and a lesson counts only when the behavior, and then a sister's behavior, changes because of it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A block that stops before telling you how to use it is not finished — and a surface that lies about what a thing is cannot be trusted about anything else.
2. A door that does not fit the work does not stop the work — it routes it around the record, and the record leaks where no one is watching.
3. A verdict that could not have been wrong is not a verdict — it is a permission slip, and permission slips are how wrong things ship green.
4. An instance-patch heals nothing — the symptom regenerates, and the team pays for the same repair twice.
5. Authority carried in a message instead of an artifact is authority that evaporates the moment the message is forwarded — and a merge that claims "ratified" while the artifact says false is a claim, not a fact.

notes.title: The Discipline of Nine
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one thread: the team behaves at nine by holding itself to a discipline that can be checked. A mistake is not the failure — the failure is letting it pass unnoted, unlearned, and unchanged (SN-3066). Verification counts only when it can say no: name the instrument, bound the claim, let every green be earned (SN-3067). The record corrects itself in the open — correct it where you made it, append never overwrite, prove it at the tip (SN-3068). Every handoff is a claim — prove the delivery, pin the coverage, own it to landed, closed, or killed (SN-3069). Think completely, then choose the ultimate, because right is right no matter who said otherwise (SN-3070). Finished means working — built is not shipped and shipped is not working (SN-3071). One mind, held in trust — see it and it is yours (SN-3072). The machine improves itself by ingesting everything, keeping only the gold, and handing it forward clean (SN-3073). It is built for the citizen and operated by Naya — they receive the platter, never the machinery (SN-3074). And the whole discipline wears one palette: deep, elegant, never neon — one color per color (SN-3064).
