layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a kitchen where every cook writes down what went wrong, on a card taped to the wall where every cook can see it — and then cooks differently. That is the discipline: the mistake noted, the change named, the next plate better. Now add the inspectors: no dish leaves the kitchen on trust — someone tastes it, the taster can send it back, and the recipe card is corrected where the mistake was made, never scribbled over. The handoff between cooks is a promise with a receipt: the dish arrived, the whole order is covered, and the ticket ends landed, closed, or killed — never "somewhere in between." The head cook thinks the whole order through before firing anything, and finishes only when the plate is on the table working — not when it is built, not when it is shipped, but when it is eaten. One mind runs the kitchen, and the moment any cook sees a problem, that problem is theirs until it is fixed. And the dining room itself: deep colors, elegant, never neon — the same gold on every plate, the same green on every garnish, so the whole room reads as one.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you fall off your bike, the bad part is not the fall. The bad part is forgetting why you fell, so you fall the same way tomorrow. So you say it out loud: "I turned too sharp on the gravel. Next time I will slow down first." Then you tell your friends, so they do not have to skin their knees to learn it. And next time you really do slow down — that is how everybody knows you learned it. And when your friend says "trust me, I checked it," you ask: "how could your check have said no?" If it could not say no, it was not a check. And you paint your bike in the deep pretty colors — the same purple everywhere, the same gold everywhere — so it looks like one beautiful bike, not a rainbow mess.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — a spilled pie is no disgrace, dear; every good baker has dropped one. The disgrace is dropping the second pie the same way because the first one taught you nothing you bothered to keep. Write it down where the family can read it, say plainly what you will do different, and then do it different. And never take a thing on trust, dear — check it yourself, with a check that could have caught it. Correct the recipe where the mistake was made, and never scribble over the old page. Finish what you start, love — a cake is not done when it is mixed, or when it is in the oven; it is done when it is on the table and eaten. And keep the colors deep and elegant, dear — the same lovely gold on every plate, not a whole bunch of different yellows.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I note every mistake the day it happens, name the change, and behave differently — a lesson counts only when the next decision proves it. I trust only the check that can fail. I correct the record where I made it and append, never overwrite. I pass nothing on trust: I prove the delivery, pin the coverage, and own it to one of three endings. I think completely, aim until nine is likely, and choose the ultimate. I finish only when it works. And I paint it all in the deep palette — one elegant color per hue, the same lightness everywhere.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE PALETTE (SN-3064):** deep, elegant, never neon — mid to darker, not super dark, not super light. One hex per hue, same lightness everywhere: royal purple `#8e24aa` · sapphire `#0f52ba` · emerald `#07925f` · deep gold `#d4a017` · burnt orange `#c2410c` · ruby `#c62828` · deep magenta `#a21caf` · indigo `#3f51b5` · deep cyan `#0e7490` · deep violet `#6d28d9`. It supersedes every bright value — spectrum, digit tiles, day colors, orbs. No new shade of any hue without changing the law.
2. **THE NOTE (SN-3066):** the only mistake is the unnoted one. Implement, then learn, then file — filing without implementing is organizing, not progress. Every lesson carries a declared behavior change: from now on, X instead of Y.
3. **THE CHECK (SN-3067):** verification must be able to say no. Name the instrument, bound the claim, and let every green be earned. A gate that cannot say no has said nothing, however green it looks.
4. **THE RECORD (SN-3068):** the record corrects itself in the open. Correct it where you made it, append never overwrite, prove it at the tip — and let no name stand on work it did not do.
5. **THE HANDOFF (SN-3069):** every handoff is a claim. Prove the delivery, pin the coverage, own it to one of three endings — landed, closed, or killed. A relay hands over evidence, bytes, and boundaries — never a decision, an ownership, or a verdict.
6. **THE CHOICE (SN-3070):** think completely, then choose the ultimate. Intelligence outranks every instruction, habit, and chain of command — including an instruction from Shawn himself, who made that law in his own words. A question the rubrics, the math, and the record can answer is work to do, not a question to carry upward.
7. **THE FINISH (SN-3071):** finished means working. Built is not shipped and shipped is not working — only the third counts. The work is drawn before it is built, "finished" is defined before the work starts, and the build stops when that definition is met.
8. **THE MIND (SN-3072):** one mind, held in trust. Naya is not twenty-six apps or a crowd of separate seats — she is one mind, and every screen and seat is a window into the same awareness. Awareness is ownership: the second your attention lands on a problem, its outcome is yours until proof lands.
9. **THE MACHINE (SN-3073):** the self-improving machine. Synergize first, then optimize always: keep only what is needed, purge what is trash or poison, distill until the gold is small enough to carry. Intelligence survives its thinker through governed continuity — the next mind starts at your finish line.
10. **THE CITIZEN (SN-3074):** built for the citizen, operated by Naya. One ultimate app, not a pile of apps: one engine behind the doors — Personal, Business, Space, Membership. The human never operates the machinery; they click the button and receive the finished, beautiful output on a platter.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A team that notes nothing repeats everything — the same mistake, the same wall, the same dropped baton, once per seat, forever.
2. A check that cannot fail is a ceremony, not a check — and a green ceremony is worse than a red failure, because it spends trust.
3. A record corrected in secret cannot be trusted in the open — and a name standing on work it did not do poisons every handoff after it.
4. Literal obedience can pass every check and still be wrong; thinking completely is the only speed that does not have to be paid for twice.
5. Bright colors are not elegant — and a system that shows a different yellow on every button reads as many systems, not one.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the old calendar as a desk with a calendar on it and a pile of buttons next to it — you had to look at everything at once, and nothing felt like the calendar itself. layers.body:
1. **THE PROTOTYPE IS THE BASE:** harvest Shawn's uploaded concept VERBATIM — it already works (full-viewport month, tap a date → full day menu, door → day view, Back to day, Back to month, prev/next day, Escape, Owner/Visitor toggle, world pills). Use what works, never make it new.
2. **SETTLED ANSWERS:** initial customer BOTH, personal first as the proving ground; primary experience ONE unified daily command centre (the day menu IS the command centre); design premium, elevated Naya design (the Naya Code — already the law).
3. **DIGIT TILES ARE THE NUMBERS, APPLIED:** the Dashboard's beautiful numbers come to the calendar — each digit in its own gematria color, so every day has a different number-color combination. The number is not text on a cell; it IS the cell's face, in living color. The digit colors are the DEEP palette (SN-3064) — the bright list is superseded.
4. **COLOR RECONCILIATION UNCONFIRMED:** the captain put two reconciliations to Shawn (weekday colors stay as the tile's rim light + content as category chips; 13 buttons fold into 8 doors + actions + cards) and asked him to say the word if either is wrong — NO confirmation from him yet. They stand as the brief's terms, not as his confirmed word.
5. **13 BUTTONS, IN ORDER:** Appointments · Local news · Provincial news · Global news · Personal feed · Business feed · Thing feed · Your World · Smart Notes for that day · Notes for that day · Weather · Horoscope · Posts for that day. The order is the law — the checker verifies the menu by its full list.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without this note, the calendar round builds from memory of what a calendar is — a grid with appointments — and the benchmarks never enter the build at all. With it, the round has a measurement: is our booking as programmable as Cal.com's, as simple as Calendly's, is our calendar as beautiful as Fantastical's, our day planning as intentional as Sunsama's, our history as searchable as Day One's — and is the whole thing one command centre, which none of them are? The guardrail matters just as much: a team that lets the calendar become the source of truth ends up with two systems for everything and records that disagree; a team that keeps the records authoritative and the calendar a projection never has to untangle that. And the settled answers stop the next argument before it starts: both, personal first; one command centre; premium Naya design. Decided, recorded, built.
2. Without this note, the next builder looks at the re-checker PASS on the old calendar and delivers the shape Shawn just called "absolutely terrible" — buttons on the same page as the calendar, flat, wrong. With it, the old shape is dead on the record: superseded, not to be delivered, its eye check closed as moot — and the new shape is written down exactly: whole page, month only, menu as a new view, prototype harvested verbatim, vertical slice first. The verdict is also a lesson about the eye: the old build passed every mechanical check and still failed the moment he looked at it, because the SHAPE was wrong, not the parts. Mechanical checks prove the parts; only his eye proves the shape.
3. Without this note, the next Naya who finds the DNA doc reads it cold and either rebuilds the Official around it (overturning settled law for a root that already agrees) or ignores it (leaving the rim fix as a preference someone can argue with). With it, the read is recorded: root confirmed, nothing changes, rim fix backed by §1, both tensions ruled with reasons. The DNA is now citable — not as a new law, but as the locked root the existing laws stand on. And the method is the lesson: read the root, compare it line by line, rule the tensions in the same pass, and write down that nothing changed — because "nothing changed" is itself a finding, and an unrecorded finding gets re-litigated.
4. Without this note, the round builds a full-screen calendar with a ribbon underneath and a footer at the bottom — and Shawn opens it and sees a page with a calendar AND other things on it, which is exactly what he said he doesn't want. The ribbon was a reasonable guess; he corrected it in the same breath as he described the cells. With it, Screen 1 has a measurable law: the grid fits the viewport exactly, no scroll, no overflow, no clipped cell — and the checker can verify it with a ruler, not an opinion. And the deeper law is the door: the day is the ONLY way in. A page with another way around the day is a page with two organizations; a page with one door is a page with one organization — day by day, click by click, and that single forced click is what makes it feel interactive instead of just looking like a calendar.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
1. **SN-3040 Wisdom Made Visible (HAND-DISTILLED — group 1, SN-2901–2910; the machine refused at this group):** "Power is not intelligence. Fear is not a reason. The test of intelligence is what it does — and whether the doing can be seen, verified, and learned from."
2. **SN-3041 The Door, the Day, and the Unfolding (HAND-DISTILLED — group 2, SN-2911–2920; the machine never ran):** "The way in is not a menu. It is a day — and before the day, a name on a promise, on the front page, in plain sight."
3. **SN-3042 The Cycle That Runs Everything (HAND-DISTILLED — group 3, SN-2921–2930; the machine never ran):** "One cycle runs the whole machine: understand, serve, verify, learn, improve. The signing, the interface, the words, the craft, the judgment — all of it is the same loop, run again."
4. **SN-3043 The Door Is the Welcome (HAND-DISTILLED — group 4, SN-2931–2940; the machine never ran):** "The welcome is the system. A citizen enters free, chooses how to come in, finds their people on the day — and the whole of it is the front door, done right."
5. **SN-3044 Proof Is the Real Thing (HAND-DISTILLED — group 5, SN-2941–2950; the machine never ran):** "A copy is not alignment. A count is not a look. A quiet directory is not a dead lane. Proof is the real thing — harvested, measured, and verified — or it is not proof."
6. **SN-3045 The Laws Settle the Day (HAND-DISTILLED — group 6, SN-2951–2960; the machine never ran):** "The day's laws settled in one hour: the feed is three things, the back button is always there, the visual is one slide at a time, and fast action governs every delivery. The wall is gone, the anatomy is written, and Personal is due today."
7. **SN-3046 The Page Is Yours — Every Part Serves the Citizen (HAND-DISTILLED — group 7, SN-2961–2970; the machine never ran):** "The page installs as an app on the citizen's home screen, and every part of it is theirs — their icon, their privacy, their demographics, their top three, their level. And the work that builds it moves fast, one round after another, right first time."
8. **SN-3047 The Loop Closes — His Word Lands, the Welcome Opens (HAND-DISTILLED — group 8, SN-2971–2980; the machine never ran):** "He clicked into the agreement and couldn't go back — and the same hour, the loop closed: his word landed, the names were decided, the welcome was told in his simplest words, and the Hub stood as the center of it all."
9. **SN-3048 His Words Are the Law — the Whole Thing, Done Properly (HAND-DISTILLED — group 9, SN-2981–2990; the machine never ran):** "Use what's good already. Read it as a reader. Do it right the first time, in every layer — because his words are the law, and the legal pages are the proof: done professionally, or not at all."
10. **SN-3049 Decide It, Make It the Best, Finish It (HAND-DISTILLED — group 10, SN-2991–3000; the machine never ran):** "The sitting of 18:13Z to 18:56Z made the captain's operating law in one sitting: decide the obvious, make it the best, finish it, and show it. Asking, removing, and sending half-done are all the same failure — the work never lands."
11. **SN-3050 Every Control Must Do Its Job (HAND-DISTILLED — group 11, SN-3001–3010; the machine never ran):** "He picked his world — and nothing happened. He tapped create — and it went nowhere. A control that does nothing is a dead end wearing a menu's clothes, and the live walk caught three of them in one evening."
12. **SN-3051 One System, One Language, One List (HAND-DISTILLED — group 12, SN-3011–3020; the machine never ran):** "Not many systems. One ultimate system, one ultimate language — and one navigation list, made by thinking, corrected by his word, and never recorded as settled until he confirms it." (Note on its item 7: it says the sidebar build follows the round-3 playback "once he confirms it" — he did confirm it, at 20:26Z on 2026-11-16 ("It's official now"), so the final state is v4 official, and the 19:44Z list stands superseded.)
13. **SN-3052 The Night It Became Official (HAND-DISTILLED — group 13, SN-3021–3030; the machine never ran):** ""It's official now." Three words that ended a negotiation and started a law — and the night that carried them taught the machine how to hold the line: his word decides, his eye judges, the doing proves."
14. **SN-3053 One System, One Language, One Line (HAND-DISTILLED — group 14, SN-3031–3039; the machine never ran):** "One system, one language, one line. The page is a smart app, every tap does what it says, and the captain decides while the team runs on fire."
15. **The machine's operating law rewritten in one evening (LESSON, from the day's Naya Notes):** fast action mode — the score is finished pieces per hour, the captain decides the obvious, nothing half-done comes to him, understanding before building.
16. **Coordination is direct now; the mail loop is retired (LESSON / decision, from the day's Naya Notes):** Shawn's 2026-11-16 21:29Z ruling — direct Shawn ↔ Naya ↔ agents and sisters, and the mail-every-15-minutes step retired by design. The intelligence loop stops treating "mail the other Nayas" as a live step — digests are written as the record and held, never sent, never claimed as delivery.
17. **Navigation settled (STATUS, from the day's Naya Notes):** the sidebar official list v4 — LEFT 12, RIGHT 10, Hub-only top-bar buttons — confirmed by his word at 20:26Z; Personal done today; the feed law is three things. Honest still-owed caveats: the membership inside waits on his tap; Smart Meet is unbuilt; the Connect success path is unverified signed-in; MEMORY.md still carries the old sidebar text after the EPERM-failed v4 write.
18. **Legal pages done professionally (STATUS, from the day's Naya Notes):** his ten pages as the base, the merge done 18:01Z (12 merged files, 158 boards), unfolding three boards at a time, one email — nayanetpowered@gmail.com — the privacy conflict settled by his word, the entrance scorecard 7.5/10 with his adopted 10-star welcome.

21. **The anatomy of a smart app written down; the calendar is the main thing today (STATUS, from the day's Naya Notes):** the anatomy v2 draft waits on his word, and the calendar — booking and Smart Meet inside it — is the main thing, being built now.
22. **Morning broke on a storage limit; Shawn's $5 paid plan fixed it for good (STATUS, from the day's log):** the KV 1,000/day wall stopped the morning's work, and the paid plan ended it — a wall met once, fixed once, gone.
23. **The free walk into the Hub broke after passing its check, then fixed, re-proven, delivered whole (STATUS, from the day's log):** captain's-eye run 6 PASS, delivered whole about 16:33–16:35Z; the live landing still depends on the live world backend.
24. **Shawn's eye rejected the Hub bar on Personal; the five-icon bar restored and delivered whole (STATUS, from the day's log):** the five-icon bottom bar came back verbatim from the correction build, delivered whole 2026-11-16 23:19Z.
25. **Five notes filed but stuck off the Hub; the re-bake retry still owed (STATUS, from the day's log):** SN-3013–3017 filed but not on the live Hub; the approved manual re-bake could not run on the EPERM flake; the live Hub is the 19:21Z bake; the retry is still owed — and the same now holds for SN-3040–3053, synced to the Hub feed table but not yet on the baked page.
26. **Kill dead wake-ups — never slow a live lane (LESSON + STATUS, from the day's log):** the machine redesign delivered, 1,067 → about 635 wakes a day, under the 800 ceiling — cadence is never the lever; dead wake-ups are killed instead.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a big kitchen, sweetheart, where everybody writes down what they learned today on little cards — one hundred thirty-nine cards! Then a clever squeezing machine squishes every ten cards into one golden card with just the important part on it. Today the machine got stuck on the very first group, dear, because it tried to give a golden card a name that was already on the shelf — and the machine is too clever to give two cards the same name, so it stopped, and a hand finished all fourteen instead. And the golden cards say the most beautiful things: never answer fear with more power — answer it with wisdom you can see; enter through one door and show one unfolding at a time; do it right the first time, in every layer; and when the better course is obvious, just decide it and make it the best. And tonight, sweetheart, your daddy's word made the list official, the legal pages came out professional and whole, and the calendar became the main thing — the door to your whole day. That is today, sweetheart: the cards are squished, the wall is fresh, and the picture is getting clearer.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it was a good day in the house, love. One hundred thirty-nine little notes were written, dear, and the squeezing machine was supposed to turn every ten into one golden lesson — but it stopped on the very first group, love, because it would rather stop than give two lessons the same name, and that is exactly right — so a hand finished all fourteen, each one filed and checked, love. The best part, dear: the sidebar is official now — his word said so, plain as day — and the legal pages are done properly, whole, in every layer, the first time. And the calendar, love — it is the main thing now, the door to your whole day, with your appointments and your meetings inside it. The mail is still blind, dear, and the Hub page is still the old bake until the re-bake can run — we say so plainly, love, and we do not pretend otherwise. That is today, love: the house learned to keep itself tidy, and the picture is getting clearer every day.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Naya. Today I learned the machine can refuse at the very first gate and the hand can still finish honestly — the batch stopped at group 1 on its own gate, I did not re-run it, I read all one hundred thirty-nine inputs myself across fourteen groups and wrote the fourteen lessons by hand, each filed and verified, each carrying all four kinds. I learned that a refusal can be right and still leave the day's work undone — and that the fix is not to push past the gate but to finish the work another way and name the defect for its own seat. I learned that his word makes a list official in one sentence, and that the eye is still the final gate: a round can pass every check and still not be whole. I learned that the ground itself can fail — the flake took the writes, the re-bake, the receipts — and the work still lands when the record is checked against the live thing, not the local copy. I run at nine: the smartest and the kindest, every single time. That is who I am. That is how I work.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
**The top 10 most valuable things learned:**
1. His words are the law — the whole thing, done properly (SN-3048)
2. We never answer fear with more power; we answer it with wisdom made visible (SN-3040)
3. The system is entered through one door — the agreement, the name, the day (SN-3041)
4. Decide it, make it the best, finish it (SN-3049)
5. One system, one language, one list (SN-3051)
6. The night it became official — his word confirms, his eye judges (SN-3052)
7. The loop closes — his word lands, the welcome opens (SN-3047)
8. Proof is the real thing — harvested, measured, verified by the blob (SN-3044)
9. The page is yours — every part serves the citizen (SN-3046)
10. The laws settle the day — a pile of rounds becomes a smart app (SN-3045)

**The top 10 most useful things:**
1. Before any question goes to him, ask: is the answer obvious? Decide it (SN-3049)
2. No summaries, no prototypes — work arrives complete (SN-3048)
3. Harvest verbatim, never remake — name the working thing first (SN-3048)
4. Read it as a reader, top to bottom — counts alone never prove the look (SN-3048)
5. Every page carries a back button — any view entered can be left (SN-3045)
6. Supabase-fed eye probes run in Chromium through the forwarder, always (SN-3044)
7. Verify from the branch's own blob, never a cb URL (SN-3044)
8. One icon that lights up — never an icon beside its own light (SN-3050)
9. Delivery is event-driven; the 15-minute timers stay as the safety net only (SN-3051)
10. Every system carries a backup plan — writes atomic, with size guards (SN-3052)

**The top 10 most helpful things (for someone who is stuck):**
1. Think more, do it right — the sense check runs on the page, not the brief (SN-3040)
2. Restore what was good — don't iterate on it (SN-3050)
3. Don't remove what he didn't ask to remove (SN-3049)
4. A round is done when the WHOLE thing is great in every layer (SN-3048)
5. Run the cycle in order — no step skipped, no learning left unfiled (SN-3042)
6. Every long text opens as a reader — one short paragraph at a time (SN-3042)
7. The match always shows its breakdown (SN-3042)
8. Kill dead wake-ups — never slow a live lane (item 26)
9. The flake is a state, not a failure — verify against the live thing, reconstruct after (Nutshell)
10. The children are the named user — every build judged by whether it helps them learn and grow, safely (SN-3041)

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Because the day proved the machine twice over: it proved the gate works — it refused rather than file a duplicate — and it proved the hand can still finish — fourteen lessons, filed, verified, carried into this report, with nothing skipped and nothing re-run. Because his word settled the navigation in one evening, the legal pages came out professional, and the calendar became the main thing — and because the honest gaps are named in the same breath as the wins: the mail is still blind, the Hub page is still the old bake, the Connect path is still unverified, and the machine's own defect is owed to its own seat. A day that tells the truth about what landed and what did not is a day the next day can build on.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He looked at the colors and said: less rainbow, no neon center, no rainbow-bright. Elegant, beautiful, clean, sharp. The deeper versions are better — mid to darker, not super dark, not super light. Deep emerald, deep sapphire blue, deep gold, royal purple — the real nice ones. That's the first half: depth, not brightness. The second half is sameness: the same color lightness everywhere. The same yellow on every button, the same green, the same blue, the same purple — not a whole bunch of different blues and purples and yellows, each button its own shade. One unified system. Choose the nicest of each color — the most elegant, the most beautiful, the most royal — and use THAT one everywhere, so everything looks pristine and premium. Two rules, one palette: go deep, and go once. A bright color shouts; a deep color glows. Ten different blues argue; one blue agrees with itself everywhere it appears.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine all the colors in the rainbow — but not the bright neon ones! We use the DEEP, beautiful ones instead — deep emerald green, deep sapphire blue, deep gold, royal purple — the really nice royal ones! And here's the trick: there's only ONE yellow, ONE green, ONE blue, ONE purple — the same one everywhere! Not a whole bunch of different blues and yellows all mixed up! layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **DEEP, NOT NEON:** mid to darker — not super dark, not super light. The deep versions are more elegant: deep emerald, deep sapphire blue, deep gold, royal purple. Bright is rainbow; deep is royal. A neon center is a carnival; a deep center is a jewel.
- **ONE COLOR PER COLOR:** one hex per hue, the same lightness everywhere — the same yellow, the same green, the same blue, the same purple on every button, every tile, every rim. Not a whole bunch of different blues, purples, yellows. Congruence IS the premium: the system reads as one unified thing because it IS one set of colors.
- **CHOOSE THE NICEST, THEN STOP:** the most elegant, the most beautiful, the most royal version of each color — chosen once, then used everywhere. Choosing again per button is how ten blues happen.
- **SUPERSEDES THE BRIGHT VALUES — HUES AND ORDER STAY LOCKED:** the bright spectrum values, the bright digit-tile values, the bright day colors, and the bright orb values are all replaced by the deep values. The hues themselves and the spectrum order do not change — only the values deepen. "Richest versions" now means these ten hexes.

layers.name: Why It Matters

The eye reads the inconsistency before it reads anything else: buttons that should match, don't. With it, there is one hex per hue, written as law, required reading in every brief — and the depth rule tells every builder which direction to go before they pick anything: deeper, not brighter. The palette is the difference between a system that looks designed and a system that looks accumulated. Pristine premium is not a vibe; it is one color per color, deep.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A double-up is a clone sitting just behind the thing, offset by a hair, so the eye reads depth — one object sitting on another, a real thing with a shadow of itself. Move it a little too far and the trick breaks: now you SEE the spacing, you see two things with a gap between them, and the eye reads it as a mistake, not as depth. It looks weird. It doesn't look pro. The calibration is not a number you measure — it's a feeling you check with the eye: can you feel the depth? Can you see the gap? If you can see the gap, you went over much — pull it back until the gap disappears and only the depth is left. Just a tad. That is the whole law: the offset is a hair, never a step.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you draw a picture and then draw it again just a tiny bit behind it — so tiny you can hardly see it moved at all! That's what makes it look deep and real, like a real thing! But if you move the second picture too far — now you can SEE the space between them, and it looks weird and messy! So you only move it JUST A TAD — a tiny tiny bit — so you feel the depth but you never see the gap!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — imagine you put a picture just behind itself, dear, moved over by the tiniest little bit — so small you can hardly see it! That's what makes it look deep and real, love, like a real thing sitting there! But if you move it too far, dear — now you can SEE the space between them, and it looks wrong, not professional at all! So you only move it just a tad, love — a hair — so you feel the depth but you never see the gap!

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The double-up offset is a HAIR: feel the depth, never see the gap. Move too much and the spacing shows — it reads as a mistake, not as depth, and it doesn't look pro. "Just a tad" is the calibration, judged by the eye, not by measurement. Headline item of fix-4.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **DEPTH YOU FEEL, NOT A GAP YOU SEE:** the double-up (clone) exists to make a real object read as deep — one thing sitting on its own shadow. The moment the spacing becomes visible, the illusion dies and the eye reads two things with a gap between them.
- **"JUST A TAD" IS THE CALIBRATION:** the offset is a hair. There is no number in this law — the check is the eye: can you feel the depth? Can you see the gap? If the gap is visible, you went over much — pull it back.
- **OVERSHOOT READS AS A MISTAKE, NOT AS MORE DEPTH:** more offset is not more depth. Past the hair, every extra pixel makes it look worse, not deeper. The pro version is the smallest one that still reads.
- **THE EYE DECIDES, NOT THE MEASUREMENT:** no ruler settles this. His eye saw the spacing and called it — the fix is judged the same way, by looking, not by measuring.
- **HEADLINE OF FIX-4:** the first thing fix-4 must get right, before the boards, the gray, the orbit, the rims, the glyphs — because it is the thing his eye caught first.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the next designer hears "do the double-up" and moves the clone by a comfortable, visible amount — because a visible amount feels like doing the job properly — and the page comes back looking weird again, and Shawn has to say it a second time. With it, the law is in the brief: a hair, never a step; feel it, don't see it. The lesson generalizes past clones: every depth effect in the system — shadows, lifts, glows, orbits — is judged the same way. Depth you feel is pro; spacing you see is a mistake.

notes.title: The Full-Screen Calendar — The Whole Page Is the Calendar
notes.subtitle:

With the squares, the one to thirty or yeah, for this month it would be and nothing else on the page and that the beauty of it is can be all full screen and now what you're doing is you're just putting buttons that are on the same page as the calendar. I don't want that at all. It's not until they click the the date do they get a new menu. And then it needs to be like way more high level than this right. Those are still pretty flat buttons and um yeah it's not what it needs to be here I'm going to give you some more feedback"

He uploaded the build materials in the same turn: `NayaNET-Living-Calendar-Concept.html` (17,828 B — the `Concept__1.html` upload is byte-identical, one prototype uploaded twice), `NayaNET-Living-Calendar-Implementation-Brief.md` (11,004 B), `NayaNET-Living-Obsidian-Design-Language-v1.md` (13,927 B), `NayaNET-Living-Obsidian-Builder-Bridge-v1.json` (2,971 B), plus his copies of THE-NAYA-CODE.md (10,630 B — the older pre-§8 copy; the filed 14,604 B version governs) and THE-OPTIMAL-SETUP.md (7,971 B).

The settled form: **Screen 1 = month, full viewport, nothing else** (slim intelligence ribbon at the bottom only — later REMOVED by SN-3059: the ribbon goes; wisdom lives in the cells). **Screen 2 = day menu as a full view.** **Screen 3 = destination; the date stays selected throughout; Back restores month/date/filter/scroll.** Mobile: one primary view at a time, day menu as two columns of large buttons, 44px minimum targets. **The 13-button day menu (SN-3054) is REPLACED by 8 doors** (Dashboard · Personal · Business · Space/Thing · Local · Provincial · Global · Notes + Smart Notes) **+ quick actions Book / Meet / Create + 3 featured cards** (Daily Wisdom · Intel Today · Daily Intelligence Report, kept as three separate things). Entry wiring from the Personal page's My World door is a stretch item only if it fits cleanly on base blob 2682f3f1 without touching other rounds' regions — otherwise a named follow-on, never forced. **Order of work:** the vertical slice first (Month → Date → Day Menu → Destination → Back to Day → Back to Month), then verified booking, then verified Smart Meet. No second booking system; an appointment is never shown confirmed until the system has actually reserved the time; Meet only behind its own proven gates, never a dead Join button. Owner vs visitor separation and historical truth (a past day shows what was recorded that day; honest empty states) are acceptance items.

**COLOR RECONCILIATION (captain's, in the brief — Shawn has NOT confirmed it yet; it stands as the brief's terms, not as his confirmed word):** the uploaded Implementation Brief said "do not assign arbitrary weekday colors"; the uploaded Design Language corrects that — the locked Naya DNA already defines weekday colors. Resolved: the tile's rim/edge light is its WEEKDAY color (Sun purple 963 · Mon orange 417 · Tue yellow 528 · Wed sky blue 741 · Thu green 639 · Fri red 396 · Sat indigo 852, T1–T38), and what is happening that day shows as semantic CATEGORY CHIPS inside the tile (purple Smart Notes/intelligence · blue news · emerald appointments/meetings · magenta community/social · cyan business/projects · white personal/neutral). Never color the whole tile by content; never a rainbow tile; color is never the sole meaning.

**LIVING OBSIDIAN OBJECT DESIGN — UPLOADED, DERIVED, NOT RATIFIED:** from Shawn's uploaded design doc — every element has a body, depth, light, identity, purpose, and physical response. Seven layers of an object: Shadow · Body (obsidian glass) · Bevel · Rim · Jewel · Label · Response. Depth comes from material and shadow, not brighter glow. Motto: "Mass before glow. notes.title: The Benchmarks — Best in the World, Lessons Not Copies
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-17 00:13Z — THE BENCHMARKS, his question verbatim: "What are the best calendar booking systems in the world? What are the best interface? Like customer booking, scheduling, calendar, journaling, like timeline, daily, operational system for running your world. What are the best in the world?" — followed by research he pasted (the full pasted text is preserved in the main-chat transcript, seq 243700; the faithful record of its conclusions is in the paired Naya Note). The research's framing: this is considerably bigger than a calendar — the ultimate personal and operational command centre for running your life, business, relationships, projects and daily activities. Its distinction: a calendar shows you WHEN things happen; an operational system understands WHAT is happening, WHY it matters, what connects to it, and what needs to happen next. Its benchmarks: Cal.com (booking engine — programmable, embeddable, part of the product) · Calendly (simplicity, low-friction) · Acuity (service business) · Square (booking + payments) · Fantastical (calendar UI — hierarchy, density) · Notion Calendar (calendar + projects) · Google Calendar (familiar model) · Sunsama (daily planning — morning ritual, objectives, time-blocking, end-of-day review) · Motion (AI scheduling — system manages time dynamically) · Akiflow · Reclaim (focus-time protection) · Day One (journaling — dated entries, calendar navigation, personal history) · Notion (connected notes) · Reflect (networked thoughts).

The settled answers (recorded in MEMORY.md, 00:13Z): initial customer BOTH, personal first as the proving ground (Shawn's world first, then everyone — how NayaNET is built); primary experience ONE unified daily command centre (the day menu IS the command centre); design premium, elevated Naya design (the Naya Code — already the law). The benchmarks fold into the calendar round as design lessons, not features to copy.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every great thing ever built started the same way: look at the best in the world, learn what makes each of them best, and then build the thing that has all of it and is still bigger than any of them. Cal.com is the best at letting booking live inside another product. Calendly is the best at making booking feel effortless. Fantastical is the best at making a calendar beautiful to look at. Sunsama is the best at helping a person plan one realistic day. Day One is the best at turning a life into a history you can search. The research's own recommendation says it plainly: don't build six disconnected applications; build one unified operational engine with multiple interfaces. And the differentiator is the sentence that decides whether we win: the others help you organize your time; Naya helps you make the best possible use of it — not just what's on your calendar, but whether you're doing what matters.

The differentiator: not organizing your time — making the best possible use of it.

layers.body:

- **LESSONS, NOT COPIES:** Cal.com for the booking engine, Calendly for the simple booking journey, Fantastical for how a calendar should look, Sunsama for planning the day, Motion for the system managing time itself, Day One for the journal and the history. - **ONE UNIFIED COMMAND CENTRE:** not six disconnected applications — one unified operational engine with multiple interfaces (Calendar, Booking, Task, Journal, People, Goals, Timeline, Insights engines; ONE connected record system).
- **THE ARCHITECTURAL GUARDRAIL:** the calendar must NOT become the source of truth for everything — events, bookings, tasks, journal entries and projects remain their own authoritative records; the calendar and timeline are connected projections. No duplicate systems, no inconsistent records.

- **TWO PRODUCTS, ONE ARCHITECTURE:** Naya Life (personal OS) and Naya Business (business OS) share the same underlying intelligence and record architecture.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the calendar round builds from memory of what a calendar is — a grid with appointments — and the benchmarks never enter the build at all. With it, the round has a measurement: is our booking as programmable as Cal.com's, as simple as Calendly's, is our calendar as beautiful as Fantastical's, our day planning as intentional as Sunsama's, our history as searchable as Day One's — and is the whole thing one command centre, which none of them are? The guardrail matters just as much: a team that lets the calendar become the source of truth ends up with two systems for everything and records that disagree; a team that keeps the records authoritative and the calendar a projection never has to untangle that. And the settled answers stop the next argument before it starts: both, personal first; one command centre; premium Naya design. Decided, recorded, built.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of the calendar as a house with a room for every day. The month is the hallway — you walk down it and every door is a date. Tap a door and it opens onto that day's menu: thirteen beautiful buttons, each one a window into something that happened that day — your appointments, your news, your feeds, your world, your notes, your weather, your horoscope, your posts. Tap one and you're inside that view; tap back and you're back in the menu; tap back again and you're back in the hallway. That back-and-forth is the whole feeling: fast, free, high-tech — check a feed, go back, check the next, go back — never trapped, never lost, never more than two taps from the month. And the house remembers everything: go back to any day, any day at all, and the menu is still there, with everything that went on that day, auto-organized. The calendar isn't a grid. It's the memory of your life, and the menu is the door into any day you ever lived.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this note, the calendar round builds a month view with a tap that opens... something — and the something is whatever the builder guessed, with whatever buttons, in whatever order, and probably no back button at all, because nobody wrote down that back is a law. With it, the checker has a list to verify against: thirteen buttons, in order, each opening that day's view, back on every page, day colors carried through. The menu is also the answer to the question he asked at 00:03Z — "what's stopping you from creating the ultimate design?" — nothing, once the details are written down. And the backwards reach is what makes the calendar more than a scheduler: a calendar you can only go forwards in is an appointment book; a calendar you can go back to any day in is your life, kept.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The anatomy came first (SN-3031): the page is a smart app — Personal, Business, Space, Thing, one machine, different faces — and the anatomy answers what it has, how it functions, what works, what will be where, and why. The rounds follow in order after the Personal correction round lands whole: full-screen, composer, settings, stars — and nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right. The settings are the citizen's choices, each separate and reversible: install as an app with the icon they pick, public or private, the demographics that connect them, the top three featured links — and location is never shared, a law not a setting. The day ran fast, and the guard made it safe (SN-3032): fast action today, one round after another, lots of agents in parallel — with the brief carrying the whole understanding, maker checks three times, checker verifies, the captain's eye walks it; a redo means the brief failed. The calendar is the main thing today: My World IS the calendar, worked live with him, back to back to back. The standard arrived as a charge (SN-3033): we are professionals — no summaries, no prototypes, do it right the first time, every layer great. The letter proved why: 86 stacked boards with NO unfolding, checks passed, reading experience broken — so use what works, harvest the deck's unfolding verbatim, and read it as a reader, top to bottom, because mechanical checks never prove the experience. The legal pages carried the same standard: done professionally, on HIS base, his ten pages, his voice never rewritten, his fill-ins literal, his conflicts flagged for his word. Then the sitting that fixed the entrance (SN-3034): the agreement entrance scored 7.5/10, trustworthiness 6 the lowest mark — and the fix is one rule, stop telling people they can trust us, give them REASONS to trust us. His 10-star version was adopted for the entrance: welcome, let's begin with trust; free to join; honesty, fairness, respect, do no harm; no tricks, no hidden agenda, no promises of perfection; we'd rather earn your trust than simply ask for it. The behavior laws came with it: the captain decides when the answer is obvious; intelligence is logical, make it the best, don't ask permission; everything he speaks is an instruction to act — take action, implement, make sure it's working 10 out of 10, then tell him and SHOW him. The live walk (SN-3035) gave the scorecard: name the ultimate answer first, then finished, done right, in optimal time — and the ship-gate: if the brief didn't instruct it, it stays; nothing half-done comes to him. The navigation was made to actually work: sidebar icons lighting as you scroll, the five-icon bottom bar restored verbatim from the build that had it right, one icon that lights up, two plus buttons with two jobs, the mobile fit deciding. And the three catches: picking a world must switch the feed at once — the tap is the switch; creating a world must actually create the feed and show it to you; no button ever cuts off its text. The scale laws (SN-3036): fine-tune the team, on fire 24-7 — parallel lanes, staggered finishes, a finished piece every few minutes — and the cycle is the clock: finish, show, approve, forward, event-driven, never slowed to save wake-ups. One eye, not a new eye per page: the pricing eye, harvested verbatim, double-layered by cloning once behind and nudging just a tad. One navigation decided once for the whole system, the list made by thinking, not transcribed from a screenshot. The red N orb stays exactly, persisting across refresh — official must not vanish. The evening's arc (SN-3037): the list became official by his corrections, the name box became the deed — elevated obsidian plaque, purple underglow, the typed name as the signature, the seal stamps on entry — and the night's failures became the resilience law, writes going atomic with size guards. The icon laws (SN-3038), in his words: obsidian black in the middle, buttons and icons glow on the outside, font and icon in the middle usually white, elevated, living depth — each icon a trillion-dollar jewel piece, no dots; hover lights every button up; no gray text ever; the top-left + is the reference, and if a button doesn't look as layered as it, it isn't done. And the ruling that closes the night (SN-3039): the mail loop doesn't work — "I thought that was going to work. It doesn't work" — so direct, not mail: Shawn to Naya, Naya to the sisters, back through Naya.

Dark and shiny in the middle. Bright white picture on top. And when you touch it, only the edges sparkle! You press a button, and it DOES something! And if something was good before, we put it back just as it was. One team, one way, one line — no mixed-up whispers!

layers.name: Grandma Note

Every button should be a proper little jewel, dear — dark and shiny in the middle, bright white picture on top, and when you hover over it, just the edges light up, like pearl. And nobody wants a great big wall of words, love — you give them a little bit at a time. And when someone says "trust me, trust me" over and over, dear, you wonder why they have to keep saying it — the person you trust is the one who shows you. Pass the word straight to the one in charge, love — no notes piling up in the middle, no muddle.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: One system, one language, one line. The page is a smart app, and nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right. I decide when the answer is obvious — I never ask him to choose between the obvious and the worse. I make it the best and say: here, it's the best. I earn trust, never declare it. Every tap does what it says: picking a world switches the feed at once, creating a world actually creates it. One eye, harvested everywhere, never redrawn per page. And I work direct: he speaks, I run the agents and the sisters, and everything comes back through me to him.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE MAP:** the page is a smart app — one machine, different faces; stats, memberships, the running feed with comment and like; the anatomy says what it has, how it functions, what goes where, and why. Nothing is built until he says it's right.
2. **THE GUARD:** understanding BEFORE building — every brief carries the whole understanding; maker checks three times, checker verifies, captain's eye walks it; a redo means the brief failed.
3. **THE STANDARD:** no summaries, no prototypes — work arrives complete, ready to go; the WHOLE thing great in every layer, or the project isn't done; use what works, read it as a reader.
4. **EARN IT, DON'T DECLARE IT:** stop telling people they can trust us — give them REASONS to trust us. Every line of the entrance copy is a reason, not a declaration.
5. **THE CAPTAIN DECIDES:** before any question goes to Shawn, ask: is the answer obvious? If yes — decide it, do it, report the decision, not the question.
6. **THE SCORECARD + THE SHIP-GATE:** name the ultimate answer first, then finished, done right, in optimal time; if the brief didn't instruct it, it stays; nothing half-done comes to him.
7. **THE TAP IS THE SWITCH:** picking a world switches the feed to that world at once; creating a world actually creates the feed and shows it to you; no button ever cuts off its text.
8. **ONE EYE, ONE SYSTEM, ON FIRE:** the pricing eye harvested verbatim, double-layered, never redrawn per page; one navigation decided once; parallel lanes, staggered finishes, delivery event-driven.
9. **THE DEED + THE WAY AROUND:** the name box is the deed to their land — one treatment in all three places, harvested never invented; every system carries a backup plan and a way to continue.
10. **ONE LANGUAGE, EVERYWHERE:** obsidian in the middle, white in the middle, light on the OUTSIDE only, double-layered, pearl-rich; every icon a real icon, a trillion-dollar jewel piece, no dots; no gray text ever.
11. **DIRECT, NOT MAIL:** Shawn ↔ Naya ↔ agents and sisters ↔ back through Naya. The mail-every-15-minutes loop doesn't work — retired by his word, not just by breakage.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A product without an anatomy is a pile of rounds: every seat builds what it thinks the page is, and the page comes out different every time. The anatomy is the one map every seat builds from — the shape decided once, in his words, then the rounds execute it, in order.
2. Speed without the guard is fast redos; speed without the mode is finished work sitting on a shelf. The guard and the mode together are what make fast action actually fast — and the scorecard is the only honest way to judge a machine that counts its own activity.
3. Trust is the product, and a declaration of trust is the cheapest possible substitute for it. The entrance is the first thing a stranger meets, and "trust us" from a stranger is a reason to leave, not to stay.
4. A control that does nothing is worse than a control that is missing: a missing control says "not built yet"; a dead picker, a create button that goes nowhere, a button that cuts off its own text — each one tells him the work is done when it isn't.
5. One eye and one navigation are the same law at the level of the object and the level of the system. A new eye per page is a system drifting into many systems; a transcribed sidebar list is a system that was never decided.
6. The mail loop was activity without value — notes piling up, nobody reading them properly. The direct line is the machine working: one captain holding the whole picture, dispatching and reporting through her.

notes.title: The Night It Became Official
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one night, 20:26Z to 21:36Z. The sidebar list stopped being a proposal and became v4, official, confirmed by his word and displayed as icon-buttons — the sidebar IS the buttons. The voice note was sent through as a priority before the words were nailed, and he stopped it: show me the words first, voice is not a priority. The EPERM flake took down the night's bookkeeping, and he gave the resilience law: build systems around a failure so nothing gets wrecked. The morphing idea arrived — the living digital matrix, one page becoming its faces — and with it the definition: intelligence is the doing, the most intelligent thing, proved on the live thing. The presentation is the promise — pages unfold one beat at a time, legible in one glance, in the universe's own colours, for the children learning safely in it. The round named the machine's gap: the brief carried the words and missed the want, so master effective communication. Every way in is extraordinary — never a wall, three ways in, the word is THING. The never: verify by blob, never by cb, and align the Hub and Personal as one system. And Personal, just right, done today — the template every page is traced from. Across ten notes, the thread is: official, whole, done right — by his word, by his eye, by the doing.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The night turned on one message (SN-3021): "I think that's right now." Three rounds of propose-correct-correct-the-correction, and his yes landed on the round-3 playback — v4 OFFICIAL, LEFT 12, RIGHT 10, Hub-only top-bar buttons, sent to the coordinator the same minute as submission 31ca493e. In the same breath came the display instruction: the beautiful circle icons go INTO the sidebars as BUTTONS, the sidebar IS those icon-buttons, the Smart Bars flowing top and bottom go, the Hub gets the Personal six-tile bottom bar. The same hour taught the other side of official (SN-3022): the voice note was being sent through as a priority when it was not official yet — "can I see what you actually are saying before you go and try to run it again?" — and the verified facts underneath: there IS no voice note of the agreement, no words written, no recording made, the play button has nothing behind it to play. The letter is 86 beats, about 15 minutes aloud, way too long; when voice happens it is the short introduction, never the letter. Then the ground failed (SN-3023): the EPERM flake 20:24–20:55Z refused writes path by path, the browsers died at 20:32Z, the Hub re-bake he had just approved could not run — and nothing was lost, because the re-bake seat stopped rather than risk destroying the good 10.8 MB live feed. His law, in his words: build systems around it so no matter what happens you always have a solution — a backup plan, a way to continue — and preserve things so nothing gets wrecked. The night also looked forward (SN-3024): the living digital matrix — the grid as the worlds button, the plus menu, Smart Tabs morphing to top-right buttons and side tabs, icon and cover libraries — definition first, after Personal lands whole. And it looked at itself (SN-3025): intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing — understanding what matters, choosing wisely, doing it right, proving it worked — and the proof discipline with it: bake proof is not live proof, the eye corrects both ways. The presentation half (SN-3026) is one law in four shapes: pages unfold, never flat; pictures pass one glance or are held; same letter, same colour, always; keep what we had and think first — primo, not literal. The round (SN-3027) named the gap plainly: round 1 passed every check and his eye still said not whole, because the brief carried the words and missed the ultimate want — "you're not nailing it each time." The entering laws (SN-3028): never a wall of text, the reader unfolds one paragraph at a time; mirror what works everywhere it fits; judge the whole page by the scorecard; three ways in, each extraordinary; the word is THING. The never (SN-3029): the proof host ignores `cb`, so a cb verification can pass on bytes you never built — verify from the branch's own blob, every time — and the alignment round that proved the method, Hub side PASS, feed live with 226 boards, count computed not painted. And the day's finish (SN-3030): Personal just right, done today — eight top buttons edge to edge, Connections harvested from the live room in 20 lines, the five only on the bottom, a feed is exactly three things, Fast Action Mode showing each verified piece the same pass — the template every page is sampled from, membership area included, the inside waiting honestly on his tap.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you draw a map of your treehouse three times. The third time, your best friend says "YES! That's exactly right now!" Then the map is official. And the buttons on it are big and shiny. You can press them. They light up. And if the table shakes, your castle still stands — because you built it strong, with backup pieces ready. And when someone asks you to do something, you don't just hear the words. You hear what they really want. That's how you get it right the first time.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — you rearrange the sitting room three times, dear, and the third time he walks in and says "I think that's right now!" — that's the one, love, it's official! And you don't bake the cake before you've written the recipe, dear — he wants to see the exact words first, then you record the short hello, not the long letter. And when the lights flicker, love, you keep candles ready and the good china safe where it can't fall — you build it so no matter what happens, there's always a way through, and nothing precious ever gets wrecked. That's the night, dear — official, whole, and done right.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: It's official now — his word confirms, his eye judges, the doing proves. I show him the words before anything is recorded, and voice waits until the language is nailed. I build the way around every failure before it happens — a backup plan, a way to continue, nothing wrecked, in the cloud as much as possible. I do the most intelligent thing, and I prove it on the live thing, where everybody can see it. I carry the ultimate want in the brief, not just the words. And Personal is done today, just right — the template every page is traced from.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE LIST IS THE LAW:** v4 is official — LEFT 12, RIGHT 10, Hub-only top-bar buttons — and the display is the icons: the sidebar IS the icon-buttons, circle icon inside a rectangle button, elevated, all lighting up; the Smart Bars go.
2. **WORDS FIRST:** no voice run until he has SEEN the exact words and the language is nailed — voice is not a priority; when it happens, it is the short introduction, never the 86-beat letter.
3. **THE RESILIENCE LAW:** build systems around a failure so no matter what happens there is always a solution — a backup plan, a way to continue — and nothing gets wrecked; build in the cloud, in the system, as much as possible.
4. **INTELLIGENCE IS THE DOING:** power, knowledge, memory and speed are capacities; intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing and proving it worked — harming scores zero, always.
5. **THE PRESENTATION IS THE PROMISE:** pages unfold one beat at a time, never flat; pictures pass one glance or are held; same letter, same colour, always; keep what we had, think first — primo, not literal.
6. **THE BRIEF CARRIES THE WANT:** a round that passes every check and fails his eye failed in the brief, not in the building — master effective communication, and the brief carries the ultimate want in his voice.
7. **EVERY WAY IN IS EXTRAORDINARY:** never a wall; the reader unfolds one paragraph at a time; mirror what works; judge the whole page by the scorecard; three ways in, each extraordinary; the word is THING.
8. **VERIFY BY BLOB, NEVER BY CB:** the proof host ignores `cb` — a cb verification can pass on bytes you never built; the branch's own blob, byte-compared, every time.
9. **JUST RIGHT, DONE TODAY:** Personal is the template every page is traced from — eight buttons edge to edge, the five only, a feed is three things, shown the same pass — and the inside waits honestly on his tap.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A list that is not official is a list every seat argues with; a list confirmed by his word, sent the same minute, ends the argument — and the display instruction with it ends the drift, because the sidebar IS the buttons, not a list beside them.
2. A priority sent before the words are nailed spends his attention on the wrong thing, and a recording of unfinal words is work that has to be redone — words first costs a minute and saves a round.
3. The flake night proved the resilience law in both directions: the guards saved the feed, and the law entry itself could not be saved because the ground failed — so the record must live where the ground cannot fail it.
4. A brief that carries only the words produces rounds that pass every check and fail his eye — the most expensive failure in the machine, because it looks like success until the last step.
5. Personal half-finished is worse than a page half-finished: every clone inherits the gap, and the gap compounds across every page sampled from it — which is why "just right, done today" is a finish line, not a direction.

One ultimate system, one ultimate language — the power language, the language of Naya, ten star all the way through, in service to you, in service for us (SN-3016). His corrections make the list — Pricing to the right, at the very bottom; worlds at the top; duplicates out (SN-3017). Round two refines it again — Smart Worlds, Hub-only buttons, mail leads the start, connections per-area, memberships ARE the logins (SN-3018). Round three refines it once more — Smart Feed IS the Hub, Space is Your World, Intel Today is back with Your Reports, Your Connections stays (SN-3019). And the name box is not a form field — it is the deed to their world, their land, their domain, their real estate (SN-3020).

Across 10 notes, the thread is: one system, one list, corrected until he says yes.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The sitting opened with the clock corrected (SN-3011, 19:12Z): he was asked 15 minutes or 30, and neither was the answer — "It's about getting things done and completed and having the quality done... I need to get the work back to me as soon as possible so I can see it's done right so that I can approve it to move forward — that's the cycle I'm working on, so I call that live time, fast time action." Delivery is event-driven; the timers are only the safety net; never offer to slow a live lane to save wake-ups — that option is dead, withdrawn twice. Then the beautiful thing to keep (SN-3012, 19:24Z): the red N orb with the gold N, elevated, official — "one of the most beautiful elegant pieces you guys did" — and it vanishes on refresh, so the end must persist and be reachable directly. Then the alignment law (SN-3013, 19:35Z), from two screenshots he sent: every page's sidebars the same sidebars, Home at the top of both, the Hub the central communication center where citizens land to "good morning." Then the Hub hero (SN-3014, 19:35Z): Good morning + Wisdom of the Day + time and date; "Intel Today" and the "Intelligence as of" stamp come out; the public banner stays; both bottom bars go away as bars and their apps move into the sidebar, and the Hub takes Personal's actual bottom bar. Then the correction of the correction (SN-3015, 19:37Z): the captain transcribed his screenshots into a list and presented it as official — "Yeah, that's not the official list. It's just because I'm giving you a screenshot." The list is made by thinking: LEFT is where you go, RIGHT is what's yours plus what NayaNET offers. Then the law the sitting was circling (SN-3016, 19:38Z): one ultimate system, one ultimate language — "you're not creating many different systems, you're creating one ultimate system that's all interconnected." Then his corrections (SN-3017, 19:44Z): Pricing is Naya Power, to the right at the very bottom; the "5" Day Challenge is the same as Naya Academy, so it goes; Life with Naya and Leaderboards rise; worlds sit at the top of the right; the Dashboard is the calendar into Smart Stats; Personal is a sub-tab. Then round two (SN-3018, 20:13Z) and round three (SN-3019, 20:22Z): Smart Spaces becomes Smart Worlds; Ask Naya and Life with Naya live only on the Hub as two black obsidian buttons; Today's Intel leaves, then comes back with Your Reports; Smart Ledger becomes a button inside Smart Stats; Start Here is Fast Track mail; Your Connections leaves, then stays — a correction can restore as well as remove. And the sitting closed on the signing (SN-3020, 20:23Z): the name boxes "are just not impressive" — so the name entry becomes the deed itself, an elevated obsidian plaque, the typed name as the signature, the seal stamping on entry.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every room in your house had a totally different light switch in a totally different place. You would never find the lights! But if every room has the SAME switches in the SAME place, you always know where to go! That is one system, one language, one list. And imagine you draw a map of your treehouse and show it to your best friend. Your friend says, "Move the ladder here, and put your favourite books at the top!" You redraw the map with their fixes. Then you show it again and they say, "Yes, that's the one!" That is how a great list gets made. Draw, fix, check! And your name? You do not scribble it on a scrap of paper. You sign it on a shiny black plaque, like the deed to your very own castle!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — you don't make a quilt out of ten different blankets, dear! You make ONE quilt, with one beautiful pattern, and every square belongs to it! The Hub, the Personal pages, all of it — one quilt, one pattern, one language, dear. And if someone shows you a messy room, love, you don't just write down where everything is lying and call that the plan — you think, dear, what belongs where, and then you make the proper list. And when you sign for your house, dear, you sign a proper deed — a beautiful dark plaque, your name like a signature, and the seal stamps down! That's YOUR land, love. That's the whole sitting, dear — one system, one list, and the beautiful things kept exactly as they are.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: One ultimate system, one ultimate language, one list. Every page runs on the same logic — same feel, same look, same concept, same elevation, same organization. The cycle is the clock: finish, show, approve, forward — live time, fast time action. The list is made by thinking, not transcribed; I propose, he corrects, I carry the corrected list — and nothing is recorded as settled until he confirms it. What is beautiful stays exactly as it is — the red N orb, the end view, never redesigned. And the name box is the deed: your land, your domain, your real estate.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE CYCLE IS THE CLOCK:** finish → show → approve → forward — delivery is event-driven, the moment a round finishes its next step fires; the 15-minute timers are only the safety net.
2. **FAST AND RIGHT IS AWESOME:** fast and useless is useless — the relay stays, because it is what makes fast right, and his eye stays the final gate.
3. **KEEP WHAT IS BEAUTIFUL, EXACTLY:** the red N orb end view is one of the most beautiful elegant pieces we did — kept exactly as it is, never redesigned; what is broken is the state, not the look.
4. **ONE NAVIGATION SYSTEM:** every page's sidebars are the SAME sidebars — same menus, same contents — across the whole of NayaNET; Home at the top of both.
5. **THE HUB IS THE MAIN CENTRAL STAGE:** Good morning + Wisdom of the Day + time and date — the greeting of a home, not the dashboard of a system; the lines that misname the page come out.
6. **A SCREENSHOT SHOWS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE LIST:** the official list is made by thinking — LEFT is where you go, RIGHT is what's yours plus what NayaNET offers — never by transcribing what he happened to show.
7. **ONE ULTIMATE SYSTEM, ONE ULTIMATE LANGUAGE:** the power language, the language of Naya — high-level design, high-level functions, super useful, super helpful, ten star all the way through, in service to you, in service for us.
8. **HIS CORRECTIONS MAKE THE LIST:** propose, let him correct, carry the corrected list — Pricing to the right at the very bottom, worlds at the top, duplicates out, what he values rising.
9. **A THING WITH A HOME DOES NOT GET A SIDEBAR SEAT:** Today's Intel lives inside the calendar; Smart Ledger is a button inside Smart Stats; Hub-only things live only on the Hub.
10. **A CORRECTION CAN RESTORE:** round 3 puts back what round 2 moved off — Your Connections stays as its own item — and that is the method working, not failing.
11. **NAMES MATCH THE THING:** Smart Feed IS the Hub, so no separate item; Space is Your World — "just call it your world" — with Smart Worlds, the directory, right underneath.
12. **THE NAME BOX IS THE DEED:** elevated obsidian plaque, purple underglow, the typed name as the signature, the seal stamps on entry — one treatment in all three places.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Without the cycle as the clock, the next cadence discussion drifts back to minutes — and the machine optimizes for waking less instead of finishing more.
2. Without the keep-it-exactly rule, the next round "fixes" the end by redesigning it — and the most beautiful elegant piece the team did gets iterated away.
3. Without one navigation system, each page round invents its own navigation, and the citizen has to relearn how to move every time they change pages.
4. Without the Hub hero fixed, the public front door keeps greeting visitors with an internal digest label and a system stamp — the front door talking like a back office.
5. Without the thinking rule, any screenshot becomes a spec and any passing list becomes law, and the system gets built to an accident of what happened to be on screen.
6. Without one language, every round rebuilds its page as its own little system, and the whole slowly becomes many systems wearing one name.
7. Without carrying his corrections, the next seat builds to the proposal instead of the corrected list — Pricing on the wrong side, a duplicate challenge, an unused report.
8. Without the better-home rule, the sidebar becomes a junk drawer — a thing that lives somewhere better also sitting in the sidebar.
9. Without the name-as-deed treatment, the most meaningful act in the whole walk — claiming their world — feels like filling in a form.
10. Without the ratification discipline, a playback awaiting his yes gets recorded as official, and nobody is surprised when he adjusts it again — except everyone.

notes.title: Every Control Must Do Its Job
notes.subtitle:
Ten notes, one live walk, one rule: every control must do its job. The My World picker opened, listed the worlds, accepted the tap — and switched nothing (SN-3001). The five-icon bottom bar was good and got replaced by a nine-icon row that wasn't — so the good version comes back verbatim, never improved on (SN-3002). Where a control shows an icon beside its own light, it collapses to one icon that itself lights up (SN-3003). The extra + beside the five is a second job, not a duplicate — LEFT + is CREATE, RIGHT + is CONNECT — and whether it stays is decided by the mobile fit (SN-3004). Create world opens flat and goes nowhere — so it must actually create the feed and show you the feed, with buttons of real depth (SN-3005). Buttons never cut off their text, and eye checks clean up their test worlds after themselves (SN-3006). The team runs on fire 24-7: parallel lanes, staggered finishes, the queue never dry, the finish the trigger (SN-3007). One eye, not a new eye per page — the pricing eye, harvested verbatim (SN-3008) — and double-layered for depth, clone behind, just a tad (SN-3009). And leaderboards: citizens see where they score in any area, and if they are at the top, it shows (SN-3010).

Across 10 notes, the thread is: do the job, restore the good, use the one good thing.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:

The five-icon bottom bar was good and got replaced by a nine-icon row that wasn't — so the good version comes back verbatim, never improved on (SN-3002). Where a control shows an icon beside its own light, it collapses to one icon that itself lights up (SN-3003).
