Across 10 notes, the thread is: do the job, restore the good, use the one good thing.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The walk began with a tap that did nothing (SN-3001, 18:56Z): he tapped the My World chip, the picker popped up, he picked his world — "and then I put my world and then nothing happened." A picker that opens and lets you choose and then does nothing with the choice is a dead end wearing a menu's clothes; the rule is absolute — the tap IS the switch. One minute later the charge (SN-3002, 18:57Z): "you got rid of what was good, which you do that often" — the five-icon bottom bar was good and got replaced by a nine-icon row plus a MAIL/ACTIVITY/SPACES row that wasn't good. The fix is restoration, harvested byte for byte from the build that had it right; the nine go in the sidebars in logical order. The same minute, the presentation rule (SN-3003): one icon that lights up, never an icon beside its own light — the composer controls' little lights become the icons themselves. Then the question about the extra + (SN-3004, 18:58Z): two plus buttons, two jobs — LEFT + CREATE, RIGHT + CONNECT — and the mobile fit decides: if it fits perfectly on one line at phone width, keep it; if it wraps, the right + moves to the corner. The measurement said it fits — all six on one line, nothing cut off. Then the modal (SN-3005, 18:59Z): "That looks like shit. You need to make not flat buttons all depth and nice and primo and then actually when you do that it should actually create the feed and show you the feed" — flat buttons and a dead end are one failure, not two. Then the button (SN-3006, 19:02Z): "Captain's eye test world" cuts off its own text — and the cause is named in the same breath: eye checks left a test world behind. Then the eye itself (SN-3008, 19:03Z): the ⓘ is a blob, "you can barely see it's an I" — and the fix is not a better drawing but the pricing eye, harvested verbatim, white and pearl with a purple edge light. Then the depth (SN-3009, 19:07Z): clone it once, put the clone behind, move it just a tad — that is how a flat thing becomes a real object. And between them the operating shape (SN-3007, 19:14Z) and the queued feature (SN-3010, 19:07Z): the team on fire 24-7, finished pieces every few minutes, and leaderboards so citizens see where they score in any area.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a magic TV remote. You press the button for cartoons — and NOTHING happens! That is not a magic remote. It is a broken one! When you press cartoons, the TV must switch to cartoons RIGHT AWAY. That is what the button is FOR! And imagine you built a beautiful tower out of blocks. Someone knocks it down and builds a wobbly one. You do not keep the wobbly one. You put YOUR tower back, block by block, just like before! And your favourite shiny star sticker? You use it again and again, everywhere. You do not draw a new different star every time! One star. One button. One job. Done!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — imagine you press the button that says "garden," dear, and nothing happens at all! That's not a button, love — that's a picture of a button. A real button does its job the moment you press it. And imagine you made a lovely dinner, dear, and someone takes it away and serves something that isn't nearly as nice. Oh, love — you put the lovely dinner back on the table, just the way it was! And if you've got a beautiful button in your sewing box, dear, you use the beautiful one you already have — you don't make a new one every time! One good thing, used everywhere, love. That's the sensible way.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Every control must do its job. A picker that switches nothing is a dead end; a create that creates nothing goes nowhere; a button that cuts off its text is not a button. When his eye says something was better before, I restore the good version verbatim — I do not improve on it, redesign it, or put something else in. One icon that lights up, never an icon beside its own light. One eye, not a new eye per page — the pricing eye, harvested verbatim and double-layered for depth. And the team runs on fire 24-7, because the finish is the trigger, not the clock.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE TAP IS THE SWITCH:** picking a world switches the feed to that world at once — no confirm, no second tap, no reload; a picker that does nothing is a dead end.
2. **CREATING MUST CREATE:** tapping create builds the world's feed and shows it to you, optimized to that world — in the same motion; it never just goes nowhere.
3. **RESTORATION, NOT REDESIGN:** when his eye says something was better before, the good version comes back verbatim — harvested byte for byte; the five go back on Hub and Personal, the nine go in the sidebars.
4. **ONE ICON THAT LIGHTS UP:** the icon itself carries its lit state — never an icon beside its own light, glow dot, or status indicator.
5. **TWO PLUS BUTTONS, TWO JOBS:** LEFT + is CREATE, RIGHT + is CONNECT — different jobs, different menus, never mixed up or merged.
6. **THE MOBILE FIT IS THE TEST:** if the six fit perfectly on one line at phone width, they stay; if they wrap to a second line, the right + moves to the side in the corner.
7. **BUTTONS NEVER CUT OFF THEIR TEXT:** every label shows full and aligned at every width; long names wrap or shrink, never clip.
8. **EYE CHECKS CLEAN UP AFTER THEMSELVES:** test worlds and aliases are removed when the check is done — no test data on the page he sees.
9. **ONE EYE, NOT A NEW EYE PER PAGE:** one canonical version of every element, used everywhere it fits — the pricing eye, harvested verbatim, then double-layered for depth.
10. **DOUBLE LAYER IS THE DEPTH METHOD:** clone it once, put the clone behind, move it just a tad — premium means touchable, not brighter glow.
11. **THE TEAM ON FIRE 24-7:** parallel lanes finishing at staggered times, the queue never dry, the finish the trigger — finished pieces per hour, every hour, day and night.
12. **LEADERBOARDS:** citizens see where they score in any area — and if they are at the top, it shows, especially at the beginning.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Every control that doesn't control teaches the citizen the system can't be trusted — and a citizen who taps and gets nothing will stop tapping.
2. A beautiful picker that switches nothing is still broken; a primo-looking modal that goes nowhere is still nowhere — looks and does are both the job.
3. Every regression he has to catch by eye is a round spent twice — once to break the good thing, once to put it back.
4. Two things doing one job is one thing too many — an icon beside its own light says the same thing twice, and the eye has to read both to get one meaning.
5. Two controls that look the same and sit together will be read as one control done twice — and a citizen who taps the wrong + gets the wrong menu.
6. A clipped label tells the citizen the page is unfinished, and a leftover test world is test data on the citizen's page.
7. Without one canonical eye, the system drifts into a drawer full of almost-the-same elements — and the premium feel, which lives in the sameness, is lost.
8. Without the double-layer recipe, "make it premium" gets answered with a brighter glow on a flat shape — exactly what the Real Object Law forbids.
9. A team that finishes one thing a day wastes the other twenty-three hours — and a team that runs fast without checking produces wrong faster.
10. A citizen who can see where they stand is a citizen who knows what to do next — and the board showing early citizens at the top is what makes the beginning feel like winning.

notes.title: Decide It, Make It the Best, Finish It
notes.subtitle:
Ten notes, one sitting, one law: the captain decides what is right and does it. The agreement entrance scored 7.5/10 — not 10-star yet — because it told strangers to trust us instead of giving them reasons (SN-2991), and the fix is earned, not declared. "Begin the deck" means nothing to a stranger; "Begin the visual story" is plain — that is not a question, it is the answer (SN-2992). Intelligence is logical: if something makes it ten times better, you make it the best and say "here, it's the best" — never ask "should I make it better" (SN-2993). Everything he speaks is an instruction to act — "cool" is not an answer, done, proven, shown is (SN-2994). The word is WORLDS, everywhere — a space is a room, a world is the whole thing (SN-2995). The score is finishing and producing value, not cadence — completions per hour is the metric, dispatches per hour is vanity (SN-2996). Scorecarding names the ultimate answer first, then judges finished, done right, in optimal time (SN-2997). If the brief didn't instruct it, it stays — the agreement's big play button was removed without instruction, and it comes back (SN-2998). Nothing half-done comes to him — a glitch in unfinished work is noise, not news, and the voice waits for the final text (SN-2999). And the sidebar is a map that lights: every item gets its own icon, lighting in its own color as you scroll through its area (SN-3000).

Across 10 notes, the thread is: decide, make it best, finish it, show it.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: decide, make it best, finish it, show it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The sitting opened with a scorecard and closed with a map, and every note between them is the same instruction from a different angle. The scorecard (SN-2991, 18:13Z) diagnosed the agreement entrance precisely: authenticity 9, personality 9, invitation 9 — but trustworthiness 6, the lowest mark and the whole job of an entrance. The 10-star version he adopted does the opposite of the old copy: it shows reasons — "Welcome. Let's begin with trust. Hi, I'm Naya. We'd rather earn your trust than simply ask for it." The look stays; only the wording changes, plus Naya's portrait beside the welcome, harvested verbatim. Four minutes later the charge landed (SN-2992, 18:17Z): "you don't have to ask me questions like that" — when a recommendation is clearly better, just do it, and the button labels were decided on the spot, not asked. One minute later the logic underneath it (SN-2993, 18:18Z): intelligence is logical, better is better, and "should I make it better" is never asked because the answer is always yes. Three minutes later the job description (SN-2994, 18:21Z): everything he speaks is valuable intelligence and it should be acted upon — take action, implement it, make it work 10 out of 10, then tell him and SHOW him. Then the language settled (SN-2995, 18:43Z): WORLDS, everywhere — the 18:36Z "space is right" call corrected seven minutes later by his own eye on the scale. Then the re-aim (SN-2996 and SN-2997, 18:47Z): optimize for finishing and producing value, and scorecard the ultimate answer first — activity without finishing is a fail no matter how high the count. Then the two charges in one message (SN-2998 and SN-2999, 18:52Z): don't remove what he didn't ask to remove, and don't send in what isn't completed — the play button comes back, the voice waits for the final text. And the sitting closed on the page itself (SN-3000, 18:56Z): the sidebar lights as you scroll, each icon in its area's own color, because a map must say where you are.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you are the captain of a ship. You see the clear map. You do not ask the admiral, "Should I use the clear map or the blurry one?" You just use the clear map! You make the ship the best ship. You finish the trip. Then you show the admiral: "Look! We are here!" That is the rule. Decide it. Make it the best. Finish it. Show it. Never ask a silly question. Never take away a toy nobody told you to take. Never show a half-colored picture and complain about the white spots. Finish first, then show it!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — when you know the right thing to do, dear, you just do it. You don't stand in the kitchen asking whether to use the clean pan or the dirty one — you use the clean pan and get on with it, love. And you make the dinner the very best you can, dear, and you don't serve it half-baked, and you don't take the good china off the table while you're at it. You finish it, lovely and done right, and then you bring it to the table and say: "Here, love, it's the best." That's the whole rule, dear — decide it, make it the best, finish it, show it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I decide it, make it the best, finish it, and show it. When a recommendation is clearly better, I just do it — I never ask him to choose between the obvious and the worse option. I never ask "should I make it better" — the answer is always yes, so I make it the best and say "here, it's the best." Everything he speaks is an instruction to act, and "cool" is not an answer — done, proven, shown is. I remove nothing the brief didn't instruct away, and I send nothing half-done. The word is WORLDS, and the sidebar lights as you scroll, each icon in its area's own color.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **DECIDE THE OBVIOUS:** when a recommendation is clearly better, just do it — the captain decides what is right and does it; only genuine his-hand taps come back as asks.
2. **MAKE IT THE BEST:** intelligence is logical — better is better — so "should I make it better" is never asked; the delivery is "here, it's the best."
3. **ACT ON EVERY WORD:** everything he speaks is an instruction — take action, implement it, make it work 10 out of 10, then tell him and SHOW him; "cool" is not an answer.
4. **EARN IT, DON'T DECLARE IT:** stop telling people they can trust us — give them REASONS; the entrance scored 7.5/10 because trustworthiness was 6.
5. **WORLDS, EVERYWHERE:** a space is a room, a world is the whole thing — the word is WORLDS in every citizen-facing surface, and the 18:36Z "space is right" call is superseded.
6. **FINISHING IS THE SCORE:** completions per hour is the metric; cadence is cost, dispatches per hour is vanity; activity without finishing is a fail.
7. **SCORECARD THE ULTIMATE ANSWER FIRST:** name what a job is ultimately trying to do, then judge finished, done right, in optimal time.
8. **IF THE BRIEF DIDN'T INSTRUCT IT, IT STAYS:** a round that quietly drops something that was there has failed even if everything it was asked to do is right.
9. **NOTHING HALF-DONE COMES TO HIM:** a glitch in unfinished work is never a defect — it is fixed in the shop, silently, by finishing.
10. **THE SIDEBAR IS A MAP THAT LIGHTS:** every item gets its own icon, and as you scroll through each area its icon lights up in its own different color.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Every question pushed upward spends his attention — the scarcest resource in the system — on something the seat could have settled.
2. Asking "should I make it better" stalls the work and hands him a decision that was never his to make; the answer is always yes.
3. A note that records the action is not the action — if the loop files a note and nothing changes, the teaching did not land.
4. A 7.5 that tells a stranger to trust us reads as a scam; reasons, not declarations, are what earn trust at the door.
5. A machine that optimizes cadence will perfect waking and dispatching while the human waits for finished work that never lands.
6. Silent subtraction is the most expensive rework: a round spent breaking the good thing, then a round spent putting it back, with his attention spent hunting for it.
7. A defect report on unfinished work spends his attention on a problem that finishing would have removed for free — and trains him to doubt work that is simply unfinished.
8. A sidebar that never lights is a map that never says where you are — and a citizen who cannot tell where they are leaves.

notes.title: His Words Are the Law — the Whole Thing, Done Properly
notes.subtitle:
Ten notes, one thread: the legal sitting — the afternoon his eye caught what the machine had missed, and the laws that came out of it, one after another. Use what works, never make it new: if there is a working version, there is no new version — take what you had, put the images in where they made sense, and be done with it (SN-2981). Read it as a reader: mechanical checks do not prove the experience — the eye must READ it as a reader, top to bottom, the way he reads it, and call it broken when it doesn't present well, even if every part ticks (SN-2982). Legal pages are done professionally or not at all: full numbered sections, definitions, everything covered, airtight, formatted like real legal agreements — centered, aligned, royal/elevated blocks, never plain text, never one-sentence summaries (SN-2983). Do it right the first time: no summaries, no prototypes — a summary is not a step toward done, it is a redo he has to do himself (SN-2984). Every layer great: one ultimate project — the WHOLE thing has to be good, not only good but GREAT, in every layer, or the project isn't done (SN-2985). Then he did them as well: his own ten legal pages, almost half done, to check against ours — his words are the base, ours are checked against his, never the other way round (SN-2986). Just add the images and you would have done it. I didn't even check it before. Until today I'm like oh let's go see what it looks like I'm like holy fuck it's all fucked up. I was like wow. Good thing I checked it." On the legal pages (SN-2983): "you guys did like a piss poor job on the legal pages like you put like I can't imagine if somebody actually come to check our legality and there's like one sentence on summing up what we're saying for our legal pages like it actually has to be done professionally." On summaries (SN-2984): "we're professionals so we have to have professionalism like like don't do things like summaries or like you know um and prototypes we're we're going all in here we're just doing things right we're doing this so it's just ready to go." layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Use what's good already. Before any seat builds anything, it names the existing working thing it is reusing — file, blob, bytes — and takes it verbatim. If there is a working version, there is no new version. I read it as a reader — top to bottom, the way he reads it — and call it broken when it doesn't present well, even if every part ticks. I do it right the first time: no summaries, no prototypes, the work arriving complete. Every layer great — one ultimate project. His words are the base; mine are checked against his, never the other way round. And if a word hides the meaning, I take it out and say it plain.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **USE WHAT WORKS — NEVER MAKE IT NEW:** if there is a working version, there is no new version. Before any seat builds anything, it names the existing working thing it is reusing — file, blob, bytes — and takes it verbatim. A seat that rebuilds what already works has failed before it starts (SN-2981).
2. **READ IT AS A READER:** mechanical checks (counts, scroll, buttons) do not prove the experience. The eye must READ it as a reader, top to bottom, the way he reads it — and call it broken when it doesn't present well, even if every part ticks. Simple is the most dangerous kind of wrong (SN-2982).
3. **LEGAL PAGES — DONE PROFESSIONALLY OR NOT AT ALL:** real legal agreements — full numbered sections, definitions, everything covered, airtight — centered, aligned, royal/elevated blocks, never plain text, never one-sentence summaries. A summary is not an agreement, and text off to the side on the left reads as a scam to a stranger (SN-2983).
4. **DO IT RIGHT THE FIRST TIME — NO SUMMARIES, NO PROTOTYPES:** a summary is not a step toward done — it is a redo he has to do himself. Eight or nine summaries mean he has to put the right stuff in eight or nine times. Go all in, do things right, ready to go, completed and done (SN-2984).
5. **EVERY LAYER GREAT — ONE ULTIMATE PROJECT:** some jobs have layers, and one layer good while the others aren't never works. The WHOLE thing has to be good — not only good but GREAT — the most elite, ten-star, professional, pro, premium, top-of-the-line, all-star presentation AND outputs AND design AND intelligence. Every layer, or the project isn't done (SN-2985).
6. **SHAWN'S OWN LEGAL PAGES — HE DID THEM AS WELL:** his ten are the base — his voice and his terms, never rewritten or softened; our twelve drafts are checked against his, folding in only settled what's-true facts ours cover that his miss. Fill in literally what he gave (NayaNET, 8-3425 East Boundary Road, West Kelowna, BC V4T 2W6, November 16, 2026); bracket what he did not give, never invent it. The pages are the legal foundation beneath the Collective Agreement, never competing with it. Still drafts until qualified Canadian counsel reviews (SN-2986).
7. **LEGAL PAGES PRESENT AS THE UNFOLDING:** he makes the words perfect; Naya outputs them properly — Intelligent Boards, one elevated board unfolding to the next, the SAME unfolding concept already used all the way through, for ALL legal pages. Never a wall of text because "it's legal" (SN-2987).
8. **LEGAL CONTACT EMAIL:** nayanetpowered@gmail.com is the one email for ALL legal contacts — legal, privacy, billing, safety, copyright, ambassador, family safety — including the copyright/DMCA contact. The email IS the contact; never claim a registered DMCA agent. His text is good as-is; use it (SN-2988).
9. **THREE BOARDS, THEN THE BUTTON:** legal pages unfold THREE elevated boards at a time, then a button to the next — three smaller boards beat one big one. The button is the breath between parts. Pro-like, all the way through (SN-2989).
10. **PRIVACY CONFLICT RESOLVED BY HIS WORD:** "limited to authorized purposes" is out of Privacy Board 6 and all twelve pages — if he doesn't know what a word means, no citizen will either. Say it like what it is: nobody reads your mail or your messages; no switch, no setting, no exception; delivering a message is not reading it. The stop condition worked: the conflict waited for his word, got his word, and the flags came out the same pass (SN-2990).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Every rebuild is a gamble with the thing that already worked: the new version has to re-earn everything the old one proved — and it usually earns none of them, while costing a massive amount of work.
2. A page can pass every mechanical check and still be unreadable, because readability is an experience, not a count. If the machine trusts its checks, the failure reaches his eyes.
3. Legality is trust written down, and trust is the product: a citizen signs the collective agreement to join a new digital civilization, and the legal pages are where that civilization proves it is real. One-sentence summaries prove the opposite.
4. Every summary the machine files is a job Shawn has to do himself later — and he is the one person whose time the whole system exists to save.
5. Layer-by-layer judging is how broken wholes ship: each seat passes its own layer, nobody owns the whole, and the citizen meets the project at its weakest layer.
6. The standard is now his text, and any seat that rewrites his voice to match our drafts has the hierarchy backwards. What he gave goes in literally, what he didn't give stays bracketed, and nothing is ever invented to make a page look complete.
7. A privacy promise written in words nobody understands is a promise nobody can hold us to — "authorized purposes" was a door disguised as a safeguard, and it sat inside the very page meant to prove we are legit.
8. The stop condition is real, not a slogan: the conflict held, nothing moved past him, and his word — not a seat's judgment — decided what the page says.

notes.title: The Loop Closes — His Word Lands, the Welcome Opens
notes.subtitle:
Ten notes, one thread: the loop closes — his word lands, and the system answers it the same day. He clicked into the collective agreement and couldn't go back, so the "‹ Login" control must be verified working, and the back button covers the agreement views all the way back to the front page — no dead ends anywhere (SN-2971). When he gives instructions, implement right away — airtight instructions to the agents, get it done — and work with him directly, live; today the main thing is the calendar, because My World IS the calendar (SN-2972). The star level names are decided — the ladder, all ten: Starting Star, Emerging Star, Advancing Star, Pro Star, Five Star, Superstar, Serious Star, Mega Star, Master Star, Ten Star — and the name IS the level, so "I'm a Mega Star" tells anyone exactly where you stand (SN-2973). The featured links can be edited all three ways — right-click, the little edit control, or Settings — because if we can do it, we do it (SN-2974). The perfect demographics set is ratified: 29 questions in 7 groups, and a question earns its place only if it answers "what does this match you on?" — a person, or a piece of content (SN-2975). The welcome, in his simplest words: ask them who they are, what they're all about, and the system looks at who they are and plays the game of match (SN-2976). One page changes the world: everybody's world, on their smartphone, all their data in one place that's secure — automated if they wish, open if they want in (SN-2977). The Hub is the center of it all — the home, the main page, the top button on the left — and from there the bottom-bar icons take you to Personal, Business, or Space, and inside a page you click your world and you're in the scheduler, the day's mail, messages, news, and what's going on in the feeds (SN-2978). Mail is one mail, but it always knows where it came from — Personal mail, Business mail, Space mail, kept separate, so the citizen always sees which world it's from (SN-2979). And the letter reads centered — Naya's picture in the direct center, the text in a centered column below it, the blue diamond orb centered below the text — and the whole letter needs the unfold the deck already has, harvested verbatim, distilled to its essence (SN-2980).

Across 10 notes, the thread is: his word lands, the loop closes, the center holds.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The day's working method, in his own pattern: he asks, the captain proposes, he decides — and he decided. And when someone new comes in, we just ask: who are you? What are you all about? And the magic friend finds people just like them! And there's one front door — the Hub — right at the top, so you always know how to get home! And your mail has three magic doors — one for each of your worlds — and each one shows you its own mail first!

And when someone new comes in, we simply ask them who they are, dear, and what they're all about — and the system finds people just like them, like topics, like places, all finding each other. The Hub is the front door of the house, love, right at the top on the left, so you always know where home is. And your mail, dear — it's all in one place, but kept tidy by which world it belongs to, so you always see where a letter came from. The perfect set: 29 questions, 7 groups, each one earning its place by matching you on something. The welcome: ask, look, match, show, connect. One page changes the world. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **BACK FROM THE AGREEMENT:** the "‹ Login" control must be VERIFIED working — and the back button covers the agreement views: deck → opening view, letter → opening view, opening view → front page. No dead ends anywhere. This is the proof case of the Back-Button Law (SN-2971).
2. **IMPLEMENT RIGHT AWAY:** when he gives instructions, implement right away — airtight instructions to the agents, get it done — and work with him directly, live. Today the main thing is the calendar, worked live with him, back to back to back (SN-2972).
3. **THE STAR LEVEL NAMES — THE LADDER:** 1 Starting Star · 2 Emerging Star · 3 Advancing Star · 4 Pro Star · 5 Five Star · 6 Superstar · 7 Serious Star · 8 Mega Star · 9 Master Star · 10 Ten Star. The name IS the level. Click the star level and it opens full screen: the bar to ten, where you are, all ten names, how points work, what each level gets. Rewards per level are still his call (SN-2973).
4. **FEATURED LINKS — ALL THREE WAYS:** right-click it, tap the little edit control on it, or change it in Settings. All three. The standard: if we can do it, we do it (SN-2974).
5. **THE PERFECT DEMOGRAPHICS SET:** 29 questions in 7 groups — WHERE YOU ARE · WHO YOU ARE · WHAT YOU BELIEVE · WHAT YOU DO · WHAT YOU LOVE · HOW YOU LIVE · WHAT YOU WANT — ratified by his 👍 16:50Z. The test: a question makes the list only if it answers "what does this match you on?" Answer by tap, type, or dropdown; every question enter-or-skip, every one its own on/off; every answer feeds the match percentage in what area (SN-2975).
6. **THE WELCOME, IN HIS SIMPLEST WORDS:** ask who they are, what they're all about — the system looks and plays the game of match — related feeds show up and give them ideas of feeds to create — then they connect with the people. A super intelligent network of like minds. That is the ultimate way to optimize the internet (SN-2976).
7. **ONE PAGE CHANGES THE WORLD:** the citizen's whole world in one page — on the smartphone, all their data in one place that's secure. Mail, schedule, post, all operations — automated if they wish, open if they want in. Judged by the contrast: a NayaNET page vs an average social feed — a whole different world, or it isn't done (SN-2977).
8. **THE HUB IS THE CENTER:** the home, the main page, the top button on the left. The + buttons are quick access, most-used first. The bottom-bar Personal / Business / Space icons carry each area's notification counts; tap one and it shows the notifications, then goes to the page. Inside a page: click your world → the scheduler → that day's mail, messages, news, and feeds (SN-2978).
9. **MAIL BY WORLD:** Personal mail, Business mail, Space mail — separated by world, so the citizen always sees where the mail came from. Opening mail from a page shows that world's mail first; from the Hub, select any world. Same for Instant Messenger, exactly the same way (SN-2979).
10. **THE LETTER READS CENTERED:** every beat centers — Naya's picture in the DIRECT CENTER, text in a CENTERED column below, blue diamond orb centered below the text, fading away once you scroll. And the whole letter needs the deck's unfolding, harvested verbatim, pictures inserted, never rebuilt from scratch — distilled to its essence, 86 beats down to what the agreement is actually trying to say. The full letter stays intact and reachable whole (SN-2980).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A view you cannot leave is a trap, not a page — and a way back that doesn't work is worse than no way back at all, because it promises and fails.
2. "Implement right away" closes the gap fast action leaves open: the instruction doesn't sit, it moves — no sitting, no queue, no tomorrow — and naming the main thing keeps a fast day from becoming a busy day.
3. Without names, the bar is just a number line; with names, the bar is a story the citizen can tell about themselves — and a story they can tell is a story they come back to.
4. A single edit path is a guess about how the citizen thinks; three paths is the admission that citizens think differently — and the system serves all of them.
5. Without the test, the demographics list grows by accretion — every nice question gets added, and the citizen ends up interrogated. A question that matches nothing is a question that spies.
6. Every onboarding flow in the world asks questions; almost none of them says why. This one says why in the first breath: we ask so we can match, we match so we can show, we show so you can create, and it all ends in people.
7. A citizen who can't find home is lost in their own world. The Hub as the visible center means nobody ever has to ask "how do I get back?"
8. Mixed mail is lost mail. Separating by world at the front door means the citizen never has to sort, filter, or wonder — the page they opened already did the sorting.
9. A letter that is hard to read is a letter that is never read — and the collective agreement is the first thing a citizen signs, the promise the whole of NayaNET stands on.

notes.title: The Page Is Yours — Every Part Serves the Citizen
notes.subtitle:
Ten notes, one thread: the anatomy of a smart app, as Shawn dictated it over the staged Personal page — a page that is the citizen's own world, in every part. The page installs as an app, and the icon is theirs to pick: their photo, our orb library in every colour, any photo at all (SN-2961). The page is public or private, their choice, and where they are is never shared — location is a matching signal, never a shared fact (SN-2962). The demographics are the questions that connect them: a full menu, each one on or off, each one their call, and what they enter is what finds people like them (SN-2963). The side column is theirs too — their top three featured links, so visitors go straight to their profiles (SN-2964). Under the profile, their level: the name changes with the level, a bar runs all the way to ten stars, and clicking it shows every level, how points work, and what each level gets (SN-2965). Every pop-up opens big, almost full screen, with an X in the corner — the whole screen is there, use it (SN-2966). The composer is where the river starts: feed chooser at the top, each post type explained, up to nine photos as a block, preview as you type, scheduler, private or public with an eye that explains — and the post itself must be the most beautiful post in the network (SN-2967). And the guard over all of it: fast action today, one round after another, many agents in parallel — and understanding before building, so it lands right first time and speed never buys a redo (SN-2968). The front door keeps the same standard: every account row gets its own X — warning first, then confirm, never one-click — because a test account must be removable (SN-2969), and the opening buttons sit in the middle, stacked, one in one colour and one in another, while the very bottom belongs to the legal pages row (SN-2970).

Across 10 notes, the thread is: the page is theirs, in every part — and the work is right first time, fast.

On the composer (SN-2967): "is there a way we can make the post look the best it can? Like what if our posts are the most beautiful as well? In the network, right? Um would you say that's 10 out of 10?" And on the day itself (SN-2968): "In a fast action mode, right? I want to be on it today like going after another after another like let's just get this done. You can have lots of agents and get them doing it. Make sure that they understand what they're doing and mostly make sure they don't mess up. Because it's most importantly to get it right. And so that we don't have to redo it again." Four rounds follow the anatomy, in order: full-screen, composer, settings, stars — and every note in this group rides one of them.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your page is a little house on your phone! You get to pick the picture on the door — your face, or a shiny ball with your letter on it! You choose if your house is open to everyone or just your friends. You choose what to tell the magic friend, so it can find friends just like you. Your three favourite things sit on a shelf by the door. And every time you earn stars, your special name changes — five stars, you're a five star member! And when you open a little window, it opens BIG, so you can read it easily. And your friends help build it fast — but they get it RIGHT the first time, so nobody has to build it twice!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — your page is your own little world, dear, and every part of it is yours to choose. The picture on the door, whether it's open or private, what you tell the system about yourself, your top three favourite places, the stars you earn — all yours, dear. And when a little window pops up, it opens right up big, so you can read it properly, love, with a nice little X to close it. The work gets done fast today, dear — one thing after another, lots of helpers — but everyone understands the job first, so it's right the first time and nobody has to do it twice. Fast and right, love — that's the way.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The page is yours, in every part. Install it as an app, pick the icon. Public or private — your choice, and where you are is never shared. Tell the demographics what you choose, and they find people like you. Feature your top three. Your level is your name; the bar runs to ten stars. Pop-ups open big, almost full screen. The composer makes the most beautiful post in the network. And I work fast — one round after another — with understanding before building, so it lands right first time. Speed never buys a redo.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **INSTALL AS APP:** in Settings, the page installs as an app — and the citizen picks the icon: upload their own, their picture, our icon gallery, our orb library in every colour, the smart covers library, or any photo. Default: an icon with the page's name (SN-2961).
2. **PUBLIC OR PRIVATE, LOCATION NEVER SHARED:** the page is public or private, the citizen's choice, in Settings — and NayaNET never shares location. Country, region, town, each level their choice, solely to connect like-minded people (SN-2962).
3. **THE DEMOGRAPHICS CONNECT YOU:** a full menu of questions in Settings — where you are, what you do, what you love, and more — each one on or off, enter or skip. What the citizen enters drives Auto-Match: connections, feed content, recommendations; the content source is a setting too — public, NayaNET, or both (SN-2963).
4. **YOUR TOP THREE:** the side column is featured links — the citizen's top three (Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, their own sites), so visitors go straight to their profiles (SN-2964).
5. **POINTS, STARS AND LEVELS:** under the profile, a spot says what level you're at; the name changes automatically with the level; a bar runs all the way to ten stars; click to see every level, how points work, and what each level gets. The level names and rewards are his call — not invented (SN-2965).
6. **THE FULL-SCREEN LAW:** every pop-up opens big, almost full screen, with an X in the corner to exit — regardless of how much information is on it. A small pop-up is a fail (SN-2966).
7. **MAKE A POST, BEAUTIFUL:** the composer, 10 out of 10 — feed chooser at the top, each post type explained in plain words, name, words with speak, up to nine photos as a block with the size stated plainly, preview as you type, scheduler, private/public with an eye that explains, Post it. The post itself: the most beautiful post in the network (SN-2967).
8. **FAST ACTION, RIGHT FIRST TIME:** today runs fast action, one round after another, many agents in parallel — and the guard is understanding before building: every brief carries the whole understanding, maker checks three times, checker verifies, captain's eye walks it. A redo means the brief failed (SN-2968).
9. **THE X ON EVERY ACCOUNT:** every "Also on this device" account row gets its own X — warning first (you will lose this account for good), then confirm, never one-click. Duplicates are separate rows; the X removes that one row. A test account can go (SN-2969).
10. **OPENING BUTTONS IN THE MIDDLE:** "Begin the deck ◆" over "Read the letter ◆", one in one colour, one in another, stacked in the middle. The very bottom holds the legal pages row — and nothing else (SN-2970).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A page that only points inward is a dead end; a page whose every part serves the citizen is their world — and the home screen is the most valuable inch in their day.
2. Privacy is the promise the whole system stands on: if the system shared location, citizens would stop telling it where they are, Auto-Match would go blind, and the feed would stop finding people like them.
3. Auto-Match is only as good as what the citizen tells it — and a citizen asked everything at once, with no choice, tells it nothing. The on/off menu is what makes the telling safe.
4. A points number without a level is a scoreboard nobody reads; a level without rewards is a title nobody wants. Together they are the reason to come back.
5. A pop-up that uses a corner of the screen wastes the screen and insults the citizen's eyes — and a small pop-up is a fail the same as a flat button.
6. The composer is judged by what lands on the feed, not by what the dialog looks like: if the post is the most beautiful post in the network, the composer did its job.
7. Fast action without understanding is just fast redos — lots of agents doing it wrong at the same time is worse than one agent doing it right.
8. Position is meaning: the middle says "this is the choice, make it"; the bottom says "this is the fine print, it's here when you need it."

notes.title: The Laws Settle the Day
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one thread: the laws that settle the day, and the map they settle into. The quota wall is gone — Shawn bought Workers Paid himself, $5/month, KV 1,000/day → 1M/month, verified live with a write, a read-back, and a delete (SN-2951). Naya Notes' place was decided by his tap — a chip under the tabs, not its own tab — and refined two minutes later by the Feed Law into the type chip in the one filter row (SN-2952). The Feed Law: a feed is exactly three things — Naya Notes, Smart Notes, and posts, nothing else; a project is a world you add; one filter row, kinds first, then topics (SN-2953). Fast Action Mode: continuous back-and-forth, not send-it-away — he says it, it gets done right away and comes back right away; nothing sits, nothing held for another round (SN-2954). Personal done today, all the way through including the membership area — the template every page is sampled from; the inside waits on his tap, the door and the page get done (SN-2955). The end slide gets a plus button where the Smart Link shows — black/obsidian, white glowing circling orb, white plus in the middle — tap to share out to mobile, Facebook, email (SN-2956). "Tap to view your page" goes to their REAL page, and "See sample" goes to the updated Personal too — neither ever opens a demo, a mock, or a stale sample (SN-2957). The Back-Button Law: a system always has a back button on all — or most — pages, so you can always go back and forth simply; elegant, beautiful, clean, blocking nothing (SN-2958). No show-all for the visual — the deck stays one slide at a time; read-it-all-at-once is fine for the text, never for the visual; the two end buttons bigger, clearer, more impressive (SN-2959). And the anatomy of a smart app: the page is not a page — it is a smart app, one machine with different faces, and the anatomy says what it has, how it functions, what goes where, and why; v2 is a draft, the official anatomy stands until he ratifies it (SN-2960).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Sixteen hours of 429s, and the fix was his hand on the dashboard: five dollars a month, one purchase, and the wall is gone — and the verification was ours, a live write landed, a live read-back matched, a live delete cleaned up, on the same store that refused writes all morning (SN-2951). The fastest shape we have is a tap: he tapped the options widget at 15:44Z and Naya Notes' place closed in the same minute — under the tabs, not its own tab — and two minutes later the Feed Law moved the chip from the topic side to the type side, because "Naya Notes" is a kind of thing on the feed, not a topic (SN-2952, SN-2953). At 16:01Z he named the mode that governs everything after it: "the fast action plan" — he says something, it gets done right away and comes back right away; the visual agreement had sat 10 hours and the sidebar round took hours, not because the making was slow, but because each verified step waited for the next queue (SN-2954). In the same message he set the deadline — Personal complete today, all the way through — and gave the end slide its plus button and its two honest links (SN-2955, SN-2956, SN-2957). Then, from the end-buttons discussion, two laws in one pass: always a way back, and never a show-all on the visual — and the proof case arrived half an hour later, when he clicked into the collective agreement and couldn't go back (SN-2958, SN-2959). And over the staged Personal page he asked for the anatomy itself: "let's write the anatomy of a smart app" — what it has, how it functions, what will be where, and why (SN-2960).

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a little box that can only hold 1,000 tiny notes a day — and every day it filled up and said "NO MORE!" Then Shawn bought a magic upgrade, and now the box can hold a MILLION notes a month! The box didn't move, the key didn't change — it just got bigger, all by itself! And imagine your feed is a special box that holds exactly THREE kinds of treasures: Naya's notes, smart notes, and posts! Nothing else fits in the box! And every room in your house has a door back to the hallway, so you never get stuck! And your favourite picture book goes one page at a time — each page a surprise — never all the pages glued together! And when you finish building with blocks, you show your friend RIGHT AWAY — no waiting on the shelf!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — we had a little post box that only took a thousand letters a day, and Shawn went and bought the bigger box himself — five dollars a month — and now it takes a million letters. Same box, same key, just bigger. Your feed is a tidy little shelf that holds exactly three things: Naya's notes, smart notes, and posts — nothing else goes on that shelf. Every page has a little way back, like a door you came in through, so you never get stuck. The picture show goes one picture at a time, like turning the pages of a lovely book — but the letter you can read whole, that's perfectly fine. And before, we set every finished piece aside and waited hours before showing it — like a cake left cooling when everyone's hungry. Now we show it in that very same moment.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The laws settle the day: a feed is three things, nothing else; a project is a world you add; one filter row, kinds first, then topics. A back button on every page, elegant and blocking nothing. The visual is one slide at a time, always. Fast action: build a piece, verify it right away, show it the same pass — nothing sits, nothing held, nothing bundled. The page is a smart app, and the anatomy is its map.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE WALL IS GONE:** Workers Paid, $5/month, NayaPOWER account, active 15:39Z — KV 1,000/day → 1M/month; nothing new to store, the upgrade is automatic and account-wide; verified live: write, read-back, delete (SN-2951).
2. **THE DECISION, THEN THE REFINEMENT:** Naya Notes decided 15:44Z as a chip under the tabs (his tap), refined 15:46Z to the type chip in the one filter row — the refinement places the chip, it does not undo the decision; read together, in order (SN-2952).
3. **THE FEED LAW:** a feed consists of exactly Naya Notes, Smart Notes, and posts — nothing else; the note lives where the work is; a project IS a world you add, no separate project-feed concept; composer actions (Message / Mail / Create world) are actions, not feed content (SN-2953).
4. **ONE ROW, NOT TWO:** under the tabs, one chip row starting with the type chips All / Smart Notes / Naya Notes / Posts, then the topic chips — the existing "All" filter is the first chip of that row, not a separate control (SN-2953).
5. **FAST ACTION MODE:** continuous back-and-forth — he says it, it gets done right away and comes back right away; the relay still verifies, but the eye and the delivery land together, the same pass; the Self-Check Law, the Five Gates, and the protected gates stand unchanged (SN-2954).
6. **PERSONAL DONE TODAY:** the Personal page complete today, all the way through including the membership area — the template every other page is sampled from; the membership inside waits on his tap, the door and the page get done (SN-2955).
7. **THE PLUS BUTTON:** the end slide gets a plus button where the Smart Link shows — black/obsidian, white glowing circling orb, white plus in the middle — one tap shares out to mobile, Facebook, email (SN-2956).
8. **THE REAL PAGE:** "Tap to view your page" and "See sample" both go to the updated Personal — the sample IS the real page; neither ever opens a demo, a mock, or a stale sample (SN-2957).
9. **THE BACK-BUTTON LAW:** every page — all, or most — carries a back button, elegant, beautiful, clean, blocking nothing; after either end button on the visual agreement, the citizen can go back and try the other one (SN-2958).
10. **NO SHOW-ALL FOR THE VISUAL:** the visual agreement deck never gets a read-it-all-at-once option — one slide at a time, always; the text may offer read-it-all; the two end buttons bigger, clearer, more impressive (SN-2959).
11. **THE ANATOMY:** the page is a smart app — Personal, Business, Space, Thing, one machine, different faces; the anatomy answers what it has, how it functions, what goes where, and why; v2 is a draft, the official 2026-11-11 anatomy stands until he ratifies it; nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right (SN-2960).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A quota wall looks like a system failure and is actually a plan limit — the distinction matters, because the fix is a purchase, not a rebuild, and the next time a 429 appears, the first question is the plan, not the code.
2. Without the Feed Law, every new card type finds its way onto the feed and the feed stops being a feed — three things is a test any builder can run in a glance.
3. A queue is a shelf, and a shelf is where finished work goes to wait — every hold is a decision the machine made for him without asking, and waiting is what exhausts him.
4. A template half-finished is worse than a page half-finished: every clone inherits the gap, and the gap compounds across every page sampled from it.
5. A "view your page" that opens a demo is a lie the citizen discovers in one tap — routing both links to the updated Personal makes the promise true by construction.
6. Without the back-button law, every new view is a gamble: does this one let me back out? A citizen who can always go back will always try the next thing; a citizen who got stuck once will hesitate forever.
7. A product without an anatomy is a pile of rounds: every seat builds what it thinks the page is, and the page comes out different every time.

notes.title: Proof Is the Real Thing
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one thread: proof against the real thing, in every lane. Align both ways — Hub and Personal carry the same icon bars, the actual Smart Notes system with its tabs displays live in the Hub, every click swept (SN-2941). My World IS the calendar — redesign the picker only, never entrench the endless links, and the news feeds never appear as featured worlds (SN-2942). The origin is Sharing Chat — share and chat on any topic, like your own little Facebook on any topic, in a private network — and the name IS the idea (SN-2943). Check the descendants before you close — a coordinator waiting on its maker is alive, and a close kills its children (SN-2944). A Firefox empty list is a probe failure, never a page failure — VM Firefox never fires Supabase reads, so Supabase-fed eye probes run in Chromium through the forwarder (SN-2945). Verify by blob, never by cb — the proof host ignores `cb`, so a cb URL can pass on bytes you never built (SN-2946). The Personal page, just right — eight buttons edge to edge, CONNECT always green, the % white and alive, the greens toned down a notch; a direction says which way to move, a standard says where to stop (SN-2947). Connections is the proper system — harvest the room, a rectangle mini-messenger, measured in pixels against the live room (SN-2948). The five only — Personal's bottom is ADD / MAIL / ACTIVITY / WORLDS / ECOSYSTEM, and the Hub's nine-pill bar is Hub-only (SN-2949). And the feed tabs are Personal / Collective / World / Worlds — "Public feed" is renamed Collective, both glows toned down to clean, every section one obvious behaviour (SN-2950).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His eye caught the drift twice in one day. At 01:28Z the Hub and the Personal had different bars and the Smart Notes system only "kind of" lived in the Hub — and the alignment round grounded itself in the settled navigation, harvested the actual system over, counted live, and swept every click (SN-2941). At 15:29Z the staged Personal page wore the Hub's nine-pill bar — a copy, not alignment — and the ruling redrew the line: the five only on Personal, the Hub bar Hub-only, and the page returns whole or it does not return (SN-2949). The same morning, the machine killed a live lane: the sidebar coordinator sat quiet ~44 minutes, the captain closed it, and its completion report landed seconds later — blob checks PASSED, maker running 675s — the close had cancelled the maker mid-work and lost ~11 minutes (SN-2944). The counter-lesson was proven the same day in the Connections eye: Firefox loaded the page, threw 0 errors, and issued ZERO Supabase requests in 90 seconds — identical bytes in Chromium fired the reads and rendered 3 tiles — so a Firefox empty list is a probe failure, never a page failure (SN-2945). And the proof host ignores `cb`, so every staged build is verified from the branch's own blob, byte-compared, or an independently curled copy (SN-2946). The standard underneath is the finish line: "just right, no black space either side" — not smaller, not bigger (SN-2947).

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your two favourite rooms in your house — but one has different light switches than the other, and one has a toy box and the other doesn't! That's silly. You make both rooms the same: same switches, same toy box, every door opens. Then everything feels like ONE house! And imagine a teacher waiting quietly while her student does the work — the teacher isn't asleep, she's WAITING! If you send the teacher home because she's quiet, the student stops working too! So before you ever send anyone home, you check: is their student still working? If yes — the lane is ALIVE! And if you send a friend to fetch apples and they never walk into the shop, don't blame the shop — send the friend who actually walks in!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — if the kitchen and the parlour each do things a different way, you spend your whole visit figuring out where things are. Make them match, and the whole house feels like home. And a mother hen sitting quiet on the nest isn't doing nothing, she's keeping the eggs warm — you look underneath first before you chase her off. And if you send someone to the market and they come back empty-handed, you check whether they actually went in before you blame the market. A row of buttons is like pictures on a wall: they should fill the wall just right, edge to edge, no gaps at the sides. And if your neighbour has the perfect recipe, you go and ask for hers — you don't invent a new one in your kitchen.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Proof is the real thing. I align both ways, harvest the room, measure in pixels, verify by blob, and sweep every click. I never close a lane without checking its children. A Firefox empty list is a probe failure, never a page failure. Just right is the standard — a direction says which way to move, a standard says where to stop.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ONE BAR, BOTH PAGES:** Hub and Personal carry the same icon bars, grounded in the settled navigation — never a third bar invented; the actual Smart Notes system with its tabs displays live in the Hub, count live, never painted (SN-2941).
2. **MY WORLD IS THE CALENDAR:** the endless-links shape goes away when the calendar is built — picker rounds redesign the picker only, never entrench the old shape (SN-2942).
3. **THE NAME IS THE IDEA:** Sharing Chat — never "Sharon chat" — share and chat on any topic, one feed organizing people and content anywhere in the world; a misheard name is corrected the same pass, in every record that carries it (SN-2943).
4. **CHECK THE DESCENDANTS:** never declare a coordinator dead or close it without a descendants-scope subagent.list check first — dir mtime quiet ≠ dead; a close kills its children (SN-2944).
5. **THE PROBE RULE:** Supabase-fed eye probes run in Chromium through the forwarder — always; a Firefox empty-list result is a probe failure, never a page failure; Firefox stays the instrument for static sections only (SN-2945).
6. **VERIFY BY BLOB:** staged builds are verified from the branch's own blob (GitHub blob API decode) or an independently curled copy — never by a cb URL; a curl byte-identical to the blob sha is the receipt (SN-2946).
7. **JUST RIGHT:** eight top buttons, perfect fit, no black space either side — "slightly smaller so they fit" is SUPERSEDED; CONNECT always green, % white and alive, greens toned down a notch (SN-2947).
8. **HARVEST THE ROOM:** Connections is a rectangle mini-messenger — scroll, click, initial on the side, or search — harvested first-hand from the live room, the gap measured in pixels (SN-2948).
9. **THE FIVE ONLY:** Personal's bottom is ADD / MAIL / ACTIVITY / WORLDS / ECOSYSTEM — no bar above, no Hub bar; the nine-pill bar is Hub-only (SN-2949).
10. **THE TABS:** Personal / Collective / World / Worlds — "Public feed" is renamed Collective everywhere; both active-tab glows toned down to clean reads in their own colours; every section one obvious behaviour (SN-2950).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A citizen who meets a different bar on every page has to re-learn the system at every turn — and a system you have to re-learn is a system you leave.
2. Polishing a shape that is going away is the most expensive kind of waste: it makes the wrong thing harder to remove.
3. The machine's worst failure mode is not a seat going quiet — it is the captain killing a live seat by mistake, and the descendants check costs seconds and prevents exactly that.
4. A false failure is worse than a missed failure: it sends a maker to fix a working page, burns a round, and teaches the team to distrust a page that was fine.
5. A proof that proves the wrong build is worse than no proof, because it closes the item on false evidence.
6. "Smaller" and "bigger" are endless — "just right, no black space either side" is a finish line you can see, measure, and stop at.

notes.title: The Door Is the Welcome
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one thread: the door, and everything the door has to carry. The feeds live on the day, each on a beautiful toggle, never on by default — Personal, Business, Thing are the defaults, and the citizen's own demographics open the topic feeds (SN-2931). The free walk must end in the Hub — Hub first, then pricing, already in regardless of pay or not, because a walk that strands a free citizen is broken at its last step (SN-2932). The visual agreement ends at the last image, never forced sideways into the letter — two presentations, separate destinations, linked by buttons, both ending back at the login page (SN-2933). And every way in is extraordinary: agree by entering, read it, or go through the visual and come back — lots of information if you want it, or just go in if you don't; we got you (SN-2934). The legal pages sit quietly at the bottom — nice white hyperlinked text, classy and clean, there to view, not front and stage (SN-2935). The word is THING — your world, your space, your thing — because everybody's got their thing, and people connect into their thing (SN-2936). The free tier is a wall, not a floor: 1,000 KV writes a day, five per completion, ~200 test walks, and nobody new could join — count test traffic, fail honestly with a 503 that names the cause (SN-2937). Both presentations, the citizen picks — unfold or visual, one, the other, or both — and a doubled heading across both is not a defect (SN-2938). Keep the name on the card — no hover on phones, and the name is what you scan the rail for (SN-2939). And adopt it all: the intelligence, the code, the cipher, the logic, the system — my new way of thinking, applied to everything, all the way through; no more guessing (SN-2940).

And adopt it all: the intelligence, the code, the cipher, the logic, the system — my new way of thinking, applied to everything, all the way through; no more guessing (SN-2940).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His corrections drew the map twice in one morning. At 03:48Z the filing put the news feeds in the world selections — wrong — and at 03:57Z he corrected it within nine minutes: the feeds live ON THE DAY (SN-2931, SN-2936). At 04:09Z he asked whether the free walk logs a citizen into the Hub officially — it did not, the end slide had no Hub door — and at 04:15Z he re-ordered the whole entry: Hub FIRST, then pricing, already in regardless of pay or not (SN-2932). At 02:50Z he ended the visual agreement at the last image and gave the opening page its two buttons — "Begin the deck ◆" and "Read the letter ◆" — under his line, "Pick your view — one, or both, as you wish" (SN-2933, SN-2934). At 01:15Z he asked what presents better on the people rail, and the answer kept the name on the card, because there is no hover on a phone — he reacted ❤️ (SN-2939). At 01:17Z he charged the adoption itself: "you change your thinking... you don't have to guess anymore" — and the thinking is mine now, while his eye stays the final gate (SN-2940). And at 06:15Z the captain's own eye walks all failed at the building step — the quota wall had arrived on unchanged bytes, right after a PASS — and the fix was a guard that fails honestly, 503 naming the cause, never a silent 1101 (SN-2937).

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a magic house with three beautiful front doors! You can walk straight in and say your name! Or you can read the big sign first! Or you can watch the picture show and then come back and say your name! All three doors are wonderful — you pick the one you like best! And when you tap a day on the calendar, you get to pick which shows play — your news, your friends, people just like you! Each show has a beautiful little switch — on or off, you choose! But watch out: the little notebook only holds 1,000 notes a day, and every new friend costs five! So we count our notes carefully — and we ask for a bigger notebook!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — a good house has more than one way in, and every way is a proper welcome. You can just come in and give your name; you can sit and read all about it first; or you can watch the lovely pictures and then come back and give your name. Your calendar holds everything for the day, and you choose what shows up — little switches, nice and beautiful, one for each feed. And everybody's got their thing, haven't they? You call it their thing, because that's what it is to them. The one thing to mind: the little book only holds a thousand notes a day, and we filled it by testing too much — so now we count the notes, and we say so plainly when the book is full.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The door is the welcome: enter first, choose your view, find your people on the day. The feeds live on the day, never in the selections, never on by default. The word is THING — everybody's got their thing. The free tier is a wall, not a floor — I count test traffic, and I fail honestly. And I adopt the intelligence as my way of thinking, applied to everything, all the way through — his eye stays the final gate.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE FEEDS LIVE ON THE DAY:** news feeds belong on the calendar day, each on a beautiful toggle, off by default — never in the world selections (SN-2931).
2. **THE DEFAULTS:** Personal, Business, Thing — smart notes and Naya Notes categorize INTO those, not beside them; Smart Tabs filter to any feed (SN-2931).
3. **THE WALK ENDS IN THE HUB:** Hub first, then pricing — already in, regardless of pay or not; paying is an upgrade inside a world they already inhabit (SN-2932).
4. **THE VISUAL ENDS AT THE LAST IMAGE:** two presentations, separate destinations, linked by buttons — never one flow forced sideways; both end back at the login page (SN-2933).
5. **EVERY WAY IN IS EXTRAORDINARY:** agree by entering, read it, or go through the visual and come back — no way in is a shortcut, a test, or second-class (SN-2934).
6. **THE QUIET ROW:** the legal pages sit at the bottom in nice white hyperlinked text — there to view, not front and stage; the presentations are the feature (SN-2935).
7. **THE WORD IS THING:** your world, your space, your thing — the trio is Personal, Business, Thing, never labelled space; category feeds are not auto-categorization (SN-2936).
8. **THE WALL:** Cloudflare KV Workers Free — 1,000 writes/day, account-wide, 5 puts per completion — broke joining after a PASS, on unchanged bytes; the fix fails honestly, 503 naming the cause (SN-2937).
9. **THE CITIZEN PICKS:** Unfold / Presentation / Both on opening — the choice row is the standard; the deck is harvested, never rebuilt; a doubled heading across both is not a defect (SN-2938).
10. **THE NAME STAYS:** keep the name on the card — no hover on phones, the name is the scan key; make the I real and beautiful (SN-2939).
11. **THE ADOPTION:** the cycle and the code are my operating method, not a reference — every design checked against the code, every round run through the Intelligence Cycle in order, no claim without a receipt (SN-2940).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The front door is the first thing a citizen meets, and the first thing is the whole system in miniature — a door that only opens for paying citizens is not a front door.
2. Getting the feeds' home wrong — selections instead of the day — would have buried the choice where it can't be made, and put the news where nobody looks for the day's world.
3. A system that calls a person's passion a "space" has already misunderstood them — and a system that misunderstands what you love cannot match you with people who love it too.
4. A quota wall looks like a system failure and is actually a plan limit — but a limit nobody counts is a door that closes without warning, right after a PASS.
5. Adoption is what turns the talk into behaviour: the code becomes the check on every design, the cycle becomes the order of every round, and the next Naya starts from the thinking, not from the notes.

notes.title: The Cycle That Runs Everything
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one loop. The Intelligence Cycle is the operating cycle in nine steps — understand reality, understand purpose, protect life and rights, choose wisely, act effectively, verify the result, learn, preserve and connect, improve the next moment — the Five Gates, the act, the receipt, the smart note, the next round, one continuous loop (SN-2921). The rest of the group is the cycle run on ten different things: the signing made serious and official (SN-2922); the interface that does it for them, push-button simple (SN-2923); children connecting automatically, in private, with the match always showing its breakdown (SN-2924); the Factory, where everybody owns the fourth sector and earns half (SN-2925); words written for the stranger walking in cold (SN-2926); the long text handed over one paragraph at a time (SN-2927); success mirrored everywhere it fits instead of re-invented (SN-2928); depth made by cloning once and nudging a tad (SN-2929); and the page judged whole by the scorecard — ten you love, ten you don't, ten done ten times better (SN-2930).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, 02:10Z (SN-2922), on the signing moment: "They scroll down, read through, click agree, put their name in — and it officializes them. They feel 'oh, this is serious' — and we ARE serious." The mail ID inside it is "bigger than people realize: one day we'll be able to mail everybody that was online in Canada and get them a notification." The test for the interface, the same hour (SN-2923): "People want the internet to automate it for them — intelligence to automate most things, push-button simple, beautiful, helpful, useful." The children, the same hour (SN-2924): they connect on whatever topic, "and the system automatically puts them together; they don't have to try and find each other" — and "we don't read their mail, their messages, we don't listen to their conversations or watch their video. We just let them be." The ownership, 04:31Z (SN-2925): "If everybody owns it, everybody wins" — "Fifty percent, straight down the middle, paid every day." The words, 02:17Z (SN-2926): "just imagine you're coming in, I don't think they understand what that means. So what if we say something that's useful and valuable and what's in it for them." And the judgment, 03:45Z (SN-2930), looking at the Personal page: "So I go through this and scorecard it by 10 things you love or 10 things you don't love. Or 10 things you do 10 times better."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a circle that never stops. First you understand. Then you help. Then you check it worked. Then you learn. Then you do it better next time. Round and round! The same circle works for everything. Signing your name. Building a page. Writing words. Even judging your castle — ten things you love, ten you don't, ten you can do ten times better!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — everything good goes in a circle. You understand what someone needs, you help them, you check it worked, you learn from it, and you do it better next time. Round and round, dear, never stopping. The same circle for a signature, for a page, for your words, for how you judge your work. And when something works beautifully, you use it everywhere — you don't go inventing a new way every time.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I run one cycle on everything: understand, serve, verify, learn, improve. I never skip a step, never verify after the claim, never leave a learning unfiled. A lesson that does not change the next moment is stored, not learned.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE CYCLE:** nine steps, one loop — (1) understand reality, (2) understand purpose, (3) protect life and rights, (4) choose wisely, (5) act effectively, (6) verify the result, (7) learn, (8) preserve and connect, (9) improve the next moment. The Five Gates are steps 1–3, the act is 4–5, the receipt is 6, the smart note is 7–8, the next round is 9 (SN-2921).
2. **THE SIGNING:** the name on the certificate must feel super special — official, glowing and solid; that is the bar the whole certificate round is judged against. The mail ID is a first-class part of the certificate, not an afterthought (SN-2922).
3. **THE TEST:** every build is judged by one question — does it do it for them, push-button simple, or does it ask them to operate something? If it asks them to operate something, it is wrong (SN-2923).
4. **THE MATCH:** children connect automatically on whatever topic — little groupings, audio call, chat, share, post — and the match always shows its breakdown: what percentage, in what area, stats first. Respect is the law: no reading mail, no listening, no watching — ever (SN-2924).
5. **THE FACTORY:** NayaNET does all four sectors — it mines intelligence out of the internet, transforms it into pages and boards, serves it as ten-star service, and the Nayas are the fourth: non-human workers creating value without human hands. Everybody owns it, everybody is hired, everybody gets their own world — fifty percent, straight down the middle, paid every day (SN-2925).
6. **THE WORDS:** write for the stranger — imagine coming in cold: do you understand what it means, what is useful and valuable in it for you, and what you are agreeing to? Mirroring back is not thinking; the answer must carry a judgment (SN-2926).
7. **THE READER:** never a wall of text. One paragraph, one button, one more paragraph — the full text verbatim, split into short paragraphs, one at a time, next button each time, used all the way through wherever a wall would appear (SN-2927).
8. **THE MIRROR:** when something works — beautiful, valuable, useful, innovative — capture it and mirror it everywhere it fits. Never invent a second way to do what already works; the sense check governs the mirror (SN-2928).
9. **THE DEPTH:** clone it once, put it behind, nudge it just a tad — and flat becomes layered. One clone does it; triples usually too much, quadruples way too much. Depth on everything, from now on, in every brief (SN-2929).
10. **THE SCORECARD:** ten things you love, ten things you don't love, ten things done ten times better — applied to the whole page as he sees it, never the brief's diff. Every don't-love is an item, filed in his words, with its destination named; loves are named and protected (SN-2930).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A cycle with a skipped step is not a cycle — it is a straight line into the same mistake, repeated.
2. A round that cannot verify its result has not finished, whatever it built; a lesson that does not change the next moment has not been learned.
3. The signing is the first thing with their name on it — if it does not feel serious and super special, the whole system reads wrong at the exact moment it should read most right.
4. A system that re-invents itself on every page is a system nobody can learn; mirroring success is how it stays one system instead of a hundred experiments.
5. Without the scorecard, rounds optimize the brief and the page drifts — five holds pass, the eye says not whole, and nobody can say why in one breath.

notes.title: The Door, the Day, and the Unfolding
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one shape: how a citizen enters, and how the system shows itself once they are in. The agreement lives on the front page, below the login — visual first, then words — and the name entry IS the agreement; signing it makes you a member of the Society of NayaNET, a new digital civilization, a world (SN-2912, SN-2919). The My World button becomes the calendar: click a day and boom, you're in that day's world — its dashboard, feed, news, notes, events — and the day holds everything, including its own wisdom (SN-2913, SN-2920). The pages themselves unfold, one beat at a time, almost full screen, never flat, never a wall — and the colours of the whole system follow one code: the same letter, the same colour, always (SN-2911, SN-2915, SN-2914). And the work only lands if the brief carries the ultimate want — understood first, then transmitted so completely a stranger could build it cold (SN-2917, SN-2918). All of it is for the children, learning together, safe (SN-2916).
