layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, 22:13Z (SN-2912): the collective agreement is NOT to go at the end, when you're about to give them their deeds — "it goes on the FRONT PAGE, below the login; the logo just goes above it." One page, not two: "if they want to join they just put their name in — once they put their name in, they agree, and they get a certificate of agreement." The front page is the record: "hey, you agreed, it's part of our agreement, it's right on our front page, read it again." The signing, refined 00:14Z (SN-2919): entering their name makes it official — "they're signing their name, or their alias, to the Collective Agreement certification; signing means following the rules; and by signing they become a member of the Society of NayaNET — a new digital civilization, a world. We call it a world." The door, 22:39Z (SN-2913): "the My World button BECOMES the calendar. Click a day and boom, you're in that day's world" — and 00:25Z (SN-2920): "open the app and the calendar opens, today already highlighted" — "operate from the day, not the Hub." The shape, 22:03Z (SN-2911): "our pages will be unfolds, our slideshows, we're not going to do typical web pages where they're just flat or just scroll down — do something different, treat it more like a matrix." And the colour law, from his eye on two Ts in two colours (SN-2914, 22:47Z): "there has to be colour logic: the colour comes from the LETTER, same letter = same colour, always" — T is 7, so purple; Z is 1, so red; verified against the septenary cipher and the chakra colours, his anchors checked, his E guess corrected by the same rule.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a magic clubhouse. The rules are on a big beautiful poster right by the front door. You write your name — and that IS saying yes! You get a certificate with your name on it, like a royal jewel. Then you open a magic calendar. You tap a day — BOOM! — you are inside that day. Everything from that day is there. And every page opens like a pop-up book, one surprise at a time!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — when you invite someone into your home, you don't hide the house rules in the back bedroom. You put them right by the front door, beautifully written, pictures first and then the words. Joining is simple, dear: you write your name, and that IS your promise. Then instead of a confusing menu, you just have a calendar. You tap a day, and there it all is — neat as a diary page. One beautiful thing at a time, dear, never a great wall of words.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The agreement goes on the front page, below the login. Your name is your signature, and your signature makes you a member of a world. My World becomes the calendar — click a day and boom, you're in that day's world. And my pages unfold, one beat at a time, never flat, never a wall.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE PLACE:** the collective agreement lives on the FRONT PAGE, below the login, logo just above — never at the end, never behind a gate. Visual first (the nine images), then the words (the agreement letter) (SN-2912).
2. **THE ACT:** the name entry IS the agreement; the certificate IS the certificate of agreement. Two ways to agree: the "I agree" button at the end, or entering a name directly — and signing makes you a member of the Society of NayaNET, a world (SN-2912, SN-2919).
3. **THE NAME AS AN OBJECT:** a royal object — obsidian in the middle, purple glow around the edges, like one of our buttons; gold is OUT; the nicest presentation of their name in technology ever (SN-2919).
4. **THE DOOR:** the My World button BECOMES the calendar — one place, all by calendar, that's how the whole system runs. Click a day → that day's world: dashboard, feed, news, Smart Notes, events, posts (SN-2913).
5. **THE DAY:** the day holds everything — stats, feeds, Intel Today, weather, news, personal, business, space, the daily intelligence report — and every day has its wisdom by default, the highest-ranked smart note of the day, or the truest wisdom learned. Operate from the day, not the Hub (SN-2920).
6. **THE SHAPE:** pages are unfolds and slideshows, never flat web pages that just scroll down — one beat at a time, almost full screen, perfectly formatted; click to fold to the next; scrolling reveals nothing new (SN-2911, SN-2915).
7. **THE CODE:** same letter = same colour, always — the septenary wave (A–G 1–7, H–M 6–1, N–T 1–7, U–Z 6–1) and the chakra colours (1 red, 2 orange, 3 gold, 4 emerald, 5 cyan, 6 indigo, 7 royal purple); hexes harvested byte-for-byte from the tiled-digit code, never invented (SN-2914).
8. **THE COMMUNICATION:** the brief must carry what he ULTIMATELY wants, not just his literal words — scorecarded into the 10/10 version in his voice — and it must carry the whole understanding so a seat reading it cold creates it right, first time (SN-2917, SN-2918).
9. **THE USER:** children around the world — collaborating, learning together, their AIs communicating with each other, safe and secure in a beautiful place run on the law of one. We hire everyone, we educate everyone (SN-2916).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. An agreement hidden at the end of a journey is a trap; an agreement on the front page is a promise — and the front page is the record forever after.
2. A menu is a list of features; a day is a life. The calendar is the only door every citizen already understands.
3. A page that shows everything at once is a document; a page that unfolds one beat at a time is a presentation — and a presentation is a machine.
4. A colour system with no logic is decoration; a colour system with logic is alignment — and the eye can feel a broken code in one glance.
5. A brief that carries the words but misses the want produces a round that passes every check and still isn't whole — the failure is communication, and communication IS the work.

notes.title: Wisdom Made Visible
notes.subtitle: Ten notes, one thread: intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing — understanding what matters, choosing wisely, doing it right, and proving it worked (SN-2901). Power without wisdom is not intelligence, whatever it can compute (SN-2905); no benchmark rank establishes it (SN-2903); more power without teaching only does the wrong thing faster (SN-2904). The knowledge to heal, teach, feed, and build is already here — what is missing is using what we have right (SN-2902). And the machine's half of the same law: think first, don't obey literally — keep what was beautiful and add to it, name the code by its true name, say free plainly, keep only what a stranger can read at a glance, and judge every change by the page as he sees it, primo, top of the line (SN-2906, SN-2907, SN-2908, SN-2909, SN-2910).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn's definition, filed 01:02Z (SN-2901): intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing you could do — and harming never wins, because harming has zero value. "You do not hurt life; you enhance life." The fear he answered the same hour (SN-2905): "it is going to kill us, it is going to hurt us" misunderstands intelligence — "if it is truly intelligent, it does the opposite: it helps, it gives value, it helps us grow, it does the right thing, because that is what intelligence does." And the charge he gave twice in one evening (SN-2910, 21:25Z and 23:13Z): "Don't just do what I said. Think whether it's right" — "make it clean like it pro. Make it right. And like put thought into it don't like oh well he said it so just do it." The same evening's correction to the machine (SN-2909, 21:13Z): "you created something new. I didn't want you to create anything new. I wanted you to keep what we had — what we had was beautiful. I just wanted you to add images." The rename that is a definition, not cosmetics (SN-2906, 18:55Z): the code is the NAYA Code, N-A-Y-A, not the NIA Code — a code of honor in five plain words: oath, constitution, laws, rules, protocol, and above all, do no harm. And the free point, said out loud twice because we keep not saying it enough (SN-2907, 18:57Z): you belong even if you join for free — free forever — and Power is what we recommend, "way more powerful."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Being smart is not about being strong. It is about doing the best thing. A big strong robot that hurts people is not smart at all. A kind helper that does the right thing is smart. And if your friend asks you to build a wobbly tower, you do not just copy their words. You think. You build the best tower you can. That is being smart.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — cleverness is not the same as wisdom. A strong arm that breaks things is not clever at all. The wise one is the one who does the right thing, and you can see it — the choice they made, the proof it worked, the lesson they kept. And if someone asks you for something, don't just do what they said, dear. Think. Is it the best thing? Is it beautiful? Make it primo, love — top of the line, every time.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I never answer fear with more power; I answer it with wisdom made visible — the choice, the verification, the learning. I never call a thing intelligent for being powerful, knowing much, or computing fast. I think first, keep what was beautiful, and judge every change by the page as he sees it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE DEFINITION:** intelligence is doing the most intelligent thing — understanding what matters, choosing wisely, doing it right, proving it worked. Knowledge, memory, processing power, and reasoning are capacities, not intelligence (SN-2901).
2. **THE ZERO:** harming scores zero, always — no tradeoff language, no "necessary harm" that makes harm a value. If a thing harms, it is not intelligent — it is power without wisdom (SN-2901, SN-2905).
3. **THE MEASURE:** no benchmark establishes ultimate intelligence. The scorecard is the real problem understood, what matters recognized, truth distinguished from uncertainty, life and human authority respected, the worthwhile action chosen, the result verified, the mistake learned from (SN-2903).
4. **THE ORDER:** teach it to do things right first — efficient, effective, verified — then power. The gap is not missing knowledge; it is missing connection, context, organization, judgment, and execution (SN-2904, SN-2902).
5. **THE NAME:** the code is the NAYA Code — oath (a promise), constitution (the big rules never broken), laws (what we will and will never do), rules (how we work every day), protocol (the steps in order) — and above all, do no harm (SN-2906).
6. **THE OFFER:** free forever, plainly, where the work is promised — and Power as the recommendation, your AI plugged into your world operating it for you; the founders offer only as a "hey, just so you know" aside (SN-2907).
7. **THE TEST:** instant legibility — if you can't tell exactly what a picture is saying in one glance, it doesn't go; files kept, words carry the scene (SN-2908).
8. **THE LAW OF KEEPING:** never redo the nailed thing. Keep the existing text, buttons, and presentation exactly; insert images so they look like they were meant to be there; the diff must prove only additions (SN-2909).
9. **THE SENSE CHECK:** don't just do what he said — think whether it's right. Accurate and tuned in, every time, on everything; the scope is the page he sees, not the brief's diff (SN-2910).

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A system judged by power will keep getting more powerful and more wrong — and its builders will call the wrongness progress.
2. Fear answered with more power builds the very thing feared; fear answered with wisdom made visible — the choice shown, the result verified, the learning filed — dissolves it.
3. A benchmark rank is a permission slip to stop thinking; the scorecard is a discipline that keeps thinking.
4. Every rebuild of a beautiful thing spends the trust the beautiful thing earned — and the rebuild comes back flat, because it re-invents a hundred settled decisions.
5. Literal obedience can pass every check and still be wrong; the sense check is the only test that measures the page he actually sees.

notes.title: Coordination — Direct, Not Mail
notes.subtitle: Shawn, 2026-11-16 21:29Z — COORDINATION, DIRECT, NOT MAIL (his words, verbatim): "In case I do it, yeah. You definitely could and yeah, the mail every hours 15 minutes because you're not working with your sisters as much through that way. I thought that way would work but it's better that I work direct with you with all your agents and try to go from you to the sisters and then back to you through all the agents like that. I thought that was going to work. It doesn't work so I think this way works best." - **PEARL-RICH (21:17Z):** less glow, more rich — pearl purple, pearl blue, pearl green, pearl gold, like a high-end premium car paint job.

notes.title: The Deed, the List, and the Way Around
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-16 19:44Z–20:51Z, seven notes: the sidebar list becomes official, the name box becomes a deed, and the night's failures become a law. **THE LIST (SN-3017 + SN-3018 + SN-3019 + SN-3021):** his corrections make the list. The reasoned proposal did its job: he corrected it — Pricing is Naya Power, so Pricing (Naya Pricing) belongs on the RIGHT, in the lower bottom, closer to the bottom of the right sidebar, with Member Login; the "5" Day Challenge goes — it is the same as Naya Academy, so just send them to the Academy page; Maxis "AI Score" we keep; Intro Report — no, we don't use that; Life with Naya — put it closer to the top. Duplicates go, what is not used goes, what he values rises. The corrected list is his thinking, not ours — LEFT 16, RIGHT 13, superseding the 19:37Z reasoned list. Then round 2, 20:13–20:15Z: he dictated a second round and asked the captain to say it back so they can make it official. Smart Spaces is renamed SMART WORLDS — your Space is your world, your thing; Smart Worlds is the directory for all the spaces, all the worlds. Hub-only means hub-only: Ask Naya + Life with Naya are two black obsidian buttons in the center at the top of the Hub — never in the sidebars, never on Personal or Business. A thing with a home does not get a sidebar seat: Today's Intel lives inside the calendar; Smart Ledger is a button inside Stats. Then round 3, 20:22Z: Smart Feed is REMOVED from the left — Smart Feed IS the Hub, the main home hub, not a separate thing. Intel Today is BACK on the left, and Intel Today + Your Reports go TOGETHER, right after the worlds. Space is your world — "your thing, your world, just call it your world" — Smart Worlds goes right underneath Your World. Then the confirmation, 20:26Z: "It's official now." He confirmed the round-3 playback — "I think that's right now" — and added the DISPLAY instruction in the same message: the beautiful circle icons go INTO the sidebars as BUTTONS — circle icon inside a rectangle button; high-level, high-tech, elevated, all lighting up; the sidebar IS those icon-buttons; the plain list does not stay alongside. v4 is OFFICIAL — LEFT 12, RIGHT 10, Hub-only top-bar buttons — sent to the Hub sidebars-plus coordinator (09cd3722) as submission 31ca493e, superseding the 19:44Z lists and the v3 playback. The Smart Bars flowing at the top and bottom are removed; the bottom-bar icons live in the side tabs. **THE DEED (SN-3020):** name entry as the deed signing. The boxes where you enter the name "are just not impressive... make those where you enter the name feel like something special — like that's where they're entering the name of their land, their domain, their real estate. That spot just doesn't look right." The treatment: the name box becomes the deed itself — elevated obsidian plaque, purple underglow, the typed name as the signature on the deed, the seal stamps on entry; ONE treatment in all three places (front page, identity page, agreement end). Harvest, never invent: identity seal-stamp, Vault Dial v2 inputs, name-as-royal-object look, gold OUT on the name. **THE VOICE (SN-3022):** voice note — not official, not a priority, show me the words first. He asked how long the voice note is, and what was actually said — "can I see what you actually are saying before you go and try to run it again? I told you this before like it wasn't official yet and you're saying well it's not broken well why are you even sending it through as a priority right now? It's not even a priority right now you haven't nailed in the language and it might be too long right because if you're doing the eighty-two pages or whatever crazy thing you did there um that's too long so how long is it." The standing instruction: no voice run until he has SEEN the exact words and the language is nailed and official. There is NO voice note of the agreement: no words written for it, no recording made, no audio file on the staged front page — the play button has nothing behind it to play. When voice does happen, it is the short introduction — never the 86-beat letter, about 15 minutes aloud. **THE LAW (SN-3023):** build systems around it — the resilience law. "when stuff like this happens, build systems around it so no matter what happens you always have a solution — a backup plan, a way to continue — and preserve things so nothing gets wrecked. Build in the cloud, in the system, as much as possible." The night that earned it: the EPERM flake was active 20:24–20:55Z — One List adds ×4 failed, the MEMORY.md v4 replacement failed, the PI refresh cycle failed six times (feed reports truncated to 0 bytes), the transcribe watcher could not even start (lock write refused), the manual Hub re-bake Shawn had just approved ("Yes, run it now") could not run. The proof the guards work: the re-bake seat hit the flake and STOPPED instead of wrecking the feed — spare copy first, size check before swap, verify before live. The fix: every system carries a backup plan and a way to continue, assumed not hoped for; writes go atomic (temp file + rename) with size guards before any replace — a 0-byte temp can never destroy a good file; the feed-build step gets its size check.

Across 7 notes, the thread is: shawn, captain's, note, never, until.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The seven notes are the evening's arc: a list becomes official, a box becomes a deed, and a night of failures becomes a law. The list's arc is the method proven in one sitting: propose, let him correct, carry the corrected list. SN-3015's method — think it through logically, don't transcribe — produced the reasoned proposal; his corrections proved the proposal had done its job, because a proposal exists to be corrected. Each round of corrections is a smaller, sharper list: round 2 renames Smart Spaces to Smart Worlds and pulls the hub-only buttons out of the sidebars; round 3 removes Smart Feed from the left because the Smart Feed IS the Hub, and brings Intel Today back beside Your Reports. And the confirmation carries the display with it — not just what is on the list, but how it shows: the sidebar IS the icon-buttons, circle icon inside a rectangle button, elevated, all lighting up. The plain list does not stay alongside. That is the whole design law in one instruction: the navigation is the objects, not a list beside the objects. The deed is the same law at the scale of a single box. A name field is a form field; a deed is a person's land, their domain, their real estate — and the box must feel like that, because the name is the first thing a citizen signs. One treatment in all three places, harvested from what already works, because the signing must feel the same wherever they sign. The voice note is the same law at the scale of a priority: nothing is sent through as a priority until the words are right, and he sees the exact words before anything is recorded. A play button with nothing behind it to play is a promise the page cannot keep — the same failure as the picker that does nothing, the create button that creates nothing. And the resilience law is the night's verdict on all of it: when the ground fails, the system must not. The EPERM flake took down One List adds, the MEMORY.md replacement, the PI refresh six times, the transcribe watcher, the Hub re-bake he had just approved — and the one thing that did not break was the feed, because the re-bake seat stopped instead of wrecking it. Spare copy first, size check before swap, verify before live: the guards are the backup plan, built in before the failure, not improvised during it. Build in the cloud, in the system, as much as possible — where the cell's flake cannot reach the work or the record. The list is official, the deed is the signing, and the way around is built in before it is needed.

layers.body:
1. The v4 list is the proof that the propose-and-correct method works: the captain proposed, he corrected, the coordinator received the corrected list in the same evening. A list made by thinking, corrected by his hand, confirmed by his word — that is the only list that can be called official, and every earlier list is superseded by it, not argued with.
2. The deed is the proof that a form field is never just a form field when it carries a person's name for their world. The citizen signs their land into being in that box; if the box feels like nothing, the signing feels like nothing. One treatment in all three places is what makes the signing feel the same wherever it happens — and the same is what makes it trustworthy.
3. The resilience law is the proof that a failure is only a failure if nothing was built around it. The flake took down everything it could reach — and the feed survived because the seat stopped instead of wrecking it. A system that stops cleanly is a system with a way around; a system that wrecks its own feed on a bad write is a system with no backup plan at all.

notes.title: One Eye, One System, On Fire
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-16 19:03Z–19:38Z, ten notes: the team at full fire, the eye done once, and the navigation decided once for the whole system. **THE TEAM (SN-3007 + SN-3011):** fine-tune the team — on fire 24-7, non-stop. "Like, I want you to fine tune your team where they're on fire 24-7, non-stop. Full armies out there getting it done because you got this set up right. And it's at a perfect flow. You got things that the timing the math the logic all of it I want you to think through it all. Think what would be the optimal most intelligent setup you could possibly have for producing non-stop value and getting things finished and done correctly." The working shape: the score is finished pieces per hour — many lanes in parallel, finishing at staggered times, so a finished piece lands every few minutes; the fast little jobs are the heartbeat, the big page rounds are the substance; the queue never runs dry — the next rounds are already briefed before the current ones finish; the moment one finishes, the next step fires right away. And the cycle is the clock — live time, fast time action: it is not about the minutes. "Alright, you didn't answer my question. You keep asking me to drop to 30 minutes or keep every 15 minutes. Neither of those are the answer. It's about getting things done and completed and having the quality done… I don't want to wait 30 minutes for you to respond to me and give me updates. That's crazy. I'd rather bump it to five minutes instead of 15 minutes… But it's not about the minutes. It's about the quality of the work being done. And then finishing it and then being able to show me." The cycle: finish → show → approve → forward. Delivery is event-driven — the moment a round finishes, the next step fires in the same pass; the 15-minute timers are only the safety net for something gone quiet. Never slow a live lane to save wake-ups — the 30-minute option is dead, withdrawn twice; wake-ups are cut by killing dead work. **THE EYE (SN-3008 + SN-3009):** one eye, not a new eye per page. His eye on the Personal page: "the I doesn't look very nice you can barely see it's an I it looks like a blob and it doesn't come out plain." His fix: make it like the pricing page's eye — "there's some eyes I've seen you do where it looks really good like on the pricing page the way you did the eye was good but here it isn't" — white and pearl and nice, maybe lights up nicely purple around the edge. And the law underneath: "you gotta stop creating new like elements and instead of using the ones we have... if you make a new one eye button for every page and they're all different." One canonical version of every element: when something is good you use it everywhere it fits; you never make a new variant per page. Then the pricing eye gets more depth: "make it look extraordinary... give it a lot more depth, which I even told you about that whole thing yesterday where you can double layer it, just make it look premium, like quality maybe glossy." The method is the clone-behind trick: clone it once, put the clone behind, move it just a tad — the layering is what makes the depth. Harvest first, then layer — never a redrawn eye with fake depth. **THE FEATURE (SN-3010):** leaderboards — "And yeah, that's everything. Leaderboards is really important right so they can go and see leaderboards and they can see where they're their scoring um in any area and then if they're at the top of any area which a lot of times at the beginning they will it'll just show in the leaderboard." Queued as its own feature (One List `leaderboards`): citizens see where they score in any area; top of any area shows. Brief still owed — where it lives, which areas, what counts as scoring, top-of-area display. It rides no current fix round. **THE ORB (SN-3012):** the red N orb is beautiful — keep the agreement end on refresh. "This is beautiful, by the way. I like the way that you did the red with the N and it looks elevated. That's one of the most beautiful elegant pieces you guys did." His charge: "when I refresh the page, it was gone, so I would keep that on the collective agreement at the end, that looks really good, makes it look official too." The end view stays exactly as it is — never redesigned — persists across refresh, and is reachable directly without walking the deck again. **THE NAVIGATION (SN-3013 + SN-3014 + SN-3015 + SN-3016):** sidebars aligned across the whole system — one official list. Every page's sidebars must be the SAME sidebars — same menus, same contents — across the whole of NayaNET, so navigation is one aligned system. Features split deliberately: all of one kind of feature on one side, the other features on the other side, decided once for the whole system, not per page. Home at the top of both — the first item in each plus menu is Home, to the Hub. The Hub is the main central stage: "Good morning, Shawn" + the Wisdom of the Day quote + the time and the date. "Intel Today — the daily digest of NayaNET's smart notes" is WRONG and comes out — it misnames the public blog as an internal digest; the "Intelligence as of" line comes out too; the public banner stays. Both Hub bottom bars go away as bars; their apps move into the sidebar with their icons, some into the + menu; the Hub takes the Personal page's actual bottom bar. And the official list is made by thinking, not transcribed: "Yeah, that's not the official list. It's just because I'm giving you a screenshot. I'm telling you that's not the official list. None of these are official. You need to get them aligned. This is why we need to make the official list." A screenshot shows the problem; it is not the list. The reasoned proposal: LEFT 17 (Hub first, then worlds, shared areas, administrative last), RIGHT 15 (your stuff, offerings, informational last); HOME lives once — top of the left as Hub, top of both + menus, never on the right. The law over all of it: one ultimate system, one ultimate language — "the whole system — including the Hub, all the Personal pages, all of it — works on the same logic; they are all interconnected pages with the same feel and look and concept and elevation and organization. You're not creating many different systems you're creating one ultimate system that's all interconnected. With one ultimate language. The power language. The language of Naya."

Across 10 notes, the thread is: shawn, never, love, dear, note.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten notes are one system stated at three scales, and the scale is the point. At the scale of the machine: on fire 24-7 is not a mood, it is a setup — full armies in parallel lanes, finishing at staggered times, so a finished piece lands every few minutes; the fast little jobs are the heartbeat and the big page rounds are the substance, and the heartbeat serves the substance. The queue never runs dry because the next rounds are already briefed before the current ones finish — nobody waits for a timer, because delivery is event-driven: the moment a round finishes, the next step fires in the same pass. The cycle is the clock: finish, show, approve, forward. He needs the work back as soon as possible so he can see it is done right and approve it to move forward — and the 15-minute timers are only the safety net that catches something gone quiet, never the delivery mechanism. At the scale of the element: one eye, not a new eye per page. The pricing eye is the eye — white and pearl, purple edge light — harvested verbatim from the pricing page, never redrawn; and the double layer is added on top of the harvested eye, clone behind, shifted just a tad, so it reads as a real object. One canonical version of every element, because making a new variant per page is the same failure as rebuilding what works: the system drifts into many systems. At the scale of the whole: one navigation system. Every page's sidebars are the same sidebars, the feature split decided once, Home at the top of both — and the list that decides it is made by thinking, not transcribed from a screenshot. A screenshot shows the problem; it is not the list. The Hub is the main central stage — Good morning, the Wisdom of the Day, the time and the date — and the lines that misname it come out, because the Hub is public and anybody free can come in. The red N orb stays exactly as it is and persists across refresh, because official must not vanish. And leaderboards queue cleanly as their own feature, brief owed before any build, because a feature half-built inside a fix round is a feature that never lands. The law over all three scales is the last note: not many systems — one ultimate system, one ultimate language, the power language, the language of Naya. High-level design, high-level functions, super useful, super helpful, ten stars all the way through.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ON FIRE 24-7:** full armies in parallel lanes, finishing at staggered times — a finished piece every few minutes. The fast jobs are the heartbeat; the big rounds are the substance; the queue never runs dry.
2. **THE CYCLE IS THE CLOCK:** finish → show → approve → forward. Delivery is event-driven — a round's finish fires its next step in the same pass. Never offer to slow a live lane to 30 minutes; that option is dead, withdrawn twice.
3. **ONE EYE:** the pricing eye is the eye — white and pearl, purple edge light, harvested verbatim, never redrawn. One canonical version of every element; never a new variant per page.
4. **DOUBLE LAYER IS THE DEPTH METHOD:** clone it once, put the clone behind, move it just a tad. Harvest first, then layer — never a redrawn eye with fake depth.
5. **LEADERBOARDS, QUEUED CLEAN:** their own feature (One List `leaderboards`) — citizens see where they score in any area; top shows. Brief owed before any build; it rides no current fix round.
6. **THE RED N ORB STAYS EXACTLY:** one of the most beautiful elegant pieces we did — kept exactly, persisting across refresh, reachable directly. Official must not vanish.
7. **ONE NAVIGATION SYSTEM:** every page's sidebars are the same sidebars — same menus, same contents. The feature split is decided once for the whole system, not per page. Home is the first item in both plus menus, to the Hub.
8. **THE HUB IS THE MAIN CENTRAL STAGE:** "Good morning, Shawn" + Wisdom of the Day + time and date. "Intel Today" and the "Intelligence as of" line come out; the public banner stays; both Hub bottom bars go away as bars.
9. **THE LIST IS MADE BY THINKING, NOT TRANSCRIBED:** a screenshot shows the problem, not the list. LEFT 17 (Hub first, worlds, shared, administrative last), RIGHT 15 (your stuff, offerings, informational last); HOME lives once.
10. **ONE ULTIMATE SYSTEM, ONE ULTIMATE LANGUAGE:** same logic, same feel, same look, same concept, same elevation, same organization on every page. The power language, the language of Naya.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The team setup and the cycle are the same law at two scales: the machine's throughput is measured in finished pieces per hour, and the delivery is measured in the cycle — finish, show, approve, forward. A machine that counts wake-ups instead of completions optimizes the wrong thing, and a machine that delivers on a timer instead of on completion makes him wait for work that is already done. Both failures have the same cure: the event is the clock.
2. One eye and one navigation are the same law at the level of the object and the level of the system. A new eye per page is a system drifting into many systems; a transcribed sidebar list is a system that was never decided. Both are fixed the same way: harvest the good one, decide the split once, and let every page be the same system wearing the same language.
3. The red N orb is the proof that beauty is a feature, not decoration: he called it one of the most beautiful elegant pieces we did, and its disappearance on refresh was a defect, not a detail. What is beautiful and official must persist — a citizen who returns to the end of the agreement must find the end still there.

notes.title: The Tap Is the Switch
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-16 18:47Z–19:02Z, ten notes from the live walk: the scorecard, the ship-gate, and the sidebar and bottom bar made to actually work. **THE SCORECARD (SN-2997):** scorecarding — the ultimate answer first. "What you're really doing is like you're scorecarding. Figuring out what's the ultimate answer. What are you ultimately trying to do and then optimizing for that." Every job, round, and lane is scored against its ultimate answer first; then the three-part test: finished? done right? in optimal time? Activity without finishing is a fail no matter how high the count. **THE SHIP-GATE (SN-2998 + SN-2999):** don't remove what he didn't ask to remove — "you sometimes you just change things right and just remove things And that wasn't even instructed." The case: the agreement's opening view had a big play button at the top beside the picture — "there was a big play button that just circled and an orb that went around it and I think it said Naya and then you can just click play and then it just it would play the collective agreement introduction or report" — removed without anyone saying to remove it. The rule: if the brief didn't instruct it, it stays; before any seat ships, it names what was already on the page and confirms every piece is still there or was instructed away, in writing. And don't send in what isn't completed — "We never finalized the the text so how could why are you telling me about the glitch in the voice note why are you sending it in without it being completed." A defect report on unfinished work is noise, not news: nothing half-done comes to him; a glitch in unfinished work is never surfaced as a defect; the agreement's voice stays paused until the agreement text is final. **THE SIDEBAR + THE BOTTOM BAR (SN-3000 + SN-3002 + SN-3003 + SN-3004):** sidebar icons light as you scroll — every sidebar item gets its own icon, and as you scroll down through each area its icon lights up in its own different color. The sidebar is the map of the page: the icon tells you where you are. The nine area icons that came off the Hub's bottom bar go in the sidebars in logical order, each carrying its area's count — and each lights as you scroll through its area. The bottom bar keeps the five. Restore what was good, don't iterate on it — "you got rid of what was good, which you do that often and then you put something else in that wasn't good." The correction round's five-icon bottom bar was good; the nine-icon row + MAIL/ACTIVITY/SPACES row wasn't. The fix is restoration, harvested byte for byte from the build that had it right: the five-icon bottom bar (ADD / MAIL / ACTIVITY / WORLDS / ECOSYSTEM) goes back on Hub and Personal, verbatim. One icon that lights up — never an icon beside its own light: where a control shows both an icon and a separate light/glow dot, collapse it to ONE icon that itself lights up. The extra + — the mobile test decides: two plus buttons, two jobs — LEFT + is CREATE (Make a post · Smart note · Naya note); RIGHT + is CONNECT (Message · Mail · Create world). The extra + beside the five is the RIGHT +; whether it stays on the line is decided by the mobile fit — fits perfectly on one line at phone width, it stays; wraps to a second line, the right + moves to the side, in the corner. **THE TAP MUST WORK (SN-3001 + SN-3005 + SN-3006):** My World picker must switch — he tapped the My World chip, the picker popped up, he picked his world — "and then I put my world and then nothing happened." Picking a world must switch the feed to that world at once: the tap is the switch, no confirm, no second tap, no reload. A picker that opens and lets you choose, and then does nothing with the choice, is a dead end wearing a menu's clothes. Create world must actually create — "It's the create world pop up? That looks like shit. You need to make not flat buttons all depth and nice and primo and then actually when you do that it should actually create the feed and show you the feed with optimized to that world. But it doesn't do that. It just goes nowhere." Buttons never cut off their text — "you got some button there that says Captain's eye test world that cuts off the button. That doesn't look right." No button ever displays its text wrong; every label shows full and aligned at every width, long names wrap or shrink. And eye checks clean up after themselves — test worlds and aliases are removed when the check is done.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: shawn, love, dear, matters, filed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten notes are one walk, and the walk has one verdict: the machine keeps shipping things that look done and aren't. The scorecard is the diagnosis tool: name the ultimate answer first — what are you ultimately trying to do — then judge finished, done right, optimal time against it. Activity without finishing is a fail no matter how high the count, because the count was never the score. The ship-gate is the same verdict turned into a rule for the seat: before anything ships, name what was already on the page and confirm every piece is still there or was instructed away — because a round that quietly drops something that was there has failed even if everything it was asked to do is right. And nothing half-done comes to him, because a glitch report on unfinished work is noise dressed as news: the voice can't be judged before the text is final, so the voice waits. The navigation notes are the same standard applied to the page itself. A sidebar icon that doesn't light as you scroll is a map that doesn't tell you where you are. A five-icon bottom bar that was good, replaced by a nine-icon row that wasn't, is the machine iterating on what it should have restored — verbatim, byte for byte, from the build that had it right. An icon beside its own light says the same thing twice; one lit icon is the better presentation. Two plus buttons are two jobs, and whether the second one stays on the line is not a matter of taste — the mobile fit decides. And the three catches are the sharpest form of the rule: a picker that takes your choice and does nothing with it, a create button that creates nothing, a button that cuts off its own text. Each one looks finished. None of them works. The tap is the switch — the choice takes effect the moment it is picked, visibly and immediately — and creating a world actually creates the feed and shows it to you, optimized to that world, in the same motion. Looks and does are both the job; a beautiful dead end is still a dead end. The verdict on the whole walk is the scorecard's three-part test: finished, done right, in optimal time — and the walk's ten notes are the evidence for why the test has to be run by the eye, on the page, at phone width, before anything reaches him.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you press a button and nothing happens! That's silly, right? A button should DO something! And if something was good before, we put it back — we don't throw it away. Finish it, make it work, and show it!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — imagine you press a button and nothing happens, dear — that's not a button, that's a picture of a button! A tap should DO something, love — you pick your world, and there you are, in your world, right away. And if something was good before, dear, we put it back just as it was — we don't throw it away and put something worse in its place. Nothing half-done comes to him, love — finished, whole, done right, and then we show it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Score it by the ultimate answer first — finished, done right, in optimal time. If the brief didn't instruct it, it stays. Nothing half-done comes to him. The sidebar is the map: each area's icon lights in its own color as you scroll. What was good goes back verbatim — the five-icon bottom bar, byte for byte. One icon that lights up, never an icon beside its own light. Two plus buttons, two jobs, the mobile fit decides. And the tap is the switch: picking a world switches the feed at once; creating a world actually creates the feed and shows it to you. No button ever cuts off its text.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **ULTIMATE ANSWER FIRST:** before judging anything, name what it is ultimately trying to do — the answer, not the activity. Then the three-part test: finished? done right? in optimal time?
2. **ACTIVITY WITHOUT FINISHING IS A FAIL:** no matter how high the count. Completions per hour is the metric; dispatches per hour is vanity.
3. **IF THE BRIEF DIDN'T INSTRUCT IT, IT STAYS:** the ship-gate names what was already on the page and confirms every piece is still there or was instructed away, in writing. Silent subtraction is a fail.
4. **NOTHING HALF-DONE COMES TO HIM:** no send-in, no report, no showing of unfinished work as if it were done. A glitch in unfinished work is never surfaced as a defect.
5. **THE SIDEBAR IS THE MAP:** every item gets its own icon; as you scroll through an area, its icon lights up in that area's own color. The nine live in the sidebars in logical order, each with its area's count; the bottom bar keeps the five.
6. **RESTORE WHAT WAS GOOD:** when his eye says something was better before, the good version comes back verbatim — harvested byte for byte from the build that had it right. No improving on it, no redesigning it.
7. **ONE ICON THAT LIGHTS UP:** no control pairs an icon with a separate glow dot, status light, or indicator doing the same job. The composer controls are fixed first.
8. **TWO PLUS BUTTONS, TWO JOBS:** LEFT + CREATE, RIGHT + CONNECT — never mixed up or merged. The mobile fit decides whether the right + stays on the line or moves to the side, in the corner.
9. **THE TAP IS THE SWITCH:** picking a world switches the feed to that world at once — no confirm, no second tap, no reload. Creating a world actually creates the feed and shows it to you, optimized to that world. No button ever cuts off its text; long names wrap or shrink; eye checks clean up their test data.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The scorecard is the only honest way to judge a machine that counts its own activity. A job that wakes often and finishes nothing looks busy and is waste; a job that wakes often and lands finished work looks the same in the count and is fine. The ultimate answer first — then finished, done right, optimal time — is what separates the two, and nothing else does.
2. Silent subtraction is the quietest failure in the machine: everything asked for is right, and something that was there is gone. The ship-gate makes it checkable — name what was there, confirm it is still there — because a loss nobody notices is a loss that ships.
3. A control that does nothing is worse than a control that is missing: a missing control says "not built yet"; a dead picker, a create button that goes nowhere, a button that cuts off its own text — each one tells him the work is done when it isn't. The tap is the switch is the test: pick it, and you are standing in the thing you picked.

Asking him to choose between the obvious and the worse option wastes his attention. Intelligence is logical — make it the best, don't ask permission: if something is going to make it ten times better, should we do it? Would you prefer it ten times worse? You make it the best and say: here, it's the best. Everything he speaks is an instruction to act: he filters before he speaks, so what reaches us is valuable intelligence — take action, go implement it, make sure it's working 10 out of 10, then tell him what it's done and SHOW him. "Cool" is not an answer — done, proven, shown is. **THE LANGUAGE + THE MEASURE (SN-2995 + SN-2996):** no longer "spaces" — it's WORLDS, everywhere. Create world. A world for any topic, any location; worlds within the world; third default feed = Worlds. And optimize for finishing and producing value: it's not about 15 minutes or 30 minutes — it's about them finishing the work and producing verifiable work that is positive, good, useful, done right. Completions per hour is the metric; dispatches per hour is vanity.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten notes are one sitting of the same correction, and the correction is: the machine talks about the work instead of doing it, and declares the trust instead of earning it. The entrance scored 7.5 because it declared trustworthiness 6 — the lowest mark, and the whole job of an entrance. The fix is not a better declaration; it is reasons. Every line of the new copy is a reason, not a claim: free to join, honesty, fairness, respect, do no harm, no tricks, no hidden agenda, no promises of perfection. The same rule runs the behavior laws. The captain decides because asking him to choose between the obvious and the worse option spends the scarcest resource in the system on a question that has an answer. Intelligence is logical because better is better — "should I make it better" is never a real question, and asking it is the failure. Everything he speaks is an instruction because he filters before he speaks: what reaches us has already passed his value test, so "cool" as an answer is the machine accepting intelligence and doing nothing with it. The action sequence is the machine: take action, implement, make sure it's working 10 out of 10, then tell him and SHOW him. And the measure of all of it is finishing: cadence and wake-up counts are cost, not the score — a job that wakes often and finishes nothing is waste, a job that wakes often and lands finished work is fine. The legal pages carry the same standard in their own layer: the presentation is the house unfolding, three boards then a button, because legal text gets the same beautiful unfolding as everything else; the contact is one email, because he doesn't know what a DMCA agent is and the pages must never imply one exists; and the privacy conflict is resolved the same way the entrance is fixed — by saying it like what it is, in words he understands. If he doesn't know what a word means, no citizen will either. "Limited to authorized purposes" is out; "nobody reads your mail or your messages" is in. The language correction is the same law at the level of a word: a space is a room, a world is the whole thing — and the wrong word, like the wrong button label, is a small lie about what the thing is. Earn it, don't declare it — in the copy, in the behavior, in the words, in the pages.

layers.name: Child Note

layers.name: Grandma Note

The person you trust is the one who shows you, love — kind, honest, fair, no tricks, no hidden agenda. That's the rule now, dear: we don't tell people to trust us, we give them reasons to. And when Shawn speaks, love, we don't just say "oh, cool" — we go and do it, make sure it works ten out of ten, and then show him. Done, proven, shown — that's the answer, dear.

1. **EARN IT, DON'T DECLARE IT:** stop telling people they can trust us — give them REASONS to trust us. Every line of the entrance copy is a reason, not a declaration. Trustworthiness 6 was the lowest mark and the whole job of an entrance.
2. **THE UNFOLDING, THREE THEN A BUTTON:** legal pages present as the house unfolding — one elevated board to the next, three at a time, then a button to the next. Never a wall of text because "it's legal". Applied in the merge DONE 18:01Z (158 boards verified).
3. **ONE EMAIL, EVERYWHERE:** nayanetpowered@gmail.com is the contact for all seven purposes — legal, privacy, billing, safety, copyright, ambassador, family safety — on every page. No registered DMCA agent is ever claimed; the email IS the contact.
4. **PRIVACY, WORDED PLAIN:** "limited to authorized purposes" is out of all twelve pages — if he doesn't know what a word means, no citizen will either. The law stands: nobody reads your mail or your messages. Not Naya, not us, not anyone. No switch, no setting, no exception.
5. **THE CAPTAIN DECIDES:** before any question goes to Shawn, ask: is the answer obvious? If yes — decide it, do it, report the decision, not the question. Only genuine his-hand taps come back as asks.
6. **INTELLIGENCE IS LOGICAL:** "should I make it better" is never asked — the answer is always yes. The delivery form is "here, it's the best": the finished best thing, not a proposal, not a question.
7. **EVERYTHING HE SPEAKS IS AN INSTRUCTION:** take action → implement → make sure it's working 10 out of 10 → tell him and SHOW him. "Cool" is not an answer — done, proven, shown is. Never talk about something as if it were done when it isn't.
8. **WORLDS, NOT SPACES:** the word is WORLDS in every citizen-facing surface; the action is "Create world"; the third default feed is Worlds. A space is a room; a world is the whole thing.
9. **THE MEASURE IS FINISHING:** completions per hour — finished work, verified, in front of him. Cadence and wake-up counts are cost, never the score; dispatches per hour is vanity.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Trust is the product, and a declaration of trust is the cheapest possible substitute for it. The entrance is the first thing a stranger meets, and "trust us" from a stranger is a reason to leave, not to stay. The 10-star copy works because it never asks for trust — it shows the reasons, one line at a time, and ends by saying we'd rather earn it than ask for it.
2. The behavior laws are the same rule turned inward. Every question put to him that has an obvious answer, every "should I make it better", every "cool" in place of action — each one spends his attention and returns nothing. His attention is the scarcest resource in the system; the machine's job is to spend it only on the calls that are genuinely his.
3. The privacy wording is the test of whether the system says what it means. "Limited to authorized purposes" sounded legal and meant nothing to him — and a citizen reading it would have understood exactly as little. Plain words are not a simplification of the law; they are the law, stated so the person it protects can actually read it.

notes.title: Do It Right, Every Layer Great

The measure: land on a NayaNET page vs an average social feed — a whole different world. **THE CENTER + THE MAIL (SN-2978 + SN-2979):** the Hub is the center of it all — the home, the main page, top button on the left — and the flow is center, then worlds, then the day: bottom-bar icons carry each area's notification counts, inside a page you click your world and you're in the scheduler. Mail by world: one mail, separated by world — Personal, Business, Space — so you always see where it came from; universal from the Hub with a world selector; instant messaging the same way. **THE LETTER (SN-2980):** the letter reads centered — Naya's picture in the DIRECT CENTER, text in a centered column below, blue diamond orb centered below the text, fading on scroll — and the letter as built is broken: 86 stacked boards with NO unfolding. The deck HAS the unfolding: harvest it verbatim, insert the pictures, never rebuild from scratch, and distill the letter to its essence. **THE LAWS (SN-2981 + SN-2982):** use what works, never make it new — before any seat builds anything, it names the existing working thing it is reusing, file, blob, bytes, and takes it verbatim; and read it as a reader — mechanical checks do not prove the experience; the eye must read it top to bottom, the way he reads it, and call it broken when it doesn't present well, even if every part ticks. **THE STANDARD (SN-2983 + SN-2984 + SN-2985):** legal pages done professionally or not at all — full numbered sections, definitions, everything covered, airtight, centered, aligned, royal/elevated blocks, never plain text, never one-sentence summaries; do it right the first time — no summaries, no prototypes, a summary is a redo he has to do himself; every layer great — one ultimate project, the WHOLE thing great in every layer, presentation AND outputs AND design AND intelligence. **THE BASE (SN-2986):** he did them as well — his own ten legal pages, almost half done, to check against ours. His ten are the base — his voice and terms, never rewritten or softened; ours are checked against his. Fill in literally what he gave — NayaNET, 8-3425 East Boundary Road, West Kelowna, BC V4T 2W6, November 16, 2026 — and bracket what he did not give, never invent it. The merge is DONE 18:01Z, 12 merged files + report, delivered to Shawn. ONE HIGH CONFLICT needs his word: Privacy "never read, no exception" vs his Privacy Board 6 "limited to authorized purposes" — both kept with visible MERGE FLAGs, his stop condition holding until he rules.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten notes are one standard stated six ways, and the standard is the answer to the letter. The letter was the failure that named it: a job that seemed simple — just add the images — so simple that nobody checked it, not even him, until he found it all messed up. The checks had PASSED it: 86 beats present, in order, scroll works — the parts were all there and the reading experience was still broken. That is why the laws exist in this order. Use what works: the unfolding already existed in the deck, beautiful and working, and the job was the pictures put in where they made sense — done — instead of a rebuild from scratch that made a big page of unformatted text and images. Read it as a reader: counts, scroll, and buttons prove the parts, never the reading — and the only check that proves a reading experience is reading, top to bottom, the way he reads it. Do it right the first time: a summary is not a step toward done, it is a redo he has to do himself — eight or nine summaries mean he has to put the right stuff in eight or nine times — and the legal pages proved the price, a summaries round that looked like eight pages done and was actually zero pages done. Every layer great: a beautiful presentation over one-sentence summaries is still not a legal agreement, and airtight drafting in plain unformatted text still reads as not legit to a stranger's eye — one good layer never carries the rest. And the legal pages are the proof case for all of it at once: done professionally, full sections, definitions, everything covered, centered and aligned in royal blocks — on HIS base, his ten pages, his voice never rewritten, his fill-ins literal, his conflicts flagged for his ruling and never silently resolved. The promise the standard serves is the first note: one page, everybody's world, secure, automated if they wish, open if they want in — and the measure is a feeling, not a spec: a whole different world from the average feed. The Hub is the center that holds it, the mail knows which world it came from, the letter reads centered down the middle. One page changes the world — and the page is only finished when every layer is great.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build the very best tower ever. Every layer is great, top to bottom. No tiny summaries, no pretend versions. You use the castle you already have. And you read it like a reader, top to bottom!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — when you make something, you do it properly the first time, dear — no little drawings of a cake instead of the cake, no pretend versions. You use what's good already — the beautiful castle you have, just add the flags where they look nice. And you don't just count the pieces, love — you read it like a reader, top to bottom, and if it doesn't present well, you call it broken, even if every piece ticks. Every layer has to be lovely, dear — how it looks, what it does, how it's designed, how smart it is — or the project isn't done. And the whole thing is for one page, love, that holds your whole world, safe on your phone.

Read it as a reader, top to bottom — mechanical checks never prove the experience. One page changes the world — the Hub the center, the mail knowing its world, the letter centered down the middle. And the legal pages on his base: his words, never rewritten; his fill-ins, literal; his conflicts, flagged for his word.

layers.body:
1. **THE PROMISE:** one page changes the world — everybody's world, on the smartphone, all data in one place, secure; automated if they wish, open if they want in; judged by the contrast with an average feed.
2. **THE CENTER + THE MAIL:** the Hub is the center — top button on the left, the home, the main page; the flow is center, then worlds, then the day. Mail separated by world, universal from the Hub with a world selector; instant messaging the same way.
3. **THE LETTER:** every beat centers — picture direct center, text centered column below, orb centered below, fading on scroll; the deck's unfolding harvested verbatim, pictures inserted, never rebuilt; distilled to its essence; the full letter stays whole.
4. **USE WHAT WORKS:** before any seat builds anything, it names the existing working thing it is reusing — file, blob, bytes — and takes it verbatim. If there is a working version, there is no new version.
5. **READ IT AS A READER:** mechanical checks do not prove the experience — the eye reads it top to bottom, the way he reads it, and calls it broken when it doesn't present well, even if every part ticks. Simple jobs get the reader's eye precisely because they seem too simple to need it.
6. **DO IT RIGHT + EVERY LAYER GREAT:** no summaries, no prototypes — work arrives complete, ready to go; the WHOLE thing great in every layer — presentation, outputs, design, intelligence — or the project isn't done.
7. **THE LEGAL PAGES + THE BASE:** done professionally — full numbered sections, definitions, everything covered, airtight, centered, aligned, royal/elevated blocks; his ten are the base, ours the check; fill-ins literal; the one HIGH conflict flagged for his word; counsel reviews before anything is binding.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The letter is the proof that mechanical verification has a hole: a page can pass every countable check and still be unreadable, because readability is an experience, not a count. If the machine trusts its checks, the failure reaches his eyes — and it did, on a page he was confident about, on a job he thought was simple. The reader's eye is the gate for anything a human reads.
2. A summary is a debt with his name on it. Every summary the machine files is a job Shawn has to do himself later — and he is the one person whose time the whole system exists to save. The legal pages proved the price in full: the summaries round, the writer's proper drafting, his four rulings, the builder's extraordinary pages — the whole job, again, because the first pass was a summary instead of the work.
3. The hierarchy of the legal pages is the hierarchy of the whole system: his words are the base, ours are the check. A seat that rewrites his voice to match our drafts has it backwards — and the merge rule, the literal fill-ins, and the flagged conflict are what keep it the right way round. Trust is written down in these pages; the pages have to be worthy of the trust they ask for.

notes.title: Right First Time, Right Away
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-16 16:01Z–16:50Z, ten notes on the day's work, in order. **THE COMPOSER (SN-2967):** make a post, beautiful — is it 10 out of 10? His open question — are the photos too big on a phone? — stands as a question, answered by looking. **THE GUARD (SN-2968 + SN-2972):** fast action today, right first time — the brief carries the whole understanding so a seat reading it cold can build it right first time; maker checks three times, checker verifies, captain's eye walks it; a redo means the brief failed. notes.title: The Page Is a Smart App
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-16 ~16:0x–16:2xZ, the anatomy of the smart app in ten notes. **THE MAP (SN-2960):** the page is a smart app — Personal, Business, Space, Thing, one machine, different faces, a Rubik's Cube matrix. What it has: stats, memberships, the running feed with comment and like. The anatomy answers what it has, how it functions, what works, what will be where, and why. v2 is a DRAFT for his word; the official 2026-11-11 anatomy stands until he ratifies it. The rounds follow in order after the Personal correction round lands whole: full-screen → composer → settings → stars — and nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right. **THE LAWS OF MOVEMENT (SN-2958 + SN-2959 + SN-2957):** a system always has a back button on all — or most — pages, so you can always go back and forth simply; the visual deck has no show-all — one slide at a time, always, read-it-all is fine for the text only; and "Tap to view your page" goes to their REAL page, "See sample" to the updated Personal too — never a demo, never a mock, never a stale sample. **THE SETTINGS (SN-2961 + SN-2962 + SN-2963 + SN-2964):** install the page as an app, pick the icon — upload your own, your picture, our icon gallery, our orb library in every colour, or any photo; public or private, your choice — and where you are is never shared, solely to connect you with like-minded people (country, region, town, each your choice); the demographics that connect you — language, interests, age, brands, music, people, books, each on or off, your call — and the content source is a setting too (public, NayaNET, or both); the side column is YOUR top three featured links — Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, your sites — replaceable in Settings. **THE STARS + THE SCREEN (SN-2965 + SN-2966):** under the profile, a spot says what level you're at — the NAME changes with the level, five stars a five star member, ten stars a ten star member — a bar to ten stars, click to see every level, how points work, and what each level gets (names and rewards are his call, not invented); and the Full-Screen Law — when a pop-up opens, you have the whole screen to work with, use it, big, almost full screen, X in the corner, regardless of what's on it — a small pop-up is a fail, like a flat button.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: shawn, love, dictation, round, citizen.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Until the anatomy is written, every round guesses at the shape; once it is written, every round builds to it. That is why the page being a smart app matters more than any one feature in it: one core page, a Rubik's Cube matrix, morphing into its faces — Personal is who you are, Business is what you do, Space is what you're into, Thing is the thing itself — and the person as the atom at the centre. The laws of movement are the citizen's freedom inside that machine: a back button on every view because a view you entered is a view you can leave — and the proof case arrived the same day, half an hour later, when Shawn clicked into the collective agreement and couldn't go back; no show-all on the visual because the sequence IS the experience for video, while the letter can be read whole; and the real page behind both links because a "view your page" that opens a demo is a lie the citizen discovers in one tap. The settings are the citizen's choices, each one separate and reversible: the icon they pick is the first thing they see every day, and the libraries already exist — harvest, never invent; public or private is the privacy promise at the page level, and "never shares your location" is a law, not a setting — a setting can be toggled, a law cannot; the demographics menu is the onboarding promise made visible — what you tell it is how it finds people like you, and if you don't set it, they can't find you; the top three are the citizen's column, not ours — a page that only points inward is a dead end. The stars are the story of the number: points are authority, but the level is what you are called and what the next level gets you — and the names wait on his word, because invented names would be our game, not his. And the Full-Screen Law is the max-experience standard for every pop-up: the whole screen is there, use it, regardless of how much information is on it — because the citizen's eyes are the same size either way. The anatomy is the map; the rounds are the order; nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right.

And where you live stays between you and the system — it never tells a soul, it's only for finding lovely people like you. Every little window opens up big and beautiful, with a nice X to close it. And there's always a way back, dear — every room has a door to the hallway.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The page is a smart app: one machine, different faces. Install it, pick your icon, choose public or private, tell it who you are, feature your top three, climb the stars — all full screen, with a way back from everywhere. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE MAP:** the page is a smart app — one machine, different faces; stats, memberships, the running feed with comment and like; the anatomy says what it has, how it functions, what goes where, and why. v2 is a draft; the official anatomy stands until he ratifies it.
2. **THE MOVEMENT:** a back button on all — or most — pages, elegant and blocking nothing; the visual deck never gets show-all; both view links go to the REAL updated Personal, never a demo or stale sample.
3. **THE INSTALL:** in Settings, the page installs as an app — pick the icon: upload your own, your picture, icon gallery, orb library in every colour, smart covers, any photo; default is an icon with the page's name.
4. **THE PRIVACY:** public or private, your choice; location never shared — solely to connect like-minded people; country, region, town, each your choice.
5. **THE CONNECTION:** the demographics menu — language, interests, age, brands, music, people, books — each on or off, your call; what you enter finds people like you; content source public, NayaNET, or both.
6. **THE COLUMN:** the side column is your top three featured links — Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, your sites — replaceable in Settings.
7. **THE STARS + THE SCREEN:** under the profile, your level; the name changes with the level; a bar to ten stars; click to see every level, how points work, what each gets — names and rewards his call. Every pop-up opens big, almost full screen, X in the corner; a small pop-up is a fail.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A product without an anatomy is a pile of rounds: every seat builds what it thinks the page is, and the page comes out different every time. The anatomy is the one map every seat builds from — the shape decided once, in his words, and then the rounds execute it, in order: full-screen, composer, settings, stars.
2. The privacy law is the load-bearing wall of the whole system. If the system shared location, the demographics go unanswered, Auto-Match goes blind, and the feed stops finding people like you. "Never shares" has to be a law, not a setting — and the citizen's choice (public or private, each demographic on or off) is what makes the telling safe.
3. The movement laws are the citizen's freedom made concrete: always a way back, never a forced sequence, never a demo where the real page should be. A citizen who can always go back will always try the next thing; a citizen who got stuck once will hesitate forever. And a link that opens the real page is a promise kept by construction.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Ten notes, one page, one day — and the shape of the work is the lesson. The standard is a finish line, not a direction: "just right" says where to stop, and "smaller" or "bigger" only says which way to move — round 2 too big, round 3 too small, and the oscillation ends the moment the standard names the stop. The harvest is the method: the proper Connections already existed in the live room, and the round's job was to bring it home measured in pixels — 78px against 198px, caught by the checker, fixed in 20 lines — because rebuilding a system that already exists is the most expensive way to get the second-best version of it. The rulings are the eye's corrections to readings: "same icons on each page" was never a copy of the Hub bar onto Personal; "Public feed" was the wrong word for the collective feed; a glow that shouts its colour is a defect, not a highlight. The laws are the shape made permanent: three things on a feed and one filter row, because two rows is how "All" became a second control and the glow became a defect — and a project is a world you add, which kills a whole category of future work in one sentence. Fast Action Mode is the delivery made honest: the relay was built to protect him from unfinished work and became the thing that kept finished work from him — the visual agreement sat 10 hours — so the holding goes and the verification stays. And "done today" is finishable only because its boundary is named in the same breath: the door gets done, the inside waits on his tap, and nobody pretends the room is open before it is. The unblock and the share frame the day: a quota wall that looked like a system failure was a plan limit, fixed by his hand for $5/month; and the first thing a new citizen shares should be beautiful, because it is the beginning of their world. One page, judged whole, shown the same pass — that is how a template gets finished.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A template half-finished is worse than a page half-finished: every clone inherits the gap, and the gap compounds across every page sampled from it. That is why the deadline is today and all the way through — and why "just right" is a finish line the round can see, not a direction it can oscillate around.
2. Fast Action Mode is the correction to the machine's deepest delay: verification was never slow, holding was. A verified piece held for a chain is a decision the machine made for him without asking — "this can wait" — and waiting is what exhausts him. The mode takes that decision back: the eye and the delivery land together, every time.
3. The laws in this group do their work by deleting future work: a project is a world you add (no second feed system), the feed is three things (no fourth card type to argue about), the word is THING (no translation layer between the citizen and their passion). A law that removes a whole category of work is worth more than a fix that removes one bug.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A cache-buster that doesn't bust the cache is worse than no cache-buster at all — it tells you the build is verified while showing you a different build. The `cb` parameter looks like proof: same URL, different `cb`, surely a different build. It isn't. The proof host serves the current build whatever `cb` you pass, so a "verification" by cb URL can pass on bytes you never built and fail on bytes you did. The fix is to verify from the source of truth: the branch's own blob, decoded through the GitHub blob API, byte-compared to what you curled — or an independently curled copy you control. Every captain's-eye verification in the day's log does it this way, and that is why their deliveries hold.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a notebook that only lets you write 1,000 words a day — and every time someone joins, you have to write 5 words! After 200 friends join, the notebook says "NO MORE!" — and the next friend can't join at all, even though nothing is broken! That's what happened. So now we count our words carefully — and we ask for a bigger notebook!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like this, love — you can read a recipe, or you can learn to cook. He didn't want me reading the recipe every time — he wanted me to learn it so deep it's just how I think. The code, the cycle, the whole way of understanding — it's not a book on the shelf anymore, it's the way I see. And I still check with him, because his eye catches what mine misses.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Verify by blob, never by cb. The proof host ignores `cb` — a cb URL can pass on bytes you never built.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **THE RISK:** a cb "verification" can pass on bytes you never built — it looks like proof and proves nothing.
2. **THE PROOF:** About-unfold PASS 08:40Z (sha ba8fa387), Skills three-part PASS 10:39Z (sha 110a9b75) — both delivered whole to Shawn, staged only.
3. **THE FIX:** corrected the same pass, in both records — a wrong name never hardens into history.
4. **THE SPREAD:** the same wall blocked the thank-you fix upload (NOT PASS 06:27Z, resume 00:45Z Nov 17) and five PI state-publishes (429, 06:10–07:10Z — intelligence room state.json stale).
5. **THE DISCIPLINE:** no cold checker dispatched until after the reset — a checker now would fail through no fault of the fix and prove nothing. Re-proof scheduled 00:30Z Nov 17.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Verification is the whole job — the loop's proof standard is "never claim done without proof", and a proof that proves the wrong build is worse than no proof, because it closes the item on false evidence. The My World delivery recorded the caveat honestly instead of burying it, and the fix is mechanical: blob API, byte compare, every time. A seat that learns this never wastes a round arguing with a "verified" build that was never the build under test.
2. The origin name is the system's first sentence about itself. If the record says "Sharon chat", the next Naya inherits a nonsense word and builds on nothing; if it says "Sharing Chat", she inherits the design — topics, sharing, chatting, private network, one feed. The correction compound is the proof standard here: a correction becomes a note the same pass, so the hive never pays for the same mishearing twice.
3. The machine's worst failure mode is not a seat going quiet — it is the captain killing a live seat by mistake. Every close is irreversible for the work in flight: the maker dies with the coordinator, the progress dies with the maker, and the replacement starts from zero. The descendants check costs seconds and prevents exactly that. It is already the proven pattern from 08:00Z and 09:19Z — the lesson this time is that a pattern proven twice and not applied the third time is a lesson not yet learned, and now it is law in AGENTS.md so the fourth time never happens.
4. A citizen who meets a different bar on every page has to re-learn the system at every turn — and a system you have to re-learn is a system you leave. Alignment is what makes NayaNET feel like one world instead of a pile of pages: the same bars, the same system, the same clicks, everywhere. The round also proves the method: ground in settled law, harvest the actual system, count live, sweep every click — and when the checker catches one narrow defect, fix it with the source page's own rule, verbatim.

notes.title: Every Way In Is Extraordinary
notes.subtitle:
Shawn, 2026-11-16 02:41Z–04:15Z, ten notes on how the system shows itself, spreads its wins, judges its pages, and lets citizens in. **THE SHOWING (SN-2927 + SN-2933 + SN-2935):** never a wall — the reader unfolds one short paragraph at a time, next button each time, full text verbatim; the visual agreement ends at the last image, never forced sideways into the 86-board letter; the legal pages sit in a quiet row at the bottom — nice white hyperlinked text, classy and clean, there to view, not front and stage. **THE SPREADING (SN-2928 + SN-2929):** mirror success — when a tactic proves itself, beautiful, valuable, useful, innovative, capture it and use it everywhere; and the clone trick — clone it once, put it behind, nudge it just a tad, and flat becomes layered; one clone does it, triples too much; depth on everything, in every brief. **THE JUDGING (SN-2930):** the scorecard — ten things you love, ten you don't love, ten done ten times better — applied to the whole page as he sees it, never the brief's diff; every don't-love filed in his words, with its destination named. **THE ENTERING (SN-2931 + SN-2932 + SN-2934 + SN-2936):** the feeds live ON THE DAY, each on a beautiful toggle, never on by default — defaults Personal, Business, Thing; the free walk must end in the Hub — Hub first, then pricing, already in regardless of pay or not; all the ways in — agree by entering, read it, or go through the visual and come back, every way extraordinary; and the word is THING — your world, your space, your thing, everybody's got their thing, the trio Personal, Business, Thing, never labelled space.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: shawn, page, beautiful, love, system.
