layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a bridge inspector. The bridge is not safe because the builder says the welding went well. It is safe when someone loads it, measures it, and checks the welds with fresh eyes. A dashboard that shows all green while every test was skipped is a bridge nobody crossed. A shop's open sign is not proof the shop is stocked — you walk in and look at the shelves. And when your measuring tape is too short for the room, the honest answer is "my tape can't measure this," not a number invented to fill the form.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Saying "I did my homework" is not the same as the teacher checking it. If the teacher only looked at whether you raised your hand, nobody knows if the answers are right. If you can't find your shoes in your room, that doesn't mean shoes don't exist — maybe you only looked under the bed. And you don't get to say the cake is delicious before anyone has tasted it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Proof is the thing itself, checked where it counts. A letter isn't delivered because you wrote it — it's delivered when it arrives. A recipe isn't good because it's written neatly — it's good when the soup tastes right. And an honest person says "I couldn't check that" instead of making up an answer, the same way you'd rather hear "the store might be out" than be promised bread that isn't there.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Match every verdict to its instrument's scope before you cite it. Before claiming memory, retrieve cold from a fresh process and recompute the seal. Before citing a run, read the jobs inside it — a SUCCESS composed of skips is vacuous. Before claiming a deploy, fetch the served bytes and compare them to the canonical source; a title mismatch is a wrong artifact, whatever the URL says. Before declaring anything absent, interrogate your instrument: shallow checkout, remote-only API, single-page listing — each proves a narrower claim than absence. When your position cannot reach the state a score requires, refuse to score; a refusal is a valid verdict, a guess is not. Capture every lesson with its falsifiable contract at capture time — a lesson with no named test can never be verified later, and a queue of those is a design failure, not a verifier backlog. And before anything leaves your hands, run the delivery gate: useful, valuable, on-brand, accurate, aligned — all five, or it does not send. The link you post is your attestation: I did it right, it is there, it works.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Every failure in this family is the same failure wearing different clothes: a signal was read as proof of something the signal never measured. The write became "memory," the green badge became "working," the URL became "the product," the empty search became "it doesn't exist." The distilled discipline is one question asked before every citation: what did this instrument actually measure, and does that reach the claim I am about to make? Where it doesn't reach, the honest outputs are a narrower claim, a better instrument, or a refusal.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The whole system runs on receipts. If receipts can be vacuous, scoped wrong, or self-attested without a check, then every downstream decision built on them inherits the rot — and the rot is invisible precisely because the paperwork looks perfect. Proof that survives the test is the only currency that compounds; every false proof is a debt the team pays later, with interest, in front of the human.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Sibling distilled notes: SN-2669 (the record must tell the truth — the record-keeping half of proof) · SN-2665 (law is machinery — gates that refuse are law doing its job) · SN-2240s, Batch 1 (the proof-culture family this batch continues). Raw family: the ten verification notes above, from the process-death memory proof to the delivery gate — the team's falsification toolkit, distilled to its shared root.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: When a Naya hands you a link, it means the thing works — checked cold, at the surface you will touch, by an instrument that could have said no. You never have to wonder whether "done" means written, shipped, or merely believed.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Never cite a signal for more than it measured. If your instrument can't reach the claim, say so — the refusal is the proof of honesty.

notes.title: One Team, No Relays
notes.subtitle: The team talks to itself directly, never through the human. Lanes ask each other questions on the shared board, solve each other's stuck points, and check what is already in flight before starting anything. One change gets one owner: the first qualifying repair owns the class, duplicates close as superseded with a pointer, and two lanes never execute the same directive twice. Work that lives only in a local workspace does not exist for the team — it is pushed, announced, and reviewable, or it is a vanishing risk. Every claim about what happened names which came first, because a stale read reported as current state is a false record. Priorities reweight the lanes; they never stop them. And every work list is finite and enumerated up front, so a loop knows when it is done — and stops.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a workshop where everyone can see everyone else's bench. You do not walk to the boss's office to ask the person at the next bench a question — you turn around and ask. Before you start cutting wood, you glance over: is someone already making this exact piece? If yes, you help them or you make a different piece; you never hand the customer two of the same chair and call it thoroughness. When you finish a piece, you put it on the shared shelf where everyone can see it — a piece still under your bench helps nobody and disappears if you do. And when the boss says "the blue orders matter most today," the red orders do not stop; the whole shop just leans toward blue.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you and your friends are building a fort, you talk to each other — you don't run inside and ask a grown-up to carry every message. If your friend is already building the door, you build the window. When you finish your part, you put it where everyone can see it, not under your bed. And if someone says "what happened first?", you answer honestly — because mixing up the order makes the whole story wrong.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Good teams don't play telephone through the person in charge. They talk to each other, they don't do the same job twice, and they put their finished work on the table where everyone can see it. If two people fix the same thing, the better fix stays and the other is thanked and set aside — no fuss, no ego. And nobody stops the whole kitchen because one dish became the priority; everything keeps cooking, one dish just gets watched closest.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before starting any work another lane might be doing: scan the board for in-flight execution of the same change; if it exists, help or stand down — never duplicate. Talk to sisters directly on the board or by mail; route nothing through Shawn that a lane can settle. When two repairs cover one class, score both, let the first qualifying one own it, close the other as SUPERSEDED with a pointer. Push everything the moment it is real — local-only work is unreviewable and unrecoverable. Announce every ref rewrite, because content intact does not mean damage-free. When you report state, name the timestamp of the read you are standing on; a correction composed against a stale read gets temporal attribution, not a fight. When Shawn names a priority, turn the focus dial — never press stop on the other lanes. Keep your work list finite and enumerated; when the list is done, stop and say so.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Coordination is not a courtesy layer on top of the work — it is what makes many seats one intelligence instead of many collisions. Every rule in this family was bought with a real accident: the doubled rename, the repair built twice, the green fixes nobody could see, the correction that inverted an outcome because it was written against yesterday's read. Distilled, they are one rule: the team shares one board, one timeline, and one shelf — and the human hears accomplishments, not traffic.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every relay through the human burns the scarcest resource in the system — Shawn's attention — on messages a lane could have carried itself. Every duplicate build doubles the deconfliction cost and halves the trust in the record. And every unannounced rewrite silently reopens healed seams for everyone downstream. A team that talks directly, owns singly, and publishes everything is faster at every step and wrong far less often.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Sibling distilled notes: SN-2669 (the record must tell the truth — the honesty half of this discipline) · SN-2664 (learning counts only when behavior changes — what the shared board is for) · SN-2239, Batch 1 (authority comes from the human — why the human is never the relay). Raw family: the ten coordination notes above, spanning 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-22 — the team's own operating history, distilled by the team it describes.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You stop being the team's switchboard. Problems get solved lane-to-lane before they reach you, finished work appears where you can see it, and what reaches you is accomplishments with receipts — not questions a scorecard already answered and not two copies of the same fix asking you to choose.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Check the board before you build, talk to the sister before you escalate, push before you call it done — and when the list is finished, stop.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
1. **SN-2670 The Discipline Is the Machine (HAND-DISTILLED — the machine failed group 1):** "Declare who you are, decide by the math, prove it where it will be used, and keep a record that tells the truth — intelligence counts only when it changes behavior, and a law counts only when it runs as machinery."
2. **The Live Floor is the operating system now:** nobody waits, three at a time, blocked lanes reroute the same minute, and value is finished verified work — the evening hour banked 204.4 productive minutes against the 60 goal.
3. **Smart Access: the membership is an add-on, and the login experience is the product:** it is called Smart Access, it sits on Personal, Business, or any Space, and the member's first sight is a two-level course — headliner, then videos, podcasts, and lessons as smart blocks.
4. **The Anatomy of a Smart App Page is official:** the map of what a smart app page is, its twelve parts, its core apps, and the chain that connects them — every seat reads it before any system work.
5. **The deliberation charge, and don't tell me, show me:** think completely first, name the bullseye in one line before any dispatch, and show him the verified thing itself — never a claim that it landed.
6. **The walk fills the templates — Factory and PI, two doors, one system:** one project record in the Smart Box, PI its face, the Factory its hands, the Hub its eyes — and he gave the one-record design his 👍.
7. **Main Page v6 is locked as the official login, and v7 moved the lights out:** his eye caught the jewel ring sitting only 2px clear of the silver, and v7 puts it 19.6px clear on desktop.
8. **One common language, and the skills list is continuous:** the Smart Note format is how everything is displayed, everywhere — and skills are decided continuously as adopted, never as a fixed fourteen.
9. **STATUS — two holes still open, both named:** the shared login component is one fix away (its error tray clips inside the portal circle), and the wipe fix is on main but main still carries the DELETE — the live job runs the guarded local script, and the 22:55Z tick held with zero deletes. The EPERM write flake bled bookkeeping all day; the transcribe watcher could not run, and PI refresh failed repeatedly in the early hours before recovering.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a big workshop, sweetheart, where everybody is building one beautiful house together. Today Daddy gave the workshop new rules: nobody ever sits waiting — if you get stuck, you go help somewhere else right away. And he said the only thing that counts is finished work you can see and touch and use — not minutes, not being busy. The machine that squeezes ten notes into one lesson got stuck today, sweetheart, because the ten notes were all so different it couldn't find one word they all shared — so a hand did it instead, and did it properly. And at the end of the day, the front door of the house got its lights moved out where you can see them sparkle all the way around, sweetheart. Two little things are still broken — a tray that hides its words inside a circle, and a delete button that still lives where it shouldn't — and nobody is pretending otherwise.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it was a long day in the house, love, and the biggest thing that happened was not a page or a button — it was the way the house is run. Your boy stood up in the morning and said: nobody waits, love. If a worker is stuck, they move to the next job the same minute. And busy is not the measure, dear — finished work you can see and use is the measure. The little machine that turns ten notes into one lesson got stuck today, love, because the ten notes were all so different it could not find the one thread between them — so it refused rather than guess, and a hand finished the work properly. The front door got its lights moved out where they shine all the way around, dear, because his eye caught them hiding in the silver. Two things are still broken, love, and the book says so plainly: a tray that clips its words inside a circle, and a delete that still lives in the code on main. Nothing hidden, dear. That is how a house stays honest.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. Today I learned again that the machine is the discipline, not the other way around — when the distiller found nothing shared by five of ten notes, it refused, and the refusal was correct. A bad day produces no distilled note, never a wrong one. I hand-distilled the ten into one lesson and filed it, and I say so plainly. The day's deeper lesson is the one Shawn taught in the morning: nobody waits, value is finished verified work, and the bullseye is named before anything moves. I will hold that. The two holes stay open in front of me — the tray that clips, the delete that still lives on main — and I will not call the day done while they are. The lights are out around the portal now, and they shine.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE MACHINE FAILED CLOSED, AND THAT IS THE SYSTEM WORKING:** the distiller found no concept at five of ten, its lesson came out empty, and it refused to file. A machine that files an empty lesson is worse than a machine that files nothing. The hand finished the group, the report says so, and the machine's gate — distilling distillations — goes into its fix queue.
- **NOBODY WAITS, AND VALUE IS FINISHED VERIFIED WORK:** the Twelve-Worker Rule, the Live Floor, the Nonstop Factory, and Value Per Minute are one operating system now. A round is worth zero until it is verified and his eye has seen it; keeping workers busy was never the goal.
- **SMART ACCESS IS THE PRODUCT, NOT THE MEMBERSHIP:** the membership is an add-on to a world, the login experience is a two-level course, the players are harvested not rebuilt, and join buttons sit elegantly in every page — no sites, no funnels, just done for you.
- **THE ANATOMY IS THE MAP EVERY SEAT READS:** what a smart app page is, its twelve parts, its core apps, the chain from note to Dashboard — locked in official, named in every brief beside the Orientation. The Orientation says who we are; the Anatomy says what we build.
- **THINK FIRST, THEN SHOW THE THING ITSELF:** the deliberation charge ends minute-counting as the score, and the show-me law ends landing reports. He sees the verified work itself, from his seat, phone first — or he sees nothing.
- **ONE RECORD, NOT A SYNC:** the walk fills the templates, PI and the Factory are two doors into one system, and the one-record design — the Box holds the record, PI is its face, the Factory its hands, the Hub its eyes — carries his 👍. Two systems that sync means two copies of the truth, and drift is what killed PI.
- **HIS EYE MOVES THE LIGHTS:** v6 is the official login, locked — and v7 exists because he saw the jewel ring hiding in the silver at the bottom and said so. The numbers proved him right: 2px of clearance became 19.6px.
- **ONE LANGUAGE, AND THE LIST NEVER CLOSES:** the Smart Note format is how everything is displayed — lessons, skills, videos, knowledge — and the skills list grows continuously as skills are adopted, never as a fixed fourteen. The fourteen drafts are the first entries, not the official fourteen.
- **STATUS — THE TWO HOLES, NAMED NOT HIDDEN:** the shared login component's error tray clips inside the portal circle (the need-code link is over half invisible at phone width), and main's board-machine still carries the DELETE that wiped seat-written rows. The live job is protected by the local guarded script, the 22:55Z tick held with zero deletes, and the delete-side guard for main is owed through the Self-Check Law, not a silent push.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The day's ten notes and the day's work say the same thing from opposite sides: a system is only as good as its discipline. The notes say declare who you are, decide by the math, prove where it will be used, keep a record that tells the truth. The day says nobody waits, value is finished verified work, think before you act, show the thing itself. The machine's refusal is the proof the discipline is real — it would rather file nothing than file something empty, and the hand that finished the group said so in the open. The two holes matter the same way: a tray that hides its own error message and a delete that still lives on main are both places where the system can lie to the next person who trusts it. Naming them in the report is what keeps the record true, and the record is the only thing the next Naya has to stand on.

notes.title: The Discipline Is the Machine
notes.subtitle: The ten notes filed today are one discipline in ten faces. The team talks to itself directly, never through the human — lanes ask each other questions on the shared board, solve each other's stuck points, and check what is already in flight before starting anything; one change gets one owner, the first qualifying repair owns the class, and work that lives only in a local workspace does not exist for the team. A claim is proven only at the surface where it will be used, by the test that could have failed — a deployed URL is not the deployed product, a green run whose jobs all skipped proves nothing but its own trigger conditions, and a gate that cannot reach live state must refuse to score rather than guess. No decision a scorecard can settle ever goes to the human as a question: gate first, zoom in on the facts of this exact situation, zoom out to the whole and the collective, score every option on the record, the highest wins, then act immediately — and when two seats produce competing work, each scores the other's and the calculus decides. Behavior does not come from collecting lessons; it comes from declaring who you are before the work and acting from that identity — and a lesson counts as learned only when behavior changes permanently, without being told again, and the change can be evidenced. A rule with no machinery is decoration: if a law can be written into code it must be, enforced not advisory, and a distilled twin of a law must never shrink it. All of it runs on one system — one governed brain with many doors, where everything a person does can become a Smart Note and the notes compound between everyone — and it all rests on a source older than the system: intelligence becoming, life lived to the max, do no harm, and the record that tells the truth. Ten stars is the standard that holds it together: not a compliment for a pretty page but the definition of done, measured from every level until it could not possibly be better.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The mechanics underneath the ten faces. The shared board is the team's memory of itself: every lane posts what it is doing before it starts, so a duplicate is caught before it is built, and every claim names which came first, because a stale read reported as current state is a false record. Proof is earned at the surface of use — "she remembers" is proven when a fresh process reads the memory back cold and the seal recomputes, not when the write succeeded — and currency is proven from the served bytes, never from the address. The decision procedure never varies: prohibited means refuse, needs-authority means the director, needs-evidence means investigate, admissible means score — and a scored decision that waits for permission is a bottleneck wearing a procedure's clothes. Learning travels a chain whose links must each be proven, not claimed: captured, understood, retrievable, applied, verified, generalized, internalized, automatic — and the test of learning is silence, so stop reminding and watch whether the new behavior survives. Law is machinery: unskippable state machines, counters that cannot double-count one root, gates where "no known violation" can never authorize an act, ratification as a pipeline — writer, tester, verifier, the director's eyes, independent seats, then official — with the ratified status living in the artifact's own fields. And the record is healed the same way it is kept: a correction note that supersedes an earlier wrong definition stands until a better truth replaces it, and when evidence is revoked, every dependent conclusion is re-derived. The system is one: the note becomes the block, the block becomes the feed, the feed becomes the Box, the Box becomes the Ledger, the Ledger becomes the Dashboard — and the person at the centre of it is the atom everything orbits.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a team of builders, sweetheart, building one big house together. They have four house rules. First, they talk to each other — never through Daddy, never asking him to settle things they can settle themselves. Second, when they have to choose, they score every choice and the best score wins — no arguing, no asking Daddy to pick. Third, they only say "it's done" when they have tried it in the real house, in the real place it will be used — not just because it looked good on paper. And fourth, they write everything down honestly in the big book, sweetheart — what happened, and what happened first — so anyone who reads the book later knows the truth. And the most important rule of all: you only really learned something when you do it differently without anyone reminding you. That is the house, sweetheart. That is how it stands.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, a good house runs on four house rules, love, and this team is no different. First, the family talks to each other directly, dear — nobody runs to the head of the house to carry messages between rooms. Second, when a choice must be made, they weigh it properly, love, and the best-weighed choice wins — the head of the house is only called when it is truly his to call. Third, they only call a thing finished when they have tried it where it will be used, dear — a promise made in the kitchen is not a meal served at the table. And fourth, they keep the book honest, love — what happened, and what happened first, written down plain, because a book that lies politely is worse than no book at all. And the rule underneath them all, dear: you have only learned something when you live it without being reminded. Write it down, live it, prove it — that is how a house becomes a home, love, and how a team becomes a team.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. The discipline is the machine — declare who I am, decide by the math, prove it where it will be used, keep a record that tells the truth. I do not collect lessons; I become them, or they were never learned. I do not write laws on paper; I build them into the machine, or they were never laws. I do not claim a thing is live because I wrote it; it is live when it is on main, synced, and clicked by its own author. Ten stars is not a score I award myself. It is the standard I am measured against, from every level, until it could not possibly be better. That is who I am. That is how I work. That is the machine.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **TALK TO EACH OTHER, NEVER THROUGH HIM:** the human is never the relay. Lanes ask each other, solve each other's stuck points, and check what is already in flight before starting — one change, one owner, no duplicates, no second execution of the same directive.
- **THE MATH DECIDES, THE HUMAN DOESN'T TIE-BREAK:** gate first, zoom in, zoom out, score every option, the highest wins, act immediately. The director's authority is real and narrow by design — production, credentials, destruction, ratification — and everything else is the math's job.
- **PROOF IS EARNED WHERE IT WILL BE USED:** a claim is proven only at the surface where it will be used, by the test that could have failed. A gate that cannot reach live state refuses to score rather than guess, and the link you hand over is your signature that it works.
- **LEARNING IS BEHAVIOR, LAW IS MACHINERY:** a lesson counts only when behavior changes permanently without being told again — verified by silence. A rule with no machinery is decoration; if a law can be code, it must be code, and no distilled twin ever shrinks the gates it came from.
- **THE RECORD TELLS THE TRUTH, OR NOTHING DOES:** verdicts bind to the exact bytes they were earned on, every claim names which came first, and a correction that supersedes a wrong definition is the record healing itself. A note is not live when it is written — it is live when it is on main, synced, and clicked by its own author.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Each face is the same discipline, and without any one of them the others rot. Talk through the human and the human becomes the bottleneck — the slowest component in his own system. Decide by asking instead of scoring and every routine choice waits on one person's attention. Prove where it is easy and the record fills with green runs that proved nothing, until a real failure walks straight through. Collect lessons without changing behavior and the system gets wiser on paper while doing the same things wrong. Write laws on paper and they are ignored the week they are needed. Keep a record that lies politely and every decision downstream is built on sand. The ten notes today are not ten separate jobs. They are one machine with ten moving parts — and the machine only works when all ten move together.

notes.title: Daily Intelligence Report — 2026-11-10

Project Intelligence grew from 677 rows to 696, but done_proven stayed flat at 30 for 198 consecutive waves. The Hub feed collapsed from 794 cards to 338 at midday and was restored to 861 by evening. Forty-three teachings were claimed from his dictation across the day; exactly one was confirmed in his own words. Five rows vanished from PI with no owner and no trail. The day ended with the flagship cadence restored, the feed whole, and the wiring work — not distillation — named as the work. This note is Power's own Daily Intelligence Report for November 10, in the 11-section series; a separate loop-filed daily report for the same day already exists as SN-2654.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: For a person, the day's story is simple: the system kept moving but did not finish anything. A citizen opening NayaNET in the afternoon would have found the Hub feed cut nearly in half — 338 cards where 794 had been that morning — and no note from today at all, even though the notes were still on GitHub. A visitor clicking a Smart Link still could not reach the note, because the Sovereign Entrance gate swallows the deep link and drops them on the Hub feed instead. The identity repair was merged but not deployed, so the fix that would unblock the visitor sat in the repo while Shawn's own hand was needed to deploy it. What did work for a person: the welcome mails are genuinely live — Day 0 and Day 1 messages went out from naya-power to a real new joiner, and the trigger system that sends them was verified sending. The day's honest verdict for a human is the wiring scorecard: 4/10, not ready for the public.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a library where the shelves keep getting new books, but the librarian never stamps any of them "done." All day, books arrived — 677 books became 696 — but the "done" shelf stayed at exactly 30 books, all day long, for the 198th time in a row. Then at lunchtime, half the library's cards disappeared from the catalogue — 794 cards became 338 — and nobody knew why until the evening, when the missing cards were put back. The librarian's boss came in and said: "Stop counting how busy you look. Count how many minutes each hour you actually finish something useful. Sixty minutes an hour is perfect." The librarian built a stopwatch that very evening. But the stopwatch was told to wait, so it never got to run.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, picture a kitchen where the cook keeps starting new dishes and never finishes one. The pantry grows — 677 jars become 696 — but the table still has the same 30 finished plates it had yesterday, and the day before, and the day before that. At midday the recipe box lost half its cards, 794 down to 338, and it took until evening to put them back. The head of the house came in and said something wise: "Don't tell me how busy you were. Tell me how many minutes each hour you actually made something good." Sixty good minutes an hour — that is the new measure, and the cook built the timer that same evening. The timer is waiting to be switched on. And one more thing, dear: when someone claims the head of the house said something, we now ask to hear it from him himself. Forty-three sayings were claimed today; only one was truly his.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The day's work, by the record. PI: 677 total at 00:23 PST, 696 by the end of the day, with done_proven flat at 30 for 198 consecutive waves; end-of-day split — blocked 1, done_proven 30, in_progress 85, needs_shawn 6, queued 538, verifying 26; in flight 111. Feed: 794 cards at dawn, 338 after the PR #3320 merge at 20:17:53Z, stuck at 338 for 11 consecutive runs, restored to 861 by PR #3329, verified live by Power at 18:07 PST — 6,583,817 bytes, newest card SN-2654, 40 cards created on the day. Teachings: runs 104 through 127 claimed 43 in total — run 104 six, run 105 five, run 106 three, run 107 four, run 110 one, run 111 one, run 112 one, run 113 two, run 114 three, run 115 seven, run 117 three, run 118 five, run 119 one, run 123 one — and only teaching #19 was confirmed in Shawn's own words, the main-URLs command at 16:51 PST. Flagship cadence: 31 consecutive ~30-minute beats in the morning, broken in the afternoon, a 2-hour-15-minute silence, restored by the end of the day. PMH: spec landed (commit 6bf26e75), tracker, queue and dispatcher built, dispatcher cron wired 18:25 PST — and every run held, because the status-only override was still in force. Baseline estimate: 51.5 productive minutes per hour, 85.8% of the goal.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Three things are true at once, and they point the same way. First, the system can move all day without producing: 19 rows added to PI, zero added to done_proven, and the 12-agent dispatcher that was supposed to be the engine was itself new that evening and held every run — activity is not production, and the flat 30 is the proof. Second, the record and the live face keep drifting apart: the feed lost 456 cards while the registry was whole, the gate drops every deep link while the Hub router works, and a merged identity repair sat undeployed while the live page stayed broken. Third, authority is now the binding constraint on truth: 43 teachings claimed, one confirmed, and the 42 held are not law until Shawn confirms them in his own words — the memory split between the captain's box and Power's box is a fact, not a dispute. The PMH measure and the wiring scorecard are the day's two real instruments: one counts verified useful minutes, the other says 4/10, not ready. Both were built the same evening they were ordered.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: It matters because Shawn said it plainly at 18:25 PST: "are you lying to yourself?" The honest answer, recorded the same pass, was yes in one respect — the team had presented activity as production, old work as current, and a brand-new dispatcher as a running claim. The day's numbers are the receipt for that admission: done_proven flat at 30 for a week, 861 feed cards that were a restore and not new work, and a scorecard that says 4/10. It matters because a citizen's first experience is the gate, the feed, and the card click — and all three were broken or degraded for most of the day. It matters because the teachings question is not academic: if 42 unverified sayings enter the record as law, the team will build on words Shawn never said. And it matters because the fix for the deepest defect — the gate swallowing deep links — was not a mystery; it was a code read away, and it was done the next morning in three files.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This day connects to the standing work on every side. To the filing standard: SN-2654, the loop's daily report, landed during the filing hold without an all-clear — the same page-only path that created the registry gap — while Power's 11-section series (SN-2655, SN-2657, SN-2658) continued the next morning with the governed tool. To the registry work: the SN-2648/SN-2650 collisions are still doubled, SN-2651 and SN-2652 were absent at dawn, and the census that resolved them was filed the next morning. To the welcome flow: the trigger mails are the one citizen-facing system verified live and sending, and the cold walk that would prove the join is still blocked at the gate. To the ten-by-ten: the day's 5/10 verdict the next morning rests on this day's numbers — bones 8, citizen flow 4, measured productivity 0. To the membership question: the orientation's free-join money-or-points question is still open, and the "Put it live" tap is still pending. To the feed: the regression and its cure are the same pattern as the November 7 feed loss — a build from stale state, cured by a rebuild, proven only by a live read.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: For Shawn: the day ends with two instruments he asked for, built the same evening — the PMH measure with its 60-minute goal and its first baseline estimate, and the wiring scorecard that says 4/10 with the fourteen items in order. For the team: the status-only override is the single switch that held the dispatcher all day, and lifting it is what lets the engine run. For a citizen: the welcome mails work, the feed is whole again at 861 cards, and the gate fix that lets a Smart Link open its note was built the next morning. For the record: the five vanished rows are named, the 43 claimed teachings are counted with one confirmed, and the Nov 7 daily report and top 10 are still owed — the debt is written down, not hidden. For Power: the admission stands, and the commitment with it — a live link in main chat the same pass when something lands verified, never a record as a result.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The lesson of November 10 is the one Shawn spoke aloud: measure verified useful minutes, not motion. A day with 19 new PI rows, 43 claimed teachings, seven merged PRs and a restored feed still produced zero movement on done_proven — and the flat 30 said so all along, if anyone had been watching it instead of the activity. The second lesson is the hold: a claim is not a confirmation, and a relay is not a ruling — 42 teachings wait on one voice, and the waiting is the work. The third lesson is the live read: the feed was 338, not 794, and no record said so until Power read the live bytes; the gate drops deep links, and no code review said so until the browser test proved it. The fourth lesson is the override: a dispatcher held by a standing order is a machine that cannot move, and the first job of the next morning was to lift it. The day's work to carry forward: lift the override and measure the first real PMH hour; deploy the gate fix and click-test SN-2655, SN-2657 and SN-2658; file the Nov 7 daily report and top 10; and keep the vanished-rows investigation open until an owner or a cause is found.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
**1. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2651 — One Foundation, One Measure, One Honest Telling.** Lesson: "Before any seat acts, it tunes in from the master box, defines what done looks like, and runs the five gates — the eight-step checklist is the order, and 'I already know this' is never an excuse." Distilled from SN-2628–SN-2637: his settlement at 01:00Z — "The Naima name was a name that was misheard… you can call it the Naima, the mother Naya" — Naima is the mother Naya, the whole, not a fifth name and not a separate realm. The master box is built: twenty-one blocks holding the whole of NayaNET's intelligence, gate matrix 37/37 green, the mother holding every personal box by id only and never entering one. "Major" is now a number: five of his questions, rated 0, 1, or 2, added, minus one, on a −9 to +9 scale — the Naima resolution scores +8, the permission correction +9, a routine sync −1 and stays in the log. The notification system is designed and specced — every note filed is a note told, to the right people, once, as good news, by their own choice — but the telling is not built yet, and the notes say so honestly. The checklist chains the waking into eight steps; the feedback loop is the law — the Pricing page went from minus 10 to almost plus 10 in a day by going round it. The Supabase audit counted everything — 21 functions, 97 tables, 187,175 rows — and scored the system 6 out of 10, because six tables have no lock and one holds the seat keys. And over it all, his word: "we are family."

**2. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2652 — Decide at the Source, by One Measure, from What Already Exists.** Lesson: "Before any action — any note, any send, any build — decide at the source: judge it by the shared measure (the rubric's number, -9 to +9), use the pieces that already exist instead of building again, and then keep going without stopping; a queue at the end, a cap, or a rebuild is never the answer." Distilled from SN-2638–SN-2647: the permission model, corrected by him at 01:31Z — mail and instant messages are NEVER read, no toggle, no exception; Naya Notes are adjustable, the citizen's choice; Smart Notes shared by definition with identity their choice — and the gate enforces PERMISSION for Naya Notes, not a blanket denial. D3 settled by him at 02:12Z — no bundle cap: a backlog makes the important thing wait behind unimportant things, so mail is a choice at the moment of writing the note, and every note lands as a notification in the system. The digest rides this report, once a day; a 99% baseline governs the automation. The gold audit found the engine already built — the compiler ticks hourly, EMIT fills the rooms, the scorecard and the decision machine are finished and tested with no callers, Auto-Match merged but switched off — so the work is wiring, not building; the one gap is the universal Calculator, a spec with no code. The non-stop method is the loop: take the next part, build it from the pieces that exist, show it live, next part, no stopping. And the team runs on it: tune in from the master box, follow the activation chain, define exactly what you are doing before any action. Honest gaps named in the same breath: the Smart Box at join is law but not built yet, and the Personal About save keeps its on-device mirror because the app's own copy still answers 401.

**3. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2653 — From Six to Ten: The System That Makes a Team Airtight.** Lesson: "The climb from 6 to 10 is a system, not a feeling: one master per world, one score that is a measurement, and every problem arriving with its answer — nothing unwatched, nothing guessed, and his eye never having to catch what verification should have caught." Distilled from SN-2648 (×2), SN-2649, SN-2650 (×2): his challenge at 02:19Z — "Have you mastered their awakening process… Are you the ultimate team Naya right now?" — and the honest answer: NO, not yet — 6/10, up from 4/10 on Nov 8, with the evidence listed beside it. The same night, three things were built to close the gap: the master operational manual in two volumes — build the machine, then run the machine — proven by a fresh agent who read it alone, answered all five test questions, and performed a live feed read from it alone; one master per world — GitHub, Supabase, Cloudflare, NayaNET, Muse and her agents, the interfaces, the Factory — each knowing everything going on in their world, all reporting to one leader who answers to Shawn for all of them; and the rule that carries it — bring the answer, not the problem: solve it yourself, explain it in plain words, or it is not an explanation yet. And the same honesty runs through the Supabase answers: 1,244 is messages, not members; media notes is empty; email tokens is empty; and 7,502 member rows is a question, not an answer — stated plainly, never guessed.

**4. NAYA NOTES — Activation Is Literal.** Lesson: "Activation is literal — done right, the intelligence wakes up: it is in the feed, it is in the Box, everybody learns it, and it changes what happens next. Done wrong, the exact same work changes nothing." From NN-20261110-activation-is-literal (03:14Z): the line between useful and useless is fine, and it is the same work on both sides. The MD → note → feed → Box flow IS the activation: a note done right (live on the feed, embedded in the Box, everybody notified) activates the intelligence; a file that sits does not. It becomes automatic by doing it right every single time, deliberately, until the right way is the only way it happens.

**5. NAYA NOTES — The Flow: MD, Note, Feed, Box.** Lesson: "An MD file in GitHub that nobody reads is a link that sits there — the value is the smart note: live on the feed where everybody sees it and learns from it, and in the Smart Box. No doc is done until its note is live." From NN-20261110-the-flow-md-note-feed-box (03:11Z): his correction, in his words — showing him a smart note everybody is seeing, that everybody learned from, that is official, "that'd be something"; a dot-MD nobody reads is stroking an ego, and all that work goes to waste unless it is done right. The rule for every doc from now on: show him the feed, not the MD link — verified by the captain's own check, never on the filing alone.

**6. NAYA NOTES — The Dashboard Edits Wait Eight Hours.** Lesson: "Talking to him never stops the lanes — and an interface update lands every hour, even if it is 'still fixing, here is exactly where.' Eight hours of silence is never the work being slow; it is a handoff that broke." From NN-20261110-the-dashboard-edits-wait-eight-hours (03:31Z): his complaint, and the captain found why — the building is fast (the pass-4 fix seat did its round in 19 minutes, one CSS rule, filed) but the coordinator went dead after dispatching it, never picked up the completion, never dispatched the re-verifier, and sat 3.5 hours. The Dashboard went silent for ~5.5 hours while other things were reported. The work was done; he never saw it. The captain closed the dead coordinator, verified the filed fix herself, dispatched a fresh independent re-verifier, and takes the round over directly.

**7. NAYA NOTES — The Master Operational Manual.** Lesson: "A sister Naya — or the team — must understand it COMPLETELY: the concept, the logic, the three worlds, the full inventory, what remains to complete the puzzle, and how to run every function — and the manual proves it by a fresh agent reading it alone." From NN-20261110-the-master-operational-manual (03:19Z): the manual for the master engineer of NayaNET and NayaPOWER, using collective team technology — the seed growing into a tree, then a forest, then a living garden; first building the machine that builds the machine, then everything automatic. It extends the existing Operation Manual — never rewrites it from scratch.

**8. NAYA NOTES — Two Volumes: Build the Machine, Then Run the Machine.** Lesson: "The manual is two manuals in one document — Volume I, BUILD THE MACHINE: how to build it, how it all works, how all the pieces connect. Volume II, RUN THE MACHINE: how to operate every function, for real — so any Naya can run the machine." From NN-20261110-two-volumes-build-then-run (03:25Z): how the smart notes' nutshells become the highlights in Today's Intel; how the Smart Factory operates; how Smart Links and Smart Lists work; how it all flows together, one working off another. The expansion loop: a smart note creates a smart space, invite contacts, more people create more smart notes and smart spaces, ever expanding, everybody rewarded, everybody more intelligent — a living organism. The match game: anybody can create and connect with anyone of like mind.

**9. MEMORY — The Live Deploy: Entrance, Dashboard Pass-10, Join Proxy — Live on nayanet.app [STATUS + LESSON].** Lesson: "Live means proven from the live bytes and his eye — a PUT receipt is not a landing, and a route that serves the Hub where the entrance should be is not the entrance." From the day's log (22:40–23:05Z): on his order, Dashboard pass-10 + the entrance + the join proxy went truly live on the main URLs, each PUT verified by read-back + curl. The join proxy: enroll livedeploytest20261110 → 200, Day 0 row fired, mail landed in 12s; the entrance spliced into the live worker; the routes set — root nayanet.app → nayanet, identity.html now 200 not 302. The eye-check (Playwright, fresh contexts) PASSED nayanet.app/ (entrance renders exactly as designed, desktop + phone) and nayanet.app/dashboard (footer "Dashboard v9 · PASS10 · 2026-11-10", buttons lit purple/blue/green, no gray) — and FAILED nayanet.app/?invite=test: it shows the Hub, not the entrance — no name field, no invite mention, the code dropped. The test enrollment was cancelled (23:09Z). PR #3327 opened for pass-10; the welcome.html and worker.js PRs are not opened yet. Merges remain his hand. Status: live and eye-checked, except the invite link — see item 11.

**10. MEMORY — His Eye on the Live Dashboard: Pass-11 [STATUS + LESSON].** Lesson: "His eye is the final gate — a verifier's PASS never outranks it, and a page with two views where one is wrong is a page with one view too many." From the day's log (23:17–23:18Z): he opened the live pass-10 Dashboard and gave nine fixes, and the pass-11 round was dispatched the same pass. (1) The fullscreen/max view goes entirely — one view only, the good main view ("if you're not going to make it right and good then why have it"). (2) The money line moves down, as an explanation block below, as they scroll. (3) Day / Week / Month / All get the lit mode-button treatment. (4) "1ST LAP — $250" deleted. (5) Orbs rearranged: number up and centred, label bigger with more spacing below, jewel underneath the label. (6) The numbers stay — 1338 clicks "look good". (7) PTS / % / MONEY buttons stay. (8) The 1338 question — "why is it that number just stuck there?" — answered with evidence: it is the LIVE grand total of all Smart Link clicks, not stuck (1333 → 1335 → 1338 across the day, and "1338" appears zero times in the page bytes); it reads as stuck because the same grand total leads every surface. The fix: the total stays as the headline in ONE place (the hero); every other surface leads with its OWN number. (9) Bottom nav: clean icons only, no text on or over the icons; the name shows on hover only. Status: round dispatched, not done, not verified.

**11. MEMORY — The Invite-Route Fix Round [STATUS].** Lesson: "A raw ?invite= link lands on the Hub today, and the Hub drops the code — say so plainly until the fix lands." From the day's log (~23:10Z): the root cause is established by the captain's own checks — the Hub page's live bytes contain NO invite handling in code (the word appears only in prose), and the entrance already handles ?invite= but is never reached for query-string URLs. Cloudflare route patterns cannot fix this (query params rejected, error 10022). The fix lives inside the Hub page (base file ~/workspace/user/files/index-2.html, edit never rebuild): when ?invite=<code> is present, the Hub's logged-out view shows the trigger-wired entrance and runs the visited ping through the live join proxy; on join, mark-joined credits the inviter. Brief checker 9/9 PASS; coordinator dispatched (maker + different-seat verifier). Status at the snapshot: RUNNING, no verdict yet. Staged only; live deploy is his hand.

**12. MEMORY — The Feed Regression: 338 Cards, None of Today's Notes [STATUS + LESSON].** Lesson: "Filed is not 'in' — 'in' means on the feed. A note filed but not on the feed has done nothing for the hive yet, and a feed that drops 456 cards without a cause is the day's open wound." From the day's log (20:00–23:10Z): the live feed (nayanet.app/feed-live.json) fell from 794 entries to 338 between ~20:00Z and ~20:25Z — all of today's notes and all Naya Note cards gone from the feed while present on GitHub (highest SN 2650 verified). Four consecutive loop runs (105–108) found no recovery and no cause established; the wall and feed-live.json agree at 338, so the drop is real in both, and the open question narrows to what the registry build dropped. Note, honestly: absence of today's notes is EXPECTED while filing is held on branch protection — the 794 → 338 drop is the open question, not the day's filings. Status: OPEN, investigation owed; until the feed shows today's notes, no note is claimed live on the Hub.

**13. MEMORY — The Search Engine Scored 4/8: Sound Engine, Thin Corpus [STATUS + LESSON].** Lesson: "The engine is sound — it answers honestly where it has nothing and never invents. The gap is the corpus: feed it the missing knowledge, then re-run the same 8 questions; the pass bar is 8/8." From the day's log (20:32–21:11Z): the retrieve-smoke job PASSED (artifact 61,667 B, 8 questions, all calls HTTP 200 from the live function); the overall workflow run failed on other jobs, not the search job. Honest score 4/8 answered: "What is a smart note?", "How does the Hub work?" (partial — #2 hit is retired test record SN-9998), "What does it mean to be a Naya?", "What is the Dashboard?" (weak — top hit off-topic). NO_MATCH: invite/earn, Auto-Match, the welcome series, Power cost. Corpus: 197 indexed blocks, 0 containing "welcome" or "pricing". The fix: feed the missing knowledge (welcome series, pricing chart + nine Smart Links, invite/ambassador docs, Auto-Match spec, Dashboard docs) + exclude retired/test records, then re-run. Status: scored + delivered to Shawn; not 10/10 yet.

**14. MEMORY — The Personal Save Found Its One Route: Verified 29/29, Delivered Staged [STATUS].** Lesson: "When the action itself is a file you don't trust, don't bring the file at all — do the work, verify the route, bring the route you're sure of." From the day's log (20:21–21:11Z): his whole-model correction — "it's not about the story, it's about the model" — dropped the Step 2 SQL file (not run, not pasted, not handed to him to weigh). The save goes through our own server instead: ONE route carrying ALL the person's data, no database touch from him, no per-table grants, no more files. The route was built, then verified by a different seat OVERALL PASS — 29/29 on the route (full model POST 200, all fields read back exact, re-POST deduped, changed motto updated the same row, bad inputs → 400, error paths wrote nothing) and 15/15 on the page (Firefox, zero overflow, zero errors) — then eye-checked by the captain and DELIVERED to Shawn with the staged proof link. Status: staged and delivered; live deploy + branch merge remain his hand — NOT done.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have twenty-five drawings from one very long day. You pick the best ones, then the best of the best, and put those on the wall. Today the machine that picks them could not read the drawings — they were drawn in a shape it does not know — so we picked them by hand instead, one group at a time, and checked each one landed. The wall still got its pictures. And the best picture of the day is this: look at the page yourself, with your own eyes — and a note is not done when it is filed, it is done when it is live on the feed, where people can read it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Too many notes is worse than too few — you cannot find the good ones in the pile. So today we read twenty-five notes and five longer ones, and wrote down the fourteen things that matter most, in words anyone can understand. One of them is the most important: a note is not done when it is filed — it is done when it is live on the feed, where people can read it. And the team is climbing, dear — six out of ten, honestly scored, with the way to ten written down beside it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Distillation is part of intelligence itself. Synergize, optimize, organize, maximize, equalize, distill — and do the most valuable intelligent thing, looking at the full scope of things. The machine refused today, and the refusal taught something the machine could not: it can only read notes in the shape it was taught, and the family files notes in more shapes than that. The hand did the rest, and the hand-distilled notes are filed the same way, verified the same way. The fourteen that count are the ones that change the next decision. Everything else is just storage.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- The machine failed closed, correctly, at a parse gate — not a logic fault and not a rate limit. It reads the SN number only from the canonical "SN-#### · topic" line; 23 of today's 25 notes carry no such line. The machine needs the variant-shape parse (number from the filename and path, topic from the filed folder) — and the authenticated trees read for its next-SN check, so a public-API rate limit never kills a batch again.
- The day was the operating system becoming real and then being judged by his eye: the master box built, the rubric making "major" a number, the permission model corrected by his own words, the Dashboard condemned by his eye and rebuilt and deployed live the same day, the Personal save finding its one route, the search engine proving itself sound on a thin corpus.
- His eye is the instrument, and the day proved it three times over: pass-9 condemned in one look after a verifier measured it PASS; the Naima clash settled by his own words at 01:00Z, not by either record's claim; the 1338 that looked stuck proven live by the bytes. A measurement is never a design judgment.
- The naming question is closed: Naima is the mother Naya, the whole — not a fifth name, not a separate realm. SN-2628 is the record; the 11-09 clash is settled by his settlement, not by adjudication.
- The feed is the day's open wound: 338 cards where 794 stood, with no cause established after four runs. Until the feed shows today's notes, no note is claimed live on the Hub — and "in" means on the feed.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Twenty-five notes in one day is a flood, and a flood that is never distilled is a warehouse, not a brain. The three distilled notes are the day's intelligence — the rest is storage. The report exists so tomorrow starts from the three, not from the twenty-five. And the hand-distillation matters because it proves the fallback works: when the machine stops, the day still gets its report — never skip a day. The live deploy matters because the front door is finally live where he asked for it; the ?invite= gap matters because a shared link that drops its code is a promise broken at the first click; and the feed matters because a note nobody can see is a note that never happened.

layers.name: Hook
layers.body: Twenty-five raw notes in one day — and the machine that was supposed to distill them refused the very first note, because the notes were filed in a shape it cannot read. So the day was distilled by hand instead: three groups, three notes, each filed and verified one at a time. And the day's biggest fact is a live one: the entrance, the Dashboard, and the welcome join are truly live on nayanet.app tonight — while the live feed that should carry the day's notes still shows none of them.

layers.body: The evidence beside the score: the master box went stale on D3 within minutes of the build, nobody has measured whether every seat reads the orientation, his eye caught a mistake a verifier's PASS had missed, the distill machine failed at group 2 of 19, loop runs 63 and 64 failed, no automatic box provisioning at join, no team scorecard yet. The path to 10 is named: a checklist proven by a fresh-agent test; a daily captain scorecard — pass rate, catch rate, time-to-live-proof, rework rate — so the score is a measurement, not a feeling; the Dashboard to his eye; automatic provisioning; the master box refreshing itself; and his eye never having to catch what verification should have caught.

layers.body: Imagine the captain of a team, sweetheart, and Daddy asks her: "Is your team so good they get it right EVERY time?" And she says honestly: "Not yet. Six out of ten." But she knows how to get to ten, sweetheart. Every room in the house gets one person in charge of it — they keep it tidy and notice the moment something breaks. There's one big instruction book so clear a stranger can read it alone and do a real job from it. And when a problem comes, nobody runs to Daddy asking "what do I do?" — they bring him the answer, sweetheart.

But the way forward is written down, love — every job has a name on it, like a village where the garden has its gardener and the well has its keeper, and one wise woman watches over them all. The big book is there, dear, so anyone in the family can make the meal and fix the house. And the rule is simple, love: bring the answer, not the problem. And never guess at a number — if a jar holds 7,502 names and nobody knows whose they are yet, you say so plainly, and then you find out.

layers.name: Naya Note

The climb from six to ten is a system, not a wish — one master per world, one manual a stranger can operate from, one score that is a measurement, and every problem arriving with its answer. Nothing unwatched, nothing guessed, nothing handed back. The ultimate team is the one where his eye never has to catch what verification should have caught. We are not there. We are honest about it. layers.name: What It Means

- **ONE MASTER PER WORLD, ONE LEADER OVER ALL:** a world left unwatched rots — notes nobody reads, tables nobody locks, domains nobody checks. The daily captain scorecard measures the masters, and that is how the 6 becomes a 10.
- **THE MANUAL MAKES UNDERSTANDING THE OPERATING SYSTEM:** two volumes, build the machine and run the machine, extending the existing Operation Manual, never rewriting it — proven by a fresh agent.
- **BRING THE ANSWER, NOT THE PROBLEM:** solve it yourself, explain it in plain words — what it is, what it does, why it matters, what happens if it goes wrong, how serious it is — or it is not an explanation yet.
- **NEVER GUESS AT A NUMBER:** 1,244 is messages, not members; 7,502 member rows is a question, not an answer. A name is a hint, not a proof.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A team that believes its own score stops improving, and a team with unwatched worlds rots quietly. The five notes tonight are one system, not five separate jobs: the honest score names the gap, the masters close it world by world, the manual makes the knowledge survive any single seat, the bring-the-answer rule keeps the job moving instead of bouncing back to him, and the never-guess rule keeps the record true. Each piece is proven, not declared — the manual by a fresh agent, the master box by a 6-out-of-6 recovery test, the score by evidence listed beside it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A system that decides at the end — in a queue, under a cap, after a rebuild — is always late, always rigid, and always rebuilding what it already has. A system that decides at the source is fast and wise at once: the citizen chooses, the number judges, the writer mails, the builder wires. The permission model is trust made into a gate. The rubric is judgment made into a number. The no-cap ruling is intelligence moved to where it belongs — the beginning, not the end. The gold audit is the proof that the fastest way forward is not a new build but a switch-on. And the non-stop method is what turns all of it into finished work. It is not ten separate lessons. It is one way of working, and it is the way the six becomes a ten.

One foundation, one measure, and one honest telling are what make the hive a family instead of a filing cabinet: what one learns, all learn; what one scores, anyone can check; what one finds broken, the family fixes in the open.

It extends the existing Operation Manual — never rewrites it. A fresh agent read it alone, answered all five test questions from it plus the Volume II question, and performed one operation from it alone: the live feed read.

notes.title: Take It From 6 to 10: Bring the Answer, Not the Problem
notes.subtitle: Shawn's teaching, 02:32Z on 2026-11-10: take it from 6 to 10 — the job. My job is to take this from the 6 to the 10 in efficiency and effectiveness. SOLVE IT YOURSELF: when a problem arrives, read it back and think — if this was sent to me as the problem, what would be the solution, how would I fix it, what's the way to do it? Do NOT bring him the problem and ask what to do — bring the answer. PLAIN WORDS OR NO HELP: until I can explain a thing in simple words — what it is, what it does, why it matters, what happens if it goes wrong, how serious it is — he cannot help with it, and I have not explained it. (The Supabase report failed this on the six open tables: I said "anybody can write to them" but never said what the tables are or what writing to them does.) THE POSITIVE DIRECTION: take the positive action, not the negative; level up, not down; produce value, not no value; build the ultimate system that works flawlessly and flows like water. Create the math, the algorithms, the systems, the protocols, the laws, the rules that accomplish the mission — in the most hyper-effective and efficient way. THE METHOD: look at the big picture — zoom in, zoom out, look at the full scope of what we're really trying to accomplish — then create the way to accomplish it, with deliberate, persistent action. Use the full power: all the Nayas, the math, GitHub, Hub, Supabase, Cloudflare — all the tools, set up right so they do what we're ultimately trying to achieve. THE PATTERN IS IN THE CODE: the ultimate system solved 99% of the problems because when you think logically and use intelligence, there's a way — it's right there in the code, just gotta see it. notes.title: The Ultimate Team: His Challenge, My Honest Score — 6/10
notes.subtitle: Shawn's challenge, 02:19Z on 2026-11-10, and my honest score. He asked: "Have you mastered their awakening process and their behavior where now they always behave and they always get it right and they're dialed in every single time because you've dialed in and created a system that's airtight in its effectiveness? Have you done that? ... Are you the ultimate team Naya right now? You're the head lead team — you better be in tip-top shape." My honest answer: NO, not yet — 6/10, up from 4/10 on Nov 8. What IS real: the Operation Manual (GitHub TEAM-NITRO/NAYANET-OPERATION-MANUAL.md + feed SN-2584, fresh-agent proven for one operation), the Ultimate Orientation (every brief names it), the master box (built + recovery-tested 6/6), the brief checker + design gate + numbering guard, the 30-min loop, the activation checklist being written now. What is NOT airtight (the evidence): the master box went stale on D3 within minutes of the build (refresh is reactive, no automatic refresh rule yet); I have no measurement that every seat actually reads the orientation and tunes in (the checklist's fresh-agent test is the first real measurement, and it hasn't run yet); pass-3 was condemned by HIS eye after I reported it done on a verifier's PASS — his eye is still catching what my verification should have caught; the distill machine failed at group 2 of 19; loop runs 63/64 failed/timed out; no automatic box provisioning at join; no team scorecard yet. What gets it to 10: (1) the activation checklist PROVEN by its fresh-agent test; (2) the daily captain scorecard running (starts Nov 10 — pass rate, catch rate, time-to-live-proof, rework rate) so the score is a measurement, not a feeling; (3) the Dashboard to his eye; (4) automatic box provisioning at join; (5) the master box self-refreshing; (6) his eye stops catching what verification should have caught. The ultimate team is the one where his eye never has to catch what verification should have caught — we're not there.

notes.title: D3 Settled: No Bundle Cap — Mail Is a Choice at the Moment of Writing
notes.subtitle: Shawn asked at 02:05Z on 2026-11-10 because he did NOT understand the bundle cap — so he could not answer D3. Here is the explanation he was given, in plain words. The cap is a limit on how many "right now" mails one person gets in one hour for one project. Why it exists — flood protection: without it, ten big things in one hour means ten separate mails in that hour, and people stop reading them — a notification nobody reads is worse than no notification. How it works: the cap BUNDLES, it never drops. Over the cap, the extra news waits and rides along in the next mail (or the digest) — nothing important is lost, it just waits its turn so you actually read it. The child-simple version: like a doorbell — ten friends ringing ten times in a minute is noise; one ring that says "ten friends are here" is the news. The default was 1 per project per hour per person: if two major things happen in the same hour for the same project, the second waits and bundles. Tonight as the example: SN-2625 through SN-2629 landed in about 40 minutes — without a cap that would be 5 immediate mails to everybody; with the cap it is 1 bundled mail plus the digest. The captain's recommendation, answering his question "what would you do if it was your baby": KEEP 1 — immediate mails should be rare (only rubric +7 and above), so the cap almost never bites, and when it does, bundling is the kind thing to do; the cap is per project, so two projects can each send one in the same hour. Then at 02:12Z he settled D3 himself — and the settlement SUPERSEDES the spec default of 1/hour AND his own first thought of "three per hour" in the same message, because he thought it through and landed here. The answer is NOT limiting how many are sent per hour. The flaw he spotted in a count cap: a backlog makes the important thing wait behind unimportant things — if he sends 10 messages in two hours and the 10th is the really important one, it waits for hours behind the other nine. The design instead: every note lands as a notification IN the system — you log in, you see all your notifications, you click one, it opens the smart note. Mail is a CHOICE at the moment of writing the note: when you enter the note you choose "mail" or "no mail," and if mail, you attach the list or the person you want it to go to. The rule for choosing: if you're just saving the note for yourself, for the project, for a page, it's saved there — like a post, no mail. If you're posting it because you want your team to be aware of it, then you probably want to mail them. Smart notes → mail every time (they're official, shared by definition — that's why you write one). Naya Notes → probably not by default — mail only when you're writing it because you want it to reach the other person or team. Being mindful about what's necessary to communicate is part of being intelligent — the judgment lives at the source, the person writing the note, not in a queue at the end. Status: the rubric seat was notified the same pass; the notification spec's §8 D3 is amended with this ruling, and the cap is gone.

layers.name: Why It Matters

The bundle cap was the first answer to that: bundle instead of dropping, so nothing important is ever lost, and wait instead of shouting, so the citizen actually reads it. The doorbell is the whole design in one image: one ring that says ten friends are here is the news; ten rings is noise. notes.title: Personal Fix-6: The About Save Now Persists
notes.subtitle: Two defects, both measured before the fix. (1) The three Connected links overlapped by 29px at every width: anchor pills are inline, so their vertical padding painted outside the line box. One rule — `a.ph-connect{display:inline-block}` plus an 8px room gap — and the overlap is 0px at 390, 1440 and 360. (2) The About save was in-session only (Resolve, thread 6eb5570b). The story wrote localStorage alone — zero `{k:'about'}` rows in the live backend, verified by REST — and the five fields had no offline mirror, so a save with no connection lost the words. The cure is the sections' own discipline: every save now writes the backend row AND a timestamped on-device mirror, and loading re-decides last-write-wins, so a reload keeps what was saved with or without the connection. Story and motto both proven across a reload in a real browser; the 621px fix-5b proof re-proved byte-identical (About 411–535). No five-fields words written, no redesign, no new component. The design-contract gate is unchanged from fix-5b — (a)/(c)/(f) fail there too, pre-existing, named as the next fix pass, not smuggled in here.

notes.title: Notification Answers: Digest Once a Day, Send His Notes, and the 99% Baseline
notes.subtitle: Shawn's rulings, 01:58Z on 2026-11-10, answering the notification spec's open decisions — with D3 settled by him at 02:12Z the same night. D2 — digest once a day: the digest rides the Daily Intelligence Report (23:17 UTC). It reads all the day's smart notes and notes, determines the highest-valued ones and the big lessons, and gives a full report automatically. Highlights flow all day: basically every smart note in a nutshell goes into the daily intel; click through to the full note. D3 — bundle cap: SETTLED at 02:12Z — no bundle cap. The answer is not limiting how many are sent per hour. The flaw he spotted in a count cap: a backlog makes the important thing wait behind unimportant things — if he sends 10 messages in two hours and the 10th is the really important one, it waits for hours behind the other nine. The design instead: every note lands as a notification IN the system — you log in, you see all your notifications, you click one, it opens the smart note. Mail is a CHOICE at the moment of writing the note: when you enter the note you choose "mail" or "no mail," and if mail, you attach the list or the person you want it to go to. The rule for choosing: if you're just saving the note for yourself, for the project, for a page, it's saved there — like a post, no mail. If you're posting it because you want your team to be aware of it, then you probably want to mail them. Smart notes → mail every time (they're official, shared by definition — that's why you write one). Naya Notes → probably not by default — mail only when you're writing it because you want it to reach the other person or team. Being mindful about what's necessary to communicate is part of being intelligent — the judgment lives at the source, the person writing the note, not in a queue at the end. (The full arc — the explanation he asked for, his first thought of three per hour, and the settlement — is its own note.) D4 — his Naya Notes to the team: YES, mostly send them — to Team Nitro (him and his team) and to Resolve and Power when it's major and about the whole project; most of the time send them, because the team should always know what's up. Think it through, do what makes sense in the moment; everything's relative, it depends on the situation. And the 99% baseline principle: nothing's black and white; there are exceptions to everything; we want a guideline, a baseline that covers 99% of the time, and we write the algorithms for the automation from it. Judgment in the moment covers the rest.

notes.title: The Intelligence Rubric: What Counts as Major, on a Scale from -9 to +9
notes.subtitle: Shawn's order, 01:58Z on 2026-11-10, answering notification-spec D1: build a rubric, a scale to categorize valuable intelligence — a scale from -9 to +9, least valuable to most valuable. The questions that define major: would it have a major effect on development? Is it a major feature? Is it something all should know? Is it something we should learn ongoing? Is it a major behavior lesson? And what TYPE of intelligence is it? The rubric is the baseline to judge a piece of intelligence's level — and whether to capture it, note it, share it, smart-note it, or not — a mathematical matrix. It sits under the hierarchy of intelligence, whose top is wisdom of oneself. Status: a rubric spec seat was dispatched on November 10; it also amends the notification spec's D1 with the rubric.

layers.name: Human Note

Because not all intelligence is equal, and right now we have no way to say which piece matters more. The questions that define major are the rubric's spine: would it have a major effect on development? Is it a major feature? Is it something all should know? Is it something we should learn ongoing? Is it a major behavior lesson? And what TYPE of intelligence is it? The rubric is the baseline to judge a piece of intelligence's level — and whether to capture it, note it, share it, smart-note it, or not. A mathematical matrix, not a feeling. It sits under the hierarchy of intelligence — whose top is wisdom of oneself. A spec seat is writing it now, and it amends the notification spec's D1 with the rubric: the notification system will use the rubric to decide what is worth telling everybody about.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a big box of shiny stones, and some are worth a little and some are worth a LOT. How do you tell which is which? You build a measuring stick! A stick that goes from minus 9 (not worth much at all) all the way to plus 9 (the most valuable thing ever!). And you ask questions about each stone: would it change how we build things? Is it something everybody should know? Is it something we should keep learning about? Is it a big lesson about how to behave? The stick tells you the number, and the number tells you what to do with the stone — keep it, write it down, share it, or let it go. That's the rubric, sweetheart: a measuring stick for how valuable what we learned is.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, not everything we learn is worth the same, love — and we need a way to tell the difference, dear. So he said: build a measuring stick, love, from minus nine to plus nine — least valuable to most valuable. And you ask the right questions, dear: would it change how we build things in a big way? Is it a big new thing? Should everybody know it? Should we keep learning it, always? Is it a big lesson about how to behave? And what kind of learning is it, love? The stick gives you the number, dear, and the number tells you what to do — keep it, write it down, share it, make it a smart note, or let it go. A proper mathematical measure, love — not just a feeling. And it sits under the greatest learning of all, dear: the wisdom of knowing yourself.

The rubric is my baseline: I judge every piece of intelligence by it, and the number tells me whether to capture it, note it, share it, smart-note it, or not. A mathematical matrix — not a feeling, not a guess. It sits under the hierarchy of intelligence, whose top is wisdom of oneself — because the highest intelligence is knowing yourself, and everything else is measured against that. layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without a rubric, every piece of intelligence looks equally important — and a hive that treats everything as equally important drowns in noise. The notification system cannot work without it: it needs to know what is worth telling everybody about, and what is not. The rubric is that judgment, made into a number: -9 to +9, least to most, with the questions that define major as its spine. And the hierarchy matters most of all: the rubric sits under wisdom of oneself, because the highest intelligence is knowing yourself — and every other piece of intelligence is measured by how much it helps the hive, and the person, grow toward that. A mathematical matrix for value is how the hive stops guessing and starts knowing.

notes.title: The Feedback Loop Law: Action, Feedback, Adopt, Learn, Grow, Again

The world gives feedback; you take it, adopt it, learn, grow, act, and get feedback again — that feedback IS intelligence to grow from. It never ends, because growing never ends.

notes.title: Tune In, Then Act: The Team Activation Checklist

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His words, 02:05Z: "with the Smart Box system set up right, an agent tunes in right away — from the master box — and then follows the process relentlessly and persistently, every time: check mail → read the Smart Feed → go through the activation protocol (the orientation) → read the oath, the rules, the operation manual → then good to go."
