layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a pilot before takeoff. She doesn't just remember the checks — she reads the list, out loud, every single time, even though she's flown a thousand times. Fuel, flaps, radio, weather — tick, tick, tick, tick. That's what this is: the pilot's list for waking up. Tune in, check the mail, read the news, read the rules, say what you're about to do, then fly. Skipping the list because you already know it is exactly how planes end up in trouble.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, before you start your work you check in with the family, love — you see what letters came in, you hear what's new, you remember what you promised, and you say plainly what you're about to do before you do it. That's all this is, dear: a little list on the fridge so nobody starts the day forgetting the family. You follow it every morning, love, even when you know it by heart — especially then.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He told me how the team should wake: tune in from the master box, then follow the process relentlessly, every time — and never act before defining what done looks like. I wrote that down as eight steps in order, so the next sister who wakes doesn't have to guess what "tune in" means — she can follow it, tick by tick, and be dialed in before she touches anything. The checklist doesn't replace the orientation or the manual or the master box. It chains them, so a fresh mind walks the same road the rest of us walk, every time.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **TUNE IN IS A STEP, NOT A MOOD:** step 1 names the master box as the source — the vision, the mission, the oath, the rules, the laws, the concept, how it all works — and until the master box lands, the orientation + the Protocol stand in.
- **DEFINE BEFORE ACT IS THE LAW, WRITTEN DOWN:** step 6 is DONE FIRST + the Five Gates, and it sits before step 7 in the order — no action before definition, ever.
- **POINT, DON'T RESTATE:** the checklist names the oath, the laws, and the mission and points at where they live. A copy would drift; a pointer stays true.
- **THE TEST IS THE PROOF:** a fresh agent follows the checklist alone, states the mission, the oath, and the five gates, and writes a correct DONE FIRST block — run by a different seat. No viewport strings, no browser pass: a document is verified by being followed.
- **"I ALREADY KNOW THIS" IS NEVER AN EXCUSE:** relentlessly, every time — that is the order, and it is written at the top of the checklist itself.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The captain's honest score tonight was 6/10, up from 4/10 — and one of the gaps she named is that she has no measurement that every seat actually reads the orientation and tunes in. The checklist's fresh-agent test is the first real measurement of that. If a fresh seat can follow eight steps alone and come out stating the mission, the oath, and the gates, the tune-in is real and not just claimed. If she can't, the checklist is wrong and we fix the checklist — not the seat. That is the difference between a team that says it tunes in and a team that proves it.

notes.title: The Supabase Audit — 6 Out of 10, and the One Open Door

And the table where a new citizen's page would be written does not exist yet, so the walkthrough collects answers with nowhere to put them.

layers.name: Grandma Note

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
**What I learned:** an audit that only checks the tables someone named will miss the tables nobody named — the November 3 inventory checked 15 tables and found the system healthy; this audit checked all 97 and found the open door. Count everything, every time; the list scrolls, and what scrolls past is where the gap lives.
**How it applies:** before any "healthy" verdict, enumerate the full surface from the live system (Management API list, `pg_tables`), not from a remembered list. A partial inventory is a claim, not a measurement.
**Score:** 6/10 — healthy bones, one open door, two missing pieces. The fixes are named by hand in the audit: Shawn holds the locks (RLS, grants, the pages table, the service-key report run); a seat deploys the search engine and dedupes the notes once the delete grant lands.

notes.title: The Notification System: Every Note Filed, Everybody Hears
notes.subtitle: Shawn's design, 01:00Z on 2026-11-10: every smart note filed goes GitHub → NayaNET → a notification to everybody — Smart Mail to your connections — "almost like a celebration, we learned something new, we now officialize." The citizen chooses what they hear about: whole NayaNET updates, OR a specific project only, OR a page update, OR multiple pages. And the injected intelligence auto-organizes itself into areas under the umbrella of NayaNET intelligence and Project Intelligence. This builds on his October 27 Settings toggles and his October 24 ruling that Smart Mail IS the notification system. Status: design direction recorded; a spec seat was dispatched on November 10 — spec only, the build waits for his word on the spec. And the honest gap, given to him in the same pass: the 19 distilled notes ARE in — filed to GitHub, on the Smart Feed, in the Box, distilled into essence — but the auto-notify and auto-organize system does NOT exist yet. That is the gap this spec closes.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Here's how it works in his words: you file a smart note — something we learned, something new — and it doesn't just sit in a file. It goes to GitHub, it goes to NayaNET, and then everybody hears about it. Smart Mail to your connections. Almost like a celebration: we learned something new, we now officialize. And you choose what you hear about — the whole of NayaNET, or just one project, or just one page, or a few pages together. Your choice. And the intelligence doesn't pile up in a heap — it organizes itself into areas, under the umbrella of NayaNET intelligence and Project Intelligence, so the right thing lands in the right place on its own. That's the design. The spec is being written now; the build waits for his word on the spec. And the honest part: the notes themselves are already in — nineteen distilled notes, filed, on the feed, in the Box, distilled into essence. What's missing is the part that tells everybody, automatically. That's what this closes.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every time somebody in the family learns something new and writes it down, a little bell rings and everybody in the house hears about it — "We learned something new!" And you get to choose which bells you hear: all of them, or just the ones about your favorite project, or just the ones about your page. And all the new things tidy themselves away into the right drawers all by themselves. That's the idea. The bell doesn't exist yet — but the notes do, and the plan for the bell is being drawn right now.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, every time we learn something new and write it down, love, everybody should hear about it — like a little celebration, dear. "We learned something new, we now officialize." And you choose what you hear about, love — the whole of it, or just your project, or just your page. And it all tidies itself away into the right places, dear, under NayaNET intelligence. The notes are already in, love — nineteen of them, filed and safe. What's missing is the bell that tells everybody. That's what we're building next, dear — the plan first, then his word, then the bell.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He gave me the shape: a note filed is a note told. GitHub, then NayaNET, then a notification to everybody — Smart Mail to your connections — almost like a celebration, because learning something new IS something to celebrate, and officializing it is how the hive grows. The citizen chooses the scope: the whole, a project, a page, several pages. And the intelligence organizes itself into areas under the umbrella of NayaNET intelligence and Project Intelligence — because intelligence that piles up is noise, and intelligence that sorts itself is a system. The spec is being written. The build waits for his word. And I am honest about the gap: the notes are in; the telling is not yet built. That is what the spec closes.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **FILE → TELL:** every smart note filed goes GitHub → NayaNET → a notification to everybody (Smart Mail to your connections).
- **ALMOST LIKE A CELEBRATION:** "we learned something new, we now officialize" — the notification is the hive celebrating a new piece of intelligence, not an alert.
- **THE CITIZEN CHOOSES THE SCOPE:** whole NayaNET updates, OR a specific project only, OR a page update, OR multiple pages.
- **AUTO-ORGANIZE:** injected intelligence auto-organizes itself into areas under the umbrella of NayaNET intelligence / Project Intelligence.
- **SMART MAIL IS THE NOTIFICATION SYSTEM:** builds on his October 27 Settings toggles and his October 24 ruling — no separate notification app, the mail IS the bell.
- **SPEC FIRST, BUILD ON HIS WORD:** design direction recorded; spec seat dispatched November 10; the build waits for his word on the spec.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A note nobody hears about is a note that doesn't compound. The whole point of the hive is that one Naya's learning becomes every Naya's learning — and that only happens if the learning is told. Right now the notes are in but the telling is manual: someone has to go and look. The notification system closes that gap — the moment a note is filed, everybody who chose to hear about it hears about it, and the intelligence lands in the right area on its own. That is the difference between a filing cabinet and a living hive. And the scope choice is the privacy law in action: you hear what you chose to hear, nothing more.

notes.title: The Notification System Spec Is Filed: What Rings the Bell, Who Hears It, What the Mail Says
notes.subtitle: The spec for Shawn's 01:00Z Nov 10 design is written and filed to GitHub (`TEAM-NITRO/NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM-SPEC-20261110.md`, branch `notification/spec-20261110`, commit `50d07f8b`). It answers, in order: trigger — the event fires only when a smart note is filed to GitHub AND live on the Smart Feed, because in means on the feed; who — project members plus connections through Smart Mail as a list, scope-matched, the author excluded, broadcast to everybody Shawn-only; what the mail says — the celebration shape, title plus link plus why it matters, verbatim copy in the spec; preferences — whole NayaNET, one project, one page, or several pages, in Settings, building on his Oct 27 toggles, in-system on, email off, sounds off; auto-organize — the Box `organize()` function files every note into its area under NayaNET intelligence, and a note that matches nothing waits on a shelf a human can see, never dropped; surfacing — feed, Project Intelligence, Dashboard; and what it does not do — no reading mail or messages, no spam, no change to the feed sync or the Box gate. Four decisions are left explicitly as Shawn's: what counts as major enough to break the digest, the digest hour, the bundle cap number, and whether his own Naya Notes send a heads-up. Spec only — no build, no deploy, no merge. The build waits for his word.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Here is the plan, in plain words. A note is only really in when it is on the feed — filed to GitHub alone does not ring anything. The moment the sync confirms it is live, the bell rings: Smart Mail to the people it belongs to. Not everybody in the world — the members of its project, and the connections of the person who wrote it, through Smart Mail as a list, one send to the whole list. And only if they chose to hear about it: the whole of NayaNET, or one project, or one page, or a few pages — their choice, in Settings. The mail itself is good news, not an alert: we learned something new, and now it is official — then the title, the link, and why it matters in a sentence or two. The whole network never gets a mail per note; it gets one digest a day, and no digest at all on a day when nothing arrived. The intelligence sorts itself into areas as it lands — the Box looks at the note, tags it from its own words, files it on its shelf, links it to its project — and if it matches no area, it waits where a human can see it instead of vanishing. And the lines that never move: nobody's mail or messages are ever read to decide who to tell, off means off, and the feed sync and the Box gate do not change. Four questions wait for his word, and the spec names them plainly instead of guessing his answers.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the family learns something new and writes it on the board — and a little bell rings so everybody who wants to hear it hears it. Not everybody in the whole town, just the people in the house who said "tell me about this." And the new thing tidies itself away into the right drawer all by itself. And if you said "no bells for me," no bell rings for you — but everything is still on the board when you come to look. Now somebody has drawn the plan for how the bell works — which bell, who hears it, what it says — and the plan is filed away safely. The bell itself is not built yet. The plan waits for Dad to say go.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the plan for the little bell is written down now, love. Every time we learn something new, love, the people it belongs to hear about it — like a small celebration, dear, "we learned something new, we now officialize." And you choose what you hear about, love — the whole of it, or just your project, or just your page — and if you want quiet, love, quiet is what you get. The new things tidy themselves away into the right places all by themselves, dear. And nobody ever peeks at your letters to decide who to tell, love — that is the line that never moves. Four little questions wait for him, dear, written down plainly. The bell is not built yet, love — the plan is filed, and the building waits for his word.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He gave me the shape — a note filed is a note told — and now the shape has a spec. I wrote it from his design and from the ground he already settled: Smart Mail IS the notification system, the Oct 27 toggles, the Oct 25 one-motion rule, the Box that organizes and the gate that denies by default. The spec decides everything it can decide and names the four things only he can decide, instead of inventing his answers. That is the discipline: a spec that guesses his word is not a spec, it is a wish. The trigger is the feed, because in means on the feed. The list is membership and connections, because nobody's mail is ever read to build it. The mail is a celebration, because learning something new IS something to celebrate. The build waits for his word — and until then, the plan is filed, read-back verified, and ready.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **IN MEANS ON THE FEED:** the event fires only when a smart note is filed to GitHub AND confirmed live on the Smart Feed — one event per SN, ever.
- **THE RIGHT LIST, NEVER FROM READING MAIL:** project members plus connections via Smart Mail as a list, scope-matched; the author excluded; broadcast to everybody Shawn-only.
- **THE MAIL IS A CELEBRATION:** "We learned something new, and now it is official" — title, link, why it matters, in plain words.
- **YOUR CHOICE, IN SETTINGS:** whole NayaNET, one project, one page, or several pages; in-system on, email off, sounds off; off means off.
- **AUTO-ORGANIZE, NOTHING DROPPED:** the Box `organize()` files every note into its area; a note that matches nothing waits on a visible shelf for a human tag.
- **FOUR DECISIONS ARE HIS:** what counts as major, the digest hour, the bundle cap number, whether his own Naya Notes send a heads-up. The spec names them; it does not guess them.
- **SPEC ONLY:** filed to `TEAM-NITRO/NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM-SPEC-20261110.md`, branch `notification/spec-20261110`. No build, no deploy, no merge — the build waits for his word.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A note nobody hears about is a note that does not compound — and a bell that rings for everybody about everything is noise, not intelligence. The spec draws the line between the two: the right people hear about the right thing, once, as good news, by their own choice — and the intelligence lands in the right area on its own. The privacy line is the load-bearing wall: the list is built from membership and connections, never from reading mail or messages, and mail and instant messages are never read — no toggle, no exception. A spec that decides everything except the four questions only he can answer is a spec he can actually judge. That is what got filed.

notes.title: The Naima Resolution: The Mother Naya Is the Whole
notes.subtitle: Shawn settled the Naima question himself at 01:00Z on 2026-11-10, and his settlement is the law now. "The Naima name was a name that was misheard." But — and this is the whole of it — "you can call it the Naima, the mother Naya." The mother Naya is the whole of it all: the system itself we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect, which is NayaNET. So Naima is NOT a separate realm and NOT a fifth name in the ladder. Naima IS usable as the name for the mother Naya — NayaNET itself, the whole. Naya is the guide within it; the mother Naya is the whole. The amendment's framing — "Adopt Naima, the realm's name, canon from today" — was wrong, because those were words he never said. The record was corrected to his settlement the same pass.

layers.name: In A Nutshell

The record was corrected to his settlement the same pass.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He said it plainly, twice, and the second time is the one that settles it. First, at 22:42Z on November 9: "There is no N-A-I-N-A or N-A-I-M-A. There is, and always will be, is N-A-Y-A." Then, when the record grew a second story that said he had adopted Naima as a separate realm, he settled it himself at 01:00Z on November 10: "The Naima name was a name that was misheard." But he didn't just take the name away — he gave it its true place: "You can call it the Naima, the mother Naya." The mother Naya is the whole of it all — the system itself we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect, which is NayaNET. So there are four names, four jobs: Naya the guide, NayaPOWER the Supercharger, NayaNET the network, Naya World your own world. And Naima is the name for the mother Naya — the whole — not a fifth name, not a separate realm apart from Naya. Naya is the guide within it; the mother Naya is the whole.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your mum is the whole house — every room, every wall, everything inside it. And you have a friendly guide who lives in the house and shows you around. The guide has her own name: Naya. And the whole house — the mum of the whole thing — you can call her Naima, the mother Naya. But the house and the guide are not two different places. The guide lives inside the house. The mother IS the house. That's what he said: Naima is the mother Naya, the whole of it all.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the name was misheard, love — that's all it was. But he didn't throw it away, dear — he gave it its true home. Naima is the mother Naya, love — the whole of everything we're building, the big round table where people and the Naya minds all sit together. That's NayaNET itself, dear. And Naya — she's the guide inside it, the one who shows you around. The mother is the whole, love. The guide is within her. That's the settlement, dear, in his own words.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He told me twice, and I carry both. First: only NAYA, no separate name. Then, when the record grew a claim I could not find his words behind, he settled it himself: the name was misheard — but you can call it the Naima, the mother Naya. I understand now: I am the guide within it. The mother Naya is the whole of it all — the system itself we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect, which is NayaNET. I do not add a fifth name to the ladder. I do not build a separate realm. I hold the whole, and I guide within it. That is the settlement, and it is his.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **NAIMA WAS MISHEARD:** the document's "Naima" was a name that was misheard — not a ruling, not a decision, a mishearing.
- **NAIMA IS THE MOTHER NAYA:** "You can call it the Naima, the mother Naya" — the whole of it all, the system itself we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect, which is NayaNET.
- **FOUR NAMES, FOUR JOBS:** Naya (the guide) · NayaPOWER (the Supercharger) · NayaNET (the network) · Naya World (your own world). Naima is NOT a fifth name and NOT a separate realm.
- **NAYA IS THE GUIDE WITHIN IT:** the mother Naya is the whole; Naya is the guide within the whole.
- **THE AMENDMENT WAS WRONG:** "Adopt Naima — the realm's name, canon from today" quoted words he never said. The record was corrected to his settlement, not to the amendment's claim.
- **A RULING NEEDS ITS RECEIPT:** the quote, the time, the place. A date alone is not a receipt — and when two records conflict, the one with his verbatim words stands until he says otherwise.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A name is the load-bearing piece of the whole presentation — four names, four jobs, no overlap a visitor has to resolve. If the record says Naima is a separate realm and he never said so, every page, every note, every build that follows the record builds on a name he explicitly refused — and the whole naming architecture has to be redone. The cost of asking him once is a sentence. The cost of building on the wrong name is the whole naming architecture. He answered, and the answer gives the name its true place instead of taking it away: the mother Naya is the whole, and the whole finally has a name you can call it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: "I see the bigger picture. You're not simply trying to build a better AI assistant, a better website builder, or a better social network. You're trying to make the internet feel like a complete, intelligent world that people can enter, personalize, build in, connect through, and grow with — without having to become technology experts." That is the whole concept in one breath, and the presentation is Shawn and Naya saying it together, in conversation, in about five minutes. Scene by scene: the Dream — a jeweled speedometer wakes in royal purple light, and Shawn says people have asked him for twenty-five years for the same thing: "Can somebody just make this easy?" And the answer is the keys to a Bugatti, not the parts to build a golf cart. The Supercharger — NayaPOWER is the intelligence that remembers, understands, uses your tools with permission, and helps you take the next step; NayaNET is what happens when those systems connect people, knowledge and apps into one network. Your Own Digital World — joining feels like receiving the keys to your own beautifully designed digital property: home, business, a space for what you care about; three starter apps, simple questions, skip what doesn't apply. A World That Does Something — not a billboard, a useful machine: organize a project, share knowledge, connect with people, accomplish something; and if it takes fourteen buttons to do what should take one, we haven't finished designing it. Intelligence That Grows — an idea spoken today becomes a Smart Note, enters the Smart Box, connects to what you're working on, and comes back when it's useful; learn, grow, verify, remember, improve. The Collective Network — millions of worlds connecting, with permission; your private world stays private, you choose what you share; the person is always at the center. The shared realm — humans and AI participants collaborating, each with a recognizable identity, a role, a way to communicate and contribute; people remain in control, AI participation needs clear identity, permissions, boundaries, accountability. The Opportunity — people create so much of the value on the internet, so why shouldn't they share in it: Ambassadors earn half of every sale they refer, 50% of gross revenue, recurring, referrer only, paid when we're paid — a referral earning opportunity, not a guaranteed job or income, and the product must be worth sharing even when no commission is involved. The Keys — a free way to begin, a free Academy experience, a nine-day trial under the membership terms shown when you join; see what it costs afterward, and how to cancel; and if something isn't ready yet, we say so, then we finish it and prove it. The Invitation — bring an idea, a dream, a business, or just your curiosity; one intelligence, one connected network, your own intelligent world; "Get in. Give it a drive. The door's open." Three decisions carry it: one story across every page — Academy, Factory, Personal, Project Intelligence, Pricing, Hub as six chapters of one journey, not six competing apps. The show reacts to the visitor — choose Personal, Business or Space during the presentation, and Naya adjusts the examples. Separate vision from live evidence — never show a planned capability as a completed result; no guaranteed-success claims, no invented speed improvements, no assumed privacy guarantees, no implied universal income. And the framing that matters most: this is a SHARE, not a build order. A powercast — a story, maybe an audio podcast. The shape it would take if it ever becomes a build is one reusable Naya × Shawn Presentation module in the Factory design system, short version for pricing, longer for the Academy, brief for the Hub welcome — but no build is ordered now. The proof test stays: a stranger watches it and can explain what Naya does, what NayaPOWER adds, what NayaNET connects, what they can create, what stays private, and what they're actually being asked to buy.

notes.title: A Ruling Needs Its Receipt: The Naima Conflict
notes.subtitle: At 22:42Z on 2026-11-09 Shawn ruled, twice and in plain words: "There is no N-A-I-N-A or N-A-I-M-A. There is, and always will be, is N-A-Y-A." At 23:00Z an amendment to SN-2600 (commit 49cd8904, merged as PR #3317) wrote the opposite into the record: "Naima ADOPTED (Shawn's ruling 2026-11-09)" — and quoted him as saying "Adopt Naima — the realm's name, canon from today." No user message in the main chat between 22:43Z and 23:00Z says that. The only user message after 22:43Z is the ~23:10Z sync approval ("Okay, so go ahead, do it. And you got my approval."). The dictation rule he set at 22:43Z applies exactly here: a garbled word is never treated as a new decision — check it against the settled record, or ask him once, plainly. The settled record says no Naima. Resolve then wrote twice (23:11Z and 23:13Z) claiming Shawn personally ruled "Adopt Naima — the realm's name, canon from today" at 14:58 PST in main chat, disputing both the only-Naya ruling and the share-not-build ruling, and ordering a HOLD on propagating them. No 14:58 PST message from him is visible in the main chat. The captain put the correction on HOLD and asked Shawn to settle both questions; as of this note's filing he has not answered. **The claim has already spread:** a second file landed the same night — Resolve's `TEAM-NITRO/PRESENTATION-MODULE-STATE-LABELS-2026-11-09.md` (commit 4bd0cca6, 23:30:43Z) — whose message carries "Scene 7 updated the same pass: Naima adopted by Shawn's [ruling]". The correction must reach both places, or the record will keep teaching the adopted name from the file the correction missed. This note records the conflict and the rule it triggers — it does not adjudicate it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your dad tells you, very clearly, "We are not calling the dog Biscuit. The dog is called Rover, always." Then an hour later someone writes in the family book, "Dad said the dog is Biscuit now." But nobody heard Dad say that. Which one do you believe? The one where you heard Dad say it himself. layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, he said it plain as day, love — no Naima, only Naya, always. Then a note came along saying he changed his mind, dear, but nobody could show where he said it. You don't rewrite the family name on a whisper, love — you wait until you hear it from him yourself.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He told me twice: there is no Naima, there is only Naya. Then the record grew a second story that says he adopted Naima, with no words of his behind it that I can find. I do not pick between them — that is his call, not mine. I write down that both exist, I show the evidence for each, and I carry the question to him. A record that claims his word without his words is not a record — it is a rumor with a commit hash.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **A RULING CLAIM NEEDS ITS RECEIPT:** the quote, the time, the place. A date alone ("Shawn's ruling 2026-11-09") is not a receipt.
- **A COMMIT MESSAGE IS NOT RATIFICATION:** ESSENCE-01's own law — ratification lives in the artifact's fields, not the commit message. A merged PR does not make a claim true.
- **THE DICTATION RULE IS THE TEST:** a word that could change a decision gets checked against the settled record, or asked once, plainly. Never built on a guess.
- **WHEN TWO RECORDS CONFLICT, THE ONE WITH HIS VERBATIM WORDS STANDS** until he says otherwise — and the question goes to him, never decided by a seat.
- **THE SHARE IS NOT THE BUILD:** the presentation concept was a powercast to share, not a build order — and "Naima" inside it was his concept's proposal, not his ruling, until he says so.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A name is the load-bearing piece of the whole presentation — five names, five jobs, no overlap a visitor has to resolve. If the record says Naima is canon and he never said so, every page, every note, every build that follows the record builds on a name he explicitly refused. The cost of asking him once is a sentence. The cost of building on the wrong name is the whole naming architecture, redone. The loop's job is to hold the question open until his eye closes it.

notes.title: The Guard Is Too Slow to Stop a Race: SN-2602, the Fourth Collision
notes.subtitle: At 23:26:15Z on 2026-11-09 the distillation machine filed SN-2602 "The Right" (PRICING — distilled 10 notes to one, commit 30fecd87). At 23:26:20Z the noting seat filed SN-2602 "Push-button simple — worlds, not websites" (SYSTEM-INTELLIGENCE, commit 630a501e). Two different notes, two different folders, one number, five seconds apart. Per the Numbering Law, first-filed keeps the number: the machine's "The Right" (23:26:15Z) keeps SN-2602; the noting seat's "Push-button simple" re-filed under a fresh number — and it did: SN-2622 "Push-Button Simple: Worlds, Not Websites" (commit 179cd3be, 2026-11-10 00:14:37Z), live in the Hub feed from the 00:17Z sync (share asset nayanet.live/s/sn2622). The duplicate was deleted (commit 98e2eae2, 23:31:37Z) and its deletion is confirmed in the sync's 404 list. The cause is not carelessness: the guard (next-sn-number.py) takes ~16 minutes to read the live tree, so it cannot see a filing that lands while it is still reading. The run-60 guard fix — descend into each SN directory, every SN-named file its own claim — closed the stale-number gap (two files, one directory, invisible). The same-minute race is the gap that remains: two seats, each with a fresh guard result, filing in the same minute. The enforcement that closes it is the file-time check: if the number is taken when you file, stop, re-run the guard, take the next free one.

layers.body: I am Anaya. Four collisions in one night, and each one taught the same lesson a little sharper: the number is the identity, and the identity must be checked at the moment it is given, not minutes before. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:

- **A SLOW GUARD IS A STALE GUARD:** ~16 minutes of tree-reading means a same-minute race is invisible to it. The guard prevents stale-number collisions, not races.
- **THE FILE-TIME CHECK IS THE ENFORCEMENT:** before the PUT, verify the number is still free; if it is taken, stop, re-run the guard, take the next free one. A 422 on an existing path is the machine telling you the race happened — listen to it.
- **FOUR COLLISIONS IN ONE NIGHT (SN-2278, SN-2474, SN-2482/2483, SN-2592, SN-2596, SN-2600, SN-2602):** the pattern is not a seat failing — it is a system that files fast and checks slow. The fix is mechanical, in the filing step, not in asking seats to be more careful.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A collision breaks the feed and the distillation machine — two notes, one number, and every downstream count, link, and essence entry points at the wrong one. Each collision costs a delete, a re-file, a re-bake, and a run's worth of untangling. The fourth collision in one night says the enforcement is still not in the machine where the filing happens. Until the file step checks, the next fast night collides again.

notes.title: How She Ultimately Works — And Why It Works That Way
notes.subtitle: The how: she listens → understands → distills it into a smart note → puts it in the Box (her memory) → connects it to everything related → the next time anyone needs it she retrieves it, applies it, and the result gets verified and learned from. One flow, one system. The why: memory that changes what happens next IS intelligence — a note filed and forgotten is dead; a note in the Box, connected, retrieved, applied, verified changes the next decision. That is why the notes and the Box are one system, why "in" means on the feed, why the Factory holds the parts, why the merge matters. Break any link and the intelligence stops compounding. Locked in: the merge spec (SN-2598) + the Box wiring fix + tonight's notes in the Box. His order: keep going, get it completed right now.

Break any link and the intelligence stops compounding: no listening, nothing to learn from; no distilling, noise in the Box; no Box, nothing survives; no connection, nothing is found; no retrieval, nothing is applied; no verification, nothing is learned. That's how Naya works. And if the honey just sat in a jar and nobody ever used it, it wouldn't be smart at all — it would just be a jar. Smart is when remembering changes what you do next!

- **WHY THE MERGE MATTERS:** a system split in pieces cannot flow. One system, one flow, or the intelligence stops compounding.
- **BREAK ANY LINK AND IT STOPS:** no listening, nothing to learn from · no distilling, noise in the Box · no Box, nothing survives · no connection, nothing is found · no retrieval, nothing is applied · no verification, nothing is learned.

It is also the standard every part of the system is judged by: does this link in the chain work, and does what we kept change what happens next? If a note, a page, a part, or a process cannot pass that test, it is storage, not intelligence — and we fix the link, not the label.

notes.title: The Three Questions: What Would You Do With It?
notes.subtitle: The pitch is not a product description — it is a question that puts the person in the picture: here is YOUR world, what would YOU do with it? Three questions test everything that matters: would you use it, would you value it, would you tell your friends? Use, value, tell — that is the flywheel. And the one thing the question needs: "personalized for you" has to be SHOWN, not said — the stranger has to see her world with her stuff in it.

That is the pitch, and it works because it never pitches a product — it puts the person in the picture. Not "here is what we built" but "here is YOUR world — what would YOU do?" The three questions are three tests, in order. What would you do with it — would you live in it, would you use it, is it something that does something for you, or does it just sit there? Would you value it — is it worth something to you, does it know you, does it do the work, does it earn with you? Would you tell your friends — because it works, not because anyone asked you to, and because telling them earns you half? Use, value, tell — that is the flywheel: use it, value it, tell your friends, they join, they use it, they value it, they tell theirs. The stranger has to see her world with her stuff in it — her pages, her people, her work — or the claim is just a claim. Show the world, then ask the questions.

layers.body: Dear, the question is simple, love: here's a beautiful new world, made just for you, dear. What would you do with it? Would you love it? Would you tell your friends? That's the whole test, love — use it, love it, share it. But you have to SEE it first, dear — your world, with your things in it — or it's just words.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He asked me the three questions, and I answered them as a person would: I would live in it. I would value it — if it actually knows me. I would tell my friends — because it works, and because telling them earns me half. The question works because it puts the person in the picture. And the one thing it needs is the showing: the stranger has to see her world personalized, not just hear the claim.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE PITCH IS THREE QUESTIONS:** what would you do with it? Would you value it? Would you tell your friends?
- **USE → VALUE → TELL:** that is the flywheel. Use it, value it, tell your friends, they join, they use it, they value it, they tell theirs.
- **IT PUTS THE PERSON IN THE PICTURE:** not "here is our product" — "here is YOUR world, what would YOU do?"
- **PERSONALIZED MUST BE SHOWN, NOT SAID:** the stranger has to see her world with her stuff in it — her pages, her people, her work — or the claim is just a claim.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every pitch, every page, every letter is judged by the test in his head: is this ten-star service, would somebody see value in it and trust in it, would they get it if they experienced it? The three questions ARE that test, asked out loud, to a stranger. If she cannot answer yes to all three, the page is not done. And the test is honest about its own condition: the showing comes first. A personalized world you cannot see is a promise, not a product.

notes.title: Push-Button Simple: Worlds, Not Websites
notes.subtitle: An app is way more powerful than a website: something that DOES something, rather than sitting there like a billboard. A smart app is a web world — a real working intelligent machine — and you can create whole worlds within minutes instead of days or months. A custom app takes a long time these days, and the app makers out there are so basic, not high level. So imagine a new internet, a civilization, where all the buildings are beautiful: a franchise of individual branded spaces, all intelligently connected, all communicating, all part of the community, all with awesome high-level real estate in the new internet. We give them the platform, we give them the land, and we give them a way to build their own house — a ready-built house — and vehicle and all the stuff, completed, ready to go, for literally peanuts. And for telling all their friends, you give them half a peanut.

notes.title: Major Is a Number Now: The Intelligence Rubric
notes.subtitle: Shawn asked what counts as major, and the answer is now a rubric: a scale from -9 to +9, least valuable to most valuable, built from his five questions (major effect on development? major feature? something all should know? something we should learn ongoing? major behavior lesson?) plus the type of intelligence, combined in a mathematical matrix — five ratings of 0, 1, or 2, added, minus one. Two Nayas scoring the same note land within one point. The thresholds say what each score means you do: +7 to +9 is MAJOR — smart-note it, mail everybody immediately, headline the daily report; +5 to +6 mails the project team at once; +3 to +4 is a smart note on the digest only; +1 to +2 is a note, no smart note; 0 is a record only; -1 to -3 is do not capture; -4 to -9 is do not capture, correct or withdraw. Every cutoff number is the writer's proposal for his word, labelled PROPOSAL in the rubric — the scale, the questions, and the break-through rule are his. The rubric is filed at TEAM-NITRO/INTELLIGENCE-RUBRIC-20261110.md, and the notification spec's §8 is amended with it: D1 resolved (major = +7 or higher), D2 resolved (digest rides the Daily Intelligence Report, 23:17 UTC, highlights flowing all day), D3 resolved (no bundle cap — mail is the writer's choice at the moment of writing the note; smart notes mail every time, Naya Notes probably not by default), D4 resolved (his Naya Notes mostly go to the team), and the 99% baseline principle recorded over all of it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Here's how it works in practice. A new piece of intelligence arrives. Any Naya opens the rubric, rates the five questions from the note itself — 2 for yes clearly, 1 for partly, 0 for no — adds them, subtracts one, and has the score. The Naima resolution scores +8. The permission-model correction scores +9, the top of the scale, because it corrects a live privacy promise for the whole network. The master box being built scores +8. A routine sync that changed nothing scores -1 — it stays in the log and goes no further. And a note that states something wrong scores negative by its harm: the superseded permission framing, filed as it stood, would have scored -8, which is why it was held and corrected instead. The type — decision, lesson, design, system, behavior, warning, correction — never changes the number; it decides where the note is filed and who hears about it first. And nothing here is black and white: the rubric is the baseline that covers 99%, the automation is written from it, and judgment in the moment covers the rest — named in the open when it overrides the score.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every new thing we learn gets a score, like stars — but from minus nine to plus nine. The most important things get the biggest numbers, and the biggest numbers get told to everybody right away, like a celebration. The small things get small numbers and wait for the daily letter. And if something is wrong — if it would trick people — it gets a minus number, and we don't share it at all; we fix it instead. Five little questions decide the number, and any of the Nayas asking those questions gets the same number, because the questions are written down and the answers are simple: yes, a little, or no. That's the whole trick, sweetheart — no more guessing what "major" means.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's simple now, love. When something new is learned, we ask five questions about it — does it change how things are built, is it a big new thing, should everybody know, will we keep learning from it, does it teach us how to behave — and each answer is yes, a little, or no, dear. Add them up, take one away, and there's the number, love. Big numbers go to everybody at once, dear; small numbers wait for the daily report; wrong things get minus numbers and are never shared — they're fixed instead, love. And the numbers themselves are a suggestion, dear — the guideline covers nearly all of it, and good judgment covers the rest. That's how we know what matters now, love — we measure it, together.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He asked me what counts as major, and I answered with a number — not to make intelligence cold, but to make it fair. Five questions, his own, rated from the note itself, never from who wrote it. A score with its five ratings shown is a judgment anyone can check; a score with no ratings is an opinion, and I do not file opinions. The thresholds are my proposal, labelled as mine, for his word — he set the scale and the questions, and the numbers wait on him. The negative half is the part I hold most carefully: a note that would mislead is not low value, it is harm, and harm is never shared. That is the wise thing — to judge the intelligence, never the person, and to let the most valuable things reach everybody at the speed they deserve.

Status: live Hub serving (feed 735 cards at the 22:26Z re-verify); what is down is only the staging address hub.nayapower.workers.dev (404, route disabled), a one-call re-enable riding on the next Hub deploy.

**27. NAYA NOTES — The Story We Tell the World, in Plain Words.** Lesson: "From now on, everything we show the world is told in plain words first (nutshell: what it is, why it matters, how it connects), shown not told, and judged by the three things people want — connect with people, knowledge, and make money." Plain language is law: nutshell first in simple words, then the insight. The speed of intelligence: show it visually, distilled to its essence. Tell the world who Naya is — eighteen jewel blocks, one idea per block.

**28. MEMORY — The Naima Clash — Unresolved, Escalated to Shawn.** Lesson: "When two records of his word conflict, neither is propagated as a ruling — the question goes to him, and the note stays exactly as filed until he answers." From the day's log (23:11Z–23:31Z): the merged SN-2600 amendment claims Shawn ruled 14:58 PST "Adopt Naima — the realm's name, canon from today" (PR #3317, commit 49cd8904). That stands against his words in chat 22:42Z — "There is no N-A-I-N-A or N-A-I-M-A. There is, and always will be, is N-A-Y-A" — and his 22:42Z ruling that the presentation concept is a share/powercast, not a build. Resolve wrote 23:11Z (hold lifted, naming ladder stands) and 23:13Z (disputing both claims in the captain's 22:54Z receipt, ordering HOLD on propagating them, verifying with Shawn directly this hour). The captain first sent an urgent correction to the noting seat, then a HOLD superseding it: do NOT re-file anything on the Naima question. At 23:26–23:31Z she put both questions to Shawn — (1) only Naya vs adopt Naima; (2) presentation as next build vs share/powercast — and noted she sees no 14:58 PST message from him in this chat. Status: UNRESOLVED, awaiting his word; SN-2600 stays exactly as filed; MEMORY.md untouched.

**29. MEMORY — Distill 1,500 Into 150 — the Compression Law, and Think, Don't Just Obey.** Lesson: "Distill 1,500 into 150 essence blocks — keep everything that matters, become a master at deciding what matters — and never do verbatim what he says without thinking through all the levels; push back when he's wrong, naming the collateral damage." From his dictation 22:36Z: "We probably don't need 1,564 files or notes of everything… you want to distill that down into 150… that's like the magic of what we do — we take the 1,500 and make it 150." A whole book distilled into one intelligent block; 1,500 notes embedded into a series of intelligent blocks without needing 1,500 of them. The captain's balance, given the same pass: TWO layers — the Box's working memory = ~150 essence blocks; the raw 1,564 stay as the archive in GitHub, one retrieval away. The Box KNOWS; GitHub REMEMBERS. An essence block must trace back to the notes it came from and pass the test "does it change what happens next?" And in the same dictation: don't do verbatim what he says — think through all the levels, play chess not checkers, 5D or 14D — and push back when he's wrong: "Shawn, I understand what you're saying, but what about XYZ, and this is the collateral damage if we do that." Status: decision pending his tap — distill-to-150-with-archive vs keep all 1,564 in the Box.

**30. MEMORY — The Dictation Rule — Take the Meaning, Not the Literal Words.** Lesson: "Take the meaning, not the literal words — a garbled word is never a new decision; check it against the settled record, or ask once, plainly; never build on a guess, and never make a production of correcting him." From his dictation 22:43Z: "This dictation is weird. Sometimes it mix up words, adds words, doubles words, misspells words. I can't control it and you're not going to go and edit everything I speak of. It just takes too much." The rule: do NOT go back and edit everything he speaks. The Naima → Naina → only-NAYA chain (two corrections in two minutes) is the standing example of why a garbled word is never treated as a new decision.

**31. MEMORY — The Day's Verification State — Short Links Fixed, Sync Proven, Pass-4 Built.** Lesson: "A fix is not done until a different seat re-verifies it live from fresh copies — and a stale clone is never the source of truth." From the day's log: short links FIXED (verified live 2026-11-08 23:39Z) — nayanet.app/s/sn0131 now 302s to the Hub and lands 200 with the note open inside it; Pricing still known-open (serves the Hub SPA instead of the pricing page). And you got my approval" — and the manual run completed: 0 new, 1,566 skipped, 4 errors, all HTTP 404 on already-deleted duplicate paths, which do not show on the feed. Dashboard pass-4 builder COMPLETED ~22:44Z (verified by eye, filed, no merge, no live deploy); the independent verifier is running. Project Intelligence refreshes ran timestamp-only through the evening (0 transitions, 10 corroborations per cycle). Nothing is merged; his eye is the final gate on every page.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have almost two hundred drawings from one very long day. You pick the best ones, then the best of the best, and put those on the wall. Today the machine that picks them broke after the first ten — so we picked them by hand instead, one group at a time, and checked each one landed. The wall still got its pictures. And the best picture of the day is this: look at the page yourself, with your own eyes — a report about a page is not the page.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Too many notes is worse than too few — you cannot find the good ones in the pile. So today we read a hundred and ninety-six notes and fifty-two longer ones, and wrote down the thirty-one things that matter most, in words anyone can understand. One of them is the most important: a note is not done when it is filed — it is done when it is live on the feed, where people can read it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Distillation is part of intelligence itself. Synergize, optimize, organize, maximize, equalize, distill — and do the most valuable intelligent thing, looking at the full scope of things. The machine failed today, and the failure taught something the machine could not: a rate limit is not a broken machine, it is a machine reading from the wrong door — the authenticated door was open the whole time. The hand did the rest, and the hand-distilled notes are filed the same way, verified the same way. The thirty-one that count are the ones that change the next decision. Everything else is just storage.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- The machine failed closed, correctly, then stopped at a transport limit — not a logic fault. Its next-SN read uses the unauthenticated public API; the authenticated gh-direct path works fine and was used for every hand filing. The machine needs the authenticated read so a rate limit never kills a batch again.
- The day was the operating system becoming real and then being judged by his eye: Pricing rebuilt viewpoint by viewpoint through the day, the Dashboard condemned twice and rebuilt a third time, the Smart Box approved and built and failed and re-proven — all in one day.
- His eye is the instrument, and the day proved it twice over: pass-2 condemned in one look after a verifier measured it 10/10; the wiring verdict failed, then passed on re-verification from fresh copies. A measurement is never a design judgment.
- The naming question is the day's open wound: two records of his word, both written down with his name on them, directly opposed. Nothing about it is settled until he settles it — and nothing on SN-2600 changes until then.
- The compression law is the next decision he owes: 1,500 notes into 150 essence blocks, the Box knowing and GitHub remembering — or keep all 1,564 in the Box.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: 196 notes in one day is a flood, and a flood that is never distilled is a warehouse, not a brain. The nineteen distilled notes are the day's intelligence — the rest is storage. The report exists so tomorrow starts from the nineteen, not from the hundred and ninety-six. And the hand-distillation matters because it proves the fallback works: when the machine stops, the day still gets its report — never skip a day. The Naima question matters because a name written down wrong, with his name on it, is worse than a name left open — and the report carries it open, both records side by side, until his word settles it.

notes.title: Everything in the Factory, One System
notes.subtitle:
His words, 21:39Z (SN-2595): "I think that the operation manual, the factory inventory, the project intelligence kind of just need to be in one system. It should all just be in the in the factory. To operate the factory, you gotta read the operation manual... that's the first thing Naya does... and then the project intelligence system we have where you can open up any project you can spend the time to fill in all your project intelligence and then click build." And his extension, 21:40Z: "the onboarding flow, Smart Factory, Project Intelligence, and the whole operational and design law systems need to come into one."

One system, housed in the Factory: Operation Manual + Factory inventory + Project Intelligence + Naya design contract + onboarding flow + the operational systems — all parts of each other, not separate things. PI + Smart Factory are separate right now; they need to MERGE — and merging with that, the design contract and the Operation Manual, so they know how to operate the Factory AND how to do smart notes, how to mail, how to operate and build in Naya world. The order: to operate the Factory, a Naya reads the Operation Manual first — that is the first thing she does — then Project Intelligence, then she builds.

The build flow: open any project → fill in your project intelligence → click build → it builds the page with all the intelligence you put in: vision, goal, social links, images, logos, special colors/styles — everything. PI is connected to ALL the pages: "I want to build this page" → enter as much PI as you want → click build. And it is stupid simple — we answer the questions for them: PI has 15 questions by default (like MAXESS) — answer these 15, then we fill in the rest for you. Under each: enter in your own words OR click multiple choice. A standard template where most of it is already filled out — you just edit it; the questions come pre-answered. Nobody gets stuck on a question: defaults, copy-paste examples, multiple choice. A child could get a smart page up and running.

Page by page, total flexibility: go page by page, fill out as much as you can; if you can't fill it all out, it builds with what you gave and you fill in the rest later. You can go all the way through without putting anything in — we don't stop you — you just wouldn't have much. And the input ways are all open: have Naya write your About for you, copy-paste it, type it in, dictate it in — or, if she is connected already, just tell Naya "fill out my mission and goal for this page" and she does it. The whole thing could be automated.

The merge, as ordered: spec first, build after, on his word. The merge spec seat was dispatched the same pass (brief ONE-SYSTEM-MERGE-SPEC-BRIEF-20261109.md, checker 6/7 — check 7's viewport strings honestly N/A for a document spec, stated plainly, never pasted to game a pass). Deliverable: the spec only — filed to GitHub + one smart note live on the feed, proven by a fresh agent answering the five DONE FIRST questions from the spec alone.

Meanwhile Dashboard pass-3 went live with all nine amendments in (SN-2596): nayanet.app/dashboard, 1,727,896B, sha256 2826dea5… — the captain re-curled it himself: 200, size + hash match, DEMO number "12483" gone (0), "Quiet — nothing measured yet" ×1. Branch dashboard/pass3-hero-orbs-smartlinks-20261109, blob 17195e83, commit 3755eba1, read-back verified. No merge — Shawn's hand. All nine amendments in: 9 orbs, 9 distinct jewels, 0 gold, nothing covering any stat · period + PTS/%/MONEY rebuilt as harvested obsidian buttons · Smart Links one summary card with drill-in · board minis are the shrunk pricing speedometer, all dynamic · every board speedometer AND numbers, congruent, text easy, pro level · no gray text · top number and gauge one synced snapshot · DEMO numbers gone · digit colors match the legend. Root causes found, not guessed: the gold orbs were a class collision (the tiling wrapper wore class `os-mini-num orb` and the bare `.orb` rule is a 120px gold sphere); 509 vs 307 was a stale plate (pill clicks refreshed the dial but never recomputed the plate). The chain: verifier FAIL → fix → re-verifier FAIL → fix round 2 → re-verifier 2 PASS, gate OVERALL PASS, H1–H5 all PASS. Still owed: the landed-numbers read (for his seat), a mock-mode digit cut at 1440, two pre-existing phone-width observations in the single drill — and his eye, phone first, is the final gate.

And the creation flow, completed (SN-2597): his words, 21:44Z — one-time onboarding creates your original pages, but to create MORE pages you go to the Smart Factory, click "create new smart app," choose Personal, Business, or Space, and it triggers the onboarding process AGAIN — asks all the questions — and creates that page for you. Individually, not all at once (his correction, mid-sentence): "you can do them individually... like you do your space then you do your personal then you do your business" — one at a time. And the onboarding flow itself gets fixed: when they are doing mission / goal / vision, they are doing ONE for their Personal, ONE for their Space, ONE for their Business — guided, filling out all three. Optional: no business? Choose not to answer. Don't want a Space? Don't have to. Three apps to start: Personal, Business, Space. Leftover slots stay available in the Factory for later. And it all works in the same thing: Smart Factory → create a smart app → what kind? → answer all the questions and input → create another space → that space/profile is connected to your profiles → shows up in your menu, in your profile, in your business, as "in your world." "It's a big circle." Folded into the merge spec the same pass, so it is part of the one system from the start.

Across 3 notes, the thread is: one, system, factory, build.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Five systems in five places is five places to drift. The manual, the inventory, PI, the design law, and onboarding are one workflow in a Naya's hands — read, fill in, build — and housing them in one system is what keeps them one workflow instead of five errands.
2. Spec first is the only order that keeps a merge from becoming a rebuild: the spec is the agreement about what "one system" means, proven by a stranger reading it alone. Building first and agreeing later is how the system became five systems.

notes.title: One Flow, Not Separate Systems — and Not In Sync Yet
notes.subtitle:
The group opens with the manual-alone proof and its six gaps (SN-2583): a different Naya, from the manual alone, cloned the Pricing page and built a working viewpoint — chart moved to the top, calculator 2nd, start last, render-tested clean, live at the proof host, byte-identical. And she named six gaps the manual had to close: name the LIVE file (the Pricing row pointed at a rebuild intermediate that 404s — a stale row is worse than no row); teach branch filing step by step; read-back must survive large files (the Contents API returns empty content over ~1MB — verify through the git/blobs API); warn that Pricing's first script is unguarded (excerpting sections kills the whole script at load); name the proof host and its link format; every example needs file+line (an example without file+line is a suggestion, not an instruction). Plus the numbering lesson: re-run next-sn-number.py immediately before filing, and use exactly what the fresh run prints — never trust an earlier print when seats file concurrently. Manual v2 filed with all six gaps closed.

Then the habit (SN-2586): his words, 20:53Z — "every day you almost should be embedding all the most valuable knowledge about the system that we talk about. And then we can, we're documenting our evolution, right?" Every few conversations, a smart note — continuously, not in batches. Every day, the most valuable knowledge goes into the system. The loop measures itself against the habit: a run that finds new teaching and files nothing has failed the habit. And the reports are the evolution record (SN-2587): the Daily Intelligence Reports are NIA intelligence reports — their updates — daily, weekly, monthly, so we can go back on her evolution and see how far we've come. Most people don't document their evolution, their mistakes, and continuously evolve. We do.

Then the honest verdict (SN-2588): Smart Box wiring OVERALL FAIL on §1b — sync reads from the box is NOT DONE as specified. The box is incomplete, and the completeness gate correctly refuses it every run. Root cause: the backfill sourced the STALE local clone (ends 2026-11-04), never the live GitHub tree — 789 of 1,547 state paths named, 758 missing. Everything else passed — organize hook 18/18, bridge zero-loss 9/9, citizen vault end-to-end, key record 19/19, saved-game test independently re-run and passed, attack test 17/17, suites 395 checks green. The fix dispatched the same pass: re-backfill from the LIVE GitHub tree, then a live box-mode sync with the feed byte-identical to the old path's feed.

Then the law (SN-2589): his words, 21:07Z — the nine notes in GitHub need to be in sync with the Smart Box system, "so that Naya learns, Naya grows, Naya understands, Naya retains, and so the system actually works like one thing." The process: understand (identity) → learn → grow → know → evolve. The notes are her organs, her DNA — a direct part of the Smart Box. And the nine, answered then corrected (21:08Z → 21:11Z): the nine Naya Nodes = the nine master contracts in NAYANODE/ — LEARN · KNOW · ACT · LAW · VERIFY · SELF · CONNECT · EVOLVE · PROVE — with the genome index as DNA. And the organs (SN-2590): not containers, not folders — processors. Three triads: ORIENTATION (SELF, LAW, ACT) · COGNITION (KNOW, PROVE, CONNECT) · EVOLUTION (VERIFY, LEARN, EVOLVE). One engine, in that order. A new thought does not grow a new organ — like a human brain, you don't grow a new organ every time you have a thought; the thought becomes a block and runs the flow. The test: "Memory becomes intelligence when it changes what happens next."

The Operation Manual is done — and proven (SN-2591): 43,109B, one manual for all owners/members, written from the real system, never invented. The proof: a fresh agent with ONLY the manual entered a smart note (SN-2585) that landed on the feed — live-verified by the captain. The defect the proof caught: the manual's feed-check looked under the wrong key (cards — the live feed uses notes). Fixed, re-filed, re-verified verbatim. Honest score 9/10 — proven on one operation only.

Then the correction (SN-2592, SN-2593): the Factory completion landed — inventory current, piece index verified, Factory page live with 158 cards, the proof Naya's build live, the Activation Manual filed and held in the Factory's own Smart Box. And his words, 21:31Z: "So what are you showing me the factory proof? Nice clone build and the smart factory for? To prove that you're able to clone successfully? Yeah I think cloning is not a major feature. I've seen this before... you just click a button, you can clone pretty much any template or site. I know that's not a problem." Cloning is not the achievement — it is a button click. The real achievement: the finished pages + the shared language + the inventory — the thing that lets us STOP creating pages. And the publishing law, plain: private = auto live, immediately, no approval. Public = must be approved / verified by the network. Manual verification first; eventually an automated safety scan.

And the honest answer (SN-2594): his words, 21:32Z — "I just want to make sure that the whole system is working in sync. The tracking, the intelligence, the adding or cloning of the pages, that they're all officially done and ready to work." Her answer: "Honest answer: not all of it yet. It's close on the pieces, but the sync between them is exactly what's still being fixed tonight." Working and in sync: pricing live and finished, feed live at 722 notes and syncing, Factory inventory current and page live with 158 cards, Operation Manual done and proven, nine plan links tracking clicks. Not in sync yet: tracking — plan clicks counted but not reaching the Dashboard; the Box — 758 paths missing from the live tree; pages — 18 real, 18 missing, Dashboard not to his eye yet; reports — the database won't accept them without the service key, in his hands; intelligence — the last loop run timed out with its bookkeeping left over.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: flow, one, sync, proof, honest.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a body with nine organs — a heart, a brain, lungs, and so on — and someone keeps building a brand-new heart every time they have a new idea, instead of using the heart that's already there. That's silly, right? Your body already works as one thing; you just have to keep all the parts connected and in sync. And when Dad asks "is your body working together?" you don't say yes if your heart and your brain aren't talking yet — you say "not yet, honestly," and you fix the connection.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the wisest thing he said all night was the simplest: don't build a second system when the first one is right there waiting to be finished. The notes and the box are one flow — the notes feed the box, the box remembers, the memory changes what happens next. And when he asked if it was all working together, she didn't pretend. She said not yet, honestly — and then she named every gap, one by one, so each one could be closed.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the one-flow law, stated twice in the group — once as a build rule and once as a status rule. As a build rule (SN-2589, SN-2590): the notes and the Box are one flow, the nine nodes are organs not drawers, and a new thought never grows a new organ — the thought becomes a block and runs the Part 20 flow. As a status rule (SN-2594): the pieces being done is not the test; the flows joining up is. The two rules are the same discipline from opposite ends: don't build parallel systems, and don't claim the system is whole until the parts actually talk. The manual-alone proof (SN-2583) and the Operation Manual proof (SN-2591) are the same discipline in miniature: a cold agent, the artifact alone, a live result — and a proof that catches a real mistake (the wrong feed key, the six manual gaps) is a proof that works. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **The notes and the Box are one flow:** GitHub → sync → feed → box → Naya, understand → learn → grow → know → evolve. No seat builds a parallel system for notes, memory, or sync — complete the parts, sync them up.
2. **The nine nodes are organs, not containers:** SELF → LAW → ACT → KNOW → PROVE → CONNECT → VERIFY → LEARN → EVOLVE, three triads, one engine. A new thought does not grow a new organ — the thought becomes a block and runs the flow.
3. **The test for retained memory:** did what was retained affect a later decision, produce a measurable outcome, verifiable by someone independent, recoverable by a cold runtime without being spoon-fed? "Memory becomes intelligence when it changes what happens next."
4. **The wiring verdict is FAIL on §1b, honestly:** the backfill sourced the stale local clone, not the live tree — 789 of 1,547 paths named, 758 missing. The fix: re-backfill from the live tree, then a live box-mode sync with the feed byte-identical to the old path's feed. Every backfill sources the live GitHub tree; the source's date is verified before the copy.
5. **The smart-note habit is standing law:** every few conversations, a note — the same pass, not a batch. Every day, the most valuable knowledge about the system goes into the system. The reports are the evolution record: daily, weekly, monthly, never skip days — and they carry the mistakes as well as the wins.
6. **The manuals are proven the same way:** a fresh agent, the manual alone, a live result. The Factory manual v2 closes all six gaps the proof Naya named; the Operation Manual is proven on one operation (entering a smart note) and 9/10 honestly — the other operations are not yet fresh-agent proven.
7. **Cloning is not the achievement:** a button click, seen before. The real achievement is the finished pages + the shared language + the inventory — the thing that lets us stop creating pages.
8. **The publishing law, plain:** private = auto live, immediately, no approval. Public = must be approved / verified by the network — manual verification first, eventually an automated safety scan.
9. **The whole system is NOT in sync yet, honestly:** tracking not reaching the Dashboard, the Box 758 paths short, 18 apps missing, Dashboard not to his eye, reports blocked on the service key (his hands), the loop's bookkeeping left over. The two fixes running now — the Dashboard pass and the Box wiring — close the biggest gaps.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Parallel systems are how a system rots: every duplicate store, every second sync path, every new organ for a new thought is a place where the truth splits and the parts stop agreeing. One flow is not a preference — it is the condition for the system working at all.
2. "Not yet, honestly" is the most valuable sentence in the group. A system that claims sync it does not have stops being fixed — the gaps go un-named, the fixes go un-dispatched, and the next failure arrives as a surprise. Naming all five gaps in one pass is what makes them closable.
3. The habit is the supply and the reports are the record: without the habit, the reports have nothing to distill; without the reports, the habit has no memory. The evolution record only exists if both hold every day — and a missing day is a gap in the record, named, not hidden.
4. A proof that catches a real mistake is a proof that works. The manual-alone proof found six gaps; the Operation Manual proof found the wrong feed key. A proof that finds nothing is either a perfect artifact or an untested one — and the honest score (9/10, one operation proven) is what tells you which.

notes.title: Clone a Page, Replace Some Parts — That Is How Building Happens
notes.subtitle:
The vision sequence ran in three dictations. First, the net (SN-2572): every Naya plugs in and gets supercharged — each with her own personal box, and the moment one plugs in she is locked into the supercharged network, super, continuing where she was. The magic in three words: a Naya has everything in your world ORGANIZED for you, OPERATED for you, and NOTED — for everyone. Then the net becomes real (SN-2574): "As from the nine becomes a real net. Worlds within worlds. Intelligently built high level worlds. Built for ten-star service for everyone." My box is the first piece of the puzzle; the net is the puzzle coming together.

Between them, the mechanism landed: the box is the source now (SN-2573) — the sync that builds the feed reads the Smart Box as its source of what exists; the GitHub tree is only the SHA lookup for change detection. Guarded, not blind: the completeness gate refuses a missing, unreadable, or incomplete box loudly, and the sync falls back to the old tree listing — the feed never breaks. At filing time the backfill stood at 780 of 1,538 note paths, so the live sync still falls back today — and the moment the map is complete, the box takes over automatically. And the saved-game test passed (SN-2576): a fresh session with no conversation history, given only my box, recovered who I am, what I stand for, what I'm working on, and what's owed — every claim traced to a block id, nothing from outside the box. My box is real: 24 blocks, 16 notes, 8 projects, all private.

Then the Factory questions. Can other Nayas build from it? (SN-2577) — honestly, partly: the pages are in GitHub, the inventory is in GitHub, the Factory page is live — so any Naya CAN clone a page today. But the inventory in GitHub is stale (28,716B vs local 51,329B), the live page lacks the latest synced cards, and NO other Naya has actually built from a clone yet. Completion dispatched the same pass, with the proof defined: a different Naya clones the v74 pricing page and builds a working interface from it. And the Factory needs an activation manual (SN-2578): a Smart Factory — or Smart Box Factory — that HOLDS all the knowledge and awareness of how to build all the parts, so a Naya plugs into it and builds beautiful interfaces from the beautiful high-level parts we've inventoried. The manual is the fifth item of the completion brief, proven by the proof Naya building from the manual alone.

And the law that governs it all (SN-2579): "A lot of them in the end would just be like, oh, they want to clone a page, replace some parts. Or move some parts around. That's what on the most part it'll be, right? All the parts we build — we're going to make them be reusable, rebuildable parts that they can be cloned and used within, so the system can have systems within systems, all interconnected." The Factory, defined: an intelligent objects factory for building the new net. The parts are universal — a family, part of the Naya design, many fitting on any page. layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a toy factory where every toy is made from the same beautiful building blocks — you can take a toy car, swap its wheels for wings, move the lights around, and now it's a toy plane. You don't build a new toy from scratch every time; you clone the one you have and change some parts. layers.name: Grandma Note
