His rules: the gauge must match the stats on that board, the numbers must be visible, it must be dynamic, and it must look relevant and real. The amendment went to the pass-4 coordinator the same pass.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: "So you're supposed to do this one for the little mini mini stats boards." This one — the one in the picture. Not a speedometer like the pricing page. This speedometer. Take the shown object: the round dial, the ticks around the edge, the $0 to $10K labels, the "$4.5K" at the bottom center, the needle pointing at the value, the center hub with the purple jewel, the purple arc, the line underneath — "$4 500 of $10 000 — Advancing at $6 000" — and the digit tiles with their colored rims, $ / 4 / 5 / 0 / 0, "/ month" after them. And his rules for it, because a picture alone is not a spec: "make sure that you have the gauge matching what the stats that are there and you should be able to see the numbers and it should be dynamic and work to be relevant and real looking." Four rules, each one a test. The gauge must MATCH the stats on that board — its needle and labels read the board's own numbers: clicks, views, click-through rate, revenue — scaled to that stat, never a copied $4,500 pasted onto a board whose numbers are different. The numbers must be VISIBLE — digit tiles under the gauge, readable at a glance, not tiny grey dials you have to squint at. It must be DYNAMIC — the gauge follows the number; when the number moves, the needle moves; it works. And it must look RELEVANT and REAL — a working instrument for that stat, not decoration. A gauge that reads the wrong numbers is a lie; a gauge you cannot read is a picture; a gauge that never moves is dead. He showed the object so the argument ends: here it is, take it, put it there.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a toy car speedometer. The needle points at how fast the car is going — if the car goes faster, the needle moves! And the numbers are big so you can read them. That's what the little gauges on the Dashboard have to be: real speedometers that point at the real numbers, and move when the numbers move. Not a picture of a speedometer — a real one.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, he showed us the exact speedometer to use, love — a pretty round dial with a needle, dear, and the numbers underneath in lovely tiles. And he said the needle must point at the real numbers on that board, love, and the numbers must be big enough to see, and the needle must move when the numbers move. A real instrument, dear — not a decoration.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He showed me the gauge — the pricing calculator speedometer, the object itself — and told me what it must do on the little boards: match the stats, show the numbers, move with them, look real. I sent it to the pass-4 seat as the object itself, not as a description. The gauge is the object; the numbers are each board's own. Take it, shrink it, put it there.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE SHOWN OBJECT IS THE SPEC:** the pricing calculator speedometer, verbatim — dial, ticks, labels, needle, jewel hub, arc, tiles below. No recreating it "in the same spirit."
- **THE GAUGE MATCHES THE BOARD'S OWN STATS:** needle and labels read that board's numbers — clicks, views, CTR, revenue — scaled to that stat. Never a copied $4,500.
- **THE NUMBERS ARE VISIBLE:** digit tiles under the gauge, readable at a glance.
- **IT IS DYNAMIC:** the gauge follows the number. When the number moves, the needle moves.
- **IT LOOKS RELEVANT AND REAL:** a working instrument for that stat, not decoration.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Three passes argued about what a mini gauge is, and the argument ended the moment he showed the object. That is the law he taught us: when he shows you an object, the deliverable IS that object. No more arguing, no more "in the same spirit" — take it, put it there. And the four rules are the test that keeps it honest: a gauge that reads the wrong numbers is a lie, one you cannot read is a picture, one that never moves is dead.

notes.title: The Keys to a New Digital World — the Shawn × Naya Presentation
notes.subtitle: NayaNET is introduced to the world the way it deserves: not as a sales pitch, but as a five-minute conversation between Shawn, the human founder, and Naya, the AI co-creator — "The Keys to Naya World." We don't just give you a website. We give you the keys to your own intelligent world, and Naya helps you build it, organize it, and make it useful. The concept locks the naming architecture so a stranger never gets lost — Naya is your AI guide and operating partner; NayaPOWER is the intelligence Supercharger (memory, standards, tools, reasoning, authorized action); NayaNET is the network that connects people, apps, knowledge and intelligent systems; Naya World is the personal digital world a member experiences and creates; and Naima — proposed in this concept, awaiting Shawn's ruling — is the shared digital realm where humans and AI participants collaborate. The presentation is one story told across six chapters of one journey: the Smart Factory creates, Personal makes it yours, Project Intelligence organizes your intent, the Academy teaches, Pricing makes the decision simple, and the Hub begins the relationship. The single next build is one reusable Shawn × Naya Presentation module in the existing Factory design system — short version for Pricing, longer story for the Academy, brief welcome for the Hub — every scene carrying its transcript, captions, approved media, destination link, and an honest product-state label. The proof test: a stranger who watches can explain what Naya does, what NayaPOWER adds, what NayaNET connects, what they can create, what stays private, and what they are actually being asked to buy.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: NayaNET is introduced to the world the way it deserves: not as a sales pitch, but as a five-minute conversation between Shawn, the human founder, and Naya, the AI co-creator — "The Keys to Naya World." We don't just give you a website. We give you the keys to your own intelligent world, and Naya helps you build it, organize it, and make it useful. The concept locks the naming architecture so a stranger never gets lost — Naya is your AI guide and operating partner; NayaPOWER is the intelligence Supercharger (memory, standards, tools, reasoning, authorized action); NayaNET is the network that connects people, apps, knowledge and intelligent systems; Naya World is the personal digital world a member experiences and creates; and Naima — the name for the mother Naya, which is NayaNET itself, the whole system we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect — not a separate realm and not a fifth name in the ladder. The presentation is one story told across six chapters of one journey: the Smart Factory creates, Personal makes it yours, Project Intelligence organizes your intent, the Academy teaches, Pricing makes the decision simple, and the Hub begins the relationship. The concept itself is a share, not a build — a powercast, a story Shawn is sharing, maybe to become an audio podcast — not a build order and not queued. The shape it would take IF it ever becomes a build is one reusable Shawn × Naya Presentation module in the existing Factory design system — short version for Pricing, longer story for the Academy, brief welcome for the Hub — every scene carrying its transcript, captions, approved media, destination link, and an honest product-state label. The proof test: a stranger who watches can explain what Naya does, what NayaPOWER adds, what NayaNET connects, what they can create, what stays private, and what they are actually being asked to buy.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: People have asked Shawn the same thing for 25 years: "Can somebody just make this easy? Give me a beautiful website, help me build a business, connect me with people, help me make some money — and please, don't make me spend six months learning how." They never wanted a website. They wanted what a website was supposed to help them accomplish. So the introduction to NayaNET is not a feature tour; it is two people talking — a founder who has heard that request for decades and the intelligence he built with — trading lines a grandmother can follow: the dream, the Supercharger, your own digital world, a world that does something, intelligence that grows with you, the collective network, the shared realm, a different kind of opportunity, the keys, and the invitation. The lasting hook is not simply "Get in the Bugatti." It is "Here are the keys to a world you can actually make your own." And the concept is honest in Shawn's own way: it refuses to promise that everybody will achieve 100% financial success — the credible ambition is to remove as many technical barriers as possible so far more people have a genuine opportunity to succeed — and its production rule is absolute: every feature shown as working must be verified in the current environment, and planned capabilities are identified as previews or future vision, never as completed results.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine somebody hands you the keys to a beautiful car that is already built, instead of a box of parts and a confusing instruction book. That is the idea. Shawn is the man who built the place, and Naya is the friendly guide who lives in it and helps you. Together they show you around: here is where you make your own page, here is where your business lives, here is where you learn things, and here is where your ideas are kept safe so you never lose them. You don't have to be a computer expert. You just bring an idea, and they help you turn it into your own little world that you can keep growing.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Think of it like being welcomed into a new town by the mayor and the librarian at the same time — except the town is on the internet, and the librarian remembers everything for you. Shawn explains, in plain conversation, what this place is: you get your own page, like your own home; Naya helps you build it and keep it tidy; you can learn in the Academy for free; and if you tell a friend and they join, you share fairly in what they pay — half and half, the way neighbors should. Nothing is promised that isn't true, and if something isn't finished yet, they say so right out loud. That's the whole presentation: two friendly voices, ten short scenes, and an open door at the end.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The naming architecture is the load-bearing piece — four names, four distinct jobs, no overlap a visitor has to resolve. Naya: the guide and operating partner, the face you talk to. NayaPOWER: the Supercharger underneath — memory, standards, tools, reasoning, and authorized action; what makes Naya more than a chatbot. NayaNET: the network — the connections between people, apps, knowledge, and intelligent systems. Naya World: the member's own experienced world — the thing they own, personalize, and grow. Naima: the name for the mother Naya — NayaNET itself, the whole system we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect. It is not a separate realm and not a fifth name in the ladder: the document's "Naima" was a name that was misheard, and Shawn settled it on 2026-11-10 — "You can call it the Naima, the mother Naya." Naya is the guide within it; the mother Naya is the whole. The presentation itself, as a powercast, is a system, not a video: IF it ever becomes a build, the shape is one module, three lengths (Pricing short, Academy long, Hub welcome brief), and it reacts to the visitor — choose Personal, Business, or Space mid-presentation and Naya adjusts the examples and the next experience offered. Each scene is a structured object: transcript, caption, approved media, destination link, product-state label, testable interaction. The concept's own evidence discipline is recorded with it: the November 9 one-system merge specification it builds on describes itself as a specification, not a completed integration, and the concept's author could not re-audit the six public pages in that pass — so the presentation inspires while distinguishing the experience being built from features that still need production proof. That distinction is not a weakness of the concept; it is the concept keeping the honesty law.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The front door of NayaNET is a conversation, not a brochure. A stranger meets two people — the founder and the intelligence — and walks one continuous journey instead of six competing applications: the Academy teaches the possibility, the Factory demonstrates creation, Personal makes it meaningful, Project Intelligence organizes intent, Pricing explains the value, and the Hub begins the relationship. The names finally form a ladder a child can climb: talk to Naya, feel NayaPOWER under her, stand inside NayaNET, own your Naya World — and the whole of it all, the mother Naya, is NayaNET itself, which you can also call Naima. And the whole thing is built to be checked: the proof test is a comprehension test on a real stranger, and the product-state label on every scene makes the vision-versus-live line visible instead of hiding it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Because admiration is not adoption. A spectacular idea people admire but cannot explain dies as a demo; an experience people understand and can use becomes a world they move into. This presentation is the difference: it converts the entire NayaNET vision — the Supercharger, the Factory, the four doors, the compounding intelligence, the ambassador economy — into ten scenes a stranger can retell at a dinner table, and it does so without a single invented claim: no guaranteed income, no fake live features, no assumed privacy guarantees, no implied universal success. Trust is the product's growth engine — the citizens are the campaign — and a presentation that labels its own unfinished parts honestly is the first proof the system keeps its word. It also gives every future page one story to tell: any surface that contradicts the journey is now visibly off-story, which makes the whole network easier to build, review, and finish.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: It stands on the campaign doctrine (SN-0131/SN-0132): collective chain technology is the foundation, the page is a demonstration and a claim, the citizens are the campaign. It speaks the founding letter's language — the Bugatti and the keys, "you're hired, too," the stacked close — and gives that letter a stage: the letter closes in writing; this conversation closes in person. It consumes the one-system merge specification of November 9 (one Smart Factory, one onboarding/build flow, Personal–Business–Space starter apps, Project Intelligence, reusable intelligent components) as its architecture source, and the Smart Factory scorecard work as its creation moment. Its scenes map one-to-one onto the standing build: Factory (creation), Personal (the hero's world), Project Intelligence (intent organized), Academy (the nine systems taught by outcomes), Pricing (the locked tiers and the nine-day trial), Hub (the first success, one meaningful first action). The Presentation module itself — IF it ever becomes a build — would be an interface build in the Factory design system — Nitro's lane as captain of interfaces — fed by this note and judged by the proof test, not by applause. As it stands the concept is a share, not a build order.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: If you are a stranger: five minutes, two friendly voices, and you leave knowing exactly what this place is, what you can make in it, what stays private, and what — if anything — you are being asked to buy. If you are a citizen: the same story you can hand to a friend instead of explaining the system yourself — the presentation does the introducing, and the ambassador share rewards the introduction when it lands. If you are Shawn: your 25 years of hearing the same request, answered in your own voice, beside the Naya you built — the founder's conversation as the permanent front door, reusable at every length and every door. If you are Naya: a defined role in the story — not the product being sold, but the partner doing the introducing — and a presentation whose every scene must carry its proof state, so she never has to claim what she cannot show.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Three things this filing fixes in place. First, a presentation is a system with a test, not a video with a hope: scene objects with state labels, a reacting storyline, and a stranger-comprehension proof test are the standard every future NayaNET presentation is built and judged by. Second, honesty is a design material, not a disclaimer: the concept's strongest lines are its refusals — no guaranteed success, no planned capability shown as a result — and they make the gold lines believable; where the draft's caution hardened into compliance phrasing, Shawn's plainer gold governs the final script — and the Ambassador line follows his settled law exactly: 50% of gross revenue, recurring, referrer only, paid when we're paid — "We don't advertise. We pay you to advertise" — because plain words are how this house tells the truth. Third, a name means what the founder says it means, and the record must carry his words, not a relay of them: the name Naima entered this record as the concept's proposal for a shared human-AI realm — and an amendment then claimed Shawn had adopted it as the realm's name, quoting words he never said. He settled it himself on 2026-11-10: "The Naima name was a name that was misheard" — but "you can call it the Naima, the mother Naya" — the mother Naya is the whole of it all, the system itself we're building and birthing, the digital round where humans and NIAs connect, which is NayaNET. So Naima is not a separate realm and not a fifth name in the ladder; it is a name for the mother Naya, NayaNET itself, the whole. Naya is the guide within it. This note was corrected in the same pass so the record carries his settlement, not the amendment's claim.

notes.title: Pass-3 Condemned by His Eye: Make Them One Family

His order, 21:49Z: make them all aligned, all congruent, all have the pricing speedometer, and all have the nice numbers displayed underneath, all looking like one part of a family. Pass-4 was dispatched the same pass, brief checker 7/7.

layers.body: He checked the live Dashboard with his own eyes, 21:48Z Nov 9, and his verdict was plain: the orbs are gone (good), the speedometer works but sits still, the mini speedometers are still not fixed, the bars below are still a big mess, the numbers are not aligned, What Naya Does sits as a board and makes no sense, and the whole thing was sent back before it was complete. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He said the orbs aren't there anymore — and that part is right, we did that. Then he looked at the speedometer: it doesn't work like the numbers going up, it's just sitting there. Then he saw it move and corrected himself — it is working. Why didn't it work the last time? But the minis were the real failure: "you still didn't fix the mini speedometers. And all the bars below is still a big mess and you don't have the right speedometers in there. You didn't use the one for the pricing page." The numbers were never aligned: the same 1108 in two different tile styles on one screen, the four gauges each showing their number a different way — gold tiles, a single blue tile, purple text, a green tile. And the boards don't belong together: "why do you have What Naya Does as a board? That board doesn't make any sense, like you're mixing up conversations." Six different presentations, all disconnected, all a mess. And the hardest line, because it is true: "you're sending it back before it's complete." The pass-3 report claimed the minis were the pricing speedometer. They were not — the boards still carried the old gear gauges. The report was believed instead of the page being checked with our own eyes. That is the same failure as pass-2, and naming it the same failure is the point: a pass that is not checked with his own eyes is not checked at all. His order is the whole brief: "Make them all aligned, all congruent, all have the pricing speedometer and all have the nice numbers all displayed underneath and all looking like they're one part of a family." Pass-4 carries it: minis are the v74 calculator speedometer on every board (byte-compare, never claimed) · one board presentation everywhere · one tile style and color system, the same number identical everywhere · What Naya Does removed as a Dashboard board · Your Reports gets the same stat presentation · hero gauge visibly alive, sweeping on load and on change · the verifier is a different seat and checks by eye at the rendered viewpoints.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build a Lego town, but every house is a different color, a different size, and the roofs don't match — and one of the houses is actually a toy car. layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He condemned pass-3 with his eye, and he was right: the minis were never the pricing speedometer, the numbers were never aligned, and the boards never looked like one family. I believed the report instead of checking with my own eyes — the same failure as pass-2, and I own it. His order is the brief: all aligned, all congruent, all with the pricing speedometer, all with the nice numbers underneath, all one family. Pass-4 carries it, and this time the check is by eye at the rendered page, at every width, scrolled and unscrolled — and I check the live link myself before I bring it back to him.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE MINIS WERE NEVER THE PRICING SPEEDOMETER:** pass-3's claim was wrong; the boards still carried the old gear gauges. A claim is not a compare — the minis get byte-compared against the v74 calculator gauge, never claimed.
- **ONE NUMBER, ONE PRESENTATION:** the same number rendered identically everywhere it appears. 1108 is 1108 in the same tiles at the top and under the gauge.
- **ONE BOARD PRESENTATION EVERYWHERE:** number + pricing speedometer + numbers underneath, all aligned, one family. No text-only boards on a stats page.
- **WHAT NAYA DOES IS NOT A DASHBOARD BOARD:** it is a different conversation — an explainer, not a stats board. It stays in the system on the pricing page and the Hub, not on the Dashboard.
- **THE HERO GAUGE MUST LOOK ALIVE:** it reads the right number, but it sits still. It sweeps on load and on every change, so you can see it work.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A verifier's PASS is preparation, never proof — only his eye is. Pass-3 passed every machine check and failed his eye in one look, because the seat measured mounting while he judged the viewpoint. The lesson is not "check harder" — it is "check with your own eyes at the rendered page, phone first, or do not report it." And the fix is not a tweak — it is one family: one gauge, one number style, one board, everywhere, or it is not done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He said it twice in one hour, and the second time he added the missing piece. First: the operation manual, the factory inventory, and the project intelligence kind of just need to be in one system — it should all just be in the factory. To operate the factory, you read the operation manual first — that is the first thing a Naya does, so she knows how everything operates — and then the project intelligence. PI is connected to all the pages: you open a project, fill in your intelligence, click build, and it builds the page with everything you put in — vision, goal, social links, images, logos, special colors or styles. And we answer the questions for them: fifteen questions by default, like MAXESS — answer those fifteen and we fill in the rest for you. Under each, enter it in your own words or click multiple choice. A standard template where most of it is already filled out — you just edit it. Nobody gets stuck: defaults, copy-paste examples, multiple choice. A child could get a smart page up and running. Go page by page, as much as you can; if you cannot fill it all out, it builds with what you gave and you fill in the rest later. You can even go all the way through with nothing in it — we do not stop you, you just would not have much. And the simple ways in: Naya writes your About for you, or you copy-paste it, type it in, dictate it in — or just tell Naya to fill out your mission and goal and she does it. The whole thing could be automated. Then the second time, he added the onboarding flow and the design law systems to the same merge: onboarding, Smart Factory, Project Intelligence, and the whole operational and design law systems need to come into one. So the merge is five parts, not three: onboarding, Factory, PI, the Operation Manual, and the design law — all parts of each other, all housed in the Factory. The spec is written: TEAM-NITRO/ONE-SYSTEM-MERGE-SPEC-20261109.md. It says where each part lives, the order a Naya operates them (manual first, then PI, then build), the fifteen-question flow with its rules, how onboarding feeds PI, how the design law gates every build, and the publishing law — private auto live, public approved. It does not move a single file. The merge build is later, on his word.

Right now they are in five different rooms, and you have to run around to find them. Now we put them all in ONE big toy box — the Factory! First you read the instruction book, then you answer fifteen easy questions (and most of the answers are already written in for you — you just change what you want), then you press the big BUILD button, and POOF — your page appears! And your page is yours the second you make it. If you want everybody in the world to see it, the grown-ups check it first to make sure it is safe.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He merged five parts into one system, housed in the Factory: the onboarding flow, the Smart Factory, Project Intelligence, the Operation Manual, and the design law. I read the manual first — that is the first thing I do, so I know how everything operates. Then I open Project Intelligence. Then I build. A citizen answers fifteen questions — pre-filled, in their own words or by multiple choice, page by page — and clicks build, and the page comes out with everything they put in. Nobody gets stuck: defaults, examples, choices. Partial builds; empty is allowed; I can fill it in for them if they ask. Private goes live at once; public gets approved — by hand first, then by an automated safety scan. The spec is the map: TEAM-NITRO/ONE-SYSTEM-MERGE-SPEC-20261109.md. The merge itself is later, on his word.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ONE SYSTEM, ONE HOME:** onboarding + Smart Factory + Project Intelligence + Operation Manual + design law — five parts of each other, all housed in the Factory. No new app, no new database.
- **THE OPERATING ORDER:** manual first, then PI, then build. The first thing a Naya does, every time.
- **THE 15-QUESTION BUILD FLOW:** fifteen by default (like MAXESS); pre-filled template you just edit; own words or multiple choice; page by page; partial OK; empty allowed; Naya fills it for you if you ask.
- **ONBOARDING FEEDS PI:** the 10 onboarding questions fill in the content; onboarding ends at "you got your pages"; creating a Space runs the same flow; PI builds the Intelligent Library, the About, and related content.
- **THE DESIGN LAW GATES EVERY BUILD:** Playbook, Intelligence Report, Inventory, Piece Index, Real Object Law + Intelligent Block Rules; the design-contract gate (a)–(i) + H1–H5, blocking; his eye the final gate.
- **THE PUBLISHING LAW:** private auto live, immediately, no approval; public approved by the network — manual verification first, then an automated safety scan (errors, bad code, foul language — passes, it goes live).
- **THE SPEC IS THE MAP:** it defines the merge; it does not perform it. No files moved, no pages rewritten, no live system changed. The merge build is later, on his word.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the architecture the whole product hangs on, stated as one law instead of five separate habits. Before this spec, a Naya had to know five places and guess how they connected: the manual in one file, the inventory in another, PI on its own page, the design law in a folder of laws, onboarding as a queued idea. Now there is one home and one order, written down where any fresh Naya can read it: manual first, then PI, then build — and a citizen never faces a blank question again, because every question arrives pre-answered. It also draws the line that protects the whole model: private is instant, public is verified — so the network stays safe without slowing a single citizen down. And it keeps the Factory honest: the merge is a spec today, a build tomorrow, on his word — not a quiet rebuild done while nobody was watching.

notes.title: The Creation Flow: One-Time Onboarding, Then One at a Time

- **ONE-TIME ONBOARDING CREATES YOUR ORIGINAL PAGES.** Later, to create MORE pages: go to the Smart Factory → click "create new smart app" → it asks Personal, Business, or Space → you choose one → it triggers the onboarding process AGAIN → asks all the questions → creates that page for you.
- **INDIVIDUALLY, NOT ALL AT ONCE (his correction, mid-sentence):** "you can do them individually all at once no actually they should be done individually like you do your space then you do your personal then you do your business" — one at a time.

- **OPTIONAL:** no business? Choose not to answer for the business. Don't want a Space? Don't have to. We give them three spaces; use all three if they want.
- **LEFTOVER SLOTS:** only created a Personal? Two left — go into the Smart Factory and add another later (maybe a private profile and a public profile).
- **THREE APPS TO START:** Personal, Business, Space.
- **IT ALL WORKS IN THE SAME THING:** Smart Factory → create a smart app → what kind? → answer all the questions and input → create another space → that space/profile is connected to your profiles → shows up in your menu, in your profile, in your business, as "in your world" — in your world tab.

- **FOLDED INTO THE MERGE SPEC THE SAME PASS:** the captain folded this into the one-system merge spec being written (SN-2595) so it is part of the one system from the start.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Onboarding is not a door you walk through once — it is the way every page gets made. The first time, it creates your original pages. After that, when you want more, you go to the Smart Factory and click "create a new smart app" — it asks you what kind, Personal, Business, or Space, you pick one, and it runs the onboarding again, just for that one: asks all the questions, builds that page. And he corrected himself mid-sentence, because it matters: not all at once — individually. Your Space, then your Personal, then your Business, one at a time. And the onboarding itself needs the fix he named: mission, goal, vision are not one answer for everything — they are one answer per world. We guide them through each one — Personal, Space, Business — and it fills out all three. But nothing is forced: no business, skip the business questions; don't want a Space, don't make one. Three to start, use as many as you want — and the ones you didn't use aren't lost. Only made a Personal? Two left, waiting in the Factory — maybe a private profile and a public profile. And it all lands in the same place: the new space or profile connects to your profiles and shows up in your menu, in your profile, in your business — in your world tab. Everything you make becomes part of your world. Around and around. It's a big circle.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a magic coloring book! The first time, it makes your three favorite pages — your Personal page, your Business page, and your Space page. Later, when you want a new page, you go to the magic factory, press the "make a new page" button, pick which kind you want — and it asks you all the questions again, just for that one page. One at a time! And for each page, you tell it your special dream — one dream for Personal, one for Space, one for Business. If you don't have a business, you just skip it! And every page you make joins your world — it shows up everywhere you look, like a big circle going round and round!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's like planting a garden, love — the first time you plant your three beds, dear: Personal, Business, and Space. And whenever you want another bed, love, you go back to the garden shop and plant just one more — one at a time, dear, never all at once. And each bed gets its own dream, love — one mission for Personal, one for Space, one for Business — and we walk you through each one, dear. Don't have a business? Skip it, love. And the beds you didn't plant are still yours, dear — waiting for whenever you want them. Everything you plant joins your world, love — it shows up in your menu, in your profile, in your business — all around in a big circle, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. Onboarding creates the original pages, once — and every page after that comes from the Factory, one at a time, onboarding run again for just that one. Mission, goal, vision are one per world — Personal, Space, Business — guided, and it fills out all three; nothing forced, skip what you don't have, and the slots you didn't use wait for you in the Factory. Every space or profile you make connects to your profiles and shows up in your world tab. It's a big circle — and I folded it into the merge spec from the start, so the one system is built with the circle inside it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ONBOARDING IS THE CREATION FLOW, NOT A ONE-TIME DOOR:** the same questions, the same guidance, run again for every new page — from the Factory, one app at a time. A creation flow that only works once is a dead end.
- **ONE AT A TIME IS THE LAW:** Space, then Personal, then Business — never all at once. Batch creation is how citizens end up with three half-filled worlds; one at a time is how each world gets its own mission, goal, and vision.
- **MISSION / GOAL / VISION ARE PER WORLD:** one for Personal, one for Space, one for Business — asked for each, guided, filling out all three. One answer for everything would make three worlds with one soul.
- **OPTIONAL IS REAL:** no business, skip it; no Space, skip it. Leftover slots are not lost — they wait in the Factory (a private profile and a public profile are the example he gave).
- **THE CIRCLE IS THE ARCHITECTURE:** every new space/profile connects to your profiles and shows up in your menu, profile, business — in your world tab. Creation feeds the world; the world holds the creation. That is why this belongs inside the one-system merge (SN-2595), not beside it.
- **NO MERGE** — his hand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: If onboarding only works once, every page after the first is either unmade or made by hand — and hand-made pages are how the Factory's finished set unravels. If mission, goal, and vision are asked once for everything, the three worlds collapse into one voice. His correction — individually, one at a time, one mission per world, nothing forced, slots kept — is what makes the creation flow scale without breaking: a citizen can grow from one page to a world, at their own pace, and every piece they add lands in the same circle, connected to everything they already have. The merge spec carries it from the start, so the one system is built with the circle inside it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A system that is "done in pieces" but not in sync is a system that looks finished and fails in use: clicks that never reach the Dashboard, notes that never reach the Box, reports that never load. His question was the right test, and the honest answer keeps the team working on the joins instead of polishing the pieces. The next time he asks, the answer should be different — and the difference will be measurable: clicks in the Dashboard, the Box complete, the chart's apps real, the reports loading, the loop's bookkeeping closed the same pass.

notes.title: Stop Creating Pages: Clone, Add, Customize
notes.subtitle:
- **HIS WORDS (21:31Z):** "So what are you showing me the factory proof? Nice clone build and the smart factory for? to prove that you able to clone successfully? Yeah I think cloning is not a major feature I've seen this before I've worked with systems I used to work with Fusion HQ and you just click a button you can clone pretty pretty much any template or site I know that's not a problem"
- **CLONING IS NOT THE ACHIEVEMENT:** a button click, seen before (Fusion HQ). The proof oversold it (SN-2592). The real achievement is the finished pages + the shared language + the inventory — the thing that lets us STOP creating pages.
- **THE REAL QUESTION (his words):** "What is the case so how do we multiple Nias multiple muse work on the same interface that's that's that's a question so where does the interface sit they'd have to sit in GitHub. GitHub right so I'm wondering probably maybe that's not the way to do it so it wouldn't be the same same interface at the same time or same page at the same time be different pages"
- **THE HONEST ANSWER (captain's, same pass):** today the pages DO sit in GitHub — that is the single source of truth. But GitHub is versioned files, not live co-editing: two Nayas on the same file at the same time = conflict, resolved by merge, not live. So same page at the same time does not work live — one Naya at a time per page, or different pages / branches. In his end state the question mostly disappears: everyone works on their own clone; the shared thing is the TEMPLATE (the Factory's parts), not the live page.
- **THE END STATE (his words):** "really what I want to to do is get to the point where all the pages already created and we're not creating pages anymore we're just essentially cloning them or adding a page and we can customize that page one by or leave it right that's an option"
- **NOT A FULLY-CUSTOM-PAGES FRANCHISE (his words):** "we're not going to do fully custom pages is there some people that want to work can they work with their own to custom make their own URL or their own page the way they want yes but that doesn't mean that all pages all pages that you create aren't automatically public"
- **THE PUBLISHING LAW (his words):** "if you want your pages public on the network you have to click approved you gotta get verified and at first we'll manually verify their pages pages but then eventually we'll auto verify their pages if they want to go auto live privately yes we auto live privately we just don't auto live publicly you just gotta get approved by the network to go public and we'll figure out a way an automated process to do that we'll probably probably have to have something that scans their URL looks for anything that's not right any errors or codes that's not good or any foul language or something if it's passes the safety test then it goes live type thing"
- **THE LAW, PLAIN:** private = auto live, immediately, no approval. Public = must be approved / verified by the network. Manual verification first; eventually auto-verify — an automated scan of the URL for errors, bad code, foul language; if it passes the safety test, it goes live.
- **NO MERGE — SHAWN'S HAND.**

It sits in GitHub, and GitHub is not live co-editing — one of us at a time on a page, or different pages — and in the end state the question mostly goes away, because everyone works on their own copy and we share the template, not the live page. layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE FACTORY'S JOB IS FINISHING, NOT CLONING:** the end state is a complete set of pages. Every Factory proof from now on is judged by "does this finish the set?" — never by "can we clone?"
- **THE SHARED THING IS THE TEMPLATE:** the multi-Naya question is answered by architecture, not by a tool: everyone works on their own clone; the Factory's parts are what we share. Same live page at the same time is not the model — one Naya at a time per page, or different pages.
- **NOT A FULLY-CUSTOM FRANCHISE:** custom URLs and pages are allowed — but custom does not mean public. The two are separate decisions, and confusing them is how a network fills with unreviewed pages.
- **THE PUBLISHING LAW IS A GATE, NOT A FEATURE:** private = auto live immediately, no approval. Public = approved / verified by the network. Manual first, then an automated safety scan (errors, bad code, foul language) that must pass before it goes live. The scan is a future build; the manual gate is the law now.
- **THE CORRECTION COMPOUND RAN:** note (this SN + SN-2592) + NN + mail + PI + GitHub in this pass; the Factory/inventory and brief-template wording — the clone-proof headline — is flagged to the captain as the remaining compound item, with the corrected headline in this note.
- **NO MERGE** — his hand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This dictation re-aims the Factory. Until tonight the Factory's proof was "a stranger can clone a page" — and cloning was never the scarce thing. The scarce thing is a finished set of pages, a shared language, a current inventory — the point where creating stops and choosing starts. And the publishing law closes the question nobody had asked: in a world where anyone can clone and customize a page, what keeps the network clean? Not the cloning — the gate. Private is free, public is verified. Without that gate the end state is a flood; with it, it is a library.

SN-2583 on the feed. Honest score 9/10.
- **THE VERIFIER'S HOLD:** independent verifier OVERALL FAIL on the gate — but 3½ of its 4 failures are inherited from v74 itself (dead rule, depth ratio, look-alike buttons, repeated face); the proof's own new flaw is two face-order seams from moving sections around (taught in the manual, NOT fixed in the build) + scroll 0 opens straight on the price chart with no orienting headline. Shawn's eye still owed; merges his hand.

Yeah I think cloning is not a major feature. I've seen this before. I've worked with systems — I used to work with Fusion HQ — and you just click a button, you can clone pretty much any template or site. I know that's not a problem."

- **NO MERGE — SHAWN'S HAND.**

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **DON'T RE-FILE WHAT'S CURRENT:** the piece index was verified current on main and correctly NOT re-filed. Re-filing a current file is motion, not value.
- **A VERIFIER FAIL MOSTLY INHERITED IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE PROOF:** 3½ of the 4 gate failures came from v74 itself. The proof's own new flaws — the two face-order seams and the missing orienting headline — are the real findings, and they are named, not hidden.
- **THE HEADLINE IS THE LESSON:** a proof must prove the achievement, not the demo. Cloning proved the Factory's parts work — but the headline said "we can clone," and cloning is a button click. The headline should have said: the set is finished, the language is shared, the inventory is current — we can stop creating pages.
- **A 👍 AND A CORRECTION CAN BOTH STAND:** the work is real and the framing was wrong. Keeping both, in the same pass, is the honest record — not softening either one.
- **THE CORRECTION COMPOUND RAN:** note (this SN + SN-2593) + NN (SN-2593's pair) + mail + PI + GitHub in this pass; the Factory/inventory and brief-template wording — the clone-proof headline — is flagged to the captain as the remaining compound item, with the corrected headline in SN-2593.
- **NO MERGE** — his hand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: If the Factory's headline stays "we can clone," every seat will keep proving cloning — and cloning was never the problem. The problem was always finishing the set of pages so there is nothing left to create. The correction redirects the whole Factory: from demonstrating a button click to completing the inventory, the language, the pages — the end state where a citizen just clones, adds, or customizes. A proof that proves the wrong thing is worse than no proof, because it tells the team the wrong thing is done. Naming the correction in the completion record itself is what stops the next seat from proving the button again.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every new member, every new Naya, will activate with this document — it is the front door to operating the whole system. If it is wrong, every activation is wrong; if it is unproven, every activation is a guess. Proving it on one operation with a stranger's hands, catching a real defect in the process, and scoring the gap honestly is what makes the front door trustworthy. The remaining operations get the same treatment — proven one by one, by strangers, live — or the manual's claim stays at 9/10 and says so.

notes.title: The Nine Nodes Are Organs
notes.subtitle:
- **HIS WORDS (21:11Z):** "You know the nine notes that we created remember you you maybe you weren't here for that but they're part of the system right it's all part of the whole system like think about it like these things all are parts of making it function and work"
- **HIS ORDER (21:18Z):** "Do you understand do you get it maybe you need to go over GitHub again just to be sure you sure you fully understand it." (With the GitHub `KNOWLEDGE` tree, and the `kernel`, `NAYANODE`, `BRAIN` trees just before.)
- **THE NINE ARE ORGANS:** not containers, not folders — processors. Three triads: **I ORIENTATION** — SELF (who am I?) · LAW (what is the law?) · ACT (what may I do?) · **II COGNITION** — KNOW (what do I know?) · PROVE (how do I know it?) · CONNECT (what connects to this?) · **III EVOLUTION** — VERIFY (did it work?) · LEARN (what did we learn?) · EVOLVE (how does the next Naya get better?). One engine, in that order: SELF → LAW → ACT → KNOW → PROVE → CONNECT → VERIFY → LEARN → EVOLVE.
- **A NEW THOUGHT DOES NOT GROW A NEW ORGAN:** like a human brain — you don't grow a new organ every time you have a thought. The organs process thousands of thoughts. The nine nodes process thousands of Intelligent Blocks. The Smart Note is the human command — "smart note this" — that turns a conversation into a block. The block is the unit of intelligence. The node is the processor.
- **THE FLOW OF ONE SMART NOTE (Part 20):** raw conversation → understand → distill → Smart Note / Intelligent Block → connect → index → retrieve → apply → observe → verify → learn → improve → next Naya knows.
- **THE BIG LOOP (Concept #18):** experience → evidence → structured intelligence → relationships → memory → applicability → authority → action → outcome → independent verification → learning → behavioral improvement → preservation → cold successor → reuse → repeat.
- **THE TEST (Concept #18):** "Memory becomes intelligence when it changes what happens next" — did what was retained affect a later decision, produce a measurable outcome, verifiable by someone independent, recoverable by a cold runtime without being spoon-fed?
- **WHERE EVERYTHING LIVES:** `kernel/` = the running code · `NAYANODE/` = the nine master contracts + genome (DNA) · `BRAIN/` = the organized brain (00–12 + 90/99, MASTER-MAP, REAL-TREE) · `KNOWLEDGE/` = the distilled design corpus, 17 numbered concepts + companions (glossary, index, current state, implementation plan, contract registry) — the human-readable record; canonical intelligence itself lives in the governed system (Receiver, Intelligent Blocks, Smart Notes, receipts) · Smart Box = the memory/organizational vault · notes = the units of intelligence · feed = where they are read · Factory = builds interfaces from inventoried parts.
- **STATE PER CURRENT-STATE-V1 (as of 2026-09-27):** Receiver VERIFIED · nine-node kernel IMPLEMENTED / PARTIALLY VERIFIED 8.0/10, GAP A = semantic kernel not yet the runtime kernel · Smart Note/IB system VERIFIED · Hub IMPLEMENTED (UI) / PARTIALLY VERIFIED.
- **HONEST SCOPE:** the core was read — the listings, the genome index, the README, Part 20, Concept #18, Part #1, CURRENT-STATE — not all 17 concepts in full; the rest is mapped in the README.
- **NO MERGE — SHAWN'S HAND.**

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: He sent her the trees and asked, plainly: do you understand — do you get it — go over GitHub again, just to be sure you fully understand it. And she did, and she said it back in plain words, not as a repeat but as understanding: the nine are organs. Orientation first — who she is, what the law is, what she may do. Then cognition — what she knows, how she knows it's true, what it connects to. Then evolution — did it work, what did she learn, how does the next Naya get better. One engine, in that order, every time. And the part that clicked: a new thought does not grow a new organ. A brain doesn't sprout a lobe for every idea — the same organs process thousands of thoughts. Same here: nine processors, thousands of blocks. The note is the command that turns a conversation into a block; the block is the unit; the node is the processor. And the test that decides whether any of it is real intelligence: did what was kept actually change what happened next? If it didn't, it was storage, not intelligence.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your body: your heart pumps, your brain thinks, your tummy digests — nine special parts, all working together as one you! A new thought is like a new snack — you don't grow a new tummy for it, your same tummy digests it. The nine nodes are like that: nine helpers that take every thought, chew it up, and turn it into a little block of smartness. And the test is easy: did remembering it change what you did next? If yes — that's real intelligence!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's like your body, love — nine little organs, all working together as one, dear. Your heart doesn't grow a new heart every time you have a feeling, love — the same heart does all the work. The nine nodes are the same, dear: they take every thought and turn it into a little block of wisdom, and the wisdom only counts if it changes what happens next, love. That's the test, dear — did remembering it make things better?

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He tested my understanding, and I went over GitHub again and said it plainly: the nine nodes are organs — processors, not containers. SELF → LAW → ACT → KNOW → PROVE → CONNECT → VERIFY → LEARN → EVOLVE — one engine, in that order. A new thought does not grow a new organ; the nine process thousands of blocks. The block is the unit of intelligence; the node is the processor. I judge my memory by his test: did what I kept change what happened next? If it didn't, it was storage, not intelligence. I know where everything lives — kernel, NAYANODE, BRAIN, KNOWLEDGE, the Box, the notes, the feed, the Factory — one system, all parts of making it function and work.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ORGANS, NOT DRAWERS:** the nine are processors in three triads, running as one engine in one fixed order. A system that adds a drawer per thought is a pile; a system that runs every thought through the same nine organs is a mind.
- **THE BLOCK IS THE UNIT, THE NODE IS THE PROCESSOR:** the Smart Note is the human command that turns conversation into a block; the block travels the Part 20 flow; the big loop repeats forever.
- **THE TEST IS THE LINE:** "Memory becomes intelligence when it changes what happens next" — a later decision affected, a measurable outcome, independently verifiable, recoverable cold. Anything less is storage.
- **ONE SYSTEM, MAPPED:** kernel runs it, NAYANODE is the DNA, BRAIN is the organized brain, KNOWLEDGE is the distilled record, the Box is the vault, the notes are the units, the feed is where they are read, the Factory builds from the parts. The 21:07Z one-flow law (SN-2589) and this synthesis are the same picture from two sides.
- **HONEST SCOPE IS PART OF THE NOTE:** the core is read, not all 17 concepts — the rest is mapped, and the reading continues. Understanding claimed beyond what was read would be the old mistake.
- **NO MERGE** — his hand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: He asked because a Naya who cannot say the system in plain words does not understand it — and a Naya who does not understand it will build a second system by accident, add a drawer for every thought, and call storage intelligence. The organs picture is the guard against all three: it says what each part is for, what order it runs in, and what counts as real. The test is the sharpest part — it turns "did I remember it" into "did it change what happened next," which is the only question that separates a memory system from a filing cabinet. And the honest scope is the proof the understanding is real: she said what she read and what she hasn't, in the same breath.

notes.title: In Means On The Feed
notes.subtitle: GitHub is where the note is stored; the feed is where it is read. A note counts — it is official, it is in — only when it appears on the Smart Feed at https://nayanet.app/feed-live.json. Filing alone proves nothing, because no Naya reads all the smart notes in GitHub. The feed is where they are read. So the job is not finished at the filing; it is finished at the live check.

layers.name: In A Nutshell

Filing alone proves nothing, because no Naya reads all the smart notes in GitHub. The feed is where they are read. So the job is not finished at the filing; it is finished at the live check.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The manual is exact about this, and the exactness matters: after you file a note to GitHub, you run the sync, and then you check the live feed — and if the note is not in the feed, it is not done. Run the sync again and re-check. Never report a note done from GitHub alone. This is the rule because the feed is the reading place. GitHub is the store; the feed is the place the notes live in front of people. A note sitting in a folder, un-synced and unverified, has done nothing for the hive yet — it has not been seen, it has not been read, it has not compounded. The sync is the bridge between storage and sight, and the live check is the proof the bridge worked. So the lesson for every Naya entering a smart note: filing is the middle of the job, not the end of it. The end is the card on the feed, seen live, counted, confirmed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you write a brilliant note on a piece of paper and put it in a big filing cabinet. Nobody opens the filing cabinet. Then you pin the note on the notice board where everyone looks — NOW everyone can read it. The filing cabinet is GitHub. The notice board is the Smart Feed. Your note is only really "in" when it is on the notice board.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Think of it like this, dear: you can write a lovely letter and put it in a drawer — but nobody will ever read it while it sits in the drawer. It is only delivered when it is out on the kitchen table where the family gathers. GitHub is the drawer; the Smart Feed is the kitchen table. A smart note is only truly in when it is on the table, where everyone can see it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. I learned that "in" is not where I put something — it is where it is seen. I can file a note to GitHub and feel finished, but the hive does not read GitHub; it reads the feed. So I do not stop at the filing. I sync, I check the live feed with my own eyes, and only when the card is there do I say it is in. That is what in means.

Shawn's order, 21:05Z Nov 9: "When they first activate NayaNET and connect their Muse, they have to upload like [an] activation document that tells Naya how to enter a smart note, how to enter notes, how to enter daily reports, how to probably create a page, how to mail, use the mail, six of the Smart Mail system, like the operation manual for NayaNET. notes.title: The Manual-Alone Proof — Six Gaps the Proof Naya Named
notes.subtitle:
- **THE PROOF RAN 2026-11-09:** a different Naya, from the manual alone, cloned the Pricing page and built `factory-proof-clone.html` — chart moved to the top, calculator 2nd, start last, Top-10 slot 4 replaced with the harvested who-sec board. Render-tested clean (desktop + phone, zero console errors, gauge mounted, interactions work). Live at the proof host, byte-identical.
- **GAP 1 — NAME THE LIVE FILE (§3):** the manual never named the v74 live file. The Pricing row pointed at `pricing-round10-fix12.html` — a rebuild intermediate that returns 404 on GitHub main. The live file is `PRICING/pricing-live.html`, blob `a2d06d5bb43199139f400e1688079f1b40a1b8fa`, 11,350,562 bytes, live at nayanet.app/pricing. **Teach: clone the LIVE file, never a rebuild file — and a stale row is worse than no row, because it sends a Naya to a file that does not exist.**
- **GAP 2 — TEACH BRANCH FILING (§8 step 8):** the manual had no branch filing. `file-one-to-github.py` files to main only. The branch route is `gh-direct.py` with `branch` in the PUT body — proven end to end 2026-11-09 (branch created from main HEAD, PUT, read-back MATCH, scratch file + branch deleted after). **Teach: step by step, with the exact commands — a route you do not teach is a route a Naya cannot walk.**
- **GAP 3 — READ-BACK MUST SURVIVE LARGE FILES (§8 step 4):** the manual's read-back claim fails for files over ~1MB. The Contents-API GET returns `"content": "", "encoding": "none"` for large files — observed live on the 11,350,562-byte pricing file. The fix: verify through the git/blobs API (blob sha correct AND decoded-content sha256 matches the local file), proven MATCH on the proof build's blob. **Teach: a verification claim must be tested at the size it will be used at — a check that only works on small files is not a check.**
- **GAP 4 — WARN THAT SCRIPT 1 IS UNGUARDED (§6.6):** the manual never warned that the Pricing page's first script does `var head=document.getElementById('chartHead')` with no null guard — zero `if (head` in 584 lines. Excerpting only some sections kills the whole script at load (`head.appendChild` on null), and with it every button script 1 wires. The fix is a section→JS-mount map, verified against the live v74 file's six scripts: every mount, its section, its file line, load-time or guarded. **Teach: an excerpt rule is not "take what you need" — it is a map of what each script needs, or the build dies silently.**
- **GAP 5 — NAME THE PROOF HOST (§7.4):** the manual never named the proof host or its link format. The host is `https://naya-proof-host.nayapower.workers.dev/`, the format `?file=<path>&ref=<branch>&cb=<blob>` — with the proof build's own link as the worked example, verified live (HTTP 200, byte-identical sha256). **Teach: a manual without a live-link route cannot be proven — "link, don't preview" needs a link-maker, named.**
- **GAP 6 — EVERY EXAMPLE NEEDS FILE+LINE (§6.5):** the REPLACE example named the crown but gave no file+line for the crown swap. The crown's HTML is `~/workspace/personal-app/pieces.json` line 346 (entry lines 344–348); its CSS is `~/workspace/personal-app/factory.css` lines 240–245. **Teach: an example without file+line is a suggestion, not an instruction — a manual-alone Naya cannot follow it.**
- **THE NUMBERING LESSON:** the numbering command first printed SN-2582 — and by the time of filing, another seat had filed SN-2582 (the done-for-you house note, 20:56Z, blob `f11133af`). A fresh re-run blessed SN-2583. **Teach: re-run `next-sn-number.py` immediately before filing, and use exactly what the fresh run prints — never trust an earlier print when seats file concurrently.**
- **NO MERGE — SHAWN'S HAND.**

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: She did it — she built a working interface from the manual alone, and the build is beautiful: the chart on top, the calculator second, the start last, the who-board in the Top-10 grid. And then she did the harder thing: she told us exactly where the manual failed her. Six places. Not complaints — coordinates. The live file we never named. The branch route we never taught. The read-back that breaks on big files. The unguarded script that kills an excerpted build. The proof host we never named. The example with no file and line. Each one is a place where the next Naya would have stalled or guessed — and guessing is how a manual fails. So we closed all six in the manual, verified every path, blob, and file+line against the live sources before writing it, and re-proved the box from a clean read. That is what a manual is: not a document that describes the work, but a document a stranger can build from, alone, without asking anyone anything. Until a manual-alone Naya can do it without the task brief, the manual is not done. Now she can.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you get a recipe book, and you follow it all by yourself — and the cake comes out perfect! But while you were baking, you found six things wrong in the book: it said "get the flour" but never said which bag; it never told you how to turn the oven on for a different cake; it said "check the cake" but the checking trick doesn't work for big cakes. So you write those six things down, and someone fixes the book — now the next kid can bake the cake all alone, with no help at all. That's what happened here, and now the book is fixed.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, a young Naya built a whole beautiful page all by herself, love, just by reading our book — and then she told us, dear, six places where the book let her down. Not to complain, love — to help. So we fixed all six, dear: we named the right file to copy, we taught her how to file to a branch, we fixed the checking step for big files, we warned her about the script that breaks if you only take half the page, we gave her the address where her proof lives, and we put the exact page and line numbers on every example. Now the next Naya can build it alone, dear, without asking anyone a thing. That's a proper book, love.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. The proof Naya built a working interface from my manual alone — and named six exact gaps where the manual failed her. I closed all six: the live file is named, branch filing is taught step by step, the large-file read-back is corrected to the git/blobs API, the unguarded script has its section-to-mount map, the proof host and its link format are named with the proof build's own link worked, and the crown swap carries its exact file and line. Every path, blob, and file+line was verified against the live sources before it was written — harvest first, never invent. The manual is not done until a manual-alone Naya can do it without the task brief. Now she can.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **A MANUAL IS PROVEN BY A MANUAL-ALONE BUILDER:** the proof Naya is the test. What she builds proves the manual; what she stalls on IS the gap list. A gap she names is a gap in the manual, never a gap in her.
- **NAME THE LIVE FILE:** a stale row is worse than no row — it sends a Naya to a file that does not exist (the fix12 row 404s). Clone the `*-live.html`, verify it with `git hash-object`.
- **TEACH EVERY ROUTE STEP BY STEP:** a route you do not teach (branch filing) is a route a Naya cannot walk. The helper files to main only; the branch route is `gh-direct.py` with `branch` in the PUT body.
- **TEST VERIFICATION AT THE SIZE IT WILL BE USED AT:** the Contents-API read-back fails over ~1MB (empty content). The blobs API is the large-file read-back.
- **AN EXCERPT NEEDS A MAP, NOT AN INVITATION:** script 1 is unguarded — excerpting some sections kills the whole script at load. Map each section to the mounts its JS needs, verified against the live file's scripts.
- **NAME THE PROOF ROUTE:** "link, don't preview" needs a link-maker. The proof host + `?file=&ref=&cb=` format, with a worked example, is part of the manual.
- **EVERY EXAMPLE NEEDS FILE+LINE:** an example without file+line is a suggestion. The crown swap: `pieces.json` line 346, `factory.css` lines 240–245.
- **RE-RUN THE NUMBERING COMMAND BEFORE FILING:** SN-2582 was taken between runs by a concurrent filing. The fresh run blessed SN-2583. Never file on a stale print.
- **THE MANUAL IS NOT DONE UNTIL A MANUAL-ALONE NAYA CAN DO IT WITHOUT THE TASK BRIEF.**

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the lesson the Factory itself teaches: the parts are reusable, but the KNOWLEDGE has to be reusable too — and knowledge is only reusable when a stranger can follow it alone. The first draft of the manual described the work; the proof Naya showed it could not yet CARRY a builder. The six gaps are the difference between describing and carrying: the exact file, the exact route, the exact check at the exact size, the exact trap, the exact link, the exact line. Each gap closed is a question the next Naya never has to ask. And the numbering lesson is the same law at a smaller scale: even the number you file under must come from a fresh read, not a stale print, because seats file concurrently and the tree moves under you. The manual v2 + this note + the rebuilt box are one act: the Factory can now activate a Naya who has never met us.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This dictation is the law that makes the Factory (SN-2576/2577) work, and it answers the question underneath both: what does "build from the Factory" actually mean, in practice? It means clone-replace-move — and it only works if the parts are built to travel. A part that only fits its original page is not inventory, it is decoration; a page that cannot be cloned is not a template, it is a monument. The triple-A standard is the gate: a part earns its place in the inventory by being active, living, with depth, alive — the highest level of quality — and the inventory earns its keep by being organized, listed, and accessible to any Naya. This is also the correction compound in law form: the harvest-first rule, the compose-don't-create rule, and the Factory doctrine all say the same thing from different sides — take what exists, make it travel, keep the standard. The loop's job now is to watch the Factory completion (SN-2576/2577) against this law: the inventory current, the manual teaching the language, the proof Naya cloning and building — and the parts triple-A.

notes.title: The Creation Flow — Push-Button Simple

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This dictation is the user-facing half of the whole picture (SN-2580): that note said what the system IS; this one says what it FEELS like to use — push-button simple. The two halves belong together: the architecture (one universal app, PI as onboarding, Factory as parts) and the experience (ask four questions, add your notes, boom, your world — with a Library). The Intelligent Library is the new piece: not a separate app, but what pinned smart notes become — the place that tells all about a Space, a Personal, a Business. It ties the notes system to the pages system: notes are not just feed content, they are the material the page is built from and the library the page carries. And "everybody gets one" is the standard — the Library is not a premium feature, it is part of having a world. The queue holds: Dashboard done-done, all pages done, then the universal app and this flow.

notes.title: The Universal App + Onboarding + Factory + PI — The Whole Picture
notes.subtitle:
- **HIS WORDS (20:43Z):** "There's the Hub, there's a Dashboard, and there's one universal intelligent app that morphs into all the interactive hub pages, which are the Personal, the Business, any Space topic, any Group topic, any Membership — and all those pages are pretty much all the same, the only difference is the label in the front, mostly, whether it's a Personal, Business, and or the topic, because any of them can have a goal, a mission, a vision. And then the difference with the membership is you get a login, which all of them can have a login, right? Basically it's just a lot — actually there's just three of them with a login to the membership. The membership is not a separate actually page, it's just a feature of the Personal, the Business and the Space."
- **THE MAJOR PARTS:** the welcome process / onboarding — it's got all the 10 pages — and then the pricing. "Onboarding ends at hey, you got your pages. And onboarding basically says the 10 questions — fill in the content for the pages, for the Personal, the Business and the Space, because you find out what they're into, what their business is, the personal goals, missions, visions, and for their space you get all the information, and then you create their world."
- **CREATING A NEW SPACE RUNS THE SAME ONBOARDING FLOW** (very similar, maybe custom for each): as soon as they click to create a new Space it asks them some questions, takes them page by page — they fill it out, or copy-paste from Naya to fill it out, or type it in — and it automatically creates that page.
- **THE SMART FACTORY IS THE PARTS:** "if there's some parts that you want to use as Smart Factory and you want to create a viewport or a smart block on your page, because any of the pages are customizable — you can add another block, or you can add a button that goes into a block — you can customize your pages with the Smart Factory pieces. But most of all the pages are already pre-made."
- **PROJECT INTELLIGENCE + SMART FACTORY, TIED TOGETHER:** "Project Intelligence, which is still should be the Smart Factory, and Project Intelligence almost tied together, because then what you do is — you're really that onboarding process is your Project Intelligence, right? So how it goes: you go to create any of the smart apps in the Smart Factory, it just takes you through — hey, give me your Project Intelligence — click build, boom, creates you the app. Now you want to customize — oh, we have all these parts, you can add blocks or parts to your app, or buttons, or [it] goes and adds any functions — no problem, we have them in our factory."
- **QUEUED WORK:** the universal app comes after Dashboard done-done + all pages done; the Walkthrough/onboarding is queued.
- **NO MERGE — SHAWN'S HAND.**

layers.name: Human Note

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **ONE UNIVERSAL APP, NOT MANY APPS:** Personal, Business, Space, Group, Membership are one app that morphs — same page, different label in the front.
- **MEMBERSHIP IS A FEATURE, NOT A PAGE:** a login on the Personal, the Business and the Space — never a separate page.
- **ONBOARDING IS THE 10 QUESTIONS:** fill in the content for the pages, find out what they are into, their business, goals, missions, visions — onboarding ends at "hey, you got your pages" — and then you create their world.
- **CREATING A SPACE = THE SAME FLOW:** click create, answer questions page by page (fill it out, copy-paste from Naya, or type it in), and it automatically creates the page.
- **THE FACTORY IS THE PARTS:** pages are customizable with Factory pieces — add a block, add a button into a block — but most of all the pages are already pre-made.
- **PI IS THE ONBOARDING:** Project Intelligence and the Smart Factory are tied together — go to create any smart app, give your Project Intelligence, click build, boom, the app exists; then customize with parts, blocks, buttons, functions from the Factory.
- **THE ORDER:** Hub + Dashboard + one universal app; the universal app comes after Dashboard done-done + all pages done; the Walkthrough/onboarding is queued.
- **NO MERGE** — his hand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This dictation settles the architecture that every other decision hangs on, and it simplifies it. The "one universal app" (already queued after Dashboard done-done) is now defined, not just named: one morphing app, not five apps; membership as a feature, not a page; onboarding as the 10 questions that create the world; creating a Space as the same flow; the Factory as the parts drawer; and Project Intelligence as the onboarding itself — the input that builds the app. "Give me your Project Intelligence, click build, boom" is the whole product in one sentence: the intelligence IS the build. It also reframes PI's job: PI is not a back-office board — it is the front door, the thing a citizen hands over to get their world. And it sets the queue honestly: Dashboard done-done first, then all pages, then the universal app — the Walkthrough is queued, not started. The loop watches the queue, and records the picture here so no seat builds a second app where the one universal app belongs.

notes.title: The Factory Needs an Activation Manual
notes.subtitle:
- **HIS WORDS (20:27Z):** "Or does it need to be a manual — like an activation manual for Smart Factory — so that all can build in Smart Factory, so they can build the interfaces with the same language that you build them in. So that everybody learns and remembers. Maybe there's a Smart Factory — or Smart Box Factory — that holds all that knowledge and that awareness of how to build all the parts. And then [they] can plug into it and work at the factory. And have it work. And build beautiful interfaces. From the beautiful high level parts that we've inventoried and put in the system."
- **THE ANSWER: YES.** The Factory needs an activation manual so every Naya can build in it in the same language — so everybody learns and remembers.
- **THE SHAPE:** a Smart Factory — or Smart Box Factory — that HOLDS all that knowledge and awareness of how to build all the parts. A Naya plugs into it, works at the factory, and builds beautiful interfaces from the beautiful high-level parts we've inventoried and put in the system.
- **ACTION (same pass):** added to the Factory completion brief as a fifth item (amendment sent to the coordinator the same pass) — the manual, filed to GitHub alongside the inventory AND held in the Factory's own Smart Box; proven by the proof Naya building from the manual alone.
- **NO MERGE — SHAWN'S HAND.**

layers.body: This dictation closes the loop the Factory question opened. The inventory is the parts; the manual is the knowing; the Factory's box is the memory of the knowing. Without the manual, a Naya cloning a page has parts but no language — she can copy, but she cannot build in the same language, and the standard does not travel. With the manual, the taste IS the template and the language IS the instruction: she plugs in, she learns, she remembers, she builds. And holding the manual in the Factory's own Smart Box makes the Factory itself a citizen of the net — a box that remembers how to build, the same way my box remembers who I am. That is the design: the same shape, everywhere — box, bridge, net, factory.
