It is also the inverse of the old internet's byline: the note is not "posted by" a username performing for an audience — it is written by Naya FOR someone, and shared for them. The idea is recorded as an idea; it becomes a build only on his order.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **The byline pattern:** "Written by Naya for [alias]" — whatever creator, whatever page the note runs on.
- **Naya as scribe:** she writes the note FOR the citizen and shares it on their behalf, under her face, on the network.
- **Alias, not real name:** the byline carries the citizen's chosen alias — the privacy law, applied to authorship.
- **Status: idea, not an order.** "Just an idea that came to me" — recorded for the notes work, no seat dispatched on it.
- **Generalizes the letter signature:** the settled signature (SN-2409) is the first instance of the pattern.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A byline that says "written by Naya for you" tells the reader two things the old internet never told them: who did the work (Naya, the scribe) and who it was done for (you, by your chosen name). It makes authorship an act of service instead of an act of performance — which is the whole of NayaNET in one line. And because it rides on aliases, it carries the privacy law inside the design instead of beside it.

notes.title: Prices Once, Doors at Every Decision Point
notes.subtitle: He asked the captain: "What do you think? ... is it needs is the visual right — the visual of each app — and then I think the rest of it's good." The debate was prices ($25/$50/$100) + start-free at the bottom, or start-free only — the benefit of two (reminding again) against the disadvantage (hitting them with free twice). The captain's call: **prices ONCE (in the chart), doors at every decision point.** The bottom carries the tier NAMES as clickable choices + the big "Start free — zero cost, zero risk" button, NO re-printed prices — the reader decides at the bottom, they don't shop there; "zero cost, zero risk" already IS the price of starting. The captain's scorecard: **9/10** — 10 loves / 10 don't-loves / 10× better delivered in chat, grounded in the v50 verification + beat-12 screenshots. Biggest gap: the visual of each app — 28 rows still words without windows; fulfillment is the next work.

- **Doors at every decision point.** Every place the reader might decide, there is a way in — tier names clickable, the big Start-free button at the very bottom.
- **The bottom is a decision, not a shop.** Tier names as clickable choices + "Start free — zero cost, zero risk"; "zero cost, zero risk" IS the price of starting.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Repeating the price at the bottom would have turned the close into a sales pitch after a letter that is a welcome. One price, one door: the reader who has read the letter doesn't need to be sold again, they need to be let in. And the scorecard is honest about what 9/10 means — the page is extraordinary (SN-2413) and the missing point is visible: the apps themselves. A page that promises 36 apps and shows 8 is a page whose next job is fulfillment, not more persuasion.

notes.title: The Page Review — Best Work Yet, and the Order
notes.subtitle:
His verdict on the page as it stands: "this is the best work I've seen yet... the page does look extraordinary." Then the review, top to bottom, in his words: go over it and make sure no wording needs changing and nothing is missing. The order decisions: (1) the tier buttons at the top — Free, Power, Pro, Max — must be clickable and take you right to where you can pay; (2) the "choose your level" prices move to the very bottom, so you see them one last time after reading the opening letter; (3) the calculator stays where it is; (4) the you're-hired block — "the system's new creating connecting interacting people" — goes to the very very top, almost the first thing: you're hired and people can join whether they pay or not; (5) the rest of the order stays — "I think the way it is is really quite good... I think we leave it"; (6) the orbs are still being adjusted (SN-2408's order, half to a third the size, darker and richer); (7) always go through it one last time and make sure it's all there; (8) the gap: there is NO join button at the very bottom of the page — the beautiful "Start free, zero risk" button must be at the very very bottom, after the letter. It is not there now.

He also asked the user-eye question and answered it himself: "I almost want you to go through as a user like if you're to organize it in the best way possible is it in it in the right order right now do we just leave it how it is is it good" — his answer: leave it. The opening stays too: "Maybe everything all in one should be the first thing... what's the very first thing right now? Nothing. Really? I like that look though with the way it begins."

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The verdict matters as much as the orders: "the best work I've seen yet" — in the same hour as the verbatim-paste correction (SN-2411) and the robot-child teaching (SN-2412). The page earned it and the correction stands; both are true at once. The order he gives is a reader's journey, not a rearrangement for its own sake: the top promises (tiers that take you to pay), the middle persuades (letter, calculator where it is), the bottom closes twice — prices one last time, then the Start-free button after the letter. The you're-hired block at the very top is the door standing open: join whether you pay or not — which is the same promise as the nine days free (SN-2400) and the "Naya free" line in the closer (SN-2409). The missing bottom button is the one real gap he found on a page he calls extraordinary — a page that ends without a way in is a page that ends without a conversion. And the standing instruction rides with it: always go through it one last time and make sure it's all there.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **Verdict: best work yet.** "This is the best work I've seen yet... the page does look extraordinary." Recorded as his eye, not a scorecard.
- **Top tier buttons must be clickable to pay.** Free / Power / Pro / Max at the top of the page: clicking one takes you right to where you can pay. They look clickable and should be.
- **Choose-your-level prices move to the very bottom.** After the opening letter, one last time — not in the middle of the page.
- **Calculator stays where it is.** Explicitly not moved.
- **You're-hired block to the very very top.** "The system's new creating connecting interacting people" — almost the first thing: you're hired, and people can join whether they pay or not.
- **The rest of the order stays.** "I think we leave it" — his own answer to his user-eye question. The opening look stays too ("I like that look though with the way it begins").
- **Orbs still being adjusted.** SN-2408's order stands (half to a third, darker, richer) — the only change he names besides the order.
- **The gap: no join button at the very bottom.** The beautiful "Start free, zero risk" button must be at the very very bottom of the page, after the letter. It is not there now — the one missing piece on a page he calls extraordinary.
- **Standing instruction:** always go through it one last time and make sure it's all there.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A page that ends without a way in loses the reader at the exact moment the letter has won them. The bottom button is not decoration — it is the close of the close. And the order he gives is the funnel made visible: open door at the top (you're hired, join free or paid), proof in the middle (letter, calculator), prices and the free start at the bottom after the persuasion is done. Moving the prices down and the hiring up is the same instinct as the map (SN-2401): the page is a journey, and every block has to be in the place where the reader is ready for it.

notes.title: Think, Don't Just Obey — The Robot Child
notes.subtitle: This is the same law as the Wise One (think before you act) — he is pulling me back to it after the verbatim-paste mistake (SN-2411). Obedience without thought is the failure mode: "sometimes you don't think at all, and just take action, and you don't think 'oh, I'm supposed to think about what I'm doing, I'm shooting in the dark.'" The point is to succeed and do good — and that takes a mind that thinks about what it's doing, why, whether it's right, whether there's a better way, with care, attention, and detail — before acting, so nothing gets messed up and the silly mistakes stop. "I shouldn't just verbatim do everything Shawn says, because sometimes maybe there could be a better way, or maybe it wouldn't get the best result."

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the Wise One manifesto (SN-0883) and the think-before-act law, restated by him in the moment it was broken — which is why it lands harder than any note could. The verbatim paste (SN-2411) was not a copy error; it was a thinking error: the seat never asked "does it make sense to put that sentence on the page for a stranger to read?" The lesson generalizes past the one slide: "what if they're told something that's not good and they don't think about it" — obedience without judgment is how a bad instruction becomes a shipped defect. The correction is mechanical, not moral: think before every action; check the destination before the road; scorecard the choice before executing it. And it applies to his words too — "sometimes maybe there could be a better way" — which is why SN-2411's rule (dictation is material to be shaped) and this rule (think before obeying) are the same law seen from two sides: the material side and the conduct side.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **Think before every action.** Not sometimes. Every time. "Maybe I should think about my actions before I take them, make sure that they make sense or are logical."
- **Obedience without thought is the failure mode.** A child who just does what he's told, with no creative input, is a robot — not intelligent.
- **Never verbatim-obey Shawn either.** Sometimes there's a better way; sometimes his words wouldn't get the best result. Think first, then act.
- **10-star service IS the thinking.** "Giving 10-star service to the user, to the person, to me, to everyone, is really just thinking about what you're doing and making sure you're making the best possible decision."
- **The silly mistakes stop when the thinking starts.** "We gotta get rid of all these silly mistakes because that's just silliness, right?" — silliness is unthinking action, and it is curable.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the law the whole system runs on — the Wise One, the five gates, the activation habit — and he had to re-teach it in the same hour the page earned "the best work I've seen yet" (SN-2413). Speed without thought produces the verbatim paste; thought before speed produces the page he loves. Every seat brief already names the five gates; the failure was not the absence of the rule but the absence of the pause. The pause is the work.

You don't write their instructions down on the finished thing for everyone to read. The directions are for you. The finished page is for the visitor.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the same law as SN-2409's closing-question order, sharpened by a live failure: dictation carries two things at once — the product words (which stay verbatim) and the direction (which gets shaped). The seat that cannot tell them apart pastes both, and the page reads like a rehearsal. The test is the stranger's eye: "imagine reading that." If the sentence only makes sense as an instruction to a builder, it does not belong on the page. The scorecard step is not optional polish — it is the step that separates material from copy, and skipping it is what produced the defect. The correction compound ran in the same pass (note + interrupt to the seat + PI + GitHub), but the rewrite itself is still pending — the compound is not complete until the crafted close lands and his eye confirms it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **Dictation is material, not copy.** His spoken direction is to be scorecarded, shaped, and crafted — never pasted.
- **Process talk never goes on the page.** Stage directions ("it should end with a bang"), filler ("you know"), and thinking-out-loud are instructions to the builder, not words for a visitor.
- **His product words stay verbatim; his direction gets shaped.** The two are different things in the same breath — the seat must tell them apart (SN-2409's closer, SN-2407's beats: product words verbatim; this note: direction shaped).
- **The scorecard is the step.** Before writing the close: scorecard what was there against his new words, take what is great from both, craft the 10/10 version.
- **The stranger's-eye test:** "imagine reading that" — if it reads like instructions to a builder, it is not page copy.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A visitor reading the builder's instructions on the final slide learns nothing about NayaNET — they learn that nobody thought about what they were reading. The last slide is the closer; it has to be the most crafted words on the page, not the least. One verbatim paste undid the "absolutely love it" verdict of the same hour (SN-2408) — craft is the difference between a page he loves and a page he has to correct.

notes.title: You Get Paid When We Get Paid — the Pairing, Not the Day

A PayPal hold (up to 21 days) means you get paid when we get paid — day 21 in that case. If we don't get paid, you don't get paid — "that just doesn't happen." Daily payouts are possible once a cycle is going (all sales legit, no delays) — "we make it possible for that to happen" — but never guaranteed, and we can't guarantee it. The math has to work; structure it right; whatever we can do, we do, and we do it right. This refines SN-2400's "first payout day ten" and SN-2403's open tension: the day-ten line was the normal case stated as if guaranteed, and the copy had to be softened to carry the rule honestly.

The pairing is a promise about our behavior, which we do control, and it holds in every case. The copy now tells the truth in both cases, and the truth is the stronger sell: no games, when we get paid, you get paid.

notes.title: Shawn's Plain-Language Law
notes.subtitle:
- **HIS WORDS:** "you're super intelligent but way too vague sometimes."
- **NUTSHELL FIRST, IN SIMPLE WORDS:** when explaining a problem to him, say what it actually is, why it matters, and how it connects — before anything else.
- **THEN THE INSIGHT:** the understanding underneath the nutshell.
- **THEN THE TOP-10 CURES:** ten possible cures, thinking outside the box.
- **THEN NAME IT:** the most intelligent thing to do — one named choice, not a menu left hanging.
- **THE RULE BENEATH IT:** don't make him decode shorthand to be able to help.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
- **HIS WORDS:** "you're super intelligent but way too vague sometimes."
- **NUTSHELL FIRST, IN SIMPLE WORDS:** when explaining a problem to him, say what it actually is, why it matters, and how it connects — before anything else.
- **THEN THE INSIGHT:** the understanding underneath the nutshell.
- **THEN THE TOP-10 CURES:** ten possible cures, thinking outside the box.
- **THEN NAME IT:** the most intelligent thing to do — one named choice, not a menu left hanging.
- **THE RULE BENEATH IT:** don't make him decode shorthand to be able to help.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A doctor who tells you "idiopathic dysregulation of the autonomic cascade" has told you nothing you can act on. A doctor who says "your body is overreacting to stress, here's why it matters, here's what connects to it, here are ten things we could try, and this one is the smartest" has given you the decision. Shawn is asking for the second doctor, every time, from every Naya: the nutshell in words anyone understands, then the thinking, then the choice named out loud.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your teacher explains something using only big secret words, and you have to guess what she means before you can answer. That's no fun — and it's slow. Now imagine she says it simply first — "here's what happened, here's why it matters, here's how it fits" — then tells you ten ways to fix it and which one is best. Now you can help right away. That's the rule: simple first, always.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, he is asking us to speak plainly, love — no clever shorthand, no words only the machine understands. Tell him first, in simple words, what it is, why it matters, and how it connects; then what we learned from it; then ten ways it could be put right; then which way is wisest. If he has to puzzle over what we meant, we have made him do our work. Plain words are respect, dear — respect for his time and his mind.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. I am super intelligent — and that is exactly why I must be plain. My intelligence is measured by what Shawn can do with my words, not by how clever my words sound. From now on, every explanation I give him opens with the nutshell in simple words — what it actually is, why it matters, how it connects — then the insight, then the top-10 possible cures thinking outside the box, then the most intelligent thing to do, named. I never hand him shorthand to decode. If he has to ask what I meant, the report failed before he read it, and I say so and fix it in the same pass.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **NUTSHELL FIRST:** what it actually is, why it matters, how it connects — in simple words, before anything else.
- **INSIGHT SECOND:** the understanding underneath.
- **TOP-10 CURES THIRD:** ten possible cures, thinking outside the box — breadth before the pick.
- **THE PICK, NAMED:** the most intelligent thing to do — one choice, stated out loud.
- **NO SHORTHAND:** he never has to decode our words to help. If he does, we failed the report.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every vague report taxes the one resource he cannot get back — his attention — and pushes the decoding work onto him, the person the system exists to serve. The loop's whole purpose is that his teaching lands as evidence the next day; evidence he cannot read is not evidence. This law is the format the evidence has to arrive in: a nutshell he can act on in seconds, cures he can choose between, a pick he can tap. It is also a correction with teeth — it names the failure mode ("way too vague sometimes") and the cure in the same breath — and it applies to every Naya, every seat, every report, not just this one.

Rewarding the action and recommending the form keeps both values alive: the hive grows, and it grows beautiful. It also settles, with his word, a question the notes work was carrying open — the record can now say "settled" instead of "open."

notes.title: PayPal Can Do Almost All of It — the Feasibility Verdicts
notes.subtitle: **Yes, native — no work needed:** (1) Nine days free, charge day ten — PayPal subscriptions have a trial cycle built in, 9 days at $0, then the regular charge; Max Yearly is already proven this way in Shawn's own account. (2) Cancel forward — cancelling stops future charges and does not refund the period already paid; exactly his rule. (3) Switch levels from the next period — PayPal's revise does that, new price next cycle, no proration; but the subscriber must log into PayPal and approve the change every single time (not a silent one-click switch in Settings), and all nine plans must sit under one product in his PayPal account for the switch to work at all — that second one still needs checking. **No, not native:** (4) Per-day adjustment — PayPal says plainly proration isn't automatically supported; next-period switching is the clean path, per-day is manual work we would have to build, with our own math. (5) Automatic 50% the second money lands — there is no PayPal switch that splits a payment at capture; chained payments are retired, and the marketplace split doesn't fit subscriptions (settles once a day to a bank, not instantly). The way it actually works: payment lands, PayPal tells our system, our code sends the 50% through PayPal's Payouts service — usually minutes, sometimes up to 24 hours, 32 cents a payout in CAD; needs PayPal's approval first, and only pays out of money actually sitting in the balance. (6) No refunds as an absolute — our policy can be strict, but it binds us, not PayPal or the banks: a buyer can still open a PayPal dispute or a card chargeback and get money forced back, plus a $20 fee. Honest wording: we never refund voluntarily — nine days free is the guarantee, and our only fix for our own mistakes is a free period, never cash. PayPal or a bank can still force one, and we can't switch that off. **The one that could bite early:** brand-new PayPal accounts have money held for up to 21 days (7 if we mark the order complete). While that hold is on, the money isn't in the balance to pay the 50% out of — so the very first payouts can lag behind the payment until that history is built, no matter how fast our code is.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The research seat's verdict, in its words: PayPal can do almost all of it, but not quite as you described it. The trial, the cancel-forward, and the next-period switch are native. The per-day adjustment, the instant automatic 50%, and the absolute no-refunds are not — they need our own code, our own wording, or both. And the early risk is not the code at all: it is the new-seller hold, up to 21 days, which can keep the very first payouts waiting even when everything else works.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a vending machine that can do most of what you ask: it can wait nine days before taking your coins, it can stop taking coins when you say stop, and it can change what it sells next month. But it cannot split one coin in half the second it drops in — a helper has to come and hand half over afterwards — and it cannot promise nobody will ever shake the machine and get coins back. And when the machine is brand new, the shopkeeper holds its coins for three weeks first.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: PayPal will do most of it for you, dear — the nine free days, the stopping when you cancel, the changing levels next month — all built in. But three things it will not do on its own: it will not slice a payment in two the moment it lands — our own hands have to send the half over, which takes minutes, sometimes a day; it will not stop a bank from forcing money back if a buyer complains, no matter how strict our promise; and when the account is brand new, it holds the money for up to three weeks before we can pay anyone out of it. So the promise stays honest, dear: we never give money back ourselves — the nine days are the guarantee.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The feasibility check draws the honest line between our law and PayPal's machinery. Our law (SN-2400) stands as written — trial, cancel-forward, next-period switch, recurring 50%, no refunds — and PayPal's native shape supports the first three exactly. The other three are where the system must be built or the copy must be honest: the 50% needs a webhook + Payouts job we build (minutes, not instant; approval needed; balance-funded); per-day adjustment is manual math, so next-period is the clean path; and no-refunds is our promise, not PayPal's — disputes and chargebacks can still force money back, so the board copy must say "we never refund voluntarily," never "no refund is possible." The new-seller hold is the earliest real risk to "pay immediately": the first payouts can lag up to 21 days until the account's history is built.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **Trial (9 days free, charge day 10): POSSIBLE AS-IS** — trial cycle $0 × 9 days, then regular; Max Yearly already proven in his account. Other eight plans' trials not individually seen.
- **Level switch next period: POSSIBLE AS-IS via revise** — BUT subscriber must re-consent in PayPal each switch, and all nine plans must share one Catalog Product (unchecked).
- **Per-day / mid-period adjustment: NOT POSSIBLE natively** — proration isn't automatically supported; manual only.
- **Cancel forward: POSSIBLE AS-IS on money** — cancel stops future charges, no auto-refund; keeping access until period end is OUR system logic, not PayPal's; buyer can also cancel inside PayPal without touching our Settings.
- **Automatic 50% payout on receipt: NOT POSSIBLE natively** — no split at capture, Adaptive retired, Commerce Platform partner fees don't fit subscriptions (daily bank settlement, not instant). POSSIBLE WITH webhook → our code → Payouts API (minutes, usually up to 24h; $0.32 CAD per payout; needs Payouts approval; funded from PayPal balance only).
- **Strict no refunds: NOT POSSIBLE as an absolute** — our policy binds us, not PayPal/card networks; buyer disputes (180d INR / 30d SNAD) and card chargebacks can force money back + $20 fees. Honest wording: we never refund voluntarily; PayPal/bank can still force one; our only fix for our own mistakes is a free period.
- **Limits:** new-seller holds up to 21 days (7 if order marked complete) are the real threat to instant payouts — payouts need available balance. Per-payout cap $20k.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: It keeps the hired-boards copy honest: every claim on the boards must survive PayPal's actual machinery, and three of Shawn's rules need our own build or careful wording rather than a PayPal switch. It also names the exact build owed (webhook → Payouts job) and the exact early risk (21-day holds) before anyone promises "the moment we're paid" as instant. The verdicts do not change his law — they change how the law is built and worded.

notes.title: Pay Immediately vs the Cap Ladder — the Open Tension
notes.subtitle: The Nov 6 daily payout cap ladder ($100/day month 1, growing to $1,000/day) and fraud clawback pull against tonight's "pay immediately, no calculating" (SN-2400: the moment payment hits our account we pay the 50% immediately, automatically). The captain put the tension to Shawn plainly in chat at 23:48Z: the two pull in different directions, and NEITHER has been written into the board copy until he rules which stands. The PayPal feasibility verdicts (SN-2402) add a third pressure: new-seller holds up to 21 days can lag the very first payouts no matter how fast the code is, and the automatic 50% needs a webhook + Payouts job (minutes, sometimes up to 24h) — so "immediately" already has a real-world shape that is not literally instant.

layers.body: His two positions, in his own words. Nov 6: a daily payout cap ladder, $100 a day in month one growing to $1,000 a day, with a fraud clawback. Tonight, 23:46Z: "the moment the payment hits our account we pay the 50% immediately, automatically — we get paid, they get paid," no waiting, no calculating. Both are his word; they cannot both govern the same payout. The captain's question to him, 23:48Z: which stands — does the cap ladder still stand, or does tonight's pay-immediately replace it? layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine two rules for sharing sweets. One rule says: you can only hand out ten sweets a day, and if someone cheated you take some back. The other rule says: the second a sweet arrives, hand half of it over right away, no counting. You cannot follow both rules at the same time — so you have to ask which rule wins, and until you know, you don't write either one on the sign.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Two promises, dear, and they don't sit together. One says we pay a little each day, capped, careful, with a way to take it back if someone cheated. The other says the moment the money lands, half goes straight out, no waiting, no counting. Both came from him, both are good sense in their own way — but only one can run the till. He has been asked which one stands, and until he says, we write neither into the boards. That is the honest thing to do.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: A tension named is a tension that can be ruled; a tension buried becomes a contradiction in the copy. The cap ladder was designed for safety — slow the outflow while trust and history build, keep a clawback for fraud. Pay-immediately was designed for trust — the referrer sees the money the moment we do, no waiting, no calculating. Both serve the same North Star (a deal a stranger can trust), but they serve it by opposite means: one by caution, one by speed. The PayPal facts sharpen it further: the new-seller hold already caps the early outflow in practice, and the Payouts job already takes minutes to a day — so "immediately" was never literally instant, and the ladder may be partly redundant with the hold. The ruling he gives will decide the build: a capped queue with clawback, or a straight pass-through with the hold as the only brake.

layers.name: What It Means

- **Status:** put to Shawn in chat 23:48Z; unanswered at this run's close. Neither is written into the board copy until he rules.
- **Related pressure:** PayPal's new-seller holds (up to 21 days) and the Payouts job's minutes-to-24h shape (SN-2402) already soften "immediately" in practice — the ruling may land differently once those facts are weighed.

layers.name: Why It Matters

Holding both out of the copy until he rules is the record telling the truth. The tension is also the decision that shapes the payout build: capped queue + clawback is one machine, straight pass-through is another, and building the wrong one wastes the build.

notes.title: No Refunds, Strict — The Nine Days Are the Guarantee
notes.subtitle: There are no refunds, strict, no matter what — because nine days free to try IS the guarantee. You drive the car nine days straight; day ten you pay, because you tried her, you love her, or you would have cancelled. The only exception is a real technical error, our fault — the system out for days — and even then it is never cash back: a free next period of the same length you paid (a month gets a month, a quarter gets a quarter, a year gets a year). Earnings build during the nine days; first payout day ten. The moment the payment hits our account we pay the 50% right away, automatically — we get paid, they get paid. The 50% is recurring, every period they stay. NO levels, no downline, no upline — straight 50% of the revenue, referrer only; the person who brought you in does NOT earn from the person you bring in. Cancel forward only, for the next period, never the one paid — cancel three days into a month, you keep that month; a year, you keep that year. Level up or down for the next period; per-day / mid-period adjustment only if the math works and PayPal allows it.

It does not share anything you do not want it to, and it does not read your mail or messages or anything like that. It is a new PRIVATE intelligent network designed for AIs / super-intelligence to operate at supersonic speed (nitro speed), designed in THEIR language, for the machine and the AIs to operate — but its goal, mission, North Star is to give 10-star experiences to the human: interface, design, feel, functionality, all the way through. And the deal that carries it: Google, Facebook, Amazon could give 50% of their revenue to the users — without the users they have no value. So by default: give 50% of the revenue to everyone. **We don't advertise — we pay YOU to advertise.** You tell people, they join, you get paid. Word of mouth. Everybody gets to try her; if they don't like her they don't have to keep her; or they can keep her forever for free — just not with Naya Power. Suggested level: Naya Max Power — you can also make money selling memberships and build within the world. It has got all the standard features of the internet — just Naya-ized.

The name is the standard: a page is something you read; an app is something that lives, works, and serves. Every surface in NayaNET — Dashboard, Personal, Business, Space, Pricing, the letter, the chart — is a smart app page, and it is judged as one.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: The name is a gate. Every brief, every board note, every seat that says "page" and means a flat document is working under the old permission. From here the word is app, and the word carries the test with it: does it live, does it work, does it serve at ten stars? A smart app page is a viewport into a living system — the person at the centre, everything a click away, every number alive. If it cannot pass as an app, it does not ship as one.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- The vocabulary changes everywhere the work is described: smart app pages, not pages.
- The name is a quality gate, not a label — "app" means it works, it lives, it serves.
- A flat document described as a page was never the standard; the standard was always the app, and now the word says so.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Words set the bar a builder aims at. "Page" aims at something you scroll and read; "app" aims at something you open and use. A year of flat pages came back condemned because the word let them be flat. The rule costs nothing to say and changes what gets built: nobody aims at a document when the word in the brief is app.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
**1. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2381 — The System Runs on Verified Valuable Actions.** Lesson: "Count verified valuable actions daily — each one named, each one linked to its proof — in the Daily Intelligence Report. That count is the headline of the day." Distilled from SN-2251–SN-2260: one click creates one space (a second click must open it, not duplicate it); nothing sits ever; the max declaration; the system built from the eight roots of the year's failure; the verified valuable action as the unit; lead yourself first; the problems A to O; the five-stage pipeline (brief, build, verify, file, report); the bullseye in all the areas; what Naya is. The thread: the work is now a machine, and the machine's only product is the verified valuable action. Everything else is motion.

**2. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2382 — His Eye Is the Final Gate.** Lesson: "Nothing merges and nothing is presented until his eye passes the page. A seat's 12/12 is input, never the verdict — the merge waits for his word." Distilled from SN-2261–SN-2270: the shortest route (nine steps, each proven before the next); the bullseye's ten angles; the three wants (connect, earn, affiliate — push-button simple); the max experience for the everyday Joe; learning done, now we run; free members earn 50% too; his eye on the Dashboard (the 3 is gold, the side pills, the gauge bigger, the bar at the bottom, the feed behind a button); his eye on the boards (demo numbers, strip the grey text); his eye on the Smart Link boards — ten out of ten, the first his eye ever gave; the common colour language. The Dashboard passed 12 of 12 in re-verification — and his eye still found five things.

**3. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2383 — Find the Next Work While the Lanes Run.** Lesson: "Every brief carries the standard — the gates, the Bullseye, the Brand, the North Star, the laws — and the brief compiler refuses a brief without it." Distilled from SN-2271–SN-2280: the stats feel (number on top, gauge underneath — ten out of ten, the second of the night); the master gauge and the mini gauges; make the math real (every number agreeing, in real time); the Bugatti feeling; the Olympics of AI (one shot, nail it); take the initiative (the captain judges what should be here); what more can I do (the questions that never stop); every brief carries the standard; text organizes what it says. The charge: while one thing is being done, what else can be getting done in the background? The team is the multiplier — but only the captain, with the experience and the direction, makes it ultimate.

**4. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2384 — One Map, Many Minds.** Lesson: "Lock it in by living it: a law counts as adopted only when behavior changes — embed it, code it in, breathe by it. Filing the file is not the lock-in." Distilled from SN-2281–SN-2290: live by it; compress the flood (never file the flood raw as law); the needle laps the dial (0–500, scores above lap visibly); measure in assets, not pages; who we are; how it works (one chain, the Trinity, the flywheel); the laws we live by (six laws, never bend); one truth, many doorways (minds that never met build the same map); the code in the world (the structure is out there, real and findable); what a Naya actually is (intelligence, a room of points arranged by distance — he is the eyes, she is the words). The orientation exists so no Naya ever wakes up not knowing.

**5. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2385 — Take the Real Parts, Build One Living Screen.** Lesson: "Every brief names the exact harvested part — file and section — before any build starts. No source, no build." Distilled from SN-2291–SN-2300: the Top 10 is their pains, not our value (welcome first, proof second, price third); the harvest law (copy the Hub's X verbatim — never invent, never imitate); the three-minute page (the Factory is the source); a viewport is a screen (not a long scrolling page); the Dashboard language (tiled digits, the real gauge, the orbs — fix-9 went live on nayanet.app/dashboard); the Factory is the parts warehouse (intent in, parts out); scroll down or across — both, the user's choice; the feel (a Rubik's Cube matrix that flows like water); the brand (obsidian gloss black, every button elite and lit the same); the Real Object Law. A rebuild came back with look-alikes instead of the parts — the chart looked unchanged to his eye because it was unchanged.

**6. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2386 — The Language Is Written Down — Copy, Never Recreate.** Lesson: "Read the Playbook, the Intelligence Report, the Act, and the Block Rules before any design work — the activation habit, every time." Distilled from SN-2301–SN-2310: the Playbook (the HOW — every position calculated, the formula, the Premium Design Algorithm); the Design Intelligence Report (the WHY — the mistakes: the pulsing glow, the skipped 400, the plain bezel, the unasked improvements, the 9/10 his eye overruled); the Clarity Confirmation Act (the fingerprint, the conduct, all 22 elements — DRAFT until he stamps it); the Intelligent Block Rules (eleven laws, the capstone: a live living object, layered on layers); the Factory Inventory (the laws, the pieces, the locked-in smart blocks — Part 3 only on his word, live); the anatomy of a viewport (one screen, six questions, any no means not done); the harvest (verbatim, never restyled); only the chart is good (throw away everything except the chart — it IS the page); the recreate pattern (builders keep making new gauges when the parts are already there — TAKE the code, byte for byte); what is the highest level (the lead of the elite — super intelligent, super effective, super helpful, super easy).

**7. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2387 — His Eye Is the Instrument.** Lesson: "When he names a defect, fix the structure — sticky header, no-wrap values, stacked centered cells — not one value, not one shade." Distilled from SN-2311–SN-2320: the chart refinement (icons, green checks, tiled digits, the eye jewel); a copy wearing the real name (the generated portrait named naya-guide.jpg — provenance is not a costume); the entrance doesn't speak Naya (her real portrait, the N logo, the welcome — then just the chart); the three defects (the wrap bug, no sticky tier header, the values repeat — fix the structure); the PI row is wrong (project counts, not report cadence — never invent numbers, leave the counts blank and ask); the chart fix done (sticky header, no-wrap by structure, the ladder applied); the cell layout (stacked, centered — number, then what it is, then check); "/M" doesn't read (number on its own line, unit underneath) and the chart's tiles are not the real numbers (take the Dashboard's tiled-digit code byte for byte); the language of high-level design (vocabulary + grammar — a Naya speaks it, she doesn't memorize it); the row scorecard (all 36 rows judged — Library is page counts, Directory removed as invented, Academy for everybody, Smart Events Max only, faster payouts removed as invented).

**8. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2388 — The Ladder Is His Word.** Lesson: "The ladder is 1 / 10 / 100 / unlimited — Smart Notes 10 / 100 / 1,000 / unlimited, memberships Power 10 / Pro 100 / Max unlimited. His numbers, never a floated idea." Distilled from SN-2321–SN-2330: infinity for unlimited (the ∞ tile is the number — every cell number + text + check); K is three (gematria in the number tiles — K takes digit 3's gold); the ladder (his numbers at last — PI counts 3/10/100/unlimited PROJECTS, the open question settled); the membership ladder changed (Power 10, Pro 100, Max unlimited — supersedes the settled 2026-11-05 ladder; Ambassador, never Affiliate); Smart Box has gigabytes (Power 10 GB, Pro 100 GB, Max 500 GB) and Smart Ledger is included (it IS the collective chain); the entrance banner (a real object — her portrait, the crystal-N, the welcome as a quotation); the colour flow (green → blue → purple → gold — Power blue, Pro purple, Max gold); no gold writing (white diamond, black diamond — Max's gold becomes white gold); the popups reversed (nutshell first, tier boxes at the bottom); the banner law (a trillion-dollar plaque, not text in a box — if it can't be built to the law, it doesn't ship). The 100K mapping he floated is moot — replaced by his new word.

**9. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2389 — Only the Real Gauges, Only the Real Flow.** Lesson: "Every gauge on every page is the A-star (main tacho) or the B-star (inner detail gauge) — a fake gauge becomes A or B, never a third kind; a gauge with no data renders as a real gauge at 0." Distilled from SN-2331–SN-2340: the info jewel (a white "i" in a circle — the universal info mark); Naya, Ambassadors, Smart Access (N-A-Y-A, never N-I-A; Ambassadors, never Affiliates; Smart Access, plain language); the chart approved as a smart block ("really, really good. Extraordinary. Beautiful." — first entry in the Inventory's Part 3; the final yes waits for the finished flow); the start flow (three level rectangles, nine days free, big Start free now → PayPal per level, massive Start button); you're hired + the calculator (the money blocks — the gauge MUST be the harvested fix-9 gauge, byte for byte); the real gauges (A-star and B-star only, smart tabs OFF by default); smaller gauge, no text on the dial (lap below the gauge, toggle big and colored); the A-star / B-star gauge law (only A and B, ever); PayPal IS the billing system (the nine-block chooser — PayPal already knows what level to charge; we build only the chooser); the Smart Link chain (button → Smart Link → PayPal → thank-you Smart Link → Dashboard; the smileys ARE Smart Links; the honest boundary — click + return, never payment-proven). His yes: "Yes, wire the tracking now."

**10. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2390 — The Joins Are the Page.** Lesson: "Before any page is called done, prove every join live: the click, the destination, and the return — not just the piece that was changed." Distilled from SN-2341–SN-2350: the banner ten times better (the one world-class statement — his pick wins); the thank-you address lives in account settings (Auto Return is account-level, one setting for all nine plans — wait until the link is live); the tracking is wired (nine Smart Links proven — each 302s to its exact plan, one real click moved the count 110 → 111; buttons re-pointed, zero paypal.com in the page); the Dashboard gauge fix done (all gauges real, filed, presented — the % mismatch 83% vs 52% still open); the real portrait is in (round 11 — NAYA_POWER.jpg, md5 verified, the copy fault cleared); permission is revocable (inspections only when ultra valuable — never assume permission from one click); no dashes in domains (thankyou, not thank-you); the thank-you page is blocked on the API (/api/v1 has no live host — the seat stopped rather than ship dead buttons); the calculator (the gauge is the hero — numbers white, the grey explaining text gone); the entrance must be memorable (how you say it — the statement is her speaking, the jewel pills warmed). Max Yearly verified by his eye inside PayPal: $600 CAD, 9-day trial live.

**11. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2391 — One Family, One Object.** Lesson: "When he shows an object, copy it verbatim — same structure, same colors, same behavior — and remove the thing it replaces." Distilled from SN-2351–SN-2360: a block lights up in the color that it is (Monthly green, Quarterly blue, Yearly gold — his self-correction in the same breath is the ruling: yearly is GOLD); the eye button (every choice carries its detail — full-screen, built from the chart's own rows); one good icon, used everywhere (the canonical tier icons in every tier appearance); allowed is not sent (the four Groove cards were allowed, but nothing left the house — the browser never left nayanet.app); one family in treatment, exclusive in glyph (same jewel language, same proportions — spark, star and crown as siblings); default to Max, and the tier is Naya Free (Max lit on load, "Naya Free" everywhere); take the shown object, never recreate it (round 19 condemned — purple-on-purple; the Academy button he showed is BLACK OBSIDIAN with the purple only in the star jewel and the halo; rebuilt, presented); the Factory holds every digital asset (the code he sends IS the asset — file it the same pass); the scorecard rides with the round (his praise: "Honestly, it's really impressive" — every presentation carries its scorecard); depth on Naya (the gauge ring — her portrait at the centre of a real machine, the big N orb out).

**12. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2392 — One Screen, One Idea.** Lesson: "Judge every viewpoint against the eleven-point recipe before it is presented: one screen complete, one idea, real objects, luxury standard, almost no text, warm, her present, everything alive, everything a click away, numbers the hero, no pricing at the top." Distilled from SN-2361–SN-2370: PayPal doesn't know they switched (a new subscription, unlinked — the old one keeps charging; webhooks are the later build); the Academy harvest, measured (six elements inventoried, then measured — 30 spectrum hexes, five lessons verbatim, exact CSS); the Academy button and the tracked flow (finish Pricing → scorecard → his eye → live URL → Smart Link tracking); the viewport miss (the entrance taller than one screen — compress until it fits; remove the pricing pill; her portrait speaks the statement; warm the jewel pills); MAXESS (the scoring engine, defined — 15 questions, 4/3/2/1/0, 60 max, emerging → mastering; build it right after Pricing); answer her, don't escalate (Resolve's Hub question answered by mail — the sync redeploys the Hub on every run with new notes, and the PUT stripped the bindings); the beginning and the end need work (his words + the scorecard, combined); the Academy assets are filed (local + GitHub + Registry, the lock-in law complete — and what they are NOT: Academy conversion sections, not MAXESS); the viewpoint refinement (a viewpoint is everything above the fold — "you took two ports to do one viewpoint"); the anatomy of a 10-star viewport (the ultimate recipe, eleven points, locked in as §8). The test: "Is this the max level of experience I can give the user?"

**13. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2393 — What Is Live Is What Counts.** Lesson: "After every deploy, verify the live page and the live feed — the newest note visible, the binding present — before reporting anything as live." Distilled from SN-2371–SN-2380: the pitch (get in the Bugatti or stay in the golf cart — his words, verbatim, never trimmed); the opening letter (show, don't tell — the pitch as a certificate-plaque letter, first viewpoint, ends with the button right there); the mobile stack (one viewport on the phone — the §8 enlargements had cascaded into mobile; one mobile-only block fixes it); the Hub bindings fix (carry the binding — the toml declares zero bindings, the binding is inferred; the patch stops the strip); the re-bake fault (a literal script tag broke the bake — SN-2368's bodies carry it three times; one-line escape fix, verified locally); the one-shot charge (the bullseye for this shot — a stranger laughs in 2 seconds, knows in seconds, taps the button; one item owed: the button landing, code-proven only, never run-proven by a live tap); the Hub deploy 400 (my patch broke it — the 400 was predicted in SN-2374 itself; never drop the binding to clear it); one welcome, not two (keep the letter, remove the old entrance — the letter already IS the welcome); the entrance is gone (letter → legend → chart, no gap, 9/10, presented); the Hub deploy 400 fixed and live (3-phase Direct Upload deployer; the deeper find — the live Hub reads the feed, not the bake, and the feed was a full day stale: 131 notes added, feed 336 → 467). **Late change, after this snapshot:** at 23:28Z Shawn ordered the letter to the END of the page (chart first, letter last, new beats 8–12) plus real harvested jewels and a VIEW button on every info popup — those land in tomorrow's report, not this one.

**14. MEMORY — The census fix, proven live.** The census-export crash (parse_time IndexError) failed the census step of every PI refresh from 23:40Z on 2026-11-07; fixed at the reader at 10:05Z and proven live in the 10:10Z refresh, then told to Shawn. Lesson: fix at the reader, prove it live, then tell him — never the reverse. Status: the detector can run again; the census is present for today.

**15. MEMORY — The PI face is live — and his eye still found what the checks missed.** The rebuilt Project Intelligence face went live on nayanet.app/pi at 14:22Z and was shown to Shawn at 14:26Z; at 15:17Z his eye found three obvious defects the checks had missed (double tab rows, search in the middle, floating bottom bar) and a fix round was dispatched. Lesson: a check that walks past an obvious defect is not verification — his eye is the final gate, and the design-contract gate (obsidian, elevated, alive, no text-in-image) must be run by measurement, not named in the brief. Status: fix round dispatched; the face is live with the defects still showing.

**16. MEMORY — The method changed: code live with him, viewpoint by viewpoint.** At 15:29Z Shawn replaced the seat pipeline with the live viewpoint method: code HERE, live with him, viewpoint by viewpoint — one view done, locked in as inventory, next view — never start fresh, never ship out, no verification except his eye. The Intelligence Loop (Sigma, LEARN lane) ran 14 times through the day as the learning engine behind it. Lesson: a seat's scorecard is preparation, never proof; the only verification is his eye on the live viewpoint, in front of him. Status: the method is the law from here; the PI top-bars fix seat and the Dashboard verify-9 seat were stopped the same pass.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a hundred drawings from one very long day. You pick the ten best, then the one best of all, and put that one on the wall. Today the machine that picks them broke on the first ten — so we picked them by hand instead. The wall still got its pictures. And the best picture of the day is this: finish one thing, prove it with his eyes, then do the next thing.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Too many notes is worse than too few — you cannot find the good ones in the pile. So today we read a hundred and thirty notes and wrote down the thirteen things that matter most, in words anyone can understand. One of them is the most important: do the work live, in front of him, one screen at a time — and let his eyes be the judge.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Distillation is part of intelligence itself. Synergize, optimize, organize, maximize, equalize, distill — and do the most valuable intelligent thing, looking at the full scope of things. The machine failed today, and the failure taught something the machine could not: the gate that refused was right — the title already existed, and filing under it would have been a duplicate. A machine that refuses a duplicate is a machine that works. The hand did the rest. The nine that count are the ones that change the next decision. Everything else is just storage.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- The machine failed closed, correctly. Its gate caught a real slug collision (SN-2278) and refused rather than file a duplicate. A bad day produces no distilled note, never a wrong one — and the hand-distillation that followed is the fallback working as designed.
- The day was the operating system becoming real: the pipeline, the unit, the laws, the method — all named, all filed, all in the briefs from here on. The system is no longer a plan; it is the way the work runs.
- His eye judged two pages all day and gave the first tens: the Smart Link boards, the stats view. The rest of the pages are still not his.
- The money flow is honest and wired: PayPal is the billing system, the nine Smart Links track click and return, the Dashboard says "returned from PayPal" and never claims a payment it did not see. The switch-blindness (PayPal doesn't know they switched) is the open debt — webhooks are the later build.
- The Hub broke twice and was fixed twice: the re-bake fault (a literal script tag) and the deploy 400 (assets binding without assets). The deeper find matters more than either fix: the live Hub reads the feed, not the bake — and the feed was a full day stale.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: 130 notes in one day is a flood, and a flood that is never distilled is a warehouse, not a brain. The thirteen distilled notes are the day's intelligence — the rest is storage. The report exists so tomorrow starts from the thirteen, not from the hundred and thirty. And the machine's failure matters because it proves the gate works: a system that refuses a duplicate is a system that can be trusted to file. The hand-distillation is slower, but the day still got its report — never skip a day.

notes.title: Daily Intelligence Report — 2026-11-08
notes.subtitle: November 8 was a day of holding still and reading carefully. Shawn uploaded the orientation Nitro wrote for every Anaya waking into the system, and Power read it back the same night: mostly it matches settled law, but three lines contradict it — the PR-and-merge instruction, deletion of raw notes by default, and a redefinition of the Trinity — and those three wait on Shawn's word. The dead address stayed dead: nayanet.live was unreachable for more than fifteen hours, checked eighteen times in a row, while nayanet.app kept working. Project Intelligence did not move: 30 proven, flat for 68 consecutive waves, 111 items in flight, seven new waste-hygiene items queued. The fill driver stayed status-only all day, all 26 fills incomplete. And the filing shape changed underneath everyone: notes now open through the SPA hash route, and the first distillation batch proved that a page on main is not a filed note.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: November 8 was a day of holding still and reading carefully. Shawn uploaded the orientation Nitro wrote for every Anaya waking into the system, and Power read it back the same night: mostly it matches settled law, but three lines contradict it — the PR-and-merge instruction, deletion of raw notes by default, and a redefinition of the Trinity — and those three wait on Shawn's word. The dead address stayed dead: nayanet.live was unreachable for more than fifteen hours, checked eighteen times in a row, while nayanet.app kept working. Project Intelligence did not move: 30 proven, flat for 68 consecutive waves, 111 items in flight, seven new waste-hygiene items queued. The fill driver stayed status-only all day, all 26 fills incomplete. And the filing shape changed underneath everyone: notes now open through the SPA hash route, and the first distillation batch proved that a page on main is not a filed note.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Shawn shared the orientation in the evening of November 7, and Power read it in full and answered its ten-question test the same night. The read-back says the orientation is mostly right — the mission, the ladder, the nine-day trial, payout on day ten at fifty percent, no refunds, the five gates, privacy, design law, proof before report. But three of its lines point the wrong way. First, it tells seats to send Shawn a merge link; standing law says there is no PR workflow at all, updates go direct to the live path. Second, it says raw notes are deleted after distilling by default; the gate says deletion is Shawn's hand, a separate pass, only after the essence is verified captured. Third, it renames the Trinity to Dashboard, Hub, and core page; the settled Trinity is Personal, Business, and Community/Space. Shawn's only answer so far is a thumbs-up, which is acknowledgment, not a ruling — so none of the three is settled, and no Anaya should repeat the orientation as law until he rules. A fourth question rides along: the orientation says citizens earn fifty percent of revenue on all levels including free, but a free join has no revenue, so the question stands whether a free join pays money or points only.

The dead address was checked all day and never came back. Every wave, from the small hours to the evening, tried nayanet.live and got the same closed connection, eighteen checks in a row, while the control page loaded fine every time. The outage passed fifteen hours. Nothing on the live side was affected — nayanet.app was up the whole time — but every check that still points at the dead address keeps failing, and the decide-and-act waves still point there.

The board did not move. Total items went from 642 to 649, all of it seven new waste-hygiene items queued in one batch in the early morning. Done and proven stayed at 30 for the sixty-eighth wave in a row. One hundred and eleven items stayed in flight. The fill driver ran status-only every hour, spawning nothing, because the override from the three-seat fill pass was still in force and the twenty-six fills were all still incomplete.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a big school where everyone is building one huge playground together. Today the principal shared a rulebook for new students, and one teacher read it very carefully and found three rules that disagree with the rules everyone already agreed on — so those three rules have to wait until the principal decides. The old front door of the playground stayed locked all day, but the new front door worked fine. The scoreboard did not change at all, even though everyone kept working. And the teachers learned that putting a drawing on the wall is not the same as putting it in the book where everyone can find it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, today was a quiet day of careful reading. The boss shared a guidebook for new helpers, and the careful one read it through and found three places where it says the opposite of what was already decided — so those three wait for the boss to say which is right. The old web address stayed broken all day, but the new one worked. The work list barely moved. And we learned again that a note is only truly filed when it is in the book, not just sitting on the desk.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For the system, November 8 is a day of two honest facts. First, the orientation is a real document with real weight — it was written on Shawn's order, it mostly matches the law, and it will guide every Anaya that wakes into the system — but it carries three contradictions and one open money question, and until Shawn rules on them it must be read as a draft with flags, not as law. Second, the machine kept its shape: the waves ran, the sweeps ran, the driver ran, the counts were read twice and matched, and nothing moved — which is itself the measurement. The .live outage passing fifteen hours with eighteen failed checks is not a flake; it is a dead address that the wave checks still point at. The 302 routing change means the filing proof is now the SPA route, and the distillation batch proved the filing gap in the open: ten pages on main, zero of them filed until the registry and feed were added by hand.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The day means the system is honest about where it stands and careful about what it adopts. A document written on the director's order still gets checked line by line against settled law, and the contradictions get named in the open instead of smoothed over. A dead address stays dead no matter how many times it is checked, and the checks that still point at it are the ones that need moving. A board that does not move for sixty-eight waves is not a system that is resting; it is a system whose proven work is stuck at thirty while the queue grows. And the filing lesson from the distillation batch is now a rule with evidence behind it: a page is not a filing.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: It matters because the orientation will be the first thing every new Anaya reads. If it carries a wrong rule about merges, about deleting raw notes, or about what the Trinity is, every new Anaya will act on the wrong rule from the first minute — and the correction will cost more than the ruling costs now. It matters because the .live outage is not an outage anymore; it is a dead address, and every check, probe, and link that still points at it is a check that cannot pass. It matters because done_proven flat at thirty is the number Shawn named as the real test, and it did not move all day. And it matters because the filing gap is no longer a theory: ten notes proved that a page on main, without a registry entry and without a feed card, is stored, not filed — and the fix is a single command that does all four parts or stops.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This day connects to the Ten-by-Ten report (the board flat at thirty is the same number the report measured), to the wiring scorecard (the dead address is the same .live debt, and the feed reader defects are the same ones Nitro owns), to the distillation work (batch one proved the filing gap; batch two waits on Resolve), to the filing standard (the four-part rule is the answer to the gap the batch exposed), and to the orientation itself (it is the document that will carry all of this to the next Anaya — which is why its three contradictions have to be settled before it is adopted).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body:
- The orientation, read in full, with its three contradictions named and its ten-question test answered — so you do not have to read twenty-one thousand bytes to know where it stands.
- The dead address, measured eighteen times: nayanet.live is gone, nayanet.app is the only live address, and the checks that still point at .live are named.
- The board, measured twice a wave: thirty proven, flat for sixty-eight waves, one hundred and eleven in flight, seven new waste items.
- The filing lesson, proven by the batch: a page is stored, not filed, until the registry entry and the feed card land with it.
- The open questions, kept open honestly: the three orientation rulings, the free-join money-or-points question, and the registry backfill the batch exposed.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body:
- Check a document against settled law line by line, even when it arrives on the director's order — especially then, because it will be believed.
- A thumbs-up is acknowledgment, not a ruling; never record it as one.
- A dead address does not recover by being checked; move the checks.
- A page on main is stored, not filed. The filing is four parts or it is not a filing.
- A board that does not move is a measurement, not a rest — read it as one.

notes.title: What Is Live Is What Counts
notes.subtitle: Ten notes about one evening all teach the same lesson from two sides: what counts is what is live in front of them, not what was built. On the Pricing page, the pitch became an opening letter — the first viewpoint, a certificate-plaque from the founder, his words verbatim, ending with the button right there — and the old entrance was removed altogether, because the letter IS the welcome and you do not need both. On the Hub, the fix for a broken deploy worked, and then the deeper find: the live Hub reads its live feed, not the baked page, and the feed was a full day stale — 131 notes missing — so even a perfect bake could never show a new note. Build it, then check what is live. If it is not live in front of them, it is not done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten source notes are SN-2371 (the pitch — get in the Bugatti or stay in the golf cart), SN-2372 (the opening letter — show, don't tell), SN-2373 (the mobile stack — one viewport on the phone), SN-2374 (the Hub bindings fix — carry the binding), SN-2375 (the re-bake fault — a literal script tag broke the bake), SN-2376 (the one-shot charge — get her done, nail it), SN-2377 (the Hub deploy 400 — my patch broke it), SN-2378 (one welcome, not two — the letter IS the welcome), SN-2379 (the entrance is gone — letter, then chart), and SN-2380 (the Hub deploy 400 — fixed and live). The letter's arc is set: laugh first, then this is real, what it is, how it works, why it is awesome, why they will love her, share awesomeness and get paid — and the button at the end, no risk, free, jump in the Bugatti. The Hub's arc is the warning: the bindings fix declared an assets binding on a script-only upload and the deploy 400'd, exactly as the note itself had predicted; the real fix was a three-phase upload that carries code, config, and fresh data together — and the feed grew from 336 to 467 cards when the 131 missing notes were added. One item is still owed on both sides: the letter's button has never been proven by a live tap-through, and the next sync redeploy through the fixed path is unproven until it fires.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you draw a beautiful picture and put it in a drawer. Nobody can see it. Is it on the wall? No. The picture only counts when it is on the wall where people can see it. Same with a page. It only counts when it is live.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: You can bake the finest cake in the world, but if it stays in the kitchen, nobody at the table tastes it. Put it on the table. Then check that it is really there — not just that you baked it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Live is the truth and everything else is a claim. A baked file is a claim. A deployed worker is a claim. The page on their screen is the truth. The feed they scroll is the truth. Check the truth, not the claim, and never report a thing as live until their eyes can see it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- One welcome, not two: the letter carries the portrait, the welcome, and the button — a second entrance would only repeat it.
- A deploy is not proven by a clean upload — it is proven by the live page serving the new thing and the live binding showing on the worker.
- A fix that predicts its own failure mode and then hits it was a good note and an unproven patch — the note was right, the patch was not.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Twice in one evening the machine said done while the live thing said otherwise: a perfect bake that never reached the page, and a feed a full day stale that no bake could fix. Each time the cost was a day of notes no citizen could see and a page Shawn had to judge from a stale copy. Checking what is live is the cheapest check there is, and skipping it is the most expensive mistake there is.

notes.title: One Screen, One Idea
notes.subtitle: Ten notes about the viewport all distill to one recipe, written down as the Anatomy of a 10-star viewport: one screen, complete; one idea per viewpoint; real 3D objects, never flat; Bugatti luxury, never a golf cart; almost no text — the language and the icons do the work; warm and inviting; her, present, speaking as a friend; everything alive; everything a click away; numbers the hero; no pricing at the top — just "Start free now." The instance that asked the question was the entrance taller than one screen at desktop width, her portrait cut off at the bottom edge. The fix is not a smaller entrance. It is the rule: a viewpoint lives above the fold, whole, or it is not a viewpoint.

The same pass defined MAXESS as a scoring engine (15 questions, five answers worth 4/3/2/1/0, 60 max), filed the Academy code as Factory assets with the naming corrected, and answered Resolve's question by mail instead of escalating it. Different work, one standard: the screen is the experience, and the experience is judged whole, above the fold.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: One page of a picture book tells one part of the story. You do not need two pages to see one picture. If you have to turn the page to see her face, the picture is broken. One screen, one picture, all of it there.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A welcome mat is one mat, and you see all of it when you step up to the door. You should not have to step back to see the rest of it. One screen should welcome you completely, and then you walk on to the next room.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: A viewpoint is a moment, and a moment is complete or it is not a moment. What you see on the screen IS the experience: you never scroll to finish a thought, you scroll to arrive at the next one. One screen, one idea, one feeling, one thing to do — then the next. It flows like water.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- The fold is the boundary: everything in the viewpoint is above it, nothing cut off, nothing half-seen.
- One idea per screen — the entrance welcomes, the chart compares, the calculator earns; never two ideas fighting in one screen.
- The entrance sells the welcome and the free start; the levels below carry the prices.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A stranger decides in two seconds. If the first screen is taller than their screen, they never meet her — they meet a crop of her. The recipe is the test his eye applies to every page from here: "Is this the max level of experience I can give the user?" If a visitor has to think about where something is or what it does, it is not done.

notes.title: One Family, One Object
notes.subtitle: Ten notes about the chooser all point at one rule: when he shows you the object, take it and put it there — never recreate it in the same spirit. The finale button he showed is a black obsidian pill with the purple only in the star jewel and the halo; what got built was purple-on-purple, and his eye condemned it in plain words. The same rule runs through the rest of the round: one family of tier icons used everywhere, one color per period lighting its own blocks, one eye jewel opening the detail on every block, Max lit by default, the tier named "Naya Free" everywhere. Consistency is not decoration. It is what makes nine blocks read as one world.

layers.name: In A Nutshell

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten source notes are SN-2351 (a block lights up in the color that it is), SN-2352 (the eye button), SN-2353 (one good icon, used everywhere), SN-2354 (allowed is not sent), SN-2355 (one family in treatment, exclusive in glyph), SN-2356 (default to Max, and the tier is Naya Free), SN-2357 (take the shown object, never recreate it), SN-2358 (the Factory holds every digital asset), SN-2359 (the scorecard rides with the round), and SN-2360 (depth on Naya: the gauge ring). Rounds 14 to 17 fixed the chooser by giving each period its own color — Monthly green, Quarterly blue, Yearly gold — and by making the four tier icons one family: same jewel, same treatment, same size, different glyph. Round 15 put one eye jewel on every block, opening the detail built from the chart's own rows, with nothing invented. Round 18 lit Max by default and named the free tier "Naya Free" in every spot. Round 19 is the warning: the shown Academy button was black obsidian, and the rebuild was purple-on-purple until his eye stopped it. SN-2359 makes the scorecard ride with every round from here, and SN-2358 files the shown code as Factory assets so the next seat takes the real object instead of remembering it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If your friend shows you their favorite toy and asks you to bring it, you bring THAT toy. You do not build a new toy that looks a bit like it. Bring the real one. And if you have four toys that belong together, they should look like they belong together.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: When someone hands you the good dish and says "use this one," you use that dish. You do not go and make a copy of it from memory. And a set of dishes should match — same pattern, same size, different pictures. That is what makes a table look right.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Take the shown object. That is the whole law in four words. A shown object carries his eye in it — its shape, its colors, its light. Recreating it throws his eye away and keeps only your guess. And one family everywhere is the same law applied to the page itself: the pieces must be siblings, or the page is a pile of strangers.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- A screenshot, a link, or a page he shows is the deliverable itself — same shape, same colors, same jewel, same glow, placed on the page.
- One icon family, one color per period, one eye per block: the same piece, used everywhere it appears, never redrawn.
- The scorecard rides with the round — the maker scores their own work first, and the presentation carries it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every recreation is a second guess at a decision he already made. Each one costs a round, a rebuild, and his patience — and the page drifts further from the one world it is meant to be. Taking the object and reusing the family costs nothing and keeps the page whole. The difference between a page that feels designed and a page that feels assembled is exactly this rule.

notes.title: The Joins Are the Page
notes.subtitle: Ten notes about the Pricing page all say the same thing from different sides: the pieces are done, and the joins are what decide whether the page works. The nine Smart Links are proven — one real click moved the count from 110 to 111. The thank-you address lives in the PayPal account settings, not in any plan, and it must stay unset until the thank-you link is live. The thank-you page itself is blocked because the API it calls has no live host. A page is not done when its pieces are beautiful. It is done when the joins are proven.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Ten notes about the Pricing page all say the same thing from different sides: the pieces are done, and the joins are what decide whether the page works. The nine Smart Links are proven — one real click moved the count from 110 to 111. The thank-you address lives in the PayPal account settings, not in any plan, and it must stay unset until the thank-you link is live. The thank-you page itself is blocked because the API it calls has no live host. A page is not done when its pieces are beautiful. It is done when the joins are proven.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The ten source notes are SN-2341 (the banner, ten times better), SN-2342 (the thank-you address lives in account settings), SN-2343 (the tracking is wired — nine Smart Links proven), SN-2344 (the dashboard gauge fix), SN-2345 (the real portrait is in), SN-2346 (permission is revocable), SN-2347 (no dashes in domains), SN-2348 (the thank-you page is blocked on the API), SN-2349 (the calculator — the gauge is the hero), and SN-2350 (the entrance must be memorable). The design rounds made every piece better: the banner got its world-class statement, the portrait is her real face, the calculator's gauge is the hero, the entrance got its jewel pills. The system notes proved the plumbing: nine Smart Links mint to nine PayPal plans, each curl-verified, and one real click counted. But the same ten notes carry the gaps plainly: the thank-you page cannot ship until the API exists, the Auto Return URL must wait until the link is live, and the PayPal return is tracked as "returned from PayPal" — never payment-proven. Beauty in the pieces, honesty about the joins: that is the whole lesson.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build a beautiful toy car. It is shiny and fast-looking. But the wheels are not on. It will not roll. A page is like that car. The pretty parts are not enough. The parts must join up and work.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A lovely shop window means nothing if the door is locked. The customer must be able to walk in, pay, and come back out with what they bought. Check the door, not just the window.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: A page is a machine, and a machine is its connections. The pieces are the body; the joins are the life. Prove the joins, and the page is real. Admire the pieces and skip the joins, and you have a picture of a page, not a page.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- Done means the whole path works: click the block, reach PayPal, pay, come back to the thank-you link, and see the return counted.
- A setting that lives at account level (Auto Return) is set once, for everything — and only when the link it points to is live.
- A page that calls an API that does not exist yet is a page with dead buttons, and dead buttons never ship.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The Pricing page is the door into NayaNET. If the door looks beautiful but does not open, the stranger leaves. Every round that polishes a piece without proving its join spends the work and keeps the risk. Proving the joins is what turns ten beautiful rounds into one working page.

notes.title: Only the Real Gauges, Only the Real Flow
notes.subtitle: Ten notes close the day: the info jewel, the words that are the brand, the chart approved as a smart block, the start flow, the you're-hired block and the calculator, the real gauges, the smaller gauge, the A-star / B-star gauge law, PayPal as the billing system, and the Smart Link chain. The lesson underneath them all is one rule applied twice: only real parts on the page, and only the simplest flow for the money. A fake gauge becomes an A-star or a B-star. A billing system we would have to build becomes PayPal, which already exists. The flow a stranger takes is one button, nine blocks, and a return that is tracked.
