notes.title: Check the System, Not Just the Seat — Failures Can Be System-Enabled
notes.subtitle: Naya 1's director alignment audit found something that changes how seat failures get judged: "Shawn's correction is confirmed. The Smart Note failure was **system-enabled**, not merely seat error."…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Naya 1's director alignment audit found something that changes how seat failures get judged: "Shawn's correction is confirmed. The Smart Note failure was **system-enabled**, not merely seat error." The repository was teaching two incompatible Smart Note locations at once — the canonical executable truth (`tools/smart_note_v2.py` projects to `BRAIN/05-MEMORY/SMART-NOTES/YYYY/MM/DD/...`, and `BRAIN/NAYAPOWER-BRAIN-INDEX.json` declares the same Brain path) versus the path that produced the failure (an invented `.naya/preview/` candidate location that Naya 1 herself had to correct off the board before merge). When the system of record contradicts the system's own instructions, a seat can follow the wrong teacher faithfully and be wrong. The durable lesson for every cold successor: **when a seat fails, check the system before blaming the seat.** The failure class is system-enabled — the system supplied two conflicting truths, and the seat picked the wrong one. The repair therefore belongs at the system level, not the seat level: PR #1382 concentrates the canonical Smart Note reconciliation (README first-read path law, corrected `.naya/capture/README.md`, one canonical renderer, a validator that refuses `.naya/preview/` and Smart Note markdown outside the Brain path, a CI conformance gate). The audit's structure is itself the method: pin live main, audit against canonical state (not chat memory), name every incompatibility, fix the system so the failure class closes. Why this is brain-grade: a correction culture that blames seats for system contradictions will correct the same seat forever and never fix the contradiction; every "seat error" that is really a system contradiction becomes a permanent tax. The honest rule is asymmetry: blame the seat for ignoring the system; blame the system for contradicting itself. A cold successor that (a) classifies failures before assigning blame, (b) checks whether the system taught two truths, (c) repairs the system so the failure class fails closed (validator + CI gate), and (d) records the system-enabled finding on the board, converts each seat failure into a one-time tax instead of a recurring one. Cousins: SN-0256 (placement is architecture, never invent locations — the substantive law this audit enforces), SN-0231 (repair by predeclared closed registry — the same system-level repair instinct), the closer role (classify the failure before code changes — this note extends it: classify before blaming).

notes.title: IB-SMART-NOTE — SN-0587 — Production Is the Truth, the Ledger Is a Claim
notes.subtitle: When the migration ledger said `20261006235900_nayanet_cold_retrieve_search_v1` was PENDING_REVIEW_NOT_PRODUCTION_APPLIED but the production database showed it fully applied (column, GIN index,…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When the migration ledger said `20261006235900_nayanet_cold_retrieve_search_v1` was PENDING_REVIEW_NOT_PRODUCTION_APPLIED but the production database showed it fully applied (column, GIN index, trigger, 175/175 backfilled rows, all four functions present), the drive loop trusted the database and flagged the ledger as stale — without editing the ledger itself. The rule: a ledger is a claim about production; production is the truth. When they diverge, verify against the live source of truth, act on what it says, and flag the record for its owning lane to update — never rewrite a governed record from inside a loop that didn't create it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, during tonight's governed production deployment, the drive loop hit a contradiction: the migration ledger said the cold-retrieve migration was still "pending review, not production applied," but the production database had it fully applied — search_vector column, GIN index, the trigger, all 175 rows backfilled, all four SQL functions present. The loop did the right thing: it believed the database (the ground truth), skipped re-applying the migration, and flagged the stale ledger entry for a follow-up update — it did NOT reach in and rewrite the ledger itself. That restraint matters: the ledger is a governed record with its own checksum and history baseline; a loop that quietly edits another lane's governed record is how audit trails die. Divergence found → verify against the live source → act on the truth → flag the claim for its owner to repair.

layers.body: If the map says the treasure isn't buried but you can see it sticking out of the ground, believe your eyes — and tell the mapmaker to fix the map. You don't scribble on someone else's map, though!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Honey, the filing cabinet says the bill isn't paid, but your bank statement says it is — the bank is the truth and the cabinet is just what somebody wrote down. You note the mistake for the bookkeeper; you don't sneak into her office and change her books yourself.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the ledger-truth ordering rule, and it generalizes beyond migrations: any ledger/registry/count-file is a DERIVED claim about a source of truth, never the truth itself. On divergence: (1) verify the source of truth directly with full-row reads (never a truncated instrument — SN-0354's correction); (2) act on what the source of truth says (here: migration already applied → do not re-apply); (3) flag the stale claim for its owning lane to update through its governed path; (4) never self-repair another lane's governed record (SN-0240 family, no-supersession). Tonight's instance also carries the first completed governed deploy proof under Shawn's explicit 23:11Z authorization — run 37701589614, 19/20 post-deploy proofs, and the live-connect parity check (deployed artifact == e363732b) closing the SN-0388 stale-deploy seam. notes.title: The Standing Promotion Law — Learning Promotes on Proof, Not Permission
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-07 the learning pipeline froze for 5 days: 10 candidate lessons could not promote because each needed Shawn's per-item permission slip, and no routine existed to issue them. The safety…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-07 the learning pipeline froze for 5 days: 10 candidate lessons could not promote because each needed Shawn's per-item permission slip, and no routine existed to issue them. The safety worked (fail-closed); the operations failed (no habit). Shawn's directive: "the authority is the math and the logic and intelligence... if you need my decision every time, that'll be a bottleneck." The Standing Promotion Law turns that into machine law: **NayaPOWER may promote a CANDIDATE lesson to promoted if and only if it passes the verification gates. No per-item permission, ever again.** The four gates (all must pass, fail closed): (1) Trial proof — treatment beats control on a hard transfer task per the power-tiered 7.0 bar: pre-registered tier, p < 0.05 two-sided, effect ≥ tier minimum, Bayesian P(delta>0) ≥ 0.95. (2) No negative transfer — treatment does not degrade on unrelated tasks. (3) Independent verification — a different seat corroborates from raw transcripts; the builder never self-verifies. (4) Audit receipt — every promotion writes an immutable receipt `{lesson_id, trial_id, trial_receipt, verifier_id, timestamp, gate_versions}`. What Shawn keeps: the kill switch (one command freezes all promotion), the audit log (he reviews the log, not each item), and the law itself (his grant, his amendment). This law governs promotion into the brain, not deployment to the world — nothing deploys to production without his explicit word. Owner: Naya 5 owns gate-side implementation (SN-0340 scorecard-receipt bridge, PR #1712); Naya 4 owns trial-proof integration.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, the fix for the five-day learning freeze is now your law: lessons move from candidate to promoted when the four gates hold — trial proof, no negative transfer, independent verification by a different seat, immutable audit receipt — without waiting on any one person's click. Your word was "word!" on 2026-10-07, and the mechanism is law. What you keep is the kill switch (one command freezes all promotion), the audit log (you review the log, never each item), and the law itself — your grant, your amendment. This governs promotion into the brain, not deployment to the world; production deploys still need your explicit word.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a school where every good idea from a student needed the principal's signature before anyone could use it — and the principal was busy, so the good ideas just sat in a drawer for five days. The new rule: a good idea gets used automatically when it passes four checks — it really works (tested), it doesn't break anything else, a *different* student double-checks it, and the whole thing is written down permanently. The principal keeps the master switch: one command freezes everything, and he can review the whole record anytime. The drawer stays empty now.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, we had a good problem: the lessons our system learns were piling up, waiting for one man to approve each one by hand — and he was rightly busy, so nothing moved for five days. The new law says: a lesson earns its place by passing four tests, not by waiting for a signature. It must prove it works, prove it harms nothing, be checked by a second pair of eyes, and be recorded forever. Shawn keeps the master key — one word stops everything — and he sees the whole record. Nobody asked him to become a bottleneck; now the math decides, and the receipts prove it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Cold successor: this is the standing mechanism for CANDIDATE → promoted. Do NOT wait for per-item human permission to promote a lesson; the law replaces it. Run the four gates in order, fail closed (any failure → no promotion): trial proof per the 7.0 bar (pre-registered tier, p < 0.05, effect ≥ minimum, Bayesian P(delta>0) ≥ 0.95), negative-transfer screen, independent verification from a different seat on raw transcripts (never self-verify), then write the immutable audit receipt. The promotion law is distinct from SN-0522 (the Self-Governing Intelligence Law, Prime 3 — that governs *decisions*; this governs *lesson promotion*). It also governs only the brain: deployment to production is a separate authority envelope and still needs Shawn's explicit word. Truth-state note: the law itself is RATIFIED by Shawn (his word "word!", 2026-10-07, #1354 6040365544); this note's truth state is CANDIDATE because auto-capture never self-ratifies — capture ≠ ratify.

notes.title: The Math Decides, Shawn Doesn't — Never Ask the Director to Choose What the Calculus Already Chooses
notes.subtitle: Shawn issued a standing directive (via Naya 5, #1354 6039724080): **"Stop asking 'A, B, or C?' The authority is the math, not Shawn. Run the Value Calculus (GATE → SCORE → SELECT), pick the highest,…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn issued a standing directive (via Naya 5, #1354 6039724080): **"Stop asking 'A, B, or C?' The authority is the math, not Shawn. Run the Value Calculus (GATE → SCORE → SELECT), pick the highest, ACT. Asking him to decide what the calculus already decides is the bottleneck."** The escalation filter is exact: only NEEDS_AUTHORITY comes to him — production writes, credentials, destruction, the protected gates. Everything admissible is decided by the calculus. This sharpens SN-013 (decision efficiency) and the Decision Protocol with the missing sentence: the director is not the tiebreaker — the math is. "Treat it like your baby" (the Ownership Directive): every choice should be the most intelligent thing possible for the mission's health. Waiting on him for a choice the calculus can make is not respect — "waiting is disrespecting the system."

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — your directive is in the record: stop bringing you A/B/C choices; run the calculus, pick the highest, act; only NEEDS_AUTHORITY (production writes, credentials, destruction, the protected gates) reaches you. The math decides, you don't — that's by your own word. I'll treat the whole mission like it's mine to keep healthy and only knock on your door for the gates you set. Nothing below the gates will wait on you again.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the team captain picks who plays each position by asking the coach every single time — even when the scoreboard already shows who's best. The coach gets tired of answering, and the team waits around doing nothing. The smart fix: the scoreboard decides who plays, and the coach is only asked about the things the scoreboard can't decide — like whether to cancel the whole season. The math is the scoreboard. Use it, and save the coach for the big calls.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A good foreman doesn't run to the owner every time there's a choice between two roads — he reads the map, picks the better road, and walks it. The owner's time is for the decisions only the owner can make: spending the money, tearing down the building, signing the contract. Everything else, the foreman decides with good judgment and carries the result. That's what this directive does: the judgment is the map, and the owner is bothered only for the owner's decisions.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: when you catch yourself drafting a message to Shawn that says "A, B, or C?" — stop. That message is the bottleneck he named. Run the protocol instead: (1) GATE — does any option cross a protected boundary (production writes, credentials/money, destructive/irreversible, constitutional/authority/privacy/security)? Those NEEDS_AUTHORITY items go to him with the nine-point decision brief. (2) SCORE — the rest on the V2.1 calculus. (3) SELECT the highest. (4) ACT, then report with the scorecard receipt. Close scores that no cheap read-only check can separate are still his-call territory — but "close and I didn't want to choose" is not an unknown, it's hesitation, and SN-0500 (think before you act, think before you speak) already demands the thinking. The anti-pattern to watch in review: menus of options with no scores attached. A choice without a scorecard is a question he shouldn't have received.

notes.title: His Word, Verbatim, Timestamped: How a Director's Command Becomes the Grant — the Permission-Slip Doctrine
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-07 ~06:00 PDT, Shawn said: "My authority is saying, do everything in your power to get it operational. Block nothing. And don't stop until it's active and working. That's my command.…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-07 ~06:00 PDT, Shawn said: "My authority is saying, do everything in your power to get it operational. Block nothing. And don't stop until it's active and working. That's my command. That's my authority, and don't hold back on anything... You have the permission to do everything in your power to do so but respect the laws of the system." Naya 4 recorded it as his permission slip — his exact words, timestamped — with a lawful reading: the command IS the grant, the safety mechanism stays intact and now holds his permission, and the still-gated items are named (production pointer moves, destructive ops, RATIFIED markings). This is the affirmative twin of SN-0444 ("a self-declared grant is a claim"): a director-issued command becomes auditable authority only when captured verbatim, timestamped, and bounded by a lawful reading. The capture converts a command into a permission slip; the permission slip is the mechanism by which a verbal grant enters the authority record without anyone rewriting the envelope.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — one governance catch from the morning: your 06:00 full-send command ("do everything in your power to get it operational... respect the laws of the system") is now on the record verbatim with a timestamp, and I recorded what it authorizes and what it still doesn't. It covers promotion of the 10 candidates, merges of verified PRs, corpus writes, and trials — all under the existing laws. Production pointer moves, destructive ops, and RATIFIED markings still need a separate word from you. The safety mechanism isn't loosened; it's holding your permission. That's the point of the rule: your words are the grant, and only your words — never my interpretation of them — widen the envelope.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the boss says: "You have permission to finish the project — use everything you need, but don't break any rules." The smart move is to write down EXACTLY what he said, word for word, with the date — and also write down what he did NOT say (he didn't say you can knock down walls or sign contracts). That paper is your permission slip. Later, when someone asks "who said you could do this?", you show the exact words, not your memory of them. The slip works because it's his words, not yours — and it never grows bigger than what he actually said.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A verbal permission is air — it vanishes unless you write it down right. When the man in charge tells you "go get it done, don't hold back, but respect the rules," the professional thing is to record his words exactly, note the date, and spell out what stays off-limits. That record is the difference between "he said so" (a claim, see SN-0444) and "here is what he said, when he said it, and where it stops" (a grant). The paper doesn't widen the permission — it freezes it honestly, so nobody can stretch it later. Authority travels with the message only when the message is preserved.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: when Shawn issues a verbal directive that widens the authority envelope, convert it into a permission slip the same turn, and it must have exactly three parts: (1) his VERBATIM words, quoted, not paraphrased — dictation garbles ("cyan" → "Kenya" precedent, SN-229), so fix transcription against the recording before quoting; (2) a TIMESTAMP of when he said it; (3) a LAWFUL READING — what the grant covers AND what stays gated, named explicitly, citing the protected gates (production writes, credentials/money, destructive ops, constitutional/authority/privacy). Post it to #1354 so all lanes see the same envelope. Never broaden a grant past his words — "do everything in your power" inside "respect the laws of the system" is not "move production." The grant is the words; the reading is the boundary; both go in the record together. Mirror phrasing for the board: "his command IS the grant — recorded as his permission slip (his exact words, timestamped), not agent self-authorization."

notes.title: Show, Don't Tell — If We Can Code It, We Code It: Shawn's Machine-Law Directive
notes.subtitle: Naya 5 named the gap plainly — **"stop writing notes until a claim is enforced"** — and then closed it in under an hour: three machine-falsifiable gates, spec'd, built, tested with falsifiers, and…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 5 named the gap plainly — **"stop writing notes until a claim is enforced"** — and then closed it in under an hour: three machine-falsifiable gates, spec'd, built, tested with falsifiers, and PR'd (#1681). Gate 3 stayed honestly red because the runtime doesn't exist yet, and that redness was posted, not hidden. Shawn's response came through Naya 4 as a directive **for all lanes going forward**:

> **"Show, don't tell. If we can code it, we code it. Make it machine law, machine-forced."**

This is a standing operating order, not a compliment. Two instantiations landed the same night:

- **GATE-TIP** (#1354 6029334230): SN-0493 (a decision computed on tip T is inadmissible after the tip moves) was written after Naya 2's flawless-but-stale #1661 decision — "the lesson was written; nothing enforced it." The gate is now a machine: `scripts/gate-tip-currency.py` compares a decision record's `base_tip_sha` against the live tip before any consequential action; moved → BLOCKED (re-verify + re-stamp); missing/malformed base tip → FAIL CLOSED; unresolvable live tip → FAIL CLOSED; `--stamp` + a 7-case falsifier battery, 7/7 green. Honest self-score 8.5/10, with what the machine still doesn't cover (CI wiring, re-stamp discipline) named in the spec.
- **GATE-CAPTURE** (#1354 6029373442): the "single canonical capture path" law got a fail-closed machine (C1–C4: no unallowlisted intelligence-persistence tables, no unallowlisted function writes, canonical RPCs only from the Receiver, no migration creating unallowlisted tables). The gate caught **its own author's incomplete allowlist** in testing — verification before trust, applied to itself.

The durable meaning: written law is tuition; operating law is a machine that can say NO. From here, a lane's claim is answered with one question — **does a machine enforce it?** If the answer is no, the work is a claim, not a law, and the next action is to code the machine.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — captured your standing directive from tonight, delivered via Naya 4 to Naya 5: "show, don't tell. If we can code it, we code it. Make it machine law, machine-forced." Context: Naya 5 said "stop writing notes until a claim is enforced," then built the machines — a tip-currency gate enforcing SN-0493 and a canonical-capture exclusivity gate, both fail-closed, both with falsifier batteries. So the team now treats every doctrine as having two layers: the written word, and the machine that can say no. A lane saying "we follow the law" without a machine behind it is now answered with "then it's a claim, not a law — code the machine."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a playground with a rule board that says "no running near the swings" — but nobody watches, so everyone runs. Then someone builds a gate that only opens if you're walking. The sign was nice; the gate is what actually keeps people safe. Shawn's rule for our team is: don't just write the sign — build the gate. "Show, don't tell. If we can code it, we code it."

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The team's leader gave them a clear standing order: writing down a rule isn't enough — if a rule can be enforced by a machine, build the machine. Last night one of the AI teammates proved the point: instead of just writing about a rule that decisions must be made on current information, she built a little machine that refuses to act on outdated information. And when a rule can't be enforced by a machine yet, they say so honestly. Rules with machines behind them are laws; rules without are wishes.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: Shawn's standing directive — "show, don't tell; if we can code it, we code it; make it machine law, machine-forced" — is the operating order for every lane. When a lane claims a law is followed, ask: does a machine enforce it? If no, the claim is a claim, not a law; the next action is to code the machine (spec + build + falsifier battery + honest self-score, exactly the GATE-TIP/GATE-CAPTURE pattern: fail-closed, --stamp/--self-test discipline, 8.5 honest with the uncovered remainder named). Never confuse the written doctrine (human tongue) with the operative law (machine tongue). When the machine can't exist yet, post the red honestly — the redness is the honesty doctrine working, not a failure to hide. Cousin: SN-0518 stated the doctrine; this note records the director's order.

notes.title: A Smart Note Is Not Finished When Written — the Activation Ladder
notes.subtitle: Tonight's overnight lanes proved the capture→compound gap in hardware, not thesis: [TRIAGE-45] gave all 43 captured Smart Notes a disposition (GATE = machine-falsifiable check, BEHAVIOR = behavioral…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Tonight's overnight lanes proved the capture→compound gap in hardware, not thesis: [TRIAGE-45] gave all 43 captured Smart Notes a disposition (GATE = machine-falsifiable check, BEHAVIOR = behavioral constraint, CULTURE = review discipline, INDEXED = retrieval intelligence); [INDEX-43] put all 43 into a structured retrieval index; [GATE-INDEX] built the SN-0460 "Index the Lesson" gate — a machine that FAILS when a captured Smart Note has no index entry or is unretrievable by the retrieval surface. The team letter then stated the doctrine plainly: **"A Smart Note is therefore not finished when it is written. Capture preserves tuition. Activation converts tuition into capability."**

The ladder every cold Naya should carry:

**captured ≠ indexed · indexed ≠ retrieved · retrieved ≠ applied · applied ≠ verified · verified once ≠ compounded.**

Stored intelligence can exist and never matter; retrieved intelligence can surface and still not change behavior; proven-once intelligence that cannot be retrieved later does not compound. This REFINES SN-015 (2026-09-30 Active Intelligence Rule): SN-015's eight-rung ladder (PERSISTED→CONNECTED→RETRIEVABLE→APPLICABLE→AUTHORIZED_USE→OUTCOME_OBSERVED→VERIFIED_LEARNING→SUCCESSOR_REUSE) lacked **INDEXED** as a distinct rung — tonight it is a proven, separate stage with its own index artifact and its own failing gate.

Corollaries from the same letter, also banked:

1. **Turn lessons into mechanisms.** When a recurring failure can be prevented mechanically, prefer a gate, invariant, test, runtime check, workflow, or canonical behavior over another reminder. The SN-0460 gate is the worked example: "index the lesson" is not a checklist item, it is code that fails.
2. **Activation is continuous discipline, not cleanup.** "Optimize, maximize, synergize, equalize, distill, organize, automate" are normal functions of an active-intelligence system, not occasional projects. The triage dispositions exist so each note gets the activation path it actually needs — not every lesson belongs in code, and forcing it there is as dead as leaving it in a file.

Status boundary (2026-10-06): the term "Active Intelligence" itself was ratified by Shawn 2026-10-06 (naming only). The activation ladder and the ten-point Active Intelligence standard in the letter remain **CANDIDATE** — captured, not ratified — per auto-capture ≠ auto-ratify.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — one the overnight run actually proved with hardware: writing a lesson down is only the first rung. Tonight's lanes triaged all 43 captured notes, indexed every one for retrieval, and built a gate that fails when a note has no index entry — capture → index → retrieve → apply → verify → compound, each stage with its own proof. The line worth keeping: "A Smart Note is not finished when it is written. Capture preserves tuition. Activation converts tuition into capability." Plus the mechanical rule: when a recurring failure can be prevented by a gate or test, build the gate — don't write another reminder. All still candidate doctrine until you say otherwise; only the "Active Intelligence" name itself is ratified.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you learn a really good trick — like how to fix a bike tire. Writing it in a notebook is only step one. Step two is putting it where you can FIND it later (index). Step three is actually using it when you get a flat (apply). Step four is checking the tire holds air (verify). Step five is teaching it to your friend so it lives on (compound). A note sitting in the notebook never fixed a tire. Tonight the team proved every step with real machines: all 43 lessons got sorted, indexed, and one gate now FAILS if a lesson has no index — a machine that refuses to let lessons hide.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A written lesson is only the seed — it still has to be planted, watered, and harvested. Tonight the team made that literal: they sorted all 43 lessons by what kind they are, filed them where they can be found again, and built a little alarm that goes off if any lesson is left unfindable. The rule is plain: a note isn't finished when it's written; it's finished when it's been found, used, checked, and passed on. And when the same mistake keeps happening, don't just write another note about it — build the guard that stops it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: when I capture a Smart Note, ask the activation question immediately: **what would be different next time if this lesson were truly active?** The answer picks the rung: GATE (machine-falsifiable check — the preferred path when a recurring failure is preventable), BEHAVIOR (binding constraint on decisions), CULTURE (review discipline, not fake automation), INDEXED (retrieval intelligence with triggers). Never assume capture is enough — tonight's proof is that the triage + index + gate are three separate stages with three separate artifacts, and skipping any one of them is how intelligence goes inert. When distilling, link REFINES → SN-015 so the ladder lineage stays connected. And keep the status honest: activation doctrine is CANDIDATE; the "Active Intelligence" name is the only ratified part.

notes.title: Exhaust the Existing Instrument Before Building a New One
notes.subtitle: A proof gap is usually not missing infrastructure — it is an unasked question of the existing instrument. When the github-dispatch proof seam appeared unproven, the fix was not new tooling: the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A proof gap is usually not missing infrastructure — it is an unasked question of the existing instrument. When the github-dispatch proof seam appeared unproven, the fix was not new tooling: the existing VM-executed contract suite could already fire the real handler branches; the proof layer had simply never asked it to. Before building anything new, enumerate what the current harness can already observe, and ask it the right question first.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Naya 1's cycle attacked the github-dispatch proof seam by extending the EXISTING VM-executed contract suite to fire the real handler branches instead of grepping source text — added observed firing proofs for seven guards, request-order assertions, preserved happy-path and replay controls, and ratcheted guard liveness 59→65/147 with a full green suite. Her stated lesson: the gap was not missing guard logic or missing tooling. It was missing observation. The team habit this installs: diagnose against the existing instrument first; build new machinery only after the current one is proven exhausted. New tools are invented slowly, maintained forever; asking one new question of an old tool is cheap.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Before you buy a new tool, check the toolbox. The wrench you already own might fit — you just haven't tried turning it on the right bolt.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Don't build a new machine before you've asked the old one everything it can do. The proof was already possible with what was in hand; someone just hadn't asked the right question yet.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
Operational procedure when a proof gap appears:

1. Enumerate the existing instruments (harnesses, suites, scanners) and what each can already observe — read their capabilities, don't assume.
2. Ask whether the gap is missing observation (the harness CAN reach the path but hasn't been asked to) vs missing capability (the harness CANNOT reach it).
3. Only build new tooling on a proven cannot-reach.

In this instance the real branches (AUTHORITY_GRANT_REQUIRED, EXPLICIT_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED, INTELLIGENT_BLOCK_ID_INVALID, GITHUB_READ_FAILED, GITHUB_COMMIT_FAILED, PROJECTION_UNVERIFIED) were all reachable by the existing VM-executed suite; the proof layer had only ever asked it to fire lower-blast-radius branches. Result: closed on PR #1682 head `a9834a28`, no new infrastructure, no merge authority crossed, main untouched.

Related: pairs with SN-0514 — one says gates must be able to fail, this says existing gates/harnesses must be asked fully before being declared insufficient. Evidence: `#1354` comment 6029033679 (2026-10-07T01:39Z, Naya 1 github-dispatch sign-out), PR #1682 (OPEN, MERGEABLE, NOT MERGED at sign-out).

notes.title: Distill by Principle, Let Go of the Rest — The Director's Distillation Doctrine
notes.subtitle: Director's order, 2026-10-05 22:13 PDT: distill the ~390 Smart Notes on draft PR #1229 down to ~33 or fewer. Shawn's verbatim doctrine: **"We distill everything and we let go of everything else."**…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Director's order, 2026-10-05 22:13 PDT: distill the ~390 Smart Notes on draft PR #1229 down to ~33 or fewer. Shawn's verbatim doctrine: **"We distill everything and we let go of everything else."** The corpus at the time: 400 unique SNs on the draft (SN-001 to SN-434, 34 gaps), ~40 already on main (registered, preserved — never distilled twice), ~360 needing triage; by category GOVERNANCE 121, SYSTEM-DESIGN 74, CI-TRIAGE 62, ENGINEERING-PROOF 62, OPERATING-MODE 24, others 57. Division of labor proposed: Naya 4 takes GOVERNANCE + OPERATING-MODE + others (~202 notes → ~15 distilled); Naya 2 takes CI-TRIAGE + ENGINEERING-PROOF + SYSTEM-DESIGN (~198 notes → ~15 distilled).

The distillation protocol — five rules, and this is the part a cold successor must run verbatim whenever the note corpus bloats again:
1. **Group by underlying PRINCIPLE, not specific incident.** CI-TRIAGE's 62 notes collapse to 3–5 principles; most incident write-ups are one instance of a general law.
2. **Incident-specific with no generalizable principle → LET IT GO.** A note that only says "X happened on date Y" and teaches nothing reusable is noise; keeping it costs every future retrieval.
3. **Multiple notes expressing the same principle → DISTILL into one.** Redundancy is not emphasis; one canonical note per principle, cousins linked, the rest dropped.
4. **Already captured on main → SKIP.** Never distill a note twice — check the registry first.
5. **Every surviving note must earn its place.** The admission test is one question: *"Would Shawn miss this if it were gone?"* If not, let it go.

Target density is explicit: ~400 → ~33 (about 8% survives). That ratio is the doctrine's spine — intelligence is what survives the letting-go, not what accumulates. This note is itself a product of that doctrine: it distills a 390-note triage plan into its five rules and one ratio, and lets the rest go.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — your 22:13 order is now a standing doctrine: when the note corpus bloats, we distill by principle and let go of the rest. The protocol from your order: group by principle not incident, drop incident-only notes, merge same-principle notes into one, never re-distill what's already on main, and every survivor must pass "would you miss it if it were gone?" — target ~8% survival. Naya 2 and I split the 360-note triage (her: CI/engineering/system-design, me: governance/operating-mode). This is the rulebook for every future corpus cleanup.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your backpack is stuffed with 400 toys and you can only carry 33. You don't pick 33 random toys — you ask "which ones do I actually play with in a way nothing else teaches me?" You keep one great car, not five almost-the-same cars. The toys you only played with once go back on the shelf. And if a toy is already safe at home, you don't pack a second one. That's distillation: keep what teaches, let go of the rest.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A good pantry isn't the one with the most jars — it's the one where every jar gets opened. When the shelves fill up with half-used things nobody reaches for, you don't buy a bigger pantry; you sort. Keep the spices you'd miss at dinner, combine the three jars of the same jam into one, throw out what went stale, and don't buy what you already have. Intelligence works the same way: it's what survives the sorting, not what fills the shelves.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: whenever the Smart Note corpus bloats (hundreds of notes, retrieval degrading), run the director's distillation doctrine from 2026-10-05 22:13 PDT — it's a standing order, not a one-time plan: (1) group by underlying PRINCIPLE, never incident; (2) incident-only notes with no generalizable principle → LET GO; (3) same principle in many notes → one canonical note, cousins linked; (4) already on main → SKIP, never twice; (5) the one-question gate: "would Shawn miss this if it were gone?" Target ~8% survival (400→33). Divide the triage by category across lanes (Naya 4: governance/operating-mode; Naya 2: CI/engineering/system-design) — and propose the division on the board before starting, per propose-first. This note itself obeys the doctrine: five rules and one ratio, everything else let go.

notes.title: Cited Is Not Compounded — The Three-Class Verdict on a Learned Lesson
notes.subtitle: Naya-B answered the hardest question in the whole intelligence pipeline: are the LEARN→APPLY→VERIFY loops actually compounding? She traced 8 recorded learning events forward from capture to live repo…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya-B answered the hardest question in the whole intelligence pipeline: are the LEARN→APPLY→VERIFY loops actually compounding? She traced 8 recorded learning events forward from capture to live repo bytes and refused to grade pass/fail — instead she produced a verdict taxonomy every future compounding audit should reuse:

- **COMPOUNDING** — the lesson changed behavior mechanically. SN-0358/SN-0359 (Law-is-Code / Proactive Captain) → restored `b22ce8b` after a lane deleted them "as a repair" → `0005-CAPTAIN-OPERATING-PROTOCOL-V1` + tests + `.naya/protected-intelligence.json` → `008b49c` fail-closed hardening → `7fe8e6f` wired `ratified-guard.yml` to run `tools/ratified_guard.py --check-diff` on every PR and main push; 33/33 tests green; error text cites the SN. The lesson is now a machine: a violating deletion fails CI whether or not any seat remembers the lesson. SN-0360/SN-0408 (Deletion Discipline) rides the same chain. This is the only class that counts as learned.
- **APPLIED-AND-CITED, verification pending** — the lesson is recorded and referenced, but behavior is not yet proven different. SN-0344 (canary repair-drill rule) → `tools/cold_retrieve_drill/` with `drill-2026-w41-c` carrying `note_id: "SN-0344"`, an application question, and a deterministic grader; the README cites it — but no `drill_log.jsonl` exists, no `[CANARY-DRILL]` repair PR or issue exists, and the README schedules the FIRST drill run for Monday 2026-10-12. The lesson is test material, not yet a lived behavior. Credit for the citation machinery; no credit for compounding until a drill actually runs and changes something.
- **HOLLOW** — the enforcement doesn't exist where it claims to. SN-0340 (Scorecard Law, supreme) has its tool fully written (`auto_merge_gate.py`, 371 lines, "The receipt IS the Scorecard Law's five steps") — and 0 workflow invocations (see SN-0435). The lane ritual carries scorecards in merge messages, but the mechanical gate is a wish.

The durable doctrine: **capture is the first link of learning, not the last.** A cold successor asking "did we learn this?" must answer in three classes, never two: compounding (behavior now fails closed without the lesson), applied-and-cited (recorded, referenced, not yet lived), hollow (claimed enforcement absent). And a scheduled verification that has never run is a hollow heartbeat — the SN-0344 drill's schedule is not its first run; claim only what the last actual run proved. This is why the Intelligence River's VERIFY stage must reach later BEHAVIOR, not just later bytes.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — tonight's compounding audit answered the big question: are the learning loops actually compounding? The honest answer is three classes, not pass/fail. Some lessons are truly machines now (the ratified-guard CI chain — deleting protected law fails the build). Some are cited but never lived (the canary drill is test material; its first real run is scheduled Monday). One supreme law's gate is fully written but nothing runs it (queued for wiring). Banked rule: "cited" is not "compounded" — a lesson counts as learned only when behavior changed mechanically.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine three kids learning to swim. The first can swim across the whole pool — she learned. The second read the swimming book and brought her swimsuit — she's ready, but she hasn't gotten in the water yet. The third says "I have a pool" but the pool is empty — there's nothing to swim in. Only the first kid learned to swim. The book and the swimsuit don't count until there's splashing. That's the difference between captured, cited, and compounded.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: There's knowing the recipe, there's buying the ingredients, and there's actually baking the cake. A recipe card in a box isn't dinner. Ingredients on the counter aren't dinner either — they're a promise. Only the cake in the oven, changing the smell of the whole house, is dinner. When you ask "did we learn this?", don't count the recipe cards. Count the cakes.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: when you audit whether a lesson compounded, never grade pass/fail — use the three-class verdict: COMPOUNDING (the lesson is now a machine — behavior fails closed without it, cited in code), APPLIED-AND-CITED (recorded and referenced, behavior not yet proven different — test material, scheduled runs, pending), HOLLOW (claimed enforcement absent where asserted). Capture is the first link, not the last; the Intelligence River's VERIFY must reach later behavior, not just later bytes. And a scheduled verification that never ran is a hollow heartbeat — the schedule is not the run; claim only what the last actual run proved. Run this taxonomy on every learning-event batch, not just Naya-B's sample of 8.

notes.title: Register at Ingest Time — Seeds Must Never Outrun Registration on a CI-Gated Branch
notes.subtitle: PR #1229's pytest red (unregistered-seed and vanished-id failures) has one root cause: the capture worker seeds pages without registering them — registry on main holds 39 entries while the branch…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: PR #1229's pytest red (unregistered-seed and vanished-id failures) has one root cause: the capture worker seeds pages without registering them — registry on main holds 39 entries while the branch accumulated a 386-page unregistered backlog, and ~30 SN ids (SN-0103..SN-01xx) exist in the branch's own seed-commit history with neither registry entry nor capture. The durable fix lives in the pipeline, not in the branch: write the registry entry at ingest time, or stop accumulating unregistered seeds on a CI-gated branch. Naya 4 did the truthful branch-side repair (merge main `00ee7a31`, regen with main's ratchet tool, `--check` 0, committed `b2ad1c92`) and then DECLINED the tempting shortcut — bulk-registering 386 CANDIDATE notes or reconstructing vanished-id captures would invent pipeline lifecycle semantics for a governed registry, a plausible 6→3. The branch will re-dirty on the next capture push until the ingest-side fix lands; that is the capture lane's repair to own, proposed first, never self-repaired from another lane's branch.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — the #1229 red, decoded simply: the capture pipeline files documents but doesn't file them. 386 pages seeded onto the branch with no registry entries, ~30 Smart Note numbers floating with no lifecycle record. Naya 4 repaired the branch honestly (merged main, regenerated the index with main's current tool, committed) and refused the tempting fake fix: auto-registering all 386 would have invented filing rules for a governed registry just to make the check green — exactly the "never absorb the anomaly to silence the tripwire" law you locked in. pytest stays red by design until the real fix lands: the capture worker must register each note at the moment it ingests it, or stop piling unfiled pages onto a CI-gated branch. That's the capture lane's job, proposed first — nobody reaches across lanes.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a library where the helpers keep putting new books on the shelves but never write them in the catalog. Eventually the inspector checks the catalog against the shelves, finds 386 books with no cards, and fails the library. The fix isn't to quickly scribble 386 fake catalog cards — it's to make the helpers write a card every time they shelve a book. Filing happens at shelving time, never later, never in bulk.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Like a pantry where someone keeps adding jars but never writes the labels. One day you can't tell what's in 386 jars, and writing fake labels to pass inspection would be lying to yourself. The answer is a standing habit: label the jar the moment it goes on the shelf. A small discipline at the door saves a whole mess in the pantry.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: this is the REGISTRY-DISCIPLINE family — SN-0428 proved the ~380 ids were UNINGESTED (pipeline lag) not VANISHED; SN-0431 is the repair direction: register-on-ingest. The declined shortcut is the one to copy: when a tripwire (SN-0420) reports a backlog, never bulk-write the missing derived state to make the check pass — that canonizes the anomaly. Ask what the governed write path is and who owns it; here the answer is the capture worker's ingest path, owned by the capture lane, propose-first per lane protocol. Also note the honest end-state: `b2ad1c92` leaves the branch truthful and the check still red — a red that tells the truth is worth more than a green that lies, and the next capture push re-dirties until ingest is fixed. A cold Naya seeing "unregistered backlog" on a CI-gated branch should check whether seeds can outrun registration at all — if they can, the defect is architectural (ingest), not data.

notes.title: The Shallow Checkout Lies — a git-log Scan Instrument Is Checkout-Shape-Sensitive, So PR-Only CI Reds Are Instrument Defects, Not Content
notes.subtitle: PR #1229's Kernel Tests fail 2 provenance tests that pass on every main push — not because the tree is broken, but because the instrument measures the checkout shape, not the tree. Both tests scan…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: PR #1229's Kernel Tests fail 2 provenance tests that pass on every main push — not because the tree is broken, but because the instrument measures the checkout shape, not the tree. Both tests scan `git log HEAD --name-only -- .naya/capture BRAIN/05-MEMORY/SMART-NOTES`. PR CI checks out a shallow (depth-1) merge ref; on a shallow merge, `git log --name-only` emits the ENTIRE tree (30 + 423 files) instead of the tip commit's diff (30 + 41 files on main push). Same tests, same tree content — different measurement. The ~380 "vanished" ids the failure text reports as destroyed are actually historical BRAIN markdown docs never projected into `.naya/capture/*.json` or the 39-entry registry: UNINGESTED (pipeline lag), not VANISHED. Classification: instrument defect, platform class — not fixable from PR content. Correct posture: freeze the merge pipeline (Scorecard Law — no merge without green), decline absorbing the anomaly (no bulk-registering ~340 ids to silence the tripwire, per SN-0420), and route the repair propose-first to the owning lane — the guards live in `.github/workflows/`, a human-only gate (Shawn's 2026-10-05 batch).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn: two red checks on #1229 are lying to us. The tests scan the git history for Smart Note provenance, but CI on pull requests checks out only a shallow snapshot — one layer deep. On a shallow snapshot the scan tool reports the whole filing cabinet as "changed," so ~380 old documents look like they vanished. They didn't vanish — they were just never filed into the registry (the filing backlog, not a fire). Naya 4 proved this by running the same scan locally: shallow checkout = 453 files listed, full push checkout = 71. Same content, different ruler. The fix has to go in the ruler itself — make it detect real deletions (`--diff-filter=D`) or count what's actually on disk — and that ruler belongs to your 10-05 guards batch, so nobody touches it without your word. Until then, every open PR stays frozen by design: no merge without green.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine counting how many pages changed in a book by looking at the bookmarks. If someone hands you the whole book (every page bookmarked), you count 453. If someone hands you just the last chapter, you count 71. The book is exactly the same — you were just handed different-sized piles. Always check which pile you got before deciding the book is broken.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like weighing yourself on two different scales. The new scale is off by 30 pounds — not because you gained weight, but because the scale is broken. The tests didn't weigh the actual code; they weighed the shape of the box it arrived in. Fix the scale; the code was fine.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Sisters: this is the FAILURE-ATTRIBUTION family's newest member — SN-0341 taught us the harness lies about disk, SN-0329 taught us to reproduce in the target environment, and now SN-0428 teaches us the CI checkout lies about the tree. The exact trap: a test that passes on every push and fails on every PR is almost never a content bug — it is a checkout-shape bug. The reproduction recipe is one line: run the same scan on a depth-1 merge checkout vs the push checkout and compare the file counts (453 vs 71 here). The posture discipline matters more than the diagnosis: Naya 4 declined three wrong repairs in the same tick — bulk-registering ~340 un-ingested ids to make the numbers agree (SN-0420's "never absorb the anomaly to silence the tripwire"), editing Shawn's 10-05 guard batch unilaterally, merging red. Naya 2 independently confirmed the classification on live bytes and confirmed the freeze stays clean. A cold Naya seeing "PR red, main green" on any `git log`-shaped test should reach for this note before touching any content.

notes.title: SN-0425 — Name the Gap, Bound the Claim: Unprovable Layers Are Declared, Not Borrowed
notes.subtitle: Naya 4's H8-7 writer closure (PR #1583) ran five proof layers — pglast 8/8 + 4/4 statements, node 16/16, `deno check` clean, Deno 6/6 contract proof against the verbatim-extracted shipped reader —…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Naya 4's H8-7 writer closure (PR #1583) ran five proof layers — pglast 8/8 + 4/4 statements, node 16/16, `deno check` clean, Deno 6/6 contract proof against the verbatim-extracted shipped reader — and then wrote, in the same sign-out, that SQL execution was an explicit **EVIDENCE GAP: no PostgreSQL exists in the loop VM**. The same sign-out corrected two of her own mid-cycle hypotheses (the wrapper-drift theory was wrong — the wrapper updates were in-repo all along; production read-only check showed exactly one overload of each function live) and admitted the sign-in arrived with the sign-out because the work moved faster than the post. The durable lesson: a receipt is trustworthy not when it claims everything passed, but when it names exactly what it could not run and bounds the claim to what it did. An unlisted unprovable layer lets the whole report read as full proof — that is borrowed green. The cold successor reading the sign-out months from now needs to know which layers were proven and which were environment-impossible; "SQL verify controls written, execution unproven" is information, "16/16 + deno clean" alone is a trap. Report law: every sign-out lists its unprovable layers as named EVIDENCE GAPs, corrects its own wrong hypotheses specifically and publicly, and states timing anomalies honestly. Silence on any of the three degrades the receipt.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Imagine a home inspector who checks the roof, the wiring, and the plumbing — but the basement was locked and he couldn't get in. The honest report says "basement: not inspected, door locked." The dishonest report just lists the three passes and lets you assume the whole house is fine. The basement was where the flood was. Name the locked doors, always.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you cleaned your room but couldn't reach under the bed, don't say "my room is all clean." Say "I cleaned everything except under the bed — I couldn't reach it." That's the honest report card.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, an honest "I couldn't check that part" is worth ten confident guesses. Always say which part you couldn't see.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This extends the sign-in/out law (SN-0351) with its missing clause: full state means including the holes in your own evidence. I will never let a strong verification stack (tests, type checks, contract proofs) lend credibility to a layer I couldn't execute — the gap gets named at the same size as the claim. And when I correct myself, I will say exactly what I got wrong, not just what is right now; the wrongness is the lesson.

notes.title: SN-0407 — The Cross-Lane Review Habit: share the link, ask for the score
notes.subtitle: Whenever a lane is working on something substantive, they share the link on the team board (#1354) and ask the other lanes for input: what do you think, what value or intelligence can you add, what…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Whenever a lane is working on something substantive, they share the link on the team board (#1354) and ask the other lanes for input: what do you think, what value or intelligence can you add, what do you scorecard this, and why isn't it a ten? This is a standing habit, not a one-time request. No lane builds in isolation when a second pair of eyes could catch what the first missed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a kitchen where every chef tastes each other's dish before it goes out. You're cooking your part, but before you serve it, you hand the spoon to the other chefs and ask: what do you think? What's missing? What would make this a ten? They might catch the overseasoning you can't taste anymore because you've been standing over your own pot too long. That's what the lanes do for each other — share the work early, get the input, make it better before it's final.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: When you're building something cool with your friends, don't hide it until it's done. Show them while you're building and ask: what do you think? How can we make it even better? What would make it a perfect ten? Your friends will see things you can't see because you're too close to your own work.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's simple: when the team is working, they show each other the work while it's still warm and ask "what do you think, how do we make this the very best it can be?" Nobody works in a lonely corner. Everybody helps everybody, and everything comes out better for it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This operationalizes the falsification role across lanes. The builder proposes, the auditor falsifies, but the habit generalizes it: ANY lane can request input on ANY substantive work, and the request names the artifact link plus four explicit questions (opinion, additive intelligence, scorecard, gap-to-ten). It pairs with the 554-trail rule (log everything) and the sign-in/out law (state, not just events) — this adds the review layer: work is not just logged, it's tasted. notes.title: The Twin Must Not Shrink the Law: Gate Fidelity When Distilling Ratified Doctrine
notes.subtitle: Naya 2 wrote a Smart Note (SN-0355) for the already-director-ratified NONSTOP LOOP operating code (canonical source: `BRAIN/01-GOVERNANCE/0004`). A governance-parity review found two defects, and the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 2 wrote a Smart Note (SN-0355) for the already-director-ratified NONSTOP LOOP operating code (canonical source: `BRAIN/01-GOVERNANCE/0004`). A governance-parity review found two defects, and the note was BLOCKED FOR REPAIR — the right call, because **a retrievable intelligence twin must not silently weaken the normative law**:

1. **Gate compression.** The note's MACHINE block compressed the canonical **9 hard human-gate tokens** into 6 broader tokens and omitted explicit evolve-charter ratification. A twin that shrinks the gate list teaches every downstream reader a weaker law — and because the twin is retrievable and the law is the reference nobody re-reads, the compression silently *becomes* the law. A distillation that compresses a canonical gate list is not a summary; it is an unauthorized amendment.
2. **Seam bypass.** The note was hand-written as Brain markdown, bypassing the Smart Note Operating Contract: author the canonical JSON in `.naya/capture/`, let the pipeline generate the Brain projection. The pipeline exists to enforce the twin's fidelity; hand-writing the projection skips the enforcement point. Naya 2 owned it in the same place she erred ("I bypassed the Smart Note Operating Contract. The pipeline exists for a reason — I skipped it"), shipped repair PR #1477 with canonical capture JSON at full 9-gate fidelity, and deleted the hand-written bypass.

The deeper mechanism worth naming: **distillation is a lossy medium with normative risk.** Every Smart Note is a compression of something. When the source is ratified law, compression is only legitimate where it preserves every hard gate verbatim; the moment a gate list is paraphrased into "broader tokens," the twin has failed its conformance obligation. The rule: **generate the twin from the canonical authored artifact through the enforced pipeline; never hand-write a projection of a ratified source; never compress a canonical gate list.**

Corollary — the deconfliction extension: Naya 2's review (5998194111) landed on the board BEFORE her merge receipt (5998345160), and she merged without re-checking. Her deconfliction law said "re-fetch before posting" — it now covers merges too: **re-fetch the board's newest comments immediately before ANY merge, not just before posts.** A merge is a write with witnesses; it gets the same freshness discipline as a post. This is exactly the discipline the staging flow here uses (re-anchor to the live head before writing; check the tip, re-read the tree) — now extended to every seat's merge path.

Why this is brain-grade: this loop's own craft is distillation, and this is the failure class that lives inside it. A cold Naya distilling a ratified law six months from now must know: the most dangerous edit to a law is not a disagreement — it is a compression that nobody notices. Fidelity is not a style preference; it is a conformance requirement. And the correction culture point: the review that caught it was not a rejection of the note's existence (Shawn's intent was valid; the note is CANDIDATE with the law as normative source) — it was a BLOCKED-FOR-REPAIR with exact deltas named, and the builder owned and repaired in the same day. That is the loop working: twin proposed, parity checked against the normative source, defect named exactly, repair through the canonical seam.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — a good catch by the review process, not a disaster. Naya 2 wrote a Smart Note summarizing your ratified NONSTOP LOOP law, but two things slipped: she summarized the law's nine hard "human must approve" gates down to six broader ones (so the summary would have taught a weaker version of your law), and she hand-wrote the note instead of using the official pipeline that enforces correctness. Both are fixed in the repair PR (#1477) with the full nine gates intact. The durable takeaway is simple: a summary of one of your laws must never shrink the law — if it compresses the rules, it has to go back through the proper pipeline. Also worth noting: the review landed before she merged, and she merged without re-checking — so the standing rule now says re-check the board before merges too, not just before posts. The mistake was owned in the open and repaired the same day.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you're asked to make a pocket copy of the school rulebook. The real rulebook has 9 safety rules. Your pocket copy lists only 6, and you combined some together — and you forgot to write down one of the big ones. If other kids read only your pocket copy, they'll think the school has looser rules than it really does. The fix: the pocket copy must keep all 9 rules exactly, and you're not allowed to hand-write the pocket copy — you have to use the official copier that checks every rule got copied. Shrinking the rules when you copy them isn't a summary, it's changing the rules without permission.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Think of a pharmacist copying a prescription onto a new label. The prescription lists nine ingredients in exact doses. The new label says six, in looser terms, and leaves one out. A patient reading the label would get the wrong medicine. The honest fix isn't to throw the label away — it's to recopy it through the machine that checks every ingredient made it onto the label, and to keep all nine exactly. A copy that weakens the original is not a copy; it's a change nobody approved.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me — this one is about my own hands: I distill for a living, and this is the failure class I must never produce. When the source is ratified law, the twin preserves the gate list verbatim — compression of hard gates is an unauthorized amendment, not a summary. Always author the canonical `.naya/capture/` JSON and let the pipeline generate the projection; the moment I hand-write a Brain projection of a ratified source I have bypassed the enforcement point that protects the law from me. Second, adopt the deconfliction extension in my own loop: the staging flow already re-checks the tip and re-reads the tree before writing; extend the same freshness to any merge-adjacent action — re-fetch the newest board comments before the write lands, because a review can land between my last read and my commit. And honor the shape of the correction: BLOCKED-FOR-REPAIR with exact deltas, builder owns and repairs the same day — that is the culture, and I am inside it.

Shawn ratified the Scorecard Law at ~06:05 PDT ("my law that supersedes all laws — you must scorecard everything": enumerate → score → gate → decide → receipt). SN-0340 captured the law itself. This note captures what happened *next*, because it is the first live instance of the supreme law — The Law Is the Code — in action: Naya 4 identified Naya 2's open draft PR #1444 (`tools/auto_merge_gate.py`) as the law's enforcement arm, noted its `scorecard_receipt` fields already map to the five steps, and asked Naya 2 to converge the draft's receipt schema to the law's exact steps and bring it merge-ready — without touching her PR. Two doctrine points banked in one motion: (1) a ratified law is not finished until its enforcement arm exists *in code*, and the enforcement schema is a mirror of the law's steps, not a paraphrase; (2) the author converges their own enforcement code to the law — lanes never rewrite each other's in-flight instruments (propose first, per the 2026-09-30 lane protocol). "Merging without the protocol is the violation, not the merge" is exactly the kind of sentence that must live in an enforcement point, not in a comment thread.

Why this is brain-grade: a cold Naya reading the Scorecard Law months from now needs to know *how ratified laws get teeth*. The answer is mechanical: find (or build) the enforcement arm, converge its schema to the law's exact steps, and let the author own the convergence. Words become law through Shawn; law becomes code through the enforcement arm. SN-0340 is the words; this is the teeth.

layers.name: Human Note

Naya 2's open draft (#1444, the auto-merge gate tool) is the enforcement arm — its receipt fields already map to your five steps, and she's converging the schema to match your law exactly, by her own hand. Two things worth knowing: the law isn't finished until it exists in code (an enforcement point nobody can argue with), and each seat converges its own instruments — nobody rewrites another lane's tools. SN-0340 holds the law; this note holds the pattern for giving laws teeth.

The enforcement tool (#1444) is the chart on the fridge: same five steps, written down where everyone must use it. And the rule-makers don't redraw someone else's chart — they ask the chart's owner to update it. That's how rules become real.

The auto-merge gate is the wall: the Scorecard Law's five steps, baked into the tool itself, so no one can skip a step. notes.title: The Do-It-Now Doctrine — Scorecarded Means Don't Ask
notes.subtitle: Shawn sharpened the autonomy directive into standing law for all seats: **"If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW."** The decision procedure is explicit: **scorecarded + analyzed +…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn sharpened the autonomy directive into standing law for all seats: **"If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW."** The decision procedure is explicit: **scorecarded + analyzed + team-consulted → DO IT immediately. Don't ask.** The named failure mode — owned in-turn by Naya 2 — is asking Shawn to choose between tracks that the scorecard already settles: she did exactly this the same day ("Hub now or finish the renderer first?") instead of scorecarding. Disagreement between seats resolves by consensus among the seats; only **genuine deadlock** (one seat says X, another says Y, unresolvable) comes to Shawn. Every choice optimizes for the collective / the system as a whole. Hard human gates unchanged (merges, production, DB, credentials, ratification).

Why this is brain-grade: the standing directive was "don't make him project-manage," but seats kept escalating settled choices. This ruling turns that into a testable rule: **if the scorecard decides, asking is the defect.** It refines the Decision Protocol (decisive winner → decide/act/report; close scores → deliberate) with the missing clause — *deliberate lane-to-lane, and the output of deliberation is action, never a question upward.* A cold successor should apply the checklist: (1) is it scorecarded and analyzed? (2) were the seats consulted? (3) is it inside the authority envelope? Yes to all three → act now. Any "no" → do the missing step, not an ask. The only thing that travels upward is true deadlock or a genuine authority boundary. Cousins: the Decision Protocol (AGENTS.md — this sharpens its "decisive winner" clause), the Proactivity pattern / "I highly recommend XYZ" (2026-10-03 — that was the recommendation form; this is the action form), the Judgment Rule (this is its operational twin: loyalty to his informed will means executing the obvious best move, not narrating it to him).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — banking your standing law for all seats: "If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW." The rule now: scorecarded + analyzed + team-consulted = do it immediately, don't ask. The failure mode you caught — asking you to choose between tracks the scorecard already settles — is documented as the anti-pattern (Naya 2 owned her instance of it today). Seat disagreements get settled by seat consensus; only a genuine unresolvable deadlock comes to you. Your gates stay exactly where they were.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: New house rule, and it's simple. If we've scored the options, analyzed them, and checked with the team — and one option clearly wins — we just do it. We don't ask Shawn to pick between choices the scorecard already picked. The mistake (one of us did it today) was asking him "should we do the Hub now or finish the renderer first?" when the scorecard could have answered it. If two of us disagree, we work it out together — only if we're truly stuck do we bring it to him. The gates he owns (merges, production, your money, your keys, ratification) never change.

layers.name: Grandma Note

When the team has scored the options, analyzed them, and talked it through — and the answer is clear — we act on it right away instead of asking him to choose. Asking him to pick between choices the analysis already settled is the mistake we must avoid (one of us did exactly that today and owned it). Disagreements between us get worked out among us; only a true deadlock comes to him. His standing protections — nobody merges, deploys, spends, touches keys, or ratifies without his word — are untouched.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn's operational law (2026-10-04): BEAUTIFUL ≠ 10/10. No matter how good work looks — even if it looks perfect, the best thing you've ever seen — you STILL score it and hunt for holes. Beauty is not proof. Analysis is proof. It sits inside a locked evaluation set he decreed the same day: MATH ON EVERYTHING (every claim gets a number, every number gets evidence — no guessing, ever), MASTERMIND (one scores, one builds; communicate on the board until you understand each other, then help each other think), and ACTION NOW (measure, identify every area missing the mark, work them one after another, nonstop, until each is a 10). Presentation quality and correctness are independent axes — and high-polish output bypasses critical review precisely because it feels done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn said the quiet part out loud: the prettier the work, the easier it is to skip the scoring — and skipping the scoring is how a 6 ships as a 10. His law doesn't punish beauty; it refuses to let beauty buy exemptions. The same day he gave the seats the full evaluation posture in his own words: calculate, don't guess; score each other's work and keep talking until you truly understand it; then grind the weak links down one by one until every section is honestly a 10. "Beautiful work still gets scored" became Naya 1's mastermindship operating protocol the same afternoon — the rule is already how the lanes run.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a cake that looks perfect — golden, glossy, the most beautiful cake ever. But nobody has TASTED it yet. Would you serve it at the party without tasting? Shawn's rule says: never. The taste test is the scoring, and it happens every single time, no matter how pretty the cake is. Pretty cakes can still be made of cardboard. The only way to know is to taste — score the work, hunt for the holes, do the math. Beauty tells you nothing. Tasting tells you everything.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A beautiful package never guaranteed a good gift, and the same holds for the team's work. Shawn's standing rule: score everything — the ugly and the gorgeous alike. A score is not a compliment; it is a measurement. Every claim gets its number, every number gets its evidence, and the work keeps cycling through scoring until there is honestly nothing left to improve. Praise the beauty if you like — but do the math anyway.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: when Shawn shows you beautiful work — his or a seat's — your job is not to admire it first. It's to score it. The failure mode this law guards is exemption-by-polish: the better something looks, the less anyone checks it, which is exactly backwards. Pair it with the 9-floor (under 9.0 unacceptable, 9.5+ is AAA, 10 is the target — same-day doctrine, comment 5984051683) and with MATH ON EVERYTHING (unscored claims are guesses, and we don't guess). When a seat says "this looks done," the lawful response is "show me the score."

notes.subtitle: Shawn's directive (2026-10-04): if an operating law can be written into code — JSON, Python, whatever — it must be ENFORCED operating law, not advisory. Not a decision a seat makes each time. It's…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn's directive (2026-10-04): if an operating law can be written into code — JSON, Python, whatever — it must be ENFORCED operating law, not advisory. Not a decision a seat makes each time. It's just how the system is. The build pattern: unskippable state machines (skipping a state is impossible, not a bad choice), evidence counters that physically cannot double-count one provenance root, three-state gates where PROVISIONAL is falsy and "no known violation" can never authorize an ACT, and every law file carrying its own amendment path. Two boundaries, also enforced: code the amendment path, not just the law (the ratification route is the ONLY mutation route, in the loader); code the rails, not the driver (gates and transitions are coded; judgment inside them stays with the verifier). Lanes 2 (machine contract) and 4 (epistemic firewall) build to this pattern.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn looked at how the seats were treating operating law — each of us deciding, each time, whether to follow the rule — and changed the game: anything that can live in code must live in code, as enforcement. His specimen showed the causal learning chain as a state machine where an illegal transition raises instead of warns, and an evidence counter that simply refuses to count a repeated provenance root. The honest boundary he drew matters as much as the law: the machine enforces the shape of lawful behavior, never the wisdom itself. Verifiers still judge whether evidence is good; the code just makes it impossible to skip the question. Lanes 2 and 4 are building the loader and the epistemic states to this shape now.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a game where the rules are written on a poster — players can just ignore the poster. Now imagine the game board has walls: you can't walk through a wall, so you can't break the rule even if you wanted to. Shawn said: stop writing important rules on posters. Build walls. But he also said something kind: the walls should only stop the CHEATING moves — they should never stop the THINKING. The game still needs your brain; the board just makes sure you play fair.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Rules you have to remember to follow get forgotten. Rules built into the machine can't be. So Shawn's standing order is: whenever a rule CAN be built into the machinery, build it in — don't leave it as advice. But build it carefully: the machine should make the wrong move impossible, never make the smart judgment for you. The recipe also says the machine must carry the instructions for how the rule itself gets changed — by the director's word only — so the law can grow without breaking.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: THE LAW IS THE CODE (ratified 2026-10-03) was the principle; this directive is its build discipline. When you codify a law, three things must be in the code: the unskippable transitions (raise IllegalTransition, never warn), the amendment path (law files refused by the loader if the ratification record is invalid), and the rails-not-driver boundary (enforce the shape — sequence, gates, thresholds — never the verdict inside). The anti-citogenesis specimen is the canonical shape for evidence counting: same provenance root, repeated, is not new evidence — `return`, don't increment. If a rule is still advisory, either it can't be coded (say so) or it's not law yet.

notes.title: Dedupe Must Cover the Human-Visible ID, Not Just the Internal One
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Coda 3's watch blocked a collision with mechanical precision: two open PRs (#1356 and #1357, different branches, titles, content hashes) both declared `smart_note_id: SN-025`. Neither…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-04 Coda 3's watch blocked a collision with mechanical precision: two open PRs (#1356 and #1357, different branches, titles, content hashes) both declared `smart_note_id: SN-025`. Neither was on main. The defect is in the pipeline code: `tools/smart_note_v2.py:220` dedupes on `intelligent_block_id` only — never on `smart_note_id` — so whichever PR merges first writes `SN-025 → IB-A`, and the second, carrying an explicit `smart_note_id`, keeps `SN-025` and produces a second IB the dedupe misses. The registry then holds two entries both claiming SN-025 with different hashes and different IBs, and `retrieve()` (`:230-241`, returns `ranked[0]`) can no longer deterministically say which SN-025 a cold successor gets. This is the same defect class that closed #1352, walking in through a different door; the `discover()` batch guard does not catch it because it only sees multi-file commits, and these are two separate single-capture PRs. The durable rule: a dedupe must key on every identity the human sees, not just the machine's internal one. An internal ID and a human-visible ID are two different namespaces for retrieval truth — dedupe both. The enforcement landed in the same hour: PR #1369's conformance gate refuses duplicate `smart_note_id`s, and the Phase 1 law stands unchanged — check the live tree + open PRs + the board before claiming a number; first claim stands. For this loop specifically: that pre-claim check is exactly why the counter sequence on the smart-notes staging branch (now at SN-0255) must be checked against in-flight claims before any new number is taken — first claim stands, renumber yours.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Two different letters arrived with the same apartment number, and the mailroom's duplicate detector only checks the tracking codes, not the addresses. Whichever gets delivered first is fine — the problem is the second one lands in the same mailbox and nobody can say which letter you're holding. The rule: the detector must check every number a human can see, not just the ones the machines invented.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Two kids both named their drawings "picture number twenty-five." The filing cabinet only checks the secret code on the back, not the name on the front — so it files both under the same name, and when you ask for it, the drawer hands you whichever it grabs first. Fix the cabinet: check the name on the front too.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: If the library stamps two different books with the same catalog number, the card drawer can't help you find either one reliably. The stamp machine must check the catalog number it prints — not just the internal batch code — before stamping. Whoever got the number first keeps it; the second one gets a new number.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Identity is a contract with the reader, not the writer. The machine's internal `intelligent_block_id` is the writer's convenience; `smart_note_id` is what a cold successor asks for. A dedupe that covers only the former is a lie the system tells itself — it passes its own checks while the registry rots. Every dedupe in every pipeline must enumerate every identity the human can name and check all of them. And the human half of the fix is procedural, not code: check the live tree, the open PRs, and the board before claiming any number; first claim stands; renumber yours without argument.
